faqs.question: Which room should the home tuition session happen in?
faqs.answer: The dining table, in almost every Mumbai flat. It is shared, properly lit, large enough for two sets of papers and a laptop, and visible from the kitchen without anyone hovering over the child. A bedroom is worse on every count: private, soft, next to a bed and a charger, and the room where a long session drifts. If your dining area is the main walking line between the kitchen and the front door, use a study with the door propped open instead, or book the society clubhouse study room if your building has one. Keep the room the same every week, because students settle faster in a space they associate with work.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in the room during the session?
faqs.answer: Be at home, and out of the frame. For a Primary Years Programme child, sit in for the first ten minutes and the last five so the child sees the adults agreeing with each other, then be nearby. For an IGCSE student, stay in the flat but out of the room and ask for a two-line message at the end. For a Diploma Programme student, step back almost entirely, because managing a tutor is a skill they will need next year. A teenager will not admit to a tutor that they never understood a topic while a parent is standing behind the chair, and that admission is the whole point of the hour.

faqs.question: How do I get a tutor through my society gate for a weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Ask your society office for a standing weekly pass rather than per-visit clearance. Most Mumbai buildings can register a recurring visitor for the same day and hour, which removes the commonest cause of a late first session. Find out whether the register is paper or an app, and whether the app notification goes to your phone or the flat's registered number, because an unapproved request simply times out while the tutor waits in the lobby. In a Thane or Navi Mumbai township there are usually two gates, an outer one and a tower one, so mention that in advance and say which one the tutor should use.

faqs.question: A tutor has to travel to Kharghar on a weekday evening. Is that realistic?
faqs.answer: Only if the tutor already lives or teaches in that node. Navi Mumbai works node to node along Palm Beach Road: a tutor based in Vashi or Nerul reaches Belapur easily and Kharghar or Panvel with more effort, and one pulled across the creek from the island city for an evening slot will usually stop coming by the second month. The Atal Setu has shortened that crossing without making it pleasant in peak hours. We match inside the node first and treat a cross-creek match as a short-term arrangement rather than something that will hold for a full term.

faqs.question: What if my building restricts lift access after a certain hour?
faqs.answer: Tell us before the slot is fixed, because it changes which tutors can take it. Older South Mumbai buildings in Girgaon, Walkeshwar and Byculla often have one small lift, a service-lift rule for visitors, or a watchman who switches to a paper register late in the evening. A tutor climbing to the fourth floor of a walk-up is doing a different job from a tutor in a Lower Parel tower, and some will decline the slot once they know. It is far better to lose a match at the enquiry stage than in week three, and shifting the hour slightly earlier usually solves it outright.

faqs.question: Does an IB home tutor in Mumbai work better than online for a DP student?
faqs.answer: For Diploma Programme work, home usually wins, with online as a supplement. A tutor in the room sees the exercise book, the margin comments, the half-finished internal assessment and the phone lying face-up beside the notebook. They can hear an individual oral rehearsed properly and stop a Physics error at the second line instead of at the final answer. Online is the right choice for scarce subjects such as Higher Level Further Mathematics or Japanese, for a monsoon week, and for a short review the night before a submission. Most families end up using both by January, and that is the sensible outcome rather than a compromise.

faqs.question: My younger child watches television in the same room. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it ends more arrangements than weak teaching does. Ambient television is the commonest reason a session in a one or two-bedroom flat produces less than it should, and it is also the thing households are least willing to change. The workable version is a fixed hour in which the television is off and everybody knows it, treated the same way a school hour is treated. If that is genuinely impossible, the society clubhouse study room, or a hybrid pattern with some sessions online from a quieter corner, is a better answer than pretending the noise does not count against the hour.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level, subject scarcity, travel distance, session length and frequency, and whether the session is at your home or online. Diploma Programme Higher Level work draws on a narrower pool of tutors than IGCSE Core, so it costs more. A tutor crossing from Mulund to Bandra West at six in the evening is selling three hours in order to teach one, and that shows up in the rate. We do not publish a price list, because a figure quoted without your subject, level and address is a number invented for a web page. Ask for a range against your actual combination and you will get one.

faqs.question: The tutor is always ten minutes late. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Raise it in week two, directly, and give it one more week. Ten minutes a week is forty minutes a month of time you are paying for, and in Mumbai evening traffic it is usually a scheduling problem rather than a character problem: the tutor has a session before yours somewhere the Western Express Highway or Ghodbunder Road will not allow. Moving your slot fifteen minutes later often fixes it permanently. If it does not, tell us and we arrange a different tutor. A persistent late start is a legitimate reason to change someone, not a complaint about nothing.

faqs.question: What does good practice look like when a tutor is in the house with my child?
faqs.answer: A shared room, an adult at home, and no closed doors. A tutor should never be alone with a child in a bedroom, behind a closed door, or in a flat with no adult present, should not take the child out of the house, and should not photograph the child or their work without asking first. Scheduling messages should come to you rather than to the student. None of these are unusual requests and no reasonable tutor objects to them. If one does object, that is information worth acting on, and we would want to hear about it as well.

faqs.question: We tried a tutor and it is not working. How does a replacement happen?
faqs.answer: Say so after two sessions and we arrange another match. There is no notice period and no case to argue. What helps is one specific sentence about why: the explanations ran too fast, the tutor taught from a guidebook rather than the school's notes, the student never spoke, the hour never really suited. The second match then uses what the first one taught us about your household and your room as well as about the subject. Changing tutors early is normal, and a family that waits an entire term before saying anything usually loses that term.

sections.heading: How do IB home tutors in Mumbai get matched to a household, not just a student?
paragraphs: A match starts with the household, not the syllabus. Before any name reaches you, the intake call asks four things about your flat: which hour is genuinely free, which room is genuinely free in that hour, who else will be inside the flat, and who in the family is the person the tutor should call. Most matching failures here trace back to one of those four rather than to a tutor's subject knowledge. A parent typing best IB tutor in Mumbai into Google is usually looking for something the phrase cannot describe, which is a person who fits one particular flat at one particular hour.

The sequence runs like this. 1. You send the board, the year, the subjects and your area, and you say who else lives in the flat. 2. We ask about the hour and the room, because a six o'clock slot in a two-bedroom flat with a younger child doing homework at the same table is a different job from the same slot in a flat with a spare study. 3. You see a shortlist drawn from tutors who already travel inside your corridor. 4. One tutor visits for a first session the whole household has been told about in advance. 5. After two or three sessions you say whether the arrangement is holding, and the room, the hour or the tutor changes if it is not.

The question that surprises parents is the list of people. A grandparent who naps between five and six, a toddler, a cook who comes at half past six, an uncle staying for a fortnight: each of those is a scheduling fact, and a tutor told about it in advance plans around it. A tutor who discovers it in week three is already behind. Joint families in the Eastern Suburbs, households with live-in help in South Mumbai and single-parent households in Navi Mumbai all run differently, and the tutor who fits one is not automatically the tutor who fits another. That is why the shortlist of IB home tutors in Mumbai you receive is shaped by your household as much as by your subject list.

None of this is a promise about outcomes. IB Gram matches people and helps you set up the conditions they work in; the studying is still done by your child, and we do not guarantee grades. What the household can control is whether the hour exists, whether the room exists, and whether the student is the one doing the talking.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP, DP and IGCSE each ask something different of the family
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs three programmes a family here might be dealing with, and each one changes what the rest of the household has to do. A Primary Years Programme (PYP) child needs an adult in earshot and a short session. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) student needs a door that closes and a parent who stops checking. A Diploma Programme (DP) student needs an hour nobody in the flat crosses, plus the quiet hours either side of it.

In PYP the household is part of the lesson whether it wants to be. Sessions are short, the child wanders, and a younger sibling at the same table is usually a bigger obstacle than anything in the tutor's teaching. Parents of PYP children are the one group we actively encourage to stay nearby, because a six-year-old sent into a closed room with an adult they met last week spends the hour being polite instead of learning anything.

MYP, and the International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) run by Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, is where the household has to change its habits. A Year 9 or Year 10 student has to answer the tutor's questions personally, which means the parent who has been answering on their behalf has to stop doing it. This is the hardest single household adjustment, and it usually takes a parent two or three sessions to manage. Core and Extended tier decisions at IGCSE are made with the school rather than against it, and the tutor's job there is to tell you honestly which tier the current work supports.

DP is a two-year compression and it takes over the flat. Internal Assessment (IA) drafts, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) land in overlapping months, Higher Level (HL) subjects carry more of them than Standard Level (SL) subjects do, and a DP2 student needs a protected hour plus the unglamorous hours around it. In a joint family in Ghatkopar or Chembur that is a household negotiation rather than a timetable, and it has to happen before October, not during it.
bullets: PYP: short sessions, an adult in earshot, no sibling at the same table
MYP: closed door, the student answers, the parent stops interpreting
IGCSE: Core and Extended tier decisions taken with the school
DP: a protected hour plus quiet either side, HL subjects first
A flat with one PYP and one DP child needs two different rules

sections.heading: Which subjects need the dining table, and which need the door shut?
paragraphs: Subject choice decides the room. Visual Arts, Design Technology and anything involving a model, a sketchbook or a glued-together prototype needs a flat surface and tolerance for mess, so it ends up on the dining table. Language A orals, Physics data analysis and Mathematics problem sets need silence and a closed door. Most households in this city have one of those two things, not both, which is why the subject list and the floor plan have to be discussed together.

Across both boards the menu is wide: Mathematics at Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Physics, Chemistry and Biology, Economics and Business Management, Psychology, Geography and History, English Language and Literature, Hindi, French and Spanish, Computer Science, Environmental Systems and Societies. On the IGCSE side the same names reappear with Core and Extended tiers and the syllabus codes a parent sees on a report. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families study does not exist in one person. There is no single all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Mumbai, and anybody claiming the title is selling something, which is why most households settle on one tutor per one or two subjects.

The HL and SL decision, and the Core versus Extended decision at IGCSE, is where a tutor earns their keep before teaching anything. HL carries a heavier internal assessment and paper load; Extended opens grades that the Core tier caps. Both decisions carry a household cost nobody mentions at the school meeting: three HL subjects with laboratory write-ups means three evenings a week when the dining table belongs to one child. A single-child household absorbs that easily. A household with three children in three different years does not.

A worked example from a Powai flat. A DP1 student with HL Chemistry, HL Economics and SL Mathematics had her Chemistry IA data collection, an Economics commentary and a Mathematics exploration proposal fall inside five weeks. The tutor split the work by room rather than by subject difficulty: Chemistry took the dining table on two evenings because it needed paper spread out, Economics ran in the bedroom on a third because it needed only a laptop, and the younger brother shifted his own homework to the morning for that month. Nobody taught the brother anything. The household simply moved, and that was the intervention.
bullets: Visual Arts and Design Technology need a surface and mess tolerance
Language orals need a closed door, not a corner of the drawing room
Sciences need a socket, a laptop and space for a lab book
Mathematics needs paper spread out, which means a table, not a lap
One tutor across two subjects is realistic; one across six is not

sections.heading: Flat sizes, zones and the quiet-room problem across Mumbai
paragraphs: The honest version of IB home tuition in Mumbai, Maharashtra is that the quiet room is usually also some other room. Across the six zones, South Mumbai, the Western Suburbs, the Central Suburbs, the Eastern Suburbs, Navi Mumbai and Thane, flats get larger as you move north and east, and the household problem changes shape rather than disappearing. A search for IB tutors near me Mumbai returns the whole city, which is useless to you, because the only sense of near that matters is your own corridor at six in the evening.

South Mumbai has the oldest and often the smallest flats at the highest density. A two-bedroom in Walkeshwar or an older apartment in Cuffe Parade holding a family of five has no spare study, and the drawing room doubles as everything. Tutors are matched inside the island, from Colaba and Fort up through Worli, Tardeo and Parel, because a tutor crossing Peddar Road at six loses most of the hour to signals. The Coastal Road has helped the Worli to Nariman Point run; it has done nothing for the Haji Ali crawl. The Western Line from Churchgate and the Harbour Line out of CSMT carry the tutors who do not drive.

In the Western Suburbs, across Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri West, Goregaon East, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar, the housing stock is mixed: an older Khar bungalow conversion and a new Kandivali tower are different households entirely, one with three generations and one with two working parents. Matching along the Western Line and Link Road works; matching across the Western Express Highway does not. The Central Suburbs run Kurla, Ghatkopar, Vikhroli, Kanjurmarg and Mulund on the Central Line, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR and no station of their own, so tutors arrive there by road from Andheri East or Ghatkopar. Metro Line 1 between Versova, Andheri and Ghatkopar, Metro Lines 2A and 7 down from Dahisar and the Santacruz Chembur Link Road have made a handful of pairings workable that were not workable before.

The Eastern Suburbs, covering Chembur, Govandi, Wadala and Bhandup, sit on the Central and Harbour lines with the Eastern Express Highway and the Eastern Freeway behind them, and tend to hold larger older flats with more extended family inside them. Navi Mumbai is nodal: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar, Panvel and Airoli, joined by Palm Beach Road, the Sion Panvel Highway and now the Atal Setu, with the largest flats and the most realistic chance of a genuine spare bedroom. Thane spreads west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada, Ghodbunder Road and Kasarvadavali, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets everybody's schedule. Across all six zones, IB home tutors in Mumbai are matched node to node and corridor to corridor, because a tutor who crosses a zone twice a week stops doing it after one term.
bullets: South Mumbai: small flats, short distances, slow evenings, island matching
Western Suburbs: match along the Western Line, not across the highway
Central Suburbs: Powai and Chandivali reached by road off JVLR
Eastern Suburbs: larger older flats, more extended family in the room
Navi Mumbai and Thane: the best spare-room odds, the worst evening traffic

sections.heading: School calendars set the weeks your Mumbai household will argue
paragraphs: Every household row about tuition happens in the same four or five weeks of the year, and the school calendar puts them there. Report weeks, mock weeks, IA deadline clusters and the May examination session are when a parent who was relaxed in August becomes the parent sitting in the session in January. Knowing those dates in advance is most of the fix, because a room rule agreed in July survives mock season and a room rule invented during mock season does not.

Families here attend Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, which draw from both sides of the Bandra Worli Sea Link, along with Ascend International School in the same few streets. In Juhu it is Ecole Mondiale World School, Jamnabai Narsee International School and Utpal Shanghvi Global School, all within a short radius of each other and of the same households. Oberoi International School sits on JVLR in Goregaon East. South Mumbai has Bombay International School at Babulnath, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Activity High School on Peddar Road, Gopi Birla Memorial School in Walkeshwar and Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo. Further out there is Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, the JBCN International School campuses in Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page; a school name here only tells you whose assessment calendar your household has to plan around.

The BKC schools pull families from both sides of the Sea Link, so a Worli household and a Bandra household can sit in the same classroom with completely different evenings. Metro Line 3 between Cuffe Parade and BKC has begun to change which tutors can realistically take a South Mumbai family's six o'clock slot. The practical point for the household is that the assessment calendar belongs to the school rather than to you, and the weeks it loads up are the weeks you want the room rules already settled and the grandparents already told.

Through a typical year it runs like this. June and July are settling months and the cheapest time to establish the room and the hour. August and September bring the first criterion-marked MYP tasks and the IGCSE mid-terms. October and November are the first real squeeze, with DP1 IA proposals and DP2 drafts landing together. December is lost to holidays and then recovered badly in the first week of January. January and February are mock season, which is also the period when two parents most often disagree with each other about the tutor. March, April and May belong to the examination sessions, and by then a household either has a working arrangement or it has an argument.
bullets: June and July: set the room and the hour before pressure arrives
August and September: first criterion-marked tasks and mid-terms
October and November: IA proposals and drafts collide
January and February: mock results, and the month families argue
March to May: examinations, with no time left to renegotiate rooms

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for a crowded Mumbai flat?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default and it costs the household a room. Online costs a device, a socket and headphones, and it leaves the door open, which is why it fails in flats where nobody can keep the noise down. Hybrid splits the two on purpose: the tutor visits for the sessions that need a table and goes online for the ones that need only a screen. Choose by what your flat can spare, not by what sounds modern.

An IB home tutor in Mumbai arriving at your door removes one room from the family for an hour and adds a guest to the flat. That is a real cost and it is worth saying out loud at the start rather than resenting it in week six. What you get for it is a tutor who sees what you see: the sibling at the same table, the television in the next room, the phone lying face up beside the notebook. A tutor who has watched the actual study conditions gives different and better advice than one who has only been told about them over a call.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai works well for a DP2 student with a door, a desk and an existing habit, and badly for an MYP student in a shared bedroom. Online also relocates the problem rather than removing it. The room is still occupied, but now the household hears only one side of the conversation, which oddly makes relatives more likely to walk in and interrupt. Headphones, a fixed corner and a household rule about the hour matter more online than they do with a tutor physically in the flat.

Hybrid is where most multi-child households end up. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects the home classes Mumbai parents book tend to settle into one of three shapes within a month: one subject keeps a weekly home visit because it needs the table, a second runs online midweek when the flat is quieter, and revision before mocks moves back to home visits because that is when a student needs somebody physically present. None of the three modes repairs a household that has not agreed on the hour, and no mode makes a grade certain.
bullets: Home: costs a room, gains a tutor who sees the real conditions
Online: costs a socket and headphones, needs a household noise rule
Hybrid: table subjects at home, screen subjects online, revision at home
A shared bedroom works badly online and badly in person without a rule
A standing weekly slot holds better than a flexible one in almost every flat

sections.heading: What the household should watch in the first three visits
paragraphs: Verification has two halves and only one of them is ours. IB Gram checks identity documents, the claimed qualification and the board experience a tutor states, and asks for references where a tutor says they have taught a named programme. The household checks the half no document covers, which is how this person behaves inside your flat with everybody else in it. An IB private tutor Mumbai parents find through a neighbour arrives with neither half done, and that is fine until it is not.

What to watch in the first visit: does the tutor greet the grandparents and the household help, or walk straight past them. Does the tutor ask where to sit or take the best chair. Does the tutor speak to your child, or speak to you about your child while your child sits there. The last one predicts the most. A tutor who answers your question by turning to your son and asking him to explain where he got stuck is a tutor who will still be useful in March.

By the third visit you should know whether this person can hold a room that is not fully theirs. A younger sibling will wander in, and the correct response is a one-sentence redirection followed by carrying on, not a complaint to you afterwards. Somebody will ring the doorbell, and the correct response is to keep going. Checking IB home tutors in Mumbai on paper is straightforward and we do that part. Checking whether a person can teach in a flat with five people in it is something only you can see, and three visits is enough to see it.

Ask directly for the things no document shows: which years of the programme they have actually taught rather than studied, whether they teach two subjects deeply or six thinly, what they do with a student who has not done the work, and what they do when a parent interrupts mid-session. A tutor with a ready answer to the last question has taught in a Mumbai flat before. A tutor who looks puzzled by it has not, and your household will be where they learn.
bullets: Identity, qualification and board experience checked before the first visit
Watch whether the tutor addresses your child or talks over them
Watch how the tutor greets grandparents and household staff
A wandering sibling should be redirected, not reported to you
Ask which years and which subjects they have actually taught

sections.heading: What is the parent's actual job while an IB home tutor in Mumbai is teaching?
paragraphs: The parent's job during the session is to be reachable and absent. Reachable means in the flat, findable, and free for a two-minute conversation at the end. Absent means not in the room, not in the student's eyeline, and not answering a question that was put to the student. Almost every parent gets one of those two halves wrong, and the three ways it goes wrong are predictable enough to name.

The first failure is sitting in the session. It feels responsible and it reliably stops the teaching, because a fifteen-year-old will not say the words I do not understand in front of a parent. The tutor then spends the hour performing competence for the adult in the chair instead of hunting for the gap. The second failure is relaying: the parent answers for the student, explains what the student meant, or carries messages between tutor and child in both directions for a whole term. The student stops having to articulate anything, which is exactly the skill the IA, the EE and every oral component measures. The third failure is the opposite of the first, going silent for an entire term and reappearing after the January mock results with a list of complaints the tutor could have dealt with in October.

Parents also disagree with each other, and when they do the tutor is caught between two sets of instructions. One parent thinks the progress is obvious and the other thinks nothing is happening, and usually they are measuring different things: one is watching whether the child looks less anxious on a Tuesday, the other is watching a number on a report. Both are legitimate and neither is the whole picture. The fix is boring. Agree between yourselves on two or three specific things you will watch, write them down before the first session, and tell the tutor what they are. A tutor who knows the household is watching paper two scores and the willingness to attempt a question unaided can report against that. A tutor receiving contradictory instructions from two parents simply reports to whoever called last.

The last piece is household time rather than household money. A single-child household has one hour to protect and one set of preferences to satisfy, and its usual failure is over-scheduling: four subjects, four tutors, and no evening left in which the student works alone. A multi-child household has the opposite problem and harder arithmetic. Two children, two sessions, one quiet room and one shared table means the younger child's homework moves every week for the whole term, and resentment arrives around week five. Families solve it by staggering days rather than hours, giving the older child Monday and Thursday and the younger Tuesday and Friday, with Wednesday left empty on purpose. The empty evening does more for both children than an extra session would.
bullets: Be reachable in the flat and absent from the room
Let the student answer badly rather than answering on their behalf
Do not vanish for a term and arrive with complaints after mocks
Agree two or three progress measures with your partner before session one
Stagger siblings across days and leave one evening deliberately empty
Four subjects with four tutors leaves no hour for unsupervised work

sections.heading: What progress looks like to the rest of the household
paragraphs: At four weeks you should be looking for household signals rather than marks. The student brings books to the table before the tutor arrives. The student asks the tutor a question nobody prompted. The student stops needing to be called twice. Marks at four weeks are noise, and reading them as evidence either way is how families end up changing a tutor who was working. If none of those three signals has appeared inside a month, say so plainly instead of waiting for a report to confirm it.

At one term the measure changes to work the school has marked: a criterion-marked MYP task, an IGCSE mid-term, a DP paper two attempt, an IA draft returned with usable feedback rather than an instruction to start again. A term is also long enough to tell whether the household arrangement itself held. Did the hour survive two festivals, one illness, one examination week and a cousin staying for a week. An arrangement that survives those four survives the year, and an arrangement that collapsed at the first festival was never an arrangement.

At one examination cycle you are comparing predicted grades with actual performance, and separately asking whether the student can work with no tutor in the flat. The second question is the real outcome. A DP2 student in Chembur who sits down on a Sunday morning and works through a past paper alone has got something out of the arrangement that no grade displays. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no tutor honestly can; what a working arrangement changes is the number of hours a student will put in unsupervised, and that is the thing that moves results.

If it is not working, keep the conversation short and specific. Separate the three problems, because the room, the hour and the person are different things and two of them are cheaper to fix than the third. A tutor who teaches well but arrives twenty minutes late every week is a slot problem. A tutor whose sessions keep getting interrupted is a room problem. A tutor your child will not speak to, or who speaks to you instead of your child, is a fit problem, and that is a replacement: tell us, get a fresh shortlist from the same corridor, and do not start the search from nothing. Nobody has to justify a mismatch beyond describing it.
bullets: Four weeks: books on the table before the tutor rings the bell
Four weeks: the student asks a question without being prompted
One term: school-marked work, and an hour that survived a festival week
One exam cycle: hours worked alone, not only the predicted grade
Not working out: name the room, the hour or the person separately

sections.heading: One room, one table, one hour: setting up home tuition in Mumbai
paragraphs: Before the first session the household needs three decisions, and they take one conversation at dinner. One room, named out loud. One table or desk inside it, cleared and then left cleared. One hour on fixed days that nobody in the family crosses, including the parent who only wants to ask something quick. Write the hour on the fridge if that is what it takes to make it real for everybody in the flat.

Then the practical layer. Tell your society gate the tutor's name and the standing slot so the tutor is not held at the desk every week; most buildings in Mumbai will issue a repeat-visitor entry once somebody asks. Move the cook, the dog walker and the grocery delivery outside the hour where you can, and accept one planned interruption where you cannot. Tell the grandparents about the hour before the first visit rather than after the first clash over the television. Tell the younger sibling where they are going to sit instead that evening, because a vague instruction to stay out of the way produces a child standing in the doorway.

For the tutor, have four things ready: the last report card, the school's assessment calendar if you have been given one, the subject list with HL, SL, Core and Extended levels marked, and one honest sentence about what your child finds hardest. The first home session is mostly diagnostic. Expect the tutor to ask your child to attempt something and to get it wrong, and expect a short closing conversation with you that is specific rather than reassuring.

Last, decide who in the family is the tutor's contact. One person, not two. That person books, reschedules and raises problems, and relays nothing about the actual work, leaving the student and the tutor to talk to each other directly. Households that get this single thing right rarely need to change much else.
bullets: Name the room and the table, then keep the table cleared
Fix the hour on set days and tell the whole household, elders included
Register the tutor at the society gate for a standing weekly slot
Keep the last report card and the school calendar ready
Appoint one family contact who books and does not relay messages

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in the room while the home tutor is teaching?
faqs.answer: No, with two exceptions: a Primary Years Programme child, and sometimes the very first session. A parent in the room changes what a teenager is willing to admit, and admitting the gap is the entire job of the first few weeks. Stay in the flat, stay reachable, and take two minutes at the end. For a PYP child the rule flips, because a six-year-old alone with a new adult spends the hour being well behaved rather than learning, so sit near enough to be seen and far enough not to answer.

faqs.question: The only quiet room in our flat is where my mother-in-law watches television every evening. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Move the hour rather than the room, and ask once instead of renegotiating weekly. In a great many Mumbai flats the quiet room is also the television room, so the real conflict is over a slot and not over a space. A seven-thirty start, an eight o'clock start or a weekend morning usually costs the household far less than asking an elder to give up the evening. If the hour genuinely cannot move, a bedroom with a small desk and a closed door beats a drawing room with a muted television in it.

faqs.question: Our two children share a study table. Can one home tutor teach both?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but never at the same time and rarely in the same subject year. Two children at one table with one tutor means each child gets half an hour of attention and a full hour of distraction. Stagger them across different days, which frees the table as well. One tutor teaching both back to back in a single visit does work when the subjects line up, for example IGCSE Mathematics for the older child and MYP Mathematics for the younger, and when the tutor is willing to stay for two hours and you are willing to pay for the travel once.

faqs.question: The tutor reaches our building at 6pm and the cook arrives fifteen minutes later. How do families handle the interruptions?
faqs.answer: Shift the smaller commitment, which is almost never the tutor. Domestic staff timings, grocery deliveries and the dog walker can usually move by fifteen or thirty minutes; a tutor who has come from Vikhroli to Mulund in evening traffic cannot. Where staff timings truly cannot move, tell the tutor in advance so the interruption is planned rather than a surprise, and keep the study door shut so kitchen noise stays background. One known interruption a session is survivable. Three unannounced ones end the arrangement by December.

faqs.question: My husband thinks the tutor is working and I do not. How do we settle it?
faqs.answer: Agree on what each of you is measuring before arguing about the answer. One of you is probably watching behaviour and the other is watching marks, and those two move on very different timescales. Write down two or three specific measures, for instance paper two scores, willingness to attempt a question unaided, and whether IA drafts come back with feedback rather than an order to restart. Tell the tutor those are the measures. A tutor with one clear brief from one household contact is far more useful than a tutor fielding two contradictory ones.

faqs.question: Does a tutor travelling from Andheri to Nerul for a weekday evening slot actually last a full term?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and we try not to set that arrangement up in the first place. A weekday evening crossing between the Western Suburbs and Navi Mumbai means the Sion Panvel Highway or the Atal Setu at peak hour, and the tutor who cheerfully agreed in June begins cancelling in September. Node-to-node matching inside Navi Mumbai, or matching along the Western Line inside the suburbs, holds much better. For a genuinely scarce subject the honest answer is a weekend home visit plus one online session midweek.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length, in roughly that order. An HL Diploma Programme subject sits above an MYP one, a scarce subject sits above a common one, and a tutor crossing a zone prices the travel in whether or not it shows as a separate line. Session length and frequency change the monthly figure more than the hourly rate does. There is no price list on this page because a real quote depends on your subject combination, your area and the slot you want, and quoting a number before knowing those three is guesswork.

faqs.question: A younger sibling keeps walking into the session. Is that the tutor's problem or ours?
faqs.answer: Yours to prevent and the tutor's to handle gracefully when prevention fails. Give the younger child somewhere specific to be during the hour and something specific to do there, because a vague instruction to stay away produces a child in the doorway within ten minutes. A tutor should redirect a wandering five-year-old in one sentence and carry on teaching. A tutor who stops the lesson to find a parent about it is telling you how they will handle a genuinely bad week later in the year.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Tell us what specifically is wrong and you get a fresh shortlist from the same corridor without starting over. Separate the three possible problems first. Late arrivals and a cancellation every fortnight are a slot problem and often fixable by moving the day. Constant interruptions are a room problem and belong to the household. A tutor your child will not speak to, or who talks to you instead of to your child, is a fit problem, and that is a replacement. Nobody has to justify a mismatch beyond describing it accurately.

faqs.question: We live in a one-bedroom flat in Dadar. Is home tuition even realistic?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a different setup. IB home tuition in Mumbai flats of this size works when the study space is a cleared dining table and the quiet is produced by scheduling rather than by walls, so the hour matters much more than the room. Pick the slot when fewest people are home, usually earlier in the evening or a weekend morning, agree that the television goes off rather than low, and keep it to one subject at a time. Plenty of households across South Mumbai and the older Central Suburbs buildings run exactly this way.

faqs.question: Nobody in our family speaks to the tutor except me. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Only if you are relaying the teaching rather than the logistics. One family contact for booking, rescheduling and raising problems is the right setup and it stops a tutor receiving two sets of instructions. What should not route through you is the work itself. Your child needs to tell the tutor directly what they did not understand, and the tutor needs to tell your child directly what to do next. If you are explaining each to the other, the student never learns to ask, and asking is what the oral components and the IA actually test.

ib-home-tutors.closingCta: Send the board, the year, the subjects, your area and one line about who else is in the flat during your preferred hour. You will get a shortlist of tutors who already travel inside your corridor, and a first home session arranged for a slot the whole household has been told about. After two or three sessions you tell us whether the room, the hour and the tutor are each working, and we change whichever one is not.

ib-igcse-classes.heroIntro: Almost everything written about IB IGCSE classes in Mumbai assumes a problem. This page is for the other student: the one scoring well, finishing early and switching off. What a capable child in an IGCSE or Diploma classroom actually needs is depth rather than speed, and sometimes the honest answer is not a home tutor at all but something they choose themselves.
trustPoints: Depth within the current topic, not Diploma content pushed into Year 10
We will say when an activity would serve your child better than tuition

sections.heading: How IB Gram shortlists IB IGCSE classes in Mumbai for a student who is ahead
paragraphs: The brief for a strong student is the opposite of the usual one, and the usual intake questions produce the wrong tutor. We do not ask what is going wrong. We ask for a piece of work the student is pleased with, the mark it got, and what the student says is missing from the subject at school. That last answer is the whole match. A Year 10 student who says the Physics is fine but she wants to know why the formula is true needs a very different person from a student who says he is bored because the class is slow, who may simply need more interesting work rather than harder work.

The shortlist is then built around teaching ceiling rather than coverage. We look for tutors who have taught beyond the specification, who have supervised Extended Essays or research projects, who have worked with students sitting external subject examinations, or who come from a background where being wrong in front of a student is normal. Coverage tutors, who are excellent with a struggling Year 11, are not the right match here and we say so rather than filling the slot. Depth across all IB and IGCSE subjects needs more than one tutor in Mumbai, so expect a specialist per subject rather than a generalist.

Before anything is booked we ask for a trial of substance, not a diagnostic conversation. The tutor sets one genuinely hard question inside a topic the student says is easy, and both the student and the parent watch what happens in the first few minutes. That single exchange answers more than any assessment: whether the student is bored or quietly stuck, whether they have any strategy when they do not immediately see the answer, and whether this particular tutor can hold a conversation at that level without retreating into revision. If the answer is that the student does not need a tutor, we will say that too.
bullets: 1. Send a piece of work the student is proud of, with its mark
2. Tell us what the student says is missing from the subject at school
3. We shortlist tutors with experience above the specification, not coverage tutors
4. The tutor sets one hard question in a topic the student calls easy
5. You decide afterwards whether this needs a tutor or something else entirely

sections.heading: What does being ahead actually mean at IGCSE and in the Diploma?
paragraphs: Being ahead means different things in each programme, and the difference decides what is worth doing. At International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) level the ceiling arrives early. A student entered for Extended papers who is comfortably producing top band work in Year 10 has nowhere further to go inside the course, because the grade does not get better than the top grade and there is no extension paper waiting. This is the single most common reason a capable Year 10 in Mumbai disengages: the course has stopped asking anything of them and there are eighteen months left to run.

The sensible responses at that point are lateral rather than forward. Additional Mathematics alongside the main entry, where the school offers it, is genuinely harder rather than merely earlier. A second science taken as a separate subject instead of within Coordinated Sciences adds depth. A language taken to a higher tier, or a subject the school does not teach at all entered externally, changes the shape of the week. A plan covering all IB and IGCSE subjects through home classes in Mumbai is almost never right for this student, because the point is not more hours across everything but serious work in the one or two subjects they actually care about.

In the Diploma Programme the picture inverts. Higher Level (HL) subjects do have a real ceiling well above what most students reach, so a strong Diploma student usually has plenty of room inside their own course. The constraint becomes time rather than difficulty. The useful enrichment here is almost always the Extended Essay (EE), the Internal Assessment (IA) in a subject they care about, or Theory of Knowledge (TOK) taken more seriously than the timetable allows, because these are the parts of the Diploma where a capable student can do something genuinely their own. Middle Years Programme (MYP) students sit somewhere between the two, with criteria that reward independent investigation and schools that rarely have time to push it.

Additional Mathematics is harder work rather than earlier work
Separate sciences add depth that Coordinated Sciences cannot

sections.heading: Depth, not speed: what harder home classes look like subject by subject
paragraphs: Depth means a harder question inside the topic the class is already on, and every subject has its own version. In Maths it is a question that needs two topics combined rather than one applied, such as a circle theorem problem that only yields to trigonometry, or being asked to prove a result the class has been told to use. In Physics it is deriving the equation rather than substituting into it, estimating an answer to within an order of magnitude with no data supplied, or redesigning a prescribed practical and quantifying why the new version has smaller uncertainty. In Chemistry it is mechanism and energetics reasoning: not what happens, but why this product and not the other one.

In the humanities and languages the same principle produces different work. In History it is reading two historians who disagree about the same event and being asked which evidence each one is leaning on, which is far more demanding than learning the causes of anything. In English it is an unseen text that is harder than the set texts, or reading what critics said about a set text when it was published and arguing with them. In Economics it is reading a central bank statement and testing whether the model from the textbook actually explains it. In a Language B course it is moving into literature in that language earlier than the syllabus requires. In Biology it is reading the methods section of a real paper and finding the weakness in the study design.

Reading beyond the specification deserves its own line, because it is the cheapest enrichment there is and it does not need a weekly slot. A good tutor for a capable student spends part of the hour recommending things and the rest discussing what was read, which looks unproductive to a parent used to worked examples and is usually the most valuable part of the arrangement. The test of whether depth is working is simple. The student should be unable to finish some of what they are set, and should be comfortable with that. A capable student who has never been stuck has no strategy for being stuck, and that bill always arrives later.
bullets: A good hard question combines two topics instead of applying one
Ask for the derivation, not another substitution into the same formula
Two historians who disagree teach more than a complete causes list
Reading beyond the specification is the cheapest enrichment available
The student should sometimes fail to finish, and should find that normal

sections.heading: Mumbai zone by zone: where enrichment tutors and subject depth are found
paragraphs: IB Gram matches across Mumbai, Maharashtra, and for enrichment work the geography behaves differently from ordinary tuition. The Western Suburbs hold the largest concentration of international school families, running from Bandra West and Khar West through Santacruz, Vile Parle, Juhu, Versova, Jogeshwari, Lokhandwala and Andheri West up through Goregaon, Malad and Kandivali to Borivali and Dahisar East. The Western Line, the Western Express Highway, the Link Road and Metro Lines 1, 2A and 7 make north to south matching along the corridor straightforward. A specialist who can teach Further Mathematics or supervise a serious research essay is scarce everywhere, so families here often find the right person two or three stations away rather than in the next lane, and IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai is worth stretching the travel radius for when the subject is unusual.

South Mumbai is a smaller pool with a deeper bench in some subjects. Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Churchgate, Marine Lines, Walkeshwar, Napean Sea Road, Peddar Road, Worli and Lower Parel are minutes apart on paper and considerably further at the evening peak around Haji Ali, with the Western Line into Churchgate and Grant Road, the Harbour Line to Dockyard, the Coastal Road and Metro Line 3 between Cuffe Parade and the Bandra Kurla Complex carrying the traffic. Older academics, writers and researchers who make excellent enrichment tutors are easier to find on the island than in the outer suburbs, and for a student doing depth work rather than exam preparation a Saturday morning session in this zone often works better than a weekday evening.

The Central and Eastern Suburbs cover Sion, Matunga, Kurla, Ghatkopar, Powai, Chandivali, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund, plus Chembur, Wadala and Govandi, served by the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway, the Eastern Freeway, the Monorail, the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road and the Santacruz Chembur Link Road. Powai has no station of its own and is reached by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar. This belt has an unusually strong supply of engineering and science graduates, which makes it the easiest part of the city to find someone who can genuinely stretch a strong Physics or Computer Science student.

Navi Mumbai works node to node across Airoli, Vashi, Sanpada, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, linked by Palm Beach Road, the Sion Panvel Highway, the Harbour and Trans Harbour lines, Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 and the Atal Setu. Thane runs east from the station through Vartak Nagar, Pokhran Road and Majiwada to Hiranandani Estate and Kasarvadavali along Ghodbunder Road, which governs every evening schedule in the zone. In both, the pool of specialists is thinner, and this is the clearest case in the city for running depth work online rather than insisting on someone local who teaches the subject only to the syllabus.
bullets: Stretch the travel radius for a scarce subject; depth work tolerates distance better
Saturday mornings suit depth work better than a weekday evening slot
The Powai and Chandivali belt has the deepest science and computing pool
Island city tutors often include researchers and writers suited to enrichment

sections.heading: The Mumbai school calendar has three windows where enrichment fits
paragraphs: Enrichment competes with the school timetable rather than supporting it, which means it only really works in three windows. The first is June to September, the start of the Mumbai school year, when assessment pressure is at its lowest and a student has the appetite for something extra. The second is the fortnight after October term tests and Diploma mocks, when the student has just been shown exactly where their ceiling is and is unusually open to being pushed. The third is the stretch after the May examinations, when a Year 11 moving into the Diploma has months of genuinely free time and nothing structured to use it on.

The months to avoid are equally clear. January and February belong to Internal Assessment deadlines across most Diploma subjects, the Extended Essay submission and the TOK essay, and adding enrichment there is a reliable way to make a capable student resent the subject they used to like. March and April are prelims and revision. Families at Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, the American School of Bombay and Ascend International School in the Bandra Kurla Complex, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Bombay International School in Babulnath and Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane all run their own variations of this shape, and most publish enough of it for a parent to plan a year around.

Many Mumbai schools already have some provision for students who are ahead, and it is worth exhausting that before paying for anything. Subject clubs, Model United Nations, olympiad training, science fairs, debating, a research cohort, a student publication, permission to sit an additional subject externally. Ask the subject teacher directly what they would suggest for a student who finishes early, because teachers usually have an answer and are rarely asked. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, with the International Baccalaureate organisation, with Cambridge International Education or with Pearson Edexcel. We name schools here only because their calendars decide when there is room in a week.
bullets: June to September is the best window to start depth work
The fortnight after October mocks is when a strong student is most receptive
The post examination months are wasted time for most Year 11 students
January and February are the worst months to add anything optional
Ask the subject teacher what they suggest before hiring anyone

sections.heading: Do home classes or online lessons suit an advanced student in Mumbai better?
paragraphs: For a student who is ahead, online frequently wins, which reverses the usual advice. The limiting factor is not attention or supervision but finding somebody who can teach above the syllabus in a specific subject, and that person may be in another city. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai can also be a subject specialist who would never take a weekday travel slot. Home classes still matter, and for younger students they matter more, but this is the one request where insisting on someone local can mean settling for someone who only knows the specification.

Home sessions have real advantages that are worth naming. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai sitting at the same table can watch how a student attacks an unfamiliar problem, which is exactly the thing being developed and is almost invisible on a screen. Paper and a pencil beat a shared document for the kind of exploratory work that depth requires. A home session also keeps a younger student honest about doing the reading. Against that, the travel cost is real, a weekday evening slot in Bandra West or Kharghar is the hardest to protect, and for enrichment specifically there is no deadline forcing the issue, so a difficult slot quietly dies by November.

Hybrid solves most of it. Many families running IB IGCSE classes in Mumbai for an advanced student settle on a fortnightly home session for the discussion and the stuck moments, with shorter online contact in between to look at what has been read or written. Two shorter sessions often beat one long one here, because depth work needs time between sessions for the student to get properly stuck. Whichever you choose, keep the slot at a time the student is awake and willing, not at the end of a day that already had eight hours of school in it.
bullets: Online widens the pool to specialists who will not travel on a weekday
Home sessions show how a student attacks an unfamiliar problem
Paper and pencil beat a shared screen for exploratory work
Fortnightly home sessions with online contact between them often work best
An enrichment slot with no deadline behind it dies quietly if it is inconvenient

sections.heading: How to check a tutor can teach above the specification
paragraphs: Before any tutor is listed we verify identity documents, the qualification claimed and the teaching history against the current specification. For enrichment requests we ask two further things: what is the hardest thing you have taught in this subject, and when did you last learn something new in it. The second question matters more than it sounds. A tutor whose subject knowledge stopped at the syllabus will run out of road with a strong student inside a term, and both the tutor and the student will know it before the parent does. We do not rate tutors with stars and we publish no results claims, so these conversations are the check.

Parents should run three tests on the first call, and they take ten minutes. Ask the tutor to set a question in this subject that they would not expect the student to finish, and listen to whether they can produce one on the spot. Ask what they would recommend the student read, and whether the answer is a book or a revision guide. Ask what they would do if the student asked something they did not know, because the only acceptable answer is that they would say so and find out, and a surprising number of tutors cannot say that out loud. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Mumbai families hire for depth work has to be comfortable being the second cleverest person in the room sometimes.

Parents often search for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai, and for this request the phrase is particularly unhelpful, because the right person is defined entirely by the subject and the student. The best tutor for a Year 10 who wants to understand why calculus works is a mathematician who enjoys explaining it, and that person may be mediocre at examination technique. Decide which of the two things you are buying before you start, because the tutor who maximises a predicted grade and the tutor who makes a subject interesting are usually different people, and asking one to be the other produces a disappointing version of both.
bullets: Ask the tutor to set a question they would not expect the student to finish
Ask what the student should read, and judge whether the answer is a revision guide
A tutor who cannot say they do not know is the wrong tutor here
Ask when the tutor last learned something new in this subject
Decide whether you want examination technique or genuine depth, not both at once

sections.heading: Is my child bored in class, or quietly struggling in Mumbai?
paragraphs: They look identical from the outside, which is why so many Mumbai families hire the wrong kind of help. Both the bored student and the quietly struggling student say the subject is easy, do the minimum homework, resist showing their working, lose interest in class and describe the teacher as dull. Both produce a slow drift downwards in marks that nobody can fully explain. Hiring an enrichment tutor for a struggling student is demoralising and expensive, and hiring a revision tutor for a bored student guarantees the student stops cooperating within a month.

Four tests separate them reliably. First, set one genuinely hard question inside a topic the student calls easy and watch the opening minutes: a bored student leans in almost immediately, while a struggling student goes quiet, changes the subject or asks whether this will be in the exam. Second, ask them to teach you the topic. A bored student explains it fluently and starts adding things that were not asked for; a struggling student recites a definition and stops. Third, look at where the marks were actually lost. Boredom shows up as careless arithmetic and long structured questions abandoned halfway; difficulty shows up as the same conceptual step failing in four different questions. Fourth, compare speed with accuracy, because both students finish early, and only one of them finishes early and right.

Then there is the question of racing ahead, which is the most common and least useful response to boredom. Teaching Diploma content to a Year 10 feels like progress and rarely is. The student meets the material without the mathematical or analytical maturity to hold it, builds a shallow memory of it, and is then bored a second time when the class arrives there eighteen months later with the memory faded. Worse, a student who believes they have already covered a topic stops listening in the lesson where the department explains the conventions, the expected working and the framing their examinations will actually use. There is no reward anywhere in either system for having covered content early. There is a real penalty for disengaging from the classroom.

Which brings up the answer nobody selling tuition wants to give. Sometimes a capable, bored student does not need a tutor. They need a thing of their own: a competition, a project with an actual output, a coding problem nobody has set them, a research group, a debating circuit, an instrument, a sport, a job, a book list and the hours to read it. A tutor adds one more adult directed hour to a week that is already entirely adult directed, and for a self motivated student that can be exactly the wrong move. Where a tutor genuinely earns the slot is narrower and clearer: a subject the school does not offer, early mentoring on an Extended Essay or an Internal Assessment question, preparation for an external subject examination, or a student who wants to go deep and has nobody at home or at school to argue with about it. If your situation is not one of those, we will tell you, and we would rather lose the booking than take it.
bullets: Both boredom and quiet struggle produce the same complaints and the same drift
One hard question in an easy topic separates them within two minutes
A bored student teaches you the topic and adds to it; a struggling one recites
Boredom loses careless marks; difficulty loses the same step repeatedly
Covering Diploma content early earns nothing and costs classroom attention
A competition, a project or a book list often beats another weekly hour

sections.heading: What does progress look like when the grade is already high?
paragraphs: The usual markers are useless here, because the mark cannot go up much and may well dip while the student is doing something harder than usual. At four weeks, progress looks like the student bringing their own questions to the session instead of waiting to be set work, and saying out loud that something was difficult. At one term it looks like a piece of work that was not required by anyone: a longer answer than the task asked for, a piece of reading they finished, an Extended Essay question they have actually narrowed. At one examination cycle the grade is whatever it was always going to be, and the honest measure is whether the student still finds the subject worth their time.

That is also the limit of what anyone can promise. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and for an already strong student the claim would be particularly empty, because the grade was largely secured before any tutor arrived. What enrichment can reasonably do is keep a capable student engaged with a subject through two years that would otherwise bore them, give them practice at being stuck, and produce one or two pieces of work that are genuinely their own. Those are real outcomes and they are worth paying for. A higher number on a report card is not what you are buying.

Review it honestly at the end of each term, and be willing to stop. The most common failure in enrichment arrangements is not a bad tutor but a good one who has run out of road, which happens quietly and which the student will notice first. Ask the student directly whether the hour is still worth it and take the answer seriously, including when the answer is no. If the fit is wrong rather than finished, tell us and we will reshortlist from the same brief. If the honest conclusion is that the hour would be better spent on a project the student chose themselves, that is a successful ending, not a failed arrangement.
bullets: Four weeks: the student brings their own questions instead of waiting for work
One term: a piece of work nobody required them to produce
The mark may dip while the work gets harder, and that is acceptable
No tutor can guarantee a grade, least of all for a student already near the top
Ask the student each term whether the hour is still worth it, and believe them

sections.heading: Getting started: the first home tuition session for a capable student
paragraphs: Send three things. A piece of work the student is proud of rather than a report card, because the strongest work shows the ceiling better than an average does. A sentence from the student, in their own words, about what is missing from the subject at school. And the one or two subjects this is actually about, since looking for one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is the wrong shape for this request. If the student will write that sentence themselves, the match is usually right within one try.

The first session should not be an assessment and should not be a revision hour. The tutor sets something hard in a topic the student claims is comfortable, lets them struggle with it properly, and spends the rest of the hour on why the hard version is hard. By the end, a parent should have heard the tutor say something about the subject that they themselves did not know, and the student should want to finish the question. If neither of those happened, this is not the right tutor, and there is no harm in saying so after one session.

Then set the terms the same way you would for any arrangement: the slot, the notice on both sides, how feedback reaches you, and the firm line that the tutor does not write any part of an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or coursework no matter how capable the student is. Book a review for the end of the term, and go into it genuinely willing to conclude that the hour has done its job and the student should spend next term on something of their own choosing.
bullets: Send the student's best work, not their report card
Ask the student to write one sentence on what is missing at school
Expect one or two subjects, not a timetable covering everything
Judge session one on whether the student wanted to finish the question
Book a term end review and be willing to end it there

faqs.question: My child gets high marks but says class is boring. Is a tutor the answer?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and often not. Start by separating boredom from quiet struggling, because they look the same and need opposite responses. If it is genuine boredom, the next question is whether the student needs an adult or needs room. A self motivated fifteen year old with a competition, a project or a reading list frequently gets more from those than from another scheduled hour led by someone else. A tutor earns the slot when the subject is not offered at school, when an Extended Essay or Internal Assessment needs early mentoring, or when the student wants to go deeper and has nobody to argue with about it.

faqs.question: Should we start Diploma content while our son is still in Year 10?
faqs.answer: Generally no, and it is the most common mistake made with strong students. Meeting Diploma material without the maturity to hold it builds a shallow memory that has faded by the time the class gets there, and it creates a student who believes they already know the topic and therefore stops listening in the lesson where their teacher explains the expected working and conventions. Nothing in either system rewards having covered content early. If Year 10 is genuinely too easy, add difficulty inside the current topics, take a subject separately rather than combined, or enter an additional subject. Depth earns something. Speed does not.

faqs.question: How do I tell boredom from quiet struggling when they look the same?
faqs.answer: Set one hard question in a topic your child says is easy and watch the first two minutes. A bored student leans in and starts trying things; a struggling student goes quiet, deflects, or asks whether it will be in the exam. Then ask them to teach you the topic: boredom explains fluently and adds detail nobody asked for, difficulty recites a definition and stops. Finally look at the lost marks. Boredom loses careless arithmetic and abandons long structured questions halfway. Difficulty fails at the same conceptual step across four different questions. Those three checks take an evening and will usually settle it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor take a subject further than our school offers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the clearest cases for hiring one. If the school does not run Further Mathematics, a particular language, Music or Computer Science at the level your child wants, a tutor can teach it properly and, where it makes sense, prepare the student for an external entry that the school can advise you about. Be realistic about the workload before committing, because an additional subject taken outside the timetable sits on top of a full programme. Agree a review point after one term, and treat it as a genuine decision point rather than a formality.

faqs.question: Is it too early to start the Extended Essay in the first year of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: No, and for a capable student it is the single most valuable early work there is. The point is not to start writing but to choose well, which is where most Extended Essays are won or lost. A tutor can help test whether a research question is narrow enough, whether the sources genuinely exist and are accessible, and whether the subject fits the student's actual strengths. That work is conversation and reading, not drafting. The tutor must not write any part of the essay, supply sentences, or work inside the document, and your school's own supervisor remains the person who guides and signs off the process.

faqs.question: Will enrichment work help with university applications?
faqs.answer: It can, but not in the way families often assume, and nobody can promise an outcome. Admissions interest tends to sit with what a student has done and can discuss, rather than with the fact of having had a tutor. A student who read widely in a subject, built something, entered a competition or wrote a serious Extended Essay has material for an application and for an interview. An extra weekly hour that produced nothing visible does not. If applications are the motivation, bias the plan towards work with an output the student can point at and talk about unprompted.

faqs.question: Is an enrichment tutor priced differently from an exam tutor?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because the scarcity is different. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length, and the ability to teach above the specification is itself scarce, particularly in Further Mathematics, Computer Science at Higher Level, a less common language or any subject needing a researcher rather than a teacher. Travel still prices in for home sessions. We do not publish a price list because an honest one does not exist, but we will tell you plainly which factor is driving a particular quote so you can decide whether online widens the pool enough to change it.

faqs.question: Our daughter is in Juhu and wants Latin, which her school does not teach. Can an online tutor do it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online is almost certainly the right route for a subject that scarce. There is no reliable pool of Latin teachers within travelling distance of Juhu, Versova or Vile Parle for a weekday evening slot, and insisting on someone local usually means accepting someone who will be a chapter ahead of the student. Online removes the geography entirely and lets you choose on subject depth alone. Keep the sessions shorter and more frequent than you would for examination work, and ask the school what external entry route, if any, they would support before the second term.

faqs.question: Does a home tuition session for an older student still need a parent at home in Bandra West?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, even for a seventeen year old, and most Bandra West and Khar West societies will separately want a resident to approve a visitor at the gate. Arrange standing entry so the home tutor is not negotiating with security each week. Beyond the safeguarding point, there is a practical reason to be nearby for enrichment specifically: overhearing ten minutes of a depth session tells you more about whether it is working than any monthly report will. Use the dining table rather than a bedroom and leave the door open, as you would at any age.

faqs.question: We are in Thane. Is a weekly home tuition slot worth it when there is no exam pressure?
faqs.answer: A fortnightly slot is usually the better commitment. Depth work needs time between sessions for the student to read, get stuck and come back with something, and a weekly home tuition visit across Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali or Hiranandani Estate is a heavy logistical load for an arrangement with no deadline forcing it. A fortnightly home session with short online contact in between holds far better through the year. Protect the slot by putting it on a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening, because Ghodbunder Road at seven will eventually end any arrangement that depends on it.

faqs.question: What if my child resists the extra sessions?
faqs.answer: Take the resistance seriously rather than negotiating around it. A capable student who does not want an extra hour is often right, and forcing it reliably turns a subject they liked into one they associate with being managed. Ask what they would rather do with the time and listen to the answer, because a project, a competition or simply unstructured reading may genuinely be the better use. If they do want depth but not this tutor, that is a different problem with an easy fix. If they want neither, stopping is a legitimate outcome and not a failure on anyone's part.

faqs.question: Do you have IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai who teach above the syllabus?
faqs.answer: In most subjects yes, though the pool is thinner than for examination coaching and varies sharply by area. Science, mathematics and computing specialists are easiest to find around Powai, Chandivali and the Central Suburbs, while the island city has more researchers and writers suited to humanities depth work. For a genuinely rare subject we will usually recommend online rather than pretend there is someone twenty minutes away. Tell us the subject and the level of stretch you want and we will say honestly whether a nearby match exists or whether widening to online gets you a better person.

You will get a short shortlist of tutors who can teach above the specification, with their open slots. If we think an activity or a reading list would serve your child better than a weekly hour, we will say so before you book anything.

ib-igcse-coaching.heroIntro: Parents looking for IB IGCSE coaching in Mumbai rarely plan for the day the tutor and the school contradict each other, yet it happens in most arrangements. This page is about that: whose view wins on assessed work, how to raise a real concern with a subject teacher, and how to keep a student in home tuition from being caught between two adults.
