sections.heading: Progress across a term of home classes in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks, look for three things and ignore grades. A problem statement from the tutor sharper than the one you supplied. Written work from week four visibly better than week one on the same kind of question. And a student who can describe what they are working on without prompting. In a two-board household, check these per child rather than as an impression of the household, because one match can be working while the other is not and the family mood averages them into a single vague feeling.

Across a term, expect movement and expect it uneven. Students starting from a failing position move fastest, because early gains come from plugging basic gaps. Students moving from a middling grade to a strong one move slowly, because that distance is precision and timing built over months. Internal assessments and coursework sit on their own draft cycles and may not move with the papers. Ask each tutor monthly which track the month's work was on, and expect a specific answer.

Across a full examination cycle, the result stands on its own. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and publishes no success rate, because a percentage drawn across two boards, multiple levels and different starting points would describe nothing real. Tutoring improves preparation, understanding and technique. It does not control the paper, the examiner, a student's health in the hall, or the hours when nobody is watching. A tutor who promises a specific grade is telling you what they do not understand about external examining.

What we commit to is the review and the replacement, per match. At two to four weeks we ask you directly about each tutor, and if one is not working we replace that one with no notice period and no penalty while the other continues. Most replacements are nobody's fault: a student who needed someone firmer, a schedule overtaken by a sport season, two people who did not click. In two-board households there is one extra cause, which is a tutor who turned out to know the other board better, and we treat that as our error rather than yours.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Bandra East
paragraphs: Gather four things before the first call. The exact subject names and codes for each child as the school writes them, which settles board and level without discussion. The most recent marked script for each, because the pattern of lost marks is the diagnosis. Two or three evening windows that genuinely work for the household as a whole, not per child. And a note on which weeks collapse: sport seasons, examination fortnights, travel.

Session one with each tutor should be a diagnosis rather than a lesson. They set a question cold, watch the attempt without helping, then read the attempt instead of correcting it. They ask what the student thought the question wanted. For a Diploma student they look at whatever internal assessment is in play. By the end they state the real problem in one sentence, and that sentence should be more precise than yours. If it only repeats your description, no diagnosis has happened and you are entitled to say so.

Expect the first fortnight to look slower than you hoped, on both boards. If the current topic rests on something that never landed two years ago, a competent tutor repairs that first, and this Friday's test will not improve. Cramming for the immediate assessment produces one good Friday and an unchanged term. Ask after session one what sessions two to four will cover, in what order, and whether the target is the next test or the examination series.

Then the household mechanics, which matter more with two tutors than one. Register both at the gate as expected weekly visitors on fixed days so nobody loses ten minutes at the intercom. Keep the two lessons in different rooms or different hours, never the same table. Phones out by prior agreement rather than weekly argument. A parent somewhere in the flat. And a written cancellation rule for both sides and both tutors. All IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Bandra East run better when these are settled in week one and never reopened.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both my children if they are on different boards?
faqs.answer: Usually they should not, even when they can. A Year 10 student on Extended-tier mathematics and a Diploma student working on a mathematical exploration need different preparation, and a tutor covering both will be genuinely strong at one of them. What you can consolidate is everything else: one brief, one shortlist conversation, and two tutors scheduled into adjacent hours on the same evening so your household has one disruption rather than two. That is what most parents actually want when they ask for a single tutor, and it is easier to arrange than finding one person who covers both well.

faqs.question: We do not know which board our child is on. How do we find out?
faqs.answer: Look for the subject code printed beside the subject name on the report card, or ask the class teacher in one line. Many schools in Mumbai teach a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel course through the middle years and then an International Baccalaureate Diploma for the last two, so a child changes awarding body without changing anything visible. If you cannot find a code, send us a photograph of the report page and we will identify it. It matters because a tutor drilling the wrong board's past papers is doing careful work against the wrong target.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Bandra East depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and no honest platform quotes one rate for both boards. Level comes first: a Higher Level Diploma specialist is priced differently from general middle-years support. Subject scarcity is the biggest single driver, since a thin local pool prices upward regardless of board. Travel distance matters because you pay for the journey as well as the lesson. Session length and frequency change the per-hour figure. And the mode matters, as online hours carry no travel. For a two-child household, ask about the combined weekly cost rather than per-hour rates, because that is the number you will actually live with.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Bandra East for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the easier corridors in Mumbai for it. A tutor based in Bandra East, BKC or Bandra West can hold a six o'clock start realistically rather than optimistically. Tutors coming from Kurla are more dependable at eight in the morning or eight at night, because junction traffic in between is unpredictable. Families whose children attend BKC schools and who live on this side of Bandra station also have access to a half past four slot, which is the best hour of the day for concentration and the first one to be taken. Give us your real windows at intake.

faqs.question: My child is going from Year 11 into the Diploma next year. When should we start?
faqs.answer: The useful window is the months around the transition rather than after it has gone wrong. Six to eight weeks before the Diploma begins, a tutor can work on the two habits that will break first: writing to a criterion rather than to a correct answer, and managing a draft cycle without being chased. That is cheap, specific work. Starting in October of DP1, after the first set of internal deadlines has collided, costs more and recovers less. If you are reading this in the Year 11 spring, this is the right moment rather than an early one.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work equally well for both boards?
faqs.answer: Not equally, no. For a Diploma student working on an internal assessment draft, online is close to as good as in person, because the work is a document two people can look at together. For a middle-years student the gap is wider, because the tutor needs to watch the method appear on paper and catch the moment attention goes. Both boards benefit from online in the same three cases: a scarce subject, the final examination run-in, and monsoon weeks. Our standing recommendation for this corridor is in person first, with online added where it does something specific.

faqs.question: Should a parent be at home while two tutors are in the flat?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the two-tutor case makes it more important rather than less. Somewhere in the flat, not in either room. You are there to let people in, to keep the two lessons from bleeding into each other, and to have a two-minute conversation with each tutor at the end, which is worth more than any written report. The practical rule is that two lessons need two rooms or two hours and never one table, because two students at one table teach each other nothing and distract each other reliably.

faqs.question: How do we manage society gate access for two weekly tutors?
faqs.answer: Register both names once, at the start, as expected weekly visitors on fixed days. Most buildings in this corridor want a visitor entry or resident confirmation per arrival, which means a tutor at the gate calling your flat while a paid hour runs. With two tutors that happens twice a week, every week, for a year or more. Give your security desk both names and both standing days, and ask whether your building issues standing visitor passes. It is one conversation and it buys back a meaningful amount of teaching time across a two-year run.

faqs.question: What if one tutor is working and the other is not?
faqs.answer: Replace the one that is not, and leave the other alone. We review each match separately at two to four weeks precisely so this decision does not get made for the household as a whole. There is no notice period, no penalty and no need to justify it beyond one sentence about what did not work, which makes the next shortlist better. In two-board households the extra cause we see is a tutor who turned out to know the other board more thoroughly, and when that happens we treat it as our matching error rather than something you should have caught.

faqs.question: Is it worth hiring a tutor who has taught both boards, or two specialists?
faqs.answer: Two specialists, with one exception. The exception is a single student crossing from the middle years into the Diploma, where a tutor who has taught both can tell them which current habits carry forward and which will stop working, and that is genuinely valuable for a year. Outside that case, depth in one syllabus beats breadth across two, and a profile claiming equal strength on both boards deserves a direct question: which did you teach most recently, and how do the two differ on one specific topic? The answer takes thirty seconds and settles it.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does each child need?
faqs.answer: One per subject per week to start, for either board, and resist beginning with more. School fills the day and homework fills the rest, so a third stream of work produces students who are busy rather than better. One well-prepared session with work completed in between beats three rushed hours. Step up to two in the run-up to mocks, final papers or a specific internal assessment deadline. In a two-child household the weekly total matters more than the per-child number, because it is competing for the same evenings and the same parent.

faqs.question: Which months are the hardest in a two-board household in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Winter and then February. Mock examinations for a middle-years student land in roughly the same stretch as Diploma internal assessment drafts and DP2 mocks, so one evening is being asked to serve two crises. February and March then bring final submissions for one child and revision for the other. The practical conclusion is that useful tutoring starts in June or August, when the corridor is quiet and you can choose the hour rather than accept what is left. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families want in January was available in August, and the home classes that start then are the ones that hold.

sections.heading: Setting up IB and IGCSE home tuition in Bandra West, step by step
paragraphs: An ongoing arrangement in Mumbai starts differently from a one-off. We ask for three things before anyone is introduced: the subjects and their boards, the two or three evening windows that genuinely repeat every week, and what you want measurably different by the end of this term. The third is the question most families skip, and it is the one that decides whether the sessions have a shape at all. A Year 10 student who keeps losing method marks in Mathematics and a Year 11 student who cannot finish a paper inside the time are two different briefs, and the same tutor would run them in completely different ways.

Then comes the trial fortnight. The first two sessions are diagnostic and reviewable, and we treat them as exactly that rather than as the opening of a commitment. After them you get the tutor's written read on where the marks are going, and we ask you separately whether the room worked. Only then does the slot become standing. Families who book an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Bandra West for a full term without that fortnight are the ones who discover in week six that the subject needed a different kind of teacher, by which point half the term has gone.

Once the slot is standing, the arrangement runs on three habits. The tutor keeps a running topic list, so anyone covering for them knows precisely where the student is. You get a short note after each session rather than a monthly summary. And there is a review point written into the calendar, usually around week four and again after the next school assessment, where the brief is either confirmed or changed. None of that is unusual anywhere in Mumbai, but it is the whole difference between a tutor teaching a plan and a tutor filling ninety minutes.

sections.heading: Two boards in one Bandra West household
paragraphs: Plenty of Bandra West households run both boards at once, because children often sit in different schools or different year groups. The International Baccalaureate (IB) side may be the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) or the Diploma Programme (DP); the Cambridge International Education side is the IGCSE years with their Core and Extended tiers. A tutor moving between the two inside one week has to switch assessment logic, not merely content. IB work is judged against published criteria and carries internal coursework that is drafted, fed back on and redrafted. IGCSE work ends in terminal papers with some school-marked components attached.

That difference shows up in what a weekly session should contain. A Diploma Programme student in DP1 spends part of the year producing coursework: an Internal Assessment (IA), an Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) work, each with school-set interim deadlines. A tutor there is partly a supervisor of drafts. An IGCSE student in Year 11 is mostly working past papers against the clock, and the tutor is partly a marker. Ask any prospective tutor which of those two jobs they have done most recently, because being fluent in one does not make somebody fluent in the other.

Levels matter for scheduling as much as for difficulty. Higher Level (HL) subjects and Extended-tier subjects need the longer session and the earlier start in the year; Standard Level (SL) and Core subjects can often be held at a lower frequency and raised closer to the exam series. Read the current subject guide or ask your school's Diploma Programme coordinator for the structure that applies to your child's cohort, because the boards revise their guides on their own cycle and last year's component list is not reliable. We will not quote a weighting at you from a page like this one.

sections.heading: How many subjects can one home tutor realistically carry?
paragraphs: Two, usually, and three only when they are genuinely adjacent. One tutor can hold Mathematics and Physics, or Economics and Business Studies, because the question styles and the marking habits overlap. Asking the same person to run Chemistry, English Literature and a second language means none of the three gets a specialist. Families booking all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Bandra West often start by asking for one tutor for everything, and the honest answer is that it costs the child more than it saves the calendar.

Subject choice across the two boards is where a tutor earns their keep before teaching anything. At IGCSE the choice is about breadth and tier: which subjects your child carries at Extended, and which are better taken at Core so the timetable survives the year. At IB the choice narrows later into Higher Level and Standard Level, and the mathematics route decision follows the degree direction rather than the current mark. A tutor who has taken students through both conversations can tell you what the coursework load looks like for each combination before you commit to it.

Each subject also brings its own internal work, and that is what fills a term. Science subjects bring practical or alternative-to-practical preparation. Languages bring speaking components recorded at school. IB subjects bring the Internal Assessment with its own draft deadlines. The coverage label for this page is plain enough: all IB and IGCSE subjects IGCSE Years 9-11 tutors in Mumbai, plus the Diploma Programme years above them. What we will not do is load three subjects onto one tutor to make a single invoice tidier. If you need three, the better arrangement is two tutors sharing the same week, with one of them holding the handover note.

sections.heading: Which Bandra West addresses a weekly home tuition slot actually survives
paragraphs: A weekly slot survives when the tutor's own commute is short enough to be boring. From inside Bandra West, or from Khar West, Bandstand, Pali Hill and Bandra East, a 6pm start is routine for thirty weeks running. From Andheri or Malad it holds in October and fails by February. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Bandra West is bought by the term, so the real question is never whether somebody can reach you once. It is whether they can reach you thirty times without resenting it.

The geography here is unusually kind. Bandra West sits at the southern end of the Western Line with Bandra station on it, Hill Road and Link Road running through it and the Western Express Highway along its eastern edge, so a tutor can arrive by train, by auto or by car and stay relaxed about which. Matching along the line rather than across it is the rule that keeps slots alive: Khar to Santacruz is a short hop and Bandra to Andheri at 6pm is not. Pali Hill and Bandstand sit slightly off the main roads, which helps in the evening and costs a few minutes of walking at the end.

The weeks that break a slot in Mumbai are predictable, so plan for them at setup. The monsoon turns a twelve-minute drive into forty. Festival weeks empty the evenings and then refill them. School examination weeks move the child's own bedtime. A tutor living inside Bandra West can shift a session by a day in any of those weeks; a tutor coming from Borivali cannot, and will simply cancel. When you set up a term, ask where the tutor actually lives rather than which areas they list, and ask what they do in a week when your road is flooded. Families in Khar West and Bandstand tend to end up with tutors from the same stretch for exactly that reason.

sections.heading: When do Mumbai school deadlines collide for IB and IGCSE siblings?
paragraphs: Most often in late November, and again in the fortnight after the mid-year break, because that is when IB coursework drafts and IGCSE mock series tend to land near each other. In Bandra West that collision happens inside single households. A family on Hill Road is minutes from BKC and minutes from Juhu, so one child may be at Dhirubhai Ambani International School, a brother or sister at Jamnabai Narsee International School and a cousin at Ecole Mondiale World School, with Billabong High International School adding a fourth calendar from Santacruz.

A tutor working in Mumbai, Maharashtra across these schools is asked about all three calendars inside a single week, and the dates do not line up. One school sets its coursework interim deadline before the winter break; another sets it after. One runs mocks in a single block; another spreads them across a month. If you are running two children on two boards, write both calendars onto one sheet and give it to each tutor at the start of the term. It is the cheapest thing you can do for the arrangement, and it stops two tutors competing for the same Sunday afternoon.

Those schools are named here as local context and nothing else. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee International School, Billabong High International School, Ecole Mondiale World School or any other school on this page, and no tutor on the platform speaks on a school's behalf. We cannot guarantee grades and will not pretend otherwise. A tutor controls the preparation, the diagnosis and the honesty of the feedback. The school runs the internal deadlines and the boards mark the papers, and a good arrangement mostly stops those three things surprising each other.

sections.heading: Home, online or both across a Mumbai term
paragraphs: Across a thirty-week arrangement the sensible default is home tutoring with an online fallback already agreed. The home session is where diagnosis happens, because a tutor in the room sees the working, the calculator habit and the moment attention goes. Agree at the start of the term what happens when the tutor is in another city, when your child is recovering from something, or when the road is closed: that week moves online rather than disappearing. An IB and IGCSE home tutoring arrangement in Bandra West with no online fallback loses four or five sessions a term to events nobody could have prevented.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Bandra West is also the right answer for a narrow set of needs inside an ongoing arrangement: a Higher Level subject with no local specialist, a fortnightly top-up between home sessions, and quick marking turnaround on drafts. Online marking of an Internal Assessment draft works genuinely well, because the document is shared anyway. Online teaching of a brand-new topic to a Year 9 student works much less well. Decide which of those two you are buying before agreeing a mixed week, and keep the home session as the one where new material is introduced.

Continuity is the part of mode choice that families underrate. One tutor across a Mumbai term beats two excellent tutors across two halves of it, because the second spends a fortnight rediscovering what the first already knew. When a tutor genuinely has to hand over, the handover should be a document: topics covered, topics still weak, the current paper timing, and the next three things planned. Ask for that in writing when you set the arrangement up rather than in the week it is needed, and a cover week costs you one session instead of three.

sections.heading: What IB Gram checks, and what you should check every month
paragraphs: Our side is documentary and it happens before any introduction: degree certificate and transcript in the subject, government photo identification, a board-specific teaching record from Mumbai or elsewhere, and references we call rather than read. For an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Bandra West we also verify the areas they genuinely travel to, because an overstated coverage list is the commonest cause of a dropped slot in month three. None of that tells you whether the teaching is any good, which is why the monthly checks belong to you.

Four things to look at every month, and together they take ten minutes. Read the session notes end to end and see whether the topic list is moving or circling. Compare the tutor's view of the weak areas with what the school report says, and ask about any gap between the two. Look at one piece of marked work and check that the feedback is about method rather than neatness. Then ask your child one question: what did you get wrong last week, and why. A student who cannot answer that is being taught at rather than with.

There is a conversation worth having at the end of the first month, and most families avoid it. Ask the tutor directly what is not working, and give them permission to say that your child is not doing the between-session work. A tutor who reports only progress is managing you. We ask the same question from our side, and when the tutor's account and the parent's account diverge we fix the brief rather than wait for the next report. Be wary of anybody who answers a question about weaknesses with a promise about the final result.

sections.heading: How many hours a week actually move a grade in Bandra West?
paragraphs: For one subject, two to three contact hours a week, split across two days rather than stacked into one, with roughly the same amount of independent work in between. That ratio matters far more than the total. A single long session with nothing done between visits produces a student who understands in the room and has forgotten by Thursday. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Bandra West is usually bought as ninety minutes twice a week, and the second session exists mainly to check that the first one stuck.

Term-long and exam-term arrangements are different products and should be priced and planned differently. A term-long arrangement can afford to rebuild: six weeks on topics that were never properly learnt, then paper technique layered on top. An exam-term arrangement cannot, and anybody promising a rebuild in eight weeks is selling you the first half and hoping. In exam term the hours go up and the scope comes down: fewer topics, more timed papers, a weekly triage list. Families in Mumbai who start in January and ask for full coverage get thin coverage of everything, which is worse than deep coverage of the five topics carrying the most marks.

Diminishing returns arrive earlier than parents expect. Past three contact hours a week in one subject, the limiting factor stops being teaching and becomes the student's own practice time and sleep. Two subjects at three hours each already fills most of a Bandra West school week once travel, school homework and one activity are counted in. The parents who get the most from the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Bandra West are usually the ones who cut an evening rather than add one, and who protect one genuinely free day. A tutor who agrees to a fifth weekday evening without asking what else is in the week is not thinking about the child.

sections.heading: What the rate covers, and what it does not
paragraphs: Ask this before the first session, not in month two. A session rate normally covers the teaching time, the travel, and the tutor's own preparation for that session. What it often does not cover, and what you should ask about explicitly, is marking done outside the session, setting and marking a full mock paper, writing a monthly report, attending a school meeting, and sessions you cancel at short notice. None of those are unreasonable things to pay for. All of them are unreasonable things to discover in week nine.

IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Bandra West depend on a short and predictable list: the board and the level, the year group, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels, how long each session runs, and whether you are booking one subject or several with the same person. A Diploma Programme Higher Level subject in exam term sits at one end of that list and a Year 9 support slot at the other. We will not print a figure here, because a number without those six factors attached is marketing rather than information, and an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Bandra West quoting a rate before asking about the subject has not understood the job.

Progress has a shape, and it is worth agreeing in advance what you will accept as evidence of it. At four weeks: a retested weak topic and method-level feedback. At one term: a school assessment that moves, or a clear written reason why it has not. Across an exam cycle: timing under control and a shorter list of genuine gaps. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anybody who does is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child. faqs.question: What happens to the home tuition slot when a tutor travels or falls ill?
faqs.answer: That is what the cover plan is for, and it should be agreed at setup rather than improvised. For a single missed week most families move the session online, because the tutor already knows the student and the topic list. For a longer absence we arrange named cover and pass on the written handover: topics covered, topics still weak, current paper timing and the next three things planned. faqs.question: How does progress reach me between sessions?
faqs.answer: Through a short written note after each session rather than a conversation at the door. It should say what was covered, what the student got wrong, what was set for the week and what the tutor plans next. Four of those notes read together tell you more than any monthly report, because you can see whether the topic list is advancing or going in circles. If the notes are only ever positive, ask directly what is not working. A tutor who cannot name a current weakness is not diagnosing anything.

faqs.question: Do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Bandra West differ between the two boards?
faqs.answer: Often, but the board itself is only one of six factors. faqs.question: Can we pause home classes during school holidays or exam weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better to plan the pauses than to cancel week by week. Most families pause for the main school breaks and keep a reduced schedule through the school's own examination weeks, when the child needs revision time more than new teaching. Tell the tutor the pause dates at the start of the term so the slot is held rather than given away. What does not work is pausing for six weeks and expecting the same evening to be free afterwards, because a good local tutor will have filled it.

faqs.question: How many evenings a week is too many?
faqs.answer: Four weekday evenings of tuition is usually the point where returns stop. By then the student has no time left to do the work each tutor sets, and sessions become a place where someone else thinks for them. Two subjects at two sessions each is already a full week once school homework, travel and one activity are counted. If three subjects genuinely need help, the better answer is to sequence them across the year rather than stack them into one week, and to protect one evening with nothing scheduled at all.

faqs.question: Will one tutor cover both my children, one in IB and one in IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single visit covering two children saves travel and keeps the slot stable. It works when the subject is the same and the levels are near enough, such as an IGCSE Year 10 student and a Diploma Programme Standard Level student in Mathematics. It works badly when the two children need the same hour, or when one needs coursework supervision and the other needs timed papers. Two back-to-back sessions in one visit is usually the practical answer rather than one shared session.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Bandstand or Khar West for an early evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the early evening is the easiest part of the day to fill in this part of Mumbai, because a tutor can take two sessions in one trip across Bandra West. A 4.30pm or 5pm start works well for younger students coming straight from school. The slots that strain are 6pm starts needing a crossing of the Western Express Highway, and anything that depends on a tutor leaving Andheri at peak. Give two windows rather than one and the term-long slot usually holds.

faqs.question: Is a ninety-minute session better than two shorter ones?
faqs.answer: For most students two shorter sessions beat one long one, because the second session tests whether the first was retained. Ninety minutes once a week suits a Diploma Programme student working on a long coursework piece, where the time is spent drafting and discussing. Two sessions of an hour suit a Year 10 or Year 11 student who needs practice checked twice in a week. The thing to avoid is three hours in a single sitting, which produces notes nobody reads and a student who is finished after forty minutes.

faqs.question: What does the tutor expect my child to do between visits?
faqs.answer: Roughly as much time again as the session itself, and specific work rather than general revision. A good tutor leaves two or three named tasks: a set of past paper questions, one topic reread with the notes closed, a corrected version of something that was marked. The point is that the next session starts with evidence instead of a conversation about what was forgotten. If nothing is being set, or nothing is being checked, the sessions will plateau by week five whatever the tutor's qualifications say.

Most Bandra West buildings will do this when a resident asks, and it removes the ten-minute wait that otherwise eats the start of every session. Give the tutor the wing and floor rather than just the building name, tell them which lift reaches your floor after seven, and say where a car can wait if parking on Hill Road is full. sections.heading: How IB and IGCSE home tuition in Bandstand gets organised for one household

The sequence we use for a two-board household: 1. You send both children's details together, with year group, board and subject for each, rather than as two separate enquiries. 2. Sending both children in one message is not administrative tidiness. It changes the shortlist. sections.heading: What changes when a student moves from IGCSE to the IB Diploma?
paragraphs: Almost everything about how work is produced, and that is the shock. An International General Certificate of Secondary Education course rewards mastery of a defined body of content, assessed in papers that reward precision and recall alongside application. The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) asks for six subjects at once, splits them into Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), adds an Internal Assessment (IA) in each, and then layers on the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK). A student who was comfortable revising for discrete examinations now has to run several long pieces of independent work in parallel while still learning content.

The failure mode is predictable and it is not academic weakness. It is project management. A Year 11 student who was good at preparing for a paper in two intense weeks finds that an IA cannot be done that way, because the thinking has to happen in stages across a term. The students who struggle most in DP1 are often not the weakest ones; they are the ones whose previous success came from a late, concentrated effort that no longer works. A tutor's job across that bridge is as much about sequencing as about subject content.

There is a second change nobody warns families about. The IGCSE pathway has clear tier and route choices made at Year 9, and by Year 11 those are settled. The DP reopens the whole question: which three subjects at HL, which three at SL, whether to take Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, whether a language will be taken at a level that is actually sustainable. A strong IGCSE grade in a subject does not reliably predict comfort at HL in the same subject, because the demand changes rather than just increasing.

For hiring that means asking a different question in DP1 than in Year 10. In Year 10 you want a tutor who knows the paper. In DP1 you want somebody who knows the paper and has supervised the internal work, because that is where the marks quietly go. We arrange IB and IGCSE home tuition in Bandstand for both stages, and we will say plainly which stage your child is in, because the tutor profile that suits one is often wrong for the other. Do not take weightings, word counts or deadline dates from this page; read the current subject guide and ask the school's coordinator.

sections.heading: Why does a student choose subjects twice between Year 9 and DP1?
paragraphs: Because the two systems ask the question at different depths. At Year 9 the choice is about breadth and tier: which optional subjects to carry, whether the sciences are taken separately or as a combined award, and whether Mathematics is entered at Core or Extended tier. Those decisions set a ceiling and they are made with limited evidence, usually in one parents' evening conversation. At the end of Year 11 the question returns in harder form, because the DP requires a structured set across subject groups with three subjects taken at HL, and the combination has to be survivable for two years alongside the EE and TOK.

Families in Bandstand often make the second choice using the first as evidence, which is only partly sound. A student who did well in a combined science award has not demonstrated that HL Biology is comfortable, because the content base is narrower than the separate subject would have given. A student entered at Core tier in Mathematics has a genuine gap to close before Analysis and Approaches at any level, and pretending otherwise produces a miserable DP1. Conversely a student who found the Extended tier straightforward may be a strong candidate for HL even if their final grade was unspectacular.

This is the most useful thing a subject specialist contributes at this moment, and it costs you one or two sessions rather than a term. Ask a tutor who has taught the subject at HL to look at your child's recent work and say what the gap between here and HL actually consists of. They will usually name two or three specific capabilities rather than giving a verdict. All IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Bandstand are quoted as if coverage were the point; the real product at this decision moment is an honest reading of readiness.

Internal work exists on both sides of the bridge and differs in kind. Several IGCSE subjects carry coursework or a written practical alternative, which schools choose between where the syllabus allows, so check which route your child's school took. In the DP every subject carries an internal assessment with its own criteria, and the sciences additionally require an investigation the student designs. A tutor who has only taught content will teach content. A tutor who has marked the internal work knows where students lose credit, and that is a different and more valuable thing.

paragraphs: Yes, with one condition: the two lessons cannot share a room or an hour. Home tuition is the right default for both children, because written method in IGCSE and worked reasoning in the DP are both things a tutor needs to watch being produced rather than receive finished. In a flat with one dining table, that means staggering. Either two different evenings, or the same evening with a real gap, or one child at the table and the other in a bedroom with a door that closes. Families who try to run both lessons simultaneously in an open-plan living area usually abandon one of them inside a month. The home classes we arrange in Mumbai are planned around the room before they are planned around the syllabus.

The honest trade-off with two sets of home classes is cost and rigidity. Two tutors travelling to the Bandstand promenade each week is two journeys priced into two arrangements, and rescheduling either one is harder because it has to fit around a travel map rather than a diary. This is the main argument for choosing tutors whose routes overlap, and for asking at the discovery call whether a tutor could take two adjacent slots if the household ever needs it.

Online is the pressure valve in a two-board household, and it is worth designing in deliberately rather than falling back on it. Put the older child's revision or feedback sessions online during a crunch month and keep the in-person slot for the younger one, who gains more from presence. Use it for scarce subjects where the right specialist lives beyond the strip. Use it for the final weeks before an examination series, when short frequent contact beats one long block. The weaknesses stay real: practical description and joint diagram work are harder, and a younger child drifts on a screen.

Most two-board families we work with in the Western Suburbs end up with a mixed week by the second term, which is not a compromise so much as the sane answer. One child in person weekly, the other in person fortnightly with online in between, adjusted when a deadline month arrives. Ask each shortlisted IB and IGCSE private tutor in Bandstand how they would handle a week where the other sibling's deadline takes priority. A tutor who treats that as normal is the one you want.

sections.heading: The Year 11 to DP1 bridge that nobody times properly
paragraphs: The gap between the end of Year 11 and the start of DP1 is the most underused period in a Mumbai international school student's life. Examinations finish, results are awaited, and a family understandably treats the whole stretch as a holiday. Then DP1 opens in the new academic year with six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, and a student who has not opened a book for weeks is asked to work in a way nobody has taught them. The students who find DP1 manageable are very often the ones who did a modest amount of targeted work in that gap, not more of the same but something different in kind.

What that work looks like is specific and short. For a student heading into HL Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, a few weeks on algebraic fluency and on functions, because the DP assumes a facility that the IGCSE course did not need to make automatic. For a student taking an HL science, practice at writing a method and an evaluation in the clipped language the mark scheme rewards, which is a writing skill rather than a content one. For anybody taking a language at a demanding level, sustained reading for pleasure in that language, which sounds soft and does more than a grammar workbook.

The second half of the bridge is organisational and it is the half that actually fails. Students arriving in DP1 have never had to carry four pieces of long independent work at once. A tutor can model that in two or three sessions: how to break an internal assessment into stages, what a first week of a long piece should produce, how to keep a TOK idea in a notebook rather than inventing one the night before a deadline. It is unglamorous and it is the difference between a DP2 spring that is busy and one that is frightening.

On cost, IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Bandstand depend on the programme and level, how scarce the subject specialists are, the travel involved, the session length and frequency, and the tutor's background, and in a two-board household the total obviously reflects two arrangements rather than one. We do not publish rates, because any figure here would be wrong for somebody. A bridge package of a few focused weeks over the gap is usually the cheapest intervention a two-board family ever buys, and almost nobody asks for it until the following December.

By the end of a term the evidence sits on paper. Fewer repeats of the same error category in the IGCSE child's marked work. faqs.question: Can one tutor teach my IGCSE child and my IB Diploma child?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and we will tell you which of the two they are stronger at. Some tutors genuinely hold a subject across both boards, most often in Mathematics or Physics, and where that is real it saves a journey and simplifies your week. More often a tutor is sharp on one board and merely competent on the other, which shows up by November. We would rather place two specialists and coordinate their slots than consolidate and quietly downgrade one child's teaching.

faqs.question: How do we stop two lessons in the same evening disturbing each other at home?
faqs.answer: Separate them by room or by hour, and decide before the first lesson rather than improvising. In most Bandstand flats the practical answer is one lesson at the dining table and the other in a bedroom with the door closed, or a real gap between the two so the table is only ever hosting one. Trying to run both at once in an open-plan living area is the most common reason a two-board household abandons one of the arrangements inside a month.

faqs.question: Do both tutors need gate passes for our building?
faqs.answer: Yes, and arrange both at once with the society office. Bandstand towers have tight parking and a single entrance, and tutors here arrive on foot after taking the train to Bandra and a rickshaw, so a standing name on the visitor list matters more than a parking space. Give the office both names with the day and time for each. Some buildings issue longer-term passes for recurring visitors, which removes the security call at the start of every lesson.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Bandstand depend on?
faqs.answer: Programme and level, how scarce the subject specialists are, the travel involved, how long and how often sessions run, and the tutor's teaching background. A Higher Level science or mathematics tutor sits above most IGCSE subject support because that pool is smaller. In a two-board household you are funding two arrangements, which is worth planning for. We do not publish rates. Ask each tutor what is included outside the lesson, whether rates change during the examination run-up, and what the cancellation terms are.

faqs.question: When should a Year 11 student start preparing for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: In the gap between the end of Year 11 examinations and the start of DP1, which is the most wasted period in the whole course. A few focused weeks on algebraic fluency before Higher Level Mathematics, or on writing scientific method in mark scheme language, does more than a term of catch-up later. Add two or three sessions on how to stage long independent work, since carrying several internal assessments at once is the skill no IGCSE course ever had to teach.

faqs.question: Does a good IGCSE grade mean my child will cope at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, because the demand changes rather than simply increasing. A student who found the Extended tier straightforward is often a strong Higher Level candidate even with an unspectacular final grade, while a student who scored well through heavy revision on a narrower combined course may find the same subject at Higher Level genuinely hard. Ask a tutor who has taught the subject at that level to look at recent work and name the specific capabilities still missing.

faqs.question: Which areas around Bandstand do your tutors cover?
faqs.answer: The reliable cluster is Bandstand with Pali Hill, Bandra West and Khar West, which is where tutor routes overlap and where a two-tutor household is cheapest to run. For a scarce subject we look along the Western Line to Santacruz, Vile Parle, Juhu and Andheri. We do not pull tutors east from Powai or Chembur for a weekday evening, because those arrangements look workable in September and come apart in December when everybody's deadlines arrive together.

faqs.question: Is online tuition a reasonable option for the older child?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in a two-board household it is often the right structural choice. A Diploma Programme student doing past papers, problem sets or feedback on an internal assessment draft loses very little online, which frees the in-person evening for a younger IGCSE child who gains more from having somebody in the room. It also makes a scarce specialist available who could never travel to Bandstand weekly. Keep practical description and joint diagram work for the in-person sessions.

faqs.question: What if one tutor is working and the other is not?
faqs.answer: Tell us at the check-in and we replace the one that is not, which happens more often in a two-board household simply because there are two matches to get right. A tutor who is excellent with your older child can be wrong for your younger one, and that is nobody's failure. There is no penalty and no need to justify it. Common subjects usually have a replacement within days; a scarce board and subject combination can take a fortnight and we will say so.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: A subject tutor can help with the subject-specific thinking behind an Extended Essay, particularly with narrowing a research question into something answerable, and can help a student build the habit of collecting Theory of Knowledge examples as they go. What a tutor must not do is write, restructure or substantially draft either piece, because both are the student's own work and schools check. Ask any tutor directly where they draw that line, and be cautious of one who sounds relaxed about it.

faqs.question: Are you connected to the schools in Juhu and Bandra Kurla Complex?

We name them because many Bandstand families attend them and because their calendars set the pressure points in a two-board household. If any tutor claims a relationship with a school, or special knowledge of how it marks internal work, stop that conversation and tell us about it.

faqs.answer: For two widely taught subjects, usually within a week of the discovery calls, because we are fitting two slots rather than one and that takes an extra round of scheduling. For a scarce board and subject combination it can be a fortnight. The thing that speeds it up most is sending both children's details together with the specific hours available, since the hours are what we test journeys against and two children's hours have to be solved as one problem.

sections.heading: How one brief covers IB and IGCSE home tuition in Bhandup, Mumbai
paragraphs: Send one enquiry for the whole household rather than two. We ask which programme each child is in, which subjects and levels each one needs, and what the week genuinely looks like at home, including the evening the younger one has football and the evening nobody is back before eight. From that we work out whether this is one tutor with two slots, two tutors on different evenings, or one tutor for the shared subject and a specialist for the harder one. Most Bhandup households with two children end up on the second or third option. A parent who asks for one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai schools teach is almost always better served by two people with narrower claims.

The reason we ask rather than assume is that the two boards reward different teaching. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE courses end in external papers with published mark schemes, so preparation is heavily about reading the question and writing to the scheme. The International Baccalaureate (IB) programmes are assessed against criteria, with internally assessed work running alongside teaching for months. A tutor who is excellent at one of those is not automatically good at the other, and a parent who hires on the subject name alone finds that out in month three.

Where two different specialists are needed, we try to place them on different nights rather than stacking them, because two hours of tuition in one evening produces one good hour and one wasted one. Honest IB and IGCSE home tuition in Bhandup is as much a timetabling exercise as an academic one.

sections.heading: Why does the jump from IGCSE to the Diploma Programme catch families out?
paragraphs: Because the work stops being marked out of a hundred and starts being judged against criteria, and because a large part of the grade is produced over months rather than in a hall. An IGCSE student is rewarded for covering content and answering precisely under timed conditions. A Diploma Programme (DP) student has to sustain an Internal Assessment (IA) in each subject, an Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) alongside teaching, which demands planning and self-management that nobody taught them in Year 11.

The second shock is the level decision. The Diploma Programme requires choices between Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), and a strong IGCSE grade does not automatically mean a student can carry that subject at Higher Level. The honest test is whether the child can work independently on unfamiliar problems, not whether they scored well on a taught syllabus. A tutor who has taught both an IGCSE cohort and a Diploma cohort can usually tell you within a few sessions, and the families who ask that question in the Middle Years Programme have far better outcomes than the ones who ask in the second term of the Diploma.

For students on the other pathway, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) into Diploma transition has a different friction. MYP students are already used to criteria, so the marking style is familiar, but the content jump at Higher Level is steeper than the MYP grade suggests, especially in Mathematics and the sciences. Meanwhile a Primary Years Programme (PYP) child is learning something else entirely: how to explain thinking out loud, which is the skill every later programme assumes and nobody formally teaches.

Treat all structural detail with suspicion unless it comes from the right place. Component weightings, word limits, paper counts and deadlines are revised by the International Baccalaureate and by the examination boards on their own cycles, and a figure a tutor remembers from an older cohort may be wrong for your child. The current subject guide and your school's programme coordinator are the only binding sources. A tutor worth hiring sends you to them rather than reciting numbers.

sections.heading: Which subjects carry across both boards, and which really do not?
paragraphs: Mathematics and the three sciences carry across better than anything else, because the underlying content overlaps heavily even though the assessment differs. A tutor who teaches IGCSE Physics competently can usually teach Standard Level Physics after reading the current guide. Languages and the humanities carry across least well. An IGCSE English course and a Diploma literature course want different essays, and a History source exercise at IGCSE is not the same task as a Diploma History paper. A parent asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Bhandup might cover should expect an honest list of three or four, not twelve.

The internally assessed work is where the boards diverge most and where tutoring earns its money. Cambridge IGCSE coursework and practical components are produced to published criteria and moderated; so is the Diploma Internal Assessment, but over a longer run and with far more student autonomy. A tutor who has supervised both knows the common failure, which is identical in each case: a research question or a task focus so broad that no amount of good writing can score in the upper bands. Fixing that in week two is cheap. Fixing it a fortnight before submission is not, and catching it early is where IB and IGCSE home tuition in Bhandup earns its keep.

Mathematics deserves a separate note because the route decisions sit on both sides of the transition. At IGCSE the decision is tier, Core or Extended, with a grade ceiling attached. In the Diploma the decision is Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation, abstract and proof-led against modelling and statistics-led, and then Higher Level or Standard Level on top. Those two decisions are connected, because an Extended tier student who found the algebra hard is rarely comfortable in Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Good tutors say that out loud.

For the scarce subjects, a short block beats a weekly slot regardless of board. Second languages, Economics, Business Studies, Computer Science and Global Perspectives have thin specialist supply across the Central Suburbs. We arrange all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Bhandup parents request on that basis: a weekly tutor for the two subjects that need steady work, plus four to six concentrated sessions on the component or topic that needs a genuine specialist.

That collision is the practical problem. The year opens around June, and the first meaningful assessments arrive before the Diwali break for both pathways. For a two-child household that means asking early matters twice as much, because you are trying to secure two slots rather than one. sections.heading: Home tuition first, with online where it genuinely helps in Mumbai
paragraphs: A tutor in the room is the default for both boards, and more so for the younger child. Sitting at the table, a tutor sees the Middle Years Programme task sheet nobody has read, the IGCSE exercise book with uncorrected work from three weeks ago, and the laboratory notebook with a half-finished data table. For a student who is still learning to work without supervision, that physical presence is the main thing the money buys. The home classes we arrange in Mumbai lead with that and treat everything else as a supplement.

Online has specific, honest uses. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Bhandup is right when a subject is scarce enough that nobody in the cluster teaches it, when a Diploma student wants a weekly twenty-minute check on an Internal Assessment draft, when the family is travelling, and when the only free slot is too late for anyone to reach by road from Powai or Andheri East. It is wrong for a Year 9 or Middle Years student who cannot hold attention alone for fifty minutes, and pretending otherwise costs a month.

Hybrid is what most two-child households here settle into, and it solves the double-booking problem. The elder child takes a weekday visit for teaching and marked written work; the younger takes a shorter weekend call for homework checking and one walked-through question, or the reverse. That split keeps both children served without two tutors arriving on consecutive evenings, and it keeps a scarce specialist in play, because they will accept a short online review they would never accept as a standing visit across the city.

On formats, siblings are the obvious temptation and usually the wrong one. Two children in different programmes cannot share a session in any useful way, and even two children on the same board a year apart will produce one bored student and one who stops asking questions. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Bhandup parents engage for each child separately costs more per hour and less per unit of progress. Where a genuine pair exists, same board, same subject, same standing, we will arrange it and say why it works.

sections.heading: Can one tutor really be checked for both boards?
paragraphs: Yes, but the check has to be done twice and most platforms do it once. We verify identity against a government photograph document and confirm the qualification at source rather than from a CV, which is board-neutral. Then we test board familiarity separately: a Cambridge mark scheme exercise for IGCSE claims and a criteria-based marking exercise for International Baccalaureate claims. A candidate who passes one and not the other goes on our list for one board only, and the profile says so. Claiming both and demonstrating one is the most common thing we see. An IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai parents hire for two boards should be able to show evidence for each of them separately.

Your own checks are quick and more important than ours, because you are judging fit. Ask which board, which level and which year they last taught, and ask it per board if they claim both. Ask how they will diagnose your child in the first hour, and listen for whether the answer involves your child's own marked work. Ask what arrives at four weeks, and what they do if homework is undone twice. Whoever a parent concludes is the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Bhandup for their household is nearly always the one who answered those most concretely.

Certain answers should end the conversation. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because nobody controls what a student writes in an examination room or how a moderator reads an Internal Assessment. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and will not predict a result. Treat as warnings a refusal to write a short fortnightly review, discomfort about a parent sitting in occasionally, an inability to name the criteria for a component they supervise, and above all any offer to draft part of an Extended Essay or a piece of coursework, which is an academic honesty matter that can cost the whole qualification.

After the match the instrument is the written note, and with two children it should be two notes, not one combined paragraph. What was covered, what improved, what is still weak, per child. When the notes merge, repeat themselves or stop, the arrangement has gone flat. Parents who tell us in week three get a replacement shortlist from the same cluster inside a week. Parents who wait until February are choosing from whoever has a free evening left, which on this corridor is a much shorter list.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma transition year, handled properly
paragraphs: The useful work happens before the Diploma starts, not after. In the final IGCSE months, while everyone is focused on the papers, two decisions are being made that matter more: which subjects to carry forward, and at which level. A tutor who knows both ends of the transition can test the right thing, which is not whether the child can score on a taught IGCSE syllabus but whether they can make progress on an unfamiliar problem without being shown. That is the skill the Diploma assumes and the IGCSE never measures.

The first Diploma term is then about systems rather than content. Students who struggle are usually not weak at the subject; they are weak at running three Internal Assessments, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge alongside teaching with deadlines months away. Tuition in that term should include planning: which component gets attention this fortnight, what a research question has to do to be viable, how to produce a draft that a supervisor can actually give feedback on. A tutor who only runs past papers in Diploma year one has misread the job.

The reverse case matters for Bhandup households too, because some students move the other way or sit the two years in different schools. A child arriving into Year 10 or Year 11 of an IGCSE course from a criteria-marked background has to learn to write for a mark scheme, which is a narrower and more mechanical skill than they are used to and is learnable in weeks with the right practice. Diagnosing which direction a student is travelling in is the first thing a tutor should establish, and it changes everything about the first month.

What this costs follows the same logic as everything else. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Bhandup depend on the board and level, how scarce the specialist is, travel absorbed, session length and frequency, and whether a tutor is being asked to supervise an assessed component rather than teach a topic. Transition support is often cheaper than parents expect because it is a short block of planning sessions rather than a year of weekly teaching. Nobody can quote a figure before knowing those variables, and a single rate offered in a first message is invented.

sections.heading: What a term of IB and IGCSE home classes in Bhandup should change
paragraphs: At four weeks, per child, you should have a named problem and visible corrections. Not a grade, and not a cheerful report. The sentence should be as specific as this: the Middle Years Programme tasks are losing marks because he never reads the criteria before starting, or she can do every IGCSE calculation and loses marks on the explanation. With two children you should receive two such sentences. If either tutor cannot produce one, that match is wrong and week four is the right time to say so.

At one term the checkable signals appear. Scores on targeted past paper or criterion tasks rise. Written answers start using command terms as the mark scheme intends. An Internal Assessment exists as a draft with data in it rather than as an idea. Middle Years students begin reading the criteria grid before starting a task, which is the single habit that shifts their marks most. School reports lag all of this by weeks, so ask each tutor for their own marked evidence rather than waiting for a report card to confirm something you can already see. A term of IB and IGCSE home classes in Bhandup should leave you with a folder of that evidence, not a feeling.

Over a full cycle the honest claim is narrow. A supported student goes into their examinations or final submissions knowing the shape of the papers, having worked under timed conditions, with the weakest topics no longer blank and the internally assessed work in on time rather than in panic. We do not guarantee grades, publish success rates or predict results, and any tutor who does is selling rather than teaching. What we will do is tell you at four weeks whether the direction is right for each child.

Occasionally the right answer is less. A household running two children through four evenings of classes a week is buying exhaustion, and the younger one usually suffers first. A child whose real obstacle is sleep, screen habits or an unassessed reading difficulty needs something tuition cannot provide. A student with solid criterion marks who is merely unchallenged needs harder reading rather than supervision. We have told families in Bhandup, Kanjurmarg and Mulund West to cut one of the two slots, and they were better off for it.

sections.heading: Starting home tuition for either board in Bhandup, Mumbai

The most recent marked work with whatever comments the school provides, the board or programme plus the exact subject levels, and the evenings that genuinely exist at home. If you are unsure whether a course is Higher Level or Standard Level, or which board a particular IGCSE subject is entered with, the school office will confirm it in a message, and some schools do use different boards for different subjects.

The first lesson for each child should be diagnostic and fairly quiet. A tutor worth keeping spends the opening stretch reading your child's own work, sets two or three questions to confirm a hypothesis, then explains what they found and what the first month will target. You should end up holding a short written plan per child: topics in order, frequency, and the date you next hear. A first session that is all talk and reassurance is one to decline, and asking for the next profile is routine rather than rude.

Then set the practical frame, which matters more with two children. Fix each slot on a different evening if two tutors are involved. faqs.question: We have one child on IGCSE and one in MYP. Can the same home tutor take both?
faqs.answer: Sometimes in Mathematics or a science, rarely in anything else. The content overlaps enough that a competent Mathematics tutor can handle an IGCSE Year 10 student and a Middle Years Programme student in the same week, but the assessment styles differ sharply: one is writing to a published mark scheme and the other is working to criteria. In English, literature, History and the languages, the tasks are different enough that one tutor usually ends up strong with one child and adequate with the other. We would rather place two specialists on two evenings than stretch one person across both, and most IB and IGCSE home tuition in Bhandup works out that way.

Bhandup station sits between Kanjurmarg and Mulund on the Central Line, so a tutor who has already taught at Mulund West at five is in Bhandup by half past six and can comfortably cover two children in sequence. The caution is academic rather than logistical: two hours in one evening usually produces one good hour and one tired one. Where both children need real teaching rather than homework supervision, two separate evenings is the better arrangement even though it is less convenient.

faqs.question: Does a strong IGCSE grade mean my child can take that subject at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most common misreading of the transition. IGCSE rewards covering a taught syllabus and answering precisely under timed conditions. Higher Level in the Diploma Programme demands progress on unfamiliar problems with limited guidance, plus a sustained Internal Assessment produced over months. A student can score highly at IGCSE and still find Higher Level uncomfortable, especially in Mathematics and the sciences. The useful test is whether they can make headway on a problem they have not been shown. Ask a tutor who has taught both ends to assess exactly that before the choices are locked.

Diploma year one difficulties are usually not subject weakness; they are the result of running an Internal Assessment in each subject, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge alongside normal teaching with deadlines months out. Useful sessions in that term include choosing which component gets attention this fortnight, testing whether a research question can actually produce enough data, and producing a draft a supervisor can give real feedback on. A tutor who only runs past papers in the first Diploma term has misunderstood the job and will be busy in the wrong place.

sections.heading: One household, two boards, and what each actually demands
paragraphs: The Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel years ask for breadth and accuracy. A Year 10 student is carrying eight or nine subjects, sitting papers that reward precise, well-structured short answers, and learning to show working so method marks survive a wrong final figure. Cambridge IGCSE reports on an A* to G scale and Edexcel International GCSE on a 9 to 1 scale, and the tiering decisions in subjects like mathematics shape what is available at sixth form. The work is wide, the marking is mechanical in the best sense, and progress is visible quickly.

The International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme asks for depth and self-management instead. Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level (SL), each carrying an internal assessment marked against criteria rather than a mark scheme, plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) sitting outside all six. A DP2 student is managing long-horizon written work while revising for papers. Nothing about that resembles a Year 10 week, which is why a household running both needs two different kinds of help rather than one tutor at two volumes.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) sits between them for younger children and introduces criterion marking, which is where most parental confusion in this district begins. A report that says criterion C is developing means something precise and nothing obvious. Home classes for an MYP child in Mumbai therefore start with the report, not the textbook. If you have a child in MYP and another in Cambridge years, expect to be reading two completely different report formats in the same week, and expect a good tutor to translate the one you are asking about rather than both.

sections.heading: Shared subjects, different mark schemes across Mumbai's two main boards
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where households most often hope one tutor will do. It can work, with a caveat: the content overlaps far more than the assessment does. An Extended tier Mathematics (0580) paper and a Diploma mathematics exploration reward almost nothing in common. One wants clean, fast, accurate method under time pressure; the other wants a sustained piece of independent mathematical writing with reasoning made explicit. A tutor who has done both recently is worth finding. A tutor who assumes the second is just harder than the first is not.

The sciences split the same way. Physics (0625) and Chemistry (0620) at Cambridge level build the experimental vocabulary that a Diploma scientific investigation then assumes, so there is real continuity in the content. The assessment is a different animal: a Cambridge practical component and a Diploma internal investigation are marked on different things, and the second expects a level of independent design decisions that the first never asks for. If both your children need science help, ask each candidate which of the two they have supervised most recently.

English and languages are where a single tutor is most likely to be genuinely useful across both boards, because the underlying skills, structure, register, use of evidence, carry across. Even there the formats differ. Parents who ask us for all IB and IGCSE subjects tuition in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) usually need two specialists and one generalist who can sit with whoever is panicking that week, and that third role is often the most valuable of the three.

sections.heading: What changes when a child moves from IGCSE into the Diploma Programme?
paragraphs: Three things change at once, which is why the first DP1 term produces so many calls from this district. The quantity of independent written work rises sharply and nobody chases it weekly. The assessment stops rewarding well-drilled short answers and starts rewarding sustained reasoning against criteria. And subject choice narrows from eight or nine subjects to six, so a weakness that could previously be carried by strength elsewhere is now sitting in a Higher Level slot for two years. Students who coped comfortably in Year 11 can look suddenly fragile in DP1 for exactly these reasons and no others.

The useful intervention is early and structural rather than content-led. A tutor working with a new DP1 student should spend the first month on how work is produced: planning before writing, drafting against criteria instead of instinct, and reading the task rather than the topic. Content gaps matter too, but they are easier to fix and families overweight them. The parent who books a tutor in October of DP1 has a straightforward job. The one who waits until the first report in DP2 is paying for repair instead.

This is also where the household budget question gets decided, so it is worth being clear about what drives it. Higher Level and scarce subjects sit above Cambridge years work because fewer people teach them well. Two children in the same building share travel, which usually makes the second arrangement cheaper than the first. Always confirm whether marking between sessions is included, because that is where the real work happens.

sections.heading: Which board is your child in Borivali East actually being assessed on?
paragraphs: Check the report header, not the school's name. A family in Borivali East can have one child marked against Middle Years Programme criteria A to D and a second sitting Cambridge IGCSE papers two years later, in the same building and the same uniform. The International Baccalaureate (IB) and Cambridge International Education assess almost nothing the same way, and a tutor who confuses the two can waste a full term being perfectly competent.

The IB runs three programmes a Mumbai family is likely to meet. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) is inquiry-led and carries no external papers, so support there is about reading stamina, number sense and the habit of explaining thinking out loud. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) spans Years 1 to 5 and marks each subject against four published criteria instead of a running percentage. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year route with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) subjects, Internal Assessment (IA) coursework, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK). Cambridge IGCSE, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE where a school offers it, runs Years 9 to 11 with a Core and Extended tier split and terminal papers at the end.

The point that catches parents here is the handover between systems. A child marked on criteria for five years meets percentage-weighted IGCSE papers, or DP mark schemes written around command terms, and the grade drops. Very often nothing has been forgotten. The output has changed shape, and nobody taught the new shape. That is a short, specific job for a tutor and a bad reason to start a general tuition habit that runs for two years.

IB Gram is an independent platform. We are not affiliated with any school named on this page, we do not speak for the IB Organization, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, and we do not guarantee grades. What we can do is make sure the person sitting at your table in Borivali East knows which of these systems your child is actually in, and what the next assessed piece of work is.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the Core or Extended tier decision
paragraphs: Subject choice is the single highest-leverage decision in either board, and it is usually made in a rush. A DP student picking three Higher Level subjects is choosing the next two years of their evenings; a Year 9 student entered for the Core tier in a subject is choosing the ceiling of the grade they can be awarded in it. Both decisions get made in a week in Borivali East, often from a form sent home on a Friday.

On the IB side the questions are specific. Does the student want Mathematics taken at Higher Level because they need it for an engineering application, or because a friend is taking it? Is the second science at HL genuinely sustainable alongside an HL essay subject? Which of the three HL subjects carries the heaviest Internal Assessment, and when is that IA due relative to the Extended Essay? A tutor who has supervised IA drafts will answer those in one sitting. A tutor who has only taught content will guess.

On the Cambridge IGCSE side the equivalent decision is the tier. Extended entry opens the full grade range and brings harder papers; Core entry caps the award and is the right call for some students in some subjects, which is a sentence schools say less often than they should. The honest version is per subject, not per child. A student can sit Extended Mathematics and Core in a language without any contradiction.

Every subject in both boards carries some internally assessed component, and that is where marks quietly leak. The mathematical exploration, the scientific investigation, the language orals, the MYP personal project in Year 5: all of them are produced at home, under a deadline, with a parent in the room and nobody quite sure what the criteria reward. Home tuition is genuinely good at this, because the work and the student and the tutor are all in the same room. Refer to the current subject guide or your school coordinator for the structure and weighting that apply to your child's cohort, because the boards revise those on their own cycle.

The academic year here starts in late spring or early summer and the first real squeeze arrives in the second half of the first term, when Year 10 and Year 11 mock papers land next to the first MYP criterion-assessed tasks of the year. In a DP household the autumn is heavier still, because the Extended Essay and the first IA drafts fall within the same few weeks as the November mocks, and the student has to produce long written work while revising content they have not finished.

January and February are the months families underestimate. DP2 students are inside the final IA deadline window and the Theory of Knowledge essay at the same time, and Year 11 IGCSE candidates are weeks away from terminal papers. A tutor booked in January is doing triage. A tutor booked in August has time to fix the actual gap, which is usually two or three years old and has nothing to do with the current chapter.

This is why we ask for the school's assessment calendar on the first call rather than the student's timetable. The timetable tells you when lessons happen.
