sections.heading: What is verified before a tutor holds a weekly slot in Mumbai
paragraphs: Before anyone is introduced, IB Gram verifies identity against government photo identification, confirms the qualification claimed, and takes references from previous teaching or tuition work. We ask which boards and syllabus versions they have taught recently, which subjects they decline, and what else they are committed to on weekday evenings. For a term-long arrangement that last question is the one that predicts failure, so we ask it in a form that is hard to answer vaguely: name the evenings you are already teaching, and where. A tutor who cannot answer that has not planned their own week, and will not plan your child's term either.

Your own checks matter more on an ongoing arrangement than on a one-off. Four things to establish before you commit a term. Who covers if the tutor is away for two weeks, and will the cover tutor get the session notes? What notice does either side give to end the arrangement? What happens to a session you cancel on the day, and to one the tutor cancels? Will you get something in writing after each session? Settle those in the first week, while everyone is agreeable, rather than in the week it goes wrong. A professional home tutor will have answers ready because they have been asked before.

On claims, be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or quotes a success rate: IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor can promise a specific result for a specific child. Parents hunting for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Cuffe Parade should treat confident numbers as a warning rather than a credential. What you can reasonably ask for is evidence of practice: a sample of the tutor's written feedback on a student's work with the name removed, and a description of how they handled a student who was not improving. Those answers tell you more than any claim about results.

sections.heading: How many hours a week actually move a grade?
paragraphs: For one subject, two hours a week across a full term is the arrangement that reliably changes something, and three is the ceiling before returns drop off because the child stops having time to do the work set. One hour a week works for maintenance and for a strong student who needs stretching, and it rarely rescues a subject that is genuinely behind. Four hours a week in one subject is almost always a sign that the real problem was diagnosed wrongly: a student who cannot read a question does not need more content, and a student who is two years behind needs a longer runway rather than a denser week.

Term-long and exam-term arrangements are different products and should be priced and planned as such. A term-long slot is cheaper per unit of progress because the tutor can build: diagnose in week one, teach for six weeks, consolidate, then test. An exam-term sprint bought in January for March papers is triage, and the honest version of it names two or three topics worth the remaining hours and abandons the rest. Both are legitimate. What does not work is buying a sprint and expecting term-long outcomes, which is the complaint behind most of the disappointment we hear in the second week of the examination season.

What IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Cuffe Parade depend on is a short list and no honest platform publishes one rate. Board and level, because Diploma Programme Higher Level work and Year 9 support are not the same preparation. Subject scarcity, which is the biggest single factor: a widely taught subject has a deep island pool, a rare language has a handful of qualified teachers in Mumbai. Travel distance, which is why a Colaba tutor can be better value for the same hour than one crossing town. Session length and frequency. And whether the rate includes planning, marking of work set between sessions, and the written note, or whether those are extra. Ask what is included before you compare two numbers.

sections.heading: How will I know between sessions that this is working?
paragraphs: Through three artefacts, all of which should exist by week two. A short written note after every session saying what was covered, what was set and what comes next. A record of marks on anything timed, kept by the tutor, so that progress is a line rather than an impression. And a fortnightly five-minute conversation with you, at the door or on the phone, against the paragraph you wrote at the start. If an arrangement has none of those after a month, you are paying for attendance. Ask for the note first, because a tutor who writes notes is usually also planning, and one who will not is usually improvising.

What the artefacts should show at four weeks is changed behaviour rather than better marks: working set out without being asked, questions read twice, a topic that has moved from blank to attempted. At one term, marks become a fair measure, with the caveat that school tests and full papers measure different things and that grade boundaries move between series, so a real two-mark gain can show as no change in the letter. The useful trend is the gap between performance on recently taught topics and on material from a year ago narrowing, because stopping old content rotting is most of what a weekly tutor is for.

The limits are worth saying plainly. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and does not publish success rates, because a figure that averages across thousands of different children tells you nothing about yours. A term of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Cuffe Parade can change how much of a syllabus a student attempts under time pressure, the quality of their written method, and their familiarity with the paper. It cannot replace two years of absence from a subject in eight weeks, and a tutor who implies otherwise is managing your expectations rather than your child's learning.

Expect the tutor to work through recent marked work, stopping at each lost mark to establish whether it was a knowledge gap, a method error, a misread question or time running out, and to come out with two or three named weaknesses. Expect the plan to say which weeks are teaching, which are consolidation, and where the collision fortnight falls. faqs.question: How many sessions a week should we book for a Year 10 IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: Start with two in one subject rather than one each in two. Two hours a week lets a tutor teach something new and then test older material in the same week, which is the pattern that stops content rotting. One hour a week suits a strong student who needs stretching or a subject that is only slightly off track. If two subjects are both genuinely weak, run the weaker one at two hours for a term and the other at one, then swap after the half-term review. Booking four thin hours across four subjects spends your money and your child's evenings without changing any of them.

faqs.question: Can we pause home tuition during the school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should decide which kind of pause before the holiday starts. A full stop is fine for a student who is on track and needs rest. For a student catching up, a reduced pattern of one session a week through the break is worth far more than the same hours crammed into the week before school restarts, because spacing is what makes material stick. Tell the tutor three weeks ahead so the slot is held rather than given away, and confirm in writing whether the slot is reserved for your return. Good evening slots in South Mumbai do not sit empty for a month.

faqs.question: What happens to our slot if the tutor travels for a fortnight?
faqs.answer: The arrangement should name a cover tutor and a handover before it starts, and this is the single most common gap in tuition arrangements made informally. Ask who covers, whether they teach the same board and level, and whether they will receive the session notes and the mark record rather than starting from nothing. A fortnight with a cover tutor who has the notes keeps momentum. A fortnight of nothing in the middle of a coursework window costs more than the sessions missed. If no cover is available, agree in advance whether the missed sessions are made up or credited.

faqs.question: Do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Cuffe Parade change between term time and exam term?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because demand and the nature of the work both change. In the exam term the same hour is heavier for the tutor, involves marking full papers between sessions, and competes with every other family wanting the same evenings. A tutor holding a term-long slot for you usually keeps their rate steady and simply has less capacity to add extra sessions; a tutor engaged fresh in January for March papers is pricing scarcity. The way to avoid the January problem is to set the arrangement up in the first term rather than the last. Ask about exam-term availability when you first agree the slot.

faqs.question: Is planning and marking included in the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: It varies, and you should ask explicitly before comparing two quotes. Some tutors price a flat hourly rate that includes preparing the session, marking work set between sessions and writing the note afterwards. Others charge for contact time only and treat marking a full paper as additional. Neither is wrong, but two rates that look different may be identical once you account for it, and the cheaper contact-only rate can end up costing more during an exam term when there is a paper to mark every week. Get the answer in writing alongside the session length and the cancellation terms.

faqs.question: How do we handle a missed session, and who absorbs the cost?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule in week one and apply it without debate thereafter. The common arrangement that works: a session you cancel with more than twenty-four hours' notice is rescheduled or credited, one cancelled on the day is charged because the tutor cannot refill that hour, and one the tutor cancels is made up or credited to you. Put it in the same message as the rate. Families who leave this undefined end up negotiating it the first time a child is ill, usually badly, and that argument is what ends more arrangements in this city than teaching quality ever does.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both our children if they are on different boards?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking because back-to-back sessions save travel and often the rate reflects that. The test is whether the tutor genuinely teaches both: Cambridge IGCSE Extended tier Mathematics and Diploma Programme Mathematics at Higher Level are related but separately demanding, and someone strong in one is not automatically safe in the other. Ask for recent teaching at each level. Where the fit is only good for one child, use two tutors rather than compromising on the weaker match, and stagger the evenings so the dining table is not contested.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers and worksheets, or do we buy them?
faqs.answer: Tutors normally bring their own materials and past papers, and you should not be buying a separate package of resources on top of the hourly rate. What to check is that the papers are for your child's current syllabus version and board, because an old specimen paper from a superseded syllabus teaches the wrong structure and students do notice. Your school may also issue its own question banks, which a tutor should use in preference to generic material. If a tutor asks you to purchase a specific textbook, ask why that one and whether the school already uses it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our building in Colaba or Nariman Point instead?
faqs.answer: Yes, the matching pool is the same across Cuffe Parade, Colaba, Nariman Point and Fort, which is why a tutor can hold two slots in different parts of the island on one evening. The practical difference is the gate protocol rather than the distance: every complex handles recurring visitors differently, and registering the tutor once with the society office saves ten minutes a week for a whole term. Tell us the exact address when you enquire so the shortlist reflects which direction tutors actually travel from, and so the slot times offered are ones that survive the evening peak.

faqs.question: What should the written note after each session contain?
faqs.answer: Four lines is enough: what was covered, what the student did well, what was set for the week, and what the tutor wants to look at next. It should take the tutor three minutes and it is the only durable record a parent has. Over a term those notes become the evidence for whether an arrangement is working, and they are what a cover tutor reads when your regular tutor is away. If notes stop arriving, that usually precedes a drift into unplanned homework help. Ask for the first one after session one rather than waiting to see whether it appears.

faqs.question: Should we change tutors between DP1 and DP2?
faqs.answer: Usually not, because continuity across the Diploma Programme is worth more than almost any upgrade in profile. The tutor who supervised the Internal Assessment work in DP1 knows which parts of the method your child actually understands and which were borrowed, and that knowledge is expensive to rebuild in the final year. Change only for a concrete reason: the tutor does not teach the Higher Level content your child has moved up to, reliability has slipped, or the relationship has gone stale and sessions have become transactional. If you do change, insist the outgoing tutor writes a handover.

faqs.question: Is an evening slot after 8pm realistic on a school night?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and booking one is how a weekly arrangement starts getting cancelled. By 8pm a Year 10 or DP1 student in Mumbai has had a full school day, travel and often a co-curricular commitment, and the hour you pay for is spent at their lowest concentration. The slots that hold for a term here are between 5:30pm and 7:30pm on weekdays, plus weekend mornings, which are genuinely underused. If no weekday evening works, a Saturday morning session with real attention beats a Wednesday 8:30pm session that gets moved twice and then dropped.

sections.heading: Turning one enquiry into a written IB and IGCSE home tuition plan
paragraphs: Most enquiries from the hill arrive as a sentence about one child and turn out to be about two. A parent writes asking for help with Chemistry and mentions in passing that the older one starts the Diploma Programme in June. Those are not two separate problems to solve in sequence; they are one timetable with one set of evenings in it, and treating them as a single planning exercise is the difference between IB and IGCSE home tuition in Cumballa Hill that holds for two years and an arrangement rebuilt every six weeks. Mumbai evenings are too short to spend rebuilding one.

So the enquiry becomes a plan in four steps. 1. Both children are written down together: year group, board, subjects, the examination or submission dates each is working towards. 2. The evenings available in your week are listed honestly, including the ones already taken by sport, music or a long school run. 3. Each subject needing help is ranked by how much of the final result is still movable, which is a different ranking from how worried anybody feels. 4. Only then are tutors matched, to slots that already exist rather than to slots a family hopes to invent.

Ranking by what is still movable changes decisions. A Year 11 subject eight weeks from an external series is largely a technique problem; a DP1 subject in its first term is almost entirely movable and deserves the better slot. Parents arrive convinced the opposite is true, because the nearer deadline feels more urgent. A counsellor who does not say this out loud is being polite rather than useful.

The output you should expect is a single page: which child, which subject, which tutor, which slot, what gets reviewed when. Where the subjects genuinely overlap, one tutor covers both children. Where they do not, two are matched and the plan says so. Families asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Cumballa Hill could carry alone usually accept the split once they see it written down with the paper differences named.

sections.heading: What changes when an IGCSE student becomes a DP1 student?
paragraphs: Almost everything about how work is produced, and very little about the content. A Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel candidate spends two years preparing for papers somebody else sets on a date somebody else picks. A Diploma Programme student starts generating assessed work themselves: Internal Assessments written during the course, an Extended Essay with its own research question, Theory of Knowledge, and subject work at Higher Level that goes deeper than anything in the earlier course. The deadline changes from an external event to a series of self-managed milestones.

That shift breaks the habits that worked before. A student who succeeded on the IGCSE by revising hard in the last six weeks has a method that fails in the Diploma Programme, because nothing can be left to the last six weeks when the coursework was due in November. The first term of DP1 is where this becomes visible, and it usually looks like a bright student suddenly producing mediocre work. It is almost never a knowledge problem.

The second change is depth at Higher Level. Three subjects go further than the previous course did, and the two or three weeks where that gap opens are specific and predictable: the first abstract topic in mathematics, the first derivation in physics, the first literary essay where plot summary earns nothing. A tutor who has taught both courses can see those weeks coming, and the useful intervention is scheduled before them rather than after the first bad mark.

The third is the quiet one. Diploma Programme marks arrive through criteria and command terms rather than as a percentage, and a student who has never been taught to read a mark scheme keeps producing good work that does not score. This is the single most common thing IB and IGCSE home tuition in Cumballa Hill is asked to fix in the first DP term, across Mumbai as much as on this hill, and it responds quickly, because it is a reading problem rather than a learning problem.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE subjects set up which IB Diploma choices?
paragraphs: Mathematics is the decision that causes the most trouble. An Extended-tier Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel candidate who found the course comfortable is not automatically ready for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, because the step is in abstraction and proof rather than in difficulty of arithmetic. A student who liked modelling and data will often be better served by Applications and Interpretation, and the honest way to test this is to attempt a few DP-style questions in the spring of Year 11 rather than to argue about it in September.

The sciences map more cleanly but with one catch. A student who sat separate sciences has covered more ground than one who sat a combined or co-ordinated route, and both can take a Higher Level science, but the second needs a bridge. The content gap is real and closeable over a summer; what cannot be closed in a hurry is the habit of designing and criticising an investigation, which the Diploma Programme assesses seriously in every science.

On the language side, first-language English maps naturally into Language A and second-language English does not always, and the difference matters because a Language A course is read as literature or as language and literature rather than as comprehension. Students who moved into English recently should have that conversation with the coordinator before choosing, not after the first essay. The language acquisition group has its own trap: picking a language up again after two years away is harder than starting it fresh.

In the commerce and humanities group, the step is in evaluation. An IGCSE Business Studies or Economics answer that explains accurately scores well; a Diploma Programme answer that only explains sits in the middle. Households running all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes in Cumballa Hill across two children often find this is where one tutor can genuinely serve both, because the skill being taught, judging and weighing rather than listing, is the same skill at two levels.

sections.heading: Weekly slots across Cumballa Hill, Kemps Corner, Breach Candy and Tardeo
paragraphs: A two-child plan needs between three and five slots a week, which is a scheduling problem rather than a tutoring one, and it is solved by geography. Tutors whose week already runs through Kemps Corner, Breach Candy and Tardeo can take a second slot in the same household on a different evening without rearranging anything. A home tutor coming from outside the island can usually manage one visit a week and almost never two, however willing they sound in June, because the rest of Mumbai is further away in the evening than it looks at noon.

The reason is the specific shape of travel here. Eight kilometres from Worli to Colaba can take forty minutes once the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals back up in the evening peak, so a tutor's willingness matters less than their existing route. Grant Road, the nearest station on the Western Line, brings in tutors who commute by train and walk up the hill, and those arrangements are among the most reliable because no traffic is involved at all.

Where a household needs several slots, ask the counsellor to look for adjacency rather than availability. Two children taught back to back by one tutor on a Tuesday is efficient and sometimes right, but two children taught on different evenings by two tutors is usually better teaching, because nobody is tired and the second child is not waiting. A family searching for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Cumballa Hill should think in terms of a weekly grid, not a single appointment.

The newer infrastructure helps only at the margins. The Coastal Road makes the western seafront run quicker outside peak hours, and Metro Line 3 (Aqua) along the Cuffe Parade to Bandra Kurla Complex axis has brought a few southern tutors into weekend range. Neither changes a Tuesday at half past six, which is why an IB and IGCSE private tutor Cumballa Hill households keep for two years is nearly always someone already working these few streets.

paragraphs: It puts both sets of deadlines in the same envelope. Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo runs the IB Diploma Programme and the IGCSE pathway together, which is why sibling pairs on different boards are so common in this one neighbourhood, and why a Cumballa Hill household often receives coursework notices for a Diploma Programme student and examination information for a Cambridge candidate in the same week. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named here, and names them because the calendar is the thing that has to be planned around.

The collision has a shape you can predict. November brings mock papers for the examination cohort and the first coursework deadlines for the Diploma Programme cohort. January and February bring final submissions and Theory of Knowledge work alongside the last mocks and the practical preparation. March and April are study leave for one child and drafting for the other. If your plan does not name which child owns the early evening slot in each of those months, it will be decided by whoever is shouting in that week.

The transition window is the part nobody schedules. Between the end of the examination series and the start of DP1 there is a stretch of weeks when a student has finished one course and not started the next, and it is the single most useful tutoring window in the whole five-year span. A bridge in that window, aimed at the specific gap between a combined science route and a Higher Level science, or between Extended-tier maths and Analysis and Approaches, costs a fraction of what repair costs in the first DP term.

One practical Mumbai detail belongs here too. The school year opens with the monsoon, so the first weeks of any new arrangement are the weeks when travel is least predictable. Set the rule in June: a session that cannot happen in person moves to video the same evening. Households that write that line into the plan lose a handful of hours a year. Households that improvise it lose a term's worth across two children.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or a summer bridge for a Cumballa Hill household
paragraphs: In-person home tuition carries the weekly teaching for both children, and that is the default for a reason. A tutor at the table sees the working, keeps the phone out of the room and starts the session by arriving, and with two children in one house the physical presence also settles whose turn it is. For anybody below about sixteen, and for any student who does not begin work unsupervised, this is not a preference but a requirement.

Online earns specific jobs rather than the whole arrangement. The first is the summer bridge: families on the hill frequently travel in the weeks between the examination series and the start of DP1, and that is exactly when the bridge work should happen, so a strong IB and IGCSE online tutor in Cumballa Hill who can run fortnightly sessions from anywhere is worth more than a local tutor you will see in August. The second is scarcity, for a language or a specialist option nobody nearby teaches. The third is the run-in, when a thirty-minute marked-question session beats a long visit.

The hybrid shape that works for a two-board household is one visit per child per week plus short shared online reviews. The visits do the teaching. The reviews do the marking conversation, the planning and the deadline check, and they can be done in twenty minutes each. Running it this way also means the plan survives a washed-out evening, a family trip or an examination week when one child needs everything and the other needs nothing.

The honest limit on all the online options is supervision, and with two children it gets harder rather than easier. One child on a call in a bedroom while the other is being taught at the table is the arrangement most likely to quietly stop working. If the house does not have two usable work spaces, say so when the plan is written, and put both children on in-person slots on different evenings instead.

sections.heading: How do you check a tutor who claims both boards?
paragraphs: Ask for specifics on each board separately and listen for dates. A tutor who has prepared Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel candidates and also taught the Diploma Programme will name the years, the levels and the components without hesitating. A tutor who has read both syllabuses will answer in general terms about concepts and confidence. Both are honest positions; only one of them can run a two-board plan, and the question costs you one minute to ask.

Then test the thing that actually differs. Ask how a strong answer in the earlier course would score in a Diploma Programme paper, and why. A tutor who can explain that an accurate explanation without evaluation sits mid-band, and can show you where in a mark scheme that happens, has taught both. This is a better test than any certificate, because it is exactly the judgement your household needs on a Tuesday evening.

On the platform side, identity documents are checked, qualifications are verified against certificates rather than claims, and teaching history is confirmed with subjects, levels and dates. A subject conversation with somebody who knows the syllabus happens before any profile is shared, and for a two-board request that conversation covers both boards rather than one. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and verification is about what a tutor has taught, not about what your children will score.

Two last checks are worth more than they sound. Can this tutor hold two slots in one household for a full term, including through examination weeks when one child's needs spike? And who writes the feedback, how long is it, and when does it arrive? Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade on either board, and politely decline anybody who will not name a subject or level they would rather not take on.

sections.heading: A month-by-month IB and IGCSE home tuition plan for Mumbai families
paragraphs: June and July are for the bridge and the audit. Bridge work closes the specific gap into the next course: abstraction and proof for a student entering Analysis and Approaches, investigation design for one entering a Higher Level science, essay structure for one entering Language A. The audit is a page per child listing every subject, its level or tier, and the single thing that went wrong last year. August and September are for scaffolding: coursework questions chosen and narrowed for the Diploma Programme child, syllabus mapping and weekly written output for the examination child.

October and November are the first honest signal. Mock papers arrive for the examination cohort and first coursework drafts for the Diploma Programme cohort, and the plan should be rewritten rather than continued at this point, because now you have evidence instead of impressions. December is a reset, not a sprint: two or three sessions aimed at one named weakness per child, and a break that is actually a break.

January and February are where the plan earns its keep. Final submissions, Theory of Knowledge work, last mocks and practical preparation collide, and the only thing that prevents a bad month is the rule written in June about who gets which evening. March and April are paper discipline for anyone sitting a series: timed sections, mark-scheme reading, question selection, and no new content. May is the series itself, when a tutor's job is to be available and calm rather than to teach.

Cost follows the plan rather than the panic. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Cumballa Hill depend on the board and level, on how scarce the subject is locally, on travel time at peak hour, on session length and frequency, and on how much marking happens between visits. Two children on a written plan usually cost less than two children handled reactively, because the hours land where they do something. Families comparing quotes across Mumbai should compare the plan, not the hourly rate, since IB and IGCSE home tuition in Cumballa Hill priced by the hour tells you nothing about how many hours you will need. Nobody can publish a ranking for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Cumballa Hill, and the phrase is worth less than a plan with four review dates in it.

sections.heading: What the plan should have changed by the four-week review
paragraphs: Four weeks in, the plan should have produced three visible things, and none of them is a mark. Each child has done the written work the tutor set, between sessions, without a standoff. Each can name the specific thing they could not do a month ago and can now. And one dated item has moved: a coursework question agreed, a syllabus section closed, a full past paper attempted under time. If the plan has produced only attendance, it is not a plan and the review is the moment to change it.

By the end of a term the two boards show progress differently, and expecting the same signal from both is a common mistake. The examination child should show a narrower mark band and fewer unattempted questions rather than a dramatic jump. The Diploma Programme child should have coursework at a stage a school supervisor can mark seriously, and should be scoring better against criteria even where the content is the same, because the reading of the mark scheme has improved.

Across a full cycle the honest claim is modest and worth stating plainly. Tutoring moved technique, closed named content gaps, and got work produced on time. It did not add two years of reading, did not change a tier entry made in Year 9, and did not produce a number anybody could have promised in September. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a tutor who tells you otherwise about either board is the tutor who will go quiet in April.

The limit specific to two-child plans is attention, yours as much as the tutor's. A household can genuinely run three to five tutoring slots a week; it cannot genuinely review eight subjects a month. Pick two things per child to watch, write them in the plan, and ignore the rest until the next review. Families who try to supervise everything end up supervising nothing, and the first casualty is the younger child, whose problems are less urgent and more fixable.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Cumballa Hill
paragraphs: Send both children in one message. For each: year group, board, subjects with codes or levels, the next dated deadline, and the one thing that went wrong last year. Then send your week: which evenings are genuinely free, which are already taken, and whether a weekend slot is possible. That is everything a counsellor needs to produce a draft plan, and it takes about ten minutes to write down.

Expect a call before any profile arrives. The call exists to rank the subjects by what is still movable and to tell you which of your assumptions about urgency is wrong, which is uncomfortable and useful. After it you should have a one-page plan naming each child, each subject, each slot, each tutor type and each review date, with the split between one tutor and two made explicit and explained.

For the first sessions, have the evidence ready rather than the reports. The most recent marked script for each child, with blanks and annotations intact, plus the school's assessment calendar for the term. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is not a real offering, so expect each tutor to tell you which subjects they should take and which need somebody else. That sentence, said in week one, is the most valuable thing in the whole arrangement.

Then let it be dull. Fixed slots, feedback you can read in two minutes, a four-week review you actually hold, and a longer review at the end of term when the mock scripts and the first drafts give you real evidence. Two boards in one household is a logistics problem more than an academic one, and in Mumbai logistics problems are solved on paper in June rather than in argument in February. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Cumballa Hill is at its best when a visitor would find nothing dramatic happening at all.

faqs.question: Can one tutor hold slots for two children on different boards in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Physically yes, and it is often a mistake. Back-to-back sessions suit the tutor's travel and nobody else: the second child gets a tired teacher, and in a two-hour block the younger one usually waits rather than works. Where the subjects genuinely overlap, such as two sciences or two commerce subjects, one tutor on two separate evenings is the better arrangement. Where the boards and papers differ, two tutors on different evenings is better still, and in South Mumbai the local pool of home tutors is usually deep enough to arrange it.

faqs.question: Should the two children share one session at home, or have separate ones?
faqs.answer: Separate, in almost every case. Siblings two or three years apart are at different points in the syllabus, and a shared session becomes a lesson pitched at the older child while the younger one copies. The exception is a short, specific shared skill: how to read a mark scheme, how to plan an essay in five minutes, how to annotate a data question. Those work well as a one-off pair session. Anything that requires individual written work and individual feedback should be taught alone, which is how home classes in most Mumbai households end up arranged.

faqs.question: When should the summer bridge between Year 11 and DP1 start?
faqs.answer: As soon as the examination series ends, while the content is still live in the student's head. The weeks between finishing one course and starting the Diploma Programme are the cheapest and most productive tutoring window in the whole five years, because nothing is due and nothing is being revised. Use them for the specific step: abstraction and proof for Analysis and Approaches, investigation design for a Higher Level science, literary essay structure for Language A. Fortnightly sessions are enough, and they can run on video while the family travels.

faqs.question: Does a strong IGCSE Maths result mean Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is safe?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. The step from Extended-tier work into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is a step in abstraction, proof and algebraic stamina rather than in arithmetic difficulty, and comfortable candidates sometimes struggle while slightly weaker but more patient ones do well. The honest test is to attempt a handful of Diploma Programme style questions in the spring of Year 11 with somebody who can read the attempt. Students who enjoyed modelling and data are often better served by Applications and Interpretation, which is a real choice rather than a lesser one.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Cumballa Hill depend on with two children?
faqs.answer: The same five factors as for one child, plus one. Board and level, how scarce the subject is locally, travel time into the island at peak hour, session length and frequency, and how much marking happens between visits. The sixth is whether one tutor covers both children, which reduces travel loading but only works where the papers genuinely overlap. A written plan usually costs less than reactive hiring, because the hours land on work that is still movable rather than on subjects where the result is already mostly set.

faqs.question: Our DP child and our IGCSE child have deadlines in the same week. Who gets the tutor?
faqs.answer: Decide it in advance, and in that specific week give the slot to whoever has the external deadline. An external examination series moves for nobody; a coursework deadline can often be discussed with a supervisor if there is a genuine reason. The better answer is not to be making the decision in the week itself at all. The plan should name, in June, which child owns the early evening slot in November, in January and in February, and the two most contested months should be settled before anybody is under pressure.

faqs.question: Is it worth tutoring a subject the child will drop after Year 11?
faqs.answer: Only if the grade itself matters for something. Some school and university pathways look at the full set of IGCSE results, so a collapsing subject can be worth a few sessions of damage limitation. If nothing downstream depends on it, the hours are better spent on a subject continuing into the Diploma Programme, where the same money buys two years of benefit rather than two months. Ask the coordinator directly whether the result is used for anything, and then decide rather than hedging.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE study habits carry into the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Some do and the most successful one does not. Content revision, past-paper practice and timed writing all transfer. The habit of leaving the heavy work until the last six weeks does not, because Diploma Programme coursework is produced during the course and cannot be compressed. Students who relied on a late sprint are often the ones with the worst first DP term, and it reads as a sudden decline in ability when it is actually a scheduling method that has stopped matching the assessment. This is fixable, and the fix is calendar work rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Can the plan be written before we choose the tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should be. The plan sets out which children, which subjects, which slots and which review dates, and it exists so that tutors are matched to real gaps in your week rather than to a wish. Writing it first also makes the split decision visible: you can see on one page where one tutor can carry both children and where two are needed. If a platform wants to send profiles before asking about your week, you are being sold a transaction rather than an arrangement.

faqs.question: What if one child progresses and the other does not?
faqs.answer: Treat them as two separate reviews, because they are. The commonest pattern on this hill is that the older child with the nearer deadline improves visibly while the younger one drifts, partly because the attention and the better slot went to the urgent case. If that is what happened, swap the slot rather than the tutor. If the younger child genuinely is not responding after four weeks of done work and clear feedback, change the match early. A replacement in week five costs nothing; one in February costs the term.

faqs.question: Will you put a predicted outcome in the plan?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a plan that contains a predicted number is a sales document rather than a schedule. What the plan does contain is checkable: which topics are covered in which order, what written work is set, what the student should be able to do by a stated date, and when each of those gets reviewed. If you want a realistic grade range for either board, the people to ask are the subject teachers at school, who hold the internal evidence and the mock scripts.

sections.heading: How IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dadar Parsi Colony is arranged, step by step
paragraphs: Treat the first conversation as a scheduling problem as much as an academic one, because that is what decides whether the arrangement lasts. Families who tell us only the subject get a tutor. Families who tell us the subject, the stage, the evenings they can defend and what else is in the week get an arrangement that is still running in March. The difference between those two outcomes is almost never the quality of the tutor. It is whether the slot was designed around a real household or around an optimistic one.

We start with the programme stage, because a Primary Years Programme (PYP) child, a Middle Years Programme (MYP) student and a Diploma Programme (DP) candidate need different people and different session shapes. Then subjects, and for a DP student the Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) split. Then the symptom in plain language rather than the grade. Then the week: school finish times, any sport or music commitment, a sibling's schedule, and the two evenings you can genuinely hold for three months rather than for a fortnight.

From there we produce three or four named tutors, each already teaching inside the island city on at least one of your evenings, each with the programme and components they have actually taught. The first session is diagnostic and the recurring slot is fixed afterwards. What we then ask of you is a review at four weeks, a short conversation rather than a form. sections.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: what changes in home tuition at each stage
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs three programmes that a child in this city may pass through, and the tutoring that works in one is actively wrong in the next. In the Primary Years Programme the learning is organised around transdisciplinary inquiry rather than subject silos, so a tutor who arrives with a worksheet pack on fractions has misunderstood the job. Sessions should be short, frequent and aimed at one skill: number sense, reading fluency, written expression. Thirty minutes twice a week beats ninety minutes once, and a month-long intervention that then stops is often the honest prescription.

In the Middle Years Programme the structure changes to eight subject groups assessed against published criteria rather than a single percentage. This is where parents most often misread a report. A child scoring unevenly across criteria in the same subject does not have a content problem, they have one specific weakness, usually in the criterion that asks for analysis or evaluation rather than knowledge. A tutor who knows the criteria finds that in one session. A tutor who does not will spend a term re-teaching content the child already knows, which is the most common waste of money in MYP tutoring.

The Diploma Programme changes the problem again. Six subjects, the Higher Level and Standard Level split, Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and the Internal Assessment (IA) in each subject, all running on school-set internal deadlines across two years. The academic difficulty is real, but the thing that breaks most DP students is sequencing. Component structures and requirements are revised by the IB on its own cycle, so treat the current subject guide and your school's coordinator as the source rather than anything inherited from an older sibling.

The practical consequence for a long arrangement is that you will change tutors at least once, probably twice, and that is normal rather than a failure. A brilliant primary tutor is usually not an MYP sciences tutor, and an MYP tutor is usually not a Higher Level mathematics specialist. Plan the handover a term before the transition instead of in the first week of the new year. An IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai families keep for a decade is rarely one person, and the families who manage it best treat the stage change as a scheduled event.
bullets: PYP: short frequent sessions on one skill, then stop deliberately
MYP: criterion-referenced marking, usually one criterion dragging

Expect to change tutors at each stage transition

sections.heading: Which subjects should stay with school and which need a tutor?
paragraphs: Keep with school anything where the child is coping and the teaching is working, which is usually more subjects than an anxious parent thinks. A tutor is worth hiring where three things are true at once: there is a measurable mark loss, the cause is identifiable, and the child has the capacity to take on another weekly commitment. If any of those is missing, hiring produces activity rather than progress. The most expensive mistake we see is a tutor for every subject at once, which exhausts the child and makes it impossible to tell what worked.

Subject choice across both boards, HL and SL decisions, and the internal assessments each subject carries are the second conversation, and it needs somebody who has taught the senior components. A student taking three Higher Level subjects that all carry a heavy written component has built a second year that will not survive. A student choosing a Higher Level science because of a university requirement they have not checked is making a four-semester commitment on a rumour. One or two sessions on this before the choices are locked is better value than a term of repair afterwards.

Within subjects, the recurring losses at each stage are specific enough to name. In MYP sciences and humanities, marks go on description where the criterion asked for analysis, and on conclusions that restate the data rather than evaluate the method. In DP mathematics the exploration fails on scope: a topic too broad, with no genuine mathematics in it, written in the last fortnight. In DP sciences the investigation fails on control and on uncertainty handling. In language and literature it fails when a student writes about theme and the question asked about technique.

A single generalist cannot cover all of that honestly, and we will say so. We are regularly asked for one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai households would like to simplify down to, and the realistic version is a specialist for the subject that is actually losing marks plus school for the rest. Ask instead for all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Dadar Parsi Colony can carry credibly at one stage, which for most tutors is two or three related subjects rather than a whole curriculum.

sections.heading: Can one tutor cover Dadar, Matunga and Sion in a single week?
paragraphs: Yes, and that is precisely the tutor you want, because a week built from three nearby students is a week that holds. Dadar Parsi Colony sits a short walk from Dadar station, where two of the city's main rail corridors meet, so a tutor can come in by train from a long way out and walk the last stretch without touching a road signal. The practical catchment for a recurring slot is Dadar itself, Matunga to the north and Sion beyond it, and most of our matches for this address come from within those three.

The reason the radius matters is attrition rather than convenience. The island city is compact and its journeys are short, but the evening signals are brutal: a tutor running the eight kilometres from Worli down towards Colaba can lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali queues once the peak sets in. Nobody sustains that twice a week for a full year, and the failure is gradual rather than announced. Tutors here are matched within the island instead of being brought down from the suburbs, which is the whole reason a long arrangement is achievable at this address.

Within the radius there are real differences worth knowing. A tutor already teaching in Matunga can take a 6.30pm Parsi Colony slot and a 8pm Dadar slot on the same evening, which is how the economics of a nearby tutor actually work and why they will protect your slot. Sion sits at the outer edge and works best when the tutor is travelling south anyway. For a household running tuition over several years this has a planning consequence. The tutor you choose in Year 6 is part of a local network, and when your child moves stage that tutor is usually the fastest route to the next one. sections.heading: How does the Mumbai school year shape a long tuition arrangement?
paragraphs: It gives you three natural review points and one trap. The year opens after the monsoon break with new content and no pressure, which is the right moment to start or to change a tutor. The first term assessments are the first honest signal and the first review point. The mock or mid-year series is the second. The final series and study leave close it. The trap is the window between the mock results and study leave, when every family in the city reaches the same conclusion at once and the only tutors with slots free are the ones nobody else wanted.

Families in these lanes attend a spread of international schools rather than one dominant local option. Don Bosco International School and JBCN International School, Parel are both within a manageable school run of Parsi Colony, and their timetables and internal deadlines decide which evenings exist in your week. Both are named here as local context and nothing else. IB Gram is an independent matching platform, is not affiliated with Don Bosco International School, JBCN International School, Parel, or any other school mentioned on this page, and has no arrangement with any school.

For a long arrangement, the useful habit is to align your review conversation with the school's reporting cycle rather than with your own anxiety. Read the report, take the component or criterion breakdown rather than the summary grade, and put it in front of the tutor. Ask what in that breakdown they expected and what surprised them. A tutor who is genuinely tracking a student will have predicted most of it. One who is surprised by all of it has not been marking closely enough, and that is a specific, fair thing to raise.

The other calendar fact worth planning for is the transition year. A child moving from the Primary Years Programme into the Middle Years Programme meets subject-by-subject expectations for the first time. A student moving from the final MYP year into the Diploma Programme meets internal deadlines that cluster rather than spread. Both transitions are much easier if the support starts in the term before rather than the term after. All IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Dadar Parsi Colony families book at those two moments do more than any amount of remedial work later.

sections.heading: Home, online or hybrid across a twelve-year run in Mumbai
paragraphs: The right mode changes as the child grows, and families who pick one and keep it for a decade get it wrong at both ends. For a primary-age child, home is the only sensible answer. The tutor needs to be in the room to see what the child does with a pencil, when they disengage and how they respond to being stuck, and a seven-year-old on a screen needs an adult present anyway, which means you are supervising rather than working. There is also a physical argument specific to this address worth using.

Parsi Colony is low-rise and quiet with large old flats, so it is one of the few places in the city where a tutor is working in a genuinely silent room. For a young child that silence is the difference between thirty productive minutes and thirty minutes of redirection. For a Diploma Programme student it means a full paper under timed conditions is actually possible at a dining table on a weekday evening, which in most Mumbai flats on a main road is not available at any price. The IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dadar Parsi Colony arrangements that work best use that deliberately rather than incidentally.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Dadar Parsi Colony becomes genuinely useful from the middle years onwards, and essential for scarce subjects. If the only specialist with real experience of your child's Higher Level component is not in the island city, a well-run screen session beats a nearby generalist, and saying otherwise would be dishonest. The conditions are specific: the student needs a tablet or document camera so the tutor sees working rather than final answers, sessions should be shorter and more frequent than home sessions, and somebody has to keep work moving between them.

Hybrid is where most long arrangements land by the senior years, and it is worth designing. One home session a week for teaching and diagnosis, one shorter online contact to mark work already produced. It demands more of the household than a single visit, because the work has to exist before the online slot or the session becomes a conversation. It also covers the monsoon evenings when the roads give up, which here is a normal feature of the calendar rather than a crisis.

sections.heading: What we check, and what you should check every year
paragraphs: Our checks happen before you are introduced to anybody. Identity against government photographic identification. Subject qualification seen as a document rather than described on a call. And programme-specific teaching history: which programme, which subjects, which components, across how many cohorts. The third is the one that matters and the one that directories skip, because a physics graduate and a tutor who has supervised a dozen scientific investigations are not the same product even though they list the same subject.

Your own checks at the hiring stage are simple and should not be skipped because somebody seems pleasant. Ask the tutor to describe the assessment components or criteria for your child's subject and say what each actually rewards. Ask what the first session will involve, and listen for whether the answer is about diagnosing your child or about their own method. Ask for one specific change they made for a student in the same year group. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, and treat reluctance to be interviewed before booking as the answer rather than an inconvenience.

The checks people forget are the annual ones, and on a long arrangement they matter more than the initial interview. Every year, ask whether this tutor is still the right stage match. A tutor who was excellent for MYP sciences may be out of their depth at Higher Level, and the signs are subtle: sessions that drift into revision of old content, marking that gets lighter, a reluctance to look at the current component requirements. Nobody will volunteer this. The year-two review is yours to run, and it is the single most valuable habit in a long arrangement.

We should be clear about our own limits, because that is part of being checkable. IB Gram matches tutors and is not a school or an employer of record. We do not guarantee grades and publish no success rate, because any figure would be unverifiable and would say nothing about your child's starting point or the time available. What we stand behind is the match: if the depth is not as described, or the slot cannot be held, we replace the tutor without requiring a long justification. Every IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dadar Parsi Colony booking rests on that, and on nothing we cannot show you.

sections.heading: Running a standing weekly slot that survives from Year 4 to Year 12
paragraphs: A long tuition arrangement fails for logistical reasons far more often than academic ones, and the failures are boringly predictable. The slot moves once for a school event and never moves back. Sessions start fifteen minutes late because the gate entry is negotiated afresh each week. The work the tutor set does not get done, so the next session becomes a repeat. A younger sibling's routine collides with the hour. None of those is about teaching, and all of them are fixable in the first fortnight if you treat the arrangement as a system rather than an appointment.

Four decisions, made once, prevent most of it. Fix the place in the flat where sessions happen and do not move it, because a child who works in the same seat at the same table every week starts working within two minutes rather than ten. Get the tutor named at the gate for standing weekly entry rather than as a fresh visitor, which in these older low-rise blocks is a two-minute conversation with the watchman and recovers close to two sessions of teaching across a term. Agree a missed-session rule before you need one. And protect the hour from the rest of the household.

The fifth decision is the one families underrate: write down what happens between sessions. A tutor who sets work and never sees it done is running a conversation, not a course. The arrangement that works has a visible place where the set work lives, a day it is due, and two minutes at the start of each session checking it. For a primary child that is a parent's job. For a Middle Years student it should be theirs with oversight. For a Diploma Programme candidate it should be entirely theirs, and if it is not, that is the first thing the tutor should be working on.

What this adds up to is a view about what tuition is for. What IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Dadar Parsi Colony buy is not primarily explanation, which is available free in a dozen places. It is accountability, diagnosis and the structure around independent work. The quiet room here makes that structure cheaper to run than almost anywhere else in Mumbai, because the hour is actually an hour rather than an hour minus the noise. Families who understand that get far more out of the same money than families buying weekly reassurance.

paragraphs: A diagnosis, not a grade. You should have seen one piece produced under realistic conditions. There should be a short written list of priorities with items deliberately left off it. If nobody can tell you what the problem is after four sessions, the tutor is delivering content rather than diagnosing, and that is a reason to change rather than to wait for the report. This is the first test we ask families to apply to IB and IGCSE home classes in Dadar Parsi Colony, Mumbai.

At one term, expect the structural things to move before the headline grade. An MYP student scoring unevenly across criteria starts scoring evenly. A Diploma Programme student whose Internal Assessment drafts described rather than analysed starts producing sections that answer the criterion. A mathematics student starts showing working an examiner can follow. School reports usually trail the underlying change by one cycle, so a flat report sitting beside visibly better work is the normal shape of progress rather than evidence of failure.

Across a full cycle the honest statement is that a well-matched tutor plus consistent independent work moves outcomes, and that neither half does much alone. We do not guarantee grades and will not publish a success rate, because the real determinants are the starting point, the time left, the subject and the hours the student puts in between sessions. Anybody naming a specific grade or point total before meeting your child is describing a sales target. On a long arrangement, that kind of promise is also a reliable predictor of a tutor who will not last the year.

There are cases where the right answer is to stop, and a platform worth using will say so. A student sleeping five hours under the Diploma Programme load needs the load reduced rather than another weekly commitment. A child who has not opened the textbook does not have a teaching problem. A child slipping in every subject at once usually has something a subject tutor cannot reach, and the school counsellor is the right first call. sections.heading: Setting up the table, the slot and the first term in Mumbai
paragraphs: Four things to have ready, and they take ten minutes. The programme stage, with subjects and levels for a Diploma Programme student. The latest report showing the criterion or component breakdown rather than the summary grade. One recent piece of marked work with the teacher's comments intact, because the comments are the brief. And the two evening windows you can defend for three months, answered honestly rather than optimistically, including what happens in exam weeks and during the monsoon.

Expect the first session to assess rather than teach. A good tutor spends most of it watching your child work, asking how revision currently happens and probing one weak area rather than covering ground. You should end with two or three written priorities and one finding you did not enjoy. A first session that concludes everything is fine and the child just needs practice has told you about the tutor, not about the child, and it is worth saying so directly.

Set up the physical arrangement in the same week. One fixed place to work, the tutor named at the gate for standing entry, a decision about whether a parent is present or nearby, and a rule for missed sessions. For primary-age children present is usually right. From the Middle Years Programme onwards nearby is better, because a student works differently with a parent watching and the tutor loses the honest picture of what the child can do unaided. Ask for two minutes at the end of each session rather than a weekly written report.

Then review at four weeks on purpose. Ask what has changed, what has not, and what the tutor needs from your household. If the answers are thin, tell us what specifically did not work and we rematch, because that detail makes the second match better than a fresh guess. On an arrangement you intend to run for years, the habit of an honest review beats the hope that it is going well, and it costs one short conversation a term. That habit is what separates useful IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dadar Parsi Colony, Mumbai from a weekly visit that nobody is measuring.

faqs.question: How long do families here usually keep one home tuition arrangement running?
faqs.answer: Commonly a full academic year with one tutor, and often several years with a sequence of tutors as the child moves stage. The arrangement that lasts is the one designed around a protected evening rather than squeezed into a hopeful gap. What ends arrangements is rarely a falling out: the slot drifts after a school event, sessions shorten, and by the third month nobody is sure what the plan was. Fix the slot, the place and the review rhythm in the first fortnight and a year of home tuition in Mumbai is unremarkable rather than fragile.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Parsi Colony for the same evening slot every week for a year?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the match was built on that basis. We look for tutors already teaching in Dadar, Matunga or Sion on your chosen evening, because a tutor with two nearby students has a reason to protect your hour. What does not hold for a year is a dedicated crossing from the suburbs: the island is compact but the evening signal queues after six are unpredictable, and the arrangement decays quietly rather than being cancelled. Ask any candidate what else is in their diary that evening.

faqs.question: Do we have to change tutors when our child moves from the MYP to the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Usually yes for the senior subjects, and it is better to plan it than to discover it. A tutor strong on Middle Years criteria is not automatically fluent in Higher Level content or in how Internal Assessment work is actually marked. The smooth version is to start the conversation a term before the transition and ask your current tutor who they would hand the student to. Occasionally a tutor spans both, in which case ask them directly to describe the senior components before assuming it.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Dadar Parsi Colony depend on?
faqs.answer: Programme stage, subject scarcity, level, session length and frequency, travel, and whether the tutor marks work between sessions. We will not print a figure because any single number would mislead most readers: primary support and Higher Level Diploma Programme work are different jobs with different supply. Island matching keeps travel sensible at this address, which genuinely affects what a slot costs. Tell us the stage, the subject and the evening window and you get a real range rather than a headline designed to start a conversation.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in the room during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: For primary-age children usually yes; from the Middle Years Programme onwards usually no. A student of eleven or older works differently when a parent is watching, generally worse, and the tutor loses the honest picture of what the child can do unaided. Nearby is the right position: close enough to hear whether teaching or chatting is happening, far enough that the child owns the hour. Ask for two minutes at the end of each session and ask what your child got wrong rather than how they did.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a gate pass each week, or can we set up standing entry?
faqs.answer: Set up standing entry in the first week and the issue disappears for the year. Give the watchman the tutor's name, the day and the time; in these older low-rise blocks that is a short conversation rather than a process. If your building uses a visitor app, add the tutor as a recurring expected visitor. Each negotiated entry costs five to ten minutes at the start of a session, which across a term is close to two full sessions of teaching lost. Tutors will not raise it, so it sits with the family.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both my children, in PYP and in MYP, in the same visit?
faqs.answer: Back to back, sometimes; combined, almost never. A tutor comfortable across both stages can run two separate sessions in one visit, which saves a journey and a slot and usually prices as two sessions. Putting both children in one hour looks efficient and is not: the stages need different pace, different material and different kinds of attention, and in practice one child gets the lighter half every week. Ask for consecutive sessions and expect the tutor to tell you honestly whether both stages are within their range.

faqs.question: What happens when a session is missed for a school trip, illness or travel?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule at the start, before it costs anybody goodwill. The arrangement that works is a notice period for cancellations, a stated number of sessions that can be rescheduled in a term, and a default that a late tutor converts the evening to an online session rather than cancelling. Over a year a household will miss three or four sessions for entirely legitimate reasons, so a rule is more useful than negotiating each one. Put it in writing in the first week, however informal the arrangement feels.

faqs.question: My child is in the PYP. Is weekly tuition at that age a good idea?
faqs.answer: Often not as a standing arrangement, and we would rather say so than sell one. At Primary Years Programme age the useful shape is two short sessions a week on one specific skill, reviewed after a month and then stopped. Reading fluency, number sense and written expression respond well to that. An open-ended weekly commitment at seven or eight mostly adds pressure. If the concern is attention, behaviour or a suspected learning difference, the school is the right first call rather than a subject tutor.

faqs.question: How do we handle a tutor who is good but not pushing our child?
faqs.answer: Say it directly and specifically, because this is the most common and most fixable complaint. Ask for three things: work set between every session with a due date, marking you can see, and a written plan naming what is being left out. A tutor who is pleasant and undemanding often believes they are being asked to keep the child comfortable. If nothing changes in two sessions, tell us and we rematch. This exact problem is why we ask for a deliberate review at four weeks rather than waiting for a report.

faqs.question: Is online tuition ever better than having the tutor in our building?
faqs.answer: For a scarce senior subject, frequently yes. If the only specialist with genuine experience of your child's Higher Level component is elsewhere in the city, a well-run online session with a document camera beats a nearby generalist, and pretending otherwise would waste your year. It also wins in a revision phase where three short contacts a week beat one long visit. For primary and early middle years, and for any student who needs the accountability of somebody physically present, home remains better.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, or only subjects?
faqs.answer: Both, and they are among the most useful short engagements we arrange. The Extended Essay usually fails on research question scope rather than writing ability, and a tutor who has supervised essays can tell in one session whether the question is answerable in the available length. Theory of Knowledge support is mostly structure and the use of real examples. These are typically a handful of sessions at specific points in the year rather than a standing slot, and we will tell you when that is the honest shape rather than extending it.

sections.heading: How we build a home tuition shortlist for a Dadar household
paragraphs: The request we can act on contains five things, and most first messages carry two. We need the International Baccalaureate (IB) programme and the year: Primary Years Programme (PYP) with the grade, Middle Years Programme (MYP) with the year number, or Diploma Programme (DP) with first or second year. We need each subject named individually. We need to know who is at home during the proposed slot, because that changes which hours are workable far more than parents expect. We need the evenings you can give. And we need one piece of real work, marked, rather than a report grade.

The filtering runs in a fixed order. Programme and subject first, because a PYP reading request and a DP Higher Level (HL) request have nothing in common. Level second, since HL and Standard Level (SL) differ in depth rather than in topic list. Household fit third, which is the filter nobody else applies: a tutor who teaches brilliantly but talks over a parent, or who cannot work in a room with a younger sibling audible, is a poor match for a small Mumbai flat however strong the subject knowledge. Travel last, and on a request for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dadar travel is the easiest constraint in the city to satisfy.

What comes back is two or three profiles. Each names the programme and levels taught, the subjects, the number of cohorts the tutor has seen through assessment, and the evenings genuinely free. We do not send ratings or testimonials, and we do not name a teacher before you request the profile. You then call whoever you want to, and the call should be about logistics as much as pedagogy. Parents who arrive after searching for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Dadar expect a directory listing; a real shortlist covering all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Dadar can competently take is far shorter than that.

The first booking is one paid diagnostic session, not a free trial, and that distinction matters for the household question specifically. In a free trial everybody is on best behaviour, including your child. In a paid working session you see the real thing: whether the tutor sets up without fuss, whether your child engages after the first fifteen minutes, whether the room you picked survives contact with reality.

sections.heading: Which IB programme is your child in, and why does it matter?
paragraphs: It matters because the three International Baccalaureate programmes need three different kinds of visitor in your home. The Primary Years Programme is inquiry-led with no external examinations, and tutoring at that stage is short, frequent and physical: reading aloud, number work on paper, a tutor who can sit beside a seven year old for forty minutes without losing the room. Those sessions almost always have to happen at home, and they almost always need a parent nearby rather than in another room.

The Middle Years Programme spans the middle school years across eight subject groups and is assessed against published criteria rather than percentages. A criterion level of five is not five out of ten and is not half marks, and misreading that is the single most common source of panic among MYP parents. Tutoring here is largely about command terms and about writing to a criterion descriptor. A sibling page covers MYP in proper detail; what belongs on this page is the household consequence, which is that MYP work produces drafts and a tutor needs somewhere to spread paper out.

The Diploma Programme is the final two years: six subjects split between Higher Level and Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and the creativity, activity, service requirement. Every subject carries at least one Internal Assessment (IA) marked in school and moderated by the IB. A DP household runs differently from an MYP one. Sessions get longer, they move later into the evening, and the tutor increasingly works on material the student produced alone during the week rather than teaching live.

Do not take weightings, deadlines or hour counts from a prospectus or from any page including this one. The IB revises its subject guides on its own cycle, so a figure that was accurate two years ago may be wrong for the session your child sits. Ask your school's IB coordinator for the current subject guide and the internal deadline calendar, and build the tuition timetable backwards from those two documents.

sections.heading: Subject spread and internal assessment across the IB years in Mumbai
paragraphs: A Diploma student carries six subjects plus three core requirements, and the subjects are not the problem. The core is. Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the internally assessed component in each subject are all produced over weeks, at home, in parallel, and they collide. The household version of that collision is a Sunday in which a student needs the dining table for a draft, the kitchen for a Chemistry data table and the quiet room for a recorded oral. A tutor who understands this schedules around it instead of adding to it.

Internal assessment is where home tuition does its most visible work, and the reason is structural rather than motivational. An IA is a long piece produced in isolation, and isolation is exactly what produces a weak one: a research question too broad, a method the student cannot actually execute in a Mumbai flat or a school laboratory, data collected before anyone checked whether it would answer the question. An outside reader who sees a draft once a week catches all three early. A student reviewing her own work does not.

When a family asks us for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai, the truthful answer is that no single person is competent across that range, and anyone claiming to be should worry you. A wide spread is covered by two or three specialists, with one holding the main weekly slot and the others taking shorter or less frequent sessions. The best IB and IGCSE tutor in Dadar for a given household is usually a combination rather than a person.

The scarcity picture is worth knowing before expectations are set. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics and English have a deep pool in South Mumbai. Business Management, Psychology, Computer Science, Global Politics, Design Technology and Visual Arts have a thin one citywide. Mandarin, German, Japanese and Language A in a mother tongue other than English or Hindi are thinner still. For the thin subjects an online specialist is frequently the right answer and not a compromise, and an IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai teaching from another suburb by video beats a local generalist guessing at the syllabus.

sections.heading: Which Dadar addresses one tutor can cover in a single evening
paragraphs: More than you would guess, and the reason is on the platform signs: Dadar (Western & Central). That one fact widens the catchment for a weekly household slot further than anywhere else in the island city, and it is why tutors agree to standing Dadar bookings they turn down for addresses a short distance south. A tutor crossing from Worli towards Colaba covers eight kilometres and can still lose most of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, which is why we match within the island rather than importing from the suburbs.

Three adjoining pockets are scheduled as one unit with Dadar. There is a household consequence of the double booking worth flagging. A tutor coming to you second in the evening is more punctual but also more tired, and a tutor coming to you first is fresher but may be watching the clock. Neither is wrong, but say which you are getting. For a younger PYP child, first in the evening is better. For a DP student working on a draft at nine at night, second is fine.
