sections.heading: What does the Mumbai school year do to a home tuition timetable?
paragraphs: It compresses it twice and relaxes it twice, and a timetable built without that in mind breaks in January. Children in this part of the city attend a small set of international schools, and two come up on nearly every call from Dadar: Don Bosco International School in Matunga and JBCN International School, Parel a short drive towards Lower Parel. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Don Bosco International School, JBCN International School, Parel, or any other school named anywhere on this page. We name them because their internal calendars decide which weeks a tutor can do real work in.

The first relaxed stretch is the long vacation and the opening weeks of term. This is when a tutor should be diagnosing properly and when internally assessed work should be scoped rather than postponed, and it is the stretch most families waste because nothing feels urgent. The first compression arrives with first-term examinations and the earliest internal draft deadlines, and the household feels it as a sudden demand for extra sessions at short notice.

The second relaxed stretch is short and sits after the first-term results, when there is evidence to act on and time to use it. The second compression is the long one: the turn of the calendar year through to external papers, with mocks, internal assessment deadlines and the Extended Essay all landing on the same households. This is where a weekly timetable has to become a fortnightly plan agreed in advance, because improvising in that stretch means cancelling.

A practical instruction for the first week of term. Ask your child to write every internal deadline for the year on a single page, then photograph it and send it to the tutor. Most students cannot produce that page, and producing it is frequently the most valuable hour of the first month. A home tuition timetable built against that page survives; one built against the tutor's availability alone does not.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for an IB student in Dadar?
paragraphs: Home first, and the argument is about information rather than comfort. A tutor in your flat sees things that decide the diagnosis: the notebook with four crossed-out attempts above the answer, the phone face-up beside the paper, the study corner that is actually a shared dining table, the younger sibling's television through a thin wall. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Dadar households hire for a weekly visit is being paid partly to notice those things. None of them is visible on a screen, and all of them change what should be recommended.

Online earns its place in three specific situations. A scarce subject, where the right Business Management or Psychology teacher for your board does not live in South Mumbai at all. Short high-frequency contact, where three thirty-minute slots across a week beat one long block because retrieval needs spacing and nobody travels across Mumbai for half an hour. And the monsoon, where a Thursday evening that would have been cancelled simply moves to a screen. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Dadar is a legitimate first choice for a DP2 student grinding through past papers.

Hybrid is where most households here settle by the second term, usually without having planned it. One longer visit for teaching and marking, one short online slot for a doubt-clearing conversation before a test or a draft deadline. For internally assessed work the pattern is better still: the student sends a draft, the tutor reads it offline and annotates it, and the online slot is spent only on the two things that need discussing rather than on silent reading.

The honest costs on both sides. Home sessions price in a journey whether or not the quote itemises it, and in Mumbai, Maharashtra that journey is the most expensive hour of the week. Online removes it and removes something else as well: the accountability of a person physically arriving at your door, which for a student avoiding a subject is a real loss. Primary Years and early Middle Years children should be taught at home almost without exception.

sections.heading: Letting a stranger into your flat: what we check and what you should
paragraphs: Three checks happen before a profile reaches you, and we would rather you know their limits than assume something broader. Identity is verified against government photo identification. Qualification is verified against the original degree certificate, not a line on a form. Programme experience is tested in conversation detailed enough to separate a teacher who has taken cohorts through internal assessment moderation from one who has read about it. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dadar who cannot describe how an IA is moderated does not reach your shortlist.

What no document establishes is whether this person works in your home. That is a different question from competence and you should treat it as one. The checks that belong to you are practical: does the tutor arrive within the agreed window, set up without needing to be hosted, decline tea politely and get to work, leave the table as they found it, and tell you something specific on the way out. A tutor who needs managing is a tutor who will be an extra household chore by the third month.

Four questions for the call. Which programme and level have you taught most recently, and across how many cohorts? What will you do, concretely, in the first session? How and how often will you report progress to me? And what would make you tell me this arrangement is not working? The fourth question separates professionals from fee collectors, because a tutor who has never considered declining a student will keep attending long after the usefulness has gone.

Two things should end the conversation. A tutor who speaks about results in aggregate rather than about your child's specific gaps. And anyone who indicates a particular grade before the diagnostic. No honest tutor offers a guaranteed grade; too much of the outcome sits outside a weekly session. We do not guarantee grades either. If a tutor claims a relationship with your child's school, verify it with the school rather than with us, and treat the claim itself as a mark against them.

sections.heading: What actually happens in ninety minutes of home tuition in Dadar
paragraphs: A good session has a shape, and knowing the shape lets you tell within three visits whether you have hired well. The first ten minutes are not teaching. They are a check on the week: what was set, what was done, what was skipped and why. A tutor who skips this step and opens the textbook immediately is teaching a syllabus rather than a student. The next fifteen minutes are usually retrieval, meaning questions on material covered two or three weeks ago rather than last week, because spacing is what moves knowledge into usable memory.

The long middle, roughly forty to fifty minutes, is the actual work, and it should look uncomfortable. Your child should be writing more than the tutor is talking. The tutor should be interrupting, asking how a step was reached, and occasionally letting a wrong answer run for two lines so the student finds the error herself. A session where the tutor explains fluently for forty minutes while the student nods is a lecture and will not move a mark sheet. If you walk past and hear only one voice, something is wrong.

The last fifteen minutes set the week: specific work, with a quantity and a deadline, written down where the student will see it. Then a thirty-second handover to the parent, which should name one thing that went well and one thing to watch. That handover is the part most tutors skip and the part you should insist on, because it is your only regular window into a relationship you are paying for but not sitting inside.

What the household contributes is smaller than parents fear and more specific than they expect. A table with a chair on each side, in a room with a door that closes. No television audible. The phone out of the room, not face-down on the table. Water on the table before the session rather than a tea tray interrupting it at the forty-minute mark. And a parent who does not sit in for a DP student and does stay within earshot for a PYP one. The IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dadar that works is boringly consistent on all five.

sections.heading: What a year of IB home classes in Mumbai realistically changes
paragraphs: At four weeks you are testing fit, not results, and four signals tell you where you stand. The tutor can describe the weak areas more precisely than the school report did. Your child can say what she is working on without checking a notebook. The notebook shows method rather than answers. And work set between sessions is being done most weeks without a fight. Missing all four at week four means the match is wrong, and in this catchment a re-match takes about a week.

At one term, twelve to fourteen sessions, the first real movement appears and it is rarely where parents look for it. In IB subjects the earliest gains come from command terms and structure: a student who writes everything she knows in answer to an explain question is losing marks she has already earned. Internal assessment work is the other early win, because a draft read by an outsider improves on the next pass in a way self-review never does. Content gains come later and more slowly.

Across a full year the honest answer is a range. Some students move substantially. Some move one grade. Some hold a grade that was sliding, which is the hardest of the three to achieve and looks from outside like nothing happened. The IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Dadar you will have paid across that year buy contact hours and an outside reader, not an outcome. We do not publish success rates and we do not guarantee grades, because an average across unlike students tells you nothing usable about your own child.

The failure mode to watch for is comfort. A long-running arrangement where everybody likes each other and nothing is being demanded is the most expensive form of tutoring there is, and it is invisible because nobody complains. Twice a year, ask for the three current topics, the evidence of movement on each, and the plan for the next month. A tutor who answers in ninety seconds is working. A tutor who talks about confidence and effort is attending.

paragraphs: Do four things this week and the first session will be worth what you pay for it. Choose the room and the table, and tell your child which it is rather than deciding on the evening. Call whoever you prefer and ask the logistics questions as well as the teaching ones: arrival window, what happens if a session is missed with notice, how progress will be reported, and whether they already teach another family in Dadar, Matunga, Dadar Parsi Colony or Prabhadevi.

The first session is paid and diagnostic. The tutor will work across topics rather than through a chapter, interrupt frequently, and leave with two or three named weaknesses and a plan for the first month. A written note follows within a day covering what was found, what the first four weeks will target, how much work to expect between sessions and when the next report will come.

Nothing after that is locked. If the tutor is wrong for your household, say so in week two or three and we re-match from the same shortlist. Evening slots between six and eight are the most requested and fill first, so ask early in the term. Tutors coming by train also need no parking, which removes a recurring friction in older buildings here.

faqs.question: Do I need to sit in on the home tuition sessions?
faqs.answer: For the first session yes, for the rest it depends on age. Attending the first lets you see how the tutor opens, whether your child speaks or goes quiet, and whether the room works. After that, a Primary Years child benefits from a parent within earshot, a Middle Years student usually does better with an adult in the flat but not the room, and a Diploma student is almost always worse off with a parent present. What you should insist on at every age is the short handover at the end of the session.

faqs.question: Where should the sessions happen in a small Mumbai flat?
faqs.answer: A table with two chairs facing each other, in a room with a door that closes, is the whole requirement. A dining table works if the television is off and the kitchen traffic stops for the duration. A bedroom desk works if the bed is not in the student's eyeline. What does not work is a sofa with a laptop, or a shared table with a sibling doing homework alongside. The single most common avoidable cause of a failed arrangement in Dadar flats is that nobody decided in advance where the sessions would happen.

faqs.question: What does IB and IGCSE home tuition cost in this area?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and a quote given before anyone asks about your subject is a guess. Cost moves on programme and level, subject scarcity, how close you are to assessment deadlines, session length and weekly frequency, and travel. The interchange compresses only the last of those, which is why comparable tutors are often less expensive here than across the island. Ask any tutor whether the rate changes nearer to examinations and whether reading drafts between sessions is included, because those two answers explain most of the variation between quotes.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does one subject need?
faqs.answer: One a week is the normal starting point, rising to two around mocks and internal assessment deadlines. If a tutor proposes three weekly sessions in a single subject from the start, ask why. Usually it means the level is wrong, there is a gap from the previous programme that nobody has addressed, or the student is doing no independent work between sessions. A good tutor will say that rather than take the extra booking, which is one reason we ask candidates what would make them decline a student.

faqs.question: What happens if we miss a session because of school or travel?
faqs.answer: Agree the policy on the first call rather than discovering it in October. Most tutors will reschedule with twenty-four hours of notice and charge for a same-day cancellation, which is reasonable given they have already committed the journey and declined another booking. What matters more is the pattern: two missed sessions in a term is life, four is a timetable that does not fit your household and should be rebuilt rather than apologised for. Tell us if that happens and we will move the slot.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both my children?
faqs.answer: Within a programme, often yes, and the second slot usually costs less because the journey is already made. Two Diploma students in related subjects, or two Middle Years children in the same subject group, work well with one tutor. A Primary Years child and a Diploma student do not, and asking one person to cover both normally means the younger one is being minded rather than taught. Where the subjects are close, as with Mathematics and Physics, one tutor across two siblings is efficient and common in households here.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work as well for IB students?
faqs.answer: For revision, scarce subjects and draft discussion, it is comparable and sometimes better. For diagnosis and for younger children, it is clearly worse. A tutor in the room reads the notebook, the crossed-out attempts and the study environment, and all three carry information a screen hides. Where online genuinely wins is reliability and spacing: a monsoon evening that would be cancelled still happens, and three short sessions across a week beat one long one for retrieval. Most Diploma households in Mumbai end up running both modes together.

faqs.question: My daughter is moving from MYP into DP. What should home tuition focus on?
faqs.answer: Independent working habits, not content. The jump that unsettles students is volume and self-management rather than conceptual difficulty: taking notes that are usable three months later, meeting a draft deadline without being chased, reading a mark scheme and understanding what it rewards. Six or eight sessions over a summer, aimed at the subjects she will take at Higher Level, change her first Diploma term considerably. A sibling page covers Middle Years tutoring in detail if that is still where she is.

faqs.question: What if there is no progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions before changing anything: which topics have been worked on, what evidence of movement exists, and what the next four weeks will cover. If the tutor cannot answer concretely, the problem is diagnosis and you should re-match. If the answers are solid but no grade has moved, that is often timing, because technique gains appear on a mark sheet before content gains do. Tell us either way. Re-matching from an existing shortlist in Dadar, Matunga or Prabhadevi is usually a one-week change rather than a restart.

faqs.question: Are your tutors associated with Don Bosco International School or JBCN International School, Parel?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and has no affiliation with Don Bosco International School, JBCN International School, Parel, or any other school mentioned here. We name local schools because that is where children in this part of Mumbai study and because their internal calendars shape the tuition year. If a tutor claims a connection to your child's school, verify it with the school directly and treat the claim with suspicion. We also do not guarantee grades, and no tutor matched here may promise one.

paragraphs: IB Gram reads your brief, shortlists two or three verified tutors who already teach that board and that year group, and arranges a free discovery call before a single lesson is booked. sections.heading: IB and IGCSE side by side: what each board asks of a Dahisar student
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) and the International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) are not two names for the same thing, and a tutor who treats them that way will waste your money. The IB runs as a continuum: the Primary Years Programme (PYP) in the early years, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) through the middle school, then the Diploma Programme (DP) in the final two years. IGCSE is a two-year qualification offered in Mumbai by Cambridge International Education and by Pearson Edexcel, sat subject by subject, with each subject standing on its own.

That structural difference changes what tuition looks like week to week. An MYP student is assessed against published criteria, so the useful question in a session is "which criterion is this task actually testing, and what does the next band up look like in your handwriting?" An IGCSE student is assessed by terminal papers, so the useful question is "what is this command word asking you to produce, and how many marks is the examiner able to award for what you have written?" A tutor who brings MYP criterion language into IGCSE revision, or past-paper drilling into a Year 7 MYP task, is working against the school.

Dahisar households frequently contain both. One child may be in IB PYP or MYP at a school in Dahisar East while an older sibling sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel IGCSE papers. Parents searching for an IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai wide often assume one person covers everything. There is no single all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Dahisar, and anyone who claims to be one deserves a second look rather than a booking. What is realistic is one tutor covering one board for one child well, and a second match for the other.

Board structures are also revised on the boards' own cycles. Subject lists, assessment components and tier names move, and a page written today can be out of date for the year your child actually sits. Treat your school's own coordinator and the current published subject guide as the authority on structure, and treat a tutor as the person who gets the work done inside it.

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards, and the internal assessments each one carries
paragraphs: Subject choice is the single decision that most changes how hard the next two years feel, and it is made at an age when children choose by teacher rather than by syllabus. Across both boards the pattern in the Western Suburbs is consistent: a student picks the science her friends picked, discovers in term two that the paper rewards a kind of writing she has never practised, and the report that follows is the reason a parent starts looking for an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dahisar.

On the IB side, every DP subject carries an Internal Assessment (IA) of some kind, plus the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) sitting across the whole Diploma. Those pieces are drafted at home, under a deadline set by the school rather than the board, and they are where a home tutor earns their fee: not writing the thing, but turning a vague research question into one that can actually be answered with the data a student in Mumbai can collect. In MYP the equivalent pressure is the criterion-marked task and, in the senior MYP years, the personal project.

On the IGCSE side the internal component varies by subject and by board. Some subjects carry coursework, some substitute an alternative-to-practical paper, and some are assessed entirely by written papers. Core and Extended tiers exist in several Cambridge subjects and the choice between them is consequential, because the ceiling differs. A tutor's first job in a new IGCSE match is to confirm which tier the school has entered the student for, which syllabus code the school is teaching, and whether the coursework component applies, before planning anything.

Where a subject is scarce, say a second language at HL or a humanities subject with a small cohort, a request for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai wide gets split into separate subject matches rather than handed to one generalist. That is slower to arrange and more honest. A generalist can hold a Year 9 together across four subjects; a Year 12 HL candidate needs someone who has marked that paper.

sections.heading: Dahisar, Borivali East, Borivali West and Mira Road: the real matching radius
paragraphs: A tutor booked for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dahisar realistically also covers Borivali East, Borivali West and Mira Road, and that radius is set by the road, not by goodwill. Dahisar is the last stop on the Western Line inside Mumbai, Maharashtra, before Mira Road begins, and the Dahisar–Western Express Highway corridor is the spine everything hangs off. Dahisar station and the Metro Lines 2A and 7 alignment running down towards Andheri and Gundavali have changed the north-south journey more than any amount of optimism about Link Road.

The Western Suburbs run north-south, so matching along the line works and matching across it does not. A tutor living near Kandivali or Borivali West reaches a flat off the highway in Dahisar in a short, predictable hop. A tutor coming up from Bandra or Khar is quick off-peak and painful at six in the evening, which is exactly when your child is free. This is why we push back on a parent who has found a profile they like in Santacruz: the first three weeks will work and the fourth will start arriving late.

Mira Road deserves its own sentence because the municipal boundary sits between it and Dahisar, and crossing it on a weekday evening is a different proposition from the map's suggestion. Families on the Mira Road side are often better matched with a tutor already working that stretch than with one based south of Dahisar station. Borivali East, by contrast, behaves almost as one catchment with Dahisar for scheduling purposes, and the two share most of the tutor pool for IB and IGCSE work.

Parents who type "IB and IGCSE tutors near me Dahisar" into Google are asking a travel question disguised as a search query. The answer we give is a travel answer: name the two evenings, name the building and the nearest landmark off the highway, and we will shortlist from the pool that can hold that slot in April as reliably as in July. Home tuition across this part of Mumbai lives or dies on whether the journey is repeatable.

sections.heading: Which months are the real pressure points in a Mumbai IB and IGCSE school year?
paragraphs: The pressure points are the weeks when an internal deadline and a mock paper collide, and in Mumbai that happens twice: once after the Diwali break, when coursework and IA drafts come due against the first serious set of mocks, and again in the run-up to the main examination series in the first half of the calendar year. Your school's published calendar is the only authority on the actual dates, and it differs between schools in the same suburb, so get it in writing in June and plan tuition backwards from it.

Dahisar carries genuine IB demand for a reason that surprises people who think of international schooling as a South Mumbai and Bandra Kurla Complex phenomenon. Singapore International School sits at Dahisar East, which is why a locality at the city's northern edge has real IB PYP and MYP families rather than a handful of commuters. JBCN International School, Borivali adds both IB and IGCSE cohorts a short hop down the highway. The practical effect is that a tutor working Dahisar can build a full week here instead of treating it as an outpost, and that is why the tutor pool holds up this far north.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Singapore International School, with JBCN International School, Borivali, or with any other school named anywhere on this page. We name them because their calendars set your term, not because we have a relationship with them. If a tutoring service implies otherwise, ask them to put the relationship in writing and watch what happens.

The calendar effect on matching is blunt. Requests for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Dahisar families need spike twice a year, and the good tutors in a scarce subject are gone first. A parent who calls in June about a Year 11 IGCSE student has a real choice of profiles. A parent who calls three weeks before a mock series is choosing from whoever is left, and we will tell you that rather than pretend the shortlist is the same one.

sections.heading: Should you book home tuition, online, or a mix in Dahisar?
paragraphs: Book home tuition first if the student is below the senior years or cannot yet work unsupervised for forty minutes; book online if the subject is scarce and the right specialist is simply not available on your side of the city. Most families arranging IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dahisar end up with a hybrid by the second term, and that is not a compromise, it is usually the correct answer for a two-board household with one free evening.

Home classes buy you three things that a screen does not. The tutor sees the actual study space, which in a Mumbai flat is often a dining table shared with a younger sibling, and can change it. The tutor sees the schoolbag, which is where unmarked worksheets and unread feedback hide. And the student cannot quietly disengage. For a Year 9 or Year 10 student who has not yet learned to sit with a hard question, the physical presence of an adult at the table is doing most of the work, and no amount of good software replaces it.

Online is the wrong choice for a Year 9 student who cannot yet work alone, and the right choice for a Year 12 Higher Level candidate who needs the one person in the city who has marked that paper. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Dahisar also solves the April problem, when the Western Express Highway stops cooperating and a 6pm slot becomes a 6:40 slot. The honest trade-off is handwriting: diagrams, working out and annotated past papers are harder to supervise through a camera, and a tutor who does not ask for a photograph of the page at the end of each session is not really marking anything.

The hybrid pattern that holds up here is one home session a week for the subject that needs supervision plus one online session for the scarce subject, with the online slot earlier in the evening because nobody has to travel to it. Families searching for an IB and IGCSE private tutor Dahisar side usually mean one-to-one at their own table, and that is what we arrange by default. We only propose online when it genuinely produces a better tutor.

sections.heading: How tutors are verified, and what you should still check yourself in Mumbai
paragraphs: Verification at IB Gram means government photo identity confirmed, qualifications seen rather than claimed, a subject-level conversation with someone who knows the syllabus, and prior teaching or tutoring history checked where it exists. That gets you a tutor who is who they say they are and knows the subject. It does not tell you whether this particular adult will work with your particular child, and no screening process anywhere can. That part is what the free discovery call is for, and it is why we send two or three profiles rather than one.

What you should check yourself takes about four minutes on the call. Ask which board and which syllabus code they last taught this subject under, and listen for whether the answer is specific. Ask what they would do in session one, and be suspicious of anyone who says they will "assess the student" without saying how. Ask what they will send you after a month. Ask directly whether they teach Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel, or both, because a tutor who has only ever taught one board and says both are the same has told you something useful.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, quotes a success rate, or claims to be the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Dahisar. We do not guarantee grades and we do not publish pass percentages, because the only honest version of that number would need to control for the student, the school and the board, and nobody is doing that arithmetic. A tutor who promises a specific grade in a first conversation is telling you how they sell, not how they teach.

The other check is a safeguarding one and it is yours to make, not ours. Lessons for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dahisar should happen in a shared room with a door open and an adult somewhere in the flat, not behind a closed bedroom door. A professional tutor expects this and will often suggest it before you do. Any tutor who finds it awkward has answered a question you should have asked.

sections.heading: Core, Extended, Higher Level, Standard Level: the Dahisar decision that sets up two years
paragraphs: Two tier decisions cause more late-night searching in this suburb than any other academic problem: whether a Cambridge IGCSE student is entered for Core or Extended, and whether a DP student takes a subject at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL). Both are made months before the consequences show up, both are reversible only inside a window the school controls, and both are frequently made on the basis of how a child felt in term one rather than what the papers actually demand.

The Core and Extended question is really a question about ceilings and about risk. Extended covers more content and reaches higher grades; Core is narrower and caps lower. A student placed on Extended who is not coping will produce worse marks than the same student on Core, and a student parked on Core who could have coped has had a university pathway quietly narrowed for her. The useful tutoring intervention is not persuasion, it is evidence: four weeks of marked Extended questions in the student's own handwriting, shown to the school, which is a far better argument than a parent's conviction.

The HL and SL question is about the Internal Assessment and about time. An HL subject carries a heavier conceptual load and, in most subjects, a more demanding internal component, and a DP2 student in Dahisar with three HLs discovers in the post-Diwali weeks that three internal assessments, the Extended Essay and a Theory of Knowledge (TOK) deadline all want the same fortnight. The sensible test is not "can she do HL maths", it is "can she do HL maths in the same term as two other HL internal assessments and a six-forty commute".

This is also where the two-board household gets genuinely difficult. A Year 11 IGCSE student choosing DP subjects for next year is making the tier decision for two boards at once: which IGCSE tier she sits now, and which DP level she enters later, with the first partly determining the second. A tutor who holds both halves of that conversation is worth more than two tutors who each hold one. Where one person cannot cover both subjects, we at least brief both tutors on the same plan.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not expect a grade to move, and if it has, be mildly suspicious of the test it moved on. What you should see at four weeks is diagnostic: a written note from the tutor naming two or three specific weaknesses, evidence that the student can now attempt a question type she previously skipped, and homework coming back marked rather than merely completed. If a month of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dahisar has produced no written account of what is wrong, the tutor has been filling time.

At one term the honest marker is whether the student's own behaviour has changed. Does she start a question she does not immediately understand, or does she still wait? Does she bring her own list of confusions to the session? Has the school's feedback shifted from "needs to show working" to something more specific? Grades usually move on the second internal assessment or the second mock, not the first, because the first one largely measures what was already in place when tuition started.

At one exam cycle you will know, and you may not like the answer. Some students move two grades, some move one, some hold a grade they were going to lose, and that last outcome is real progress that looks like nothing on paper. We do not guarantee grades and will not quote a figure for how often a student improves, because the student, the school and the subject do more of the work than the tutor does. What we will do is replace a match that is not working, at any point, without an argument.

The limits are worth saying plainly. A tutor cannot fix a subject chosen wrongly two years ago, cannot replace a teacher the student has stopped listening to, and cannot create four hours of study a week that the student does not have. Home tuition in Mumbai works best as a correction to a specific, named problem. Where the problem is actually workload, timetable or subject fit, the right advice is a conversation with the school, and we will say so even though it loses us the booking.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dahisar: what to have ready
paragraphs: Have four things ready and the first match usually lands inside a few days: the board and syllabus code, the most recent school report or marked paper, the two evenings that are genuinely free, and your building's location relative to the Western Express Highway or Dahisar station. The report matters more than parents expect. A tutor reading a real teacher's comment learns more in two minutes than from twenty minutes of a parent's summary, and it changes which profiles we shortlist.

Session one, done properly, is a diagnosis rather than a lesson. A good tutor spends it watching the student attempt work she has already been set, because that is where the error pattern lives. Expect them to ask for her notebook, her last marked paper and her textbook, to work through two or three questions while narrating nothing and listening to everything, and to end by telling you both what they think the actual problem is. Expect, at the end, a plan for the next three sessions that you can repeat back.

What should not happen in session one is a sales pitch for a package, a diagnostic test the tutor sells separately, or a promise about an outcome. Also not a lecture: if the tutor talked for fifty minutes of an hour, the student has learned how clever the tutor is. Families comparing an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dahisar against a nearby group class should ask the group class the same question about session one and compare the answers.

After that, the rhythm is simple and deliberately boring. Weekly sessions at a fixed slot, homework set and marked, a short written review at the two-to-four week mark, and a decision point at the end of the first month where you continue, change tutor, or stop. There is no lock-in. A family that stops after three weeks because the problem turned out to be a timetable clash has used this service correctly.

Name two evenings that are genuinely free, not theoretically free

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Dahisar actually depend on?
faqs.answer: IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Dahisar depend on five things, and we will not quote a price list because anyone who does is guessing about your case. Board and level come first: a Diploma Programme Higher Level subject costs more than a Year 9 Middle Years Programme subject because fewer tutors can teach it. Then subject scarcity, which is why a second language or a specialist humanities subject sits above mainstream science. Then travel distance and the time of your slot, since a 6pm booking off the Western Express Highway costs a tutor more of the evening than a 4pm one. Then session length and frequency.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Dahisar from Borivali or Andheri for an evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes from Borivali, usually yes from Kandivali and Malad, and honestly it depends from Andheri. The Western Line and the Metro Lines 2A and 7 alignment have made the Andheri run workable, but a 6pm weekday slot in Dahisar means leaving Andheri in the worst part of the peak, and a match that depends on that journey tends to drift late by the second month. We prefer to shortlist from Dahisar, Borivali East, Borivali West and Mira Road for weekday evening bookings, and open the radius wider for weekend mornings when the highway behaves.

faqs.question: Does someone need to be at home while the home tuition session runs?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, though not in the room. This is a safeguarding norm rather than a rule we invented, and professional tutors in Mumbai expect it. Keep the session in a shared space with the door open, the dining table or a study corner rather than a bedroom. A parent sitting in on every session usually makes things worse: the student performs for the parent instead of working, and the tutor cannot see the honest version of the mistake. Drop in at the end, ask the tutor what happened, and read the homework they set.

faqs.question: My son is in IGCSE Year 11 and wants to do the IB Diploma. Can one tutor cover both?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking for specifically, because this transition is the hardest handover in the two-board household. A tutor who has taught both Cambridge IGCSE and the Diploma Programme can use the Year 11 year to build the habits the Diploma actually needs: independent reading, a research question that can be answered, written work produced to a deadline the student set herself. Where a single tutor cannot cover both subjects to the required depth, we match separately and brief both tutors on the same plan, which is slower to set up and more honest than pretending one person covers everything.

faqs.question: Is online tuition good enough for a Year 9 student, or is home tuition better?
faqs.answer: For most Year 9 students, home tuition is better, and we will say so even when an online tutor would be easier to arrange. A fourteen-year-old who has not yet learned to sit with a question she cannot do needs an adult at the table, not an adult on a screen. Online becomes the right answer two or three years later, when the student can work unsupervised and the limiting factor is finding someone who has actually marked that Higher Level paper. The exception is a short online bridge while we find the right local match.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace the match, with no argument and no fee for the switch. Three sessions is a reasonable point to judge: enough for a diagnosis to exist, not enough to have lost a term. What helps is being specific about why, because "it isn't working" and "he explains well but never marks the homework" lead to very different replacements. Most failed matches here are not about competence, they are about pace or personality, and both are fixable by changing the person. Roughly one in a handful of matches gets changed, and nobody treats it as a complaint.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask the tutor for the written diagnosis first, because the absence of that document is the real problem more often than the absence of progress. A month should produce a named list of weaknesses and evidence that the student now attempts question types she used to skip, even if no grade has moved. If the tutor cannot produce that, change the tutor. If the tutor can produce it and the school's feedback still has not shifted, the issue may be workload or subject fit rather than teaching, and that is a conversation with the school.

faqs.question: Do you cover Mira Road and Borivali East as well as Dahisar?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they behave differently for scheduling. Borivali East and Dahisar share most of the same tutor pool and a booking in one is usually fillable from the other with no travel penalty. Mira Road sits across the municipal boundary and crossing it on a weekday evening is slower than the map suggests, so Mira Road families are generally matched with a tutor already working that side rather than one based south of Dahisar station. Borivali West is comfortable for both. Tell us the building and the nearest landmark and we will be straight about who can hold the slot.

faqs.question: Which subjects are hardest to staff this far north in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Second languages at Higher Level, specialist humanities with small cohorts, and anything requiring experience of a specific internal assessment are the hard ones in Dahisar. Mainstream mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, economics and English are straightforward at both boards. The scarcity is geographic rather than absolute: the tutor exists in Mumbai, just not within a repeatable weekday-evening drive of the Dahisar–Western Express Highway corridor. For those subjects we usually propose an online specialist, and we say so at the shortlist stage rather than after you have paid for a month.

faqs.question: My daughter is in IB PYP at a school in Dahisar East. Is home tuition appropriate that young?
faqs.answer: Often it is not, and that is the honest answer even though PYP enquiries from Dahisar East are common. A Primary Years Programme child who is reading and inquiring happily does not need a tutor, she needs time. Home classes make sense at that age for a specific, named gap: a child who has moved boards mid-year, one who is behind in number fluency or decoding, or one learning in English at school and another language at home. If you cannot name the gap in a sentence, wait a term and talk to the class teacher.

faqs.question: Can we book two children on different boards in the same evening at our building?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most common requests we get in this part of the Western Suburbs. Two back-to-back one-to-one sessions in the same flat works well when the subjects are close enough that one tutor covers both, and it halves the travel problem that makes weekday evenings hard here. Where the boards or levels are too far apart, the alternative is two tutors on two different evenings, or one home session and one online. What does not work is teaching two children of different ages together to save an hour.

paragraphs: We take the two children separately and only then look for an overlap, because the reverse order produces a compromise that suits neither. For the household we want one more thing: which evenings are genuinely free for two consecutive hours, because a shared journey is the only reason a good tutor anywhere in Mumbai will take two siblings rather than two separate families.

Overlap is realistic in Mathematics and the sciences up to about the end of Year 11 and the Middle Years Programme. A strong graduate teacher can handle a Year 10 Cambridge mathematics syllabus and a Middle Years Programme mathematics group in consecutive hours without either child being short-changed. Overlap stops being realistic at Higher Level in the Diploma Programme, where the subject knowledge needed is narrower and deeper, and a tutor who claims both ends of that range is usually strongest in the middle of it.

What you get back is either one name with two slots, or two names with a note explaining why splitting is the better call. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dombivli covering two children is genuinely more convenient, and in about half the households we see it is also the right answer. In the other half the younger child ends up supervised rather than taught, and nobody notices until the reports arrive.

sections.heading: One house, two boards: how do the programmes actually differ?
paragraphs: They differ most in what a student is asked to produce alone. The International General Certificate of Secondary Education is largely a set of written examinations taken at the end of a two-year course, with coursework or practical components in some subjects, and it rewards a student who can answer a well-defined question accurately under time pressure. The International Baccalaureate (IB) spreads assessment across the programme: the Middle Years Programme (MYP) marks work against published criteria throughout, and the Diploma Programme (DP) adds an Internal Assessment (IA) in most subjects, plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE).

That difference changes what tutoring looks like in the same house. For the IGCSE child the tutor's work is mostly precision: command words, method marks, paper discipline, finishing on time. For the IB child the tutor's work is mostly design and judgement: choosing a workable research question, justifying a method, structuring an argument that is not simply correct but defensible. A tutor who treats the second child like the first will produce tidy, accurate work that sits in the middle bands and nobody will be able to say why.

Levels and tiers are the other split. Several Cambridge syllabuses are tiered, and the route chosen in Year 9 sets the accessible grade range, so the decision needs to be made with the subject teacher in writing before entries close. The Diploma Programme instead asks for Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices across six subjects, and the step from Standard to Higher is a change in what questions may assume rather than extra chapters. Both decisions get made at the wrong moment in most Mumbai schools: during a busy term, on the basis of one test.

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards, and the coursework each one sets
paragraphs: Mathematics and the sciences are where a two-board household shares a tutor most successfully, and the reason is that the content genuinely overlaps even when the assessment does not. Algebraic fluency, graph interpretation and experimental reasoning sit under both boards, so a tutor working with a Year 10 student on reverse percentages in one hour and an MYP student on the same skill in the next is not switching subjects, only switching marking conventions. English, Economics and the humanities overlap much less, because what counts as a good answer differs sharply.

Coursework is the part families underestimate on both boards. Where an IGCSE syllabus carries a coursework or practical component it is prepared at school over weeks, marked there against published criteria and moderated by the board. The IB equivalents run longer and demand more independence: a science investigation, a mathematics exploration, a long essay with a supervisor. In both cases the draft deadline is the real deadline, and a student who treats it as provisional has given away marks that cost nothing. The all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Dombivli who only ever sees finished work has no useful view of this.

Scarcity is the practical constraint on this belt. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, English and Economics have a real local pool across both boards. Arts, Psychology, Business, Computer Science and most second languages do not, and the thin end gets thinner at Higher Level. That is where a household with two children usually ends up mixing a local tutor for the crowded subjects with an online specialist for the thin one, rather than insisting that one person in Mumbai, Maharashtra cover everything.
Ask your school coordinator for the current syllabus documents on both boards, since Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel and the IB all revise content and assessment on their own cycles.

sections.heading: Sharing one tutor across Dombivli, Kalyan, Thane West and Palava City
paragraphs: A shared journey is the economics that makes two-child tutoring work here, and it only works inside one travel cluster. Dombivli station anchors the catchment; tutors come in on the Central Line and take an auto for the last stretch. Kalyan sits next door. The Palava City towers are the easiest address of all to staff, because several international-board families live close enough together that a tutor can fill an evening without moving far, which is why sibling pairs there are rarely a scheduling problem.

Thane West is the outer limit and the reason is the road rather than the distance. Thane runs eastward from its own station along Pokhran Road and Majiwada before opening onto Ghodbunder Road, and that final leg is where evenings disappear: the run towards Kasarvadavali takes about twenty minutes mid-afternoon and close to an hour once the peak builds. A tutor crossing that leg before reaching Dombivli will be on their third hour of travelling by the time your second child sits down.

Which is why we ask a question that sounds intrusive and is not. Where are your other students this term? An IB and IGCSE private tutor Dombivli parents can keep for two years is one whose whole evening lives on this belt. The arrangement that fails is a tutor with one student here, one in Kalyan and one at the far end of Ghodbunder Road, and it fails in week six, usually with the second sibling's slot being the one quietly dropped.

Parents also search IB and IGCSE tutors near me Dombivli and get coaching centres with group timetables. For two children on two different boards, a centre is rarely the answer: the two of them need different rooms at the same hour, which is exactly what home tuition across this part of Mumbai solves.

sections.heading: Two school calendars colliding in one Dombivli household
paragraphs: January is the month that breaks two-child households, and it is predictable enough to plan for in September. The international-board schools here are outward, in Thane and Palava, at places such as Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School and NES International School, and their calendars run broadly in parallel: mock examinations for the Year 11 child land in the same few weeks as final internal assessment submissions, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay for a Diploma Programme sibling. One evening, two crises, one tutor.

The practical answer is to front-load. Families who book in September, run a light two-hour week per child through the first term and raise the intensity only in December come through January intact. Families who book in January are asking a tutor to do triage for two children at once, and the honest outcome is that one child gets the better service. Nobody says which one at the time, but the reports in March make it clear.

The school day leaves little room either. A child who leaves Dombivli before seven for a school in Thane or Palava is home around five, and with two children travelling the house runs on one usable weekday hour each. That is why consecutive back-to-back slots, one tutor and a parent who protects the window matter more here than the identity of the tutor. IB Gram is an independent platform and has no affiliation with either school named here; they appear because their calendars set the pressure points families actually live with.

Weekends do disproportionate work in a two-board house. Two longer Saturday sessions with rested children beat four tired weekday hours, and they also make the trip worthwhile for a specialist who would not come for a single hour.

sections.heading: Does home tuition still work when two children need it in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Yes, and it works better than the alternatives for exactly this situation, with one condition: the children must be in different rooms. The home tuition we arrange in Mumbai for sibling pairs runs as consecutive hours, not a joint session, because a joint session becomes a lesson pitched at the midpoint and both children lose. The younger one listens to material they cannot use and the older one revises material they already have. Parents often propose the joint hour to save money, and it is the one shortcut we argue against consistently.

Online earns its place for the thin subject rather than for the whole arrangement. If your Year 10 child needs Cambridge Business Studies and no local specialist exists on this belt, an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Dombivli with genuine syllabus experience is better than a nearby generalist teaching it for the first time. Online is also the fallback that saves the week when one child is ill or on a school trip. It is the wrong medium for a child below Year 9 who cannot yet work alone for twenty minutes.

Hybrid is the realistic shape for most two-board households, and the cost is coordination rather than money. One tutor in the house for the shared subjects, one online specialist for the thin one, and a named adult who reads both sets of session notes. Where nobody can do that, take one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents commonly ask for and accept less depth at the top end. Four tutors across two children with no coordinator is the most expensive configuration we see, and it is usually assembled by accident.

sections.heading: Can one tutor really be verified for both boards?
paragraphs: Only for the boards and stages they have actually taught, and we state them separately on the profile for that reason. Verification covers identity from a government photo identity document, the degree certificate for the subject proposed, and references from families the tutor has taught previously. What goes on the profile is specific: which board, which syllabus codes or programme stage, which years, and when. A tutor listed for Cambridge Mathematics and the Middle Years Programme has shown us both; one listed for a single board has shown us one.

Your own check is quicker and better. Hand the tutor one marked paper from each child and ask them to say where the marks went in both. For the IGCSE paper you want to hear about command words, missing units and absent method. For the IB work you want to hear about criteria, the research question and whether the method was justified. A tutor who answers both in the same vocabulary has probably only taught one of them, and the second child is the one who will suffer for it.

Be wary of any tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or quotes a success rate for either board. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, because the examination boards mark the papers and set the boundaries. There is no single best IB and IGCSE tutor in Dombivli either, whatever a listings page implies: there is a tutor whose boards, stages and style fit these two particular children this year. Ask instead what they expect to fix in four weeks per child, and get it in writing where you can check it later.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma Programme switch, and what it costs families in Mumbai
paragraphs: The switch is harder than families expect and strong IGCSE grades do not predict it. What changes is the amount of unsupervised judgement a student must exercise. In Year 11 the questions were set, bounded and marked against a scheme; in DP1 the student is asked to choose a research question for an internal assessment, decide what evidence would answer it, justify the method and write at length without a template. A student who has succeeded by being accurate and obedient will find the first term of the Diploma Programme genuinely disorienting.

Three specific gaps show up every year. The first is long-form writing: the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay need a planning habit nobody taught in Year 11, and more past papers will not supply it. The second is depth at Higher Level, where a question may present an unfamiliar situation and expect the student to select the model themselves. The third is time management across six subjects plus the core, which is a different problem from managing eight examination subjects that all end at once.

This is where IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dombivli has its clearest value, because the transition term is short and the habits formed in it last two years. The most useful work in DP1 is not content coverage: it is supervised practice at designing a question, drafting badly, and revising. A tutor who can only teach content will keep the student comfortable through DP1 and leave the internal assessment to collapse in DP2, which is the commonest version of this story we hear from Mumbai families.

Fees across two children follow the ordinary drivers, with one addition. sections.heading: What should a term of home classes change for each child?
paragraphs: Judge each child against their own board and nothing else, which sounds obvious and is rarely done. For the IGCSE child, four weeks should bring annotated questions, visible method and homework done on the first reminder. For the IB child, four weeks should bring a student who can say which criterion a task is assessed against and who has started a draft early rather than the night before. Comparing the two children's progress against each other is the single most destructive thing a Mumbai household can do with tutoring.

At one term, expect movement on the agreed target for each child and nothing wider. A tutor who spent twelve weeks on examination technique has no claim on a coursework mark. Agree each child's target in writing at the start so there is something checkable at the end. A term is also when an honest tutor raises the uncomfortable conversation if it needs raising: the wrong tier for the Year 10 child, the wrong Higher Level choice for the DP1 child. In December those are solvable problems.

Across an examination cycle the only fair measure is whether each child found the papers predictable. We do not guarantee grades, publish success rates, or claim any connection with the schools named here. What is promised is a stated diagnosis per child, a named target per child, written session notes, and a replacement tutor arranged quickly when a match is wrong for either of them. The all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Dombivli parents book through us are judged on that, separately for each child.

faqs.answer: In Mathematics and the sciences up to roughly Year 11 and the Middle Years Programme, usually yes, as two consecutive hours in different rooms. It stops being realistic at Higher Level in the Diploma Programme, where the depth required narrows the pool of capable tutors sharply, and a tutor who claims the whole range comfortably is generally strongest in the middle of it. faqs.question: Should the two children share one session to save money?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the one shortcut we argue against consistently. A joint session gets pitched at the midpoint between two different boards and two different stages, so the younger child hears material they cannot use while the older one revisits work they already have. Both pay in attention and neither gets diagnosed properly. Consecutive hours with the same tutor already save the travel, which is the cost that actually matters on this belt, and they leave each child with their own hour and their own session notes.

faqs.question: My child is moving from Year 11 into DP1. What should tutoring focus on?
faqs.answer: Designing work rather than covering content, because that is what actually changes. In Year 11 the questions were set and bounded; in the Diploma Programme the student chooses a research question for an internal assessment, decides what would answer it, justifies the method and writes at length without a template. Strong IGCSE grades do not predict comfort with that. faqs.answer: Yes, and a two-hour booking is considerably easier to staff than a one-hour one, because it justifies the journey. faqs.question: How do the two boards' deadlines collide during the year?
faqs.answer: Most painfully in January. Mock examinations for a Year 11 child land in the same weeks as final internal assessment submissions, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay for a Diploma Programme sibling, and the schools in Thane and Palava run broadly parallel calendars. One evening then holds two crises. The practical defence is to front-load: book in September, run a light week per child through the first term, and raise intensity in December. Booking in January means asking a tutor to triage two children at once.

faqs.question: Do we need two different tutors for English across the two boards?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, more so than for Mathematics or the sciences. What counts as a good answer differs sharply: an IGCSE response is marked for precision against a set question, while IB work is marked against criteria that reward argument, evidence handling and sometimes comparison across texts. A tutor who teaches both in the same register will produce accurate, tidy work for the IB child that sits in the middle bands, and the reason will be invisible on the page. Worse, it changes the older child's session: students perform rather than admit confusion when a sibling is in the room, and admitting confusion is most of what a diagnostic hour is for. faqs.question: What if one tutor works for one child and not the other?

paragraphs: Start by writing down who needs what, because households asking about both boards almost always have two separate requests bundled into one message. A Year 10 student needs technique on a specific board's papers and help with an internally assessed component. A Diploma Programme student needs subject depth at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL) and supervision of an Internal Assessment (IA). Those are different jobs and sometimes different people, and treating them as one request is what produces a tutor who is adequate for both children and good for neither.

So we ask for the pair of situations separately: year group, board, subjects, and what the last report actually said in words. Then one shared question, which is the scheduling one. Two children in the same flat can often be taught back to back on one evening, and if the subjects align that halves the travel load for the tutor and changes the arithmetic for you. Where the subjects do not align, we say so rather than stretching one person across a Year 10 Chemistry paper and a Diploma Programme Economics IA in the same two hours.

Matching then runs outward along the node chain. Ulwe adjoins Dronagiri and suits a single hour. sections.heading: One family, two boards: how PYP, MYP, DP and IGCSE fit together
paragraphs: The two systems are not rivals and in Navi Mumbai they are frequently sequential rather than parallel. The International Baccalaureate runs three programmes: the Primary Years Programme (PYP) to about Year 5, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) across Years 6 to 10, and the Diploma Programme (DP) in the final two years. IGCSE is a two year qualification across Years 9 to 11, awarded by Cambridge International Education or by Pearson Edexcel. Many schools teach IGCSE in Years 9 to 11 and then move students into the Diploma Programme, which is why one child can pass through both.

That sequence explains the most common confusion we hear from families here. A parent will say their child is in the IB school and is doing Cambridge papers, and both statements are true. The school is an IB World School offering the Diploma Programme in the senior years while using IGCSE for the middle ones. The practical consequence is that a tutor needs to know which system the child is being assessed under right now, because MYP criterion marking and IGCSE mark schemes reward different things in the same subject.

Where a household genuinely runs both at once, usually with siblings, the useful mental model is this: IGCSE is content and technique measured by external papers plus internally assessed coursework, and MYP is skills measured against published criteria with no external paper. A Year 10 IGCSE student is practising for an examiner. A Year 9 MYP student is practising for a criterion. A tutor who treats both the same will give one of your children exactly the wrong feedback, and it will look like diligence.

The Diploma Programme sits above both in demand. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service, inside eighteen months. Families searching for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Dronagiri while one child is in DP2 and another in Year 10 are usually best served by accepting two tutors, because the Diploma Programme child needs subject depth and the IGCSE child needs paper discipline, and very few people carry both at a high level.

An IB World School using Cambridge papers in the middle years is normal

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards, and the coursework each one carries
paragraphs: Both boards attach internally assessed work to most subjects, and in both systems that work is where ordinary students quietly lose ground. On the IGCSE side it appears as coursework or as a practical component, with an alternative route the school chooses rather than the family. On the Diploma Programme side every subject carries an internal assessment: an investigation the student designs in the sciences, an exploration on a self chosen topic in Mathematics, recorded oral work in languages, a written investigation in the humanities. Different names, same failure mode, which is a student who can do the subject and cannot produce the artefact.

The level decisions in the two systems also rhyme without matching. IGCSE offers two tiers in several subjects, and the school normally proposes which one a student is entered for. The Diploma Programme asks for three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Both decisions get made faster than families would like and both constrain what follows. A household with children at each stage will be having both conversations within a year of each other, which is an argument for a tutor who has seen the whole arc rather than one stage of it.

A family wanting one person across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Dronagiri might reasonably claim is describing a primary school arrangement. Past Year 8, the sensible shape is two specialists: one covering Mathematics and the sciences and one covering languages or the humanities, used by both children where the subjects allow. That is also the cheapest way to get all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Dronagiri covered properly, because two focused hours beat four hours with somebody reading two different syllabuses the night before.

One warning about syllabus detail. Component structures, tier arrangements, grading scales and assessment routes are revised on each board's own cycle, and the IB and the examination boards do not revise in step. Anything printed about structure ages quickly. Take the current shape of your child's assessments from the school coordinator or the live subject guide, and treat a tutor who speaks confidently about a retired component as somebody who has not opened one recently.

IGCSE tiering and DP level choice are different decisions with the same effect
Two specialists across two children beats one generalist across four subjects

sections.heading: Covering Dronagiri, Ulwe, Panvel and Kharghar from one weekly slot
paragraphs: A household needing two children taught is in a stronger negotiating position than a household needing one, and the reason is travel. Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, each a short drive from the next on the Sion–Panvel Highway and Palm Beach Road, and tutors are matched node to node. A tutor driving in from Kharghar for ninety minutes is giving up an evening. The same drive for two consecutive sessions is a sensible use of one, and that changes who will say yes.

Ulwe adjoins the node and is the realistic source for a short single session, which suits a younger MYP or PYP child. Kharghar is where most of the experienced subject teachers live and is the usual origin for a two child evening. Panvel has the largest teaching population of the three and is worth the longer drive for a scarce Higher Level subject or an uncommon language. Beyond Belapur the tutor needs another reason to be on this side, and pulling someone across the creek from the island city for a weekday evening lesson rarely holds for a full term even with the Atal Setu.

Rail matters for the children rather than the tutor. Targhar and Bamandongri are the nearest stations, on the Harbour Line towards Panvel. The Trans-Harbour Line links Thane to Vashi, and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 runs Belapur to Pendhar. None of that is how a tutor reaches a seven o clock slot carrying two sets of past papers; they are on the road, and the road in the evening peak is the actual constraint on who is available to you.

The arrangement that holds is the one built into an existing route. Ask in the first call where else the tutor teaches on that day, and aim to be first or last on it. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dronagiri running as a two child evening block, same day, same times, every week, is the single most durable shape we see in this node. The arrangement that fails is the one assembled from two separate favours on two different evenings, because favours do not survive a monsoon week on the Sion–Panvel Highway.

sections.heading: Why do two children at the same Navi Mumbai school sit different boards?
paragraphs: Because most international schools here use one system for the middle years and another for the senior ones, so siblings two or three years apart are genuinely in different assessment worlds inside the same building. Families in this node commonly attend D.Y. Patil International School at Nerul and Ryan Global School, reached by school transport along Palm Beach Road and the Sion–Panvel Highway. IB Gram names these as local context only, has no arrangement with either, and is not affiliated with any school in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

The two calendars overlap awkwardly, and that overlap is the thing a household with two children should plan around. The academic year opens around June. IGCSE Year 11 mock examinations fall across November to January, with coursework deadlines and predicted grades for applications in the same stretch. Diploma Programme internal assessment and Extended Essay final deadlines cluster through January and February, and external papers for both systems run in the main spring and early summer series. So a household can have a Year 11 student in mocks and a DP2 student in IA deadlines in the same fortnight, which is the worst two weeks of the year in that flat.

The practical answer is sequencing rather than intensity. Decide in advance which child gets the extra session in that fortnight, and tell the tutor in October rather than in January. Families who plan that conversation early keep the arrangement stable. Families who discover the clash when it arrives end up moving both children's slots twice in a month, and a travelling tutor who loses two evenings to rescheduling starts preferring their Kharghar students, which is arithmetic rather than rudeness.

One more calendar note that applies to both boards here. The strongest local teachers fill their weekday evenings early in the academic year, so a household looking for two tutors in February is choosing from whoever is left in a pool that was never deep. Searching in June or July costs nothing and buys the ability to be wrong once. In a node this new, that single advantage matters more than any other decision a parent makes about tutoring.

sections.heading: Can one home tuition slot in Mumbai serve two children?
paragraphs: Yes if they are taught consecutively, and almost never if they are taught together. Two children at different stages in the same hour means one of them is waiting, and the one waiting is usually the one who needed the help more. What works is a two hour block of home tuition on the same evening split into two separate sessions, with a short handover in the middle while the tutor writes notes. The travel cost is paid once, both children get undivided attention, and the tutor has a reason to protect that evening for a whole year.

There is one genuine exception. Two children within a year of each other, on the same board, in the same subject and at a similar level can be taught together productively, and the peer effect sometimes helps. Beyond that the pairing degrades fast. A Year 9 and a Year 11 in the same subject do not share a lesson, and a DP1 student and an MYP student share nothing but a surname. A home tutor in Mumbai agreeing to teach two children at different stages in one hour is agreeing to something they cannot deliver.

Online changes the arithmetic for the second child specifically. Where one child needs a subject the node cannot supply, pairing a visiting tutor for the first child with an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Dronagiri for the second is often the best available combination, and it removes the scheduling knot entirely because the online session can sit on a different evening without costing anybody a drive. For Diploma Programme internal assessment supervision in particular, a screen is not a compromise.

The honest limits are worth stating. Online is the wrong choice for a child below about Year 8 who cannot work unsupervised, and for any student who has started avoiding the subject, because the intervention they need is a person taking the book out of their bag. And where both children are in that category, a single evening with a visiting tutor covering both consecutively is the only shape that works, which means accepting whichever subjects that one tutor genuinely covers rather than the subjects you would have chosen.

sections.heading: What should a tutor claiming both boards be able to prove?
paragraphs: Three specific things, and a tutor who has really taught both answers all three without pausing. Which Diploma Programme subjects at which level, and when. Which IGCSE board and which subject codes, and when. And one concrete difference in how they would teach the same topic under each system, which is the question that separates experience from a line on a profile. A teacher who has done both will immediately talk about criterion language versus mark scheme discipline. Somebody who has not will talk about covering the syllabus thoroughly.

Our checks run before you see anybody. Identity verified against a government photograph document and matched to the person who attends. A degree in the subject taught rather than a general teaching qualification spread across six subjects. Board relevant teaching history asked about separately for the IB, for Cambridge International Education and for Pearson Edexcel, because a profile claiming all three gets questioned on all three and claims that do not survive questioning do not reach you.

References come from families, and the three questions we ask them are deliberately narrow: did the tutor arrive when they said, did they communicate when something changed, and did the student's written work visibly alter. In a household with two children the first two matter more than usual, because a late arrival does not shorten one session, it shortens both. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Dronagiri running a two child evening has to be the reliable kind, and reliability is the quality references actually reveal.

One category of claim ends the conversation. Be wary of anybody offering a guaranteed grade, quoting a success percentage, or implying a relationship with a school or with an examination authority. We do not guarantee grades, we publish no success rates, and IB Gram is not affiliated with any school named here. Somebody presenting themselves as a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai with equal authority in every one of them has answered a question about judgement rather than range.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma Programme jump, and who should teach it?
paragraphs: The jump from Year 11 into the Diploma Programme is the steepest academic step most students in this node will take, and it is badly served because tutors tend to specialise on one side of it. A student who did well in IGCSE Mathematics at the harder tier arrives in Higher Level Mathematics and finds that knowing the method is no longer the task. The questions are longer, the reasoning has to be written out, and marks go to justification rather than to the answer. The same student who scored strongly eight months earlier is suddenly mid table, and nothing about their ability has changed.

The second part of the jump is independence. IGCSE coursework is scaffolded by the school. A Diploma Programme internal assessment is a piece of work the student scopes themselves, and the single most common failure is a research question that cannot be answered in the space available. That is not a content problem and no amount of subject revision fixes it. It is a planning skill, and the time to teach it is the summer between Year 11 and DP1, which is precisely when nobody is thinking about tutoring.

Third is the core. Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the service component have no IGCSE equivalent, and students who were efficient at managing discrete subjects find that three open ended commitments with distant deadlines defeat their usual methods. A tutor who has only taught IGCSE will treat TOK as an essay subject. One who has supervised it knows the problem is almost always the claim being argued, not the writing.

For a household already arranging IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dronagiri, this is the one place where a single tutor across both systems genuinely earns their premium, and it is worth asking for explicitly. What that person does differently is small and decisive: they start the student writing justification in Year 11 rather than in DP1, they get the Higher Level choice discussed before the school asks for it, and they use the summer gap to teach scoping rather than content. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Dronagiri reflect scarcity, and a tutor with real experience on both sides of that step is scarce, which is the honest reason they cost more.
