sections.heading: Two children, two boards, one visit: grouping the subjects
paragraphs: The practical question in a mixed-board household is which pairs of requests can share a tutor. Mathematics pairs well across boards, because the technique is continuous from Extended work into the Diploma Programme. Physics and Chemistry pair within a board and rarely across levels, since a Higher Level paper and a Year 10 Extended paper demand different habits from the same person in the same hour. English pairs badly across boards and well within one.

So the grouping we usually propose looks like this. One tutor for Mathematics across both children, an hour each, consecutive. A second tutor for the Diploma Programme science, longer and less often. A third only where a scarce subject genuinely demands it. All IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Ghatkopar East arrangements end up with between one and three people in the house across a week, and three is the point at which the household starts resenting the whole thing.

The younger sibling listening in is a real effect and worth planning for rather than suppressing. A Year 8 student who overhears a Diploma Programme Mathematics session picks up vocabulary and loses nothing at all. A Year 10 student who overhears her sister being taught the same topic at a different level gets confused and starts using a method that will not earn marks on her paper. Where the subjects overlap, separate the rooms. Where they do not, do not bother.

Coursework is the thing to stagger deliberately. An IGCSE internally assessed component and a Diploma Programme Internal Assessment landing in the same fortnight will take the entire household down with them. Look at both schools' calendars in September, mark the collisions, and front-load the work on whichever one is more forgiving. A tutor who asks to see both calendars in the first week is doing the job properly rather than politely.

sections.heading: One tutor, two boards, and the roads around Ghatkopar East
paragraphs: A two-child IB and IGCSE home tuition arrangement in Ghatkopar East needs a tutor who can give the household two consecutive hours, which narrows the pool to people inside a short drive. Ghatkopar East, Ghatkopar West, Vikhroli, Chembur, Powai and Chandivali is the working list. Two hours of teaching plus fifty minutes of travel each way is a four-hour evening, and nobody sustains that past October.

The geography helps more than it hinders. Ghatkopar East runs towards the Eastern Express Highway, so a tutor from Vikhroli or Powai arrives with their evening largely intact and can take two hours rather than one. The catch is the metro. Metro Line 1 terminates at Ghatkopar and the east side sits a further ten minutes from the station than the west side does, so a tutor arriving by metro is already ten minutes into their margin before anything starts. For a single hour that is survivable. For a double it is not.

Chembur and Vikhroli are therefore the first places we look for a double slot, with Kanjurmarg and Mulund down the Central Line as the second tier and Kurla reachable through the Santacruz–Chembur Link Road (SCLR). Powai and Chandivali hang off JVLR with no station of their own, which sounds like a disadvantage and is not, because the tutors there drive anyway and already know the route in the evening peak.

sections.heading: Why Mumbai schools change board between Year 11 and Year 12
paragraphs: Many Mumbai schools run Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel IGCSE to Year 11 and then the IB Diploma Programme for the final two years, which is how a household ends up on two boards without ever choosing to be. Witty International School and Hiranandani Foundation School both sit in that bracket locally, and both are named here as context only. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with either, nor with Cambridge International Education, Pearson Edexcel or the IB Organization.

The handover creates a window in the Mumbai calendar that almost nobody uses. Year 11 finishes its papers and the Diploma Programme year begins shortly afterwards, leaving a gap with no homework, no assessment and a student who is still in academic gear. Two or three weeks of work in that gap on algebraic technique, laboratory independence and academic writing does more than a whole term of catch-up in October. We say this every year, and roughly one family in five acts on it.

The rest of the year collides in predictable places. The IGCSE child's mocks land in January. The Diploma Programme child's Internal Assessment drafts land in January and February. Both schools' reporting cycles close around October. A household with children on both boards therefore gets one calm term, the one just after the monsoon, and two difficult ones. Planning the tuition around that shape beats reacting to it in February.

A practical note about reporting. The two boards describe progress in different languages, so a parent ends up comparing criteria levels against percentage marks and drawing a conclusion that is not actually available. Read each child's report against that child's own previous report and nothing else. A tutor who starts comparing siblings across boards should be stopped on the spot, because the comparison means nothing and the children can hear it.

sections.heading: Can one home tutor cover both boards in the same evening?
paragraphs: Sometimes, and only in a few subjects. A tutor can hold Mathematics across an IGCSE Year 10 and a Diploma Programme Standard Level student in consecutive hours without the quality dropping. The same tutor holding Year 9 science and Higher Level Chemistry in one visit will teach the second badly, because the switch costs more than the travel saved. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Ghatkopar East remains the right default for both children; it is the sharing that has limits.

Online changes the arithmetic for one child and not the other. A Diploma Programme student with a scarce Higher Level subject is well served by an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Ghatkopar East reach, because she can work alone between sessions and mostly needs direction and marking. A Year 9 or Year 10 student generally is not, since the tutor needs to watch the written page as it is produced and sometimes take the pen. The common split is the older child online for the scarce subject and the younger one at the table.

Hybrid across a household is the arrangement that survives a Mumbai year. One tutor visiting for a double on a fixed weekday or Saturday, one online specialist for whichever subject this area cannot staff, and short online check-ins before deadlines. It absorbs the monsoon, it absorbs one child's exam leave without wrecking the other's slot, and it does not depend on anybody making three separate journeys a week into this suburb.

One thing to refuse outright. If a tutor offers to take both children together in a single hour because the subjects look adjacent, decline. Two children on two boards in one hour is two half-lessons, and the younger one always receives the smaller half. Pairing works only where board, level and subject are identical, which in a mixed-board household they almost never are.

sections.heading: The Year 11 to DP1 handover, in a Mumbai school year
paragraphs: The move from Year 11 into Diploma Programme 1 is the sharpest academic step a Mumbai student takes, and it is the one nobody prepares for, because it happens during a holiday. The student finishes her IGCSE papers in good standing, takes six weeks off, and arrives in a programme that assumes an independence she has never actually been asked for.

Here is the specific shape of it. A student from a Chembur campus living in Ghatkopar East finishes Extended Mathematics and a combined science course comfortably. In September she is asked to choose a research question for a scientific investigation, decide what to measure, and justify the method. She has never done any of those three things, because her IGCSE practicals told her what to do each time. Her content knowledge is fine. She writes a weak first draft, the school flags it, and the family concludes she has fallen behind in Physics, which she has not.

The second part of the step is volume and scheduling. Six IGCSE subjects with homework becomes six Diploma Programme subjects with coursework, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the Creativity, Activity, Service commitment. Nothing individually is harder. The simultaneity is harder. A student who has never kept a calendar now needs one, and IB and IGCSE home tuition in Ghatkopar East that handles this well spends the first fortnight on planning rather than on content.

What to do about it is unglamorous and effective. Use the June gap for three things: algebraic technique, one practice at designing an experiment from a blank page, and one piece of academic writing with a claim and a counterclaim in it. That is perhaps eight sessions in total. It does not need the strongest tutor in Mumbai, it needs a competent one early, and the families who do this in June are the ones who stop calling us in November.

sections.heading: What should a term of home tuition change for each child?
paragraphs: Different things, which is exactly why they need reviewing separately. For the IGCSE child the measurable change after four weeks is in marked papers: working written down, command words answered as asked, fewer blank parts. For the Diploma Programme child it shows in drafts: a narrower research question, an evaluation paragraph that exists at all, a bibliography that was not assembled the night before submission.

Over a full term the IGCSE child should be able to sit a paper and mark it against the published scheme herself. The Diploma Programme child should be able to take an assignment brief and produce a plan without being asked to. Both of those are independence, which is the only outcome a tutor can genuinely manufacture. Grades follow or they do not, depending on the school, the student's own work and which paper comes up on the day.

We do not guarantee grades and this site publishes no success rates. In a two-child household that matters twice over, because a service willing to promise one child's grade will cheerfully promise the other's, and the promise costs them nothing to make. What we will give you instead is a written review per child every two to four weeks naming one thing secure and one thing not, which is checkable in a way a promise never is.

Sometimes the honest recommendation is less tuition rather than more. A household with two children in weekly sessions, both carrying homework and coursework, can reach a point where the tutoring is part of the problem rather than the fix. If one child is coping, stop that arrangement and move the hour to the child who is not. We would rather halve a household's bill than watch two tired children get slower.

faqs.question: Does Extended IGCSE Mathematics prepare a student for IB Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: It prepares the manipulation and not the reasoning. A confident Extended candidate arrives able to handle the algebra in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, which is a real advantage, and is then surprised by proof, by the expectation of justifying a step, and by questions that give no clue about the method. That gap closes in roughly a term with targeted work. A Core candidate moving into Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation faces the opposite problem, strong on modelling and short on manipulation.

faqs.question: My child moves from IGCSE to the Diploma Programme in June. What should we do first?
faqs.answer: Use the gap, and spend it on independence rather than content. Three things pay for themselves: algebraic technique kept warm, one practice at designing an experiment from a blank page, and one piece of writing that holds a claim against a counterclaim. That is around eight sessions and it addresses the actual step, which is being asked to decide things rather than follow instructions. Families who do this in June are noticeably less likely to be in difficulty by November.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Ghatkopar East for two consecutive hours?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they come from inside the short radius. faqs.question: Is it a problem if the younger child listens in at home?
faqs.answer: Only when the subjects overlap. A Year 8 student overhearing a Diploma Programme Mathematics session absorbs vocabulary and loses nothing. A Year 10 student overhearing her sister being taught the same topic at a different level starts using a method that will not earn marks on her own paper, which is a genuine problem and worth separating rooms for. Tell the tutor which case you are in rather than leaving them to discover it when a wrong method appears in homework.

faqs.question: Do you offer online tuition for one child and home visits for the other?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the more common arrangements in this suburb. A Diploma Programme student with a scarce Higher Level subject works well online, because she can read and draft between sessions and mainly needs direction and marking. A Year 9 or Year 10 student usually needs somebody at the table who can see the page as it is written. Running one child each way is cheaper and more reliable than forcing both into whichever mode suits the parent.

faqs.question: What if one child's tutor is working and the other's is not?
faqs.answer: We change the one that is not, and we do not touch the one that is. Separate written reviews exist for exactly this reason, because a single combined note tends to average away the weaker arrangement. Tell us what specifically is not working, since pace, manner, subject depth and language of instruction need different replacements. There is no fee for the change and no obligation to replace both tutors just because one needs replacing.

faqs.question: Should both children have the same tutor for consistency?
faqs.answer: Consistency is worth less than subject match, so only where the subject allows it. One tutor across both children works for Mathematics and sometimes for English within a single board. It works badly across a board and level boundary in the sciences, where the habits being taught are genuinely different. The convenience of one person in the house is real, and it is not worth a term of mediocre teaching for the child who got the weaker half of the expertise.

faqs.question: How long should we keep both arrangements running?
faqs.answer: Until each child can work without the tutor, which will not happen at the same time. The IGCSE child is finished when she can sit a paper and mark it against the published scheme herself. The Diploma Programme child is finished when she can plan a piece of coursework from the brief without being prompted. Stopping one arrangement while the other continues is normal and sensible. Keeping both running out of habit is a cost with nothing attached to it.

sections.heading: Does IGCSE prepare a child for the Diploma Programme?
paragraphs: Partly, and the gaps are predictable enough to plan for. The International General Certificate of Secondary Education builds strong examination technique: students learn to read a question, answer to a mark scheme, and work under timed conditions. Those habits transfer directly to Diploma Programme (DP) written papers and are a real advantage over students arriving from systems with more coursework. What IGCSE does not build is the independent extended-writing muscle the DP asks for almost immediately.

The three places the gap shows are the internal assessment, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK). An IGCSE student is used to tasks with a stated question and a known structure. A DP internal assessment asks the student to invent the question, defend why it is worth asking, and then sustain an argument over several thousand words with a supervisor who checks in rather than teaches. Students who were comfortable at IGCSE often have their first genuine academic crisis in the DP1 internal assessment, and it is a skills crisis rather than a content one.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) route into the DP has the mirror-image profile. MYP students arrive fluent in criteria, command terms and reflective writing, and less fluent in sitting a long written paper to time. Both routes work. Both need a different first six months, and a tutor who does not know which route your child came from will teach the wrong thing for a term.

For families in Mumbai choosing between the two at the Year 9 decision point, the honest answer is that the board matters less than the school's teaching and your child's working style. We do not have a preferred answer and we will not pretend one route is superior.

sections.heading: Where the two boards ask for different habits in the same subject
paragraphs: Take Mathematics. An IGCSE student is rewarded for clean method lines and accurate arithmetic under time pressure, with a non-calculator paper that exposes weak algebra. A DP student taking Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is rewarded for justification and for the exploration, which is a piece of mathematical writing rather than a calculation. The same child moving from one to the other has to learn that showing method is no longer enough and explaining why the method is valid has become the marked skill.

Take the sciences. IGCSE Chemistry asks for precise experimental description and recall-plus-application answers. DP Chemistry asks for the same, plus an internal assessment where the student designs the investigation and the evaluation of uncertainty carries real weight. Subject choice across both boards, Higher Level and Standard Level and Core and Extended decisions, and the internal assessments each one carries are the live questions in a household running both boards, because the older child's experience is a poor guide to the younger one's.

Take English. IGCSE rewards a reliable essay structure applied under time. DP English A asks for sustained close analysis and, in the literature route, for the student to build an argument about a text nobody has told them what to think about. Parents who assume their younger child will find it easier because the older one coped are frequently surprised.

A brief naming all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Ghatkopar West might be asked to cover is where almost every two-child enquiry starts. We narrow it to the two or three that matter, usually one per child.

sections.heading: What a Mumbai school year looks like with two boards in one house
paragraphs: Families in Ghatkopar West use schools across the Central Suburbs, Witty International School and Hiranandani Foundation School among them, and when two children sit different boards the household calendar has two sets of pressure points instead of one. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Witty International School, Hiranandani Foundation School or any other school named here. We map their terms because the collisions are what make the year hard.

The IGCSE child peaks in December and January with mocks, then again in February as coursework or practical components are finalised, and then goes quiet into study leave and the May and June series. The IB child peaks differently: the first-term report in late October or November, then internal assessment deadlines clustering in January and February, with the Extended Essay deadline sitting somewhere unhelpful nearby. February is therefore the month when both children need more, and it is also the month when experienced tutors across Mumbai have no capacity left.

The practical consequence for a two-child household is that you cannot buy your way out of February in February. Households that get through it comfortably have booked by September, have a tutor who knows both children, and have agreed in advance which child gets the extra session when both need one. That last conversation is uncomfortable and much better had in October than in a crisis.

April and May bring a different problem: the IGCSE child is on study leave and at home all day while the IB child is still in school. The temptation to fill the quiet hours with extra tutoring is strong and usually wrong, because a student sitting papers needs recovery time more than another ninety minutes.

A tutor whose dual claim is thin will describe both in the same vocabulary, usually the vocabulary of general subject expertise, and that tells you which board they actually taught.

Our checks are documentary and we describe their limits honestly. Two notes, not one. A tutor who writes one note for both children has not really diagnosed either.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade for either child. We do not guarantee grades. sections.heading: The IGCSE to IB transition year in Mumbai, and what it actually costs
paragraphs: The expensive year is DP1, and families consistently budget for the wrong one. Most households plan heavy support for Year 11 because the papers are visible and the mocks are frightening, then assume the first DP year will be a settling-in period. It is the opposite. A student who did well at IGCSE arrives in DP1 with good examination habits and no experience of designing their own question, and the first internal assessment is where that shows. The second term of DP1 is where the damage either gets caught or becomes a two-year problem.

What the transition actually requires is unglamorous. Three or four sessions on what a research question has to do, how a supervisor relationship works, and why a draft is submitted for comment rather than approval. Then subject-specific work on extended writing: holding an argument across sections, using evidence rather than listing it, and writing to a criterion descriptor rather than to a word count. None of this is content teaching, which is why schools often do not provide it and why parents mistake the need for it as a subject weakness.

The second real cost is subject choice. A student who took six IGCSEs comfortably and then selects three Higher Level subjects on the strength of that has misread the signal, because IGCSE performance predicts DP performance imperfectly, and particularly so in Mathematics and the sciences where the Higher Level step is steep. One honest conversation with someone who has taught both levels in April of Year 11 saves a subject change in October of DP1.

Families comparing IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Ghatkopar West across the transition usually find DP1 support costs more per hour than IGCSE support, because the teachers who can do it are fewer. Budgeting for Year 11 home tuition in Mumbai and nothing for DP1 is the common mistake we see here.

sections.heading: How do you measure progress when two children started together?
paragraphs: Measure them separately and on different clocks, because they are solving different problems. For the IGCSE child at four weeks, the marker is self-marking accuracy: can they predict their own score on a paper to within a few marks? For the IB child at four weeks, the marker is whether a vague piece of work has become a specific one, usually visible as a research question that now names a variable and a method. Comparing the two children's progress against each other is the fastest way to misread both.

At one term, expect targeted components to move and reported grades to lag for both children. School grades average a term's work including the weeks before any tutor arrived. For the IB child, a predicted grade is a teacher's accumulated judgement and is the slowest figure on the report to shift. Look at the most recent marked piece of work in each case rather than the summary line.

Across a full cycle, consistent weekly work with competent tutors helps most students, and we will not reduce that to a number. We do not guarantee grades, we publish no success rate, and we quote no fees on a page. faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both an IB and an IGCSE child in our home?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and only where the subject ladder is genuinely shared. The same tutor can reasonably take IGCSE Mathematics and MYP Mathematics in consecutive slots, or IGCSE and Diploma Programme Chemistry if they have taught both. A single tutor covering IGCSE Business Studies and DP Mathematics is making a wide claim on thin experience. faqs.question: Does IGCSE actually prepare a child for IB Diploma Programme work?
faqs.answer: It prepares them well for the papers and poorly for the independent work. IGCSE students arrive in the Diploma Programme fluent in answering to a mark scheme under time, which is a real advantage. What they have not done is invent their own research question, work with a supervisor rather than a teacher, or sustain an argument over several thousand words. That is why the DP1 internal assessment is where strong IGCSE students often have their first genuine difficulty, and why three or four sessions on those skills in DP1 are worth more than a term of content revision.

faqs.answer: Register the tutor once as a standing weekly visitor and the double slot becomes a single entry, which most buildings along the Ghatkopar West–LBS Marg stretch will arrange on a resident's request. faqs.question: One child is improving and the other is not. What do we change?
faqs.answer: Change the arrangement that is not working rather than reviewing both. Siblings progress on different clocks and for different reasons, so a comparison tells you very little. If the younger child's tutor has drifted into going over school homework, that is a plan problem we can fix with the same tutor. If the child has stopped asking questions in sessions, that is a fit problem and we move them to a different profile.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for the younger child while the older one is in the room?
faqs.answer: It can, with headphones and a separate surface, and it is often the only way two sessions fit one flat. The better configuration is usually the reverse of what parents expect: put the older, self-driven child online with a specialist and keep the physical slot for the younger child who needs someone present. Online is the wrong choice for a Grade 6 or Grade 7 student who has not yet learned to start work unprompted, however convenient the logistics look.

faqs.question: Should we use the same tutor when the older child moves from IGCSE to DP?
faqs.answer: Only if that tutor has genuinely taught the Diploma Programme, including internal assessment supervision. Continuity is valuable and knowing the child is a real advantage, but the DP asks for things an IGCSE specialist may never have done: research question design, criterion-based extended writing, supervisor relationships. Ask them directly which internal assessments they have supervised and listen for specifics. If the answer is vague, keep them for content and add a DP-experienced tutor for the transition work rather than hoping.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week is too many for a household?
faqs.answer: Four across two children is usually the ceiling, and three is better. Every session consumes an evening for the child, a slot in the flat and a parent's attention, and past a certain point the family's week becomes the limiting factor rather than the teaching. A student with four tutoring hours and no unstructured time stops consolidating anything. We would rather run two well-targeted sessions per child with real work set between them than four sessions that fill the diary and the child's remaining capacity.

sections.heading: Two boards in one household: which tutor goes where?
paragraphs: Start by naming what each child is actually doing, because the words families use are rarely precise. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs as the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the two-year Diploma Programme (DP) with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) subjects. The International General Certificate of Secondary Education is a separate qualification offered here by Cambridge International Education and by Pearson Edexcel, typically across Years 9 to 11. Many schools in Thane run a hybrid pathway, taking students through Middle Years or a national curriculum and then into an international course at Year 9, which is why one household frequently sits across both systems without having chosen to.

The practical allocation rule is simple. Match the tutor to the examination the child will sit, not to the subject name. A tutor who has prepared Cambridge candidates knows what that board's papers reward and how its coursework is handled. A tutor who has taught Diploma Programme internal assessments knows how that moderation works. Those skills do not transfer automatically, and the place they fail most visibly is examination technique rather than content: the student knows the material and answers in the wrong shape.

Where the two systems genuinely rhyme is in the underlying skills, and that is worth exploiting. Data handling, algebraic fluency, structuring an argument from evidence, reading a command word and answering only what was asked. A tutor working with a Year 10 Cambridge student on those is building precisely what the same child will need two years later in Diploma Programme Year 1. So the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Ghodbunder Road for a Year 10 student is often one who is thinking about the transition ahead rather than only about the next series.

What we will not do is tell you which pathway your younger child should take after the international course, or quote you paper structures, durations or weightings for either system. Both the IB and the examination boards revise their documents on their own cycles, so the current syllabus and your school's coordinator are the only reliable sources for what a particular cohort faces. Ask for the subject codes in writing and give them to any tutor you interview.

sections.heading: Where the two boards diverge, subject by subject
paragraphs: Mathematics diverges most and earliest. On the international course the decision is about tier, with the broader syllabus opening the higher grades and the narrower one capping them. In the Diploma Programme the decision is about route, Analysis and Approaches with its proof and calculus demands against Applications and Interpretation with its modelling and technology emphasis, and then about Higher or Standard Level within that. A student who finished a narrow tier and then wants a demanding Diploma route has a real gap, and the honest window for closing it is the year before, not the first term after.

The sciences diverge in how practical work is assessed. The international courses handle laboratory skills through dedicated papers or coursework depending on the board and the entry, while the Diploma Programme requires an individual scientific investigation designed and written by the student. These train different things. A student who has only answered written questions about methods they never performed arrives at the Diploma investigation without the habit of planning a measurement, controlling a variable or stating an uncertainty. A tutor who sees that coming can build it a year early, which is the single most useful cross-board intervention we see on this corridor.

English and the humanities diverge in what counts as a good answer. International papers reward a tightly structured response to a specific question with evidence used precisely. Diploma Programme assessment adds extended independent writing and, in the humanities, an internally assessed investigation with its own conventions. The skill that carries across is using a source as evidence rather than retelling it, and a student weak at that in Year 10 will be weak at it in Diploma Programme Year 1 unless somebody addresses it directly.

Across both systems the strongest case for one-to-one work is anything individual: coursework, investigations, explorations, the Extended Essay (EE). Twelve students in a room cannot be taken through twelve different pieces of independent work, which is why all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Ghodbunder Road families book in the first term tend to be aimed at coursework rather than revision. Most IB and IGCSE home tuition in Ghodbunder Road, Mumbai that starts in June is aimed at exactly this. The weakest case is re-teaching content a student already knows, and a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents hire to do that is paying for the smallest possible gain.

sections.heading: Choosing subjects at the point the two systems meet
paragraphs: The junction between an international course at Year 11 and the Diploma Programme at Year 12 is where the most consequential decision in a child's schooling gets made, usually in a hurry and usually with incomplete information. Six Diploma subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Those choices are constrained by what the child studied before, by what the school can actually timetable, and by what a university pathway needs. The constraint parents most often discover too late is that a narrow Mathematics tier at the earlier stage makes the more demanding Diploma Mathematics route a genuine stretch rather than a formality.

A tutor's useful contribution here is diagnostic rather than advisory. Not telling you what to pick, which is the school's job and your family's decision, but telling you honestly whether the child's current fluency in a subject supports Higher Level in it. That answer comes from marked work rather than from enthusiasm. A student who enjoys Biology and loses marks consistently on data analysis questions will find Higher Level Biology harder than the enjoyment suggests, and somebody should say so in Year 11 rather than in the second term of Diploma Programme Year 1 when changing subjects is painful.

The second thing worth doing at this junction is building the two habits the Diploma Programme assumes and the earlier course does not demand much of. Writing to a mark allocation under time, and producing a genuinely finished draft rather than a nearly finished one. Independent assessed work in the Diploma Programme has deadlines that do not move and moderation that does not negotiate, and a student whose previous experience was coursework with generous internal resubmission will be surprised by that. Four or five sessions in Year 11 on timed writing is worth more than twenty in Diploma Programme Year 2 spent recovering from a missed deadline.

If one child is at this junction and another is further back, the planning conversation is worth having once for the household rather than twice. The younger child's tier and route decisions can be made with the older one's experience in hand, which is the one real advantage of being across two systems at once. sections.heading: What changes at four weeks, and what will not
paragraphs: Four weeks in, judge both arrangements on the same three signals and judge them separately. Each child can say what they worked on without being prompted, which means the sessions have a structure. The careless layer has thinned, with fewer dropped units, fewer unread questions and fewer abandoned answers. And each tutor can name the weakness in one sentence precise enough to disagree with. It is common for one of the two arrangements to clear all three and the other to clear none, and the mistake families make is treating that as a verdict on the whole decision rather than on one tutor.

At one term, expect visible mechanics and modest movement in marks. Coursework drafted ahead of a deadline. Timed practice treated as normal rather than as a special event. One grade or band of movement is a reasonable expectation where the problem was process rather than knowledge, and sometimes more when the whole issue was technique. Where foundations are genuinely thin, longer, and a tutor who promises otherwise in October is managing you rather than teaching your child.

At one examination cycle the honest statement is narrow. Tutoring closes the gap between what a student understands and what they can demonstrate under assessment conditions. It does not replace classroom teaching, it cannot repair a subject or tier chosen badly, and it does nothing for a student who has decided not to engage. We have seen students in this part of Mumbai move substantially and others stay flat, and the variable was almost never how good the tutor was. It was whether work happened between sessions.

So we do not guarantee grades, we publish no success rates, and we do not ask for a commitment to a term. Each arrangement is reviewed every two to four weeks on its own and a tutor is replaced with no notice period and nothing forfeited. With two children this flexibility is the point rather than a concession: the common outcome of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Ghodbunder Road, Mumbai is that one child needs a home tutor all year and the other needs two focused blocks, and an arrangement you can change every fortnight lets you find that out cheaply.

sections.heading: How one enquiry for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Girgaon becomes a weekly fixture
paragraphs: Almost every arrangement that collapses collapses for a household reason rather than an academic one. The teaching was fine. The hour stopped working. A younger child's class moved, a parent's return home shifted later, a flat that had a free corner in June did not have one in October, and within a month the lesson was being rescheduled rather than held. So the matching here starts with the week your family actually lives, and the subject question comes second.

We ask for the hour you want and then we ask what else is in it. Who else is at home then. Whether the room is in use. Whether the slot depends on one person being punctual, because a slot that only works when nobody is delayed on the Western Line is not a slot. Parents who name two or three defensible hours instead of one ideal hour get placed faster and keep the arrangement longer, which sounds like administration and is actually the single strongest predictor of whether this works.

Then comes programme and subject. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the Diploma Programme (DP), and a tutor strong in one is not automatically useful in another. We keep those pools separate, record which year groups and which subjects a person has genuinely taught, and match against that. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Girgaon who is excellent with a Year 4 reader may be the wrong choice entirely for a DP2 Internal Assessment (IA) that is unravelling, and we would rather say so than place the easy match. One enquiry naming an all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Girgaon therefore tends to come back as a shortlist built around a child rather than around a board.

What you receive is a set of profiles with the programme, the subjects, the year groups and the current teaching load each tutor carries. You choose who to meet and the introduction is free. If the arrangement needs to end, it ends through IB Gram rather than through an awkward exchange at your front door, and we treat the reason as information for the next match rather than as a complaint about anybody.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP and DP under one roof: sequencing two children's home tuition
paragraphs: Households with two children in different programmes make up a large share of the enquiries that reach us from South Mumbai, and the instinct is almost always wrong. The instinct is to find one tutor who can cover both, on the reasonable theory that it is simpler and cheaper. In practice the two children need different things at different intensities, and a single tutor splitting ninety minutes between a Year 4 child and a Year 11 child gives neither of them a lesson. What they give is supervised homework, which the household could have organised itself.

Sequencing works better than sharing. A Primary Years Programme child usually needs short, frequent, early work: twenty-five minutes of reading aloud, number facts, handwriting stamina, done before they are tired. A Middle Years Programme student needs a longer block later, because criteria-based tasks cannot be started and abandoned. A Diploma Programme student needs the latest slot and the longest, and often needs the flat quiet rather than merely available. Put those three needs on a week in that order and the same table serves all of them without anyone competing for it.

The honest trade-off is cost, and it is worth stating plainly rather than dressing up. Two tutors cost more than one. What they buy is two diagnoses, two sets of expertise and two arrangements that can be ended independently, which matters because the commonest outcome is that one child's tuition works brilliantly and the other's does not. A shared arrangement makes that impossible to see and impossible to unwind. Families who ask us about IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Girgaon for two children are usually surprised that staggering the start dates by a month costs less than starting both at once and keeping both out of politeness.

Programme structure itself should come from your school, not from this page. Do not take criteria counts, component weightings, word limits or deadline months from anything written for marketing purposes, including briefs and comparison pages. The IB revises subject guides on its own cycle and your school sets internal dates ahead of official ones. Ask the programme coordinator for the current guide and the school's calendar, and hand both to the tutor in week one. An IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai parents keep for several years will ask for them unprompted.

sections.heading: Which subjects really need the tutor in the room?
paragraphs: The ones where the error is invisible in the finished work. Mathematics is the clearest case: a wrong answer tells you almost nothing, while watching the student attempt the question tells you everything. Did they read it twice. Did they draw anything. Did they reach for the calculator before they had a plan. Did they abandon the method they knew because it felt slow. A tutor beside them sees all of it in ninety seconds, and no amount of marking afterwards recovers that information.

Reading and early writing are the second case, and they are the strongest argument for home classes with a young child. A Primary Years Programme student reading aloud reveals exactly where fluency breaks, which words they are guessing from shape, and how long they can sustain attention before the voice goes flat. That is a diagnosis you can only make in the room. The same is true of handwriting stamina, which looks like carelessness on paper and like fatigue in person, and needs opposite treatment depending on which it is.

At the other end, some work genuinely suits a screen. A Diploma Programme student revising a written draft is often better served by a shared document with comments in the margin than by two people leaning over one laptop at a crowded table. Marking a timed paper, where the student needs to see annotations build up on their own script, works well remotely. So does a short mid-week clarification that would not justify a journey across Mumbai. These are real advantages rather than consolations.

The subjects in the middle depend on the student rather than the subject. A confident Middle Years Programme student working through criteria-based tasks may do perfectly well with alternating formats. An anxious one needs a person in the room until the anxiety has somewhere to go. This is why we ask what the student is like before we ask what they are struggling with, and why a request for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Girgaon parents imagine as one weekly visit often becomes a more interesting arrangement once somebody has actually asked about the child.

sections.heading: Home tuition across Girgaon, Grant Road, Marine Drive and Walkeshwar
paragraphs: The working catchment for a Girgaon address runs north to Grant Road, west along Marine Drive and up the hill to Walkeshwar, and the reason it stops there is time rather than willingness. South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, which is precisely when households want lessons. Tutors here are therefore matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs.

Charni Road station on the Western Line, between Churchgate and Mumbai Central, is what makes the arrangement robust. A tutor living near Marine Lines, Grant Road or Charni Road itself arrives by train and is unaffected by whatever the roads are doing, which is why rail-based tutors hold evening slots through the monsoon when car-based ones start sending apologies. The Harbour Line brings people in from the Dockyard Road and Sewri side and suits afternoons better than evenings. Metro Line 3 along the Cuffe Parade to Bandra Kurla Complex alignment has made a Worli or Lower Parel tutor viable for a five o'clock lesson, and the Coastal Road has shortened the journey home afterwards more than the journey in.

Walkeshwar deserves a specific note because it misleads people. It is close on a map and slower in a vehicle, since the climb and the one-way system add minutes that no map application accounts for. For a late-afternoon lesson it is fine. For a seven o'clock start it is riskier than Grant Road, which is further away and one stop up a railway line. Parents who type IB and IGCSE tutors near me Girgaon and then filter by distance alone end up with exactly this mistake.

Within Girgaon itself, the thing that varies is not distance but access. Older buildings and chawl entrances are often set behind the main road, lanes are narrower than they look, and lifts sometimes stop running after a certain hour. Send written directions rather than only a map pin: the lane, the landmark, the floor, the lift's hours, and whatever the watchman needs in order to let a weekly visitor through. Home tuition across this part of Mumbai runs far more smoothly when the first visit is an arrival rather than an expedition.

sections.heading: What the Mumbai school week actually leaves room for
paragraphs: Before fixing an hour, look honestly at what the school week leaves. Children around Girgaon attend a compact set of South Mumbai schools, Bombay International School at Babulnath and Gopi Birla Memorial School at Walkeshwar among them, and most of them finish late enough that a child is home, changed and fed well into the evening. Those schools are named here as local context only. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with Bombay International School, Gopi Birla Memorial School or any other school mentioned anywhere on this site.

A student who has spent an hour getting back from Babulnath has a real limit on what they can absorb at seven. This is the argument for home tuition that nobody makes well: not convenience, but the removal of a second journey from a day that already had two. A child who would have travelled again to a coaching centre arrives at the lesson with something left. The flip side is that the household has to protect the hour, because the lesson is now happening in the same room where everything else happens.

The year has a shape worth planning against. June to the Diwali break is teaching time, and it is when steady weekly work pays the most and almost nobody calls. Reports land around the break, which is why tutor diaries across South Mumbai fill in the first fortnight of November. The second half of the year carries the assessed work: investigations, explorations, the Extended Essay (EE) progression for DP1, the Middle Years Programme personal project for Year 5, and for DP2 a run of deadlines compressed into a few months.

Schools set internal submission dates ahead of official ones so staff have time to mark and moderate, and those internal dates are the ones that matter to your week. Ask for them in writing, put them on a calendar the tutor can see, and let the tutor plan backwards from them. The commonest avoidable crisis in IB and IGCSE home tuition in Girgaon is a draft that was due to a teacher a fortnight before the family believed it was due to anyone.

sections.heading: Does home tuition in Girgaon work better than online for a younger child?
paragraphs: For a Primary Years Programme or early Middle Years Programme child, yes, and the gap is wide enough to be worth paying for. The things that limit a young student are attention, fluency and the willingness to begin, and all three are managed by presence rather than instruction. A tutor in the room can put a hand on a page, slow a reading, hold a pause, notice that the child has stopped looking at the text two minutes before the comprehension answer goes wrong. Online, that child performs attention convincingly while absorbing very little.

For a Diploma Programme student the calculation changes. Older students can hold a session on a screen, and some prefer it: no adult in the room, a shared document, a recording to replay. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Girgaon also solves genuine scarcity, because a less common Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL) subject may have no specialist on the island at all, and a nearby generalist is the worse option by a long way. Treating online as second best is a mistake once the student is sixteen.

Most households here end up hybrid without planning it. The main lesson happens at home, where the tutor can push and the student cannot hide, and a shorter mid-week session happens online to mark a paper or clear one topic. That pattern absorbs the things that will definitely happen: a changed school timetable, a tutor held at a signal, a monsoon week, a flat full of visiting relatives in October. It also means a missed Tuesday does not become a missed fortnight.

What makes the hybrid half work is infrastructure the household has to provide, and in Girgaon that is not guaranteed. An online session needs a device the student controls for the hour, a corner nobody walks through, and a connection that holds in the evening. Study space varies enormously from one address to the next here, and plenty of flats cannot offer that corner. If yours is one of them, say so when we are matching rather than six weeks in, and the arrangement should lean on home classes instead.

paragraphs: Somebody whose government photo identity, claimed qualification and stated teaching experience have been checked before you ever saw their profile, including which programme, which subjects and which year groups they have actually taught. Experience is tested by asking for operational detail that cannot be improvised. A person who has supervised Diploma Programme investigations can tell you in two sentences where students lose criterion marks on evaluation. For home tuition there is a second layer that online work does not need, because this is a stranger entering a family's living space every week for most of a year. We ask about current commitments and existing students in the area, since a tutor with several families already on the island is the one still arriving on time in February. We confirm the exact day and hour rather than general availability. And we ask how they handle a household where a parent is present, a sibling is nearby and the television is on, because the honest answer to that question varies a great deal.

Your own checks matter and are not impolite. Ask for identity on the first visit. Ask to see one piece of work the tutor has marked with their own annotations, which is the most informative document in this entire process. Households hunting for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Girgaon are usually describing somebody who will still be arriving reliably in February, and that is a question about habits rather than credentials. Ask what they will do in the first forty minutes. Ask what they will tell you at four weeks if it is not working. One more thing is worth agreeing explicitly rather than assuming. Decide whether the tutor will send you a short note after each session or a summary each month, and which you actually want. Weekly notes suit an anxious household and irritate a busy one. Monthly summaries suit a confident household and hide a drifting arrangement. Say which you prefer at the start, and treat a tutor who sends nothing for six weeks as a problem to raise rather than as a style to tolerate.

sections.heading: Agreeing the room: the first session every Girgaon family should insist on
paragraphs: Girgaon's older chawl-and-building mix means study space varies enormously from one home to the next, so the first session here is usually spent agreeing where lessons will actually happen before a single page of syllabus is opened. That is not wasted time. It is the most load-bearing half hour of the whole arrangement, and families who skip it spend the following term renegotiating the same thing every week while the lesson starts ten minutes late.

Here is the version that works, drawn from how it usually goes. A family off a lane near Charni Road has one main room with a dining table, a kitchen along one side, and a smaller room where a grandparent rests in the evening. The first instinct is to put the lesson at the dining table at seven, which is when the kitchen is busiest. What they settle on instead is six fifteen at the same table with the television off and the youngest child taken to a neighbour's for the hour, or, on the days that is impossible, the smaller room with a folding table brought in. Both options are written down. The tutor knows which applies before they arrive.

The details that decide it are mundane and specific. Enough surface for two open papers, a notebook and a calculator without anything being stacked. A chair at the right height, because a student working at a low table writes badly and tires fast. Light from the side rather than behind the page. A plug within reach if a device is involved. Somewhere for a bag. And an agreement about who else may be in the room, which is the one families find hardest to state out loud and the one that matters most.

Write the outcome down and send it to the tutor. Two lines is enough: the room, the time, the fallback, who moves what. A standing arrangement survives a changed school timetable and a visiting relative in a way an unspoken one does not. Families setting up IB and IGCSE home classes in Girgaon who do this in week one almost never raise space with us again, and families who do not raise it in week six as though it were a new problem.

paragraphs: At four weeks the changes you should see are domestic as much as academic. The student gets the table ready before the tutor arrives rather than being called to it. They know what the session will cover. They can name a weakness in a teacher's words instead of saying the subject is hard. And the tutor can show you a written list with topics closed on one side and open on the other. If the household still treats the hour as an interruption after a month, something in the arrangement is wrong and raising it now costs one conversation instead of a term.

At a term, ask for evidence you can hold. For a Middle Years Programme student that is a task marked against the published criteria with the levels explained to you in plain language. For a Diploma Programme student it is a timed paper marked against a real scheme, set beside the one from week one. Read past the total. A finished paper, visible method and a student who can predict their own errors before the marking are the three signals that turn into grades months later.

Across a full cycle, good home tuition produces a student who understands the architecture of their own assessment: which components carry the weight, what the command words demand, where their own time disappears. It does not produce certainty. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, no tutor here is allowed to promise one, and a first conversation that opens with a predicted score rather than a diagnosis has told you how that person works. We would rather lose the enquiry.

The limits are worth naming because families spend real money ignoring them. Tuition cannot replace attending school. It cannot fix a subject chosen for the wrong reasons until that conversation has happened. It cannot compress two missed years into six weeks, although it can tell a student honestly where a last fortnight is best spent. And an arrangement built on one steady hour a week across a term outperforms a burst of sessions in the final month, which is the pattern households in Mumbai, Maharashtra default to when the panic arrives.

paragraphs: Send five things: the programme and year group, the subjects, two or three weekly hours your household can defend, one piece of recent marked work, and written directions to your door including the lift's hours and whatever the watchman needs. That last item sounds trivial and is the difference between a first visit that starts on time and one that starts flustered twenty minutes late with everybody slightly annoyed.

Expect the first session to do two jobs. The tutor diagnoses: something unseen, a look at the work you sent, and enough questions to establish whether the gap is knowledge, method or timing, since those three look identical on a report and need different treatment. Then the room gets agreed, properly, with a fallback, and written down. Both halves matter and the second one is the half families skip.

Afterwards you should receive a short written summary naming the topics the tutor intends to work on, in what order, and how often they think sessions need to happen. Read it for specifics. A summary full of topics and papers is a plan; a summary full of confidence and potential is a sales document. If it disappoints you, tell us instead of the tutor and a different profile goes out. Nobody has to have an uncomfortable conversation in a doorway.

On scope, start narrow. If you are weighing a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents often ask about against one specialist for the subject that is hurting, take the specialist. It is cheaper, quicker to judge and easier to replace, and in a month you will know what a good arrangement looks like in your own flat. faqs.question: Should I sit in the room during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: For a young child, be nearby and not at the table. For a teenager, leave the room. The presence of a parent changes what a student is willing to admit they do not understand, and admitting it is most of the work. With a Primary Years Programme child there is a case for sitting in on the first session so you can see how the tutor works, then withdrawing to within earshot. With a Diploma Programme student, sitting in almost always makes the hour worse. Ask for a short note afterwards instead; that gives you the information without costing your child the candour.

faqs.question: Both my children need help and we have one table. How does that work?
faqs.answer: By sequencing rather than sharing. Put the younger child earlier and shorter, because attention fades and the work is naturally brief, then give the older one the later, longer block when the flat is quieter. One tutor splitting ninety minutes between a Year 4 child and a Year 11 student delivers supervised homework to both rather than a lesson to either. Two separate arrangements cost more and buy you two real diagnoses plus the ability to end one without disturbing the other, which matters because one of them usually works better than the other.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor teach my MYP daughter and my DP son?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, within one subject family, and you should test the claim rather than accept it. Ask which Diploma Programme subjects at which level the tutor has actually taught, for how long, and whether they have supervised the assessed component. Then ask the same about the Middle Years Programme criteria your daughter is marked against. A mathematics specialist who has taught both genuinely exists. Somebody claiming to cover Middle Years humanities and Diploma Programme chemistry is making a claim worth probing. An honest tutor will tell you which of the two they are stronger in, and that answer is useful either way.

faqs.question: Who should be at home when the tutor arrives?
faqs.answer: An adult, for the first few visits at least, and then whatever your household is comfortable with. Most families in South Mumbai keep an adult present throughout, and plenty of arrangements run perfectly well with a grandparent or household help at home instead of a parent. What matters is that somebody can open the door, settle any question about the room, and confirm the session happened. Agree it explicitly rather than leaving it to chance, because a tutor arriving to a locked door once will quietly start treating the slot as unreliable.

faqs.question: We rearranged the room once and it did not last. How do we make it stick?
faqs.answer: Write it down and give the tutor a copy. Two lines covering the room, the time, who moves what, and one named fallback for the days the main arrangement fails. Unwritten arrangements decay because every member of the household remembers a slightly different version, and by week five the lesson is happening wherever there is space. In Girgaon, where study space varies a great deal from one home to the next, the fallback matters as much as the main plan. A folding table in a quieter room is a perfectly good answer as long as everybody knows it is the answer.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to the building's common area or a reading room?
faqs.answer: If your building has one and it is genuinely quiet, yes, and it solves a real problem for households without a spare corner. Check three things first. Whether the space can be booked for the same hour every week, because a lesson that relocates each session loses time to settling. Whether other residents pass through it, since an interrupted hour teaches very little. And whether the lighting and table height are usable, as common rooms are often furnished for conversation rather than for writing. Confirm with the management committee before relying on it for a whole term.

faqs.question: What happens to the slot when our flat is full of relatives in October?
faqs.answer: Plan for it now rather than cancelling then. October and the weeks around Diwali fill South Mumbai flats with visitors, and this is the single commonest reason a good arrangement breaks for a fortnight and never fully recovers. The workable answers are to move the session online for those weeks, to shift it to an earlier hour before the house wakes up, or to use the building's common space if it is bookable. Tell the tutor in September which you intend to do. A planned switch holds; an improvised one turns into two missed weeks.

faqs.question: Do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Girgaon change if two children share the session?
faqs.answer: They usually change less than parents hope, because the tutor's hour is the cost and splitting attention does not halve it. Some tutors will quote a modest reduction for siblings taught together where the year groups are genuinely close and the subject is the same. Where the children are in different programmes, a shared session is poor value regardless of the figure, since neither child gets a full lesson. The larger drivers of cost are programme, level, subject scarcity and travel. Ask for the per-child position in writing before the first session rather than after.

faqs.question: A tutor keeps arriving fifteen minutes late from Walkeshwar. How do I raise it?
faqs.answer: Directly, early and once. Say that the session is scheduled at a particular time, that the student is ready then, and ask whether that hour is realistic given the journey. Walkeshwar looks close to Girgaon on a map and behaves differently in a vehicle, because the climb and the one-way system add time no map application accounts for. The honest resolution is often to move the slot fifteen minutes later rather than to insist on the original. If lateness continues after that conversation, tell us and we will handle the change of tutor.

faqs.question: How do we end an arrangement that is simply not working?
faqs.answer: Tell IB Gram rather than the tutor, and say what specifically has not happened. There is no notice period to argue about and no awkward conversation at your door, which is the part most parents dread and the reason many bad arrangements run on for months. Give the detail: no written diagnosis, no timed work, nothing moved in six weeks, the student dreads the hour. We use it to make the next match better. Ending an arrangement is a normal event here, not a complaint, and it happens in both directions.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need parking, and what if the lane has none?
faqs.answer: Most tutors working inside South Mumbai do not drive to lessons, precisely because parking in Girgaon's older lanes ranges from difficult to impossible. They arrive by train to Charni Road or Grant Road, or by an app-based ride dropped at the main road. If a candidate's arrangement depends on parking outside your building, treat it as a reason to check the slot carefully, because a tutor circling for ten minutes twice a week will start arriving late. sections.heading: What actually changes between IGCSE and the IB Diploma?
paragraphs: Three things change and none of them is difficulty of content. The first is who designs the task. IGCSE assessment hands your child a question written by somebody else; the Diploma Programme (DP) asks them to design their own investigation, their own exploration, their own essay title. A student who was excellent at answering questions can be genuinely lost when told to invent one, and that is the single most common first shock in DP1. The second change is volume of independent writing: the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) have no IGCSE equivalent at all.

The third is how marks are described. IGCSE papers reward answering a command word precisely and showing method. DP coursework is marked against published criteria with named strands, so a student has to read the criteria as instructions rather than as a rubric they will see afterwards. Both boards publish their language and both expect students to use it, but the vocabulary is not shared. A student who was fluent in state, describe, explain and suggest arrives in DP1 and meets evaluate, to what extent, and a criterion that asks for personal engagement.

Going the other way happens here too, usually when a family changes schools. A student leaving the Middle Years Programme (MYP) for IGCSE Year 10 loses criterion marking and gains timed papers, which sounds easier and is not: MYP work is continuous and forgiving of a bad week, while an IGCSE paper is a single sitting. Our profile labels sometimes read all IB and IGCSE subjects IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor Mumbai, and that is a category rather than a match. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Goregaon East may be asked for, the right question is which assessment system they have actually worked inside.

sections.heading: Which subjects transfer cleanly from Year 11 into DP1
paragraphs: Mathematics transfers best and still catches families out. Algebraic fluency built on Extended IGCSE papers is real preparation, and a student who can rearrange, factorise and handle functions without stopping to think has bought themselves a comfortable DP1. What does not transfer is the modelling demand. DP mathematics comes in two routes, one weighted towards analysis and proof and one towards applications and interpretation, and the choice between them should be made with your child's school coordinator on the basis of the subjects they want afterwards rather than on which sounds easier. Ask the coordinator, not a tutor, and certainly not a page like this one.

Science transfers partially. Laboratory confidence and the habit of controlling a variable carry over directly, and a student who practised the alternative to practical paper at IGCSE has an unfair advantage in DP1 data analysis. The gap is coursework design. The DP science Internal Assessment is an investigation the student invents, and the usual failure is a research question that is too broad to measure, not a weak experiment. A tutor who has supervised that specific component will spend the first fortnight making your child write three versions of their question and discard two, which is the most useful thing anyone can do at that point.

Languages and humanities transfer least predictably. IGCSE English trains structured response under timing; DP Language A asks for sustained analysis of chosen texts and a different kind of essay entirely. History and Economics both add a documents-based or data-based component with its own conventions. For families booking all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Goregaon East has tutors for, the practical rule is to keep the quantitative subjects with one person where possible and treat each language or humanity as its own match. One well-chosen tutor per subject beats one tutor stretched across six.

Practically, put the younger child first while attention is available, keep the two lessons shorter than you would a single one, and expect the whole block to run close to three hours including the gap.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our society for back-to-back sibling sessions?
faqs.answer: Inside this catchment, usually gladly, because a three-hour block at one address is the most efficient evening a tutor can get. The workable pool is Goregaon East, Jogeshwari, Malad East and Powai, measured on drive time rather than distance. Families inside the Oberoi Garden City towers have the best position in this part of Mumbai, since a tutor already teaching in the cluster can add two consecutive lessons without starting a car. Register the tutor once with your society office as a standing weekly visitor with the day and time, and the gate stops being a weekly conversation. Two-child home tuition in Mumbai lives or dies on that one administrative message.

faqs.question: My child moves from IGCSE Year 11 into DP1 next year. When should tuition start?
faqs.answer: The useful window is the term before, not the first month of DP1. What a student needs at that point is not content but practice at designing a task: writing a research question narrow enough to measure, reading criteria as instructions, and handling command terms like evaluate and to what extent. Six weeks of that before DP1 begins removes the most common first shock, which is being told to invent the question rather than answer one. Starting in DP1 October also works, but by then the student has usually formed a habit that has to be unlearned.

faqs.question: Does Extended IGCSE Mathematics prepare a student for Higher Level DP mathematics?
faqs.answer: It prepares the fluency, not the modelling. A student who can rearrange, factorise and work with functions without pausing has a genuinely easier DP1, and that is worth a great deal. What Extended papers do not practise is choosing an approach for an unfamiliar problem or building a model from a real situation, which is where DP mathematics differs most. The route decision between the analysis-weighted and applications-weighted courses should be made with your child's school coordinator on the basis of what they want to study afterwards, not on which course sounds more manageable.

faqs.question: We changed schools from IB MYP to IGCSE Year 10. What is the real difference?
faqs.answer: The marking stops being continuous. In the Middle Years Programme, work is assessed against criteria across the year, so a bad fortnight is absorbed. IGCSE compresses the judgement into timed papers at the end, which punishes gaps that MYP would have smoothed over, and rewards two skills MYP never explicitly taught: writing method on the page and answering a command word to exactly the length required. Most students manage the content transition easily and struggle with the timing. Six weeks of past paper work under a clock is the standard fix, and it works better than re-teaching topics.

faqs.question: Can both children share one tutor for science?
faqs.answer: Within the same subject family, often yes; across the IGCSE to DP step, check carefully. A chemistry specialist who has supervised DP internal assessments can usually handle an IGCSE sibling without difficulty, because the IGCSE demand is a subset of what they already do. The reverse is less safe: a strong IGCSE science tutor may never have supervised a DP investigation, and that component is where the marks sit. Ask the specific question, which is whether they have supervised a DP science IA from research question to final draft, rather than whether they can teach the subject.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book two children at once?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, for a reason that has nothing to do with discounts. Back-to-back sessions at one address remove an entire journey, and travel is one of the five things that set rates here along with board, level, subject scarcity and session length. A tutor running your two lessons consecutively inside the Oberoi Garden City cluster is pricing almost no travel at all. What we will not do is quote a figure on a page: you get the real number against each shortlisted profile before you commit. Two children sharing one single session, however, is a false economy.

faqs.question: Can one child have a weekday evening slot and the other a weekend one?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most two-child households it is the better structure. Bus routes in this corridor land children home inside one tight afternoon band, so weekday evening slots are the most contested thing in the suburb and splitting across the week roughly doubles your choice. It also protects attention: the second sibling in a three-hour weekday block is being taught at the worst hour of their day. A common arrangement here is one child on a weekday evening and the other on a Saturday morning, with the tutor marking work in between.

faqs.question: What should we prepare before the first sessions?
faqs.answer: Per child, three items. The most recent marked work including the teacher's written comments, because the comments carry the diagnosis and the grade does not. The subject and level written exactly as the school writes it, since Mathematics and Higher Level Mathematics produce different shortlists. And one quiet surface each with the phone somewhere else. For the DP child, add their current assessment brief if they have one. Households that bring these get a first session that diagnoses; households that bring a verbal summary of the problem get a first session spent gathering information.

faqs.question: What if one child is progressing and the other is not?
faqs.answer: Change one arrangement, not both, and change it at the four-week review rather than waiting for a report. Siblings on different programmes respond on different timelines, and the common mistake is reading the slower child's lack of visible movement as a failure when their progress is hiding inside coursework drafts. Ask each tutor for two pieces of work side by side. If the earlier piece does not exist, nothing was being tracked and that is the actual problem. We will re-shortlist for one child while leaving the other arrangement exactly as it is.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching service, written as two words, and it is not affiliated with the International Baccalaureate Organization, Cambridge International Education, Pearson Edexcel, Oberoi International School, Witty International School or any other school in Mumbai. We run no batches and own no syllabus; tutors teach your children's school syllabuses in your home or online. We name local schools only because their calendars decide when households here come under pressure. We do not guarantee grades and we publish no success rate, because such a figure would describe our intake rather than your children.

sections.heading: Which programme and tier is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: Most confusion in this search is a naming problem. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs three programmes a Mumbai family will meet: the Primary Years Programme (PYP) in the early years, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) through the middle school, and the Diploma Programme (DP) in the final two years. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel run IGCSE across Years 9 to 11, and a child doing IGCSE is not doing IB, even if the school has IB in its name and offers both pathways on the same campus.

Inside IGCSE the decision that matters is tier. Most subjects are entered at Core or Extended, and the entry decides the grade range available before a single paper is written. Schools usually decide in Year 9 or early Year 10 based on internal assessments, and parents often discover the decision after it has been made. A tutor's first useful act is sometimes not teaching content at all but telling you honestly whether an Extended entry is realistic for this child in this subject, or whether a secure Core grade serves them better.

Inside the Diploma Programme the equivalent fork is Higher Level (HL) versus Standard Level (SL). Three subjects at HL and three at SL is the usual pattern, and HL means more content, more depth and a heavier paper load rather than simply harder questions. A child who was comfortable in MYP can find the HL step genuinely steep, particularly in the sciences and in mathematics, and the first term of DP1 is where that shows up. Switching level later is possible but gets harder as the school year goes on.

A tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 a tutor in Mumbai may be asked to teach is a useful generalist for a younger child, but from Year 10 onwards specialism beats breadth. We would rather send you a profile who teaches two subjects properly than one who claims eight. That is the single most reliable filter a parent can apply themselves on a discovery call.
