A tutor who claims both the Diploma Programme and Cambridge experience is asked to evidence both separately, because the claim is common and the reality is often one board taught properly and the other read about.

Your own checks are quicker and in some ways better. Ask the tutor to describe the Internal Assessment in the DP subject and the coursework arrangement in the IGCSE subject in the same breath. Someone who has taught both will distinguish them instantly and without hedging. Ask what the first session would look like for each child, and listen for two different answers. Ask for a four-week written review per child. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or quotes a pass percentage, and decline anyone who describes themselves as the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Hiranandani Gardens, because that claim cannot be checked and nobody serious makes it.

Inside a township there is a practical layer too. A tutor coming weekly needs gate clearance, and the quickest route is for you to register the standing slot with your tower desk in the first week. For a two-child arrangement the tutor is in your flat for two or three hours, which is longer than most visitors, so tell the building manager that rather than letting it become a question later. Keep the door of the study room open for the first few weeks as ordinary care.

One last check that costs nothing: ask who marks the homework. A tutor who sets work and reviews it verbally next week is not marking. A tutor who writes on the page, with a correction the child has to redo, is. In a two-board household that written trail is the only way you will be able to tell, four weeks in, which child is actually moving.

sections.heading: One tutor inside the gate, two children, and the schedule that survives March
paragraphs: Hiranandani Foundation School sits inside Hiranandani Gardens, which produces a situation that exists in very few places in Mumbai: a child can walk home from school, and a tutor can hold four families without leaving the township. For a two-board household that is not a convenience, it is the thing that makes the arrangement viable at all. The tutor's travel cost across a week is one journey, not six, so the hours go into teaching rather than into JVLR.

It creates a density effect worth understanding before you rely on it. A tutor with four local families has a very full evening block between 4pm and 9pm, and that block is allocated by September. If you come looking in December for two slots on the same evening, the tutor who would have been perfect has nothing left. The families who get the good local tutors here are not the ones paying more; they are the ones who asked in July. For IB and IGCSE home tuition in Hiranandani Gardens the booking calendar is genuinely the binding constraint.

The second effect is informational. A tutor teaching two children from the same school knows what the Year 10 Chemistry test actually asked and how the DP1 cohort's IA briefing was worded, because they have seen both. That is valuable and it is also a boundary you should set explicitly. Ask the tutor to keep each child's diagnostic notes, marks and review separate, and not to discuss your children with the other families inside the gate. Most tutors will do this without being asked; saying it out loud costs nothing and prevents the awkward conversation.

The third effect is on replacement. If a tutor inside the township is not working out, the next best local option may be the tutor your neighbour already uses, with no hours free. So we keep one honest rule: if the fit is wrong, tell us at three sessions, not at three months. In September a rematch inside Powai is easy. In February it usually means an online tutor from elsewhere in Mumbai, which is a perfectly good answer but not the one you started with.

What all this adds up to is a practical sequence for a two-child flat here: ask early, book the examination child's slot first, keep the sibling's hours flexible, and set the privacy boundary on day one. Families who do those four things rarely need to rearrange anything in March, which is the month when rearranging is hardest.

sections.heading: What progress looks like when two children in Mumbai are on different boards
paragraphs: Judge them on different timescales, because the boards give you different evidence. For the IGCSE child, four weeks should produce a visible change in written method: corrections in the book, command words recognised, time taken per question dropping. Marks on a school test may not move for a term, and that is normal. For the IB child, four weeks should produce a clearer line of reasoning in a criterion task and a better first draft of whatever Internal Assessment is live, which you can see on the page even before any mark exists.

At one term, roughly a dozen sessions each, the honest pattern is improvement on the worked topics and no change elsewhere. If the Year 10's algebra was the focus, algebra should move while geography stays flat. If the DP student's exploration structure was the focus, the exploration should read better while Paper 1 performance is unchanged. A uniform improvement across everything usually means an easier test. No change anywhere means the sessions have become revision company, and you should raise it that week rather than at the end of term.

Across a full cycle the realistic claim is modest and specific. Students losing marks to technique, structure and timing recover a lot, because those are trainable inside months. Students with a genuine foundational gap, particularly in numeracy, improve steadily but do not transform in one year. We do not guarantee grades, we do not publish success rates, and we are suspicious of anyone who does, because the figure would depend entirely on which students they chose to count. What IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Hiranandani Gardens buy is attention and marking, not an outcome.

The hardest honest conversation is when one child is clearly moving and the other is not. That is usually a fit problem rather than an effort problem, and it is why we review each child separately rather than reporting on the flat as a whole. Replacement for one child while keeping the tutor for the other is completely normal and we arrange it without charge.

faqs.question: Can one tutor really teach both my IB and my IGCSE child?
faqs.answer: In Maths, Physics and usually Chemistry, yes. The content overlaps enough that a tutor comfortable with Diploma Programme material can handle an Extended-tier Cambridge paper, and the harder board sets the ceiling. In English, History and most languages the two boards ask for genuinely different skills and different assessment forms, and a single tutor ends up competent at one and approximate at the other. We will tell you which case you are in rather than selling the convenient answer, because a half-match across two children costs more in lost months than a second tutor costs in fees.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building for two back-to-back sessions?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the arrangement tutors prefer here. Two children in one flat means one journey for two or three hours of teaching, which is why local tutors price it better per child than two separate visits. The constraint is the tutor's own commute: someone from Chandivali, Powai or Kanjurmarg can run a 5pm to 8pm block comfortably, while a tutor crossing from the Western Suburbs along the SCLR will manage it for a month and then start arriving late. We match inside the corridor for double slots.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Hiranandani Gardens depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level first, because Higher Level Diploma Programme subjects and Extended-tier papers need more preparation per hour. Then subject scarcity: a second language or a specialist Higher Level science costs more than Maths because the pool is thin. Then the tutor's experience, particularly board teaching or marking history. Then travel distance, since a tutor crossing Mumbai prices road time in. Then session length and frequency. A household booking IB and IGCSE home tuition in Hiranandani Gardens for two children usually sees a lower per-child figure, because the travel is shared across both sessions. faqs.question: My younger child is in MYP and the report has no percentages. How do I know if there is a problem?
faqs.answer: Read the criterion strands rather than the overall comment. Middle Years Programme work is marked against published criteria, so a report showing consistent strength in one strand and weakness in another is telling you precisely where the gap is, even without a percentage. The common pattern is a child who knows the content but cannot structure an argument or reflect on method. Ask the subject teacher which criterion is weakest and what a stronger response would look like. That answer is the brief a tutor needs, and it is far more useful than a mark out of a hundred.

faqs.question: We are moving our child from IGCSE into the Diploma Programme next year. What should tuition do now?
faqs.answer: Build the two habits the IGCSE does not require. The first is sustained independent writing with a method the student chose and can defend, because every Diploma Programme subject carries an Internal Assessment and nothing in the IGCSE rehearses it. The second is reasoning shown on the page rather than answers produced quickly. A term of work on those two things before Diploma Programme Year 1 starts is worth more than a term of content preview, and it is the single most useful use of a transition summer for students coming off Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel papers.

faqs.question: Do you have any connection with Hiranandani Foundation School or Podar International School?

faqs.question: One child is improving and the other is not. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Review them separately and treat it as a fit problem until proven otherwise. We write a four-week review per child precisely so this is visible rather than averaged away. The common causes are a tutor whose strength is one board, a pace that suits one child's temperament and not the other's, or a shared session that was never appropriate across two boards. Replacing the tutor for one child while keeping them for the other is routine and costs nothing, and it is usually the right answer rather than pushing both children through the same arrangement.

faqs.question: Can the two children share a single session to save money?
faqs.answer: Not across boards. Two children on different boards in one hour means each gets half a lesson aimed at someone else's assessment, and the weaker student loses the most. Sharing can work between neighbours on the same board, the same tier and the same year group, which inside a township is more achievable than elsewhere because the students sit identical school papers. For siblings on different boards the saving comes from sharing the travel, not the hour: one visit, two consecutive sessions, one journey priced between you.

faqs.question: Does online tuition actually work for an IB student?
faqs.answer: It works well for some parts of the Diploma Programme and badly for others. Discussing an Internal Assessment draft, working through a past paper question, or reviewing feedback are all fine on a screen with a shared document. Building a habit in a student who is avoiding work is not: for that you need someone in the room. The practical test is whether your child would open the document unprompted. If yes, online saves travel and widens the pool across Mumbai. If no, pay the travel and keep IB and IGCSE home tuition in Hiranandani Gardens as the weekly anchor, with online used only for review.

faqs.question: How early should we book an evening home tuition slot for next year?
faqs.answer: July if you can, September at the latest. Local tutors inside Powai and Chandivali fill their 4pm to 9pm weekday block early, and a two-child household needs a bigger piece of that block than most. Families who enquire in December are choosing from whoever is left, which usually means a longer commute or an online match. The pool across Mumbai is large, so you will find someone good at any point in the year, but the specific advantage of a tutor five minutes from your gate is gone by the second term.

faqs.answer: Tell the tutor as early as you can and expect them to hold the slot only if you have agreed that in advance. The arrangement that works is to agree at the start how pauses are handled: slot held, slot released, or reduced hours through the gap. There is no lock-in contract with us, so the pause terms are between you and the tutor, and worth settling in writing in week one.

sections.heading: Two boards, two logics: what changes between IGCSE and the IB Diploma?
paragraphs: The International General Certificate of Secondary Education is a terminal examination system, and the IB Diploma Programme is a portfolio-plus-examination system. That one sentence explains most of what parents find confusing. At IGCSE the grade comes overwhelmingly from papers sat in a single series, with coursework in some subjects, which means revision technique and paper discipline carry enormous weight in the final months. In the DP the grade accumulates across two years through Internal Assessments, Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and final papers, so a bad term in DP1 is harder to recover from than a bad term in Year 10.

The practical consequence for tutoring is the shape of the work, not its difficulty. An IGCSE candidate needs timed papers, mark scheme familiarity and a clean approach to multi-step questions. A DP student needs deadline management as much as teaching, because the drafts and the EE do not wait for the subject to feel comfortable. Families running both at once often schedule the IGCSE child for intensive blocks near mocks and the DP child for a steady weekly slot across the year, which is the opposite of what intuition suggests.

Tiers and levels are the other place the two systems diverge. IGCSE subjects frequently split into Core and Extended entries, with the tier capping the grade available. The DP splits into Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), with HL adding content and depth rather than capping anything. Both decisions are made earlier than families expect and both are hard to reverse. Entry rules, level changes and deadlines are set by the boards and your school, so confirm them with the examinations officer or IB coordinator rather than with any website. Parents hunting for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Jogeshwari are usually looking for two specialists rather than one person, and the sooner that is accepted the better the term goes.

sections.heading: Subject choice at both ends, and the assessments that follow it
paragraphs: Subject choice at IGCSE sets up the DP two years later, and that link is the most under-discussed thing in a mixed-board household. A student who drops a science at Year 10, or takes Core-tier Mathematics, narrows what is realistic at Higher Level in the DP, and nobody mentions it at the time. If you have one child choosing IGCSE options and another already in the DP, you are holding both ends of the same decision, which is a genuine advantage if you use it. Ask your older child's coordinator which IGCSE foundations actually mattered.

Each system then loads its own internal work. At IGCSE several subjects carry coursework or practical components owned and marked by the school. In the DP every subject carries an Internal Assessment, mathematics carries an exploration, the sciences carry an investigation, and above them sit TOK and the EE. Those are the pieces parents cannot help with and where a specialist earns the fee. Asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Jogeshwari from one person sounds efficient and produces a generalist who cannot supervise either.

What a tutor should bring to any of it is the marking language rather than the content. What explain demands that describe does not. Why a conclusion has to refer back to the research question. Where method marks sit in a long calculation. This is teachable in weeks and it is where most of the recoverable marks live in both systems. Component names, weightings, word limits and submission windows change between syllabus versions, so take structure from the current guide for the year your child is sitting, and from the school. A single home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai does not exist, while a specialist for one subject at one stage almost always does.

sections.heading: When a Mumbai household runs on two school calendars at once
paragraphs: Two boards means two sets of deadlines that do not line up, and the collision is predictable enough to plan for. Bombay Cambridge International School at Andheri East runs the Cambridge pathway, with mocks in the winter and a terminal series in the spring. Oberoi International School on JVLR at Goregaon East runs the IB route through the Primary Years Programme, MYP and DP, where Internal Assessment drafts and criterion-marked tasks arrive through the autumn. A household with one child at each lives through two separate crunches rather than one shared one.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform, not affiliated with Oberoi International School, Bombay Cambridge International School or any other school named on this page, and with no connection to the International Baccalaureate organisation, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. The schools are named because families in this part of Mumbai, Maharashtra attend them and their calendars decide when tutoring is worth paying for. We do not guarantee grades, for either child.

If you want one planning rule, it is this: protect the autumn for the DP child and the winter for the IGCSE child. From late October the MYP criteria marks and DP drafts arrive together, which is when IB households in Jogeshwari start looking. December and January are IGCSE mock season, which is when the other half of the household panics. By March both children are in revision and nobody is available to help either of them. Booking home classes in September costs the same per session as booking them in March and buys three times as much work across Mumbai's school year.

sections.heading: Does home tuition in Mumbai work when two children share the slot?
paragraphs: Only if they are at the same stage in the same subject, and usually not even then. Two children taught together means the pace is set by the slower one and the attention is split exactly when one of them needs it, which is why we normally arrange consecutive individual slots instead. The exception that genuinely works is two students in the same IGCSE subject and tier sitting the same series, where timed paper practice and mark scheme discussion can be shared productively. A DP student and a Year 9 student in the same session is not a saving, it is two half-lessons.

What does work across a mixed-board household is mixing the modes. Put the child who will not start work alone with a tutor in the room, and let the self-managing DP student take a shorter online session for draft feedback and question clearing. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Jogeshwari is a reasonable answer for a scarce subject such as Economics or Accounting, and the wrong answer for a twelve-year-old who needs supervision rather than explanation.

Hybrid is what most two-child households here settle into by the second month: one in-person session each per week and one online top-up for whichever child has a deadline. It keeps the evenings survivable and it protects the week when heavy rain shuts the Western Express Highway. Honest trade-off: online sessions need a parent to enforce the start time and a laptop with the work open, not a phone. Families who accept that get real value. Families who do not spend a term paying for a child watching a screen, which is why home classes stay the anchor of most arrangements we make in Mumbai.

sections.heading: Checking a tutor who claims to teach both boards
paragraphs: Some tutors genuinely teach both systems well, and many claim to. The difference shows up in one question: ask them to describe how the same topic is assessed differently in each. A tutor who can explain that an IGCSE question rewards a clean multi-step method while a DP Internal Assessment rewards a justified methodology and an evaluation of its limits has taught both. A tutor who answers in generalities about concepts and understanding has taught one and read about the other. Any IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai worth hiring will answer that question in specifics within a minute.

Our own checks cover identity, the qualification claimed, the specific boards and stages taught, and a reference from that recent teaching. During vetting every tutor is asked to talk through a piece of real marked student work and explain where the marks were lost. That exercise removes more applicants than any document check does, and it removes almost everyone who claims comprehensive coverage of both systems at every level.

Your own list is short and you should use it on the call. Which board and stage did you teach last academic year? Name the papers or the assessment components in my child's subject. What will you show me after four weeks? Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, quotes a success rate, or says they handle every subject on both boards. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Jogeshwari who says honestly that they only do one of the two is more useful than one who says yes to everything.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma Programme crossing, and the year it goes wrong
paragraphs: The hardest year in a mixed-board household is the one where a child finishes Year 11 and starts DP1, because almost everything that worked stops working. A student who got good IGCSE grades through disciplined revision in the last three months arrives in a system where the marks accumulate from week four and cannot be caught up in a sprint. Parents read the first DP1 report as a shock. It is usually a method problem: the child is still waiting for the revision phase that the DP never has.

The specific failures are predictable. Note-taking that was adequate for a terminal paper is not adequate for an Internal Assessment two years later. A student who never had to choose a research question now has to choose several. Reading loads in TOK and the humanities are far higher than anything at IGCSE. And Higher Level Mathematics assumes an Extended-tier fluency that a Core-tier candidate never built. Each of those has a different remedy and the useful time to apply them is the first term of DP1, not the second year.

This is where a household running both boards has an advantage over one that does not. You can see the crossing coming, because you are watching the younger child build the habits the older child needed. Use the IGCSE years to build the two things the DP actually requires: working that someone else can follow, and a student who can start a piece of work without being told to. Families arranging IB and IGCSE home tuition in Jogeshwari in the Year 11 summer, rather than in DP1 November, consistently get an easier crossing.

sections.heading: What should four weeks of home classes change in Jogeshwari?
paragraphs: Four specific things, and a grade is not one of them. Each child should be able to say what a task is asking before starting it. The written work should have a structure someone else can follow. The tutor should be able to name the weak topics rather than describing the subject. And the slot should have held four times. In a two-child household there is a fifth: the two arrangements should be assessed separately, because a parent who is pleased with one tutor tends to give the other one longer than it deserves.

Across a term the two boards show progress differently. IGCSE progress appears on timed papers, so sit one at the start and one at the end and compare them against the real mark scheme. DP progress appears in drafts and in how early the student starts them, which is less satisfying to look at and more predictive of the final grade. A DP student who begins an Internal Assessment draft three weeks before it is due has changed more than one whose test mark moved by two points. Four weeks of home tuition in Mumbai should produce that kind of change, not a reassuring report.

We do not guarantee grades, publish no success rates and will not claim to be the strongest option in Mumbai, since none of that is checkable. What we will do at each review is tell you when the limiting factor is not teaching. A subject chosen for the wrong reason, an entry tier that caps the outcome, four tutors across two children and no time left to do the homework. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Jogeshwari are worth paying when they are aimed at a real obstacle.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Jogeshwari, Mumbai
paragraphs: Send one message covering both children. For the IGCSE child: the board, the tier per subject and the exam series. For the IB child: the programme, the year group and whether each subject is Higher Level or Standard Level. For both: the most recent marked work rather than the grade, and the evenings that genuinely exist. Say if you want consecutive slots, because that changes which tutors we approach first.

Each first session should be a diagnosis rather than a lesson. Expect the tutor to go through recent marked work question by question, ask the student to explain two of their own answers, set one piece under timing or to a deadline, and finish with three named topics in priority order. You should know what the next month holds by the end of the hour. If a first session was a chapter delivered from the tutor's own notes, raise it at the four-week review rather than hoping it corrects itself. Good home tuition in Mumbai starts from your child's last marked script and works outwards from the errors in it.

Logistics that save the first week: a table in a room with a door, the calculator and textbook out, phones elsewhere, and both tutors' names left at the building gate in advance so nobody loses twenty minutes downstairs. If a subject is scarce, say so rather than compromising. Jogeshwari sits where JVLR meets the Western Line, which makes an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Jogeshwari findable for subjects that would be hard to source two stations further north.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach my IGCSE child and my IB child?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and only where the subject and the gap in level are both narrow. A Mathematics teacher who works with an IGCSE Year 10 student and an MYP Year 4 student can often do both well. The same person covering IGCSE Extended Mathematics and Diploma Programme Higher Level Mathematics in one evening is far rarer, because the second involves an exploration and a different kind of reasoning. Ask any tutor claiming both to describe how the same topic is assessed differently on each board. The answer separates genuine dual-board teachers from people who have read a syllabus summary.

faqs.question: Can two tutors visit our building on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is usually the better arrangement. Consecutive individual slots mean each child gets full attention, the tutors each make one journey, and your household loses one evening rather than two. Register both names at the security desk in advance with the fixed weekly times, since the first visit is the one that gets delayed while someone calls upstairs. Most buildings around Jogeshwari will issue standing entry for regular weekly tuition once a resident confirms it. Ask the tutors to arrive ten minutes apart rather than together.

faqs.question: Should both children have home tuition or only the one struggling?
faqs.answer: Start with the child where the gap between current work and the school's expectation is widest, and resist symmetry for its own sake. Adding a tutor for the second child because the first has one is how households end up with four sessions a week and no time for homework. The exception is the year a child crosses from Year 11 into the Diploma Programme, where a short, deliberate block of work on note-taking and independent starting is worth more than waiting for the first DP1 report to arrive.

faqs.question: How do travel and evening timing work for tutors coming here?
faqs.answer: Earlier is better and the difference is large. A tutor coming along JVLR from Powai, or on Metro Line 1 from Andheri East, reaches Jogeshwari comfortably for a half past five or six o'clock start. After seven the Western Express Highway peak makes the same journey unpredictable, and unpredictable slots are the ones that quietly stop in month two. For two children, an early start matters twice over, because the second session begins when the first ends. Offer two possible evenings and we will tell you which produces the better shortlist.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Jogeshwari depend on?
faqs.answer: Stage and subject scarcity first, then travel, then session length and frequency. Diploma Programme Higher Level work and Extended-tier IGCSE sciences sit above earlier-year support, because the pool of people who teach them is much smaller. Scarce subjects such as Economics, Accounting and less common languages cost more again. Travel matters here in a specific way: a tutor already working the Andheri East to Powai run absorbs the journey, while one crossing the suburbs prices it in. Ask for a per session and a monthly figure, and ask about missed sessions before you book.

faqs.question: Is one board easier than the other?
faqs.answer: They are differently demanding rather than harder or easier, and the honest comparison is about shape. IGCSE concentrates the pressure into a final series, which suits a student who performs under exam conditions and punishes one who does not. The Diploma Programme spreads it across two years of Internal Assessments, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which suits a student who works steadily and punishes one who sprints. Choose on the child rather than on reputation, and ask the school which of its own students have moved between the two and how it went.

faqs.question: My child is moving from IGCSE to the IB Diploma. When should we start help?
faqs.answer: The summer between Year 11 and DP1, if you can, and the first term of DP1 at the latest. The crossing fails in a predictable way: a student who earned good IGCSE grades through a disciplined final sprint arrives in a system where marks accumulate from the first weeks. Work in that window on note-taking that will still be useful in two years, on starting a piece of writing without being told to, and on the mathematics fluency that Higher Level assumes. Waiting for the first DP1 report means losing a term to a diagnosis you could have made in advance.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to Oberoi International School, Bombay Cambridge International School or any other school named on this site, and no connection to the International Baccalaureate organisation, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools are named because families here attend them and their calendars decide when tutoring is useful. Any tutor or service implying a formal relationship with a named school, or implying that a school endorses them, is making a claim worth checking with the school before you pay anything.

faqs.question: What happens if one tutor works out and the other does not?
faqs.answer: We replace the one that is not working and leave the other alone, usually within the week, with no notice period and nothing to negotiate. This is exactly why we review each child separately. Parents who are pleased with one arrangement tend to extend the benefit of the doubt to the other for a month longer than they should. Tell us what specifically failed, since a stage mismatch needs a different specialist while a clash of style needs a different personality, and the two produce very different shortlists.

faqs.question: Do we need a tutor for Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Usually not a weekly one, and sometimes a few targeted sessions. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are supervised by the school, and a tutor who starts restructuring either can put a student at odds with their supervisor. Where outside help genuinely pays is at two moments: choosing a workable research question, and reading a first draft for structure and argument rather than content. Three or four sessions at the right points beat a standing weekly slot, and your child's supervisor should know that outside help is being used.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come at the weekend instead of a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a two-child household it is often the better answer. A weekend morning is long enough for one child to sit a timed paper and the other to work through a draft, which split weekday hours cannot do. Weekend slots also reach tutors who have no weekday evening left, including people travelling down from Kandivali and Borivali on Metro Lines 2A and 7. The trade-off is that the weekend is the only unstructured time your children have, so one weekend and one weekday session usually beats two weekend ones.

faqs.question: How many subjects should each child start with?
faqs.answer: One each, and a second only if the evenings genuinely exist after homework. The commonest mistake in mixed-board households is starting four tutors across two children in the same month, which leaves everyone with more work set and less time to do it. Pick the subject per child where the gap to the school's expectation is widest, fix the method there, and watch whether it transfers. If two subjects are genuinely urgent for one child, alternate them weekly rather than stacking two sessions onto a single evening.

sections.heading: Setting up IB and IGCSE home tuition in Juhu that survives a full term
paragraphs: Arrangements fail for boring reasons, so the setup is built around the boring reasons. Before a tutor is suggested, we establish three things: which evening is genuinely protected in your child's week, which board and year each child in the house is in, and what the single outcome is that would make you call this worthwhile. Families who skip the third question end up six weeks into a pleasant engagement that nobody can evaluate. Families who answer it get a tutor who plans backwards from it.

Then the slot is designed before the teacher is chosen, which is the reverse of how most parents approach it. A tutor is matched to an evening you can defend against football practice, Diploma Programme rehearsals and your own travel, because a slot that moves weekly stops being a routine and becomes a negotiation. For most households in the Juhu–JVPD corridor the workable windows are late afternoon on a weekday or a fixed weekend morning, and a tutor who already teaches nearby on that day is worth more than one with a better CV and a worse diary.

The first session is diagnostic and the fourth is a review, and both are scheduled at the start rather than promised vaguely. A trial runs at your flat so you see the arrangement as it will actually be, not as a phone call describes it. After four weeks there is a proper conversation about what has changed, what has not, and whether the plan or the person needs adjusting. Setting that date in advance is what makes it happen; a review nobody booked is a review nobody holds.

Only after all of that does continuity get discussed, and it should be discussed on day one rather than in the week it breaks. Who covers a session if the tutor has a family obligation. What happens during your child's school exam leave. Whether the arrangement pauses or thins out in the summer. These are the questions that decide whether IB and IGCSE home tuition in Juhu lasts three terms or three months, and they cost nothing to answer in advance.

sections.heading: Which board is setting the deadlines in your house?
paragraphs: Whichever child has the nearer non-negotiable deadline, and in a two-board household that answer changes twice a year. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs on internally assessed coursework that is handed in against school-set dates spread through the year: Primary Years Programme (PYP) exhibition work, Middle Years Programme (MYP) personal project milestones, and in the Diploma Programme (DP) a sequence of Internal Assessment (IA) drafts, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) tasks. Cambridge IGCSE concentrates far more of its weight into a terminal examination series with mocks ahead of it.

That structural difference has a practical consequence most families discover late. An IB child's pressure arrives as a rolling series of submission dates that can be planned around months in advance, while an IGCSE child's pressure arrives as a wall. So the sensible pattern for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Juhu is uneven by design: steady, lighter support for the IB child timed to land three weeks before each draft deadline, and a flatter baseline for the Cambridge child that steepens sharply through the mock and final series.

The choice points also differ, and both deserve a tutor's input rather than only the school's. On the Cambridge side it is the Core and Extended tier decision, usually taken in Year 9 or early Year 10, which quietly sets a ceiling on what a candidate can be awarded. On the IB side it is Higher Level and Standard Level allocation, taken at the start of the Diploma Programme and painful to reverse later. Both decisions are made on evidence a good tutor can supply: what the child can currently do unaided, under time pressure, without prompting.

Do not take weightings, submission windows or paper structures from any brief, article or forum, including this page. The IB and Cambridge International Education both revise subject guides on their own cycles, so the structure that applies to the year your child actually sits sits in the current subject guide and with the school's Diploma Programme coordinator or examinations officer. What you should expect a tutor to know is which components your child faces, what each one rewards, and roughly when in the school year each one bites.

sections.heading: How many subjects can a single weekly arrangement carry?
paragraphs: Two subjects per tutor, three at a stretch, and beyond that you are buying supervision rather than teaching. The arithmetic is unforgiving: a ninety-minute session split across four subjects gives each one twenty-two minutes, which is enough to review homework and not enough to repair anything. Parents arrive at four-subject arrangements by accretion, adding a subject each time a report disappoints, and then wonder why nothing moves. The honest fix is to cut the list, not extend the hour.

Depth also varies by what the subject is made of. Mathematics and the sciences reward frequent short contact because the skills compound and errors are specific and correctable. Essay subjects reward fewer, longer sessions built around a redraft cycle, since there is no point meeting weekly if nothing has been written in between. Coursework-bearing components in both boards sit differently again: the tutor's work there is planning, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafting, and the authenticity declaration stays with the candidate and the school.

When a household genuinely needs breadth, two specialists on alternating evenings beats one generalist on five. It costs a little more in coordination and considerably less in wasted hours, and it means each tutor is teaching the subject they actually know rather than revising alongside your child. IB Gram's panel covers all IB and IGCSE subjects and the tutor in Juhu you keep will usually be matched narrowly on purpose, with a second name added only where the first cannot cover a component properly.

One more thing about stacking subjects: the limiting resource is almost never tuition time, it is your child's unsupervised practice time. Every extra tutored hour removes an hour in which the work gets consolidated alone, which is where learning actually sticks. A week with three tutored sessions and no quiet practice produces a student who recognises everything and can do nothing under exam conditions. Build the week around the practice first, then fit the sessions in around it.

sections.heading: What a standing Juhu slot costs a tutor in travel every week
paragraphs: Worth understanding, because that cost is what makes an arrangement durable or fragile. A tutor holding a weekly evening in Juhu is spending unpaid time on the road twice, and the size of that unpaid block decides whether your slot is the one they protect or the one they quietly drop when their diary tightens. Tutors drawn from Juhu itself and JVPD Scheme are effectively neighbours. Vile Parle West keeps them on the convenient side of the Western Express Highway and near the Vile Parle / Santacruz station access. Khar West is one stop along the Western Line with a straightforward Link Road run outside peak hour.

The geometry of the Western Suburbs explains why those four places and not others. The suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, so a tutor travelling Bandra to Andheri is quick off-peak and painful at 6pm. Matching along the line, Khar to Santacruz or Malad to Kandivali, works far better than matching across it. A standing arrangement therefore survives best when the tutor's whole evening runs in one direction: a 5pm student in Khar West and a 7pm student in Juhu is a sustainable week, while two students on opposite sides of the highway is not.

This is why we would rather tell you the travel reality than sell you a wider radius. A tutor from Andheri West or Goregaon can absolutely hold a Juhu slot, and plenty do, usually by picking a time that dodges the worst of the highway or by using Metro Line 1 between Versova, Andheri and Ghatkopar and Metro Lines 2A and 7 along the Dahisar to Andheri corridor. What they cannot do is hold a 7.30pm Juhu slot three terms running while also keeping students further north. Something gives, and it is rarely the student who lives closest to them.

For families comparing all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Juhu providers offer, ask one question that cuts through everything: where does the tutor go immediately before and immediately after my session? An answer that describes a tidy run along one corridor is a slot that will still exist in March. An answer that criss-crosses Mumbai is a slot that will be renegotiated by December. Parents searching for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Juhu are really asking about this travel arithmetic, whether or not they would put it that way.

sections.heading: Two report cycles in one Juhu, Mumbai household
paragraphs: Juhu holds the deepest IB school cluster outside the Bandra Kurla Complex. Ecole Mondiale World School, Jamnabai Narsee International School and Utpal Shanghvi Global School sit within a few kilometres of each other, with Billabong High International School also serving families here, so PYP, MYP, Diploma Programme and Cambridge requests all land on the same small local pool. The consequence specific to this corridor is that two-board households are normal rather than unusual: an older child on a Cambridge pathway and a younger one in the MYP, or two children at different campuses with entirely different reporting rhythms.

That produces a scheduling problem no single-board family has. One child's report arrives with criterion-referenced descriptors and a comment on approaches to learning; the other's arrives with percentage scores against mock papers. They land in different months. They trigger different conversations. A household running one tuition arrangement across both is effectively running two calendars, and the arrangement needs to know in advance which month belongs to which child, otherwise the louder deadline takes the hours every time and the quieter child drifts.

The practical answer is to map the year once, in September, with both school calendars side by side. Mark the Diploma Programme draft deadlines, the MYP project milestones, the Cambridge mock window and the final series. Then decide in advance which four to six weeks belong to which child, and tell the tutor. A tutor who knows in October that February belongs to the Cambridge candidate plans the autumn differently. A tutor told in February plans nothing; they just absorb the panic.

What a good one will do is tell you which weeks of the Mumbai school year are going to hurt, and get ahead of them.

sections.heading: Keeping home classes running when the week falls apart in Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tuition is the lead arrangement here and the one most families start with, because a tutor at your table sees the real exercise book, the abandoned working and the question your child skipped rather than a clean screen. It also holds attendance together, since nobody has to travel and the session happens whether or not anyone feels motivated. For a long-running engagement across two boards, IB and IGCSE home tuition in Juhu is usually the spine of the plan, with everything else arranged around it.

The reason to set up an online capability anyway is continuity, not preference. Over three terms a weekly slot will be hit by a monsoon evening that defeats the road, a tutor with a fever, a school event that moves the whole family's schedule, and a week when your child is away. Each of those is a lost session if home tuition is the only mode available, and a moved session if it is not. Agreeing in week one that the fallback is an online meeting the same evening converts most of those losses into inconvenience.

Cover when a tutor is genuinely unavailable for a stretch is the harder case, and it should be answered before it happens. The options are a short pause with work set remotely, a stand-in from the same verified pool with a written handover of what has been covered, or a temporary online arrangement with the original tutor from wherever they are. All three are acceptable; what is not acceptable is finding out on the evening itself. Ask how a prospective tutor has handled a two-week absence before, and whether an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Juhu can be slotted in as cover without restarting the diagnosis.

Hybrid, once families try it for continuity reasons, often becomes the permanent shape. The main teaching happens in person weekly, a shorter online check runs midweek to look at marked work and unstick one problem, and the whole thing moves online for a fortnight when circumstances demand. It also solves the scarce-subject problem without drama: a nearby tutor for the regular evening, a distant specialist online for the component that needs genuine depth. Decide the mix deliberately rather than drifting into it after a cancellation.

sections.heading: Re-checking a tutor in Mumbai after two terms, not before the first session
paragraphs: The initial checks are the easy half. Before any name reaches you, IB Gram verifies government photo identity, the qualifications claimed, and the board and level experience relevant to your request, so a tutor who says they teach Diploma Programme Chemistry and Cambridge IGCSE Biology is asked which components and which years, and the answer is matched against their record. References from previous families are checked where they exist. That is the standard everyone advertises, and it only tells you whether somebody was suitable on the day they joined.

What nobody checks is the second half: whether the arrangement is still doing what it was hired to do after two terms. Long engagements drift. Sessions become homework supervision. The original weakness gets fixed and nobody notices the plan was never updated. A tutor who was excellent for Year 9 consolidation may be the wrong person for Year 11 examination technique, and because the relationship is comfortable, the mismatch can run for months. The parent is the only person positioned to catch this, which is why the four-week review should repeat every term rather than once at the start.

The termly re-check is four questions and it takes ten minutes. What are the two weaknesses you are working on now, and are they the same ones as last term. What has my child done unaided in the last fortnight that they could not do before. What is the next assessment and what is the plan for it. What would you change if we had one extra hour a week, or one fewer. A tutor who answers those crisply is working from a plan. A tutor who answers in generalities is working from habit.

On claims, hold the line the whole way through, not just at the start. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and you should be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, publishes a success rate, or implies a relationship with a school. A good sign in the other direction is a tutor who volunteers bad news early: that a target is unrealistic from here, that the hours are being wasted, or that a different subject needs the slot more. Parents comparing the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Juhu on charm alone tend to miss how much that honesty is worth.
bullets: Identity, qualifications and component experience verified before shortlisting
Repeat the four-week review every term, not once
Ask whether this term's weaknesses differ from last term's
Be wary of quoted success rates or promises about a grade
Value a tutor who volunteers bad news early

sections.heading: How many hours a week of home tuition actually move a grade?
paragraphs: For one subject, ninety minutes a week outside the examination term and two sessions a week inside it, with the second session shorter rather than longer. That is the shape that works for most students across both boards, and the reason is not generosity with your money: beyond roughly three hours a week in a single subject, additional tutored time displaces the independent practice that converts explanation into recall. The student who is tutored five hours a week and practises none is the student who understands everything in the room and freezes in the hall.

Term-long and examination-term arrangements are different products and should be priced and planned as such. A term-long arrangement is about coverage and habit: topics in sequence, work set and marked, weaknesses logged and revisited. An examination-term arrangement is about yield per hour: past papers under time, mark schemes read properly, and ruthless prioritisation of the topics where marks are still recoverable. Families who run the first shape all the way into the final six weeks waste the most valuable part of the year on syllabus they will not be asked.

What the rate includes is the question parents ask last and should ask second. A sensible arrangement covers the session itself, work set for the gap, marking of that work, and a short written or verbal update to you. It does not automatically cover marking a full mock paper, reading a Diploma Programme Internal Assessment draft end to end, attending a parent meeting, or a three-hour revision block in study week. Those are real work and most tutors will do them, as extra. Establish that boundary while everyone is relaxed rather than in the week before a deadline.

Fees across Mumbai depend on five things and we will tell you which one is moving yours. Board and level, since Higher Level Diploma Programme work and Year 11 Extended work are priced differently from middle-school support. Subject scarcity, which is the largest single factor. Travel distance, because a tutor crossing two suburbs in evening traffic is selling an hour they cannot teach in. Session length and frequency. And the tutor's own examining or school background. We will not publish a price list for IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Juhu, because any number printed here would be wrong for most of the families reading it. Ask any IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai families recommend to say which of those five factors is driving their rate, and treat a flat citywide figure as a sign that nobody has looked at your case.
bullets: One subject: ninety minutes weekly, two shorter sessions in exam term
Past three hours a week, tutoring displaces independent practice
Term-long buys coverage; exam-term buys yield per hour
Mock marking and draft reading sit outside the standard rate
Rates move on level, scarcity, travel, frequency and background

sections.heading: How progress reaches you between sessions in Mumbai
paragraphs: Through marked work and two sentences, weekly, and if you are not getting both you cannot evaluate anything. The marked work matters more than the message: a page your child attempted alone, with a tutor's corrections on it, tells you in thirty seconds what a paragraph of reassurance cannot. The two sentences should name what was covered and what was still shaky. Any tutor can produce this in the time it takes to send a message from the lift, and a tutor who will not produce it for three terms is asking you to take progress on trust. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families keep across several years is usually just one who marks the work and reports it without being chased.

The four-week mark is about habits, not marks. Expect to see your child reading a question before attacking it, working more legibly, attempting past-paper questions without being nagged, and a tutor who can name two specific weaknesses and the plan for each. At one term, internal test scores usually move, unevenly, and the real gain shows up as fewer avoidable losses: units dropped, command words misread, the last question abandoned for time. Across a full examination cycle, honest teaching improves the odds and narrows the spread of outcomes. It does not eliminate the spread, and we do not guarantee grades.

Some limits cannot be argued with and are better said plainly. A two-year gap in foundational algebra or in written English cannot be closed in the six weeks before a terminal paper, and the right plan at that point is triage: maximise the marks that are still reachable and stop pretending about the rest. A student who does nothing between sessions improves slowly whoever teaches them. And no arrangement fixes a subject that was the wrong choice, which is why the tier and level decisions earlier on this page matter more than any number of hours later.

When the arrangement stops working, move early. Tell us what specifically is wrong, whether it is timing, teaching style, level experience or a personality mismatch, and we return to the same verified pool. Most changes in the Juhu–JVPD corridor happen for scheduling reasons rather than competence. A replacement usually starts inside a week and receives a handover of coverage so your child is not restarted from zero, and you are not committed to a term you have already stopped believing in.
bullets: Weekly marked work plus two sentences is the minimum reporting
Four weeks: habits and two named weaknesses, not grades
One term: fewer avoidable losses and uneven score movement
Six weeks out, triage recoverable marks honestly
Replacements start inside a week with a coverage handover

sections.heading: Starting a term of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Juhu
paragraphs: Send four things and the setup takes days rather than weeks. The most recent report for each child with the teacher comments left in. The board, year and subjects, including which tier or level each subject sits at. The one evening per child you can genuinely protect, allowing for a tutor arriving from Khar West or Vile Parle West at that hour. And one sentence per child on what you want changed, because a parent who writes that the problem is unfinished Internal Assessment drafts gets a sharper first session than one who writes that school is going badly.

You will get two or three verified names, and you speak to each before anything is booked. A trial session runs at your flat. The fourth session is the review, booked on the day you start. Cover arrangements, the online fallback for a monsoon evening, and the rules for school exam leave are all agreed in that first week, in writing, while nobody is under pressure. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Juhu families keep for years is almost always one whose arrangement was set up properly in week one.

Timing in this corridor is worth one specific warning. The Juhu cluster's Diploma Programme deadline waves take the experienced local tutors off the market twice a year, and the Cambridge mock window takes another slice. A request made six weeks before those crunches produces a materially better shortlist than the identical request made during them, at the same rate. If you already know February is going to be difficult, start the conversation in November, which is also when the rest of Mumbai has not yet begun looking.

Nothing on this page is a promise about an outcome. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named here, and we do not guarantee grades. What we will do is tell you what the arrangement includes, what it costs you in hours as well as money, what the first month should look like, and when the honest answer is that your child needs fewer tutored hours and more quiet practice instead.
bullets: Send reports, boards, tiers and one protected evening per child
Interview two or three verified names before booking anything
Agree cover, online fallback and exam-leave rules in writing
Start six weeks before the Juhu deadline crunches
Expect honesty about hours, including fewer of them

faqs.question: What does a typical week of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Juhu look like?
faqs.answer: One protected session per subject per week, work set for the gap, that work marked before the next session, and a short message to you about what moved. Outside the examination term that is usually ninety minutes; inside it, a second shorter session is added. The parts parents overlook are the gap and the message, which is where most of the actual learning and nearly all of the accountability live. A week with a long session and nothing in between produces a child who follows along in the room and stalls on their own.

faqs.question: What happens to our slot when the tutor is away for a week?
faqs.answer: It should be answered before it happens, and there are three acceptable answers. The tutor runs the session online from wherever they are. A stand-in from the same verified pool takes it with a written handover of what has been covered. Or the week pauses with work set remotely and the session is made up later. Which one applies depends on the subject and how close an assessment is. The unacceptable version is finding out on the evening itself, so ask any prospective tutor how they handled a two-week absence previously.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover a Diploma Programme child and an IGCSE child at home in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is worth testing rather than assuming. It works when the subject is shared and the two students are far enough apart in level that the tutor teaches them in sequence rather than together, which realistically means two separate hours back to back rather than one blended session. It stops working when both children have assessments in the same fortnight, because one of them always loses. In a two-board household we usually recommend separate tutors on separate evenings, which costs more in coordination and far less in wasted attention.

faqs.question: Should we pay by session or commit to a full term?
faqs.answer: Pay in short blocks and review at four weeks. Session-by-session sounds flexible but tends to produce a casual arrangement that gets cancelled whenever the week is busy, which is exactly when the session is most needed. A full term paid up front removes your leverage if the match is wrong. A block of four to six sessions with a scheduled review keeps both the commitment and the exit. Whatever the structure, agree in advance what happens to a session cancelled by you with less than a day's notice.

faqs.question: Does the rate cover marking and feedback between sessions?
faqs.answer: Ordinary homework marking and a short update to you should be included, and most tutors treat that as part of the job. What usually sits outside the standard rate is heavier work: marking a full mock paper against a mark scheme, reading a Diploma Programme Internal Assessment draft end to end, writing a formal progress report, attending a school meeting, or running a long revision block during study week. All of that is real work and most tutors will do it as an addition. Settle the boundary in week one rather than the week before a deadline.

faqs.question: How much notice do you need to cancel an evening session?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four hours is the fair standard, and it protects both sides. A tutor who has already set out from Khar West or Vile Parle West has spent the unpaid half of their evening, so a same-day cancellation is usually chargeable, while a session cancelled with proper notice should simply be rescheduled. Agree this explicitly at the start, including what happens when school activities move at short notice, which in the Juhu cluster happens several times a term. A clear rule prevents the awkward conversation entirely.

faqs.question: Can we pause home tuition during school exam leave and restart afterwards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a pause is often the right call rather than a concession. During a school examination fortnight most students need quiet revision time more than new teaching, so a reduced arrangement, one short session a week focused on technique and paper strategy, usually beats either a full schedule or a complete stop. Tell the tutor the dates as soon as the school publishes them, because a tutor who knows in advance can fill that period with another student rather than losing the income and the slot.

faqs.question: Where in the flat should a home tuition session actually happen?
faqs.answer: At a table in a shared space, with the television off and younger siblings out of earshot. A bedroom desk sounds focused and usually is not, because the bed, the phone charger and the door all work against ninety minutes of concentration. The practical requirements are simple: a surface big enough for two past papers side by side, a chair your child can sit upright in, decent light, a plug point and a reliable internet connection for the weeks the session runs online. A parent within earshot but not hovering over the page is the right distance.

faqs.question: Do we increase the hours in the exam term or keep them steady all year?
faqs.answer: Increase frequency rather than session length, and change the content rather than just the volume. Two shorter sessions a week beat one long one as papers approach, because retrieval works better spaced out than stacked. The content should switch from syllabus coverage to timed past papers, mark scheme reading and prioritising the topics where marks are still recoverable. Adding a third or fourth hour of the same term-time teaching in the final six weeks is the most common way families spend more and gain less.

faqs.question: What should the tutor send us between sessions?
faqs.answer: Marked work and two sentences, every week. The marked work is the evidence, since a page your child attempted alone with corrections on it tells you more in thirty seconds than any summary. The two sentences should say what was covered and what is still shaky. Once a term you should also get something longer: what has changed, what the next assessment is, and what the plan for it is. If a tutor resists that level of reporting across three terms, they are asking you to take progress entirely on trust.

faqs.question: Is it better to switch tutors between IGCSE and the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, at least for the examined subjects. The two boards reward genuinely different things: Cambridge IGCSE pays for accurate, well-structured answers to tightly specified questions, while the Diploma Programme pays for sustained independent work on internally assessed tasks plus examination papers with a different command vocabulary. A tutor strong at one is not automatically strong at the other. Where a good relationship already exists, ask directly which Diploma Programme components they have taught through to a final series, and believe the answer either way.

faqs.question: How does parking and building access work for a tutor who drives to Juhu?
faqs.answer: Settle it once and it never resurfaces. Tell your society office or security desk that the same visitor is coming weekly on a fixed day so the name sits on a standing list rather than being re-argued at the gate each week, and tell the tutor where a visitor car can actually stand in your lane. Parking is the quiet reason some tutors prefer public transport to this corridor, which is one more argument for hiring from Juhu, JVPD Scheme, Vile Parle West or Khar West where the trip can be made without a car.

sections.heading: How IB and IGCSE home tuition in JVPD Scheme gets arranged
paragraphs: A household brief is not two separate enquiries typed into one message, and treating it as one is how families end up with two tutors arriving on the same evening and nobody at the table. We ask for the shape of the week first: who is home when, who leaves again for an activity, which evening is already lost to something, and whether one adult is available to open the door. Only then do we ask about subjects. On these plots the limiting resource is usually the study table, not the budget.

Once the week is mapped, the matching question is whether one tutor can genuinely serve both children or whether two are needed. The honest test is subject and level, not goodwill. A tutor who has taught Mathematics to Year 10 and to Middle Years Programme (MYP) Year 4 can often hold both; a tutor who claims Extended sciences for Year 11 and Higher Level Chemistry for a Diploma Programme (DP) student should be asked which internal assessments he has actually supervised. IB and IGCSE home tuition in JVPD Scheme works best when the answer is specific rather than enthusiastic.

The shortlist is then two or three verified profiles, with the household constraint stated plainly to each of them: back-to-back slots, two children, one table. Tutors who have run that arrangement before say so immediately and tell you how they handle the twenty minutes in the middle. Tutors who have not will agree and then discover in week two that two consecutive hours in one house is harder work than two hours in two houses.

After that it is the ordinary sequence, with one addition. A free discovery call with each candidate. A diagnostic session per child rather than per booking, because the two children need separate written assessments. Payment only once you have chosen. And a single review conversation at two to four weeks covering both, so you are not holding two parallel relationships with two sets of notes you have to reconcile yourself. Most IB and IGCSE home tutor arrangements in JVPD Scheme begin exactly this way.
bullets: 1. Map the week first: who is home when, and which evening is already gone
2. Decide honestly whether one tutor can serve both levels, or two are needed
3. State the household constraint to every candidate before shortlisting
4. A separate diagnostic and written assessment for each child
5. One review conversation at two to four weeks, covering both children

sections.heading: IGCSE to Diploma Programme: what actually changes in Year 12?
paragraphs: Three things change and all of them catch families out. The volume of independent writing rises sharply, because the Diploma Programme carries an Internal Assessment (IA) in almost every subject plus the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK). The marking shifts from answering set questions to constructing arguments. And the subject count drops while the depth of each rises, so a student who coped by being broadly competent suddenly has nowhere to hide.

The students who struggle most in DP1 are rarely the weakest in Year 11. They are the ones who scored well by being organised and well-taught, and who have never designed anything themselves. Asked to choose their own research question for an IA, they produce something unanswerable or something trivial, and two months disappear. A tutor who has supervised that process before saves most of those two months, which is why the handover between the two boards is worth planning rather than discovering.

On the other side, the Primary Years Programme (PYP) and MYP children in the same household are on a different clock entirely. MYP marks come from criteria A to D rather than a percentage, so a child can know the content and still score poorly because the criterion being assessed was communication or inquiry. Parents comparing a Year 10 report with an MYP Year 3 report are comparing two different languages, and a tutor covering both should be able to translate each into the other for you.

Structures change between cohorts. The International Baccalaureate revises subject guides on its own cycle and the examination boards revise specifications on theirs, so paper formats and assessment routes shift. Nothing on this page should be treated as the current structure for your child's session. Ask the school's Diploma coordinator or subject teacher for the version that applies, and bring it to the first session so the tutor plans against the right document.
bullets: Independent writing rises sharply: an IA in nearly every DP subject
Marking shifts from answering questions to constructing an argument
Strong Year 11 students often struggle most with choosing a research question
MYP criteria A to D are a different language from an IGCSE percentage
Confirm current structures with the coordinator, never with a tutoring site

sections.heading: Choosing subjects once, for both boards
paragraphs: The two decisions parents here treat as separate are in fact one decision taken twice. The Core or Extended tier entry a school makes in Year 9, and the Higher Level or Standard Level choice made at the end of Year 11, sit on the same line. A student entered for Core Mathematics who later wants Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is starting the conversation two years late, and the same applies in the sciences. Anyone offering all IB and IGCSE subjects tuition in JVPD Scheme should be able to explain that sequence before they explain their teaching method. The home tuition we arrange in Mumbai starts from that sequence rather than from a subject list.

The useful question at both points is identical: does this child read about the subject voluntarily? If not, three Higher Levels chosen to impress an admissions office will produce two years of grinding and a set of predicted grades nobody is happy with. A household with one strong Higher Level and two comfortable ones generally looks better in DP2 than one with three ambitious ones, and the same logic governs whether Extended is the right entry at Year 9.

Assessment type matters as much as subject. Some subjects reward a student who writes well under timed conditions; others reward one who can plan and sustain a long independent piece. Those are different children, and they often live in the same house. A tutor who has taught both boards can tell you which of your two children should be steered towards which kind of subject, which is advice worth more than another hour of content coverage.

On the IB side the internal assessments are not interchangeable pieces of work. The sciences want a self-designed investigation with a defensible method and honest treatment of uncertainty. Mathematics wants an exploration built on a question the student genuinely chose. English A wants oral work and essays on the texts the school taught. A tutor who has supervised the specific one your child faces knows where marks leak, and it is almost always in method and evaluation rather than in the result.
bullets: The Year 9 tier entry and the Year 11 level choice are one decision, taken twice
Core Mathematics closes off Higher Level Analysis and Approaches later
Ask whether the child reads about the subject without being asked
Timed-writing subjects and long-project subjects suit different children

sections.heading: One tutor, two children, four roads in Mumbai
paragraphs: The working area for a household arrangement is JVPD Scheme, Juhu, Vile Parle West and Santacruz West, and the reason is simple arithmetic. A tutor teaching two children back to back is committing two and a half hours to one address, which only makes sense if the journey is short. Vile Parle is the nearest station and anchors the cluster for tutors arriving by train; the Western Express Highway and Link Road carry the rest, and the final stretch into the plots is local road at any hour.

That two-and-a-half-hour block is also the strongest card you hold. For a tutor, one journey producing two sessions is better paid per hour of his day than two journeys producing two sessions, which is why an IB and IGCSE private tutor in JVPD Scheme will often price a household block more sensibly than two separate bookings. It is worth asking for explicitly rather than hoping it is offered. Families who ask get it; families who book two slots a week apart rarely do.

Direction beats distance here as everywhere in the Western Suburbs. Santacruz West to these plots at six in the evening is a short hop. A similar distance from Chembur means the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road at its worst, twice over for a household block, and that arrangement does not survive a monsoon. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made the approach from the north more predictable, and Metro Line 1 helps a tutor coming from Versova, but neither removes the last kilometre.

One caveat we give every household. If the two children need genuinely different specialists, a single tutor is the wrong economy and we will say so. Two children with one scarce Higher Level subject between them are better served by a specialist for that subject plus a local tutor for the rest. Searching for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in JVPD Scheme and hoping one person covers everything is how a family ends up with a pleasant arrangement and no progress.

sections.heading: What a JVPD Scheme household's year looks like with two boards running
paragraphs: Two children in two programmes means two calendars, and they do not align. Children on these plots attend schools in the immediate area, Ecole Mondiale World School, Jamnabai Narsee International School and Utpal Shanghvi Global School among them, and the schools run their assessment cycles to their own schedules. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to those schools or to any other school named here; they are listed because their calendars decide which weeks in your house are quiet and which are not.

The practical collision is January and February. For a Year 11 that fortnight is coursework completion and timed practice before the series. For a DP2 student it is IA drafts and an EE checkpoint. For an MYP Year 5 student it is the personal project. A household can have all three landing in the same ten days, and the family that has thought about it in September handles it; the family that discovers it in January redistributes panic rather than work.

There is a second collision in April and May, when one child is sitting papers and the other is still having ordinary school weeks. The quiet-house requirement of the examinee usually wins, which means the younger child's sessions move to a different room or a different evening for six weeks. Deciding that in March rather than in May is worth doing, and a tutor who has worked in a two-board household will raise it himself.

The planning value of a single tutor across both boards is mostly here. He sees both calendars at once, knows that the Tuesday before a DP mock is not a Tuesday to introduce new content to the younger child, and can shift the balance of the block between the two of them week by week. An IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai working with one child cannot do that, however good he is, because he only sees half of the house.

January and February collide: coursework, IA drafts, personal project
April and May: the examinee's quiet house displaces the younger child's slot
Decide the examination-season arrangement in March, not in May

sections.heading: Can one home tuition slot serve two children?
paragraphs: Sometimes, and only in one configuration: back-to-back rather than simultaneous. Two children taught at the same table at the same time means each gets half a tutor and both learn to wait, and the younger one learns that interrupting works. Two consecutive forty-five or sixty-minute sessions with a short gap works, and on these plots that is usually what happens, because JVPD is planned as bungalows and low-rise houses rather than towers and the ground-floor study table is a shared resource rather than a private room.

That layout is the thing which makes a household arrangement practical here in a way it is not in a tower flat. The tutor stays put, the children swap, nobody travels, and a parent moving through the room hears both halves. It also means the second child's session is the one that degrades, because by then the table is untidy, dinner is closer, and attention is thinner. Give the harder subject the first slot, not the second, and rotate which child goes first across the term.

Online changes the arithmetic rather than replacing the arrangement. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in JVPD Scheme can take the second child on a different evening entirely at no travel cost, which is often better than squeezing both into one visit. Screens work well for essay feedback, worked solutions, IA draft comments and a pre-mock clinic. They work badly for a student who needs somebody beside her while she attempts the question herself, and worse for anyone who has learned to nod convincingly on camera.

Most two-child households here settle on a hybrid shape by the second term: one in-person block a week covering both children back to back, plus one online session for whichever child is closer to an assessment. It flexes without renegotiating, costs less than two full in-person bookings, and survives the evenings when Mumbai weather closes the road into the scheme. Household home classes in Mumbai almost always end up in that shape within two months, whatever was agreed at the start.
bullets: Back-to-back works; simultaneous teaching of two children does not
Give the harder subject the first slot, and rotate who goes first
