sections.heading: What to verify when a tutor covers both boards in Mumbai
paragraphs: Dual-board claims need more checking than single-board ones, because the claim is twice as large and the evidence is usually half as specific. Our own checks come first: photo identity verified against the profile name, degree and teaching certificates read rather than counted, subject depth tested in conversation by somebody who teaches the subject, and previous families called and asked about reliability before ability. None of that establishes that a tutor who is strong on one board is adequate on the other, which is why a dual-board home tutor in Mumbai gets one extra conversation before his profile is sent to anybody.

So ask for the evidence separately. Which board, which syllabus code and which series did he most recently prepare an IGCSE student for. Which IB subject at which level, in which examination session, and which internal assessment did he supervise. A tutor with real dual experience answers both without hesitating and usually volunteers which of the two he is stronger on. A tutor who answers the second question with a general statement about the IB has told you where the gap is.

Then the four questions that work for any hire. Can he describe a student who did not improve, and what he changed. What arrives in writing after each session. What does he do when the work has not been done. How would he handle two children at one table on one evening. Parents hunting for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in JVPD Scheme are really hunting for clean answers to those, and the last one is specific to a household brief.

Be wary of anyone who offers a guaranteed grade, publishes a success rate, or implies a relationship with a school or an examination board. None of it can be checked, and a dual-board claim plus a guarantee is a particularly poor combination. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai who tells you he is strong on IGCSE Mathematics and would not take a Higher Level Chemistry IA is being useful. One who says he covers everything is telling you he has not thought about it.
bullets: Ask for board, syllabus code and series for the IGCSE side separately
Ask for subject, level, session and supervised IA for the IB side
A genuine dual-board tutor volunteers which board he is stronger on
Ask how he would handle two children at one table on one evening
A guarantee plus a claim to cover everything is a reason to stop

sections.heading: Why is the summer between Year 11 and DP1 the cheapest term you will buy?
paragraphs: Because it is the only stretch of the two boards where nothing is due, and because the work available in it is the work that compounds. A student going into DP1 can spend those weeks learning what an Internal Assessment is, reading two past explorations, practising the kind of independent writing the Diploma Programme assumes and she has never been asked for. None of that is urgent, which is exactly why it is cheap, and all of it removes a month of confusion in September.

The second thing the summer buys is a corrected subject choice. Several students discover in those weeks that the Higher Level they selected in April is not the one they want, and that discovery in June is nearly free while the same discovery in November is expensive. A tutor who works through two or three weeks of Higher Level-level material with a student before DP1 starts gives you real information rather than a prediction, and the school can usually still accommodate a change at that point.

What it costs follows the same rules as everything else. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in JVPD Scheme turn on the programme, the level, the subject's scarcity, the tutor's examination experience, the session length and the travel involved. Summer blocks are often priced better than term-time ones because tutors have gaps, and a household booking two children into a morning block gets a better deal than one buying scattered evening hours in November. We do not set rates and do not publish a price list; a single figure for all of Mumbai would be invented.

The one warning about summer work is over-buying. Four weeks of daily sessions through April and May produces a tired student in June and no retained benefit. Two sessions a week for six weeks, with reading between them, does more. A tutor who proposes an intensive camp for a student who has just finished Year 11 papers is selling capacity rather than teaching, and the right answer is a shorter plan and a holiday.

sections.heading: What should two boards under one roof look like at four weeks?
paragraphs: Two separate written assessments, not one combined report, and one changed habit per child. At four weeks nobody should be showing you a grade. What should exist is evidence that each child has been diagnosed individually: the Year 11 student underlining command words before she writes, the MYP student producing a conclusion that refers to her data. If the notes treat the two children as one case, the tutor is managing a booking rather than teaching two people.

By one term both sets of marks should move, and the explanation should differ between the children because the diagnoses did. He should be able to show you a September and a November piece for each and point at what is now right. He should also be willing to say the unwelcome thing, and in a two-child household there is usually one: that the block is working for one child and not the other, and that the second needs a different tutor. A good tutor raises that himself.

Over a full cycle the honest position is narrow. Consistent teaching plus real practice reliably improves what each student can produce under pressure, and it does not determine results. Illness, a hard paper and ordinary nerves sit outside anyone's control, which is why we do not guarantee grades for either child and will not imply otherwise to keep a household booking. A household arrangement is more profitable for us than a single one, which is precisely why we say this plainly.

There are also households where the answer is less tuition rather than more. Two children in weekly sessions, plus activities, plus a school week, can produce a house with no unstructured hours in it, and that is its own problem. If one child is coping and the other is not, buy for one. If both are coping and you are buying reassurance, we will tell you that too, and the home tuition we arrange in Mumbai is easier to stop than most families expect.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home classes in JVPD Scheme
paragraphs: One message with the shape of the household is enough. Both children's year groups and programmes. The subjects that worry you for each, in order. The evenings genuinely free, and which adult is at home on them. Whether you want a back-to-back block or two separate arrangements. If you are unsure about the last one, say so; it is the question we answer most often and the answer depends on the levels rather than on your preference.

Have the documents ready for two diagnostics rather than one. Each child's most recent report, with criterion scores or tiers exactly as the school wrote them. The last two pieces of marked work in each child's weakest subject, annotations intact. The next six weeks of deadlines for both from the school portal. Parents who send these in advance get a first session that teaches rather than one that interviews, which is worth a fortnight across two children.

The first visit then runs as two diagnostics with a gap. Twenty minutes of unseen questions per child, a review of the marked work with each of them rather than about them, and one taught topic each so both finish able to do something new. Fifteen minutes with you at the end covering both, repeated in writing the same evening as two separate notes. That separation matters: one note for two children is the first sign of a block being run as a single hour.

From there it is a weekly block, written notes per child, a single review conversation inside a month, and a plan for the January collision before it arrives. Agree the reschedule policy at the start, because a household block loses more evenings to weather and examinations than a single slot does. You can change tutor for one child, for both, or stop entirely, with no notice period and no penalty.
bullets: Send both year groups, both subject lists, and which adult is home when
Say whether you want a back-to-back block or two separate arrangements

faqs.question: Can one tutor really handle IB and IGCSE home tuition in JVPD Scheme for two children?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends entirely on the two levels rather than on the tutor's willingness. Mathematics for a Year 10 student and for an MYP Year 4 student is a realistic pair. Extended sciences for Year 11 alongside Higher Level Chemistry for a DP student almost never is. Ask which syllabus codes and which internal assessments he has personally worked on for each child's programme. If the answer is specific for one and general for the other, you have found the gap.

faqs.question: How do back-to-back sessions work in practice at home on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: The tutor stays at one table and the children swap, usually with a ten or fifteen minute gap in between. On these plots that means the ground-floor study or dining table, which is the natural venue because JVPD is low-rise houses rather than tower flats. Give the harder subject the first slot, because the second session always runs on thinner attention. Rotate which child goes first across the term so the same one is not always taught at eight o'clock.

faqs.question: Is a household block cheaper than two separate bookings?
faqs.answer: Usually, and you have to ask for it. A tutor making one journey for two sessions earns more per hour of his evening than one making two journeys, so the saving is real rather than a discount. It is largest when the travel is longest, which is another reason the arrangement works best with a tutor from inside the Juhu, Vile Parle West and Santacruz West cluster. We do not set rates, so this is a conversation you have directly with the tutor.

faqs.question: What changes when my child moves from Year 11 into the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: The amount of independent work rises sharply and the marking changes character. Every DP subject carries an internal assessment, with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge on top, and all of them require a student to design something rather than answer something. Students who scored well in Year 11 through organisation often struggle most with choosing a research question. Using the summer between the two to learn what an IA actually is removes most of that first-term confusion.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor keep going across the transition year?
faqs.answer: If he has genuine DP experience in that subject, yes, and continuity is worth a lot at that point. He already knows the student's habits, which halves the diagnostic work in DP1. If his experience is IGCSE only, keeping him for continuity is a mistake that shows up in the IA, and the better pattern is to keep him for one subject while adding a DP specialist for the Higher Levels. Ask for his supervised IA history before deciding.

faqs.question: Two children, one examination season. How do we handle the house in April?
faqs.answer: Decide it in March. The child sitting papers needs a quiet house, so the younger child's sessions usually move to a different room, a different evening or online for about six weeks. Agree that with the tutor before it becomes urgent, and tell the younger child it is temporary and why. Families in Juhu and JVPD Scheme who plan this report that the six weeks pass without incident; families who improvise lose two sessions and have an argument.

faqs.question: What if one child is progressing and the other is not?
faqs.answer: Split the arrangement rather than persisting with the block. The usual cause is a level or manner mismatch rather than poor teaching: a tutor pitched correctly for a Year 10 student may be too brisk for an MYP child who needs encouragement. We will replace for one child and keep the other, at no penalty and with no notice period, and the new tutor starts from the existing diagnostic notes. A block that suits one child is not worth keeping for the other's sake.

faqs.question: Do you cover the Primary Years Programme as well?
faqs.answer: Yes, though the honest advice for a PYP child is usually shorter and more frequent sessions rather than a weekly hour. At that age the useful work is reading fluency, number confidence and the habit of answering a question in a full sentence, and thirty minutes three times a week beats ninety minutes once. That schedule only works with a tutor inside this cluster. If the concern is attention or a suspected learning difference, the school's coordinator is the better first call.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for the IB side of a household arrangement?
faqs.answer: For parts of it, well. IA draft feedback, worked solutions on a shared screen, essay comments and a clinic before a mock all transfer with little loss, and online is how a family keeps a scarce Higher Level specialist who lives in Thane or Navi Mumbai. What does not transfer is sitting beside a student while she attempts a question herself. Most two-child households here run one in-person block plus one online session for whichever child is closer to an assessment.

faqs.question: How do we compare two tutors when the brief covers two boards?
faqs.answer: Compare them on the child you are more worried about, not on the breadth of the claim. Breadth is easy to assert and hard to verify, and a tutor who is excellent for your Year 11 student and adequate for your DP student is a better hire than one who is adequate for both. Ask each candidate what he would teach in the first fortnight for each child, then compare the two answers for the harder case. The vaguer answer is your answer.

faqs.question: Can we start with one diagnostic session before committing to anything?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a two-child household we recommend it. One diagnostic per child, paid for individually, with written assessments for both and no obligation to continue. It is the cheapest way to find out whether one tutor can serve both, and it occasionally produces the useful finding that only one child needs tuition at all. We would rather tell you that after two sessions than take a household booking for a year on the assumption that both do.

sections.heading: How IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kalyan is arranged, step by step
paragraphs: Three facts decide the match and the rest is detail: which board each child is on, which hour you can genuinely protect every week, and where in Kalyan you live. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching service based in Mumbai, Maharashtra, not a coaching chain with a branch near Kalyan station, so a match is an agreement between one tutor's week and one household's week. Households on this corridor frequently have two children on different boards, and that changes the arrangement more than most parents expect.

We ask for the board and syllabus or programme for each child separately. One child sitting Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel papers in Year 10 and an older sibling in the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (DP) is two different tutoring briefs, not one discounted booking. Occasionally one tutor genuinely covers both at the level required, usually in Mathematics or the sciences at the lower end, and we will say so when it is true. More often the saving is false and shows up as the weaker of the two children being carried.

Then the household questions, which are the ones this page exists for. Which room will the session happen in. Who is at home at that hour. Whether the building requires a visitor pass each week or once. Whether a sibling or a television occupies the same space. Whether there is a printer, because past papers on a phone screen are close to useless. These answers change who we propose, because a tutor willing to teach at a kitchen counter with a cook working beside them is a different person from one who needs a closed door.

You get two or three names with their board experience, travel origin and the slots they will hold, then one diagnostic session, then a decision. Ask for the makeup rule in writing at that point: what happens if your child is ill, what happens if the tutor cannot travel, and how many sessions can be carried. That single clause prevents most of the disputes that end IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kalyan arrangements by December.

sections.heading: One family, two boards: what changes between IGCSE and the Diploma Programme
paragraphs: The short version: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE courses in Years 9 to 11 end in a terminal written series against a published mark scheme, while the IB Diploma Programme spreads the assessment across two years and attaches a piece of independent coursework to almost every subject. A student who was excellent at the first often struggles with the second for reasons that have nothing to do with ability, and a tutor who has only taught one of them will misdiagnose the problem.

What transfers is content. What does not transfer is the working method. IGCSE rewards a student who can produce the expected answer efficiently under timing. DP rewards a student who can sustain an independent investigation over weeks, choose a defensible question, and evaluate their own method honestly. The habits that earned marks in Year 11 actively get in the way in Year 12, where there is nobody to tell you the right answer in advance.

For a Kalyan household with children on both boards, the practical consequence is scheduling rather than teaching. The IGCSE child's demand spikes hard around mocks and the final series and then stops. The DP child's demand is steadier and peaks around internal assessment drafts, Extended Essay (EE) milestones and the Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay, which arrive at different points. Two children, two very different annual shapes, one weekly slot that cannot be in two rooms at once.

We plan those shapes together rather than separately, because the family has one evening calendar. That usually means the younger child takes the steady weekly slot and the older one takes blocks around deadlines, or the reverse in the IGCSE examination term. Parents who book both children into identical weekly arrangements in August end up cancelling half of them by November, which is an expensive way to learn the same lesson. Dual-board households are common in this part of Mumbai and the scheduling, not the teaching, is what defeats most of them.

Content transfers between boards; working method does not

sections.heading: Internal assessments on both boards, and the handover year
paragraphs: Both boards make a student produce something independently, and both pages of this website keep coming back to it because it is where most of the recoverable marks sit. On the IGCSE side it is the practical or alternative-to-practical component in the sciences, the case-study application in Business Studies and Economics, and the directed writing task in English First Language. On the IB side it is the individual investigation in the sciences, the exploration in DP Mathematics, the historical investigation, the individual oral in languages. IB Gram covers all IB and IGCSE subjects and the tutor in Kalyan you hire should be able to name the one your child faces without looking it up.

The handover year is where a dual-board household needs the most help. A Year 11 student finishing Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel papers and starting the Diploma Programme a few months later has to choose six subjects, decide which three sit at Higher Level (HL), and adjust to criterion-referenced marking after two years of mark schemes. Getting the HL choice wrong is the single most expensive mistake available, and it is usually made in a hurry in the gap between the two courses.

A useful tutor in that window does something quite specific: they look at the student's actual IGCSE scripts, not the grades, and say where the thinking was strong. A student who wrote tidy, accurate, efficient answers may be a poor fit for three write-up-heavy HL subjects. A student who was untidy but original often does better in the DP than their IGCSE grades suggest. That is a judgement, not a prediction, and we do not guarantee grades on the strength of it.

Subject scarcity bites the same way on both boards and worse at the top end. HL Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, HL Physics and HL Chemistry, and on the IGCSE side Extended Mathematics and Additional Mathematics, are the hardest things to staff in person this far along the Central Line. We will not reproduce component weightings or paper structures here, because both boards revise their subject guides on their own cycles and the current version belongs to your school's coordinator. The home tuition in Mumbai we arrange for those four subjects is online more often than not, for that reason alone.

sections.heading: Which Kalyan addresses a weekly home tutor can actually keep
paragraphs: A standing weekly visit is a promise about a journey, so the address decides whether it is keepable. Kalyan junction is a major railway node with little international-board teaching capacity of its own, which means the dependable in-person pool sits within Kalyan itself and in Dombivli, one stop down the Central Line, where a tutor already teaching two students adds a third on the same evening. Palava City is reachable by the same road route and carries a township's entry formalities. Thane West supplies more subject depth and considerably less reliability after six in the evening.

The limiting factor is one stretch of road. Thane spreads west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets the schedule: a tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in around twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, with Kalyan sitting beyond the end of it. Thane tutors largely cover Thane, and Mulund tutors sometimes cross over, so a weekly weekday visit from the far side of Thane is the arrangement most likely to lapse.

Inside a gated township the last two hundred metres matter as much as the twenty kilometres before them. A tutor who has to be registered at the gate, wait for a resident to authorise entry, and then find the right wing will lose ten minutes of a sixty-minute session every week unless it is sorted once properly. Get a standing visitor arrangement if your building allows it, send the tower and wing in advance, and tell the tutor which gate to use rather than which address to type into a map.

There is an arrangement worth proposing to a neighbour. Two children in adjacent buildings on the same board at the same level, taking consecutive slots, turns a marginal trip into a worthwhile evening for a tutor. We cannot create that for you, but if you mention a neighbour's child when you enquire, the odds of holding a fixed weekly time for a full year improve materially. No other corner of Mumbai rewards that one piece of neighbour coordination as heavily as this corridor does.

sections.heading: Why a Kalyan family often changes board at Year 11
paragraphs: The nearest international-board options to Kalyan are Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane, which follows an IGCSE pathway, and NES International School in Mulund West, which runs both international boards. Many families here therefore start on Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel because that is what was reachable, and then look at Diploma Programme places further into the city for Years 12 and 13. That sequence is the reason a dual-board household is so common on this corridor and so rare in the western half of Mumbai.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School, NES International School or any other school named on this page. We name them because their calendars govern when tutoring is useful and when it is wasted. A tutor who has taught students from the same school already knows the mock weeks, the reporting language and how early drafts are demanded, which saves a fortnight of discovery at your expense.

The year has fixed compression points on both boards, and a household running both feels them twice. IGCSE mocks reset every plan in the fortnight afterwards. DP internal assessment drafts, Extended Essay milestones and the TOK essay bunch together, with the TOK essay usually the piece that drifts because no single subject teacher owns it. Report weeks on either board produce a wave of enquiries that fills local tutors' diaries within days.

Then there is the commute, which is the part of the calendar nobody writes down. A Kalyan child travelling daily to Thane or Mulund arrives home with less attention left than a classmate living near the school, and a parent scheduling a seven o'clock session is often buying the worst hour of that child's day. Families here who put the substantial session on a weekend morning and keep weekday slots short and specific consistently get more from the same number of hours.

sections.heading: What does a home tuition hour in Kalyan need from your household?
paragraphs: A table, a chair at the right height, light the student can read by, a closed door or at least a quiet corner, the television off, siblings elsewhere, and the phone in another room. That is the whole list, and the number of sessions that underperform because one of those items is missing is larger than the number that underperform because of the tutor. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kalyan at a cleared dining table beats the same tutor in a bedroom with a screen competing for attention.

Two household details are worth deciding before the first visit. First, whether someone will be at home: for a Year 9 student an adult should be in the flat though not in the room, while for an older DP student it is usually better if no parent is present, because a teenager being observed performs instead of struggling honestly and the struggle is the diagnostic. Second, the two-minute debrief at the end. A tutor who leaves without a word tells you nothing; one who gives you two sentences at the door every week is worth keeping.

The online alternative exists and has real advantages, which matter here because the subject you need may not be reachable in person. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Kalyan can be a specialist who has marked the exact paper, sessions can be recorded for revision, shared screens handle marked-up past papers and graphs better than a notebook, and no lesson is lost to the Ghodbunder Road stretch in the monsoon. Online is the wrong choice for a Year 9 student who cannot yet work unsupervised, and we would rather say that than take the booking.

Hybrid is what most households on this corridor end up running, and the useful discipline is to fix the shape rather than improvise it. A weekly in-person hour for the child who needs presence, an online specialist hour for the subject that needs depth, and named in-person blocks before mocks and draft deadlines, agreed in advance. Write down the makeup rule and the travel assumption at the same time, and the arrangement will usually still be running in March. The hybrid plans we write across Mumbai name their in-person weeks in advance rather than leaving them to be requested.

sections.heading: Who is coming into your flat, and how was that checked?
paragraphs: Before a profile reaches you we confirm identity with documents, check that the degree is in the subject being taught rather than adjacent to it, take a teaching history with dates and institutions, follow up references where they exist, and hold a subject conversation about a specific recent paper on the board claimed. That last step removes more applicants than the paperwork does, because plenty of capable graduates cannot explain what a particular command word expects. A household buying IB and IGCSE home tutoring in Kalyan is buying that distinction as much as the hour itself.

You should still do the things only you can do. Note the name on the gate register and keep it consistent week to week, so a substitute arriving unannounced is noticed. Ask the tutor not to reschedule through the student. Agree that sessions happen in the agreed room, not in a bedroom, and that the door stays open or the room is visible. None of this implies suspicion of anybody; it is the ordinary hygiene of letting a professional into your home every week, and good tutors expect it.

We publish no rankings and no success rates. Parents search for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Kalyan and no honest service can resolve that phrase, because fit is specific to a child: the tutor who suits a confident Year 11 chasing the top band is frequently wrong for a Year 9 who needs rebuilding from Year 7 algebra. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a match is a judgement we expect to revisit rather than a verdict to defend. An IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai listings rank highly is a listing, not an assessment of your child.

Two answers should end a conversation. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because nobody can see next May's script in October. And be cautious of a tutor who will not name anything they would decline to teach, since both boards are wide and anybody claiming all of it at examination depth has looked closely at none of it.

sections.heading: The standing weekly slot: the logistics nobody costs in Mumbai
paragraphs: Kalyan is a major junction and the furthest point on this corridor from the city's international school cluster, so a tutor coming to your door is spending more of their evening on your family than on anyone else they teach in Mumbai. That is the hidden content of the rate, and understanding it makes the fee conversation straightforward instead of adversarial. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Kalyan depend on the board and level, on how scarce the specific subject is, on session length, on frequency, and on travel, and here travel is the largest single swing because the trip is long in both directions.

Frequency works in your favour and most parents never ask about it. Two fixed weekly slots at the same address are worth considerably more to a tutor's diary than one floating session, because the second one costs no extra travel. The same logic applies to two children in one flat, or two children in neighbouring buildings taking consecutive hours. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Kalyan families engage for a single hour a week on a variable day is being asked for the most expensive possible arrangement and will price it accordingly.

The clauses that actually cause arguments are small and easy to settle in advance. What happens when the student is ill: is the session forfeited, carried, or replaced online. What happens when the tutor cannot travel: is there an online fallback that evening or a makeup at the weekend. How much notice either side gives. Whether the monsoon changes the default. Whether intensive blocks before mocks are booked and paid separately. Settle those five in the first week and you will almost never need to discuss money again.

The last piece is knowing when to pause. A household running IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kalyan through an entire year without a break usually gets diminishing value in the quiet months. Scaling down after the examination series and scaling up before the next pressure point costs less and works better than a flat weekly habit maintained out of inertia. Tutors generally prefer it too, because a block they have been warned about is a block they can hold.

sections.heading: Is home tuition in Mumbai working by week four?
paragraphs: Count the delivered sessions first, because on this corridor that is the live risk and it is the one metric nobody tracks. Four agreed sessions, four sessions delivered at the agreed hour, is itself a result. Then look at the work rather than the marks: a question read properly before being attempted, a full attempt where there used to be a blank page, homework arriving before the deadline rather than during the next session. Marks at four weeks are noise, whichever board your child is on. The first month of home tuition in Mumbai is measured in delivered hours before anything academic.

By one term, ask for something narrow. One component clearly better beats a general sense of improvement across six subjects. On the IGCSE side the quickest responders are the experimental-reasoning questions in the sciences and the directed writing task in English First Language. On the IB side it is usually an internal assessment draft that now has a defensible research question instead of a topic, or a criterion level moving on the strand the tutor actually targeted.

By one examination cycle the honest answer depends on when you started and on what you bought. A Year 9 or Year 10 student has room to change the tier conversation itself; a DP1 student has room to rebuild foundations. A student starting a term before final papers can fix timing, layout and command-word reading and stop losing marks they already know how to earn, but cannot absorb two years of content. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and publishes no success rate, because an average across other people's children tells you nothing about yours.

And there are households where more hours is the wrong purchase. If the real cause is sleep, five hours of screen time, an undiagnosed learning difference, or a subject chosen to satisfy a parent, home tuition buys a delay at an hourly rate. We have told families in Kalyan to speak to the school counsellor first and occasionally to change nothing, because a child in the middle band who sleeps properly and reads for pleasure is not a problem requiring a solution.

One term: one clearly improved component beats six vaguely improved subjects
IB: a draft with a defensible research question is the clearest early signal
A term before final papers buys technique, not missing content

sections.heading: Setting up IB and IGCSE home classes in Mumbai from Kalyan
paragraphs: Send five things and the first session becomes useful rather than introductory. The board and level for each child separately. One marked script per weak subject with the teacher's comments intact. The weekly hour you can protect and who will be at home for it. Your area within Kalyan, Dombivli, Palava City or Thane West. And the gate rule for your building, including whether a visitor pass is needed every week or once.

Say in the first message whether you want one tutor across two children or two tutors, and we will tell you honestly whether one is realistic at the levels involved. Say whether a weekend morning is possible, because that answer changes the size of the pool we are matching from more than anything else you can tell us. If you want intensive blocks before mocks or draft deadlines, name them now; they are easy to reserve months ahead and close to impossible to find in the fortnight they are needed.

The first session is a diagnostic, not a lesson. The tutor puts a question in front of the student, watches them attempt it, and asks them to narrate their reasoning. They are looking for where the understanding actually broke, which is usually earlier than the topic that prompted your search. Expect very little teaching that hour, no more than one question of homework, and a short conversation with you at the door afterwards.

What should come back in writing is five lines: what the first month targets, in what order, what you should see by week four, the exact weekly hour committed, and the makeup rule. If any of those is missing, ask for it before the second session. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents hope to find does not exist, but a tutor who will write those five lines down does, and they are the ones worth keeping.
bullets: Send board and level per child, plus one marked script per weak subject
Name the protected hour and who will be at home for it
Give the gate rule and whether a pass is weekly or one-time
Reserve pre-mock and pre-deadline blocks months in advance
Get the weekly hour and the makeup rule in writing before session two

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both my children if they are on different boards?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, at the lower levels, and rarely well at the top. Mathematics and the sciences up to around Year 10 overlap enough that a competent tutor genuinely covers a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel student and an International Baccalaureate Middle Years Programme student in the same evening. A Diploma Programme Higher Level subject alongside an IGCSE subject is a different matter, and the usual outcome is that the harder brief gets carried rather than taught. Ask the tutor directly which of the two they are stronger on; the honest ones answer without hesitating.

faqs.question: What should the room look like for a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: A table the student can write on, a chair at the right height, light they can read by, the television off, siblings elsewhere and the phone in another room. A dining table cleared for the hour beats a bedroom almost every time, because a bed invites slouching and a screen invites drifting. A printer is the other thing worth having, since past papers read on a phone are close to useless and marking up a printed paper is half the technique being taught. None of this is fussiness; sessions genuinely underperform when it is missing.

faqs.question: How does a tutor get through our society gate every week?
faqs.answer: Set it up once rather than every week. Most buildings in and around Kalyan and Palava City will accept a standing visitor arrangement for a regular tutor if a resident registers it with the gate, and that saves ten minutes of a sixty-minute session each time. Send the tower, wing and which gate to use in advance rather than an address to type into a map. Also tell the tutor whether the lift is reliable at that hour. These details sound trivial until they have cost you four hours across a term.

faqs.question: What happens to a missed session when my child is ill?
faqs.answer: Whatever you agreed in writing in week one, which is why agreeing it then matters. The common arrangements are a carry-forward with reasonable notice, a switch to online that evening, or a weekend makeup. Problems arise when nothing was agreed and both sides assume something different in December. Ask for the notice period, the tutor's own absence policy, whether the monsoon changes the default, and how intensive blocks before mocks are handled. Five sentences settled early prevents nearly every money conversation that otherwise follows.

faqs.question: Do we pay for the tutor's travel time to Kalyan?
faqs.answer: Usually as part of the rate rather than as a separate line, and on this corridor it is the largest single factor in the figure. A tutor reaching Kalyan from Dombivli spends far less of their evening on you than one coming from Thane West or Mulund, and the rate reflects that honestly even when nothing is itemised. Two fixed weekly slots, or two children in consecutive hours, spread the same travel across more teaching and are genuinely cheaper per hour. Ask for the online rate from the same tutor and the trade becomes visible.

faqs.question: Should I sit in on the session?
faqs.answer: For a Year 9 student, be in the flat but not in the room. For an older Middle Years Programme or Diploma Programme student, stay out: a teenager under parental observation performs rather than struggling honestly, and the struggle is exactly the information the tutor needs. What you should insist on instead is a two-minute conversation at the door afterwards. A tutor who can tell you in two sentences what happened and what the student will do before next week is giving you more than an hour of watching would.

faqs.question: My child moves from IGCSE to the Diploma Programme next year. What should we do now?
faqs.answer: Spend an hour on the Higher Level choice with somebody who will read the actual scripts rather than the grades. The DP asks for sustained independent work, and a student who produced tidy efficient IGCSE answers is not automatically suited to three write-up-heavy Higher Level subjects. A student who was untidy but original often does better than their IGCSE grades suggest. That is a judgement rather than a prediction and we do not guarantee outcomes from it, but it is the cheapest intervention available in the whole handover year.

faqs.question: Is online as good as a tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: For a focused Year 10 or a Diploma Programme student, frequently yes, and sometimes better because the specialist you need may not live within reach of Kalyan. Shared screens handle marked-up papers and graphs well, sessions can be recorded for revision, and nothing is lost to traffic or weather. For a student who cannot work unsupervised for twenty minutes, no, and we will say so rather than take the booking. The honest test is not the child's age but whether they can hold attention alone, and most parents already know the answer.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come for an evening slot on a weekday?
faqs.answer: From within Kalyan or Dombivli, usually yes, with seven o'clock workable and eight o'clock easier to hold through a full year. From Thane West it is the arrangement most likely to lapse, because the Ghodbunder Road stretch takes close to an hour in the peak. The second half of the question is your own child, who has commuted back from Thane or Mulund and may have least to give at exactly seven. Several households here get more from one weekend morning than from two tired weekday evenings.

faqs.question: How do we handle two children needing the same hour?
faqs.answer: Stagger them rather than splitting the tutor, and let the annual shapes do the work. The IGCSE child's demand spikes around mocks and the final series and then falls away; the Diploma Programme child's is steadier with peaks at draft deadlines. So give the steady weekly slot to one and run blocks for the other, then swap when the examination term arrives. Households that book both children into identical weekly arrangements in August typically cancel half of them by November.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is competent but my child will not talk to them?
faqs.answer: Change the tutor, and do it early. A teenager who will not speak in sessions learns very little from a technically strong teacher, and that rarely repairs itself over a term. Tell us what the style problem was rather than the subject one: too fast, too talkative, unwilling to let a silence sit, or too similar to a teacher the student already dislikes. We go back to the panel with that note. There is no probation to serve out and nobody takes the request personally.

faqs.question: Do you work in Dombivli, Palava City and Thane West too?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for matching purposes they are one pool with Kalyan. A tutor accepting a Kalyan student is usually already travelling the Central Line corridor through Dombivli, and Palava City sits on the same road route. Thane West tutors reach all of them, more dependably at weekends than on weekday evenings. If a neighbour's child studies the same board at the same level, mention it when you enquire: consecutive slots in adjacent buildings make the journey worth a tutor's evening and improve your chances of keeping a fixed weekly hour.

ib-igcse-home-tuition-in-kalyan.closingCta: Send the board and level for each child, the weekly hour you can protect, your area, and your building's gate rule. You will get two or three named tutors with their board experience, travel origin and the slots they will hold, usually within a day or two. Book one diagnostic session, then ask for the first-month plan, the committed hour and the makeup rule in writing. If the match is wrong, say so and we go back to the panel.

One child in Year 10 on Cambridge, a younger one in the Middle Years Programme, one protected weekday evening between them. This page is about building an arrangement that survives several years and two different boards, not a single term.

sections.heading: How one household in Kamothe gets home tuition for two different boards
paragraphs: Start with the household, not the subject. We ask how many children, which year group each is in, which board or programme each sits, and which evenings the family can genuinely hold. That last answer is usually one evening and a weekend morning, and it is the real constraint. A family with a Year 10 Cambridge student and a Year 7 Middle Years Programme (MYP) student does not need two separate searches; it needs one tutor who can take back-to-back slots on a Tuesday plus a specialist for whichever subject the generalist cannot hold.

Back-to-back matters more than it sounds. A tutor travelling fifteen minutes from Kharghar for one ninety-minute session is spending two hours of their evening; the same trip for two consecutive sessions is three hours for double the work, which makes your household the arrangement they protect rather than the one they drop when something else comes up. It also usually reduces the per-hour figure, because the travel is amortised. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kamothe is far more stable at the household level than at the student level, and most families discover this by accident in year two.

What you receive is a plan rather than a list. Typically two names: one who can carry the younger child across subjects and the near-term needs of the older one, and one subject specialist for the pressure point. Each profile carries the degree, the boards and codes or programmes taught, the year groups handled, and the real door-to-door time to your sector at the hour you named. You speak to both directly, because IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching service and the engagement is yours. We keep the record so a replacement, or a stage change, comes with a handover.
bullets: 1. Tell us every child, every year group and every board in the household
2. Name the one evening and one weekend slot you can genuinely protect
3. We look for a tutor who can take two consecutive slots from Kharghar or Panvel
4. A specialist is added only for the subject the generalist cannot hold
5. Trial week, written review at four weeks, handover notes at each stage change

sections.heading: PYP to MYP to IGCSE to DP: where the handovers hurt
paragraphs: Four stages, three handovers, and the handovers are where households lose time. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs roughly Years 1 to 5 around transdisciplinary units, so the tutoring is about reading stamina, number sense and asking a researchable question. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers Years 6 to 10 and introduces four assessment criteria per subject, which is where most parents first see a grade they cannot interpret. The International General Certificate of Secondary Education covers Years 9 to 11 with Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel codes, Core and Extended tiers, and a terminal series. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the final two years with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), Internal Assessment (IA) in each subject, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK).

The PYP to MYP handover catches families out because the content gets easier relative to the marking. A child who was comfortable in Year 5 can land a grade 4 in Year 7 purely because criterion C and criterion D ask for communication and reflection that nobody has taught. The MYP to IGCSE handover is the opposite: the marking gets blunter and the content load jumps, and students who coasted on good classroom participation discover that a Cambridge 0580 Extended paper does not reward participation. Both handovers are predictable and both are cheap to prepare for a term in advance, which almost nobody does.

Schools in Navi Mumbai run different combinations, so check which path your child is actually on rather than assuming. Some run MYP to DP with no IGCSE at all; some run IGCSE in Years 9 to 11 and then DP; some offer IGCSE and then a different senior pathway. The all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Kamothe households engage is usually needed most in the year a handover lands, not in the year a grade drops. IB Gram does not guarantee grades at any of these stages, and we will say when a hoped-for timeline is not realistic. Home tuition in Mumbai does not change the pathway; it changes whether a handover year is survived or lost.

MYP, Years 6-10: four criteria per subject, with C and D the usual surprise
IGCSE, Years 9-11: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel codes, Core or Extended tier
DP: HL and SL choices, an IA per subject, the Extended Essay and TOK
Confirm your school's actual pathway rather than assuming the usual one

sections.heading: Subject choice twice over: Core or Extended, then HL or SL
paragraphs: A household on this pathway makes the same category of decision twice, four years apart, and the first one constrains the second. In Year 9 the school sets option blocks and a provisional tier: Core tier caps the top grade available, Extended opens it and sets harder papers. In DP1 the student picks three subjects at Higher Level. A child entered at Core tier for Mathematics in Year 10 has a harder route into HL Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches two years later, not because of a rule but because the algebraic fluency was never built. Nobody explains this link at the point the tier is chosen, which is why it is the most valuable conversation a tutor has with a Year 10 family.

The assessment work differs sharply between the two halves. On the IGCSE side the mark-earning skills are command words, precise method and timing: Cambridge 0580 at Extended tier sets Papers 2 and 4 with real non-calculator demands, the Sciences want significant figures and a repeatable written method, First Language English wants an argument sustained across a whole response. On the IB side every DP subject carries an internally assessed component, and those are where students lose ground quietly: a Science investigation needs a research question narrow enough to answer, a Mathematics exploration needs genuine mathematical content rather than a survey with a chart.

We name papers, components and skills and send you to the current subject guide or syllabus document for structure, because both the IB and the examination boards revise on their own cycles and a figure that was accurate when a brief was written may not apply to your child's session. Ask the school's Diploma coordinator or examinations officer for the dates and the current specification. What a tutor can do is read the actual task sheet your school issued and mark one piece of work against the published criteria in front of the student, which is the single habit that separates a tutor who moves a grade from one who delivers pleasant revision.

sections.heading: One tutor, two children, four Navi Mumbai nodes
paragraphs: Kharghar is where most of these arrangements come from. It has the largest concentration of international-school teaching staff on this stretch, it is one stop along the Harbour Line, and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 between Belapur and Pendhar gives a Kharghar tutor a second route into Kamothe. For a household booking two consecutive slots, that redundancy is worth more than a credential, because a single blocked road would otherwise cancel three hours of work rather than ninety minutes. Panvel supplies the rest, and a Panvel tutor coming towards Kamothe in the early evening travels against the heavier flow on the Sion-Panvel Highway, so arrival times hold. This is why IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kamothe is drawn from these two nodes rather than from the wider Mumbai pool.

CBD Belapur is where we look for the specialist half of a household arrangement. Economics, Business, Accounting, Computer Science and the second languages are thin on this stretch, and a Belapur tutor can cover them, usually best on a weekend morning when node-to-node travel is cheap. Khandeshwar is the practical hinge for train-based tutors, who arrive there and cover the last stretch into the sectors by auto; that chain is dependable for a five or six o'clock start and progressively less so late, which is one more reason the back-to-back pattern starts early rather than at eight.

Nerul and Vashi are the instructive exclusions, and they matter more for a household than for a single student. Both are larger nodes and both sit one node too far for a standing weekday evening in Kamothe, which is counter-intuitive because Nerul looks closer on a map than it behaves on a Thursday. The Atal Setu and Palm Beach Road have improved journeys without making an island-city tutor viable midweek. When a household depends on one tutor for two children, the cost of that tutor giving up in November is doubled, so we are stricter about node matching for families than for individuals.
bullets: Kharghar: two independent routes, the deepest pool, the safest double slot
Panvel: against the evening flow towards Kamothe, so arrivals stay predictable
CBD Belapur: the specialist half of a household arrangement, best at weekends

sections.heading: Why do the Kamothe school calendars collide for siblings?
paragraphs: Because the boards put their pressure points in the same months. Children from these sectors are bussed out to international schools, among them D.Y. Patil International School and Ryan Global School, named purely as local context. IB Gram is an independent platform, is not affiliated with D.Y. Patil International School, Ryan Global School or any other school named on this page, and makes no claim of any relationship with any of them. The practical consequence is that one bus timetable governs the whole household and one study window, roughly half past five to half past eight, has to absorb two children's work.

The collisions are predictable. Late September into October brings MYP summative tasks and DP1 Internal Assessment proposals at the same time. Late November into January brings Year 11 mocks and, for a DP2 sibling, IA final submissions alongside the Extended Essay. February and March are past papers for both. A household with children at two stages therefore has two or three fortnights a year when a single evening slot cannot serve both, and the arrangement that survives is the one that planned for it in July rather than negotiating in December.

What that means in practice is booking structurally rather than reactively. Hold a weekday double slot for the term, and agree in advance that during the two collision fortnights the older child takes both halves and the younger one moves to a weekend morning. Tutors in Kharghar and Panvel who hold a half past six weekday pair fill those slots by late July, so a household calling in November is choosing from eight o'clock starts and weekends. Families here who get the arrangement they want are the ones who move in June, before either child has anything due.

Late September to October: MYP summatives meet DP1 IA proposals
Late November to January: Year 11 mocks meet DP2 IA and the Extended Essay

sections.heading: Can one home tuition slot in Kamothe serve two children?
paragraphs: Not simultaneously, and yes consecutively. Two children of different ages in the same room produces a session that works for neither, because the younger one needs supervised method and the older one needs quiet concentration with intervention. Two consecutive ninety-minute slots on the same evening, or a ninety plus sixty split, works well and is the pattern most households here settle into. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kamothe arriving at half past five and leaving at half past eight has done two real sessions and one trip, which is why they protect that evening.

Online has a specific place in a household plan. A DP2 or Year 11 student doing timed past papers who already starts work unprompted loses little online, which frees the home slot for the sibling who genuinely needs an adult beside the page. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Kamothe is also the honest answer for a scarce subject, and a strong remote Economics specialist beats a nearby generalist. Online is the wrong choice for a Primary Years Programme child or a Year 9 student who cannot work unsupervised for forty minutes, and we will say so rather than solve a scheduling problem at the student's expense.

The hybrid that works for two children is usually asymmetric by design. The younger child gets the home slot every week; the older one gets a home slot plus one short online checkpoint, or online through the paper-practice run and in person the rest of the year. Decide this in week one and get it priced once. The mistake households make is treating the arrangement as two independent engagements, which doubles the travel, doubles the cancellation risk and loses the per-hour advantage that made the double slot worth having. The home classes we help arrange across this part of Mumbai are quoted once for the household, not per child.

Two consecutive slots on one evening, or a ninety plus sixty split

sections.heading: What should I check before a tutor becomes a three-year fixture?
paragraphs: Check breadth honestly, because a household arrangement asks more of a tutor than a single-subject one. Ask which boards and programmes they have taught and in which year groups, and ask them to describe the difference between how an MYP criterion is applied and how a Cambridge mark scheme credits a six-mark explain question. A tutor who can do both has genuinely worked across the pathway. A tutor who answers one well and generalises the other will be fine for a year and thin at the handover, which is exactly when you will need them most.

Our checks run before you meet anyone. The degree is confirmed against a certificate rather than a CV line, government photo identity is confirmed, and board or programme claims are tested by description rather than by a list. We also sanity-check travel, because a tutor who insists Kamothe is twenty minutes from Nerul at seven in the evening has told us something about their judgement. For a household booking two consecutive slots we additionally check that the tutor has actually run back-to-back sessions before, because managing the handover between two children in one evening is a skill of its own.

Three claims should end a conversation at any stage. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because the paper, the day and the student all vary. A quoted pass percentage is an invented statistic. An offer to cover six Diploma Programme or IGCSE subjects single-handed describes something nobody does well, and it is a particular temptation to make when a household asks for breadth. We do not guarantee grades. What we offer instead is a replacement from the same node pool with a handover of coverage, and an IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai families can swap in a week is worth more than one who promises outcomes.
bullets: Ask the tutor to contrast an MYP criterion with a Cambridge mark scheme
Degree certificate and government photo identity confirmed before introduction
Travel claims tested against the actual evening, not an off-peak estimate

sections.heading: The Year 11 to DP1 handover, and why families lose a term in it
paragraphs: The gap between finishing an IGCSE series and starting the Diploma Programme is where households most often lose a term, and the cause is a reasonable misreading. A student finishes Year 11 with strong Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel results, the family concludes the subject is secure, and tutoring stops over the long break. DP1 then begins with three subjects at Higher Level and an assessment model that rewards nothing the student has practised. The first internal grades come back two bands lower than Year 11, the family panics in October, and the tutor they want is already booked.

The specific discontinuities are worth naming. Extended tier Mathematics rewards accurate procedure; HL Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches rewards proof and justification, which is a different cognitive act. IGCSE Sciences reward a correctly written method; a DP Science Internal Assessment rewards a research question you designed yourself and a defensible analysis of your own messy data. First Language English rewards a controlled response to a set task; DP English rewards comparative argument about material you have not seen. None of this is harder in a general sense. It is simply unpractised, and six weeks of DP1 is not long enough to discover it safely.

The arrangement that avoids the lost term is unglamorous: keep a light touch across the handover. Four or five sessions across the break, aimed at proof technique, at designing a research question, at reading unseen material under time pressure, converts a two-band drop into a half-band one. Families here who do this treat the tutor as a fixture across the pathway rather than a response to a bad report, and the all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Kamothe households run for several years are almost always the ones that bridged this gap deliberately. There are no guarantees in it, including from us, and it remains the cheapest term we have seen anyone buy.

sections.heading: How long does a good tutoring arrangement last in Kamothe?
paragraphs: Two to four years, when it is built at household level and matched node to node, and about one term when it is not. The arrangements that last share three features: the tutor lives in Kharghar or Panvel, the slot is the same evening every week, and the logistics were settled in the first fortnight rather than renegotiated in the third month. The ones that end early almost always had a long commute, a moving slot, or an unspoken disagreement about what a missed session costs. None of those are academic problems and all of them end tutoring arrangements. Home tuition across Mumbai stops for logistical reasons far more often than for academic ones, and that is the part a family can control.

Judge the academic side at four weeks on evidence rather than atmosphere. Each child should be able to name their two weakest topics in specific terms. There should be at least one piece of work where you can see the tutor's correction and then the student applying it unprompted. The tutor should be able to name three things fixed and two still open, per child. Technique gains appear in four to six weeks because exam behaviour is learnable; content repair from an earlier year takes a term or more. We do not guarantee grades, and we will tell you when the timeline you want does not exist.

When it is not working, raise it in week three in behavioural language: the child has stopped preparing, the hour has become homework supervision, the slot keeps moving, the two sessions have collapsed into one long one. We return to the Kharghar and Panvel pool, put forward a replacement, and pass on the coverage notes so the second tutor does not restart from zero. For a household this matters double, because a mismatch costs two children a term. One swap in month one followed by three settled years is the most common successful pattern we see here, and it is a good outcome rather than a failed start.

Four weeks: specific self-diagnosis and one applied correction, per child

sections.heading: Setting up IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kamothe, Mumbai
paragraphs: Send three documents per child and the first session stops being an introduction. The latest report including the written comments, which usually name the weakness more plainly than the grade. The two most recent marked assessments with the teacher's annotations left on, which show what each school is actually penalising. And the current unit plan, task sheet, option booklet or Internal Assessment brief, which shows what is coming. Send them at the enquiry stage. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai households brief properly arrives with a plan rather than spending the first hour finding the problem.

Session one for each child should be observation rather than exposition. Expect the tutor to set work slightly below the stated level and watch, because that is where diagnostic errors appear. Expect questions about how the student revises, which is usually re-reading and therefore close to useless. Expect a short written plan afterwards naming the two things to rebuild and the order. In a double slot, expect a five-minute gap between children rather than an instant switch, because the tutor needs to write the first note while it is fresh.

Then settle the household logistics once. Pick one room and keep it the same room for both children. Give the security desk the tutor's name, number and the fixed evening so entry becomes standing rather than a visitor pass each time. Agree the fee for the double slot, the payment rhythm, the cancellation notice and what happens when one child is ill but the other is not, in writing, with the tutor directly. That last clause is the one households forget and the one that causes the first argument. Families in Kamothe, Maharashtra, who settle all of it in week one are usually the ones still running the same home tuition arrangement in Mumbai three years later, with the same tutor and the same evening.

Two recent marked assessments per child, annotations intact
Option booklet, unit plan or Internal Assessment brief as applicable
One room, one fixed evening, standing gate entry for the tutor

faqs.question: Can one tutor really handle both an IGCSE and an IB child in our home?
faqs.answer: Across two adjacent stages, often yes; across the whole pathway, rarely. A tutor comfortable with Middle Years Programme Years 8 to 10 and Cambridge Extended tier can usually hold a Year 9 and a Year 11 student on consecutive slots. A Primary Years Programme child and a DP2 Higher Level student need different people. Ask the candidate to contrast how an MYP criterion is applied with what a Cambridge six-mark explain question credits. If they can do both convincingly, the double slot will work; if not, add a specialist.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our Kamothe building twice in one evening for two children?
faqs.answer: They travel once and teach twice, which is the point. A Kharghar or Panvel tutor spending fifteen to twenty-five minutes on the Sion-Panvel Highway for a single ninety-minute session gives up two hours of their evening; for two consecutive sessions they give up three and earn double, which makes your household the slot they protect. It usually also lowers the per-hour figure. This is the strongest practical reason to arrange both children together rather than running two separate searches.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Kamothe depend on?
faqs.answer: Stage, subject scarcity, travel, session length and frequency, and for a household also whether the slots are consecutive. A Diploma Programme Higher Level subject commands more than a Middle Years Programme session. Economics or Accounting costs more here than Mathematics because fewer people nearby teach them. A Panvel tutor crossing twice a week prices that travel in, and a double slot amortises it. We publish no rate card, because quoting one would mean inventing a figure. Agree everything with the tutor directly and in writing.

faqs.question: Our society issues a visitor pass per entry. Does that work for a three-hour evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth converting to standing entry in the first week. Give the security desk the tutor's name, phone number and the fixed evening, and most Kamothe buildings will register them once rather than issuing a fresh pass each visit. For a double slot the saving is larger than it looks, because ten minutes at the gate comes out of the younger child's session. Ask the tutor to carry photo identity regardless, and check where visitor vehicles are meant to park before the first evening.

faqs.question: Should we stop tuition after the IGCSE exams and restart in DP1?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most expensive gap in the pathway. Students finish Year 11 strong, tuition stops over the break, and DP1 starts with an assessment model that rewards nothing they have practised. Higher Level Mathematics wants proof rather than procedure; a Diploma Programme Internal Assessment wants a research question the student designed. Four or five light sessions across the break on those specific skills change the first DP report substantially. Families who do this rarely need a crisis search in October, when the good slots are gone.

faqs.question: Who is the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Kamothe for a household like ours?
faqs.answer: There is no general answer and any service that gives you one is guessing. The right tutor for a Year 10 Cambridge student and a Year 7 MYP sibling is defined by whether they can hold both convincingly and reach you reliably, not by a ranking. We narrow it to two names whose stage experience matches and whose node keeps a double slot sustainable, then you judge fit over a trial week. Fit between particular students and a particular teacher is the variable nobody can screen for in advance.

faqs.question: Nobody is home before seven on weekdays. Can a double slot still work?
faqs.answer: It becomes hard, because two consecutive sessions from 7:15pm would run past nine for the younger child. The usual solution is to split: the older, more independent student takes a weekday evening slot, and the younger child takes a weekend morning when an adult is in the flat. Ask the tutor for a three-line written note after each session either way. For a Primary Years Programme child an adult at home genuinely matters, because it keeps the session non-negotiable rather than optional.

faqs.question: Which subjects should we expect to need a second, specialist tutor for?
faqs.answer: Economics, Business Management or Business Studies, Accounting, Computer Science, Psychology and the second languages. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English are supplied comfortably from Kharghar and Panvel, so a capable generalist can often carry them across two stages. The scarce subjects are usually best served by a strong online specialist or a CBD Belapur tutor on a weekend morning. Parents typing IB and IGCSE tutors near me Kamothe and finding nothing for Accounting are meeting a real supply limit, not a search failure.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work across both boards, or only for the older child?
faqs.answer: Mainly the older and more independent child. A Year 11 or DP2 student working through timed past papers who already sits down and starts loses very little online, and putting them online frees the home slot for the sibling who needs an adult beside the page. For a Primary Years Programme child or a Year 9 student who cannot work unsupervised for forty minutes, online is clearly worse and we will say so. Apply that forty-minute test honestly to each child separately rather than to the household.

faqs.question: One child is improving and the other is not. Do we change tutors for both?
faqs.answer: No, change only the half that is not working. Ask the tutor to name three things fixed and two still open for each child. If the answer is specific for one and vague for the other, the likely cause is a stage mismatch rather than a bad tutor, and the fix is adding a specialist for the weaker half while keeping the working slot intact. Tell us which half is failing and we will match from the same Kharghar and Panvel pool, with coverage notes handed over.

faqs.question: We may move to Kharghar or Panvel next year. Does the arrangement continue?
faqs.answer: Almost always, because the tutor already lives in one of those nodes and the move usually shortens their trip rather than lengthening it. Send us the new address and the new gate protocol and the same slot carries over. A move to Vashi, Nerul or across the creek is different, and in that case we would match you to a tutor in the new node rather than ask the existing one to follow you along the highway. Node-to-node matching is what made the arrangement stable in the first place.

faqs.question: Is an IB and IGCSE private tutor Kamothe households hire better than a coaching class?
faqs.answer: For most of this pathway, yes, because the assessment is individual. Your child's Internal Assessment research question, your child's coursework draft, your child's specific criterion weakness. A room of twenty cannot work on one student's draft, and a tutor who reads the actual task sheet your school issued can. The honest exception is a Year 11 or DP2 student who only needs timed practice and company while doing it, where a small focused group sometimes beats one-to-one on both cost and motivation.

sections.heading: How IB Gram builds a shortlist for home tuition in Kandivali East
paragraphs: A shortlist for this part of Mumbai is built from four facts, and a request that carries all four is usually answered the same day. Those facts are the board, the exact year group, the subject with its level or tier, and the two evening windows your child can genuinely sit down and work. Everything else is negotiable. What is not negotiable is the first fact, because a tutor who is strong on Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics at Extended tier is not automatically the right person for a Diploma Programme (DP) student writing a mathematical exploration, and a parent who writes only "maths tuition, Class 10" will get a shortlist built on a guess.

The cross-board request is the one this page exists for. Families along the Kandivali East–Thakur Complex corridor often hold two boards at once: an older child inside the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme and a younger one working through Cambridge IGCSE Years 9 to 11, or a single child who sat IGCSE and has just walked into DP1. Those two requests look identical on a form and are completely different jobs. We separate them before matching rather than after, because a tutor asked to switch register mid-session between criterion-marked IB work and a mark-scheme-driven IGCSE paper tends to do neither well.

Travel is the second filter, and in the Western Suburbs it decides more than most parents expect. The suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, so a tutor coming down from Dahisar or up from Malad East reaches you quickly, while the same person crossing the city east to west at 6pm will cancel by week five. We match along the line. A standing 7pm Tuesday slot that holds for a full term is worth more than a slightly stronger profile who arrives late twice a month, and we will say so on the call rather than let you discover it in October.

The process itself is short and you can hold us to each step of it. Nothing is charged, booked or committed before the discovery call, and the shortlist is deliberately two or three profiles rather than a long list, because comparing eight strangers is how families end up choosing on price.

sections.heading: Which board decision are you actually asking a tutor to help with?
paragraphs: Most searches for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kandivali East are really one of three decisions in disguise, and naming yours shortens the whole exercise. The first is a subject-choice decision: which six subjects, at which Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) split, or whether a Year 9 student should be entered for Core or Extended tier. The second is a transition decision: a child who has finished Cambridge IGCSE and is now inside the IB Diploma Programme, where the assessment grammar changes completely. The third is simple repair, where one subject has slipped and the family wants it fixed before the next reporting cycle.

The transition is the one that catches careful families out, and it is worth being blunt about. Cambridge IGCSE rewards a student who can recognise a question type and execute a method cleanly against a published mark scheme. The International Baccalaureate rewards something else: command terms, justification, and in the sciences and humanities a written internal assessment that is marked against criteria rather than a list of acceptable answers. A student who collected a strong set of IGCSE results by drilling past papers can genuinely struggle in DP1 while doing nothing wrong, and the honest read is that the method changed, not the child.

Tier and level choices deserve the same honesty. Extended tier at Cambridge IGCSE is the right entry for a student heading towards a science or economics pathway at DP, and the wrong entry for a student who is still insecure with algebraic manipulation in Year 9, where a clean Core result and a confident start to DP beats a scraped Extended grade. At DP the HL decision is about load as much as ability: three Higher Level subjects plus the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) is a real workload, and a tutor who tells you every ambitious child should take four HL subjects is not thinking about your child.

A tutor cannot make these choices for you, and should not try. What a good one does is lay out what each route demands week by week, tell you what the school's own coordinator will likely advise, and send you back to that coordinator with better questions. IB Gram is an independent platform and not affiliated with any school named on this page, so nobody here has a stake in which pathway you pick.
