faqs.question: Can one tutor teach two children in the same hour at home?
faqs.answer: Only if they are on the same board, in the same subject and close in ability, and even then an hour split between two is not two hours of teaching. Siblings two years apart or on different boards should have separate slots with separate tutors, placed back to back on the same evening so the household gives up one evening rather than two. What one tutor can usefully do across two children is set a single standard for how work is presented, which is worth more than it sounds in a house with two sets of exercise books.

faqs.question: Do the sessions have to be in a separate room?
faqs.answer: A room that can be closed matters more than a room that is dedicated. In a two-bedroom flat the practical answer is usually a rota: the child being taught gets the bedroom with the door shut, and the rest of the household stays out of it for the hour. What does not work is the dining table while dinner is being prepared, or a sofa with a television behind it. Keep the same room each week if you can, because the setting itself becomes part of the habit, and habit is most of what tutoring at this age is building.

faqs.question: Can two sessions run back to back on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for two-child households in Mumbai it is the arrangement that holds up best. Two tutors, one after the other, say 6.30 and 7.45, with the room already set and one gate registration covering both. The household loses one evening a week instead of two, and the second tutor arrives when the first leaves rather than hunting for parking at a different hour. Tell both tutors the plan, because the first one running fifteen minutes over affects somebody else, and a polite word at the start prevents that.

faqs.question: How do I register a tutor at the building gate for a standing slot?
faqs.answer: Ask the manager or the committee for a recurring weekly visitor entry rather than approving each visit. Give the name, the day and the time, and ask what identification the tutor should carry. Where the complex uses an app, check whether a recurring entry is possible, because live approval fails the week nobody is looking at a phone at 6.25pm. Also ask where a tutor on a two-wheeler or in a car should park, which at this end of Ghodbunder Road is often the tighter constraint. One conversation covers all of it for the year.

faqs.question: Is home tuition worth it when my child already has school support?
faqs.answer: Sometimes not, and it is worth asking the school first. Where a school runs a genuine support slot with a subject teacher who knows the child, that is better than a tutor and it is already paid for. A tutor is worth hiring when the gap is specific and the school cannot give it individual time: a criterion the child keeps losing, an Internal Assessment with no plan, or a two-year foundation hole. Ask the subject teacher what they would work on if they had an hour a week alone with your child, and hire against that answer.

faqs.question: Does a two-child household pay twice?
faqs.answer: For teaching, yes, because two children at different stages need two tutors and two hours of preparation and marking. Where you save is travel and coordination: a tutor covering two slots in one building on one evening is making one journey, and most will reflect that. The other saving is organisational rather than financial. One room, one hour block, one gate entry and one set of household rules is far easier to sustain for two years than four separate arrangements, and sustainability is what actually determines the result.

faqs.question: My child finishes IGCSE in May and starts the Diploma Programme in July. When should tutoring start?
faqs.answer: Use the gap, because it is the cheapest teaching you will ever buy. Four to six weeks in May and June, at one or two sessions a week, is enough to diagnose the candidate Higher Level subjects and to start the self-direction work that the Diploma Programme assumes and IGCSE never taught. Spend part of it on how to plan a piece of work with no teacher-set deadline. Families on this road who do this arrive in DP1 knowing which Higher Level choices were realistic, rather than discovering it in November.

faqs.question: Should I sit in on the session?
faqs.answer: For the first two or three, yes, and after that it depends on the age. Being present early lets you judge the tutor and signals to the child that this is serious. Staying out of the room afterwards stops you answering on their behalf, which is the commonest way a parent undermines a session without meaning to. Primary Years Programme children are the exception and benefit from a parent nearby for longer. By the Diploma Programme, a three-minute conversation with the tutor at the end of each hour is more useful than sitting in.

faqs.question: What if my two children need the same subject at different levels?
faqs.answer: Mathematics is the one case where a single tutor often works, in consecutive hours rather than together, because the algebra underneath is continuous even though the papers are not. The same is rarely true in the sciences, where the assessment logic diverges sharply between an IGCSE written paper and a Diploma Programme Internal Assessment. Ask the tutor directly whether they have taught both levels in the last two years. If the answer covers one properly and the other vaguely, take two tutors and put the slots back to back.

faqs.question: Is a tutor in our flat safe, and what should we check?
faqs.answer: Ask for and look at photo identification on the first visit, keep the session in a room with an open or glazed door, and have an adult or trusted help in the flat for the early weeks. IB Gram verifies identity and documented experience before a profile is shown, and that is a floor rather than a substitute for your own judgement. Register the tutor properly at the gate so there is a record of each visit. And ask your child after a month how the sessions feel, in a conversation where a negative answer is genuinely allowed.

faqs.question: Can the hour change every week to fit our schedule?
faqs.answer: It can, and it is the surest way to lose a good tutor. A floating slot means the tutor cannot plan a route, cannot take another student near you, and will eventually replace you with a family who can hold a fixed hour. It also removes the habit, which for a child under sixteen is doing more work than the teaching is. If your week genuinely varies, pick the one hour that is stable even in a bad week and keep that, then add occasional extra sessions around it rather than moving the fixed one.

faqs.question: How long before we see something in the report card?
faqs.answer: One full reporting cycle, usually a term, and the earlier signals are in the marked work rather than the report. By four weeks you should see method set out and the longest question attempted. By eight weeks, fewer repeated errors of the same type. The report lags both of those because it is written against work done earlier in the term. Judge the arrangement on the exercise book and the marked papers, and treat the report as confirmation rather than as the test. If the book has not changed by week six, the report will not either.

sections.heading: How IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kemps Corner is arranged for two children
paragraphs: The enquiry usually arrives as one request and has to be split into two. A Year 10 on a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel pathway and a DP1 student in the International Baccalaureate (IB) are not the same job, even in the same subject, and the first thing we do is separate them on paper. Year group, board, subject, level and the hour each child can realistically work. Two rows, not one, because a single row produces a single tutor and a single tutor usually disappoints one of the children.

Then we ask which of the two is actually urgent. Almost always one is: a Year 11 approaching papers, or a DP2 student with internal assessment drafts due. The other child is often coasting rather than failing. Starting both at once feels fair and frequently means neither gets enough. We would rather place one strong specialist properly in June and add the second in August, and we will say so even though it is the smaller booking.

Scheduling is where this gets specific to Kemps Corner. If both children are to be taught on the same evening, the sequence matters more than the subject. One tutor covering a sibling pair back to back from four o'clock is efficient and holds; two tutors arriving separately at six and seven do not, because the second one is crossing the flyover at the worst possible moment. We build the shortlist around the evening you can actually offer rather than the ideal one.

You then speak to the candidates yourself, separately for each child if the boards differ. Ask each tutor which board and which level they are teaching this academic year. A tutor who claims both boards across several year groups may genuinely do it, and may also be describing a decade of varied experience rather than current practice. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kemps Corner works best when every tutor on the list is current on the specific thing your child is sitting.

sections.heading: One household, two boards: how IB and IGCSE sit side by side
paragraphs: These are two different qualification systems that happen to be taught in the same Mumbai schools, often to siblings in the same flat. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs as a continuum: the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) across Years 1 to 5, and the Diploma Programme (DP) in the final two years with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) subjects, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK). The Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel qualifications sit as a standalone two-year block in Years 9 to 11.

The marking philosophies are what confuse parents running both. IB programmes before the Diploma assess against published criteria, so a piece of work is judged strand by strand and a strong effort can score poorly on the criterion it was actually set against. The Years 9 to 11 qualifications are marked against mark schemes on written papers, where method credit and command words drive the score. A child can be strong in one system and weaker in the other without being a different student.

Many Mumbai schools run both, which is why a single household ends up with children in each. A school may teach the Years 9 to 11 qualifications and then its own Diploma Programme, or offer the IB continuum from the primary years. That pathway decision was made when your children were enrolled and is not usually revisited, so the practical question is not which is better but what each child needs this term. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Kemps Corner can be matched, one child at a time.

Our own listing line reads all IB and IGCSE subjects IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor Mumbai, which is an accurate category and a poor plan. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families imagine hiring would have to be current on two marking systems in several subjects simultaneously, and very few people genuinely are. Two good specialists beat one impressive generalist in almost every two-child household we have placed.

The Years 9 to 11 qualifications are a standalone two-year block

sections.heading: Which subjects can share a tutor across both boards?
paragraphs: Mathematics is the most shareable, with caveats. A tutor teaching Diploma Programme mathematics is generally comfortable with the Years 9 to 11 syllabus underneath it, because the content is a subset and the techniques are familiar. What they may not know is how the written papers at the lower level reward working, or the non-calculator expectations in one of the components. Ask them specifically. A tutor who answers with the paper structure has taught it; one who says the maths is the same has not.

The sciences are moderately shareable within one discipline. A chemistry teacher can usually handle both boards in chemistry, since the underlying content overlaps, but the assessed practical work does not transfer. The Diploma Programme carries an internally assessed scientific investigation with its own expectations around variables and evaluation. The Years 9 to 11 qualifications assess practical skills either in the laboratory or on paper depending on the variant chosen by the school. These are different pieces of coaching.

Languages and the humanities are the least shareable and the place where households most often overreach. English in the Diploma Programme is a literature or language-and-literature course with its own assessment structure; English in Years 9 to 11 is a different qualification with different components, sometimes including internally conducted speaking work. A tutor strong in one is frequently merely adequate in the other. If both your children need English, assume two tutors until a candidate proves otherwise.

Whatever you share, do not share the planning. Each child needs their own list of what is due and when, and their own diagnosis. Do not take weightings, paper durations or mark totals from any website, including this one, because both the IB and the awarding bodies revise their documents on their own cycles. Get the current guide or specification from each child's coordinator. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kemps Corner built on two correct documents is a different service from the same hours built on assumptions.

sections.heading: Two slots in one Kemps Corner evening across Cumballa Hill and Breach Candy
paragraphs: Running two children through one evening is a geography problem before it is a timetable problem. Kemps Corner sits at the junction where Peddar Road, August Kranti Marg and the roads up to Cumballa Hill meet beneath the flyover, and Breach Candy lies just west towards the sea. A tutor whose evening already runs through those streets can take a sibling pair back to back without adding a single journey. A tutor arriving from elsewhere is making one trip for two hours, which is a far better deal for them than one trip for one hour.

That is the quiet advantage of a two-child household here. Because the travel cost is fixed and the teaching time doubles, a sibling pair is an attractive booking for a good tutor, and you will often get a better candidate than a single-child enquiry at the same hour. The condition is that the two hours are consecutive. Two separate visits on two separate evenings removes the advantage entirely and leaves you competing for scarce slots twice.

The approach route still decides reliability. Grant Road, on the Western Line between Churchgate and Mumbai Central, is the dependable arrival for a tutor coming by train. From the north the numbers are worse than they look: eight kilometres from Worli to Colaba can take forty minutes once the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals back up, because South Mumbai is dense and short but slow. Tutors are therefore matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs.

None of the newer infrastructure changes this for weekly tutoring. Metro Line 3 from Cuffe Parade to the Bandra Kurla Complex, the Coastal Road, the Harbour Line and the Eastern Freeway have all altered how Mumbai, Maharashtra commutes without making a Borivali tutor viable for two consecutive hours in Kemps Corner. Parents who search IB and IGCSE tutors near me Kemps Corner and then ask for routes rather than distances end up with arrangements that hold through August.

sections.heading: Do IB and IGCSE deadlines collide in the Mumbai school year?
paragraphs: Yes, and the collision is predictable enough to plan around. The Mumbai school year runs June to April. For a Years 9 to 11 student the pressure builds towards internal mocks in the winter months and then the final papers. For a Diploma Programme student the internal assessment drafts, the Extended Essay progress points and Theory of Knowledge work cluster through the same winter window. If you have one child on each pathway, January and February are the weeks when both need an adult's attention at once.

Plan the tutoring around that rather than discovering it. The useful months for both children are June, July and August, when nothing is yet due and a tutor can fix foundations instead of firefighting. By December the Year 11 child needs more hours and the Diploma Programme child needs them too, and the household has one evening per day. Households that front-load the quiet months reach January with one child needing support instead of two.

Families around Kemps Corner mostly attend a small group of nearby schools, several of which teach both pathways. Activity High School is a short walk down Peddar Road. Aditya Birla World Academy sits at Tardeo across the flyover. Bombay International School is at Babulnath. Each sets its own internal assessment dates inside the relevant framework, which means two siblings at the same school can still have different crunch fortnights depending on their subject sets.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Activity High School, Aditya Birla World Academy, Bombay International School or any other school named here. We name them because their calendars are the clock any tutor works to in this part of Mumbai. We do not quote school results, we claim no standing inside any institution, and we do not guarantee grades for either board.

sections.heading: Home classes for one child and online for the other in Mumbai
paragraphs: A two-child household rarely wants the same mode for both, and splitting is usually right. The younger or less self-managing child takes the in-person hour, because the value there is supervision and watching the pen. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kemps Corner sitting beside a Year 9 student can see which step is being skipped, which no screen reliably shows. The older, more disciplined child can often take an online session for draft review or past-paper marking without losing anything.

The mode split also solves the evening arithmetic. One home visit plus one online session means only one person has to physically arrive, so the flyover can only ruin half your week. On a heavy monsoon evening the online hour still happens. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Kemps Corner is particularly sensible where a Diploma Programme Higher Level specialism is scarce on the island and the right teacher is simply elsewhere in the city.

If both children do need in-person hours, book them consecutively with the same tutor where the subject allows, and accept two tutors on two evenings where it does not. What does not work is two tutors on the same evening arriving independently: one of them will be late most weeks, and the child waiting is the one who loses. Consecutive sibling hours sometimes attract a different arrangement because the travel is shared, and that is worth asking about directly. sections.heading: What should a Mumbai parent check before booking two tutors?
paragraphs: Ask each candidate the same four questions and compare the answers side by side. Which board and which level are you teaching this academic year? Which components or criteria does that involve? What would the first three sessions cover for this child specifically? And where do you travel from, with what else in your evening? A tutor who gives you four concrete answers has a current practice. One who answers in general terms about international curricula may be describing experience from several years ago.

Our checks happen before you speak to anyone. Identity against a government document. The qualification, weighted towards what has been taught rather than studied, because a subject degree is not a teaching record. Teaching history with at least one reference from somebody who has watched them teach. And the level and board claim specifically, since the most commonly overstated item on a tutoring profile is Higher Level or Extended-tier experience.

When you are hiring two people at once, check the handover as well. Each tutor should send two written lines after a session, and you should read both, because a pattern in one child often explains something in the other. Decline nothing on the grounds of politeness: if a tutor will not put the slot, the fee basis, the cancellation rule and the reporting habit into a message before the first visit, that tells you how the next six months will go.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade on either board, and treat a quoted success rate as a prompt for harder questions. We do not guarantee grades. Parents search best IB and IGCSE tutor in Kemps Corner, and no such ranking exists for either system, let alone both. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Kemps Corner neighbours recommend may be excellent, and deserves the same four questions as anyone we introduce.

sections.heading: What changes when your child moves from IGCSE into the Diploma Programme?
paragraphs: Almost everything about how work is judged, and very little about the content. A student finishing Year 11 has spent two years learning to answer written questions against a mark scheme, where method credit is explicit and a well-rehearsed technique earns reliably. The Diploma Programme asks for something different: six subjects chosen deliberately, three at Higher Level with real depth, internally assessed coursework that is planned rather than answered, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge sitting across the whole thing.

The specific shock is the coursework. A Year 11 student has rarely had to design anything. In the Diploma Programme a science student plans an investigation, chooses variables, justifies a method and evaluates it. A mathematics student picks an exploration topic that has to contain genuine mathematics rather than a tidy application. These are open tasks with deadlines months away, and students who thrived on structured papers often stall completely on the first one. This is the most common reason a strong Year 11 result is followed by a difficult DP1 report.

The second shock is depth at Higher Level. Content that was covered once in Years 9 to 11 returns with more treatment and harder questions, and the pace assumes the foundation is solid. A student who passed the earlier papers by memorising methods usually finds this out in October of DP1, which is exactly when families in Kemps Corner start enquiring. A tutor at that point is working on understanding rather than coverage, and it takes a term rather than a month.

What to do about it is unglamorous and effective. Use the gap summer, after Year 11 papers and before the Diploma Programme starts, for two things: shoring up the mathematics or language that the chosen Higher Level subjects will assume, and practising one open-ended piece of work with no mark scheme attached. A handful of sessions then is worth considerably more than a crisis booking in November. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kemps Corner arranged across that transition is the single most useful thing a two-board household can plan.

sections.heading: Realistic progress when home tuition runs for two children
paragraphs: Expect the two children to move at different speeds, and do not read the difference as a judgement on either. A Year 11 student with a technique gap can show visible change in a month, because showing working and reading command words are habits rather than knowledge. A Diploma Programme student struggling with Higher Level depth or with an open coursework task will show nothing measurable for six weeks and then move substantially. Judging both at four weeks against the same yardstick is the commonest mistake in two-child households.

What should be true for both at four weeks is that the tutor can name the problem precisely and show you work that demonstrates it. By one term you should see a change in method you can recognise without subject knowledge: working shown, structure before sentences, a method section another person could follow, a plan written before a draft. Grade bands may not have moved for either child, and a band is a wide instrument that hides real improvement.

By one exam cycle the honest question for both is the same: has the gap between unhurried work and timed or assessed work narrowed? For the Years 9 to 11 child that means the examination hall. For the Diploma Programme child it means the moderated coursework and the papers together. That gap is what home tuition narrows, and it narrows unevenly. We do not guarantee grades for either child, because the marks come from work they produce without us in the room.

There are also two-child households we advise not to book at all, or to book only half of. If one child's marks fell across every subject at once, if either child is exhausted rather than confused, or if the real problem is a classroom relationship, more instruction is the wrong instrument and the year head is the right first call. We say that before taking a booking rather than after, and in a two-child enquiry it quite often applies to one of the two.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both our children if they are on different boards?
faqs.answer: In mathematics, often yes. In the sciences, within one discipline, sometimes. In English and the humanities, usually not. The reason is that the content overlaps far more than the assessment does: criterion marking in the International Baccalaureate and mark-scheme marking on written papers reward different behaviours, and coursework expectations differ entirely. Ask any candidate which board and level they are teaching this academic year for each child, and what the components involve. If the answer is confident for one child and vague for the other, hire them for one child and find a second tutor.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building for two consecutive hours in the evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the arrangement most worth asking for. A tutor crossing the Kemps Corner flyover at six for a single hour has given up a large part of their evening. The same journey for two consecutive hours is a much better proposition, which is why sibling pairs frequently attract a stronger candidate than a single-child enquiry at the same time. Confirm the building entry once with the watchman for a named visitor at a fixed day and hour, and give the tutor the flat number, wing and lift in writing before the first visit.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home when two children are being taught?
faqs.answer: An adult in the flat is sensible, particularly for the younger child, but not in the room for either session. Teenagers work less honestly with a parent listening and the tutor needs them to admit what they do not understand. Be available for the last five minutes of each hour instead, because hearing both summaries back to back often reveals something neither tutor would mention alone. If both parents work late, staff at home is fine provided somebody can let the tutor in without a phone call upstairs every week.

faqs.question: Where should two children study if the flat has one usable table?
faqs.answer: Stagger rather than share. Two consecutive hours at the same table works better than two simultaneous sessions in different corners, because neither child concentrates with another lesson audible. If you must run them together, separate rooms and closed doors, not two ends of a living room. Keep each child's textbooks and exercise books in a separate drawer so the handover between hours costs nothing. Families who sort this once stop losing ten minutes of every session to furniture and fetching.

faqs.question: Our Year 11 child starts the Diploma Programme next year. When should we start tutoring?
faqs.answer: The summer between the two, and almost nobody does. After the Year 11 papers and before the Diploma Programme begins, a handful of sessions can shore up the mathematics or language that the chosen Higher Level subjects will assume, and give the student one experience of an open-ended piece of work with no mark scheme to follow. That is the specific thing that trips strong Year 11 students in DP1. It is cheaper, calmer and more effective than the crisis booking that typically follows a difficult October report.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Kemps Corner depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level, how scarce the subject specialism is on the island, how far the tutor travels, how long each session runs, and how many sessions a week you book. For two children there is a sixth factor worth raising directly: whether consecutive hours with one tutor change the arrangement, since the travel cost is shared. A Diploma Programme Higher Level specialist in a thin subject sits at the higher end, a Years 9 to 11 generalist who walks from Cumballa Hill at the lower. We publish no price list because any figure would mislead most readers.

faqs.question: Should we start both children at the same time?
faqs.answer: Usually not. One child is almost always genuinely urgent and the other is coasting rather than failing, and a household has one evening per day. Start with the urgent child in the quiet months, get that arrangement stable, then add the second. Beginning both at once feels even-handed and tends to leave both sessions shallow, especially once winter deadlines land on both pathways in the same fortnight. Tell us which child is urgent and we will build the shortlist accordingly rather than quoting for two placements.

faqs.question: Is an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Kemps Corner sensible for one of the two?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and it is the easiest way to make two children work in one evening. Put the older, more self-managing child online for draft review and past-paper marking, and keep the in-person hour for the child who needs supervision and whose written working someone has to watch. It also means only one person has to physically arrive, so a jammed flyover approach can only cost you half a week. The pattern to avoid is both children drifting online by February because it was convenient in December.

faqs.question: One tutor is working and the other is not. What happens?
faqs.answer: Tell us about the one that is not and leave the other alone. We rematch for that child only, passing on the outgoing tutor's notes so the replacement does not bill you to repeat a month of diagnosis. Most mismatches are fit rather than competence, so say which: too gentle for a child who needs pushing, or too fast for one who stops asking questions. Where consecutive sibling hours are involved, we try to preserve the sequence, because losing a good two-hour evening slot in this part of Mumbai is harder to recover from than changing a tutor.

faqs.question: Which areas around Kemps Corner share the same tutor pool?
faqs.answer: Cumballa Hill, Breach Candy and Peddar Road are effectively one catchment with Kemps Corner, and a tutor matched to you is usually teaching in at least one of them during the same week. Tardeo, Babulnath and the area around Grant Road station extend the pool at the easier hours, and the island down towards Colaba is treated as a single unit. We avoid pulling tutors from the Western or Eastern Suburbs of Mumbai for weekday evening work, and that applies twice over when two consecutive hours are involved.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell us how each child will finish?
faqs.answer: No, for either board. We do not guarantee grades, and a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade is selling certainty the assessment does not allow. What a competent tutor will give you after a few weeks is a defensible read per child: which topics or criteria are secure, which are not, what range is realistic if the remaining months are used well, and what specifically would have to change to reach the upper end. If anyone quotes a success rate across their students, ask what population that number is counting.

sections.heading: From IGCSE into the Diploma Programme: what actually transfers?
paragraphs: Content transfers; assessment habits mostly do not. A student arriving in Diploma Programme (DP) year one from a strong International General Certificate of Secondary Education background has the mathematical and scientific vocabulary they need and a working knowledge of how to revise for a terminal paper. What they do not have is experience of extended independent work. The Internal Assessment (IA), the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) all ask a student to define their own question and defend their own method, which is a skill nobody needed in Year 11.

That mismatch is the single most predictable crisis in the two-board household, and it arrives about eight weeks into DP1. A student who scored well in Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel examinations suddenly produces a mediocre first IA draft, and the family concludes the child has stopped working. Usually they have not. They are applying Year 11 technique, which rewarded completeness and neat recall, to a task that rewards narrowness, justification and honest handling of uncertainty. A tutor who has taken students through this handover names it in the first session instead of treating it as a motivation problem.

The Higher Level and Standard Level decision is the other transfer point parents underestimate. A grade that looked strong at IGCSE does not automatically mean Higher Level is the right call in that subject, because Higher Level asks for depth of reasoning rather than more of the same content. Equally, a middling IGCSE result does not rule out Standard Level success. This decision belongs with your school's Diploma Programme coordinator, and a good tutor's contribution is an honest read on working speed and independence rather than an opinion on ambition.

If your household has a Year 11 student and a DP student at once, there is an advantage available: the older one has already crossed the bridge. Used carefully, that is worth more than an extra session. We often suggest that the DP1 student explains their IA research question to the Year 11 at the dinner table, which forces precision on one and previews the demand for the other. It costs nothing and it is the sort of thing IB and IGCSE home tuition in Khar West should be arranged around rather than ignored.

sections.heading: Subject by subject: where the two boards reward different things
paragraphs: In Mathematics the divergence is largest. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel at Extended tier reward accurate, fast, well-presented method on familiar question types. Mathematics in the Diploma Programme, whether Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, asks for reasoning about unfamiliar situations and carries an exploration that the student designs. A tutor who drills past paper types will serve the first well and the second badly. A tutor who only works conceptually will frustrate a Year 10 who needs to stop losing method marks. These are different jobs and we staff them differently.

In the sciences the overlap is real and usable. The content ladder from IGCSE Physics or Chemistry into the Diploma Programme is continuous enough that one strong subject teacher can hold both, and the main difference is the assessment: an alternative-to-practical or laboratory paper at IGCSE against a designed investigation with uncertainty analysis at DP. A tutor who can explain why a repeated measurement matters will make sense to both children in the same house, which is why science is the subject where a shared tutor most often works.

English and the humanities sit somewhere between. First Language English at IGCSE is largely about directed response and reading precision; Language A in the Diploma Programme is about sustained argument from textual evidence with no safety net of a comprehension question. History moves from source provenance at IGCSE to historiography and essay construction at DP. A tutor who understands both can show a Year 11 that the skill they are learning now is the junior version of the one their sibling is struggling with, which is a genuinely useful thing for both to hear.

We do not reproduce component weightings, paper durations or mark totals anywhere here, for either board. Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel and the International Baccalaureate revise their documents on separate cycles, and a figure remembered from a tutor's last cohort may be wrong for your child's session. Take the structure from the current syllabus or subject guide and from the school's coordinator. Use an IB and IGCSE private tutor Khar West parents hire for the craft: the method line, the research question, the paragraph that proves.

The practical consequence is that your household has roughly two crunch periods rather than one, and they sometimes overlap.

sections.heading: Does home tuition in Mumbai work when siblings sit different boards?
paragraphs: Yes, and it is usually the most efficient arrangement available, provided you do not try to make one tutor do everything. The reason home tuition suits a two-board household is logistical rather than pedagogical: one adult arrives at one address and two children get taught, back to back, without anybody travelling. Two consecutive separate lessons on one visit makes an awkward hour worth protecting for the tutor and removes the gate problem, because one visitor registration covers one arrival rather than two on different days.

The condition is that the subject genuinely spans both boards. Science works. Mathematics across Extended tier and Higher Level usually does not. Where it does not, the sensible structure is one tutor at your table for the subject that overlaps, and a second tutor, often online, for the one that does not. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Khar West earns their place exactly here: the scarce specialist for one child, reached without a journey, while the other child's session stays in person.

Online has a second use in this household specifically. The Diploma Programme student is usually old enough to work well on a screen, share a draft and take written feedback, while the Year 10 or Year 11 student often is not. So the natural split is in-person for the younger child and online or hybrid for the older one, which is the reverse of what most families assume when they book. It also frees the in-person slot to be earlier in the evening, which the younger child needs more.

Hybrid is where nearly every two-board family here settles by the second month. One in-person visit a week covering both children where possible, plus online sessions for drafts, marking walkthroughs and the question that surfaces at 10pm. Through the monsoon the in-person session converts to online without the week being lost. Changing mode mid-term costs nothing with us, and in a household with two syllabuses running you should expect to change at least once. Most IB and IGCSE home tuition in Khar West settles into this shape by about the second month.

sections.heading: How do you verify a tutor who claims both boards?
paragraphs: Ask them to distinguish the two, in detail, without prompting. The question that works is simple: what would you do differently teaching this topic to a Year 10 on Cambridge papers and to a Standard Level student in the Diploma Programme? A tutor who genuinely holds both answers immediately and concretely, usually in terms of assessment demand rather than content. A tutor who has taught one and read about the other gives you a general answer about covering the syllabus and building fundamentals, which tells you everything.

On our side, verification covers identity against government photo identification, the subject degree rather than a general teaching certificate, and teaching history recorded per board and per level, so Cambridge Chemistry at Extended tier and Chemistry at Higher Level are logged as two separate competences rather than one. References where the tutor has worked in Mumbai schools. And a live teaching sample on a topic they do not select, where we watch whether the first question to the student arrives inside three minutes and whether a second explanation exists when the first one fails.

There are checks only a parent can make, and in a two-board household there is one extra. Ask how many years on each board at each level, separately. Ask what they would look at first in each child's most recent marked work. Ask what they will show you after four weeks, per child. And ask whether they would rather hand one of the two children to a colleague, because the tutors worth having say yes to that question more often than the ones who want both slots.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade on either board. Nobody honest can, we do not guarantee grades, and the offer is a judgement signal. The same applies to a quoted session count given before anyone has seen the work, and to a profile that lists every subject across both systems. A search for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Khar West should resolve into two well-matched people rather than one impressive claim. Good IB and IGCSE home tuition in Khar West looks like two narrow appointments, not one broad one.

sections.heading: The Year 11 to DP1 gap in Mumbai: the most underused weeks in the two-board household
paragraphs: Between the end of the IGCSE external series and the start of Diploma Programme year one there is a stretch of weeks with no school pressure in it at all, and almost every family here wastes it. The student has just finished a terminal examination series and wants to do nothing, which is reasonable. The parents are relieved and do not want a fight, which is also reasonable. Then DP1 begins, the first Internal Assessment brief arrives, and the student meets independent assessment with no preparation for it whatsoever.

A modest intervention in those weeks pays for itself several times over, and it is not more content. Four or five sessions on one thing: how to turn a vague interest into a researchable question. That is the skill the Internal Assessment and the Extended Essay both rest on, and it is the one no part of IGCSE ever asked for. A tutor can run it as a workshop rather than a course, taking a topic the student actually cares about and narrowing it ruthlessly until it is answerable, then widening it until it is interesting again.

The second useful thing in that gap is subject-specific reading rather than subject-specific teaching. A student heading into Higher Level Chemistry benefits more from reading one real paper badly and discussing it than from pre-learning the first unit, because the first unit will be taught anyway and the habit of reading above your level will not be. The same is true for Language A, where reading two books from the prescribed list before term starts changes the whole first semester.

There is a Khar West specific reason this window is easy to use. Tutors on this corridor work the line rather than the roads, holding families from Bandra through to Juhu, and in those weeks their evenings are unusually open because the exam cohort has finished. That is the one period in the year when the strong local specialists have time, so a family asking for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Khar West in that window gets a choice they will not have in October. Most parents only discover this after they have lived through a difficult DP1.

sections.heading: From IGCSE to the Diploma Programme: what actually transfers?
paragraphs: Content transfers reasonably well and assessment habits transfer badly, which is why the first term of the Diploma Programme catches out strong IGCSE students. A student who scored highly in IGCSE Mathematics walks into Diploma Programme (DP) Mathematics with most of the algebra and trigonometry already in place. What they do not have is the habit of justifying a method, writing to a command term, or producing extended independent work. Those are the three things the International Baccalaureate (IB) assesses hardest and the three the IGCSE route does not drill.

The reverse journey matters too, because many Kharghar families have a younger child in the Middle Years Programme (MYP) heading towards an IGCSE entry at a different school. MYP marks against published criteria and rewards reflection and process. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel papers reward precision, completeness and keeping to the mark scheme. A student who has learned to write reflectively has to learn to write economically, and a tutor who has taught both routes can name that difference in week one instead of six months later.

The practical reading for a household running both boards is that the two children need different coaching styles even in the same subject. The IGCSE student needs question technique, time discipline and working shown. The IB student needs reasoning made visible, independent planning for Internal Assessment (IA) work, and the ability to sustain an argument. A tutor who treats them identically is teaching one of them badly. This is the main reason we ask about each child separately rather than taking a household enquiry.

For the live structure of any programme or subject, use the board's current syllabus or the IB's current subject guide and your school's coordinator. Both the IB and the examination boards revise on their own cycles, so a paper layout or a component description from a few years ago may not match what your child sits. A tutor who says they will check the live documents before session two is doing the job properly rather than hedging.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended across both boards
paragraphs: Each board asks a family to make one irreversible-feeling choice, and the two choices land at different ages. At IGCSE the decision is the tier: many subjects are entered at one of two levels, commonly described as Core and Extended, with different papers and different grade ranges, and the school makes that entry earlier than parents expect. In the Diploma Programme the decision is Higher Level versus Standard Level across six subjects, usually three at HL, and it quietly decides which university courses stay open.

In a household running both, the two decisions interact in a way nobody warns you about. A Year 10 student entered at the lower tier in Mathematics has a harder route into Diploma Programme Mathematics two years later, so the tier decision is not only about the IGCSE result. We raise this with Kharghar parents because it is the single most consequential thing a tutor can influence cheaply, and because it only works if somebody is looking two years ahead rather than at the next report.

Internally assessed work exists on both sides and the rules are the same: a tutor coaches the skill and never touches the writing. IGCSE carries coursework or an alternative written component depending on the subject and board. The IB carries an exploration in Mathematics, an investigation in the sciences, oral and written tasks in Language A, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Any tutor who offers to produce that work should be removed from the shortlist, because the school submits an academic-honesty declaration in your child's name.

Local supply is good in the mainstream and thin at the edges on both boards. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics, Business and English are reliably available from tutors between CBD Belapur and Panvel, which is why requests for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Kharghar families send us can usually be filled locally. Psychology, Visual Arts at HL, Music, Drama and rarer languages are scarce across Navi Mumbai, and a parent asking about all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Kharghar can cover deserves that answered honestly in the first call.

paragraphs: Within the node chain, yes, and the chain is the reason. Navi Mumbai was planned as a sequence of nodes running Vashi, Nerul, CBD Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, connected by the Sion–Panvel Highway and Palm Beach Road, each a short drive from the next. A tutor living in Kharghar can hold a standing slot here, another in CBD Belapur, a third in Kamothe and a weekend one in Panvel, and still eat dinner at home. That is what makes extended ninety-minute sibling visits possible rather than theoretical.

Each neighbour behaves slightly differently. CBD Belapur is the closest and shares the Metro alignment with Kharghar, which matters for the many capable tutors who travel without a car. Kamothe sits just across the highway and is the simplest address to add to an evening already running in Kharghar. Panvel is the far end, and we tell Panvel families directly that a weekday six o'clock arrival is comfortable in the dry months and optimistic in the monsoon, while a weekend morning holds all year.

The arrangement we decline to set up is a tutor crossing from the island city. Reaching Kharghar from Chembur or Wadala over the Atal Setu (MTHL) or along the Harbour Line (Vashi–Panvel) looks straightforward on a map and works for about a month. The return leg at half past eight is what ends it, and when two children are sharing a ninety-minute visit the stakes are doubled, because one cancellation costs two children a week. The IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kharghar that lasts is staffed from this side of the water.

If you are not in Kharghar itself, say so when you enquire, because the shortlist and the realistic start time both change. Searches for IB and IGCSE tutors near me Kharghar come from all four nodes, and a Kamothe or CBD Belapur address usually gets more choice of evening than a Panvel one. We would rather set the expectation correctly at the start than have you renegotiate the slot in week five.

sections.heading: Why does a Kharghar school calendar carry two sets of deadlines?
paragraphs: Because a school running both pathways has to satisfy two different assessment regimes in the same academic year, and the dates do not line up. Children around Kharghar attend schools including D.Y. Patil International School and Ryan Global School, both on international pathways. A school with an IGCSE cohort and an IB cohort will have coursework and oral components falling due for one group while the other is submitting Internal Assessment drafts, and the two sets of parents hear about completely different pressure weeks.

For a household with a child in each cohort, that means the family calendar has two peaks rather than one. The pre-Diwali report usually covers both children and reads as a single event, but the real pressure arrives separately: an IGCSE mock season in the new year, and an IB deadline cluster that depends on the Diploma coordinator rather than the examinations officer. Writing both children's fixed dates on one sheet in September is the most useful hour a parent can spend, and it changes what both tutors prioritise.

The monsoon applies to everybody equally. Between June and September the Sion–Panvel Highway and the approach roads into the Kharghar sectors slow unpredictably, and a six o'clock visit for two children becomes a quarter past often enough to compress the younger child's half of the session. Families who move the shared slot to a later start or a weekend morning for those four months lose far fewer sessions than those who hold the original time and then cancel twice.

IB Gram is an independent platform. We are not affiliated with D.Y. Patil International School, Ryan Global School or any other school in Mumbai, Maharashtra, and we name them only to describe where local families actually are. We also have no access to internal school calendars, so each tutor should take the dates from the child's own planner in week one and plan backwards from the nearest fixed one.

sections.heading: Home classes for two children in Kharghar: scheduling the week
paragraphs: The arrangement that works best for two children is one longer home tuition visit with a clean split rather than two short ones on different evenings. A ninety-minute visit divided into two forty-five minute halves, with the second child doing set work in another room during the first half, gets both children taught and keeps one journey instead of two. It only works when the tutor lives close enough to commit to ninety minutes, which is the practical reason this page keeps returning to distance.

The split has to be enforced or it collapses. The older child, usually the one with examinations closer, will absorb the whole session if allowed, and the younger one ends up with fifteen minutes and a worksheet. We ask tutors to hold the clock and to report what each child covered, and we ask parents to check that report rather than assume. A shared slot that has drifted into a single-child slot is the most common way this arrangement fails, and it is easy to spot in week three.

Online has a real place in a two-board household, and it is usually the second subject rather than the first. A scarce IB subject with no local teacher, or a short marking session for an IGCSE student in the final weeks, is better done on a call than not done at all. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Kharghar is the right answer for those cases and the wrong one for a younger child who cannot yet work unsupervised for twenty minutes. Hybrid, with one visit and one call, suits most DP students by the second term.

Parents comparing options sometimes ask for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Kharghar as a shortcut past all of this. There is no single person who is best for two children on two boards. What exists is a good match per child, and an IB and IGCSE private tutor Kharghar families keep for years is usually the one who was honest in the first week about which child needed more of the hour.

sections.heading: Checking a tutor who claims both IB and IGCSE experience
paragraphs: Treat the two claims as separate and ask for evidence of each. A tutor who has taught Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel for years may have read an IB guide once, and a tutor from an IB school may never have seen a Core-tier paper. We verify government photo identity, the degree certificate for the subject, and each board or programme claim with a school name and a span of years rather than a line on a form. We also check that the nodes they list are nodes they genuinely travel to each week.

The test you can run yourself takes ten minutes per claim. For the IGCSE side, hand them a structured question from a recent paper and ask where the marks sit and what loses them; expect command words, working shown and units in the answer. For the IB side, ask how the internal assessment in that subject is marked and what separates an adequate response from a strong one; expect criterion strands and the role of the moderator. Vague answers about practice and hard work mean the claim is thin.

Two offers should end a conversation on either board. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because no honest teacher can give one and the offer shows how else they will handle a difficult truth. And refuse any offer to write coursework, an Internal Assessment or an Extended Essay, because the school submits an academic-honesty declaration in your child's name and the consequence falls on the student. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and will not list a tutor who claims to.

With two children the gate logistics matter more, not less. A tutor staying ninety minutes needs a standing weekly entry registered once at your society office rather than signed in each week, and in several Kharghar complexes the flat owner has to lodge that in person. We provide a photograph and identity number for the purpose. Tell us the building's visitor rule when you enquire, and the paperwork is ready before the first visit rather than after the third.

sections.heading: Is it cheaper to run both boards through one tutor in Kharghar?
paragraphs: It is usually cheaper per child and occasionally a false economy, and the deciding factor is how far apart the two children are. One tutor across two children in the same subject within a few years of each other is genuinely efficient: one journey, one relationship with the household, and often a better rate for the second child because travel is already paid for. One tutor across an HL Diploma Programme candidate and a Year 9 student in a different subject is two jobs billed as one, and the weaker half shows up in a report.

Six things move what IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Kharghar come to, and none of them is a published list. The programme and level, the board and tier, how scarce the subject is locally, how far the tutor travels into your sector, how long and how often sessions run, and whether written work is marked between visits. The last of those explains most of the apparently inexplicable gaps between two quotes for the same subject on the same street. One is buying contact time, the other is buying feedback on drafts.

The second-child discount is real but worth interrogating. Ask whether the ninety minutes is genuinely split or whether the younger child is being supervised rather than taught, and ask what each child will have covered by the Diwali break. A tutor who answers both precisely is offering a shared slot. A tutor who answers warmly but generally is offering one lesson with an audience, and you will discover which in about a month.

Where the two children are too far apart to share, running two tutors is not twice the cost of one in practice, because the second tutor often takes a shorter session. Our usual recommendation to Kharghar households is to put the money where the nearer deadline is. A Year 11 facing examinations this year has a harder constraint than a Year 8 who has time, and the IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kharghar we arrange is weighted that way unless you tell us otherwise.

sections.heading: What four weeks looks like when two children share a tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: By week four you should have two separate progress stories, not one. Each child should be able to say what a task is asking before starting it, each should have notes organised by topic, and each should be completing the work set between visits. If one child's half of the session has quietly shrunk, that is visible by the fourth visit and is the moment to fix it. The most common failure in a shared slot is not a bad tutor but an unenforced clock.

At one term the marks move at different speeds for the two boards, which can look alarming if you expect symmetry. The IGCSE child usually shows measurable movement first, because the mark schemes are explicit and technique converts quickly. The IB child may show no mark change at all while their reasoning and planning improve, which is real progress that a report card does not capture. Judge the IB child on whether an Internal Assessment plan now has dates on it rather than on a predicted grade.

Across a full cycle the honest claim is about preparation rather than ability, on both boards. We do not guarantee grades, we do not publish success rates, and we would be cautious of any Mumbai service that offers either, because the arithmetic behind such a figure is never shown. What consistent home tuition in Mumbai produces is a student who has written the kind of answer their paper asks for, under time, and had it marked properly before it counts.

If the arrangement fails for one child and works for the other, we re-match for that child only and keep the working half intact. Tell us in week two rather than week eight, because by the eighth session the child who got the thin half of the hour has usually concluded the subject is the problem. There is no charge for a re-match. Tell us whether it was pace, manner, punctuality or depth, and the replacement shortlist changes accordingly.

faqs.question: Can one home tutor teach our Year 10 IGCSE child and our MYP child together?
faqs.answer: In the same subject and within a few years of each other, often yes, and most of our shared home classes in this node are exactly that. Mathematics is the clearest case: the content runs along similar lines even though the assessment differs, so one tutor can take a ninety-minute visit split into two halves. Where it stops working is a large gap in level, such as a Diploma Programme Higher Level candidate alongside a Year 9 student, or two different subjects. Then you are paying one person to do two jobs, and the younger child reliably gets the thinner half.

faqs.question: Our older child moves from IGCSE to the Diploma Programme next year. What should a tutor do now?
faqs.answer: Spend this year on the habits the Diploma Programme assesses and IGCSE does not. That means justifying a method rather than only reaching an answer, writing to a command term, and sustaining a piece of independent work over weeks instead of days. The content carries over well; the working style does not. A tutor who has taught both routes can introduce those three habits during Year 11 without disturbing examination preparation, which is far cheaper than discovering the gap in the first Diploma Programme term.

faqs.question: How do we split a ninety-minute session fairly between two children?
faqs.answer: Set the split in writing before the first visit and ask the tutor to report what each child covered. Forty-five minutes each is the usual arrangement, with the second child working on set tasks in another room during the first half. The drift is always in the same direction, towards the child with the nearer examination, so check the report rather than assume. If one child's half has shrunk by week three, say so then; it is an easy correction early and an entrenched habit by week eight.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Kharghar for a longer evening visit?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided they live inside the node, and that is precisely why we staff from here. A ninety-minute visit is only sustainable when the journey either side is ten or fifteen minutes, which is realistic from a Kharghar sector, CBD Belapur or Kamothe. A tutor coming from across the creek can manage a sixty-minute session for a month before the return journey makes the arrangement fail. Register a standing gate entry for the tutor in week one so the longer visit is not eaten by the barrier.

faqs.question: Does the tier our Year 10 child is entered for affect their Diploma Programme options?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than most families realise, and this is the strongest argument for thinking two years ahead. A student entered at the lower tier in Mathematics has a harder route into Diploma Programme Mathematics, and the entry is made by the school earlier than parents expect. A tutor's most valuable contribution in Year 9 or early Year 10 is often producing evidence that the harder tier is realistic, by having the student sit a timed past paper at each tier and marking it against the published scheme.

faqs.question: Which board is better for university applications?
faqs.answer: Neither, at the stage these two sit at. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel IGCSEs are treated as equivalent school-leaving qualifications at that point, and the International Baccalaureate Diploma is a separate later qualification rather than a competitor to them. What universities actually read is the final set of results and the reference. Choosing a board for prestige rather than for the fit between the school and the child is the common mistake, and it is one a tutor cannot repair afterwards.

faqs.question: What do two children of home tuition in Kharghar cost compared with one?
faqs.answer: Less than double in most arrangements, and we will not quote a figure we would have to invent. Where one tutor takes both children in a shared slot, the travel is already paid for and many tutors price the second child lower. Where two separate tutors are needed, the second session is often shorter, so the total is still below twice the first. Six factors move any of these numbers: programme, level or tier, subject scarcity, travel, session length and frequency, and marking between visits.

faqs.question: We are in Kamothe rather than Kharghar. Does a shared sibling slot still work?
faqs.answer: Yes, and Kamothe is one of the easier addresses for it. Kamothe sits immediately across the Sion–Panvel Highway from Kharghar, so a tutor already teaching here can add a longer visit in Kamothe on the same evening without a real journey. CBD Belapur works similarly and shares the Metro alignment. Panvel is the address where we are candid: a weekday ninety-minute visit there is comfortable in the dry months and a weekend morning is the arrangement that survives the monsoon.

faqs.question: One child is improving and the other is not. Do we change tutors?
faqs.answer: Change for the child it is failing and keep the other arrangement untouched. A shared slot that works for one child and not the other is usually a clock problem rather than a competence problem, so the first step is to check what each child actually covered each week. If the split has been honest and one child is still stuck, we re-match for that child at no charge. Keeping a working relationship in place while replacing the other half is almost always better than starting over.

faqs.question: Do both children need to be present for the whole visit?
faqs.answer: No, and it works better when they are not. The usual pattern has the second child working on set tasks elsewhere in the flat during the first half, then swapping. Two children in the room for ninety minutes means neither gets taught properly and the older one answers for the younger. What does need to be consistent is the location: a common area with the door open rather than a bedroom, which also makes the split easy for a parent to observe without sitting in.

faqs.question: Can one of the two children be taught online while the other has a home visit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a scarce subject it is often the best plan available. A household can reasonably run a Diploma Programme Higher Level subject online with a specialist who lives elsewhere while the younger child has a weekly visit from a local tutor. The caution is the younger child: online works poorly for a student who cannot yet work alone for twenty minutes, so if one of the two must go online, it should normally be the older one.

faqs.question: Can you tell us what results to expect for either child?
faqs.answer: No, and any service that offers a figure is selling rather than forecasting. We do not guarantee grades and we do not publish success rates, because the method behind such numbers is never shown. What tutoring changes is preparation: whether each child has attempted the kinds of questions their own board will ask, understands how their work is marked, and finishes internally assessed work before the deadline rather than during it. On two boards at once, that is already a substantial amount of ground to hold.

sections.heading: From IGCSE Year 11 into DP1: what actually changes?
paragraphs: The workload stops being set for your child and starts being set by your child, and that is the whole transition in one sentence. Through the IGCSE years a student is given tasks with deadlines, a syllabus to cover and papers to practise. In the Diploma Programme (DP) a student carries an Internal Assessment (IA) in every subject, an Extended Essay (EE), a Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay and Creativity, Activity, Service commitments, most of which are independent work with distant deadlines. Students who were organised by their school in Year 11 and not by themselves tend to hit the wall in the first DP1 reporting cycle, around November.

The second change is depth over breadth. IGCSE rewards accurate coverage of a defined content range across more subjects. The DP narrows to six subject groups and asks for sustained analysis in three Higher Level (HL) subjects, where a question can require combining two topics the student learned months apart. A student who got strong IGCSE grades through disciplined revision sometimes finds HL harder than a weaker but more curious classmate, which is counterintuitive and worth knowing before you panic about a first DP1 report.

There is also a route that skips IGCSE entirely. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs to roughly Year 11 and is assessed against published criteria rather than external papers, so a student arriving in DP1 from MYP has met criterion-based marking already but has never sat a high-stakes external examination. A student arriving from IGCSE has the opposite profile. Both gaps are teachable and they are different gaps, which is the main reason IB Gram asks about the route rather than just the year group.

For either route, confirm the structure with the current IB subject guide or your school's DP coordinator and with the current Cambridge or Edexcel syllabus for the IGCSE subjects, rather than any summary you read online. Both the IB and the examination boards revise their documents on their own cycles, and component names and assessment patterns change between cohorts. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Kolshet Road families hire should be working from this year's document, not the one they were taught from.

sections.heading: Choosing subjects twice: Year 9 and again for the IB Diploma in Mumbai
paragraphs: Families on this corridor make two consequential subject decisions four years apart, and the first one constrains the second more than anyone tells them. At Year 9 the choice is which IGCSE subjects to carry and at which tier, where Cambridge Core covers a narrower content range and caps the awardable grade while Extended covers the full range. At DP selection the choice is six subject groups, three at Higher Level, and some combinations are effectively closed to a student who dropped a subject or sat it at the lower tier. A student who left Extended Mathematics behind in Year 10 will find Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level very hard going.

The practical rule worth following is to keep the doors open for the subjects your child might want and close the ones they certainly will not. That means taking Extended Mathematics if there is any chance of a quantitative Diploma route, keeping a separate science rather than a combined award if medicine or engineering is in the conversation, and not dropping a second language on the assumption it will not be needed. None of this requires knowing what a fourteen-year-old wants to do. It requires not foreclosing it at fourteen.

The assessment work also looks different on either side of the line. IGCSE coursework and controlled assessments are school-set, bounded tasks with clear instructions. DP Internal Assessments are independent research pieces, and the commonest failure is a research question too broad to be answered in the available length, which takes an hour to fix in September and cannot be fixed in February. IB Gram lists tutors for all IB and IGCSE subjects and the tutor in Kolshet Road matched to each child works to that child's own assessment calendar rather than a blended one.

Across all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Kolshet Road families arrange, the single instruction that improves the first lesson most is a list: each child's codes or subject guides, the next three deadlines, and the two topics the last report flagged. Parents who send that get a diagnostic lesson aimed at something. Parents who send help with maths and science get a lesson spent working out what to aim at.

sections.heading: Which Thane schools run which board, and why it matters in Mumbai
paragraphs: Families near Kolshet Road send children to a small set of schools and the board pathway differs between them, which is exactly how a household ends up with two boards under one roof. Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane runs a Cambridge IGCSE pathway. NES International School covers IB and Cambridge routes. Billabong High International School has a Thane campus, and some families travel further into Mumbai, to Oberoi International School on JVLR or Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai. Those names are local context only. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of them.

Two calendars in one house is the practical problem, and it is worse than it sounds. The IGCSE child's heaviest weeks are pre-boards and coursework deadlines in January and February, with the main examination series after that. The Diploma child's heaviest weeks are also January and February, when Internal Assessment drafts cluster, the Extended Essay hits its school-set deadline and the Theory of Knowledge essay needs finishing. One fortnight can carry a Year 11 pre-board timetable and three independent DP pieces, in the same flat, with one dining table.

Planning around that is the single most useful thing a parent on this corridor can do in August. Ask each child's school for the internal deadlines in writing: coursework dates, mock windows, the EE and IA submission dates. Put both calendars on one sheet. Then book home tuition in Mumbai against the gaps rather than against the crunch, because a tutor engaged in June can front-load the work and a tutor engaged in late January is scheduling around other people's emergencies.

One honest statement about outcomes, since this page is about two children and the temptation to promise is doubled. We do not guarantee grades, for either board, and a tutor who talks in guaranteed outcomes during a DP cycle or an IGCSE series is describing a sales script. What is controllable is whether each child walks in having written to a real structure, sat papers to time, and met the command terms before the examination hall.

sections.heading: Home tuition for two children on different boards in Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here because it is the only mode that scales to a household rather than a student. One tutor arriving at your tower can teach a Year 10 at 5.30pm and a DP1 student at 7pm, use the same dining table, and leave two written notes. The same arrangement run as two separate centre batches means two commutes through the Ghodbunder evening and four hours of family logistics. The IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kolshet Road model is not just more attentive, it is less disruptive to the rest of the week.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Kolshet Road earns its place in two specific situations. The first is a thin-pool subject, which in the DP usually means Higher Level Psychology, Higher Level Economics or a language, and at IGCSE means Computer Science, Accounting or Additional Mathematics. The second is the June and July monsoon, when in-person reliability drops for everybody on this road. Screen-shared Internal Assessment drafting is also genuinely better online than over a shoulder, because both people see the same cursor.

Online is the wrong choice for a younger child and should be refused rather than sold. A Primary Years Programme student or a Year 7 needs an adult in the room, and a thirteen-year-old who has gone quiet on a call has a second tab open. Where two siblings are far apart in age, the common and sensible answer is split-mode: in-person for the younger child, online for the older one who is doing timed papers and draft feedback. Most Kolshet Road families with two children end up there by the second term.

One rule holds for every mode. The slots go in a calendar and do not move weekly. Arrangements that get rescheduled by message every Sunday die around week eight, and with two children the collapse is faster because one child's cancellation becomes the other's too. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families keep for a full year is almost always one with a standing, defended slot in both children's weeks.

sections.heading: Can one tutor really be credible on both boards?
paragraphs: Sometimes, and the test is specific rather than general. A tutor who genuinely teaches both will talk about them differently: criteria and research questions for the Diploma Programme, components and command words for IGCSE, without blending the vocabulary. A tutor who is stretching will describe both in the same language and reach for syllabus as a catch-all. Ask them to explain how a Mathematics Internal Assessment is marked and then how a Cambridge Extended paper is structured. Two distinct answers mean two real bodies of experience. One fuzzy answer means you need two tutors.

IB Gram verifies identity before any profile is shortlisted, and checks board-specific teaching claims separately from academic qualifications, because a physics degree evidences subject knowledge and not having prepared a cohort for any particular examination. Tutors are asked which programmes, subjects, levels, codes and series they have taught, and for a contactable reference from a family or a school. Where a tutor claims both boards, both claims are checked, and the shortlist says which board the reference actually covers.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, publishes a success rate, or implies a working relationship with a named Thane school. On both boards the final assessment is external and criterion-referenced, so none of those are things an honest teacher can offer. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. There is no single best IB and IGCSE tutor in Kolshet Road either, because the right person for a Year 9 who has lost confidence is not the right person for a DP2 student finishing an Extended Essay.

The last part of verification is domestic and matters more with two children in the house. Lessons happen in a shared room with an adult or household member present somewhere in the flat, agreed on the phone call rather than raised later. Every visitor along this corridor is logged at the gate, so the tutor's name and number sit in the society record from the first lesson, which is a genuine safeguard. When two siblings are taught consecutively, agree who sits where during the other's session, because a bored younger sibling in the room is the commonest reason a good tutor loses a DP student's attention.
