sections.heading: Do Core and Extended mean the same as HL and SL?
paragraphs: No, and confusing them costs families real money. Core and Extended are tiers within one IGCSE subject: the same syllabus split into an accessible route and a fuller one, with the tier capping the grade available. Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) in the Diploma Programme are different courses with different content and different teaching time. A child moving from Extended to Standard Level has not stepped down a level; she has changed qualification.

The second confusion is between coursework and internal assessment. In Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel, non-examined components are marked in school and moderated by the board, and not every school enters its cohort for the coursework route at all. In the Diploma Programme every subject carries an Internal Assessment (IA) and there is no version of the course without one, plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) sitting outside the six subjects. A tutor who uses 'coursework' and 'IA' interchangeably does not know one of the two systems.

Third, the assessment grammar differs. IGCSE papers are marked against a published mark scheme, which rewards specific wording, method lines and stated accuracy. Middle Years Programme and Diploma work is assessed against criteria, which reward demonstrated skills described in level bands. The practical consequence is that an IGCSE student learns to produce what the scheme asks for, while an IB student learns to recognise which criterion a task is actually testing. Both are teachable. They are not the same lesson, and a tutor who knows only one of them teaches it in both places.

Finally the calendar. Cambridge runs a main series in May and June with a smaller one in October and November, and Edexcel adds a January window. The Diploma's May session is preceded by a January and February crunch of internal deadlines. In a household running both boards those two calendars collide in exactly one place: the December to February stretch, when a Year 11 is sitting mocks while a DP1 or DP2 student is finishing drafts. Plan that period in September, because planning it in December is just watching it happen.

sections.heading: Which subjects translate between the boards, and which do not?
paragraphs: Mathematics and the sciences translate reasonably well; the humanities and languages translate badly. An Extended IGCSE mathematician starting Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level will recognise most of the algebra and will be surprised by the modelling and the technology expectations. A Cambridge science student entering an IB science will recognise the content and will not recognise the investigation, which asks her to design something rather than follow a method printed on a sheet.

The humanities are where the gap bites hardest. An IGCSE History candidate has learned to answer source questions against a mark scheme. An IB History student has to produce a historical investigation with her own question, evaluate her own sources and write reflectively about method. The skills overlap; the task does not. English behaves similarly: a strong Cambridge English Language candidate who writes well in a directed task can struggle with unseen close reading and the comparative demands of a literature course until somebody teaches her what is now being rewarded.

Languages are the quietest problem of the three. Level placement between an IGCSE language and a Diploma Language B is routinely misjudged in both directions, because the IGCSE grade measures something different from the Diploma's level descriptors. A student can arrive with an excellent certificate and be placed where she coasts for two years, or where she drowns. Ask the school to justify the placement with evidence from actual written and spoken work rather than from the previous grade, and get a tutor's second opinion inside the first month rather than in the second year.

A note on structures. Component names, paper counts and what each one covers differ between the boards and change on each board's own revision cycle, so take them from the current syllabus or specification and from your school's coordinator rather than from any tutoring page. IB Gram arranges help across all IB and IGCSE subjects and the tutor in Lonavala you are introduced to should say plainly which board, which subject and which years they have taught, and where the edge of that experience sits.

sections.heading: One household, two boards, and the Mumbai map in between
paragraphs: The practical geography is that both children are usually taught from the same place, and it is rarely Lonavala itself. The tutor pools serving this town sit at Panvel, Kalyan and Kamothe, with Thane behind them, and the realistic weekly arrangement for most households is online teaching with in-person blocks in the school holidays. That is not a limitation of the platform. It is what a hill town on the expressway with boarding and weekend-home families actually supports week after week.

Panvel matters more than its size suggests, because the Mumbai–Pune Expressway meets the Sion-Panvel Highway there. A tutor coming from Panvel can chain two sessions, which is precisely what a two-child household needs and precisely why a Panvel-based tutor is more likely to sustain a fortnightly visit than somebody further in. Kamothe, beside Kharghar on the Harbour Line, became easier to reach after the Atal Setu opened. Kalyan, on the Central Line beyond Thane, supplies a large share of the mathematics and science teaching along this corridor.

Thane is the useful case study because it shows the mechanism inside one town. The place runs west to east from Thane station along Pokhran Road and Majiwada and out along Ghodbunder Road, and Ghodbunder sets everybody's schedule: about twenty minutes to Kasarvadavali off-peak and close to an hour once the evening builds. That single stretch is why Thane tutors keep to Thane and Mulund tutors cross over only occasionally. If an hour inside one suburb reshapes a tutor's working week, the ghat climb reshapes it altogether.

For a two-board household the implication is specific. Home tuition across this corner of Mumbai should be bought as one plan with two threads rather than as two separate hunts. One tutor from Panvel for a fortnightly in-person session covering both children on the same visit, where the subjects allow it. Online specialists for whatever that person cannot teach, chosen for having taught the board in question. And a block in each long holiday where the in-person work concentrates. Parents searching IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Lonavala are usually, quite correctly, looking for exactly this hybrid.

paragraphs: Ask, because many Mumbai schools do and the answer decides whether your two children are on one pathway or two. A school running Cambridge IGCSE to Year 11 and then the IB Diploma produces a predictable transition and usually some form of bridging. A school running IGCSE into A Level, or the IB from the Primary Years upwards, produces a different one. Families moving up here mid-stream often discover the mismatch only after enrolling.

The calendar to request in June is short and covers both children at once. Mock windows for each year group. Internal deadlines for any coursework or internal assessment. Entry and option deadlines, which land earlier than parents expect them to. The Mumbai school year runs June to April, so the predictable shape is first reports in August, mocks in December, drafts and submissions through January and February, and examinations from March onward. With both children's dates on a single sheet you can see the collision before it happens rather than during it.

Boarding complicates matters in a way worth planning for. If one child boards and the other is a day student, the household carries two calendars and two sets of permissions, and some residential schools restrict outside tutors during prep hours. Ask before booking anything. For weekend-home families, the child at a day school in Navi Mumbai or Thane is effectively a city student on weekdays, which means a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai near that campus may be easier to arrange than anybody local to this hill.

sections.heading: Home classes, online lessons and holiday blocks for two children
paragraphs: Home classes come first, and with two children they come first for a practical reason as well as a teaching one: a tutor already in the house can take one child and then the other on a single visit, which halves the travel cost of the whole arrangement. For a younger Cambridge candidate who needs supervision rather than expertise, that visit is the entire product. Where somebody suitable lives close enough, IB and IGCSE home tuition in Lonavala is the best value available in this town by a wide margin.

It usually is not available, and the reason is supply rather than willingness. This is a hill town on the expressway whose families are boarders and weekend-home households, so almost all sustained teaching runs online with occasional intensive in-person blocks. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Lonavala is chosen for having taught the specific board and level in question, which matters most for the older child, where the subject is harder and the pool of people who have really taught it is thinner.

Online with two children needs rules that single-child households can skip. Separate sessions, never a shared screen, because a Year 10 and a DP1 student have nothing to gain from each other's hour. One room, one device, one timetable on the wall, so nobody is negotiating at seven in the evening. Working photographed and sent before each lesson. And an adult in the house, which on a weekday in a weekend-home household may mean a grandparent or somebody who works there, briefed on the single rule that the phone stays in another room.

The holiday block is where a two-board household gains the most, because one tutor travelling up for three days can serve both children. Use it for what weekly sessions cannot do: a coursework folder for the younger child, an internal assessment draft for the older one, a full timed paper each, marked the same day. Book Diwali in September. sections.heading: How do you check a tutor who claims both boards?
paragraphs: Ask for the specifics of each board separately and listen for the gap. Which Cambridge syllabus number or Edexcel specification code did you last teach, and in which year? Which IB programme and level, and have you supervised an internal assessment? Somebody genuinely experienced in both answers with different levels of detail for each and will tell you which is their stronger side. A tutor who answers both with equal confidence and equal vagueness has taught neither recently.

The platform checks are the same for everybody and worth stating. Government photo identification seen rather than described. Degree certificates seen. Claimed experience matched to a named school and a named syllabus with the years stated. References taken from previous families where they exist. A board a tutor has not taught is recorded as untested rather than quietly folded into a general claim, which matters disproportionately on a page like this one, where claiming both boards is the easiest way to look more useful than you are.

Your own test takes one marked script per child. Ask each candidate to mark a page in front of you against the right instrument: the published mark scheme for the IGCSE child and the published criteria for the IB child. Watch whether they reach for the correct one in each case, because reaching for a mark scheme on a criterion-assessed task is the giveaway. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, since no honest teacher can offer one, and a tutor offering it for two children across two boards is reciting a script.

Families often arrive here having searched best IB and IGCSE tutor in Lonavala, which returns directory pages rather than a judgement. A better use of the same ten minutes: send both candidates the same two scripts and ask what they would do in the first fortnight for each child. One replies with subject names. The other replies with mechanisms, and will quite possibly say that one of the two children needs a different person. That honesty is the signal worth hiring, wherever the tutor happens to live.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma Programme transition in Lonavala, step by step
paragraphs: The transition fails in the first term of DP1 rather than at the end of Year 11, and it fails in four predictable places: level choice, writing volume, the internal assessment, and independent time management. A strong set of IGCSE grades is a good predictor of content readiness and a poor predictor of all four. This is the most useful thing a family running both boards can plan for, and the window to do the planning in is the April to June gap between the two courses.

Level choice first. Higher Level is not Extended with extra homework; it is a different quantity of content taught at a different pace, and three of them run alongside Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and three Standard Level subjects. The honest test is not the IGCSE grade but whether the child reads the subject voluntarily. A student who earned an excellent Extended mathematics result by drilling past papers may dislike Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, where proof and derivation carry more weight than familiar question types do.

Writing volume second. IGCSE answers are short, scheme-shaped and numerous. Diploma work asks for sustained argument: an Extended Essay running to thousands of words, Theory of Knowledge essays, internal assessments with discussion sections that have to reach a conclusion. A student who has never written more than a page without a template finds this genuinely hard, and the fix is mechanical and unglamorous. One piece of extended writing a fortnight through the April to June gap and the first term, read and marked by somebody who will say exactly where the argument stops being an argument.

Third and fourth, the internal assessment and the diary. IB internal assessments are designed by the student, which is a new skill rather than a harder version of coursework, and the research question is where most of the marks are won or lost. And nobody checks the Diploma timetable on your behalf: a Year 11 student has a school-set deadline for everything, while a DP1 student has dates spread across eighteen months. A tutor's job in that first term is as much about a calendar on the wall as about content, which is why IB and IGCSE home tuition in Lonavala for a transition year is bought as project management as well as teaching.

sections.heading: What one term of home tuition changes across two boards in Mumbai

That is the only honest four-week deliverable and it applies equally to a Year 10 Cambridge candidate and a DP1 student, though it surfaces differently: the younger one starts writing method lines, the older one starts noticing which criterion a task is testing. Grades have not moved and will not have moved yet.

At one term, the younger child's gains are usually mechanical and visible while the older child's are structural and harder to see. A Year 10 student fixes reading errors, writes working and attempts the last question, which reads as a few marks a paper. A DP1 student produces an internal assessment draft with a defensible research question and a first piece of extended writing that holds together. The second looks like less and is worth more, and a parent comparing the two children on a grade sheet will reach exactly the wrong conclusion.

At one examination cycle grades move for some students and not for others, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades on either board. No tutor working through the platform may suggest otherwise. What a careful arrangement removes is the avoidable loss, and it differs between the two children: method marks and timing for the IGCSE candidate, a thin internal assessment and a late Extended Essay for the Diploma student. Those are the honest arguments for home tuition across this part of Mumbai, and they are enough on their own.

If one of the two arrangements is not working, change that one and leave the other alone. Households tend to treat tutoring as a single decision and either persevere with both or abandon both, when the usual truth is that one match is good and one is not. Say at four sessions which child is not progressing and why, in symptoms rather than verdicts. A replacement for one child is arranged without touching the other's timetable, and the incoming tutor is briefed on what failed so the second attempt is genuinely different.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach my Year 10 Cambridge child and my DP1 child at home?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, under narrow conditions, and you should test them rather than assume. The subjects need to be adjacent, the year gap small, and the sessions separate with separate notes. Mathematics for an Extended candidate and a Standard Level Diploma student is plausible. Cambridge Biology and Higher Level Biology is already a stretch, and English across Year 9 and an Extended Essay is not one person's work. Where it does fit, IB and IGCSE home tuition in Lonavala arranged as one visit covering both children is the cheapest workable plan in this town, because the travel is shared.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel up for one visit and see both children?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the arrangement most likely to survive the term, because one journey justifies two sessions. A tutor from Panvel or Kalyan who would never sustain a weekly climb for a single ninety-minute lesson will often commit to a fortnightly visit covering two children back to back. Agree the running order, the gap between sessions and what happens on a wet evening before the first visit. Put the fallback in writing: either the pair of sessions moves online that day, or they shift to the following weekend.

faqs.question: My daughter has excellent IGCSE grades. Why is DP1 going badly?
faqs.answer: Because IGCSE grades predict content readiness and almost nothing else that the Diploma demands. The four usual causes are a Higher Level chosen on results rather than appetite, extended writing she has never had to do, an internal assessment she is expected to design rather than complete, and eighteen months of deadlines nobody checks weekly. Diagnose which of the four it is before buying any teaching. A tutor who starts by reviewing her subject choices and her calendar rather than her content knowledge is reading the situation correctly.

faqs.question: Is Extended the same as Higher Level?
faqs.answer: No, and the two words sit at different layers of the system. Extended is a tier inside one IGCSE subject, covering more of the same syllabus and lifting the grade ceiling. Higher Level is a separate Diploma course with more content, more teaching time and more demanding assessment than its Standard Level counterpart. A student can do Extended IGCSE Mathematics and then sensibly take Standard Level in the Diploma without that being a step down. Ask the school's coordinator to explain the placement in terms of the course, not the previous grade.

faqs.question: We are moving to Lonavala mid-year from a Cambridge school. What breaks?
faqs.answer: Three things, usually. The subject set, because block timetables rarely match between schools and something has to be dropped or picked up late. Any non-examined component already underway, which may not transfer and may need restarting under the new school's arrangements. And the entry, since the receiving school handles the examination entry and its deadlines may already have passed. Ask the new school's examinations officer those three questions in writing before the first day, and get a tutor on the subject that was picked up late.

faqs.question: Which board should we choose if we genuinely have the option?
faqs.answer: Choose on the child, not the reputation. A student who likes clear tasks, defined mark schemes and frequent short assessments usually does better through IGCSE and then A Level. A student who reads widely, writes at length and tolerates ambiguity usually does better in the Diploma. Consider also the household: the Diploma's internal assessments and Extended Essay need adult attention over eighteen months, which a weekend-home family on this hill should be honest about. Neither route is harder in general, and both are harder for the wrong child.

faqs.question: Do coursework and internal assessment need the same kind of help?
faqs.answer: No, and the difference matters for who you hire. Coursework is set by the school within a board's framework, so the help needed is scope, structure and keeping to the deadline. An internal assessment is designed by the student, so the help needed starts a layer earlier, at the research question, and a tutor who begins with structure has already skipped the part where the marks are decided. In both cases the work must be the student's own, and the school's authenticity rules define exactly what support is permitted.

faqs.question: How do we handle December when one child has mocks and the other has drafts?
faqs.answer: Plan it in September and protect different days for each child. The mock candidate needs timed papers and marking, which is best done at weekends when a parent can invigilate. The Diploma student needs long uninterrupted stretches for drafting, which is best done on weekday evenings or in the holiday itself. Trying to serve both on the same two evenings is how families lose both. Write the two sets of dates on one sheet in September and decide then which child gets the Diwali block, because they cannot both have it.

faqs.question: Does online work for both children, or only the older one?
faqs.answer: It works better for the older one, reliably. A Diploma student can read, annotate and work alone for an hour, which is what online teaching requires. A Year 9 or Year 10 student often cannot, so for the younger child home classes with somebody present are worth paying more for. The common compromise in this town is an online specialist for the older child and a local tutor or a supervising parent for the younger one, with both brought together into the same holiday block when a tutor travels up.

A single tutor seeing both children in one trip costs less per hour than two separate weekly arrangements, which is the main reason IB and IGCSE home tuition in Lonavala is worth planning as one household decision. faqs.question: One tutor is working and the other is not. Do we change both?
faqs.answer: Change only the one that is not working, and say precisely what is wrong. Households often treat tutoring as a single verdict and either keep both arrangements out of inertia or cancel both out of frustration, when the usual position is that one match is good. Describe symptoms rather than conclusions: no written notes, nothing done between sessions, silence for the whole hour. A replacement for one child is arranged without disturbing the other child's timetable, and the new tutor is briefed on what failed the first time.

sections.heading: What changes when a child moves from Year 11 into the Diploma Programme?
paragraphs: Almost everything about how work is produced and almost nothing about the content. The Diploma Programme (DP) asks a student to carry several long pieces of work over two years while ordinary teaching continues: an Internal Assessment (IA) in each subject, the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK), and the creativity, activity and service component. None of those is a homework task with a weekend deadline. They are managed projects, and the skill they demand is planning, not recall. A student who coped by revising hard in the final fortnight has no transferable strategy for any of it.

The International Baccalaureate (IB) also changes what counts as a good answer. Diploma assessment rewards reasoning that is visible on the page, evaluation that weighs something against something else, and command terms answered as asked. A student arriving from a board where a correct final answer carried most of the credit has to be retrained to show the thinking, and that retraining takes about a term. It is the single most common reason a strong Year 11 student has a shaky DP1 first report, and it is entirely fixable if somebody names it early.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) route into the Diploma Programme has the opposite problem. An MYP student already understands criterion-marked work and inquiry-led tasks, but may be unused to the sheer volume of content in Higher Level subjects. For both routes the Higher Level and Standard Level decision is the structural one to get right, because Higher Level is a different course rather than a harder version, and it is chosen before anybody has seen how the student copes with DP work. Confirm current structure with your school's Diploma coordinator and the live subject guide rather than any web page.

This page leads on the International Baccalaureate side, because that is where the crossing hurts. Families wanting Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel depth for Years 9 to 11 have their own pages on this site, and the Primary Years Programme (PYP) and MYP stages are covered separately too. If your household spans both, say so at the enquiry and we will match each child to a tutor who works at that stage rather than one who claims the full range.

sections.heading: Subject choice, Higher Level and the assessments that follow
paragraphs: The Diploma Programme makes a student choose across six subject groups, with some taken at Higher Level and some at Standard Level, and the decision is made in the spring before DP1 starts on the basis of very little evidence. The mistakes we see are consistent. A student takes Higher Level mathematics because a university page mentioned it and discovers the course assumes a fluency she never built. A student takes a science at Higher Level without realising the Internal Assessment will require independent experimental design. A student drops the second language she was good at in favour of one she finds interesting and loses a reliable source of marks.

Each subject then carries its own internally assessed component, and these are where most of our DP enquiries from Lower Parel actually originate. In the sciences the assessment demands a research question narrow enough to produce defensible data, which is where weak submissions die rather than in the write-up. In mathematics the exploration must contain real mathematics done by the student, not a well-presented account of a topic. In language and literature the marks sit in how closely the response reads the text in front of it. In individuals and societies the command terms do the dividing.

Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are the two pieces families underestimate hardest, and both reward the same thing: a narrow, answerable question and reasoning you can follow. A student who chooses an Extended Essay topic because it sounds impressive will spend months discovering it cannot be answered in the length available. A tutor is most useful here before the question is fixed, which is months earlier than most parents think to ask. We arrange all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Lower Parel at that stage specifically, and the earlier request is always the cheaper one.

Where a household spans two boards, the subject conversation differs per child and should not be merged. A Year 10 student is choosing between content routes within a subject; a DP1 student is managing assessment deadlines across six. Giving both children the same tutor on the logic that the subject name matches produces a tutor pulled between two assessment vocabularies. The wider panel covers all IB and IGCSE subjects and the tutor in Lower Parel each child meets should be the one who works at that child's stage.

paragraphs: Families here send children to a small group of schools, and when two children sit different boards you are managing two assessment rhythms in one flat. The two rhythms do not align, which is the practical headache. The International Baccalaureate pressure point for a DP1 student falls in the middle of the year, when Internal Assessment drafts, Extended Essay progress checks and Theory of Knowledge work converge inside a few weeks. A Year 10 sibling's pressure point falls after the first substantial internal assessments and again at mocks. So the household has roughly three separate crunch periods rather than one, and the mistake is planning tutoring around whichever child shouted most recently.

The fix is dull and effective: ask each school for its own assessment calendar at the start of the year and put both on one sheet. Once you can see the overlaps you can decide where the money goes. A fortnight where a DP1 Internal Assessment draft lands at the same time as a Year 9 unit test is a fortnight to add a session for one child and pause the other, not a fortnight to spread everyone thinner. Tutors cannot see that sheet unless you show it to them, and most never ask.

The arrangement that survives is one where the tutor works through the assignment the school has already set, which also gives you something real to judge progress against.

sections.heading: Should home tuition in Mumbai be shared between two children?
paragraphs: Only when the children are at the same programme stage in the same subject, which in a two-board household is almost never the case. The temptation is obvious and the failure is reliable: a DP1 student and a Year 9 student cannot be taught together even in mathematics, because one is being trained to show evaluative reasoning for an externally moderated component and the other is being taught content. The tutor ends up teaching the midpoint and both children leave short. Two siblings in the same DP year and the same subject can share, with the honest caveat that one of them will be ahead.

Where sharing does work is sharing a tutor's evening rather than a session. One tutor, one visit, two consecutive forty-five or sixty-minute blocks, one child then the other. The tutor's travel is paid once, the building clears her once, and the arrangement is cheap enough for her to keep through the monsoon. This is the single most useful thing a two-child household in a Lower Parel tower can ask for, and it is also why we want the building name and the wing before we shortlist anyone.

Online earns its place differently for each child. For a DP1 student an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Lower Parel is genuinely strong for Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge support, which is mostly draft reading and hard questions, and for scarce Higher Level subjects where no specialist lives near the island. For a younger sibling it is weaker, because the thing that keeps a Year 9 student working is often a person in the room. So the sensible household pattern is frequently in-person for the younger child and hybrid for the older one, which is the reverse of what most parents assume.

Hybrid is where our longer two-child arrangements in South Mumbai settle. One in-person visit a week covering both children in sequence, plus an online review session for whichever child has a deadline that fortnight. It cuts travel exposure, which in this district is the main cause of a tutor quietly becoming unreliable, and it gives you a way to move intensity between children without renegotiating the whole timetable. sections.heading: Can one tutor be checked for both boards?
paragraphs: Yes, and the check has to be done separately for each, which is precisely why dual claims deserve scrutiny. We verify identity against a government photo document and see the qualification rather than take it on trust. Then we record stage-specific evidence: which programmes and which years, which subjects, at which level, and whether the person has supervised Internal Assessment work or marked criterion-based tasks in practice. A tutor with real Diploma Programme supervision history and a tutor who has taught Years 9 to 11 for a decade are both credible, and they are different hires for different children.

The test we actually run is a marking test. We hand over anonymised student work, usually a weak Internal Assessment introduction, and ask what the tutor would say to that student tonight. A strong answer names the criterion, identifies the one change that moves the level, and gives the student an action. A weak answer explains the topic again. Subject knowledge is necessary and plentiful. Knowing where a level is lost is the scarce thing, and it is what separates a usable IB and IGCSE private tutor in Lower Parel from a well-qualified stranger.

Your own checks are the ones that catch what we cannot. Ask which programme stage and which year the tutor most recently taught, and be sceptical if the answer spans everything from Year 7 to DP2. Ask what the first session will look like and listen for diagnosis rather than teaching. Ask what you will get in writing at four weeks. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, quotes a predicted score, or hints at a relationship with your child's school, because those are selling behaviours.

After the match, the signals that matter are mundane and reach us only if you send them. Arrival drifting later each week, usually because the previous slot is too far away. Sessions becoming homework supervision, which means the plan has run out. A tutor who talks to you more than to the student. One child's slot quietly absorbing the other's time. We ask for a four-week note from you as well as from the tutor for exactly this reason, and in a two-child household we ask about each child separately.

sections.heading: The Year 11 to DP1 bridge nobody plans for in Lower Parel
paragraphs: The crossing from a Year 11 examination year into DP1 is the most under-prepared transition we see in this district, and the reason is a timing accident. Year 11 ends with examinations, the family exhales, the summer passes, and DP1 starts with subject choices already locked and three long-horizon components quietly beginning. By the time the first report arrives the student has been producing work for a term under rules nobody explained to her. The content is rarely the problem. The problem is that the previous two years rewarded a different skill and nobody flagged the switch.

What specifically changes is worth spelling out. Credit moves from the final answer to the visible reasoning. Evaluation becomes a scored behaviour rather than a stylistic flourish, which means weighing one thing against another and saying so explicitly. Deadlines stop being weekly and become monthly, which punishes a student with no planning habit. And for the first time the student is expected to design something, whether an experiment, an exploration or an essay question, instead of completing something designed for her. Each of those is teachable in about six weeks if it is named.

This is where the district's own rhythm actually helps, for once. Lower Parel is offices by day and towers by night: the mills became Kamala Mills and the Phoenix complex, the residential towers grew around their edges, and parents come up the lift between half past six and half past seven. Tutoring here is therefore a 7pm business, which means the evening sessions land after school and after whatever the student has already attempted alone. For bridge work that sequencing is genuinely useful, because the tutor is reacting to a real attempt rather than pre-teaching tomorrow's lesson.

The practical plan for a bridge engagement is short and specific. Six to eight weeks of home tuition, one session a week, built around the student's first real DP task rather than around the syllabus. Week one, read a marked piece of her own work and name what the markers wanted. Weeks two to four, rebuild one piece to criterion standard with the student doing the writing. Weeks five to eight, apply the same method to an Internal Assessment plan or an Extended Essay question. Towers like Lodha World Towers and Indiabulls Blu hold enough DP families that such a tutor is often already in your building on some evening of the week.

sections.heading: What four weeks of home classes should show you
paragraphs: Four weeks of home classes tells you about the match and nothing reliable about the grade, so judge it on three observable things. The tutor should be able to name, without notes, the specific criterion or error type your child repeatedly loses marks on. Your child should be able to explain one thing out loud that she could not explain in week one, whether a method or what an assessment criterion is asking for. And the written work coming home should look different: more attempts, more visible reasoning, including reasoning that turns out wrong. If none of the three has happened, the match is wrong.

By one term, around twelve to fourteen sessions, school feedback starts to move and it moves unevenly. For a Diploma Programme student the first visible change is usually in draft feedback: fewer structural comments, more content ones, which is exactly the right direction. Reported grades and criterion levels lag real understanding by weeks, so the most common honest mid-term picture is clearly better work alongside a barely moved number. In a two-child household expect the two children to progress at different speeds and resist reading one against the other.

Across a full cycle the outcomes vary genuinely, and we will not pretend otherwise. Some students move a long way. Others arrive at their final assessments steadier, having stopped the avoidable losses, with a result close to what was always likely, which is worth real money even when the number is unchanged. No IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai can reach a Higher Level choice made before anyone had evidence, a subject taken for the wrong reason, or a hard year at home. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, publishes no success rates, and will not predict a score for your child.

What we do commit to is that you will not be guessing. A written diagnostic after session one and a written review at four weeks, per child, in plain language. If a fit is wrong, message us and we shortlist again with no notice period and no argument. Most replacements have dull causes: a timetable clash nobody could solve, a style mismatch, a tutor stronger in an adjacent subject than the one you needed. Catching that in week four costs a month. Catching it in month four can cost a DP1 year, which is the one loss that does not recover.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Lower Parel, Mumbai

For the household: the evening slots you genuinely have, and your building name with the wing. That last detail is not administrative trivia in a tower district; it determines whether a tutor is already clearing your gate on some evening of the week, which in turn determines how soon you can start and how long the arrangement lasts.

The first visit for each child is a diagnostic, not a lesson, and it should feel slightly anticlimactic. For a Diploma Programme student the tutor reads a recent marked piece and any Internal Assessment draft, then asks the student to talk through one problem and probes where understanding actually stops. For a younger sibling it is a cold attempt at a past question and a line-by-line read of a marked test. faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both my children if they are on different boards?
faqs.answer: Sometimes in mathematics or the sciences, rarely elsewhere, and never in the same session. The reasoning in a Diploma Programme Internal Assessment and the reasoning in a Year 10 unit test are assessed against different things, so a tutor teaching both children at once ends up teaching neither properly. What works well is one tutor, one visit, two consecutive blocks with one child then the other. If the subjects are languages or humanities, assume you need two different people, because the assessment vocabulary does not transfer the way subject content does.

faqs.question: How does a tutor get a gate pass for two sessions in one evening?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once as a recurring visitor and specify the full window, not a single hour. Towers here run visitor clearance at the desk, so a tutor arriving unregistered at 7pm loses time from a paid hour, and a tutor leaving and re-entering between two children's slots can lose it twice. One call to building management in week one with the name, the day and the whole time block usually settles it. Then send the tutor the gate number, the wing and the lift bank so the first visit does not start at the desk.

faqs.question: My son starts DP1 next year. When should home tuition begin?
faqs.answer: Before the first report, not after it. The crossing from Year 11 into the Diploma Programme changes how work is produced rather than what is covered: credit moves to visible reasoning, evaluation becomes a scored behaviour, deadlines become monthly, and the student is expected to design tasks rather than complete them. None of that is announced. A six to eight week engagement in the first term, built around his own first marked DP task, costs far less than discovering the gap in DP2 when the Internal Assessments are already written.

faqs.question: Which child should we prioritise if we can only afford one tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually the one with long-horizon work in progress, which normally means the Diploma Programme student. A single bad test in Year 9 is recoverable with effort; a term of Internal Assessment and Extended Essay drift in DP1 is not, because the components are produced once and carried forward. That is an uncomfortable answer in a household where the younger child is the one complaining. The compromise that works is a full arrangement for the urgent child and a short diagnostic plus a study plan for the other, revisited at the end of the term.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for the older child or the younger one?
faqs.answer: Usually the older one, which surprises most parents. Online is genuinely strong for Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge support, which is mostly draft reading and hard questions, and for scarce Higher Level subjects where no specialist lives near the island. It is weaker for a Year 9 or Year 10 student, because physical presence is often what keeps that student present and working. So the common household pattern is in-person for the younger child and hybrid for the older one, rather than the other way round.

faqs.question: What if one tutor is working and the other is not?
faqs.answer: Replace the one that is not, immediately, and keep the one that is. There is no package and no notice period, so the two arrangements are independent. We ask for one concrete detail rather than a general complaint, because the detail changes the next shortlist: consistent lateness points us towards tutors already holding a slot in your building, and sessions sliding into homework supervision points us towards someone with more assessment supervision behind them. Judge each tutor against the four-week test for that child, not against the sibling's tutor.

faqs.question: Do you cover Parel, Worli and Prabhadevi for both children?
faqs.answer: Yes, those three plus Lower Parel are a single matching cluster and the same pool serves every stage. Parel sits immediately east and pairs easily for consecutive slots. Worli runs west towards the sea face, where travel time depends on Annie Besant Road. Prabhadevi runs north and behaves structurally like Lower Parel: towers, one gate, a busy lift around eight. Dadar, Mahalaxmi and Byculla come into range street by street. What we will not do is bring a tutor down from the suburbs for a weekday evening slot.

faqs.question: How do we fit two children into the evening slots this building allows?
faqs.answer: Treat the evening as inventory and spend it deliberately. This district runs on office hours, so flats become usable around seven and the practical blocks are roughly seven and half past eight. Two children taught in person during the week consumes most of that. The efficient pattern is one tutor visiting once and teaching both in sequence, or one child in person and one online on a different evening. Decide which before you start, because renegotiating a tutor's slot in month two is how arrangements here quietly collapse.

faqs.question: Our children are at JBCN International School, Parel. Does that help?
faqs.answer: It helps a little, and the assessment calendar helps far more. We are not affiliated with JBCN International School, Parel, Aditya Birla World Academy or any other school; we name them as local context only. A school running both pathways may give your two children either one shared calendar or two separate ones, and you need to know which. Ask for each child's assessment calendar at the start of the year, put both on one sheet, and hand it to the tutors in week one. That sheet shapes the term more than school familiarity does.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level maths a mistake if my child found Year 11 maths hard?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the decision deserves evidence rather than ambition. Higher Level is a different course, not a harder version of Standard Level, and it assumes a fluency that has to already exist. A tutor can give you useful evidence within three sessions by testing whether your child can hold a multi-step method without prompting and whether she can explain why a method works. Take that evidence to the Diploma coordinator before the choice locks. Changing level after DP1 has started is possible at some schools and disruptive at all of them.

faqs.question: What should a four-week review actually contain?
faqs.answer: Two or three paragraphs per child in plain language, naming the specific criterion or error type being targeted, what has changed, and what the next month will cover. It should not be a list of topics taught, because that tells you nothing about whether anything landed. Our tutors send theirs and we ask you for a short note too, covering arrival times, whether your child takes out her own work unprompted, and whether sessions are teaching or supervising. In a two-child household we ask about each child separately, because averaging the two hides the problem.

faqs.question: Can we start in the middle of a term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and mid-term is often the better moment because there is real marked work to diagnose from. Send the most recent marked piece per child and two evening windows, and a shortlist usually comes back within a couple of working days. The first visit can often be scheduled the same week, and faster if a panel tutor already teaches in your tower. The only genuine constraint in this district is slot availability: the 7pm blocks fill from October onwards, so a mid-term start sometimes means taking the later block for a few weeks.

sections.heading: How does weekly IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mahalaxmi get set up?
paragraphs: The setup takes about a week and three decisions. First the subject and the weekly hours, then the fixed slot, then the tutor. Most families get this order wrong and pick the tutor first, which is why arrangements collapse in week five when a 6pm Wednesday turns out to clash with a swimming lesson that nobody mentioned.

We start with the timetable rather than the teaching. Tell us which two or three evenings are genuinely free after school transport, food and whatever else already occupies the week. In the towers along this corridor the realistic window is between half past six and half past eight on weekdays, with Saturday mornings open for longer work. Once that window is fixed we look only at tutors who can hold it every week until the end of term, which immediately removes a third of the pool and saves everybody three wasted conversations.

Then comes the teaching question. We ask what the school is reporting, what the last marked paper looked like, and whether the problem is content, technique or work rate. Those three need different tutors. A content gap wants someone who will reteach a topic sequence properly. A technique problem wants someone who marks like an examiner. A work-rate problem wants someone who sets short, checkable tasks and follows up, and who is willing to be slightly unpopular about it in week two. Most requests for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mahalaxmi turn out to be the third kind rather than the first, which is the opposite of what parents across Mumbai expect when they write to us.

Only after that do you see profiles. You get two or three, each with the board and syllabus they work from, the years they teach, the area they travel from, and the slot they are offering. You speak to them directly. Nothing is confirmed, and no fee is paid, until you have had that call. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school or residential society named anywhere on this page.

sections.heading: Two boards, one household: planning MYP, DP and IGCSE years together
paragraphs: Plenty of families around Mahalaxmi run both boards at once, usually because one child started in an International Baccalaureate (IB) continuum school and a sibling moved to a Cambridge pathway, or because the school itself offers the International General Certificate of Secondary Education through to Years 10 and 11 and the IB Diploma Programme (DP) after that. The arrangements those two children need are not the same, and treating them as one booking is where the money gets wasted.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) years reward a steady, low-intensity arrangement. One session a week, aimed at writing quality and at the criteria the school is marking against, does more than three sessions of content cramming. In the IGCSE years the shape changes: Years 9 to 11 run on a syllabus with external papers at the end, so the arrangement becomes content coverage first and past papers later, and the hours should rise in the final two terms rather than staying flat.

Diploma Programme years are the most demanding to schedule because the deadlines are internal as well as external. A DP1 student has Internal Assessment (IA) work beginning in several subjects at once, and a DP2 student carries the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) alongside Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) papers. Home tuition here is often two subjects on two evenings with a short third slot in the weeks a draft is due. Do not take a component weighting or a submission deadline from any tutor or any website, including this one. Those come from the current subject guide and from your school's Diploma coordinator, and both change.

What a good tutor does across both boards is stop treating the syllabus as a reading list. A home tutor working with an MYP student on a science investigation and an IGCSE sibling on Paper 4 structured questions is doing two different jobs in the same flat, and the planning should show it. If you want one tutor for both children, ask them to describe those two jobs separately before you agree. The answer tells you whether you are buying teaching or a convenient visit.

sections.heading: How many hours a week does each subject actually need?
paragraphs: For most subjects, one ninety-minute session a week moves a grade over a term, provided the student does the work in between. Two sessions a week are justified in three cases: an HL subject in the Diploma Programme, a subject where the student is two topics behind the class, or the eight weeks before a paper. Beyond two sessions a week you are usually buying supervision rather than teaching, and a student with four tutored hours and no independent study time gets worse, not better.

Mathematics and the sciences absorb hours differently. In Mathematics the work between sessions is the lesson; a tutor who uses the full slot teaching and sets nothing to attempt alone has given your child a demonstration rather than practice. In Physics and Chemistry the practical and data-handling work needs its own time, because designing a fair test and handling uncertainty are separate skills from solving the numerical questions, and they are where capable students quietly lose marks. In the Diploma Programme, Internal Assessment work needs blocks rather than slices: an hour on a draft achieves very little, and ninety minutes with the criteria open achieves a lot.

Language and humanities subjects run on a different rhythm. English, Economics and History are improved by frequent short pieces of writing that somebody actually marks, not by longer lessons. The most effective arrangement we see in these subjects is a weekly session where the previous week's timed piece is marked line by line in front of the student, followed by one new piece set with a visible clock. That is unglamorous and it works. Subject choice across both boards also matters for scheduling: a student taking two essay subjects cannot have both tutored on consecutive evenings or nothing gets written in between.

Our roster covers all IB and IGCSE subjects and the tutor in Mahalaxmi matched for your child should be honest about hours. If a tutor recommends three sessions a week in October for a Year 10 student who has not yet sat a mock, ask what the third session will do that the first two cannot. A tutor who cannot answer that is pricing their calendar rather than planning your child's term.

sections.heading: Scheduling a Mahalaxmi tutor across Tardeo, Worli and Byculla
paragraphs: IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mahalaxmi lives or dies on the tutor's own travel pattern, so it is worth understanding where they are before and after your slot. Tutors serving the Mahalaxmi–Haji Ali corridor typically hold two or three evening slots a night and arrange them geographically: Tardeo then Mahalaxmi, or Mahalaxmi then Worli. If your slot is the middle one in that chain it is the most stable, because the tutor is already nearby. If it is the first, a delayed finish somewhere else pushes your start time.

The island is short on distance and long on time. The run between Worli and Colaba is only about eight kilometres and can still take most of an hour once the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals back up after six. That is why tutors here are matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs, and why a tutor who offers to come from Andheri every Tuesday for a term should be politely declined. The arrangement will hold until the first week of heavy rain.

Of the three neighbouring areas, Tardeo gives the most schedule flexibility, Byculla the most weather reliability, and Worli the fastest off-peak run with the least predictable peak. Mahalaxmi station on the Western Line matters more than parents expect, because a meaningful share of tutors travel by train from Grant Road, Mumbai Central and Churchgate and then walk or take a short ride. Those tutors are unaffected by road jams and affected instead by train disruption, which fails differently and less often.

Set two things in writing in week one and the rest of the term runs itself. First, a standing fifteen-minute grace window, so a tutor stuck at a signal is not improvising an apology every fortnight. Second, a rule for genuine non-arrival: the session moves online the same evening or is made up on the weekend, agreed in advance rather than negotiated in the moment. Families along this corridor who set those two rules in June lose almost no sessions to the monsoon. Families who do not lose three or four and spend the rest of the term mildly annoyed.

sections.heading: Term dates, mock weeks and the Mumbai months that need extra hours
paragraphs: The school year around Mahalaxmi runs June to April, and the hours a tutoring arrangement needs are not flat across it. Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo and Bombay International School at Babulnath take much of the IGCSE and IB cohort here, with Activity High School on Peddar Road and the Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort taking a good share of the rest. Their calendars are broadly aligned, which means the pressure weeks for this whole corridor arrive together.

June to August is the cheap time to start and almost nobody does. The syllabus is open, the student is not under deadline pressure, and a content gap from last year can be rebuilt without competing with a test. September and October bring the first internal assessments and the first honest reports. Late November is the first real crunch, when mock weeks and Diploma Programme draft deadlines overlap, and every tutor on the island is already booked. January is the second, with final mocks and submission dates, followed by February and March when the external series begins.

A sensible arrangement anticipates this. Keep the baseline at one session a week from June, add a second in the fortnight before mocks rather than permanently, and plan the exam-term push in December rather than in February when nothing is available. Families in Mumbai, Maharashtra who try to buy extra hours in late January find that the good tutors have no capacity and the available ones are available for a reason.

Naming these schools is local context only. IB Gram is not affiliated with Aditya Birla World Academy, Bombay International School or any other school mentioned, and we do not guarantee grades. A tutor who claims knowledge of a particular school's internal marking should be asked to explain exactly what they mean, because the usual honest answer is that they have taught several students from there and recognise the house style of feedback, which is useful and much less dramatic than it sounds.

sections.heading: Home classes every week, with online as the continuity plan
paragraphs: IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mahalaxmi leads over every other format for a reason that is mostly architectural. Mahalaxmi is tower territory, and a flat in Raheja Vivarea, Lodha Bellissimo or Piramal Aranya is usually a high-floor apartment with a study room that closes. The mill-land redevelopment produced exactly this: homes designed with a work space, which means a home tutor walks into a room already suited to two hours of concentration instead of competing with a television.

Online is not the budget alternative. It is the continuity mechanism that keeps a term-long arrangement intact. A tutor travelling for a week, a flooded road in July, a child home with fever but well enough to work, a family trip where two sessions would otherwise be lost: in all four cases a video session keeps the thread rather than restarting it in a fortnight. An arrangement with an agreed online fallback typically delivers four to six more sessions across a term than one without, and those are the sessions that produce the change.

Hybrid by design suits Diploma Programme students particularly well. The weekly home session carries the teaching and the diagnosis; a shorter midweek online slot carries the marking and the correction of a draft or a timed piece. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mahalaxmi can do the second job efficiently, because marking a document together on a shared screen is often better than marking it on paper across a table. What online cannot do is notice the three distractions a tutor in the room removes without mentioning them.

Centre-based coaching is the third option and the one we rarely recommend for this corridor. The travel it adds in the evening peak cancels the cost advantage, group pace cannot serve a student who is two topics behind, and a child who has a study room at home gains nothing by sitting in a classroom at eight at night. If you want a group setting for motivation reasons, that is a legitimate choice, but make it for that reason rather than for the fee.

sections.heading: Who is in your flat every Tuesday, and how was that person checked?
paragraphs: A weekly arrangement means a named adult enters your home around thirty times a term, so verification matters more here than on any one-off booking. Every tutor listed has their identity confirmed against a government photograph document, their subject qualification checked at degree level, and their board experience tested in conversation rather than taken from a resume. We also confirm the areas they can realistically serve on a weekday evening, which is why the Mahalaxmi shortlist is short.

The identity check and your society's visitor process should line up. Give the society office the tutor's name and identity number once, with the day and the time, and ask for a standing weekly entry authorised from your flat. Raheja Vivarea, Lodha Bellissimo and Piramal Aranya each run their own version of gate registration, app-based in some towers and register-based in others. Doing this in week one removes a lobby phone call from every single session and is the single highest-return five minutes of admin in the whole arrangement.

Then there is the check that only a parent can make, and it happens in month two rather than week one. Is the tutor arriving prepared, with last week's work marked? Does your child's description of the session match the tutor's written note? Is the plan being adjusted, or is the same worksheet format reappearing in a different colour? A tutor who is competent in the first session and coasting by the eighth is more common across Mumbai than an incompetent one, and only you are positioned to see it.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, a guaranteed number of marks, or a promise about a specific school's results. The examination boards award grades and the student earns them. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and publishes no success rates, and a parent searching for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mahalaxmi should treat confident numerical promises as the clearest available signal to keep looking.

sections.heading: What does the hourly rate include, and what does it not?
paragraphs: The rate for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mahalaxmi covers the teaching hour, the preparation behind it and the tutor's travel to your building. It does not usually cover marking long pieces outside the session, writing detailed reports, attending school meetings, producing custom question banks, or holding extra slots at short notice in exam term. Those are real work, and a tutor who absorbs all of them silently either burns out or quietly reduces preparation time, which is worse. Ask what is included in the first conversation so there is nothing to renegotiate in November.

IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mahalaxmi depend on a handful of variables and no page can honestly quote a figure without them. Board and level come first: a Higher Level Diploma Programme subject commands more than a Core-tier IGCSE one. Subject scarcity comes second, and it is the biggest single swing: Mathematics and the sciences have depth on the island, while Computer Science, Additional Mathematics and some second languages do not. Then travel, since a tutor crossing Haji Ali at seven in the evening for a single hour is pricing that journey in. Then session length, where ninety minutes is usually better value per unit of learning than sixty. Then frequency and term length, because a committed term is worth more to a tutor than a fortnight of trials.

Two structures are common and they behave differently. A per-session arrangement is flexible and tends to drift: sessions get skipped, the tutor fills the slot with another student, and by December your Tuesday has gone. A term commitment holds the slot, usually improves the rate per hour, and makes the tutor plan across weeks instead of one lesson at a time. For a student with external papers at the end of the year, the term commitment is almost always the right structure, and the flexibility you give up was mostly illusory.

Watch for the things that are not fees but behave like them. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mahalaxmi who needs ten minutes at the gate every week is costing you a session a term in lobby time. A tutor who arrives without last week's marked work is costing you the first fifteen minutes while they read it. A tutor whose own schedule means your slot is always the last of the evening is costing you attention. None of these shows up in a quote, and all of them show up in the result.

sections.heading: Reporting between sessions: how a Mumbai parent knows it is working
paragraphs: The thing most parents actually buy with IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mahalaxmi is information, and most never ask for it. Agree in week one that the tutor sends a two or three line note after every session: what was covered, what the student got wrong, and what they are expected to do before next week. That note takes a tutor three minutes and gives you a term-long record, which is what makes the four-week and twelve-week conversations possible at all.

At four weeks, read the four notes together rather than asking for a verdict. You should see named topics, not themes. You should see at least one shift in approach. You should see tasks set and either done or not done, which is often the most useful line in the whole record. A student who has not completed the between-session work in four weeks has a work-rate problem, and more tutored hours will not fix it. That is a conversation with your child, not a different tutor.

At one term the evidence should come from the school, not from the tutor. Movement in internal assessments and in teacher comments is the measure; progress on the tutor's own worksheets is not. Expect gains where the tutor said at the start they would come, and expect at least one area that has not moved. A term report that claims improvement everywhere is a report nobody checked. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and the honest framing is that an arrangement like this improves the odds and the technique rather than fixing a result.

Across a full exam cycle the limits are worth stating plainly. Home tuition reliably changes exam technique, work habits and confidence in a specific subject. It cannot cover a syllabus the school has not taught, and it cannot compress two years into eight weeks. Some families here search for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mahalaxmi in February for a May series, and the right answer is sometimes to pick one paper and work on it properly rather than four and achieve nothing in any of them.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mahalaxmi, Mumbai next week
paragraphs: Three pieces of information get you a shortlist: the board and year group for each child, the subjects you want covered, and the two or three evening windows that genuinely work in your flat. Add the most recent marked paper if you have one. It is worth more than a report card because it shows where the marks went rather than where the student feels weak, and it lets the tutor plan the first session before they arrive.

The first session is diagnostic and should be booked as such. The tutor watches more than they teach: a few questions from the current topic, one from last term, one under a clock. By the end you should have two named topics to rebuild, one technique problem to drill, and a plan for the next four weeks. Ask for that plan in writing. A tutor who cannot produce it after ninety minutes with your child has not been paying attention.

Set the logistics in the same week. Register the standing weekly visitor entry with your society office, agree the grace window and the missed-session rule, decide where in the flat the lesson happens, and confirm who is at home to admit the tutor. In a high-floor tower, build the lift into your arithmetic, because a tutor on time at the gate can still be five minutes late at your door and that compounds over thirty sessions.

faqs.question: How many hours a week should IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mahalaxmi run?
faqs.answer: For IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mahalaxmi, one ninety-minute session a week per subject is the right starting point for most students, rising to two in the eight weeks before a paper or where there is a genuine content gap. Higher Level Diploma Programme subjects often need two from the start. Beyond two sessions a week per subject you are mostly buying supervision, and the student loses the independent study time that makes tutoring work at all. Start at one, review at four weeks with the tutor's session notes in front of you, and add hours for a specific reason rather than as a general reassurance.

faqs.question: Should we book for the whole term or just the exam term?
faqs.answer: Book the term if your child has external papers at the end of the year. A term commitment holds your slot, usually improves the hourly value, and makes the tutor plan across weeks instead of lesson by lesson. Exam-term-only bookings have two problems in this corridor: the good tutors have no capacity left by late January, and eight weeks is not enough to rebuild content that was never properly learned. If budget forces a choice, run one session a week all year rather than four a week in February. The steady version produces more.

faqs.question: What happens if our regular home tutor is away for two weeks?
faqs.answer: You have three options and should pick one in advance rather than in the moment. The tutor can run those sessions online from wherever they are, which keeps continuity and is usually the best choice. We can place a briefed replacement who receives the session notes and the current plan, which works for content teaching and less well for essay marking. Or the sessions pause and are made up on weekends. The one arrangement that fails is leaving it undecided, because a two-week gap with no plan tends to become a five-week gap and a restart.

faqs.question: How will I know what happened in a session I did not sit in on?
faqs.answer: Through a written note, agreed in week one as part of the arrangement. Two or three lines after each session covering what was taught, what the student got wrong, and what they must do before next week. This costs the tutor three minutes and gives you a record that makes every later conversation possible. Across four weeks those notes show you whether topics are named or vague, whether the approach has changed, and whether the between-session work is being done. That last line is usually the most informative thing in the whole arrangement.

faqs.question: Do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mahalaxmi change mid-term?
faqs.answer: They should not, and a clear agreement at the start prevents it. What does change is the volume: an extra session before mocks, a longer slot for Internal Assessment drafting, or weekend hours in the exam run-in all cost more because they are more work. Agree at the outset what the rate covers and what counts as extra, including long-form marking, written reports and short-notice sessions. Fees themselves depend on board and level, subject scarcity, travel, session length, frequency and whether you commit to a term, and no honest figure can be quoted before those are known.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor teach my Year 9 and my Diploma Programme child?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and only if the subjects are genuinely related and the tutor can describe the two jobs separately. Teaching Middle Years Programme science and Higher Level Physics in the same flat on the same evening demands different preparation, different language and different expectations about independent work. The convenience of one visit matters in a tower where every entry involves a gate and a lift, so it is worth asking. If the tutor's answer blurs the two children into one plan, take two tutors on two evenings and accept the extra scheduling.

faqs.question: Is a two-hour session better than two one-hour sessions?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject. For Internal Assessment drafting, extended writing or a full past paper under timed conditions, one long block is clearly better because the work cannot be meaningfully split. For Mathematics and the sciences, two shorter sessions usually beat one long one, because the gap between them is where practice happens and a tutor can check whether a correction actually stuck. In a corridor where travel eats the evening, many families compromise on one ninety-minute session in person and one short online follow-up, which captures most of the benefit of both.

faqs.question: Can a tutor from Worli commit to the same evening slot for a whole term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that commitment is what we screen for before listing anyone for this area. Tutors coming from Worli, Tardeo or Byculla typically build an evening chain of two or three slots arranged geographically, and your slot being the middle one makes it the most stable. Ask directly whether your time is their first, middle or last booking of the evening. A last slot is quieter and more relaxed; a first slot is the one that slips when the previous commitment overruns. Also agree a fifteen-minute grace window so a signal jam is not a weekly apology.

faqs.question: What is not included in the rate?
faqs.answer: Usually anything that happens outside the session. Marking long essays or full past papers between visits, writing a formal progress report, attending a school meeting, building a custom question bank, and holding additional slots at short notice in exam term are all real work that most tutors price separately. Ask in the first conversation rather than assuming, because the alternative is a tutor who absorbs it quietly and reduces preparation time to compensate. Clarity here also protects the tutor, and an arrangement that is fair to both sides is the one that survives to March. Experienced tutors in Mumbai raise this themselves.

faqs.question: Do we pay for a session we cancel the morning of?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because the tutor has reserved the time and travel and cannot refill a slot that morning. The fairer question is what the cancellation policy is, and it should be agreed in week one: a notice period, a number of goodwill cancellations per term, and whether a late cancellation converts into an online session instead of being lost. Families who set this out at the start rarely argue about it later. Those who do not end up negotiating in November, which is exactly when neither side has the patience for it.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need parking at our building?
faqs.answer: Many do not, because a meaningful share of tutors on this corridor travel by train to Mahalaxmi station or by autorickshaw from Tardeo and Worli. For those who drive, visitor parking in these towers is limited and often the real reason a session starts ten minutes late. Ask your society office whether visitor parking can be pre-authorised for a standing weekly slot, and if it cannot, say so during matching. It is a legitimate filter: a tutor who can reach you without parking is a more reliable long-term fit than one circling the lane every Tuesday.

faqs.question: What if progress stalls halfway through the term?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a diagnostic question before a replacement question. Put the session notes next to the school's feedback and look for the mismatch: often the tutor is teaching the content competently while the marks are being lost on timing, presentation of method, or a component nobody has addressed. If the plan was sound and the fit is wrong, we replace the tutor and brief the new one with the existing notes so nothing restarts from zero. If the real problem is that work is not happening between sessions, more hours will not help and we will tell you that plainly.

sections.heading: Can one tutor cover both IB and IGCSE in the same house?
paragraphs: Sometimes, and the answer depends entirely on which subjects and which levels. A tutor with a mathematics background can realistically handle IGCSE Extended Mathematics for a Year 10 student and Standard Level Applications and Interpretation for a Diploma Programme student, because the content overlaps heavily and the difference is in question style and the internally assessed exploration. The same tutor cannot credibly cover IGCSE Business Studies and Higher Level Chemistry, and anyone who offers to is offering supervision.

The boards themselves differ in ways that matter. The International General Certificate of Secondary Education is awarded by Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel, with specification codes, paper structures and practical arrangements that are not interchangeable between them. The International Baccalaureate runs the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma Programme, where Higher Level and Standard Level, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the internally assessed components set the shape of the work. A tutor fluent in both systems exists; a tutor fluent in both systems across unrelated subjects generally does not. We will not put one home tutor in Mumbai across two unrelated subjects simply to save a journey.

Where one tutor does work, the gain is not only financial. The tutor sees both children, understands the household's rhythm, and can tell you something useful about how your younger child is tracking toward the pathway the older one is already on. That continuity is worth real money when the younger child reaches the point of choosing between a Diploma Programme and an A Level route in the sixth form.

For current structures, tier availability and component requirements on either board, use the syllabus or subject guide in force for your child's cohort and ask the school coordinator. Both the International Baccalaureate and the examination boards revise their documents on their own cycles, and a tutor working from an older edition is preparing for a version of the course that has shifted.
