sections.heading: Where the two boards actually diverge, subject by subject
paragraphs: In mathematics the divergence is mostly in what is rewarded. IGCSE Extended papers want visible method on multi-step questions; a correct answer with compressed working loses most of the marks. Diploma Programme mathematics adds the mathematical exploration, which is an extended independent piece marked against published criteria, and the skill it demands is choosing a question narrow enough to be answered properly. A student who is strong at one of those can be weak at the other, which is why a household with children on both pathways often needs the same tutor to work in two completely different registers.

In the sciences the divergence is the practical component. IGCSE Physics and Chemistry assess practical skills either in a laboratory paper or in an alternative-to-practical written paper depending on the school, focused on experimental design, variable control and reading uncertainty. The Diploma Programme sciences carry an internally assessed scientific investigation, which is a longer independent piece where the marks go to the quality of the research question and the handling of data rather than to procedural accuracy. Both reward the same underlying habit and test it very differently.

In the humanities and languages the pattern repeats. IGCSE History and Geography turn on command words and source handling. Diploma Programme equivalents add an internally assessed investigation and, in languages, oral assessment where the course your child is entered in matters enormously. IB Gram lists tutors for all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mahim can reach, and we match subject by subject rather than by board label, because the label tells you less than the component does.

The practical consequence for a two-board household is that you should ask about components, not subjects. Not can you teach chemistry, but have you supervised a scientific investigation and have you prepared students for an alternative-to-practical paper? A tutor who can answer both specifically is rare and worth scheduling around, and worth building a household's home classes in Mumbai around rather than splitting across two people.

sections.heading: One tutor, two children, four addresses around Mahim
paragraphs: A tutor working a Mahim evening can hold more than one household in the same trip, and that is why this part of Mumbai suits a two-child arrangement. Mahim Junction carries the Western Line and the Harbour Line, and the Mahim Causeway takes the road traffic between the island city and the suburbs. Dadar sits a stop away, Prabhadevi is a short run south on the island side, and Bandra West is directly across the causeway. A tutor with bookings in two of those plus yours has a week that works.

Set that against the corridor logic. The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, so a tutor travelling Bandra to Andheri is quick off-peak and painful at 6pm, and matching along the line works far better than matching across it. A Mahim household is at the southern anchor, which means your realistic catchment includes island-side tutors as well as suburban ones. For a family needing both IGCSE and Diploma Programme cover, that doubled catchment is the difference between finding one good pairing and settling for two mediocre ones.

What we do with that in practice is schedule the household as a block. One visit, two consecutive hours, one journey. If both children need the same tutor it is a single booking. If they need different tutors, we try to put the two visits on different evenings rather than the same one, because two tutors in a two-bedroom flat at the same hour means one of them is teaching in a bedroom with a door that does not close properly.

Parents searching IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mahim are generally imagining a single solution, and for a two-child household that instinct is right. The answer is not necessarily one tutor; it is one schedule. Our all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mahim are built as a household plan rather than as separate bookings that happen to share an address.

sections.heading: How two boards collide in one Mumbai school calendar
paragraphs: If both children attend the same school the collision is predictable and brutal. International schools in Mumbai, Maharashtra mostly run June to April with a long Diwali break, and the assessment pressure concentrates in the same windows for everybody. Late in the monsoon term the first serious coursework and internal tests land. In the winter, mocks run for the IGCSE year while the Diploma Programme year is finishing internally assessed drafts. One fortnight in the new year can carry an IGCSE mock timetable, a Diploma Programme Internal Assessment deadline and a Theory of Knowledge submission in the same house.

If the two children attend different schools it is worse in a different way, because the pressure points no longer coincide and the household never gets a quiet month. Families from Mahim send children in several directions: Jamnabai Narsee International School up in Juhu, Don Bosco International School in Matunga, and others further along the corridor. Two different bus schedules means two different arrival times and two different workable slots, and that is the constraint we plan around before anything else.

The useful move is to map the year once, in June, with both children's assessment calendars side by side on one sheet. Mark the fortnights where both are loaded. Those are the weeks where you want an extra session for one child and no session at all for the other, and knowing them in advance is the difference between a plan and a scramble. A tutor hired in July can build around that map. A tutor hired in January is reacting to it. Most of the home tuition in Mumbai that survives a full year was arranged against a calendar rather than against a bad report.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Jamnabai Narsee International School, Don Bosco International School or any other school mentioned here. We name them because their calendars and bus routes set the real constraints in a two-child household, not because we have any relationship with them.

sections.heading: Back-to-back home classes, or one at home and one online?
paragraphs: Back-to-back at home is the arrangement most two-child households in Mahim end up preferring, and for good reasons. One journey, one tutor who knows the family, two hours of work and a single evening disrupted rather than two. It also means the younger child sees the older one being taught, which in practice does more for a Year 10 student's attitude to study than any amount of parental encouragement. We arrange a great deal of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mahim exactly this way.

The split arrangement, one child at home and one online, solves a different problem. If the two children need genuinely different specialists and your flat has one usable study surface, running the older child's Diploma Programme session online on a different evening frees the room and widens the pool to specialists who are nowhere near the causeway. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mahim is a sensible choice for a self-managing Diploma Programme student and a poor one for a Year 9 child who needs an adult beside them.

The arrangement we advise against is two tutors in the flat at the same hour. It sounds efficient and it is not. Sound carries, the better room goes to whoever arrived first, and both sessions end up at roughly seventy percent. If both children must be taught on the same evening, stagger the start times by an hour and accept a longer evening, or put one of them online.

Hybrid also absorbs the weeks when nothing in Mumbai moves at 6.30pm. Agreeing in June that a session goes online rather than being lost when the tutor cannot cross the causeway is a five-minute conversation that saves several sessions over a monsoon.

sections.heading: Verifying a tutor who will teach two of your children in Mumbai
paragraphs: The stakes are slightly higher with two children, because a bad match now has to be unwound twice and because the tutor will be in your home for two hours a week rather than one. Our checks happen before a profile is listed: identity, the degree and any teaching qualification claimed, and the teaching history checked subject by subject, board by board and level by level. A tutor who cannot describe what students lose marks on in a component they claim to have taught does not get listed for it.

Your own checks should be sharper than usual in one specific respect. Ask the tutor to describe, separately, how they would handle each child. If the answer is the same shape for a Year 10 IGCSE student and a Diploma Programme Higher Level student, they are planning to teach topics rather than courses. A good answer differs: for the younger one, close the method gaps and build timed paper discipline; for the older one, work on the internally assessed piece and the extension topics. Any IB and IGCSE private tutor in Mahim worth hiring will give you two different plans without being prompted.

Then watch the first month for the thing only a two-child household can see: whether the tutor gives both children the same quality of attention. It is common and human for a tutor to prefer the more responsive child, and it shows up as the second session drifting into supervised homework. The signal is in the written notes. If one child's note is detailed and the other's is a sentence, say so in week two rather than month three.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade for either child, and treat a quoted pass rate the same way. We do not guarantee grades. Outcomes on both boards depend on the student's own work across two years and on external marking that nobody in your home influences.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma Programme bridge, and the year it is won
paragraphs: The hardest transition in this system is not the first Diploma Programme examination. It is the first term of Diploma Programme year one, and it is won or lost in the final IGCSE year. An IGCSE student is taught a defined specification and assessed largely on recall and technique under timed conditions. A Diploma Programme student is handed a course with internally assessed components, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, and is expected to manage independent work across two years. The habits that produce good IGCSE grades do not automatically produce a functioning Diploma Programme student.

What transfers is method, and what does not transfer is dependence. A Year 11 student who revises by rereading notes the night before and still scores well has a method that will fail them by the second Diploma Programme term, because nobody will tell them when to start the exploration or the investigation. This is the single most useful thing a tutor can work on in the final IGCSE year, and almost nobody asks for it, because the presenting problem is always a subject rather than a habit.

In a two-board household you have an advantage the single-child family does not: the older child is living the answer in the next room. We have seen Mahim families use this deliberately. The tutor who teaches the Diploma Programme student at 6pm and the IGCSE student at 7pm can tell the younger one, concretely, what the older one wishes they had started three weeks earlier. That is a more credible warning than any parent can deliver.

Mahim's geography makes this pairing easy to staff. Mahim is the causeway crossing between the island city and the suburbs, so it is the natural midpoint for a tutor holding one Dadar family and one Bandra family, which means a tutor can build a viable week around your household plus two others without fighting the corridor. The two-hour block in one flat is the single most attractive booking shape a Mumbai tutor can be offered, and it buys you better people than two separate hours would.

The tier and subject choices made in the final IGCSE year are the other half of the bridge. Extended tier mathematics, a science taken seriously, and a language entered at the right level between first language and acquired language all shape which Diploma Programme subjects are comfortable two years later. Those decisions are worth a short, time-limited piece of tutoring on their own, and they are much cheaper to get right in Year 10 than to work around in Year 12.

sections.heading: What should four weeks look like with two children in tuition?
paragraphs: Different for each child, and that is the point. For the IGCSE student, four weeks should change the shape of a written answer: method shown line by line, command words underlined, a six-mark question planned before it is written. For the Diploma Programme student it should change the planning: a research question narrowed, a draft timeline that exists on paper, a reading list that is actually being used. If both children show the same kind of change, the tutor is probably teaching one course and adapting it, which is the failure mode this arrangement is prone to.

At one term, expect the school's own feedback to shift for both and expect the tutor to have told you something specific about each. The most valuable diagnosis we have heard in a two-board household was that the younger child was not weaker than the older one at all; they were being compared to a sibling two years further along and had stopped trying. That is not a tutoring problem, and naming it was worth more than a term of sessions.

Over a full cycle the honest range is wide for both children and will probably differ between them. Siblings are not comparable: different subjects, different boards, different years, different temperaments. We do not guarantee grades, we publish no success rates, and we would be suspicious of anyone in Mumbai who offered either for a household rather than a student. What we commit to is verified specialists, stable hours, an honest review every few weeks and a free replacement where the fit is wrong.

There is a version of this where you should hire nobody for one of the children. If the younger one is coping and has simply been enrolled because the older one has a tutor, you are buying a fifth evening commitment and a comparison they did not ask for. Start with the child who needs it. The other can be added in a term if the need is real, and a second home tutor in Mumbai is easier to add mid-year than to unwind.

faqs.question: Can one tutor really teach both my children at home on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Often yes, in consecutive hours, and it is usually the best arrangement available. One journey means the booking is cheap for the tutor to keep, which is the main reason placements survive to February. It works cleanly when the subjects are adjacent, such as mathematics across both boards, and it works badly when they are not. What rarely works is two different tutors in a small flat at the same hour, because sound carries and the second session loses the better room and roughly a third of its value.

faqs.question: How does a tutor get into our building for a standing weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Add them once rather than arguing weekly. Most Mahim buildings will put a regular visitor on a standing list at the gate if a resident confirms the day and time. Tell the tutor which entrance to use, whether the lift needs a resident card in the evening, and where to wait if they arrive early. Five minutes of admin in week one prevents the first ten minutes of every session being spent downstairs, which across a two-hour household booking adds up to a lost session every few weeks.

faqs.question: Do my two children need different tutors if they are on different boards?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subjects, not the boards. Mathematics across IGCSE Extended and Diploma Programme Standard Level overlaps enough that one capable tutor can cover both, in different registers. IGCSE Business Studies and Higher Level Chemistry do not overlap at all and need two people. Ask any candidate to describe both plans separately. If the two descriptions sound the same, they intend to teach topics rather than courses, and you should hire two tutors instead.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mahim depend on?
faqs.answer: Board, level, subject scarcity, session length and travel. A Higher Level Diploma Programme specialist costs more than a Year 9 tutor because fewer people in Mumbai have taught the course. A two-hour household booking often costs less per child than two separate hours, because the tutor travels once. We publish no rate card, since any figure would be wrong for most enquiries. Raise it on the discovery call and ask what the rate reflects, including whether a second consecutive hour is priced differently.

faqs.question: Which months are worst in a household with children on both pathways?
faqs.answer: The winter weeks after the Diwali break, when IGCSE mocks and Diploma Programme internally assessed deadlines overlap, and the late monsoon term when both years get their first serious coursework. If your children are at different schools the windows do not coincide, which means no quiet month but also no single catastrophic fortnight. Map both assessment calendars onto one sheet in June. Those overlapping fortnights are where you want an extra session for one child and none for the other.

faqs.question: Our flat has one study table. Does home tuition still work?
faqs.answer: Yes, with staggered timing. Run the two children consecutively rather than simultaneously, or move the older child's Diploma Programme session online on a different evening to free the table. One usable surface with a plug socket and no screen in the sightline is enough for a good session; two sessions competing for it is not. This is the single most common practical constraint in Mahim flats and it is solved by the schedule rather than by furniture.

faqs.question: Should the younger child start tutoring just because the older one has?
faqs.answer: No. If the younger child is coping, enrolling them adds an evening commitment and an unhelpful comparison. Start with the child who needs it, and add the second only if a specific need appears. The one exception is a time-limited piece of work in the final IGCSE year on independent study habits, which genuinely pays off in the first Diploma Programme term and is worth a short block of sessions even for a student whose grades are fine.

faqs.question: How do we handle the IGCSE to Diploma Programme transition?
faqs.answer: Work on habits in the final IGCSE year, not content in the first Diploma Programme term. The student who revises by rereading notes the night before will struggle by the second Diploma term, because nobody will tell them when to start the exploration or the investigation. Tier and language entry decisions matter too: Extended tier mathematics and the right language course shape which Diploma subjects feel comfortable later. A short block of tutoring aimed at those decisions is cheaper than fixing the consequences in Year 12.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Mahim for a two-hour evening booking?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a two-hour block is the most attractive shape a Mumbai tutor can be offered, because one journey covers two paid hours. Tutors reach Mahim from Dadar, Prabhadevi or Bandra West across the causeway rather than driving down the Western Express Highway, which is quick off-peak and slow at 6pm. If you can start at 5.30pm rather than 6.30pm you will have a wider choice of genuinely board-matched tutors, because the earlier block fits either side of their other bookings.

faqs.question: Do tutors understand what local international schools expect?
faqs.answer: A tutor who has taught students from schools like Jamnabai Narsee International School or Don Bosco International School knows roughly when mocks fall, how internally assessed deadlines are paced and how predicted grades are handled across the Mumbai year. That changes what they prioritise in October versus January, which matters more in a two-child household than in a single one. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with either school, or with any school we name as local context.

faqs.question: Can you promise results for either child?
faqs.answer: No, and we do not guarantee grades for either board. Outcomes depend on each student's own work across two years, the series or session they sit, and external marking that nobody in your flat influences. Siblings also are not comparable: different subjects, years and temperaments produce different arcs. What we commit to is verified subject specialists, stable weekly hours, two separate honest reviews rather than one household summary, and a free replacement for either placement if the fit is wrong.

sections.heading: Which stage is your child actually in: PYP, MYP, DP or Cambridge IGCSE?
paragraphs: Parents in Thane often use IB and IGCSE as one word, and the schools here make that understandable. A family on Pokhran Road can have one child sitting Cambridge papers in Year 11 and another being assessed on criteria in MYP, in buildings two kilometres apart. The two systems are not variations of each other. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs on transdisciplinary units and almost no formal testing, so a PYP parent asking for home tuition is usually asking for reading fluency, number sense or English as an additional language support rather than exam coaching. MYP introduces subject criteria, command terms and a personal project, and marks arrive as criterion levels rather than percentages, which is where most of the confusion between the boards begins.

Cambridge IGCSE at Years 9 to 11 is the opposite shape. It is a linear course with a tier decision inside it: Core or Extended in several subjects, and a Foundation or Higher style split in others. The decision gets made in Year 9 or early Year 10 and it caps what a student can be awarded, so it deserves far more thought than it usually gets. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Majiwada who has taught both boards will tell you within a fortnight whether a child entered for Core is actually an Extended candidate who lost confidence, or an Extended candidate who is being quietly destroyed by the pace.

The Diploma Programme sits on top of all of it, and the handover is the genuinely dangerous moment. A student who did well at IGCSE by being organised and revising past papers meets Theory of Knowledge (TOK), an Extended Essay (EE), and six subjects that each want an Internal Assessment (IA) written to criteria nobody has explained to them yet. Standard Level (SL) and HL are not simply easier and harder versions of the same course; HL adds material and depth that changes how a subject has to be studied. We match tutors against the specific stage, not against the acronym, because a strong MYP teacher is not automatically a strong DP one.

If you are not sure which stage applies, the school's programme coordinator is the right person to confirm it, and the current subject guide is the only reliable source for how any course is assessed this year. The IB and the Cambridge boards both revise guides on their own cycles, and we will not quote a structure at you that may have changed since your older child sat it.

sections.heading: What do HL, SL, Core and Extended actually commit you to?
paragraphs: Subject choice across both boards is the request we get most often from this part of Thane, and it is rarely really about which subject a child likes. It is about what each choice drags along behind it. An IGCSE science taken as three separate subjects carries three sets of papers and three practical skillsets. The same sciences taken as a combined award carry one. At DP, choosing Mathematics at Higher Level commits a student to a mathematical exploration written to criteria as well as the papers, and choosing a science at HL commits them to a scientific investigation on top of the additional higher level material. Nobody tells a Year 11 student that when they tick the box in the option block.

The internal assessments are where home tuition earns its place, because they are the part of both boards that happens at your dining table rather than in an exam hall. An MYP criterion-based task, an IGCSE coursework component where the syllabus still has one, and a DP internal assessment all reward something school lessons have little time for: planning, redrafting, and reading the criteria as instructions rather than as decoration. A tutor covering all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Majiwada can honestly take on will not pretend to teach six of them, and should say which two or three they are genuinely strong in.

Language choices deserve their own conversation. A student who has done Hindi at MYP and wants to carry it into DP as Language A faces a different course from the one they left, and a student picking up Spanish ab initio in DP1 is starting from zero in a two-year window. In Thane, Marathi and Hindi availability at a school can quietly decide a child's entire language pathway. We match on the exact course code and level where the brief gives one, because Mathematics at two different levels is two different hires.

For the structure of any of this, use the current subject guide and the school's coordinator. We will tell you what the papers and components ask a student to do, what skills they reward, and what a tutor should be working on in week one. We will not quote you a weighting, a paper length or a mark total, because those are the parts the boards revise and the parts a page like this gets wrong.

sections.heading: Home tuition across Majiwada, Thane West, Pokhran Road and Kolshet Road
paragraphs: Majiwada is not a self-contained suburb and it does not behave like one. It is the hinge of Thane, Mumbai, Maharashtra, and the areas we send tutors to from here form a short, honest list: Thane West towards the station, Pokhran Road to the south, and Kolshet Road heading out towards the creek. Those three plus Majiwada itself are a single matching pool, because a tutor who takes work in any one of them can take work in the others without changing how their week is built. Push beyond that and you are asking somebody to cross the Ghodbunder stretch twice in an evening, which is a commitment that sounds fine in September and falls apart in the monsoon.

Thane spreads west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets the schedule. A tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes when the road is clear and close to an hour once the evening peak builds. That is not a traffic complaint, it is a scheduling constraint, and it is why home tuition across this part of Mumbai works best when the slot is built around the tutor's direction of travel rather than around the clock. Thane tutors cover Thane. A tutor based in Mulund will sometimes cross over for a strong subject match, and occasionally one will come up the Eastern Express Highway for an HL subject that is genuinely scarce, but we treat that as the exception and we say so before you commit to it.

Inside Majiwada, Lodha Splendora is the address that comes up most, and large complexes change the logistics rather than the teaching. A standing weekly slot inside a gated development needs the tutor registered properly at the gate once, not argued about every Tuesday. The practical version of that is a resident-initiated visitor entry, a tutor who carries photo identification, and a fixed day and time so the security desk recognises the arrangement. Lessons happen at a dining table, in a study, or in a society reading room where the family prefers it.

paragraphs: The pressure points are predictable, which is the useful part. Families in Majiwada mostly send children to Smt. August and September look calm and are not. This is when MYP criterion tasks start landing and when DP1 students are told, usually in one assembly, that an Extended Essay exists. October and November are when the first real marks come home, and the volume of requests we get from Thane roughly doubles in that fortnight for the simple reason that a criterion level of three in writing is much harder to argue with than a general sense that things are fine.

January and February are the hard months. IGCSE mocks, DP mocks, internal assessment deadlines and the TOK essay stack into the same weeks, and a Year 11 student at a school on the Pokhran Road corridor can genuinely have four pieces of assessed work due in eight days. A tutor booked in January is doing triage, not teaching. March to May belongs to the exam boards, and from then on the only sensible work is past papers, timing and keeping a student calm. June is when the next year's subject choices get made quietly and badly, and a single session spent on the option block then is worth more than a term of catch-up later.

There is one local wrinkle worth planning around. Because Majiwada is the junction every Thane tutor passes through, the slots here get taken first in the October rush. A family that waits until the report arrives is competing for the same evening hours as every other family on this stretch of Mumbai, and the honest consequence is a four o'clock slot or a Saturday morning rather than the seven o'clock one you wanted.

sections.heading: Should IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai ever move online?
paragraphs: Start with the default, because for almost every family here it is the right one. A tutor at your table sees what a report cannot: which questions the student skips, how long they sit before writing anything, whether the notebook is organised or a pile. An IB and IGCSE home tuition in Majiwada arrangement also removes the part of tuition that actually kills consistency, which is a thirteen-year-old travelling to a centre on Ghodbunder Road at seven in the evening. Home classes in Majiwada hold for a full term more often than centre-based arrangements do, and the reason is logistical rather than pedagogical.

Online has two situations where it genuinely wins. The first is scarcity. If you need a DP HL subject that only a handful of people in Mumbai teach well, an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Majiwada beats a nearby generalist, and it is not close. The second is the exam term, when a student wants three short sessions a week rather than two long ones and nobody has the travel budget for that. Online loses on the things that are easy to underestimate: a tutor cannot see the page the student is actually writing on unless you set up a document camera, and a tired student is much better at appearing to pay attention on a screen.

Hybrid is what most families here settle into by the second term without planning it. The weekday session is at home, the top-up before a test is online, and the arrangement survives a week when the road is flooded or the tutor is in Pune. If you want that, agree it at the start rather than drifting into it, because a tutor who has not budgeted for online sessions will treat them as a favour and the quality shows. We will also say plainly that online is the weaker option for PYP and early MYP children, where the work is as much about sitting down and starting as it is about content.

One more honest trade-off. Going online widens your choice of tutor enormously and narrows your ability to judge them. In person, you hear the session from the next room and you know by week three whether it is working. On a screen you are relying on reported progress, so ask for the shared document, the problem set, the marked draft. All IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes in Majiwada should leave a paper trail you can read without being a teacher.

sections.heading: How a tutor is checked before they ring your doorbell in Majiwada
paragraphs: Before a profile reaches you, we check identity against government photo identification, we check the qualification claimed in the subject being taught rather than a general degree, and we check board experience as a specific question: which year groups, which boards, which components, for how long. A person who has taught MYP Sciences for four years is a different hire from a person who has taught state-board Physics for ten, and both are better than a person who is vague about the difference. Contactable references from previous families are part of it, and so is a direct conversation about the areas and slots that person can actually sustain rather than the ones they would like.

The checks we cannot do are the ones you can, and they are the more important half. Put the tutor in front of your child for one session and listen from the next room. You are not listening for expertise, you are listening for whether questions get asked and whether your child answers them. Ask the tutor what they intend to cover in the first three weeks and whether they can name the criteria or the paper they are working towards. Ask them to mark one piece of your child's existing work in front of you, which is the fastest way to find out whether somebody knows a board or has only read about it.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, and be equally wary of one who will teach any subject at any level on any day. Scarcity is real: good DP HL teachers are busy, and a completely open calendar in October is information. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Majiwada who tells you honestly that they are strong at IGCSE Mathematics and weak at DP Analysis and Approaches is worth more than one who claims both, because you can build around a known limit.

Insist on the boring things in writing. The day, the time, the duration, the subject, how a missed session is handled, and how much notice either side gives to stop. Most arrangements that go wrong in Thane go wrong on logistics rather than teaching, and a parent who agreed the cancellation rule in week one does not have an argument about it in week nine. An IB and IGCSE home tuition in Majiwada arrangement is a working relationship with a professional, and it should be set up like one.

sections.heading: Why Majiwada junction sets the clock for every Thane home tuition timetable
paragraphs: Every tutor in Thane quotes their travel time from Majiwada junction, and once you understand why, you can build a timetable that survives the year. The junction is where Ghodbunder Road leaves the Eastern Express Highway, which makes it the only point the whole district passes through. A tutor explaining their Tuesday will say twenty minutes to Kasarvadavali, ten to Kolshet Road, eight to Thane West, and they are counting from here whether they live here or not. For a family in Majiwada this is unusually good news: you are at the zero point of everybody else's estimate, which is why this stretch has more realistic tutor availability than anywhere further out on Ghodbunder Road.

It also tells you how to choose a slot. Work backwards from the tutor's previous commitment instead of forwards from your convenience. Subject scarcity, because the pool of people who can teach HL Physics well in Mumbai is small and they know it. Travel, because a tutor adding a dedicated trip across the Ghodbunder stretch is charging for an hour of road as well as an hour of teaching, and a tutor already passing through is not. Which means the cheapest honest way to arrange a home tutor in Majiwada is to be flexible about the hour and inflexible about the subject match. sections.heading: What four weeks of home tuition in Mumbai should actually change
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not expect a mark to move, and a tutor who promises one is telling you what you want to hear. What should have changed is smaller and more diagnostic. Your child should be able to say what they are bad at, specifically, rather than saying the subject is hard. Homework should be starting earlier in the evening. The tutor should be able to name two or three things they are working on and why, and those things should match what the school report said rather than a generic syllabus order. If none of that has happened in a month, the match is wrong and you should say so.

At one term, marks start to answer. A criterion level moving from three to five, an IGCSE Extended paper where the long questions are now attempted instead of abandoned, a DP internal assessment that has a plan and a deadline rather than a vague intention. This is also the point where the honest limits show up. A student who is two years behind in algebra does not finish a term level with the class, and a tutor who says they will is setting up a bad conversation in March. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and we would rather lose a booking than let somebody imply otherwise.

Across a full exam cycle, the things that actually move are examination technique, coverage of the parts of the course a student has been quietly avoiding, and the internal assessment marks, which are the most controllable part of both boards. Those are real gains and they are worth paying for. What tuition cannot fix is a subject taken at the wrong level, a student who does not want to be in the room, or six months of missed foundations in eight weeks. We will tell you which of those we think we are looking at after the first three sessions.

The failure modes are worth naming too. The most common is a tutor who becomes a homework helper: the sessions are pleasant, the work gets finished, and nothing is learned. The second is a tutor who teaches the subject beautifully and ignores the assessment, which produces a student who understands Physics and cannot answer a Paper 2 question. The third is a schedule that was never realistic, which is why so much of this page is about roads. Home tuition in this part of Mumbai lives or dies on whether the Tuesday slot is still happening in February.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home classes in Majiwada
paragraphs: Three things make the first message useful. The board and year group, written as the school writes it rather than as you remember it. The most recent report or marked piece of work, including the teacher comments, because a criterion level with a comment tells a tutor more than a term's worth of conversation. And two slots that genuinely work in your week, with a note on which one you would defend if the tutor asked to move it. Parents who send those three things get a shortlist in days. Parents who send a subject name get a longer conversation first.

Session one is a diagnosis, not a lesson, and you should expect it to look slightly unproductive. A good tutor spends the first forty minutes on the student's own work: the questions they got wrong, the draft they abandoned, the topic they say they understand. By the end of it they should be able to tell you two specific gaps and what order they intend to close them in. If session one was a general introduction to the syllabus, the tutor has not started working yet. Have the textbook, the notebook and the school portal login to hand, and have somewhere with a table rather than a sofa.

Practicalities at this end of Thane are simple if you handle them once. Register the tutor at your gate for a standing weekly entry rather than as a fresh visitor each week, keep the slot on the same day so the security desk recognises it, and tell us in advance about building rules that affect timing. For a family searching IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Majiwada, the arrangement that lasts is almost always the one where the gate, the slot and the direction of travel were all sorted out in the first week.

After that the job is review rather than search. Ask the tutor for a short note every third or fourth session: what was covered, what the student can now do unaided, what is next. Read the marked work rather than the summary. If the notes stop arriving, that is usually the earliest signal that an arrangement is drifting, and it is far easier to fix in week six than in February. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai will not exist, but a tutor who is honest about the two subjects they own is exactly what you are looking for.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Lodha Splendora for a seven o'clock weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but it depends entirely on where they finish their previous session. A tutor coming from Thane West or Kolshet Road will hold a seven o'clock slot comfortably through the year. A tutor coming back from Kasarvadavali at six will manage it in October and start arriving late by July, because that stretch of Ghodbunder Road roughly triples in the evening peak. We would rather offer you a reliable five or a Saturday morning than a seven that quietly becomes seven twenty. Tell us the slot you want and the slot you would accept, and we will be honest about which one survives the monsoon.

faqs.question: How does society gate access work for a weekly home tutor?
faqs.answer: Set it up once as a standing arrangement rather than as a visitor each week. In most Thane complexes, including the larger developments here, that means the resident initiates the entry, the tutor carries photo identification matching the name on the profile, and the same day and time repeats so the security desk recognises the pattern. Tell us at the matching stage if your building requires pre-registration a day ahead, caps visitor hours, or restricts entry during society events, because those rules change which tutors can realistically commit. Lessons themselves happen wherever the family prefers: a dining table, a study, or a society reading room.

faqs.question: My daughter moves from IGCSE to the Diploma Programme next year. Should we start tuition now?
faqs.answer: Starting in the final IGCSE term is usually better value than starting in Diploma Programme year one. The handover is where students lose ground: a child who succeeded at IGCSE through organisation and past papers meets Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay, and six subjects each wanting an Internal Assessment written to unfamiliar criteria. A few sessions before the switch can sort out the subject and level choices, which is the decision with the longest consequences, and build the independent reading habit the Diploma Programme assumes. Once Diploma Programme year one starts, a tutor is working around deadlines instead of ahead of them.

faqs.question: Is online tuition genuinely as good as a tutor at the dining table for MYP?
faqs.answer: For Middle Years Programme students, usually not. Younger students lose more online than older ones, because a large part of the work is starting, staying seated and organising a notebook, and a screen makes all three harder to supervise. Online becomes the better choice when the subject is scarce: a strong Higher Level specialist on a screen beats a nearby generalist in the room, and that trade is worth making. For MYP criterion tasks and early subject confidence, we recommend home sessions first and online as the backup for a flooded road or a travelling tutor, agreed in advance rather than improvised.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What now?
faqs.answer: Treat it as information rather than a failure, and ask three questions before changing anything. Can your child name a specific weakness they could not name four weeks ago? Is homework starting earlier in the evening? Can the tutor name what they are working on and why, in terms that match the school report? If all three answers are no, the match is wrong and we will replace the tutor without an argument. If two are yes and the mark has not moved, that is normal: marks lag understanding by a reporting cycle, and four weeks is diagnosis time rather than results time.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: Tell us in the first two sessions rather than the eighth. Most mismatches are not about competence: the tutor is strong but pitched at the wrong level, or the personality does not land, or the slot was always going to slip. We ask what specifically did not work, because that is what makes the second match better than a reshuffle, and we send fresh profiles rather than defending the first choice. There is no obligation to continue with somebody who is not right for your child, and no useful purpose in waiting for a report to confirm what you already heard from the next room.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both boards in the same household?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking for when the subject is the same. A mathematics specialist who teaches Cambridge Extended and Middle Years Programme criteria can genuinely handle a Year 10 and a Year 8 in one visit, which saves travel and makes a standing slot much easier to sustain. Across different subjects it rarely works well. A person claiming to cover all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 lands with a tutor in Mumbai who is spread too thin to be useful in any of them. Ask which two or three subjects they would defend, and believe the answer.

faqs.question: Which areas around Majiwada do your tutors actually travel to?
faqs.answer: The reliable pool from here is Majiwada itself, Thane West towards the station, Pokhran Road to the south and Kolshet Road out towards the creek. Those four behave as one area because a tutor working in any of them can take work in the others without rebuilding their week. Beyond that, a tutor from Mulund will sometimes cross over for a strong subject match, and we flag that as an exception rather than presenting it as local coverage. We would rather tell you that an area is at the edge of what a tutor can sustain than watch a good arrangement collapse in the monsoon.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but be there for the first one and be in the flat for the early weeks. You are not supervising the teaching; you are checking that questions are being asked and answered, which you can hear from the next room. For younger Primary Years Programme and Middle Years Programme children, having an adult in the house keeps the session from drifting into conversation. By the second term most families are comfortable leaving a Diploma Programme student to it. The practical minimum is that somebody can let the tutor in and that the study space is not the room where the television is on.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 Extended candidate need?
faqs.answer: Two is the usual answer for one subject, and one is enough if the problem is narrow. Two sessions a week lets a tutor teach in the first and check retention in the second, which is where the actual learning happens. Three or more in a single subject usually means something structural is wrong: the tier is wrong, the foundations are missing, or the student is being used as a repository for other people's anxiety. In the exam term, shorter and more frequent beats long and weekly, and that is the point at which switching a session online makes practical sense.

sections.heading: Arranging IB and IGCSE home tuition in Malabar Hill for one household
paragraphs: A single-child request is easy to match. A household with a Year 10 on a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel entry and a Diploma Programme student upstairs is a scheduling problem first and a teaching problem second. The useful first question is therefore not which subjects, but whether you want one tutor across both children or two. Our answer is usually one tutor for two children in the same broad subject area and two tutors when the subjects diverge, because a single visit covering two consecutive hours costs one journey up the hill and one society entry instead of two of each.

What that requires is a tutor genuinely checked on both boards, and we treat those as separate checks rather than one. Teaching Mathematics (0580) to a Year 10 and teaching a Diploma Programme mathematics course to a DP1 student are different jobs with different assessed components, and plenty of competent people do one well and the other adequately. We ask for evidence of recent teaching on each, and we tell you when a candidate is strong on one board and merely serviceable on the other, so the decision stays yours.

Then the practical layer, which on the Malabar Hill ridge is not an afterthought. Two consecutive hours on a fixed evening is a far easier thing for a tutor in Mumbai to protect than two separate visits, because the climb up from Kemps Corner is paid once. We confirm the day, the start time, the building and the visitor registration before a name is introduced, and we write it down. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Malabar Hill covering two children in one sitting is the most stable arrangement available here, and stability is what makes a two-year engagement work.

The first meeting is diagnostic for both children separately, even when one tutor is doing it. Each gets their recent marked work read, each gets asked to attempt something aloud, and each gets a written note. Two notes, not one. We review at four weeks, we do not guarantee grades, and IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named on this page.

sections.heading: Which board is which, and where do they meet?
paragraphs: The International General Certificate of Secondary Education is a two-year pre-sixteen qualification offered by Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel, assessed mostly by written papers at the end with some practical, oral or coursework components along the way. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs three programmes: the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the Diploma Programme (DP), the last of which is a two-year post-sixteen course. They meet at exactly one point, and it is the point families on this ridge care about: Year 11 IGCSE results feed directly into Diploma Programme subject and level choices.

In practice a Malabar Hill household can hold both at once in several ways. One child sits IGCSE while an older sibling is in DP2. One child moves from IGCSE straight into the Diploma Programme at the same school. Or a child does the MYP rather than IGCSE and joins the Diploma Programme from there, which is a different transition with a different shape. A tutor should be able to tell you which of these you are in without you explaining it twice. Most requests for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Malabar Hill come from one of those three households.

The structural differences matter when you hire. IGCSE is subject-by-subject: a weak subject can be worked on in isolation without disturbing anything else. The Diploma Programme is a package, with six subjects, three usually at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and an Internal Assessment (IA) in nearly every subject. Fixing one DP subject in isolation is harder, because the student's problem is often total load rather than that subject.

We will not reproduce paper structures, component weightings or assessment patterns for either board here. Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel and the IB all revise specifications and subject guides on their own cycles, and a figure that was accurate when a sibling sat the course may be wrong for the session your younger child sits. Ask the school for the current specification or subject guide per subject, in writing. A good IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai families keep for years will ask you for the same documents before planning a term.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma Programme jump, subject by subject
paragraphs: The jump is not uniform, and treating it as one general step is why DP1 goes badly for students who sailed through Year 11. In mathematics it is the sharpest: the pace assumes fluency with algebraic manipulation that IGCSE rewarded but did not require at speed, and a student who relied on a calculator through Year 11 feels it within a month. In the sciences the content step is moderate and the assessment step is large, because the Diploma Programme asks for a self-designed investigation rather than a prescribed practical. In the humanities the step is almost entirely about writing: longer, more structured, more explicitly argued.

Languages behave differently again. A student who scored well in a second language at IGCSE may find the Diploma Programme version asks for sustained oral performance and interpretation rather than accuracy on set tasks. This is where families most often discover that the tier or level they were comfortable at does not translate, and it is worth a conversation in Year 11 rather than November of DP1.

The practical consequence for hiring is that the useful tutoring window opens in Year 11 and not in DP1. A tutor working with a Year 11 student in the final months before their written series can, in the same sessions, start building the algebraic fluency or the essay structure the Diploma Programme will demand. That costs nothing extra and removes most of the DP1 shock. All IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Malabar Hill covers can be approached this way, and almost nobody asks for it, because the transition is invisible until it has already happened.

The level decision is the other place where the two boards touch. A strong IGCSE result in a subject is evidence for Higher Level and not proof of fitness for it, because what Higher Level adds is sustained independent work rather than more content. The question to ask is not whether your child can manage Higher Level in one subject but what the three Higher Level subjects together demand in the same fortnight, and whether that fortnight collides with the Extended Essay deadline. Load, not difficulty, is what breaks DP students on this ridge as everywhere else in Mumbai.

sections.heading: One tutor, two children, one climb up the Malabar Hill ridge
paragraphs: Walkeshwar sits directly below the ridge and shares the same schools, which is why most of our matching on this hill starts there. Napean Sea Road runs off the far slope, and Kemps Corner anchors the foot of the climb, where anyone arriving from elsewhere in Mumbai begins the last stretch. Charni Road and Grant Road are the nearest stations on the Western Line, and a tutor off either train still has the ascent in front of them. For a two-child household, that ascent is the whole economic argument for consecutive hours: the journey is the cost, and splitting it across two children halves it.

The wider island is short in distance and slow in practice. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers roughly eight kilometres and can still lose a large part of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, which is why tutors in Mumbai, Maharashtra are matched within the island here rather than brought down from the suburbs. The Coastal Road has helped some north-south runs and Metro Line 3 on the Aqua corridor from Cuffe Parade towards the Bandra Kurla Complex has helped tutors who live further out. Neither has changed the final climb, and a tutor arriving from the Western Suburbs for a two-hour double session will still find July harder than September.

The two-hour double has one real risk, and it is worth naming. The second child gets the tired tutor. Some tutors are honest about this and will not teach two consecutive hours of demanding Higher Level work; others handle it comfortably when the second hour is lighter in kind, such as IGCSE consolidation after Diploma Programme teaching. Ask directly which order they prefer and why, and alternate which child goes first across the term if both hours are heavy.

In towers such as Il Palazzo and Vijay Apartments the entry arrangement is the same whether one child or two is being taught: register the tutor once with the society office as a recurring visitor, with a name, a photograph identity and the fixed day and time. Two children do not need two registrations. Lessons go at a dining table or in a study with the door closed, and a double session needs a room that can be held for two hours without the household needing it back, which is a real consideration in a smaller flat.

sections.heading: Malabar Hill schools that run both boards under one roof
paragraphs: Malabar Hill and Walkeshwar share the Gopi Birla Memorial School and Bombay International School catchment, and for a dual-board household this matters in a specific way: Bombay International School at Babulnath runs both an IGCSE pathway and the IB Diploma Programme, so a family can have two children on two boards in one school, with one set of term dates and two entirely different assessment calendars. Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort takes a further share of these families and runs a comparable dual pathway. A tutor who already works inside one of these schools' cohorts knows how the two calendars interact, which is information no directory listing can advertise.

The practical effect is that pressure arrives twice rather than once. The IGCSE internal examination window and the Diploma Programme internal assessment deadlines do not line up, so a household with children on both boards gets two separate crunch periods in a year rather than one shared one. That is mostly good news, because a tutor's evening is only contested in one of them, but it means the four-week review for one child may land in the other child's worst fortnight. We schedule around that deliberately rather than discovering it.

The academic year has a shape worth planning from. June opens under heavy monsoon, which tests whether a tutor's travel promise is real and is when a local match proves its value. The weeks around Diwali break momentum for both boards and make a natural review point. The turn of the calendar year brings Year 11 mocks and DP2 internal assessment deadlines into roughly the same weeks, and a household with one child in each will feel that month properly. By the final term before the written series, useful new intervention has largely closed for both and the work is technique.

Those school names are local context and nothing more. A tutor may know how a school marks internal work from having taught its students, and should describe it to you in exactly those terms.

sections.heading: Home tuition for two children in Mumbai: how the hour splits
paragraphs: IB and IGCSE home tuition in Malabar Hill is the format that makes a dual-board household workable, because a tutor in the flat can teach two children in sequence and see both sets of written work on the same table. That is not a convenience; it is how a tutor notices that the younger child has the same method problem the older one had two years ago. The cost is rigidity. A travelling tutor serves a limited number of families in an evening, so a two-hour double is a substantial block of their week and a late cancellation is a large loss rather than a small one. Agree the cancellation terms at the start.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Malabar Hill makes sense in narrower circumstances than parents expect. It is right when one child's subject has few local specialists, which happens more often on the Diploma Programme side than the IGCSE side. It is right for short pre-deadline sessions, where travel would exceed teaching. It is right through the worst monsoon weeks. What it cannot do is supervise fresh handwritten working, and a document camera aimed at the page closes most of that gap cheaply.

The combination most dual-board households settle into is one in-person double session a week plus separate short online contacts for whichever child is in a deadline month. That keeps the journey count at one, keeps the tutor, and gives each child a second point of contact in the week when they need it rather than permanently. Through the January crunch, that second contact for the DP2 child is often what keeps an internal assessment draft on the school's own deadline.

One warning specific to the double session. Do not let the younger child's hour become the overflow for the older child's crisis. It happens quietly: a DP2 deadline runs long, the Year 10 hour shrinks to forty minutes, and by the third month the younger child has lost a third of their teaching without anyone deciding it. Fix the two start times, not just the arrival time, and say out loud that both hours are protected.

sections.heading: Can one tutor really be checked for both boards in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Yes, but only as two separate checks, and a parent should insist on seeing them that way. We verify identity once, then evidence of recent teaching for each board and level claimed, then references we telephone ourselves rather than read. A tutor who has prepared Year 11 students for a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel entry and has separately taught a Diploma Programme course in the same subject is a genuine dual-board tutor. One who has taught the subject in general and is confident about both is not, whatever their qualifications say.

The question that exposes it quickly is about the assessed components. Ask what they would do with a Diploma Programme internal assessment draft, and separately what they would do with an IGCSE practical or coursework component. A real dual-board tutor gives two different answers, because the criteria and the boundaries differ. A generalist gives one answer with the nouns swapped. This takes two minutes and is the single most useful filter available to a parent in Mumbai hiring across boards.

Then ask what they will refuse. On a Diploma Programme internal assessment and on any IGCSE coursework, a tutor helps a student choose an answerable question, teaches the structure the criteria reward, and reads drafts against those criteria. They do not write sections, dictate sentences, supply analysis or source data. That boundary protects your child's academic honesty declaration, which is a far worse thing to lose than a few marks. An answer that sounds like a boundary is the right answer; a vague one is a real risk.

Finally, test for candour. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, quotes a success rate, or treats a predicted grade as something that can be managed. Parents typing best IB and IGCSE tutor in Malabar Hill into a search box are usually after exactly that honesty, and an IB and IGCSE private tutor Malabar Hill neighbours already use should still be put through the same two-board test. A recommendation tells you they are reliable and reach the building. It does not tell you they are strong on both boards.

sections.heading: What changes between Year 11 and Diploma Programme year one?
paragraphs: The workload stops being a list and becomes a system. In Year 11 a student can be behind in one subject and fine in the rest, and the fix is local. In Diploma Programme year one, six subjects, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and an internal assessment in nearly every subject all draw on the same evenings, so being behind in one subject means being behind everywhere within a month. Students who managed IGCSE by working hard the week before a test discover that the method has no DP equivalent, and that discovery usually arrives in the second term.

The second change is that nobody tells you the real deadlines. Schools set internal deadlines for drafts and submissions that sit well ahead of any external date, and those internal dates are the ones that govern a student's life. A family that knows them in September plans a year. A family that hears about them in January manages a crisis. Ask the coordinator for the internal deadline calendar in writing and put it on a wall. It is the single most useful document in a DP household.

The third change is the nature of help. In Year 11, a tutor can teach content and the marks follow. In the Diploma Programme, a tutor's most valuable work is often structural: helping a student sequence three internal assessments and an Extended Essay across a term so that none of them is written in the last fortnight. That is not subject teaching and many excellent subject tutors do not offer it. If your child's problem is load rather than understanding, say so when you enquire, because it changes who we look for.

A double session for two children on one visit is the most efficient configuration there is on this hill, because one journey is paid once. An isolated weekend hour for a single child is the least, so families comparing quotes for IB and IGCSE home classes in Malabar Hill should compare configurations rather than hourly figures. No honest platform publishes one number across all that, and anybody who does is quoting an average that fits nobody.

sections.heading: What does progress look like when two children share a tutor?
paragraphs: It looks like two separate conversations, and if you are only getting one, something is being neglected. At four weeks each child should have a named diagnosis in concrete terms, each should be able to say what they are working on without prompting, and the two start times should not have drifted. Ask for the tutor's read on each child separately, in writing if that is easier. A tutor who talks about the household rather than the children is managing a slot rather than teaching two students.

At one term the signals differ by board, which is useful. The IGCSE child should be losing fewer avoidable marks on past papers: units carried through, working shown, the right command word answered. The Diploma Programme child should be producing drafts that come back with structural comments rather than content corrections, and should be sequencing work across weeks rather than nights. Those are different kinds of improvement and they arrive on different timescales, which is why one review date for both children is usually a mistake.

Across a full examination cycle the honest range is wide for both boards. Technique problems respond quickly. Conceptual gaps respond slowly and durably. Load problems in the Diploma Programme respond to structure rather than to teaching, and sometimes not at all if the subject combination was wrong from the start. We do not guarantee grades for either child, we publish no success rate, and anyone in this market quoting one has invented it. What we commit to is verified tutors, a protected slot for each child, and an honest review. That is the deal on every IB and IGCSE home tutor in Malabar Hill we place, and on every home tuition arrangement we set up elsewhere in Mumbai.

If the match works for one child and not the other, say so and do not compromise. The common and wrong response is to keep a tutor who is excellent with the Diploma Programme student and merely adequate with the Year 10, because changing feels disruptive. Splitting into two tutors costs a second journey and a second gate entry and is frequently the right call. We re-shortlist for one child while leaving the other arrangement untouched, using the existing diagnostic note so the replacement starts informed.

That calendar is the document that most changes what a tutor plans, and almost no family produces it at a first meeting.

Read both notes. Ask one question about each. If the two notes read identically, that is information: a tutor who has genuinely diagnosed two children will not produce the same paragraph twice.

faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is usually the best arrangement on this ridge. faqs.answer: No, one registration covers the tutor regardless of how many children they teach in the visit. faqs.question: When should we start preparing for the Diploma Programme jump?
faqs.answer: In Year 11, well before the written series, and almost nobody does. A tutor working with a Year 11 student can build the algebraic fluency, the longer essay structure or the independent investigation habits the Diploma Programme will demand inside the sessions already happening, at no extra cost. Starting in DP1 means doing that remedial work while six new subjects, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are all arriving at once. The transition is invisible until it has already gone wrong, which is why it is worth raising early.

faqs.question: My child did well at IGCSE. Does that mean Higher Level is safe?
faqs.answer: It is evidence, not proof. A strong IGCSE result shows the subject is within reach; what Higher Level adds is sustained independent work rather than extra content, and that is a different capacity. The better question is what your child's three Higher Level subjects together demand in the same fortnight, and whether that fortnight collides with the Extended Essay deadline. Load breaks more Diploma Programme students than difficulty does, and the combination is decided in a couple of weeks that deserve more thought than they usually get.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to hire one tutor for both children than two specialists?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because the journey is paid once, but it is only worth it if the tutor is genuinely strong on both boards. Ask them separately what they would do with a Diploma Programme internal assessment draft and with an IGCSE practical or coursework component. Two different answers means a real dual-board tutor. One answer with the nouns swapped means you are buying a saving at the cost of one child's teaching, which almost always turns out to be the more expensive option by the end of the year.

faqs.question: How do two different assessment calendars work in one household?
faqs.answer: They mostly do not overlap, which is the good news, and they create two separate crunch periods instead of one. The IGCSE internal examination window and the Diploma Programme internal assessment deadlines fall at different points, so the tutor's evening is contested in one of them at a time. The planning problem is that one child's four-week review can land in the other child's worst fortnight. Set the two review dates independently rather than together, and ask each school for its internal deadline calendar in writing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor from Worli or Fort keep a two-hour evening slot here?
faqs.answer: A two-hour block is actually easier to protect from a distance than a single hour, because the journey is amortised across more teaching. Even so, a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers about eight kilometres and can still lose much of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at peak, with the climb from Kemps Corner on top. It holds when the evening never moves. We match within the island by default and tell you when we have gone outside that rule.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a dual-board household?
faqs.answer: As a supplement it works well, as the main format less so. The sensible pattern is one in-person double session a week plus separate short online contacts for whichever child is in a deadline month. Online is genuinely strong for a scarce Diploma Programme subject where the island has no specialist, and for a quick review of a marked paper. It is weak at supervising fresh handwritten working, which a document camera largely fixes. Keeping at least one in-person session preserves the thing a double visit is actually for.

faqs.question: The tutor is excellent with my DP child and adequate with my Year 10. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Split into two tutors and accept the second journey. This is the most common compromise families make and the one they regret, because keeping a convenient arrangement that serves one child well quietly costs the other child a year. Tell us and we re-shortlist for the Year 10 alone, leaving the Diploma Programme arrangement untouched and carrying over the existing diagnostic note. The extra journey and the second gate registration cost less than a wasted IGCSE year does.

faqs.question: There has been no progress for one child after a month. What happens?
faqs.answer: Raise it at that child's four-week review and expect a replacement rather than a defence. At four weeks we are looking for a specific named diagnosis, a child who can say what they are working on, and start times that have not drifted. If those are missing for one child, the match is wrong for that child regardless of how the other is doing. We re-shortlist using the first tutor's written note, and you are not asked to justify the request or raise it with the tutor yourself.

faqs.question: Who sets the internal deadlines, and why do they matter more than exam dates?
faqs.answer: The school sets them, and they matter because they are the dates a student actually lives by. Internal deadlines for drafts and submissions sit well ahead of any external date, and in the Diploma Programme they are what determine whether a term is calm or chaotic. A family holding that calendar in September can plan a year; a family hearing about it in January is managing a crisis. Ask the coordinator for it in writing and put it somewhere visible, because a tutor can only plan backwards from dates they know.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with Bombay International School or Gopi Birla Memorial School?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Bombay International School, Gopi Birla Memorial School, Cathedral and John Connon School or any other institution named on this page. They appear here because they define the catchment Malabar Hill and Walkeshwar families live inside and because several of them run both an IGCSE pathway and the IB Diploma Programme under one roof. A tutor may know how a school marks internal work from having taught its students, but nobody here speaks for a school.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram arrange IB and IGCSE home tuition in Malad East for two children?
paragraphs: Usually as two bookings with one schedule, not as one tutor stretched across both boards. The International Baccalaureate (IB) and the International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) are examined differently, marked differently and taught differently, and the number of people genuinely strong in both at the same subject and level is small. What we can do, and what most families here actually want, is place two verified specialists into consecutive slots on the same evening so the flat only has a visitor once. That is what IB and IGCSE home tuition in Malad East means in practice for most households here.

The briefing is a single message covering both children. For each one: board, programme or year group, the two or three subjects losing marks, and the earliest realistic start time after their school bus arrives. Siblings usually get home at different times, so send both. We then build the shortlist around a shared evening window rather than around two independent searches, which is the difference between a workable Tuesday and two inconvenient ones.

Where a single tutor genuinely does serve both children, it is normally at the lower end: a Middle Years Programme (MYP) Year 3 student and an IGCSE Year 9 student doing Mathematics are closer in content than their labels suggest, and a strong Mathematics teacher can run a ninety-minute double with a handover in the middle. That stops working somewhere around Year 10, when the IGCSE papers and the MYP criteria pull apart, and it stops entirely once Higher Level (HL) Diploma Programme (DP) work begins.

If either match is wrong, say so in the first fortnight and the replacement costs nothing. We would rather swap one of two tutors in week two than hold a tidy schedule together while a child drifts. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, publishes no success rates and has no influence over external moderation on either board, which is worth saying plainly before you spend anything.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP, DP and IGCSE: what the two boards ask of a Mumbai family
paragraphs: The two systems ask for different habits, and a household running both has to hold both in mind. IB work is internally assessed in part, continuous, and judged against published criteria that the student is expected to understand and quote. IGCSE work is almost entirely externally examined at the end, so the whole two-year run points at a set of papers marked by someone the student will never meet. A child who is good at one is not automatically good at the other.

On the IB side, the Primary Years Programme runs on units of inquiry and the tutor's job is reasoning and reading rather than content. The Middle Years Programme covers its own Years 1 to 5 across eight subject groups with criterion-referenced marking, and the Year 5 personal project sits at the end. The Diploma Programme is the final two years: six subject groups, three subjects usually at HL and three at Standard Level (SL), each carrying an Internal Assessment (IA), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service.

On the IGCSE side there are two boards under one name. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel use different subject codes, different paper structures and different command word vocabularies, and several Cambridge subjects are entered at Core or Extended with the entry capping the grade range. Get your codes and tier in writing from the school's examinations officer. Confirm current structure for both systems with your school's coordinator or the live subject guides, because boards revise these on their own cycles.

For a family in Malad East the practical consequence is about attention, not prestige. Most families asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects from one tutor in Malad East are trying to simplify a household timetable, and the simplification that actually works is shared scheduling rather than a shared tutor. Two specialists on one evening is simple. One generalist across two boards looks simple and produces two half-served children.
