sections.heading: Where the two boards' subject structures actually diverge
paragraphs: They diverge most sharply in Mathematics and least in the sciences at the lower years. IGCSE Mathematics splits into Core and Extended, with Extended carrying functions, harder trigonometry and more demanding probability that simply do not appear on Core papers. The IB route splits differently, into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at HL and SL, and the choice is about the kind of mathematical thinking a student is suited to rather than about a ceiling. A family moving a child from one system to the other needs to know which gap they are inheriting.

In the sciences the lower years overlap enough that one teacher often serves both children, and then they separate decisively. IGCSE separates into Combined Science or individual Biology, Chemistry and Physics entries, with practical or alternative-to-practical components rewarding precise writing about method, control of variables and error. DP sciences carry an IA built on an individually designed investigation, where the research question has to be narrow enough to answer with school equipment. The IGCSE practical register is excellent preparation for that IA, and families rarely notice the connection.

Languages diverge in the opposite direction. IGCSE first and second language entries are broadly comparable in demand, while the IB Group 1 and Group 2 decision is genuinely consequential: a student who speaks Hindi at home but has never written analytically in it will find Hindi A harder than the timetable suggests, and the Language B route is sometimes the honest call. English is the one subject where work done for either board transfers almost completely, because audience, form and purpose are the same skills under different labels.

The humanities and the arts are where a two-board household feels the workload most. IGCSE History and Geography reward structured source work under time pressure. The equivalent IB subjects want sustained independent writing. Running both in one flat means two very different sets of expectations about what an evening of study looks like, and all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Malad East families book should be sequenced with that in mind rather than treated as interchangeable hours.

sections.heading: One tutor, two boards, four areas: Malad East, Malad West, Goregaon East and Kandivali East
paragraphs: A two-booking household needs tutors from the directions that can hold consecutive slots, and that narrows the map in a useful way. Malad East sits on the Malad East side of the Western Express Highway, with Malad as the nearest station on the Western Line between Bandra and Dahisar, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 serving the same corridor from Dahisar through Andheri to Gundavali. The effect of the highway position is that a tutor can plan a 5.30pm and a 7.15pm arrival on the same road without either becoming a gamble. IB and IGCSE home classes in Malad East are scheduled around that fact rather than around a map.

Kandivali East and Goregaon East are the two directions that make back-to-back scheduling work. Both sit one stop away on the same side of the tracks, both are reached by a clean highway run, and the Goregaon East pool towards the JVLR end is the deepest for IB specialists while the Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel supply spreads more evenly across both. Malad West is the direction that breaks a double booking: the crossing and Link Road traffic make a second consecutive slot unpredictable even when the first one held.

The one thing genuinely true here and not elsewhere in Malad is that tutors quote highway timings rather than Link Road ones, and that an Oberoi International or Thakur International run is quick from this side. That is why a two-child, two-board evening is realistic in Malad East and awkward three hundred metres west. Families who have moved within Malad notice the difference inside a month, usually when a tutor who was reliable at the old address starts arriving late at the new one.

The wider Mumbai rule is the one that explains all of it. A tutor travelling Bandra to Andheri is quick off-peak and painful at 6pm, so matching along the Western Line, Khar to Santacruz or Malad to Kandivali, works far better than matching across it. Parents typing IB and IGCSE tutors near me Malad East into a search box are given a radius when what they need is a corridor, and for a two-booking household the corridor is the only thing that makes the evening fit together.

sections.heading: Which Mumbai schools run both pathways, and why does that matter at Year 11?
paragraphs: Several schools families here use offer IGCSE through Year 11 and the Diploma Programme afterwards, which is exactly why the two-board household is so common in this part of Mumbai. Children in Malad East are mostly at Witty International School, Oberoi International School or Thakur International School. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Witty International School, Oberoi International School, Thakur International School or any other school named here; we name them as local context because their calendars set every deadline a tutor plans around.

The two calendars collide in specific months and that collision is the planning problem. March and April bring IGCSE pre-boards and end-of-year examinations at the same time as DP mocks and the final run of IA deadlines. The winter break carries DP2 IA drafting on one side and IGCSE past-paper work on the other. A household with one child in each system has two sets of pressure in the same fortnight and one dining table, which is a scheduling problem long before it is an academic one.

June and July are the quiet window on both sides and almost nobody uses them. For an IGCSE Year 10 student those weeks are when method can still be rebuilt rather than patched. For an IB student they are when the previous year's gaps can be closed without a deadline in the way. Scarce specialists on both boards in the Western Suburbs are committed by late July in most years, so a family booking in October is choosing from whoever is left on a Thursday.

Bus times decide the shape of the evening. From the highway side of Malad East the school runs are quick, but siblings at different schools still arrive home twenty or forty minutes apart, and that gap is what makes a consecutive-slot arrangement possible or impossible. Send both arrival times when you brief us. It is the single most useful piece of logistical information a two-child household can give.

sections.heading: Can home tuition in Mumbai cover both boards in the same week?
paragraphs: Yes, and the practical shape is two home visits on one evening rather than four visits across a week. A tutor at the table is the right default on both boards because the work being assessed is written, and watching a student write is how a tutor finds the habit costing them marks. For an IGCSE student that is paper technique under time pressure. For an IB student it is criteria language and IA method. Both need observation rather than description, which is why home tuition in Mumbai stays the default on both boards.

The honest trade-off for a two-board household is that presence costs travel and travel costs reliability twice over. Two tutors means two journeys and two chances of a 6.45pm phone call. This is why the direction matters more than the distance here: a Kandivali East and a Goregaon East tutor on the same highway are two reliable journeys, while adding a Malad West tutor to the same evening introduces the weak link. Count lessons that happened rather than lessons booked, and the pattern becomes obvious by October.

Online earns a place on both boards for specific reasons. On the IB side it is scarce HL subjects, where an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Malad East may be the only genuine specialist available. On the IGCSE side it is marking turnaround and the exam-leave weeks, when short daily sessions and a script marked the same evening beat a weekly visit. A mixed household often ends up with the younger child at the table and the older one on a screen, which looks inconsistent and is correct.

Online is the wrong choice for a Year 8 or Year 9 student who cannot yet begin work unprompted, on either board, and we would rather say so than take the booking. The arrangement most two-board families in Mumbai settle into by the second term is one supervised visit each per week plus one shared online marking session, which survives the monsoon and the collision month in a way four weekly visits does not.

sections.heading: What IB Gram verifies when a tutor claims both boards in Malad East
paragraphs: Dual-board claims get the closest scrutiny we apply, because they are the easiest thing to overstate and the hardest for a parent to test. Every tutor has had identity and qualification documents verified, and for anyone presenting as a both-boards teacher we confirm which board, which subject and which level they have actually taught, year by year, rather than accepting a combined claim. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Malad East parents find through a building group has usually had none of this checked and may be entirely credible, which is precisely the problem.

What verification cannot settle is fit with a particular child, and in a two-child household there are two fits to get right. A tutor who suits a focused sixteen-year-old may be wrong for a distractible twelve-year-old, and the same household often needs two quite different temperaments. We treat a mismatch as our error rather than the tutor's and replace without a fee, which matters more when you are coordinating two bookings. Every IB and IGCSE home tutor in Malad East we place is reviewed in writing at four weeks for exactly this reason.

Run these checks on the call yourself. Ask which board and level they taught last year and the year before, separately rather than together. Ask an IB candidate to explain how they would narrow a Sciences IA research question. Ask an IGCSE candidate to distinguish two command words with an example. Ask both what they will send you after four weeks. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade on either board, because external examiners and moderators award grades and no tutor sits in that process.

Then ask the Mumbai question, twice. Where do you live, which route will you take, and what time would you leave to arrive by 6.30pm. If you are running consecutive slots, ask each tutor whether a 5.30pm or a 7.15pm start suits their journey better and build the evening around the honest answer. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects across Mumbai does not exist, so a candidate claiming every subject on both boards has told you something useful about their general precision.

sections.heading: What happens in the handover from IGCSE Year 11 to DP Year 12?
paragraphs: Three things change at once, and the summer between the two years is the only cheap time to address them. First, assessment stops being a single terminal set of papers and becomes continuous, with internal assessments running alongside teaching from the first term. Second, the student is expected to understand the criteria they are marked against and to use that vocabulary themselves, which no IGCSE paper ever required. Third, independent extended writing arrives in the form of the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, and nothing in Year 11 trained anyone for it.

The students who struggle most are usually the strong IGCSE performers, which surprises every family it happens to. A student who scored well by mastering paper technique has learned to produce a short, tightly-shaped answer against a mark scheme. That skill is nearly useless for an IA, where the marks come from a well-chosen question, a defensible method and honest evaluation across several thousand words. The habit that produced the good IGCSE result actively gets in the way for the first term of DP.

A worked example makes it concrete. Take a student who finished IGCSE Chemistry comfortably and begins HL Chemistry. Their first IA proposal is a textbook experiment with a variable the school's equipment cannot control properly, written up in the compact style that earned marks on an IGCSE structured question. The tutor's work in that first term is not content at all. It is teaching the student to narrow a question until it is answerable, to justify a method rather than describe it, and to write at a length they have never been asked for.

The practical plan is six to eight weeks of bridging work across the summer and the first term, covering criteria vocabulary, one short piece of extended independent writing, and the mathematical or practical gaps specific to the subjects chosen. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Malad East is often at its most valuable precisely here, in a window with no deadlines in it. Parents searching best IB and IGCSE tutor in Malad East in September are usually a term late for the thing that would have helped most.

sections.heading: What IB and IGCSE home classes in Mumbai should show by the second month
paragraphs: By four weeks you should see behaviour change on both boards, and the signals differ by system. For the IGCSE child, open the book and look for separated scoring points, visible working and the ability to say what a command word wants before writing. For the IB child, listen for criteria language used unprompted and the ability to explain why an answer that was factually correct did not score. A parent with no subject knowledge can test both of these at dinner, which is why they are the right tests.

By one term the marks should move and the movement should be explainable in each system's own terms. On the IGCSE side, name the paper section that improved. On the IB side, name the criterion. If a number has risen but nobody can identify what changed, treat it as an easier assessment rather than progress. If nothing has moved after a full term of sessions that actually happened, the issue is the match, the diagnosis or the frequency, and more hours will solve none of them.

Across a full cycle the honest statement is the same on both boards: tutoring changes the slope and earlier starts compound. Two years of marked work and corrected method is a different thing from a mock season, however good the tutor. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, publishes no success rates, and has no influence over external examination or moderation on either board. Any tutor quoting you a figure has invented it.

The limits are worth stating in a household running two systems, because the temptation to over-schedule is strongest there. Tuition will not install two missing years of Mathematics in six weeks, will not replace the reading and writing done between visits, and cannot move a closed Core entry into the Extended grade range. What two reviewed runs of home tuition in Mumbai reliably do is stop two children competing for the same hour of adult attention, which in a two-board family is half the actual problem.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach my IB child and my IGCSE child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes below Year 10, rarely after it. A Middle Years Programme Year 3 student and an IGCSE Year 9 student doing Mathematics are closer in content than their labels suggest, and a strong Mathematics teacher can run a ninety-minute double with a handover in the middle. Once IGCSE paper technique and Middle Years Programme criteria pull apart, and certainly once Higher Level Diploma Programme work starts, two specialists do better. What usually solves the real problem is shared scheduling rather than a shared tutor: two verified people in consecutive slots on one evening.

faqs.question: Can two tutors visit our building on the same evening, back to back?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Malad East it works better than in most of the Western Suburbs. Because this side feeds the Western Express Highway directly, a tutor can hold a 5.30pm and another a 7.15pm arrival on the same road without either becoming a gamble. Keep both tutors on the same highway direction, Kandivali East or Goregaon East, and the evening holds. Add a Malad West tutor to the sequence and the crossing becomes the weak link. Put both names on the standing visitor list so the gate is not renegotiated twice a week.

faqs.question: My child finished IGCSE well but is struggling in Diploma Programme term one. Why?
faqs.answer: Because strong IGCSE technique actively hinders the first Internal Assessment. A student who scored well learned to produce short, tightly-shaped answers against a mark scheme. An Internal Assessment rewards a well-chosen question, a defensible method and honest evaluation over several thousand words, which is a different craft. The fix is not more content. It is six to eight weeks of work on narrowing a research question, justifying rather than describing a method, and writing at unfamiliar length. The summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is the cheapest time to do it.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be home when two tutors are visiting?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat for both sessions, though not in either room. The useful habit is catching the last five minutes of each, when the tutor states what was covered and what the child must do before the next visit. In a two-child household that handover is also how you stop the two sets of homework colliding on the same evening. By Diploma Programme level the fortnightly written review carries more information than any doorstep summary, and hovering during timed work makes the writing worse.

faqs.question: Which months are hardest for a family running both boards?
faqs.answer: March and April, without much competition. IGCSE pre-boards and end-of-year examinations land at the same time as Diploma Programme mocks and the last run of Internal Assessment deadlines, so one household has two sets of pressure in the same fortnight and one dining table. The winter break is the second pinch point, carrying Internal Assessment drafting on one side and past-paper work on the other. Plan the term before each of those, and use June and July, which are quiet on both boards and almost universally wasted.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel matter if we are heading into the Diploma Programme anyway?
faqs.answer: They matter for the next two years and barely at all afterwards. The two boards use different subject codes, paper structures and command word vocabularies, so the past papers your child practises on have to match their actual entry; a year of the wrong board's papers is the most expensive avoidable error in Year 10. Get the codes in writing from the examinations officer. What carries forward into the Diploma Programme is the writing discipline and the practical register, not the board name, and the practical register transfers unusually well.

faqs.question: Our society needs a gate pass for each visitor. How do two weekly tutors work?
faqs.answer: Put both names on the standing visitor list for their fixed weekly times rather than registering each lesson. Buildings in this part of Mumbai will usually allow it for recurring bookings once a resident asks, and with two tutors the saving is twenty minutes a week rather than ten, which across a school year is a meaningful number of lessons. Tell both tutors which gate to use and whether a photo identity record is needed. If the second tutor arrives while the first is still inside, warn the gate so nobody is turned away.

faqs.question: Is online tuition sensible for one child and home tuition for the other?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it looks inconsistent while being correct. The younger child who still needs an adult in the room to begin work belongs at the table. The older one taking a scarce Higher Level subject, or running through IGCSE exam leave where short daily sessions and same-evening marking matter more than presence, may be better served online. sections.heading: From IGCSE Year 11 into IB DP1: what actually changes?
paragraphs: Three things change at once, which is why the first term of DP1 unsettles students who sailed through IGCSE. The first is the shape of the question. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel papers reward a well-structured answer to a defined task; a Diploma Programme paper more often asks a student to select an approach, justify it and evaluate the result. A student trained to answer exactly what is asked suddenly has to decide what is being asked. That is a skill, it is teachable, and nobody teaches it in the summer between the two. Every Mumbai school we deal with assumes the student will work it out alone.

The second is internal assessment. IGCSE coursework, where a subject carries it, is a defined task with a clear brief. The Diploma Programme asks for an Internal Assessment (IA) in nearly every subject, an Extended Essay (EE) of the student's own design and Theory of Knowledge (TOK), all running alongside six subjects. A DP1 student is now managing long independent work with distant deadlines, having spent two years managing short tasks with near ones. The students who struggle in DP1 are rarely the weaker ones; they are the ones who were well organised inside a structure that has been removed.

The third is level. Three Higher Level (HL) subjects and three Standard Level (SL) subjects replace a flat set of IGCSE courses, and Higher Level is a genuine step up in both content and expected independence. A student who scored well in IGCSE Mathematics can still find Higher Level mathematics a different activity. This is where honest advice in the first term is worth more than a year of tutoring later, and where a tutor who has taught both systems is genuinely more useful than two who have each taught one.

What this means practically is that the transition deserves its own short piece of work rather than being left to resolve itself. Six to eight weeks over the break and into the first term, aimed at question-reading, at starting independent work early, and at the specific HL subject most likely to bite. Families who do that do not need a crisis intervention in February. The IB and IGCSE home tutor in Malad West arrangements we make for transition students are usually short and front-loaded rather than year-long.

sections.heading: Choosing Diploma Programme subjects from IGCSE results
paragraphs: Read the IGCSE result as information about how a subject was learned, not only about how well. A student who scored highly in Cambridge Mathematics because they are quick and accurate with routine procedures is a different candidate for Higher Level mathematics than one who scored the same mark by solving unfamiliar problems slowly. The first will find Higher Level a shock and Standard Level comfortable; the second may be fine at Higher Level despite a less impressive paper. A tutor who taught the student through IGCSE can tell you which you have, which is one reason to keep the same tutor across the transition where the subject allows it. Few families in Mumbai think of continuity as a reason to hire early, and it is one of the better ones.

The science choice carries the most regret. An IGCSE student who enjoyed the practical component and found the theory heavy going will meet a Diploma Programme science where the Internal Assessment is an investigation they must design and defend, which plays to exactly that strength. The reverse student, strong on recall and uncomfortable with open-ended design, often does better at Standard Level than at Higher Level even with a strong IGCSE grade. Neither of those is visible from a certificate, and both are visible to a tutor who has watched the child work for a term.

Language choices are the ones families here get wrong most often, because the Diploma Programme language requirement is structurally different from an IGCSE language course. A second language taken casually at IGCSE becomes a two-year commitment with its own assessed components, and a student who has been coasting will feel it in DP1. Ask the school's coordinator what the pathway is for your child specifically, and verify anything structural against the current subject guide rather than against what a sibling did three years ago, since the IB and the boards revise their guides on their own cycles.

For a family asking what all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Malad West coverage means at this moment, the practical answer is advice before teaching. Two sessions spent on subject selection with someone who knows both systems is worth more than twenty sessions spent repairing a bad choice. We will match for that conversation alone if that is all you need, and we will say so if we think you do not need a tutor yet.

sections.heading: Does home tuition work when two children sit different boards?
paragraphs: Yes, and it is usually the format that makes a two-board household manageable rather than the one that complicates it. Home tuition means the tutors come to one address, which removes two sets of journeys from your week and keeps both children in the same study space with the same rules. The alternative, sending one child to a class on Link Road and the other somewhere else, consumes more of a parent's evening than any tutoring arrangement. The home classes in Mumbai we arrange for two-board families are generally built as one shared evening rather than two separate ones.

The honest constraint is space. Two children, two tutors and one dining table does not work, and nor does one child being taught in the room where the other is supposed to be revising. If your flat has only one usable surface, place the tutors back to back rather than in parallel, and give the waiting child something to do that is not in that room. We ask about study space on the first call because the answer determines whether a shared evening is realistic or whether two separate evenings are the lesser evil.

Online earns its place differently for each child. For the Diploma Programme student it works well: an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Malad West arrangement can deliver IA feedback, paper technique and marked work with no loss, and for a scarce Higher Level subject it may be the only way to reach the right specialist. For a Year 9 or Year 10 student it works less well, because that student needs someone to notice they have stopped writing. If you are going to run one child online and one in person, run the older one on the screen. That holds across Mumbai and it holds in a two-bedroom flat in Malad West in particular.

Hybrid is the practical landing place, and in a two-board household it also solves the diary. One in-person session each per week on the shared evening, plus one online session for whichever child is closer to a deadline. During the October cluster the online hour goes to the DP child; during January it goes to the IGCSE child. That flexibility is the main argument for keeping both arrangements with one coordinator rather than hiring the two tutors separately through different channels.

sections.heading: How do you check a tutor who claims to teach both boards?
paragraphs: Ask for specifics on each board separately and compare the two answers. Which syllabus codes have you taught on Cambridge or Edexcel, and in which years? Which IB programme and which level, and when? Where do students lose marks in each system, and how do your lessons differ between them? A tutor with real experience of both will answer the third question with obvious differences, because the two jobs feel different to teach. A tutor who has taught one and read about the other will produce a general answer about conceptual clarity, and you will hear it immediately.

There is a legitimate version of the dual-board tutor and it is worth knowing what it looks like. Mathematics and the sciences carry enough common ground that a teacher who has taught Cambridge mathematics for years can teach Standard Level Diploma mathematics competently, and the reverse. What transfers much less well is anything assessment-specific: Internal Assessment supervision, Extended Essay guidance, Theory of Knowledge, and the particular habits of each board's examiners. Hire the dual-board tutor for teaching content across your two children. Do not hire them to supervise an IA on the strength of their IGCSE record.

On our side the checks are identical for both halves of the household: government photo identification matched to the person attending, a degree in the subject rather than a general qualification, a teaching history naming board, programme, level and years, and references we contact ourselves. The standard does not drop because a household in Mumbai wants one hire instead of two. We will not list a tutor as dual-board unless both halves of that history check out, which is why our shortlists for two-board families are often two different people.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade on either board, or who quotes a success rate. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and the outcome rests on two years of each child's own work. What a good tutor will commit to is a written diagnosis after the first session with each child, a named target for four weeks, and marked work you can read. In a two-child arrangement, insist on that reporting separately for each child, because the commonest failure in a shared evening is that the quieter child's progress stops being discussed.

sections.heading: The first term of DP1 in Mumbai after an IGCSE Year 11
paragraphs: Here is what that term looks like from the inside, because it is the single most common reason a Malad West family calls us naming both boards. September is deceptive: content is introductory, the student is pleased to be in the Diploma Programme, and the work feels manageable. October is when the three Higher Level subjects reveal their depth at the same time as the first Internal Assessment is mentioned and Theory of Knowledge starts asking questions that have no retrievable answer. November brings the first proper assessments. A student who topped an IGCSE cohort can come home with a grade four and no explanation they find acceptable.

The diagnosis is almost always one of three things, and they need different work. Either the student cannot yet handle a question that does not tell them what to do, which is question-reading and takes a few weeks of guided practice on past paper material. Or they cannot plan long independent work, which is a scheduling and drafting problem and needs a tutor who will sit with them and break an Internal Assessment into dated steps. Or a Higher Level subject is genuinely the wrong choice, which needs to be identified in the first term while a change is still administratively possible rather than in April when it is not.

What makes the third case painful is that families treat a level change as a failure, and schools are sometimes slow to raise it. It is not a failure. A student carrying three Higher Level subjects badly produces a worse diploma and a worse year than one carrying two Higher Level subjects well. An honest tutor will tell you which case you are in after four to six weeks, with evidence from marked work rather than an opinion. A tutor who reassures you through the whole of the first term is not helping, and the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Malad West for a transition student is the one willing to have that conversation early.

On cost, the transition period is usually front-loaded and then light, which is worth saying because families budget for it as if it were year-long. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Malad West depend on the level, on subject scarcity, on travel and on session length, and a Higher Level science specialist costs more than general support anywhere in Mumbai. The common shape for a transition is two sessions a week for the first six to eight weeks, then one, then fortnightly maintenance once the student is managing their own deadlines. We do not publish a price list, and any quote offered before the subjects and levels are known is a guess.

sections.heading: What should four weeks of home tuition in Malad West change?
paragraphs: In a two-board household, ask the question separately for each child, because the answers look different. For the IGCSE child at four weeks you want precision: they can name the specific loss rather than the subject, they are attempting questions they used to leave blank, and marked work has come back to you. For the Diploma Programme child at four weeks you want structure: an Internal Assessment broken into dated steps, a first draft of something, and evidence that they have started reading questions before answering them rather than after.

By the end of a term the two diverge further. The IGCSE child should show movement on the targeted question types, usually the structured questions before the open ones, and usually the practical paper before the theory. The DP child may show no mark movement at all and still be in much better shape, because the first term of the Diploma Programme is about building working habits whose payoff arrives in the mock series. Judging a DP1 student by November marks alone is the most common mistake we see parents make, and it leads to tutors being changed when the arrangement was working.

Across a full year, the fair test for both children is whether the subject and level set is right. For the IGCSE child that is the tier question. For the DP child it is the Higher Level question. A good tutor raises both unprompted and brings marked work to the conversation. The uncomfortable version of this conversation is the valuable one, and a tutor who only ever reports progress is managing you.

The limits are the same for both halves of the household. Tutoring cannot fix attendance, cannot reconstruct two years of a syllabus in six weeks, and does not work on a student who has not agreed to it. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. What a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families hire can reliably supply is a diagnosis you can read, a plan you can check, and marked work that shows whether the plan is working.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach my Year 10 IGCSE son and my DP1 daughter?
faqs.answer: For mathematics, often yes. For anything assessment-specific, no. The content overlap between Cambridge mathematics and Standard Level Diploma mathematics is real enough that a strong teacher can carry both, and that arrangement saves you a second evening. Internal Assessment supervision, Extended Essay guidance and Theory of Knowledge are different work entirely, and a tutor whose record is in IGCSE should not be supervising a DP investigation. We will propose a single tutor where it genuinely holds and two where it does not, rather than giving you the convenient answer.

faqs.question: Can both tutors come to our building on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Usually, if both are based inside the Malad, Kandivali and Goregaon band. We schedule them back to back rather than in parallel so one study space serves both lessons, and we check the two journeys against each other so the second tutor is not arriving while the first is still teaching. Where one tutor has to travel from Andheri or further, a shared evening becomes fragile and we will tell you that upfront rather than discovering it in week three. Protecting one evening instead of two is usually worth a small compromise on the hour.

faqs.question: My daughter got good IGCSE grades and is struggling in DP1. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always one of three things, and they need different fixes. She may not yet handle questions that do not tell her what to do, which is question-reading and takes a few weeks of guided past paper work. She may not be able to plan long independent work, which is what the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay demand and what IGCSE never required. Or a Higher Level subject may be the wrong choice, which needs identifying in the first term while a change is still possible. Good IGCSE grades do not predict which of the three you have.

faqs.question: Is the IGCSE to DP jump the same for every subject?
faqs.answer: No, and the sciences and mathematics are where it is felt hardest. In those subjects Higher Level adds both depth and an expectation of independent investigation, so a student who was accurate and quick at IGCSE can still find the new work unfamiliar. Languages change structurally rather than in difficulty, with their own assessed components over two years. Humanities often feel the most continuous. Ask your school's coordinator about the pathway for each specific subject and check the current guide, since the IB revises subject guides on its own cycle.

faqs.question: What do fees depend on when we need two tutors?

A Higher Level science specialist for the DP child costs more than general support for the IGCSE child, which is the usual shape of a two-board household's spend. Travel is priced in, so two tutors from inside the Malad and Kandivali band cost less in total than one local tutor and one from Bandra. faqs.question: Our society requires a gate pass per visitor. Does that complicate two tutors?
faqs.answer: Slightly, and it is worth doing once properly. Register both tutors as recurring visitors in the same written request to your building, with names and numbers exactly as they appear on their identification, and keep the slots at the same hours each week so security learns the pattern. Buildings along this corridor generally accommodate standing weekly lessons without difficulty. The failure we see is a family registering one tutor and forgetting the second, which produces a twenty-minute delay on an evening that was already tightly scheduled.

faqs.answer: No, and we will say so. Plenty of households hire for the child in difficulty and then add the sibling out of fairness, which usually produces a reluctant student and a wasted hour. Hire for a named problem. If the younger child has no diagnosable gap, the better use of the same money is a few sessions of subject or tier advice before their choices are locked in, which is cheap and prevents the expensive problem two years later. Fairness between siblings is not a teaching objective.

faqs.question: Which board is better for my children?
faqs.answer: Neither, and anyone who answers that question confidently is selling something. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE courses suit students who do well with defined tasks and clear mark schemes. The Diploma Programme suits students who can manage long independent work and enjoy being asked to justify a position. Most students can do well in either with the right support. The useful question is which system suits this particular child's working habits, and a tutor who has taught both can give you a grounded view of that in two sessions.

faqs.question: Are you affiliated with Witty International School or Billabong High International School?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching service with no affiliation to Witty International School, Billabong High International School, the IB Organization, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. We name local campuses because their calendars decide when each of your children comes under pressure, and because a tutor should know which school each child attends. Any tutor who implies they represent a school, or offers to obtain internal material from one, should be declined and reported to us.

faqs.question: When is the best time to start if we are planning for a transition year?
faqs.answer: The weeks after IGCSE papers finish and before DP1 begins, which is the most useful and least used window in the whole two years. sections.heading: What changes when a student moves from IGCSE into the Diploma Programme?
paragraphs: Almost everything about how work is produced, and very little about the content. IGCSE rewards a student who can answer a short structured question accurately against a published mark scheme. The Diploma Programme (DP) rewards a student who can sustain an argument, design an investigation, and manage long pieces of independent work across two years. A Year 11 student with excellent paper technique can arrive in DP1 and struggle immediately, and nothing about their IGCSE grades predicts it.

The specific shocks are consistent. Six subjects split between Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) rather than eight or nine at a single standard. Internal assessments that are individual pieces of work with no model answer. The Extended Essay (EE), which requires choosing a question nobody has set. Theory of Knowledge (TOK), which has no content to revise in the familiar sense. Deadlines set by the school months in advance, with no weekly test to make the student keep up.

A tutor who has taught both sides of that boundary is worth seeking out for exactly one year. They know that the IGCSE habit of waiting for the teacher to say what will be examined is the single biggest handicap in DP1, and they can name it rather than treating the student as suddenly lazy. Families asking for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Manpada during this year are usually buying the translation, not extra content.

The reverse transition matters less often but does happen, when a student moves school or board mid-stage. Here the risk is content sequencing rather than habits: two boards cover the same topics in different orders, so a transferring student can have a genuine hole in the middle of a subject that nobody has noticed because they are performing acceptably elsewhere. An all IB and IGCSE subjects IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor Mumbai search often starts with precisely this discovery.

sections.heading: Which subjects transfer across the two boards, and which do not?
paragraphs: Mathematics transfers best, in the sense that a strong IGCSE mathematician usually copes with Standard Level and often with Higher Level, provided algebraic fluency is genuine rather than calculator-assisted. The sciences transfer unevenly: content overlaps heavily while the investigative component is a different kind of task entirely, and a student who scored well on structured science questions may have no experience of designing an inquiry. English transfers least predictably, because analytical writing at Diploma Programme level asks for a sustained reading rather than a correct one.

Within IGCSE itself, tier placement is the fact that governs everything else. Where a subject offers two tiers, the one your child is entered at caps the available grade however well the paper goes, and the decision is taken at school earlier than most families notice. If the cap is going to matter for a Diploma Programme application, the conversation with the subject teacher belongs at the end of Year 10, with recent marked work in hand, not in Year 11.

Internal and coursework components exist on both boards and are the part of the qualification a tutor can genuinely influence, because the student gets more than one pass at understanding the task. Science investigations, mathematical explorations, language oral work, business and economics commentaries, and the IGCSE practical or speaking components all reward structure and planning. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Manpada may be asked to cover, these are the hours with the clearest return.

We name papers and skills and no structures here. Component weightings, mark totals and paper timings are revised by the IB, by Cambridge International Education and by Pearson Edexcel on their own cycles, so the current subject guide or syllabus and your school's coordinator are the only reliable sources for the year your child sits. Be cautious of anybody quoting a weighting from memory in a first meeting, because it means the specification has not been opened recently.

sections.heading: Why the Year 11 to DP1 summer is the cheapest tutoring you will ever buy
paragraphs: Because a few hours before the Diploma Programme starts prevents a term of damage once it has. The students who struggle most in DP1 are rarely weak; they are students who were excellent at a system that told them what to learn, dropped into one that does not. Six or eight sessions across the gap between the IGCSE series and the start of DP1 can establish how an internal assessment is actually marked, what an inquiry question looks like, and how to plan work that has no weekly test attached.

The content side of that bridge is narrow and specific. For mathematics it is algebraic fluency without a calculator, because Standard Level and Higher Level both assume it and IGCSE practice often hides the gap. For the sciences it is uncertainty, data handling and the structure of an investigation, none of which a structured IGCSE paper requires. For English it is the move from finding the correct reading to defending one reading well. Each is teachable in a handful of focused hours.

The habits side matters more and is almost never addressed. A DP1 student has to start a piece of work that is due in four months, which no part of IGCSE trained them to do. A tutor working that summer can set one long task with interim deadlines and let the student experience the failure to start in a context where it costs nothing. That single rehearsal is worth more than any amount of content revision done in the same hours.

There is a local reason to do this in the summer rather than in September on this particular road. Once term begins, the evening slot on Ghodbunder Road is contested, the school load is real, and a 7pm start through Manpada traffic is unreliable. In June and early July, daytime and late-morning sessions are available, tutors have capacity, and the work is unhurried. Families here who use that window arrive in DP1 with the translation already done, and it is the one piece of advice we repeat to every Mumbai household at this stage.

sections.heading: IGCSE to Diploma Programme: what actually carries over?
paragraphs: Content carries over generously and habits barely carry at all, which is the single most useful thing a dual-board tutor can tell a parent. A student who has finished an IGCSE science arrives in the Diploma Programme knowing most of the first term's material. What they do not arrive with is the habit of writing against published criteria, of designing their own investigation rather than following a method sheet, or of defending a judgement in prose. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel both train a student to answer the question in front of them extremely well. The Diploma Programme then asks them to decide what the question should be.

Mathematics is the clearest case of the gap. A strong Extended-tier student has fluent algebra and reliable technique, and meets a programme where marks depend on justifying each step and on writing an extended exploration of a self-chosen topic. The technique transfers; the explanation does not, because nobody asked for explanation before. The same pattern appears in the languages, where a student who has handled set-text questions comfortably now faces oral and written tasks on texts they must interpret rather than summarise.

In the other direction, a child moving from an IB middle-years classroom into an IGCSE year group has the opposite adjustment. They are used to being marked against criteria that reward process, and they meet a paper that rewards the correct answer in the available marks and nothing else. Both transitions take roughly a term to settle, and both are much easier with somebody at the table who has taught both sides. This is where IB and IGCSE home tuition earns its keep on this corridor, and it is why we weight dual experience so heavily when we shortlist.

sections.heading: Subject choice twice over: Core or Extended, then HL or SL
paragraphs: A dual-board household makes the same category of decision twice, four or five years apart, and usually with no joined-up advice. The first is tier: several IGCSE subjects split into a Core route capped lower and an Extended route that reaches the top of the range while asking harder questions. The second is level: in the Diploma Programme three subjects sit at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), and those choices close or keep open university doors two years later. Parents who have been through the first decision assume the second works the same way. It does not.

The useful link between them is evidence rather than ambition. Tier should follow the Year 9 marked papers: losses bunched on the last parts of multi-step questions point to an Extended candidate who needs method discipline, while losses spread evenly including the accessible marks point to Core being the honest call this year. Level should follow a different reading, because HL is not Extended with more hours. HL adds depth, additional topics and a heavier internal assessment load, and a student who coped with Extended by working hard rather than by thinking flexibly often finds three HLs unsustainable.

Every Diploma subject also carries an internal assessment the student designs: a scientific investigation, a mathematical exploration, oral and written tasks on texts, a commentary built from sourced material. Each needs a question narrow enough to answer and data a student can obtain from a flat in Walkeshwar or Nariman Point. Weightings and component structures change on the boards' and the IB's own cycles, so take them from the current subject guide and from your school's coordinator rather than from any tutoring page. Booking all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Marine Drive style for a household making both decisions at once is mostly about getting that evidence read properly.

sections.heading: Two Mumbai school calendars running in one household
paragraphs: Marine Drive addresses are a short drive from both Cathedral in Fort and Bombay International at Babulnath, and that single geographic fact produces most of the requests on this page. Cathedral and John Connon School and Bombay International School each run their own internal calendar of coursework deadlines, practicals, draft dates and mock examinations. Two children at two schools therefore live under two sets of pressure weeks that do not align, and a parent trying to plan one family timetable around both is doing genuinely difficult work with no help from either school.

The practical consequence is that the household has roughly five crunch periods a year rather than three. One child's coursework window lands in September while the other's draft deadline lands in November. One school's mocks run early in December, the other's in January. A tutor who holds both calendars can shift the weekly balance between the children rather than giving each a fixed half: four weeks weighted towards the child with a December deadline, then four weeks the other way. Families who write both calendars onto one sheet in July are visibly calmer in December than families who discover the overlap when it arrives.

sections.heading: Can home tuition really cover two children in one evening?
paragraphs: Yes, in a specific format, and badly in every other. The arrangement that works is two consecutive blocks with a clean handover: forty-five minutes with the younger child while the older one works independently in another room, then a swap, with the tutor leaving written notes for each. Home tuition makes this possible in a way online does not, because the tutor is already there and because a child working independently next door is still being supervised in practice. What does not work is both children at the same table at once, which produces two half-taught students and a tutor refereeing.

Online has two honest uses in a dual-board household. The first is a scarce specialist: if one child needs a Diploma subject with few teachers in the city, an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Marine Drive arrangement may be the only route to somebody who has genuinely supervised that assessment. The second is the fortnight before either child's papers, when short frequent contact over marked questions beats a long visit. Online is a poor fit for the younger child in almost every case, which is why dual households rarely go fully remote.

Hybrid is what most of these families settle into by the second term. One visit a week where both children get a block, one shorter online slot for whichever child is in a deadline week. That pattern absorbs a July downpour, a signal failure on the Western Line, and the week when one school's mocks swallow everything. It also lets the tutor flex time between the children without renegotiating the fee every fortnight. Households running all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Marine Drive style lean on the online half most heavily in November and February.

sections.heading: Dual-board fluency is rare: how we test it in Mumbai
paragraphs: A profile claiming both systems is common and genuine dual fluency is not, so we test rather than accept. Alongside the standard checks on government photo identification and on degrees and teaching qualifications, we ask a tutor to describe how the same topic is assessed differently in each system, and to name a mistake students routinely make when they cross from one to the other. Across Mumbai that question separates the two groups faster than any certificate does: a tutor who has actually taught both answers in specifics within a sentence or two. A tutor who has taught one and read about the other reaches for generalities about both being rigorous.

We also ask which assessed components they have supervised on each side, and which subjects they will decline. The decline answer is the most informative one on a dual-board profile, because the temptation to claim everything is strongest here. Then two telephone references, not written testimonials. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Marine Drive families keep for several years is nearly always one who named a limit at the start rather than one who claimed the whole range.

Your own test takes one session. Ask the tutor to look at one marked paper from each child and say what each one is losing marks for. If the two answers are differently shaped, you have somebody who sees both systems. If both answers sound the same, you have a generalist. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade for either child; the useful version names a weakness per child, a plan and a date to review. Setting up IB and IGCSE home tuition in Marine Drive on those terms gives you something to judge in six weeks.

sections.heading: Does an A* at IGCSE predict a 7 at Higher Level?
paragraphs: It predicts less than parents expect, and this is the single most common misunderstanding in a dual-board household. A top IGCSE grade shows that a student can answer well-posed questions accurately and under time pressure, which is a real and valuable skill. A top Diploma grade at Higher Level additionally requires sustained independent work, a defensible judgement in writing, and an internal assessment the student designed and carried through over months. The first predicts the second only where the student also has the habits the first never tested.

We see the consequence every year on this corridor. A student who finished IGCSE comfortably takes three Higher Levels on the strength of it, finds the first DP1 report mediocre, and concludes they have become worse at the subject. They have not. They have met a different assessment and are being measured on something nobody asked of them before. The remedy is narrow and works: time spent on command terms, on structuring to the marks available, on planning an investigation, and on writing a paragraph that takes a position. Four to six sessions over the holidays between the two years does more than a term of content revision afterwards.

Which is why the most valuable thing a dual-board tutor does on this page is the handover itself. Somebody who taught the child through the IGCSE year and stays through the first Diploma term already knows the student's writing, their arithmetic habits and which topics were papered over. In Mumbai that continuity is worth more than a marginally stronger subject specialist starting cold in July. Parents comparing IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Marine Drive should price that continuity explicitly, because it is the part that does not appear on an hourly rate and the part that most reliably pays back.

sections.heading: Progress across two boards, four weeks to one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: In a two-child arrangement the four-week test is different from a single-child one: look for whether each child can tell you what their own session covered, and whether the tutor's notes distinguish between them. A tutor who sends one message about both children is not tracking two students. Look also at whether the weekly balance has already shifted once in response to a deadline. A plan that has not changed in four weeks is a plan nobody is reading, whatever the Mumbai school calendar has thrown at it. Marks will not have moved yet in either system, and they should not have.

By the end of a term the gains should be visibly different for each child, because the two systems reward different things. The IGCSE child should be laying out working so method marks survive a slip, reading the command word before writing, and attempting the last part of a multi-step question. The Diploma child should be producing a paragraph with a position in it, and should have a workable internal assessment question rather than an ambitious one. If both children's progress sounds identical when the tutor describes it, one of the two descriptions is probably borrowed.

Across a full examination cycle the two children will almost certainly not move by the same amount, and planning for that is more honest than hoping otherwise. Some students move several grades, some move one, some hold a grade that was sliding, which never looks like a result and often is one. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor on this platform may promise a specific outcome to a family in Marine Drive or anywhere else in Mumbai, Maharashtra. Parents searching for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Marine Drive are really buying familiarity with two sets of papers, earlier working and less panic in March, and there are no guarantees attached to any of it.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Marine Drive
paragraphs: Send six things for a two-child household and the first session becomes work rather than an interview. Both current reports with the written comments. faqs.question: Can one tutor travel to our Marine Drive building and teach both children in one evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is already on the island and the format is two consecutive blocks rather than one shared session. That second surface is the part families forget, and without it the child waiting drifts to a phone and loses the hour. A bedroom desk with the door open is fine. faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Marine Drive depend on in a two-child household?
faqs.answer: Six things, and we publish no figures because any number here would mislead somebody. Rates move with the programme and level, since Diploma work commands more than middle-years work and Higher Level more than Standard Level. They move with subject scarcity, sharply for dual-board fluency. They move with travel, because an hour lost to the evening signals is priced in. They move with total session length rather than with headcount, so a double block is not two full fees. And they move with frequency. Ask for a monthly total for the household and compare that.

faqs.question: Our children are in Year 9 and Diploma Programme year two. One tutor or two?
faqs.answer: Two, without hesitation. That gap spans two assessment regimes with nothing meaningful in common: one child needs tier evidence and method discipline, the other needs internal assessment supervision and timed-paper triage before a May session. A single tutor across that range will do one job properly and the other badly, and the one that suffers is usually the Diploma candidate because their deadlines are louder. Spend the same monthly total on two correctly matched tutors on alternating evenings and both children get taught.

faqs.question: When should we start if one child moves into the Diploma Programme next year?
faqs.answer: In the holidays between the two years, and with the tutor who already taught the IGCSE year if that is possible. Four to six sessions on command terms, on structuring to the marks available, and on planning a piece of independent research will do more than a term of content revision in October. It also uses the window when nobody has a deadline, which is the only time this work gets proper attention. Use the same sessions to settle Higher Level choices with somebody who has taught those subjects rather than read about them.

faqs.question: Which months are hardest in a dual-board household in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: November and December first, then February into April. The winter block brings one child's mocks and the other's draft deadlines into the same few weeks, and it is also when every strong tutor on the island is already committed, so searching then returns very little. February onwards belongs to timed papers for whichever child has a session coming. The quiet windows are July to early September and most of January. Starting in a quiet window is the single cheapest advantage available to a two-child household on this corridor.

faqs.question: One child is progressing and the other is not. What do we change?
faqs.answer: Usually the tutor for one child rather than the arrangement for both, and that is a normal outcome rather than a failure. Tell us which child and give one specific example, and we replace that half of the engagement while leaving the working half alone. We will also say so if what you describe is not a tutor problem, for instance a child doing nothing between visits or a subject choice made badly. Six weeks is enough to tell the difference between a poor match and a student who is not working.

faqs.question: Do the two children need the same tutor for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Only where the subject and the assessment genuinely align, which is rarer than it looks. Two children in mathematics, one at Extended tier and one in a Diploma course, are doing related mathematics assessed on entirely different terms, so a shared tutor needs real fluency in both rather than confidence in one. Where it does work well is two children inside the same system two or three years apart, since the criteria and command vocabulary are continuous and the younger one benefits from hearing the older one's work pulled apart.

faqs.question: Is online a sensible option for the older child only?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is one of the better compromises available here. A Diploma candidate can work productively with a remote specialist over marked questions and a shared document, while the younger child keeps a tutor in the room where presence does most of the work. That split also solves the scarce-subject problem, since the city may not contain a local specialist for a particular Higher Level subject. Keep one in-person anchor in the week for the household, because an entirely remote arrangement loses the accountability that makes the rest function.

faqs.question: How many subjects can one household realistically tutor at once?
faqs.answer: Three across two children, four at the very most, and that is a ceiling rather than a target. Every added subject adds an evening, and an evening added to a day that already ends at seven produces tired children rather than better results. Choose the subjects where marks are genuinely being lost instead of the ones where the grade is merely not excellent. If more than four subjects look urgent, the conversation to have is with each school about the entry or level list, not with more tutors about availability.

faqs.question: When is tuition the wrong answer for a dual-board household?
faqs.answer: When the real problem is the household timetable rather than either child's understanding. Two children, two schools and four tutoring slots a week leaves no evening for either of them to work alone, and independent work is exactly what both systems reward. If sleep, screen hours or a subject chosen for the wrong reason is the constraint, tuition makes the week worse. If one child is anxious about examinations rather than behind on content, start with the school counsellor. Tuition is precise against a named gap and blunt against everything else.

sections.heading: Two boards in one building: what actually differs?
paragraphs: The marking philosophy differs, and everything else follows from that. The IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) assesses every subject against published criteria, so a student is judged on named strands of skill and can score unevenly across them in the same subject. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE assess mainly through terminal written papers against a mark scheme, where a mark is earned by a specific statement or a specific step of working. A child moving between those two cultures has to change how they write, not what they know.

This is the mistake we spend most time undoing in two-board households. An MYP-trained student sitting an IGCSE paper writes a thoughtful, well-structured response that does not contain the three specific phrases the mark scheme needed, and loses marks they could see no reason for losing. An IGCSE-trained student writing an MYP task produces tight, correct answers that ignore a whole criterion. Both children are competent. Both have been trained for the wrong reader.

At the senior end the structures diverge again. The Diploma Programme (DP) carries Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) subjects, an Internal Assessment (IA) in each, plus the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK). IGCSE Years 9 to 11 carries a Core and Extended tier decision in several Cambridge subjects and a practical or coursework component whose format depends on the board and the subject. The two workloads peak at different times, which is the one genuine advantage of running both in one house.

We will not reproduce weightings, paper lengths or mark totals from any syllabus here. The IB revises its subject guides on its own cycle and both examination boards revise their specifications on theirs, so a figure printed on a page like this ages badly. For each child, the current guide and the school's coordinator are the only sources worth trusting, and any IB and IGCSE home tutor in Matunga worth hiring will tell you the same.

sections.heading: Can one tutor teach the same subject on both boards?
paragraphs: In Mathematics and the sciences, frequently yes, and it is the arrangement worth asking for. The content overlap between an IGCSE Extended course and the early part of a Standard Level Diploma course is substantial, and a tutor who teaches both routinely will switch registers between a Year 10 and a Diploma Programme student without confusing either. In English and the humanities it is harder, because the assessment formats are further apart and the reading lists share nothing.

The test to apply is specific. Ask the tutor to describe, in one sentence each, what an MYP criterion-based task rewards and what an IGCSE mark scheme rewards. A tutor who genuinely teaches both will answer crisply and differently. A tutor who has taught one and read about the other will produce an answer that applies to neither in particular. This is a thirty-second check on a call and it is more informative than any qualification on a profile.

Where one tutor does span both children, insist on separate records. The practical failure mode in a shared arrangement is not incompetence, it is drift: the child with the nearer deadline absorbs the attention, and three months later nobody can say what the other one covered. One written note per child per session fixes it, and it is a condition we place on tutors rather than a request we pass on. A search for an all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Matunga, or for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Matunga, will not surface this distinction at all.

Subject by subject, a few realities worth knowing in advance. Mathematics travels best between boards. Physics and Chemistry travel well at the content level and less well on practical assessment, because the routes differ. Languages travel poorly, since the speaking and listening components are structured quite differently. Economics and Business Management have deep local supply. Some Language B options and the narrower group 3 subjects are thin across Mumbai, and for those we will recommend going online rather than accepting a willing generalist.

sections.heading: Why Matunga, Dadar, Sion and Wadala share one tutor pool
paragraphs: Because the rail geometry makes them one patch. Matunga sits on the Central Line, Matunga Road is a Western Line station, and Kings Circle on the Harbour Line reaches part of the corridor, so a tutor living along any of those three lines can serve all four areas without planning a route. For a two-board household this matters twice over, because you are protecting two evening slots rather than one, and a tutor without a fallback route will eventually lose one of them.

Dadar holds the deepest supply, courtesy of the interchange. Sion sits to the north near the Eastern Express Highway. Wadala connects down the Eastern Freeway, which pulls the southern island closer than the map suggests and occasionally makes a specialist from further down genuinely viable for a later slot. Treating the four areas as one labour market rather than insisting on the same few streets roughly triples the number of subject specialists available to you, which is exactly what a household needing two different boards wants.

The reason we do not look further is the shape of traffic in Mumbai, Maharashtra. Distances here are short and journeys are not. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers a few kilometres and can still lose a large part of the evening to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals. The Coastal Road has improved some journeys and Metro Line 3 has improved others, and the operating rule has not changed: tutors are matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs.

So when we arrange IB and IGCSE home classes in Matunga for two children, the first filter is route reliability and the second is subject. A tutor from Dadar or Sion will make both evenings through the monsoon. A tutor from Goregaon will make one of them, and the child whose slot gets dropped will be whichever one has the later deadline, which is the opposite of how you would choose.

sections.heading: The Matunga school that runs both pathways under one roof
paragraphs: Don Bosco International School at Matunga runs both the IB and the IGCSE pathways, and its students make up the bulk of the international-board demand between Dadar and Sion. That single fact explains why two-board households are ordinary here rather than unusual. Siblings can be in the same building on different pathways, and a child can move between them at a transition year, which means a parent on this corridor needs to understand both systems whether they expected to or not.

The practical effect on tutoring is a timetable advantage. One school, two pathways, means the assessment calendar for both your children comes from the same source, and you can plan the year in one sitting. It also means local tutors are often fluent in both, because that is what the local demand has required of them. Elsewhere in Mumbai a tutor who covers both boards is a specialist; between Dadar and Sion it is closer to a job requirement.

JBCN International School, Parel is the other name that appears constantly in enquiries from this corridor, close enough that families here commute to it daily, and it also offers both pathways. Its term pattern falls at slightly different points, which spreads tutor demand a little. If your two children are at different schools, send both calendars, because the collisions you are trying to avoid are between schools rather than between boards.

On naming schools at all: IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Don Bosco International School, with JBCN International School, Parel, or with any other school mentioned anywhere on this page. We name them because the dual-pathway reality of this corridor is the entire reason this page exists, and because knowing which calendars a tutor already tracks is genuinely useful. It is local context and not a relationship, and no tutor should present it as one.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or both when two boards are running in Mumbai
paragraphs: The main sessions belong at your table, one child at a time, on separate evenings. Separate evenings is the part parents resist because it looks inefficient, and it is the single change that most improves a two-board arrangement. Two children taught back to back in the same room means the second one waits, the first one lingers, and the tutor compresses whichever session runs second. Two evenings costs no more per hour and produces two proper sessions instead of one and a half.

Online earns its place in the gaps between those evenings, and in a two-board house the gaps are busy. A Diploma Programme internal assessment draft needs comment on a Sunday. A Year 10 past paper needs marking before Tuesday. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Matunga can handle both in twenty minutes each without anybody travelling at seven in the evening, and that is where the hybrid pattern comes from rather than from any preference about technology.

Pure online for the main sessions works for a self-motivated Diploma Programme student and reliably fails for a distracted Year 10. If you have one of each, do not apply the same answer to both. The younger child needs a person in the room to hold the ninety minutes together; the older one may genuinely prefer the screen and lose nothing. Two-board households are also two-age households, and the mode decision should follow the age rather than the household.

A planning note specific to this corridor. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Matunga is usually arranged around a seven o'clock and an eight-thirty start, because that is when two children in different year groups are both free and the roads across this part of Mumbai have eased. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Matunga covering both children will normally take the younger one first, while concentration is still available, and the Diploma Programme student second. Reverse that order and the thirteen-year-old gets the session nobody can use.

The honest trade-offs. Home sessions carry travel in the rate and occasional monsoon lateness. Online loses engagement with younger students and makes handwritten working slower to diagnose. Hybrid requires one written record per child or the two halves drift apart. We ask for those records as a condition, because in a house with two children and two boards the record is the only thing that stops one of them disappearing from view.
bullets: Separate evenings per child, which costs nothing and fixes compression
Online handles draft comments and paper marking between sessions
