sections.heading: Checking a tutor who claims both boards in Mumbai
paragraphs: A claim to cover both boards is the one we probe hardest, because it is the easiest claim to make and the hardest to fake in a conversation. Before any profile reaches you we verify photo identity against government identification, confirm the subject qualification, and confirm separately that the tutor has taught the IB programme at the level stated and the Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel specification at the level stated. Two confirmations, not one inference. A tutor who has taught MYP Mathematics has not thereby taught IGCSE Mathematics, and the reverse is equally true.

We also ask about availability across the whole year rather than this month, because a two-slot household is more fragile than a one-slot household. A tutor collecting six evenings across the city cannot reliably hold two of your evenings once the rains start. Where a tutor is new to the platform, the profile says so. None of this appears in a directory listing, which is why the checking otherwise gets done by the parent over two slow months.

Your own checks matter more in a two-board house than in a single-board one. Ask the tutor to distinguish criterion-based marking from mark-scheme marking in a sentence each. Ask how they would keep two children's records separate. Ask what they will show you about each child after four weeks. Write all three answers down, because in week six you will be deciding whether a vague feeling of improvement is real, and the written answer is the only thing that will settle it.

Be wary of anyone who offers a guaranteed grade, publishes a pass rate, or suggests an official connection to a school. Those are not things an honest tutor can offer. In a two-board household there is a second warning sign worth watching for: a tutor who treats the two boards as interchangeable. That is not flexibility, it is a gap in experience that your children will pay for in marks they cannot account for.
bullets: Both boards confirmed separately, never inferred from one another
Availability checked across the year, because two slots are fragile
Ask them to distinguish criterion marking from mark-scheme marking
Ask how two children's records will be kept separate
A tutor who calls the boards interchangeable has taught only one

sections.heading: What does IB and IGCSE home tuition in Matunga cost for two children?
paragraphs: More than one child and less than double, if it is planned properly. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Matunga depend on board, level, subject scarcity, session length and travel, and the only one of those a two-child household can genuinely optimise is travel. A single tutor making one journey for two consecutive sessions prices that journey once. Two tutors on two evenings each price their own. Whether the saving is worth the compression described earlier depends on the age gap, and we will give you a straight view rather than a preference.

The larger saving is in sequencing rather than in bundling. Because the Diploma Programme internal assessment calendar and the IGCSE coursework calendar peak in different months, you can run one child intensively while the other is on maintenance, then swap. A household that runs both children at two sessions a week all year is buying a lot of hours it does not need. A household that alternates buys roughly the same outcome for noticeably fewer total hours, which is the actual cost lever.

Level and scarcity move the rate in the predictable direction. A Higher Level Diploma science costs more per hour than general Year 9 support, because fewer people can teach it well, and an uncommon Language B costs more again regardless of anyone's preference. Travel on this corridor is mercifully cheap, which is the quiet benefit of matching inside Matunga, Dadar, Sion and Wadala rather than insisting on a name from Bandra.

We publish no price list and will not invent one. What we will say is that any tutor should be able to break a rate down against those five factors on a call without hedging, and that the single largest discount available to you is timing. Starting in June or July, when the year has just opened, buys a full diagnostic month at a normal rate for both children. Starting in January buys whatever evenings are left at the point when every family on this corridor is asking at once.
bullets: One tutor across two children prices the journey once, not twice
Sequencing beats bundling: alternate intensity as deadlines alternate
Higher Level and scarce subjects move the rate, not distance
Local matching keeps travel the smallest part of the rate
Starting in June is the only real discount on offer

sections.heading: Four weeks with two boards running: what should change?
paragraphs: Something visible for each child, separately, and that is the whole point of separate records. For the IGCSE child, fewer marks lost to unshown working on a marked paper, and an ability to name the command word they keep misreading. For the IB child, a draft that exists, and a sentence explaining which criterion or which assessment objective they have been missing. One child improving and the other unchanged is the classic four-week result in a shared arrangement, and it is a scheduling failure rather than a teaching one.

At one term, both children's workloads should be under control, which in a two-board household is a higher bar than it sounds. It means neither child is working the night before a submission, the two calendars have stopped surprising you, and you can say what each of them is working on this fortnight without asking. Control is most of what a term buys, and in a house with two deadlines systems it is worth more than a grade change.

Across a full cycle, honest tuition moves many students meaningfully and some barely at all. We will not publish a figure and no tutor on the platform may promise one for either of your children. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. What we will commit to is procedural: a written diagnosis per child after the first session, a note per child per session, and a four-week review that includes the uncomfortable version where we say one of the two arrangements should stop.

The limits, stated for this specific case. Tuition cannot make two boards into one, so a child who has to change pathways will still have an adjustment to make. It cannot absorb an overloaded subject selection for either child. And it cannot run two intensive arrangements in a flat where only one quiet room exists, which is a practical constraint families discover in week three and which is worth thinking about in week zero.
bullets: A separate visible change per child, or the schedule is the problem
IGCSE child: fewer marks lost to working, command word identified
IB child: a draft that exists and a named criterion being missed
One term: two calendars that no longer surprise you

sections.heading: Starting home classes in Matunga for both children
paragraphs: Prepare four things. One marked assessment per child, with the teacher comments still on them. Both school calendars, or photographs of the two portal pages. A decision about which two evenings are protected, one per child. And a one-line answer per child to the question of what you most want fixed this term, because that line is what we match against.

Each first session is a diagnosis for that child and nothing else. For the IGCSE child the tutor separates content gaps, unshown method, misread command words and poor timing, which look identical in a percentage and need different responses. For the IB child the work is identifying which criterion or assessment objective is losing marks and whether the internal assessment has a workable research question yet. Each session ends with a written note. Two notes, two children, no merging.

After that the pattern is one protected evening per child, a note each time, and a review with us at two to four weeks covering both arrangements. Either tutor can be replaced on request with no notice period. Some families describe what they have set up as an IB and IGCSE private tutor Matunga arrangement, which is accurate; the part that makes it work is that each child has their own brief, their own slot and their own record.

If you are in Matunga, Dadar, Sion or Wadala, send both children's boards, years and subjects and your two protected evenings. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents hope to find does not exist as one person, so name the subject that matters most for each child and we will match accordingly.
bullets: One marked assessment and one calendar per child, not a combined set
Protect one evening per child rather than one shared evening
A one-line target per child is what we actually match against
Two first sessions, two diagnoses, two written notes, no merging
Either tutor replaced on request, with no notice period

faqs.question: Can one tutor really cover both my IB and my IGCSE child?
faqs.answer: In Mathematics and the sciences, often yes; in languages and humanities, usually not. The content overlap between IGCSE Extended work and the early part of a Standard Level Diploma course is real, so a tutor who teaches both routinely will switch registers comfortably. Test it on the call by asking them to describe what criterion-based marking rewards and what a mark scheme rewards, in one sentence each. A tutor who has genuinely taught both answers crisply and differently. One who has taught one of them will produce something that fits neither.

faqs.question: Should both children be taught on the same evening to save the travel?
faqs.answer: It saves money and costs quality, and usually the trade is bad. Back-to-back sessions in one flat mean the second child waits, the first lingers, and whichever session runs second gets compressed. If the age gap is large and one child only needs thirty minutes of review, it can work. For two children who both need real teaching, separate evenings is the arrangement that holds. The travel saving is smaller than parents expect on this corridor, because journeys inside Matunga, Dadar and Sion are short anyway.

faqs.question: My Year 10 child may move into the Diploma Programme. How early should we prepare?
faqs.answer: From the middle of Year 11, in a specific way: by changing how answers are written rather than by starting Diploma content. The adjustment that catches students is the move from mark-scheme writing to criterion-based writing, where a correct answer that ignores a criterion scores poorly. A few weeks of work on that, using the school's own task sheets, is worth more than a head start on Higher Level material. Your school's coordinator will tell you which subjects the transition is roughest in.

faqs.question: Do the two boards' deadlines clash in the same months?
faqs.answer: Mostly they alternate, which is the one genuine advantage of running both. Diploma Programme internal assessment drafts and Extended Essay milestones fall at different points from Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel coursework and practical submissions. Send us both school calendars and we will schedule so that the intense months for one child are maintenance months for the other. Running both children at full intensity all year is the most common way a two-board household overspends without getting a better result.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building for two slots a week?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they live on this corridor, and that is exactly why we filter on route reliability before subject. Matunga station on the Central Line, Matunga Road on the Western Line and Kings Circle on the Harbour Line give a tutor a train when the road fails. Someone from Dadar or Sion will make both evenings through the monsoon. Someone from the western suburbs will make one of them, and the slot that gets dropped is never the one you would have chosen to drop.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Matunga depend on?
faqs.answer: Board, level, subject scarcity, session length and travel. A Higher Level Diploma science prices above general Year 9 support because fewer people teach it well, and an uncommon language prices above both. Travel is the smallest component when matching stays inside this corridor. We publish no price list and will not invent a figure. The genuine saving available to a two-child household is sequencing: alternate which child is intensive as the two calendars peak, rather than paying for two intensive arrangements all year.

faqs.question: How do I stop one child getting all the attention?
faqs.answer: Insist on one written note per child per session and read both. Drift is the standard failure in shared arrangements, and it is never announced; the child with the nearer deadline simply absorbs the time. A separate note makes it visible within a fortnight. We place that requirement on tutors rather than passing on a request, and if the notes stop arriving for one child, treat it as the first sign rather than waiting for a report card to confirm it.

faqs.question: Does online work for one child and not the other?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and you should not apply one answer to both. A motivated Diploma Programme student often loses nothing on a screen, particularly for draft feedback and single-question checks. A distracted Year 10 loses the session within a fortnight and needs a person in the room to hold ninety minutes together. Mode should follow the child's age and temperament rather than the household's convenience, which means a two-board house commonly ends up with one home arrangement and one hybrid one.

faqs.question: Where do two tutors sit if the flat only has one quiet room?
faqs.answer: On different evenings, which is the practical reason separate scheduling matters as much as the pedagogical one. Flats on this corridor are often compact and a single cleared dining table is usually the only workable surface. Trying to run two sessions simultaneously in one home produces two poor ones. Decide which evening belongs to which child before anybody starts, because renegotiating it in week three tends to end with the quieter child losing their slot.

faqs.question: My children are at Don Bosco International School. Does that simplify things?
faqs.answer: It does, because the school runs both pathways, so both calendars come from one source and you can plan the year in a single sitting. Local tutors here are also often fluent in both boards, since that is what demand between Dadar and Sion has required. To be clear, IB Gram is not affiliated with Don Bosco International School or with any other school named on this page. Knowing a school's assessment rhythm is useful local knowledge and nothing more than that.

faqs.question: Can we start with one child and add the second later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is often the sensible order. Start with whichever child has the nearer deadline or the clearer problem, see how the arrangement runs for a month, then add the second with the benefit of knowing what works in your household. Adding a second child to a working arrangement is easy. Starting two at once, in a flat with one table, with two calendars nobody has mapped yet, is how families end up cancelling both by October.

faqs.question: Will you promise a result for either child?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no tutor on the platform may promise a grade or publish a success rate for either of your children. What we will commit to is specific and checkable: a written diagnosis per child after the first session, a separate note per child per session, and an honest four-week review that includes telling you if one of the two arrangements should stop. A tutor who offers a number before meeting a child has skipped the diagnosis entirely.

sections.heading: How a request for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mazgaon becomes a standing weekly slot
paragraphs: Most enquiries from Mazgaon arrive with one subject named and a date attached: a Year 10 mock three weeks away, or a first-year Diploma Programme (DP) report that came back thinner than the family expected. The first question back is not about the subject. It is about the week. A slot that still exists in February is worth more than four emergency sessions in January, so what gets matched here is an arrangement rather than simply a person, and the arrangement is built around the two evenings a family can actually protect.

Mazgaon sits on the Harbour Line at Dockyard Road, which means the tutor pool and the school run point in opposite directions. Tutors reach you from Chembur, Govandi and Wadala in one easy hop, while your child is coming back north from Fort or Babulnath after a full day. Those two clocks rarely agree. A 6pm start that suits a tutor arriving from the east can land twenty minutes after a tired Year 11 student has walked in, so the slot gets set against the school's dismissal time first and the tutor's travel second.

After that the shortlist is short on purpose. Two or three names, each one teaching the exact board and level your child is entered for, with a note on what they are strongest at. You talk to them before any money moves. The first paid session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson: the tutor works through recent school work, one set of past paper questions and the last report, then writes you a summary of what is actually wrong. Many families discover the problem is two topics deep and not a whole subject.

Only then does the weekly commitment get fixed. Hours per week, which evenings, how long each session runs, who is told when a session moves, and how long the arrangement is booked for. Putting those five things in writing at the start is the single biggest reason an arrangement for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mazgaon is still running at the end of a term.
bullets: 1. Send the board, the year group, the subject and the two evenings that are genuinely free.
2. We shortlist from the island pool first, so travel does not eat into the hour.
3. You speak to each shortlisted tutor yourself before any session is booked.
4. The first session runs as a diagnostic and ends in a written summary to you.
5. You fix the weekly slot for a term, or ask for a different name without explaining why.

sections.heading: Which boards and levels does one Mazgaon tutor need to hold at once?
paragraphs: In a Mazgaon flat the answer is usually two, not one. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the Diploma Programme (DP), while Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel run IGCSE across Years 9 to 11. Families at Bombay International School and Cathedral and John Connon School often have one child in Year 10 IGCSE and an older sibling in DP, which means two syllabuses, two assessment calendars and two different kinds of homework arriving in the same evening in Mumbai.

A tutor who teaches both boards in the same subject is common and useful; a tutor who claims four subjects across both boards is rare and usually a warning sign. The honest split is by subject family. One person can hold IGCSE Mathematics and DP Mathematics, or IGCSE Physics and DP Physics, because the content ladders upward. Expecting one person to hold DP Chemistry at Higher Level (HL) and IGCSE English Literature equally well is asking for a generalist, and a generalist is exactly who you do not want for a Higher Level science in the second year.

Level sets the hours more than the board does. A Standard Level (SL) subject in the first Diploma year often needs one session a week; the same subject at Higher Level in the second year, with an Internal Assessment (IA) running alongside, needs a longer session or a second one in the weeks a draft is due. At IGCSE the equivalent decision is Core or Extended tier, and it changes what the weekly hour is for: Core work is mostly about securing the standard questions, Extended work is about the last part of the long ones.

So the question to settle before booking is not which board, it is how many separate arrangements the household needs. Two children on two pathways with one tutor between them usually means one of them gets the leftover half hour. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mazgaon who takes one child for a clean hour, with a second tutor for the sibling, holds together far longer than a shared ninety minutes split down the middle.
bullets: PYP, MYP and DP each report differently, so ask which one the report came from.
IGCSE sits at Years 9 to 11, and the tier decision usually lands in Year 9.
One tutor across two boards works inside a subject family, not across four subjects.

sections.heading: How many subjects can one home tutor realistically carry each week?
paragraphs: Three is the practical ceiling for one tutor, and two is better. Each subject carries its own internal assessment, and that is where weekly hours get eaten. In the Diploma Programme the Internal Assessment differs by subject: a mathematical exploration, a scientific investigation, a historical investigation, an oral in a language. Each has its own drafting cycle set by the school rather than by the board, so your child's Physics draft and her History draft can land in the same fortnight even though the subjects share nothing at all.

At IGCSE the equivalent load is coursework and practical components, which again vary by subject and by what the school has entered. Mathematics at Extended tier is almost entirely written papers, so the weekly hour goes on technique and on the non-calculator work students lose marks on. A language or a literature subject carries pieces that have to be drafted and redrafted, which means the tutor is reading between sessions and not only teaching inside them. That reading time is part of the arrangement and worth asking about before you book.

This is why all IB and IGCSE subjects a home tutor in Mazgaon can cover is the wrong way to shop. Ask instead which two subjects are actually costing the grade, and put the hours there. A parent who books three subjects at one hour each usually ends the term with three subjects that moved slightly; a parent who books two subjects at ninety minutes ends it with two that moved properly. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) are a separate case, needing a few intense sessions at the right moment rather than a standing weekly slot.

One more thing about subject count. The tutor a household needs most is often not the one for the weakest subject. It is the one for the subject sitting a band below where the rest of the application sits. Mazgaon families applying to universities in the UK, the US and Canada tend to feel that gap in Mathematics or a science, and that is where an extra hour a week pays back most visibly.

sections.heading: Which Mumbai addresses the same Mazgaon tutor can reach
paragraphs: A tutor who takes a weekly slot in Mazgaon almost always holds two or three other addresses within a few kilometres, and that is what makes the slot survivable. The usual spread is Byculla to the north, Sewri along the Harbour Line to the east, and Fort to the south. Those stops form one working circuit. A tutor finishing in Byculla at 5.30pm reaches Mazgaon comfortably for 6.15pm; the same tutor finishing in Fort at the same time is fighting the office exit the whole way back.

South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow, and parents here underestimate it because the map looks friendly. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. Tutors here are matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs. The Eastern Freeway and the Harbour Line change the calculation on the eastern side: Chembur, Govandi and Wadala are genuinely closer to Dockyard Road at 6pm than Bandra is.

Metro Line 3 on the Aqua corridor from Cuffe Parade to BKC and the Coastal Road have made some crossings faster, but neither helps the 6pm run into Mazgaon much, because demand here runs north to south on the old roads. The practical result is that IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mazgaon is best served by a tutor who already teaches in Byculla, Sewri or Fort, and who can therefore absorb a traffic day without cancelling. A tutor travelling across Mumbai from Andheri for one hour will cancel eventually, however good they are.

If you live closer to the Sewri end, say so when you enquire. The difference between the Dockyard Road side and the Sewri side is ten minutes on a good evening and half an hour on a bad one, and it changes which names make the shortlist. IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mazgaon is a reasonable thing to search for, and proximity is a real factor, just not the only one that decides a match.

sections.heading: Term dates, mock weeks and the hours a Mumbai family actually needs
paragraphs: The international-board school year in Mumbai starts in June and runs to the following April or May, and the pressure points are predictable enough to plan an arrangement around. October and November bring the first serious internal assessments and the first report that makes parents search. December and January are mock season for Year 11 and for second-year Diploma students. February and March are when internal assessment deadlines stack up on each other. The written examinations themselves fall in April and May.

Mazgaon families mostly travel south for school. Bombay International School at Babulnath and Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort set the daily rhythm for a lot of this neighbourhood, and the bus or the car leaves early and gets back late. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Bombay International School, Cathedral and John Connon School or any other school named on this page. We name them because their calendars decide when your evenings are free, not because we have any relationship with them.

That southward school run is why a Mazgaon arrangement usually settles on later weekday slots or weekend mornings. A child who gets home at 4.45pm needs a break before a serious hour of work. Saturday mornings are the most reliable slot in this part of Mumbai and the first to go, so families who book in June get them and families who book in December do not. If your child's school tests on Mondays, ask for a Thursday or Friday session so the work lands before the test rather than after it.

Plan the hours against the calendar instead of against the panic. Two sessions a week from June through September, dropping to one when the term settles, then back to two through the February draft crunch, costs about what three months of emergency help in March costs and does considerably more with the time. IGCSE home tuition in Mazgaon booked in June is a different service from the same tuition booked in April, even with the same tutor in the same chair.

sections.heading: Should a term-long arrangement ever move online?
paragraphs: Home tutoring is the default here and should be. A tutor at your dining table sees what a camera does not: the phone face-down beside the notebook, the handwriting that collapses in the last ten minutes, the child who does every question in her head and writes nothing down. For Years 9 to 11, and for anyone who needs supervision as much as teaching, home classes do a job online cannot. That is why IB and IGCSE home classes in Mazgaon is the service most families here start with.

Online earns its place in two situations. The first is scarcity: if your child needs Higher Level Economics or a less common language at Diploma level, the right specialist may be in Pune or Bengaluru, and a sharp online tutor beats a nearby generalist every time. The second is the examination run, when a thirty-minute screen share to mark one question is more useful than a full hour with travel attached. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mazgaon also keeps running in heavy monsoon weeks when a tutor genuinely cannot get through.

Hybrid is what most term-long arrangements actually settle into, and it is worth designing rather than drifting into. One home session a week for the teaching and the supervision, one short online session for marking and question practice. The home session holds the discipline; the online one adds frequency without adding travel. Families along the Harbour Line use this a great deal, because it lets them keep a tutor who lives in Chembur or Govandi without asking that tutor to cross Mumbai twice a week through the evening peak.

The honest trade-off is this. Online sessions need a parent to set up the room, a tablet or a document camera so the tutor can see working as it happens, and a student old enough to stay honest on screen. Below Year 9 that rarely holds. Above Year 11 it usually does. Decide which one you are buying before the term starts, rather than after two cancelled evenings have already cost you a fortnight.

sections.heading: What IB Gram checks, and what you should check in the first fortnight
paragraphs: Every tutor on IB Gram is checked on four things before being sent to an address: identity, the qualification they claim, the boards and levels they have actually taught, and references from families they have taught in Mumbai. Teaching the board is the one that matters most and the one parents forget to ask about. Someone with a strong mathematics degree who has never taught Cambridge Extended papers will teach your child mathematics beautifully and still miss how the marks are awarded on the page.

What you should check is different, and nobody can do it for you. In the first fortnight look for three things: does the tutor know what your child's school has actually entered her for, do they ask to see the last piece of marked school work, and can they tell you after two sessions what the specific problem is rather than that your child needs more practice. A tutor who cannot name the problem by the third session has not diagnosed anything yet.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, quotes a success rate, or tells you the school is teaching it wrong. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor does either. Parents who search for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mazgaon are usually looking for the right one, and the right one is identifiable by behaviour: punctual, prepared, willing to say what they do not teach. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Mazgaon families recommend to each other is almost always someone boring and consistent rather than impressive in the first meeting.

Ask for the tutor's own notes after the second session. A tutor who writes three lines of substance is worth keeping; a tutor who writes covered chapter four is not. This is also the moment to raise anything uncomfortable about timekeeping or tone, because a small correction in week two works and the same conversation in week eight turns into a replacement.
bullets: Identity, qualification, boards taught and Mumbai references are checked before any match.

sections.heading: Hours per week, term length and what the rate does not cover
paragraphs: Nobody can publish a sensible rate for this, and any site that does is quoting a number for a different child. What the rate depends on is knowable: the board and level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels, how long each session runs, and how many sessions a week you commit to. A Higher Level Diploma science in the second year costs more per hour than a Year 9 IGCSE subject, because the pool of people who can teach it well is far smaller.

Travel is a real line item in South Mumbai even over short distances, because forty minutes in the Peddar Road and Haji Ali crawl is forty minutes the tutor cannot teach in. A tutor already working in Byculla or Fort prices differently from one crossing the island. Session length matters more than parents expect: ninety minutes is not one and a half times an hour of value, it is closer to double, because the first fifteen minutes of any session go on settling and recap whatever the length. What IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mazgaon depend on, in short, is scarcity and friction.

Ask what the rate does not cover, because this is where arrangements sour. Usual exclusions: marking a full mock paper between sessions, reading an internal assessment draft, extra sessions in the week before an examination, and travel on a day you move the slot at short notice. Usual inclusions: short notes after each session and a reply to a question on a weekday. Settle the cancellation rule too. The fair version runs both ways, with reasonable notice from you, reasonable notice from the tutor, and a slot held for the term rather than resold.

Term-long or exam-term is the last decision. A term-long arrangement is cheaper per unit of progress and almost always the right call from June. An exam-term booking makes sense only when the diagnosis is narrow, for instance a Year 11 student who is secure everywhere except the last part of the long questions. If a tutor is away for a fortnight, ask now who covers. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families share between two siblings is the arrangement that breaks first when somebody travels.

sections.heading: What reaches you between sessions, and what four weeks can honestly change
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at the grade. You should be looking at four smaller things: your child opening the book before the tutor arrives, the tutor able to name the two topics that were actually broken, a visible change in how working is written down, and one piece of school work that came back better for a reason you can both explain. If none of those four has moved in a month, the match is wrong and it is worth saying so out loud.

At one term, a grade band usually moves if the diagnosis was right and the hours were kept. A Year 10 student who was losing marks on method rather than on concept tends to move fastest. A Diploma student in the second year moves more slowly, because by then the gap is often conceptual and sits two years back. Over one examination cycle the realistic picture is steadier work, fewer careless losses and a child who knows what the examiner is asking for, which is not the same thing as a promised number.

Between sessions, insist on something written. Three or four lines after each session naming what was covered, what was set and what is still weak is enough, and it takes a tutor five minutes. Parents who get this never need to ask how it is going, and parents who do not get it end up hovering in the doorway. Ask for a longer note once a month. For Mumbai households where both parents work in Fort or BKC and get home after the session has ended, that monthly note is the whole relationship.

If it is not working, say so early and plainly. A replacement runs the same way as the original match: you tell us what did not fit, we shortlist again from the island pool, and the new tutor starts with the previous tutor's notes so your child does not repeat four weeks of diagnosis. Changing a tutor in week three is ordinary and costs nothing but one conversation.
bullets: Week four: look at habits and diagnosis, not at the grade.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home classes in Mazgaon: the first week
paragraphs: Have four things ready and the first week does itself: the most recent school report, two pieces of marked work with the teacher's comments still on them, the school's assessment calendar for the term, and the two evenings you can genuinely protect. The report tells a tutor where the school thinks your child is. The marked work tells them where the marks are actually going. The calendar tells them what to teach first, which is rarely what the parent assumed it would be.

The first session is a diagnostic. Expect the tutor to spend a good part of it watching your child work rather than talking, to ask her to explain a question she got wrong, and to leave with a short list of topics in priority order. Expect a written summary within a day or two. Expect no promises about outcomes. If a tutor opens by telling you what grade is achievable, that is the session to end early and the match to decline.

Set the room before the tutor arrives. A table, two chairs, a light that works, the phone in another room, and a parent within earshot for the first couple of sessions if your child is below Year 9. Tell the building security desk the tutor's name and the weekly time once rather than every week, because a standing entry saves ten minutes of your tutor's hour every single session. Families on the Sewri side of Mazgaon who book a 6pm slot should give the tutor a five minute window either way through the monsoon.

From there the arrangement is ordinary. One or two sessions a week, notes after each one, a longer note monthly, a review at the end of the term. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mazgaon works when it is boring and consistent, which is the opposite of how most tuition is sold. If you want to start, send the board, the year group and the subject, and say which evenings are free.
bullets: Bring the report, two pieces of marked work and the term calendar.
Protect two evenings before you book anything at all.
Register the tutor at the security desk once, not weekly.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mazgaon actually need?
faqs.answer: One session a week per subject is the floor, and ninety minutes is better than sixty. Two subjects at one session each is the most common arrangement in Mazgaon households, and it holds through a normal term. Add a second session in the fortnight an internal assessment draft is due or a mock is coming, then drop back. Three subjects at an hour each usually produces three subjects that moved a little, which is not what you were buying. The exception is a second-year Diploma student in a Higher Level science, where two sessions a week from October is the honest recommendation.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Mazgaon for a weekday evening slot in the peak?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is already working on the island. Tutors who teach in Byculla, Sewri or Fort reach Mazgaon in the evening peak reliably, and the Harbour Line and the Eastern Freeway make Chembur, Govandi and Wadala workable too. A tutor coming down from the western suburbs for one hour is the match that cancels in week six. South Mumbai is short-distance but slow: eight kilometres from Worli to Colaba can cost forty minutes at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals. We match within the island for exactly this reason, and we will say if your preferred slot needs a different evening.

faqs.question: What should I tell the building gate about a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once as a standing weekly visitor with the name, the day and the time, rather than calling it in each week. Ten minutes lost at the gate is ten minutes of a sixty minute session, and it happens every week otherwise. Give the tutor the flat number, the entrance to use, and a phone number that is answered during the session. If your building requires an app approval for every visit, say so at the matching stage, because some tutors will not take a slot where entry is uncertain. Also say where the tutor should wait if your child is still travelling back from Fort.

faqs.question: What happens if my tutor is away for two weeks?
faqs.answer: Ask that before you book, because the answer varies by tutor. The arrangement we recommend is a named substitute at the same board and level who takes the slot using the regular tutor's notes, or a clean pause with the slot held for the return. What should not happen is a silent cancellation, or a stand-in who starts the diagnosis from the beginning. If the absence falls in a critical fortnight, such as a mock run or an internal assessment deadline, tell us and we will shortlist a short-term tutor instead of losing the weeks.

faqs.question: What does the rate include, and what sits outside it?
faqs.answer: Typically the rate covers the session itself, short notes afterwards, and a reply to a question during the week. What sits outside it varies and should be agreed in writing: marking a full mock paper, reading an internal assessment draft, additional sessions in the week before an examination, and travel on a day you move the slot late. We do not publish rates because they move with board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length, and a published number would be wrong for most of the families reading it.

faqs.question: Should I book for the whole term or only for the exam months?
faqs.answer: Book for the term if you can, and for the exam months only if the diagnosis is narrow. A term-long arrangement lets a tutor fix causes; an exam-term booking lets them patch symptoms, which is fine if the symptom is genuinely all that is wrong. A Year 11 student who is secure across the syllabus but loses marks on the last part of long questions is a reasonable exam-term case. A Year 10 student whose method has been shaky since Year 8 is not, and six weeks in March will not change that.

faqs.question: Do you cover both boards in one household?
faqs.answer: Yes, and usually with two tutors rather than one. Families at Bombay International School and Cathedral and John Connon School often have a Year 10 IGCSE child and a Diploma Programme sibling, and the two need different things on different evenings. One tutor can reasonably hold IGCSE and Diploma work in the same subject family, since the content ladders upward. Splitting one ninety minute visit between two children on two boards sounds efficient and in practice gives one of them the leftover half hour, which is the complaint we hear most often.

faqs.question: How soon can home classes start after I enquire?
faqs.answer: Usually within a week for mainstream subjects in South Mumbai, and longer for scarce ones. Shortlisting takes a day or two, your call with the tutor another day, and the first session lands on your next free evening. Scarce subjects, a specific Higher Level science or a less common language, can take a fortnight or may need an online specialist. The slowest period is December and January, when mock season has already taken the good evening slots across Mumbai, and the fastest is June, when the year has just started.

faqs.question: My child's school says tuition is unnecessary. Are they wrong?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and the comment is worth taking seriously. A good subject teacher who says your child does not need a tutor is often telling you the gap is effort or organisation rather than teaching, and no tutor fixes effort from outside. Where a school is usually wrong is on pace: a class of twenty five cannot wait for one student to secure a topic, and a weekly hour at your table can. Ask the teacher one question before deciding, which is whether the marks are being lost on concept or on method.

faqs.question: What should I do if there is no visible progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Say so directly, to the tutor first and to us second. After four weeks ask the tutor two questions: which two specific topics were broken, and what has changed in how your child works. A tutor who can answer both is probably on track even if the marks have not moved yet; a tutor who answers with more practice is not. If the answers are thin, we shortlist again from the same island pool and the new tutor starts with the old notes. Changing in week five is ordinary and nobody will be offended.

We write about their calendars because those calendars decide which evenings are free in Mazgaon and when the assessment pressure lands, not because we have any relationship with them. We also do not guarantee grades, publish success rates or claim that any school endorses us. What we do is match verified subject tutors and say honestly what an hour a week can and cannot change.

sections.heading: How a Mira Road home tuition request becomes a shortlist
paragraphs: Most enquiries for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mira Road arrive as a single line: Year 10 Maths, urgent. That line is not enough to match on, and a platform that acts on it immediately is guessing. The first thing we do is turn it into a brief with four pieces of information in it. Which board, because Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel set papers differently and the International Baccalaureate (IB) assesses differently again. Which year and which level, because Core and Extended at IGCSE are genuinely different courses, and Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) in the IB Diploma Programme (DP) are too. What the school has already said, because a report comment is usually more diagnostic than a parent's summary of it. And what time the child is actually free, which in Mira Road is the question that decides everything else.

That last point is not a formality here. A child travelling from Mira Road to a school in Dahisar East or Borivali leaves early and gets back when the Western Express Highway is at its worst. A slot that looks fine on paper at 5.30pm can collide with a bus that reaches the gate at 5.50pm three days out of five. So we write the real arrival time into the brief and match to it, rather than offering a tutor a slot the family cannot keep.

Only then do we look at who is available. We work outward from the Mira Road–Mira Bhayandar stretch first, then along the line towards Dahisar and Borivali, and only after that do we consider a tutor who would have to travel further. A tutor who lives thirty minutes away and teaches the right board at the right level will outlast a better-credentialled tutor who has to cross the city, because the second one cancels in July and again in September and the family loses a term of momentum.
The process from brief to first lesson runs like this:

1. You send the brief: board, year, subject, level, the report comment if you have it, and the two or three evenings that genuinely work. 2. We shortlist two or three verified tutors who teach that exact board and level and can reach Mira Road at that hour. 3. You take a free discovery call with the one you prefer, ask your own questions, and decide. 4. Lessons start, and we review with you at the two-to-four week mark against what the brief said you wanted fixed.

If none of the shortlist feels right, say so on the call and we go back and look again. Nothing is booked, charged or scheduled before you agree, and there is no package you have to buy to see the profiles.

sections.heading: Which board and level is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: A Mira Road parent usually knows the school's name and the child's year, and is much less certain about the board label underneath. It matters, because the wrong label produces the wrong tutor. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are both IGCSE in everyday speech, and both run across Years 9 to 11, but the paper structures, the formula support and the coursework expectations differ enough that a tutor who has taught only one will be slow on the other. The IB side has three layers: the Primary Years Programme (PYP) in the early years, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) through the middle school, and the Diploma Programme (DP) in the last two years. A child in MYP Year 4 and a child in DP1 are not doing scaled versions of the same thing.

The practical consequence for IGCSE Years 9 to 11 is the tier decision. Core and Extended cover different content and cap at different grades, and schools enter students on evidence from Year 9 and early Year 10. Families in Mira Road often meet this decision at a parents' evening in Dahisar or Borivali, with twenty minutes to discuss it, and then come home and search for a tutor. An honest tutor will not tell you which tier to pick. What a good one will do in the first fortnight is work through two or three past Extended questions with your child and tell you plainly whether the gap is content, speed or exam technique, which is the information the school conversation actually needs.

On the IB side the equivalent fork is HL and SL, and it is chosen a year before the exams that depend on it. HL is not SL with extra homework; in several subjects it adds whole topics and a different depth of expected reasoning. Where a child is carrying three HLs and struggling in one, the useful question is not how to survive it but whether the combination was ever right. A tutor who teaches the subject at both levels can say something useful about that. A tutor who only ever taught SL cannot.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Singapore International School, JBCN International School, Borivali, or any other school named on this page. We match tutors and we tell you what we checked. We do not guarantee grades, and no tutor in our network is permitted to promise a specific one.

sections.heading: What subjects and internal assessments does a Mira Road tutor need to match?
paragraphs: Across both boards the pattern is the same: written papers decide most of the grade, and one or two pieces of internally assessed work decide the rest. Those internal pieces are where Mira Road families most often lose marks that were available, because they are the part of the course with no textbook chapter attached and the part a tutor is most constrained in helping with.

At IGCSE the pieces vary by subject. Sciences carry practical or alternative-to-practical assessment, so a student has to be fluent in writing a method someone else could repeat, identifying the variable that was not controlled, and reading a graph for what the gradient physically means. Languages carry speaking and writing components, assessed for range and accuracy rather than for enthusiasm. Mathematics at Extended tier carries no coursework but does carry a paper that assumes a graphic display calculator in some syllabuses and penalises calculator dependence in others. Business and Economics carry data response, where the marks sit in applying one named concept to the stimulus rather than in reciting the definition.

On the IB side every DP subject carries an Internal Assessment (IA), the Diploma core adds the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK), and MYP subjects are marked against criteria A to D rather than against a single percentage. That criteria structure confuses parents more than anything else in the programme, because a child can be strong on knowledge and weak on communication and come home with a number that looks like a middling average. A tutor who has marked against those criteria will show you which criterion is dragging and what a better response to that criterion looks like.

The line a tutor must not cross is authorship. A tutor may teach the skill, mark a past question, read a draft the school has permitted and ask hard questions about the reasoning. A tutor may not write, rewrite or supply the work. Be wary of anyone who offers a guaranteed grade on an internal piece, because the only way to deliver that is to do the work, and the school's own authentication process is designed to catch exactly that. When you book all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mira Road families ask about, this is the boundary we set out on the discovery call, in writing, before anything starts.
A brief that simply reads all IB and IGCSE subjects IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor Mumbai is too broad to match well, which is why we push for the subject and the level up front.

sections.heading: Home tuition across Mira Road, Bhayandar, Dahisar and Vasai
paragraphs: A tutor who takes on IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mira Road almost never teaches only Mira Road. The viable radius runs north to Bhayandar, south to Dahisar and, for a tutor who lives on that side, out to Vasai. Those four places are a single working area for anyone travelling by train, because the Western Line links them directly and the stops are close together. They are not a single working area by road at 6.30pm, which is why we ask how a tutor travels before we ask how far they will go.

Mira Road station is the anchor. A tutor coming from Dahisar or Borivali on the line is at Mira Road station in a few stops, and the walk or rickshaw from the station to most buildings here is short. The same journey by car on the Western Express Highway in the evening peak is unpredictable in a way that destroys a weekly schedule. So when a family in Mira Road asks for an evening slot, we weight a tutor who commutes by train far more heavily than one who drives, even if the driver lives closer on a map.

Bhayandar matters for a different reason: it widens the pool. A tutor living in Bhayandar reaches Mira Road more easily than almost anyone else, and for scarce subjects that one stop of difference is often what makes a match possible at all. Dahisar matters because it is where a lot of the schooling is, so tutors who already teach there are often open to a Mira Road slot immediately after. Vasai is the edge of the sensible radius. A Vasai tutor will hold a weekend slot in Mira Road reliably and a weekday 6pm slot much less reliably, and it is fairer to everyone to say that at the start.

The wider pattern across the Western Suburbs of Mumbai is that matching works along the line and fails across it. A tutor travelling Khar to Santacruz or Malad to Kandivali is making a short, predictable hop. A tutor asked to come from Bandra or Andheri up to Mira Road is making a journey that is fine in July and painful by September. Parents searching IB and IGCSE tutors near me Mira Road are generally right to want someone close, and the reason is scheduling durability rather than distance itself.

sections.heading: The school calendar Mira Road families in Mumbai live by
paragraphs: International-board schooling in Mumbai, Maharashtra sets a calendar that has very little to do with the state board year, and families in Mira Road live by it at one remove, because the school is a bus ride away. The academic year opens in June, the first real assessment wave lands in August and September, and the long run from October to December is where most of the internal work is set and collected. January and February are mock season. The IB and IGCSE May exam sitting then arrives while everyone is still recovering from mocks.

The pressure points are predictable enough to plan around. August is when the first set of marks arrives and the first honest picture of a new year's difficulty appears, which is why tuition enquiries from Mira Road spike then. October and November are when two or three internal deadlines collide, and a DP1 student can find a Physics investigation draft, a Mathematics exploration outline and a TOK presentation all landing in the same three weeks. February is when a mock result forces a conversation about tier or level that should have happened in Year 9. April is the last month in which new content can realistically be taught before the May papers.

Children from Mira Road attend international-board schools in the surrounding area rather than in Mira Road itself, and Singapore International School and JBCN International School, Borivali are two of the names that come up most often in enquiries from this corridor. They are named here as local context only. IB Gram has no relationship with either, we are not affiliated with any school, and nothing on this page should be read as a school endorsement of us or of a tutor.

What the commute does to the calendar is worth saying plainly. A child who spends a long stretch of each day on a bus has less discretionary evening time than a classmate who lives near the school, and the difference shows up hardest in the October crunch. The practical answer is not more hours; it is earlier hours. Families here who start in June or July, when the week is still light, tend to arrive at October with a tutor already in place and a working routine. sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid in Mumbai's far north?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default and the lead service, and for most families in Mira Road it is the right one. A tutor in the room reads the things a screen hides: a child who has stopped writing, a worked solution copied without understanding, a page of notes that has not been opened since August. For Years 9 to 11 particularly, where the issue is as often working habit as it is content, physical presence does real work. A good IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mira Road also sees the study space, and will say if the only available desk is in a room with a television in it.

Online is not the fallback here that it is further south, and this is the one genuinely distinctive thing about tutoring in Mira Road. Because the suburb sits beyond the municipal boundary and the international-board schools are in Dahisar, Borivali and beyond, the local pool of specialist tutors is thinner than it is in Andheri or Bandra. Online tutoring therefore takes a much larger share of the market here than it does in the Western Suburbs further south. For a scarce subject at HL, or an Edexcel syllabus that few local tutors have taught, an online specialist is frequently better than the nearest available in-person option, and pretending otherwise would cost your child the better teacher. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mira Road also removes the travel variable entirely, which matters on a 7pm weekday slot.

Hybrid is what most Mira Road families settle into once they have run both for a month. The shape that works is one in-person session a week for the diagnostic and habit work, and one shorter online session for drilling, past-paper marking or a quick pre-test review. It is also the arrangement that survives the monsoon, when a washed-out Western Express Highway can take out an in-person slot with no notice and the online slot still happens.

The honest trade-offs: home tuition costs more because travel is real time, and a tutor who travels an hour each way will either charge for it or quietly stop coming. Online is cheaper and more punctual but needs a device, a stable connection and a parent willing to check in occasionally during the first fortnight. Hybrid costs admin, because two slots are two things to coordinate. There is no single right answer, and anyone who tells you home classes always beat online has not tried to staff a DP HL subject in this part of Mumbai.

paragraphs: Verification on IB Gram means specific, boring, checkable things rather than a badge. We confirm government identity. We confirm the degree claimed, in the subject claimed. We ask for evidence of having actually taught the board and level in question, which in practice means a school, a cohort and a sitting, not a sentence about being familiar with the curriculum. We check professional references where a tutor has taught in a school. And we record what we could not verify, which is as useful to you as what we could.

What we do not do is pretend a check is something it is not. We have no access to examiner registers and we do not publish success rates, because a tutor's past students' grades depend on those students. If a profile says a tutor has taught Extended tier Mathematics for several cohorts, that is what we confirmed. It is not a prediction about your child. Any IB and IGCSE private tutor Mira Road families are introduced to through us has been through the same checks, and we will tell you on the call exactly which ones applied.

Then there is the part only you can do, and it is the part that decides whether the match holds. On the discovery call, ask which board and syllabus they have taught and when. Ask what they would look at in the first session, and listen for whether the answer is diagnostic or generic. Ask what they will send you after four weeks. Ask how they handle a missed session and a session where the child has clearly done nothing. And ask about the commute in concrete terms: which station, which road, what time they would leave. A tutor who has not thought about reaching Mira Road at 6.30pm will discover the problem in week three.

On the household side, two checks are worth making for home tuition specifically. First, your building's visitor process, because a tutor who has to argue at the gate every week will start arriving late. Most societies here will add a regular visitor to a standing list if you ask the committee once. Second, the room. A tutor working at a dining table in a living room with the family around will spend half the session managing attention rather than teaching. Neither of these is the tutor's problem to solve, and both are easy to fix in the first week.

sections.heading: Why the municipal boundary changes tuition in Mira Road, Mumbai
paragraphs: Mira Road sits outside the municipal boundary of Mumbai proper, and that single administrative fact shapes tutoring here more than any other local detail. International-board schools cluster where the municipal city is, so the schools that Mira Road children attend are mostly in Dahisar, Borivali and the suburbs south of them. The children commute out and back daily. The consequence for tutoring is a thinner local supply of board-specialist tutors than the demand would suggest, because tutors tend to live near the schools they teach in, and the schools are not here.

This produces three effects a parent should plan around. The first is scarcity in specific subjects rather than across the board. Mathematics and the sciences at IGCSE are usually matchable locally. DP HL Physics, HL Chemistry, Economics at HL, and the less common languages are much harder to staff from within the Mira Road, Bhayandar and Dahisar pool, and the wait for an in-person match in those can run into weeks. The second is that online tutoring is normal here, not a compromise. The share of families running at least one online slot a week is visibly higher than in the Western Suburbs closer to town. The third is timing: the evening window is compressed, because the commute eats the early evening.

The practical plan follows from that. Decide which of your child's needs genuinely requires a person in the room, and which does not. Habit, attention, handwriting under time pressure and the first diagnostic fortnight want a person. Past-paper marking, a focused topic repair, and revision drilling do not. Book the in-person slot for the weekend or the later weekday evening where the bus is not a factor, and put the online slot at the awkward hour. Families who do this get a specialist for the hard subject and a physically present tutor for the habits, instead of compromising on both.

It also changes how fees work out, and this is the honest version. What IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mira Road depend on is board, level, subject scarcity, how far the tutor travels and how long the session runs. A DP HL science tutor travelling from Borivali for ninety minutes is at the top of whatever range you are quoted; an IGCSE Maths tutor living in Bhayandar for a sixty-minute online slot is at the bottom. No platform can honestly name the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mira Road or a single fair price, because both depend on a subject, a level and a travel distance nobody knows until you say what you need. We will not quote you a figure before we know those three things.

The last effect is one families notice only in the second term. Because the school is far away, the parent has fewer informal channels into it. You do not run into the subject teacher at the gate. A tutor who reads the school's own assessment language and reports back in it partly replaces that missing channel, and that is a real part of what you are buying here that a family living opposite the school is not.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: Four weeks is a diagnostic window, not a results window. What should have changed by then is the quality of the information you have. A tutor who has used four sessions well can tell you which specific topics are missing, whether the problem is content or exam technique or working habit, and what the realistic ceiling looks like for this sitting. Your child should be able to attempt a past question in the right format without being prompted through it. If after four weeks all you have is a report that sessions are going well, that is a failed month regardless of how pleasant the sessions were.

One term is where marks should move, and the first place they move is rarely the overall grade. It shows up as a recovered topic, a paper section that used to be left blank and is now attempted, a method mark that is now being collected because the working is written out. Grade boundaries are unforgiving at the top, so a child can gain a meaningful number of marks and stay on the same grade for a term before crossing. A tutor who understands this will show you the marks rather than the grade. A tutor who only ever discusses the grade is managing your expectations instead of teaching your child.

One exam cycle is the honest horizon for a grade change, and even then it is a probability and not a promise. Two full terms of consistent weekly work, with the internal assessments handled properly rather than rescued at the deadline, is what usually produces a visible shift. Six weeks before the papers is not. We will say so when a parent calls in March about a May sitting, because the useful work at that point is triage: securing the marks that are reachable rather than attempting the whole syllabus.

Two limits stated plainly. We do not guarantee grades, and we do not allow tutors in our network to promise them either; a tutor who promises a specific grade is telling you something about their sales process rather than their teaching. And some matches simply do not work, for reasons that are nobody's fault. If that happens, tell us in the two-to-four week review or whenever you notice. We replace the tutor from the same verified pool, you do not restart the search, and you are not locked into a package that makes leaving expensive.

sections.heading: Starting home classes in Mira Road, Mumbai
paragraphs: Three things make the first conversation useful, and all three take you about ten minutes to gather. The most recent report or progress sheet, because the subject teacher's comment tells a tutor more in two lines than a parent's summary does in ten. A clear statement of board, year and level, including the tier or HL and SL split if it has been decided. And the two or three evenings that genuinely work once the bus from Dahisar or Borivali has arrived, with the real time rather than the hopeful one.

The discovery call is free and it is a conversation, not a sales pitch. You will be talking to the tutor, not to a salesperson, and the right outcome is sometimes that you decide not to proceed. Ask the questions from the verification section. Ask what the first session will cover. If the answer to that is a generic assessment, press for specifics: which topics, which paper, what they expect to learn from it.

Session one with a good tutor is diagnostic and slightly uncomfortable. Expect past-paper questions rather than a lecture, questions about what your child does when they are stuck, a look at the notes and the folder, and a candid summary at the end that may not be what you hoped to hear. A tutor who spends the first session being reassuring has wasted it. By the end of it you should have a short list of what will be worked on for the next month and roughly in what order.

After that the rhythm is simple. Weekly sessions at a fixed time, a standing gate entry sorted out in the first week so nobody is arguing with security at 6.45pm, and a review with us at two to four weeks against the brief you originally sent. If it is working, carry on. If it is not, we look again. Families looking for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai wide go through the same process; the Mira Road version just pays more attention to the clock.

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually travel to Mira Road for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the realistic pool is tutors already living or teaching between Bhayandar, Mira Road, Dahisar and Borivali. The honest caveat is the hour. faqs.question: How does a home tutor get past our building gate every week?
faqs.answer: In most Mira Road societies the fix is a one-time request to the committee or the security desk to add a regular visitor to the standing list. Do it in the first week. faqs.question: Is online tuition really as good, given most tutors are not based here?
faqs.answer: For some things it is better, and in Mira Road that matters more than it would further south. Because international-board schools sit in Dahisar and Borivali rather than here, the local specialist pool is thin, so an online tutor is often a genuinely better subject match than the nearest available in-person one. It works less well for the first diagnostic fortnight, for a child who needs supervision to start work, and for handwriting speed under time pressure. Most families here end up running one of each.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10 and the school is deciding Core or Extended. Can a tutor help?
faqs.answer: A tutor can give you evidence, not a verdict. The decision belongs to the school, which has two years of classwork you have not seen. What a tutor can do inside a fortnight is work through a few Extended-tier past questions with your child and tell you whether the gap is missing content, slow working or exam technique, because those have very different implications. Take that to the school conversation. A tutor who tells you confidently which tier to insist on, having met your child twice, is overreaching.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one subject for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but do not force it. A Maths and Physics combination is common and usually genuine at IGCSE level. Maths and Economics works less often than people assume. At IB Diploma Programme Higher Level, cross-subject tutors get rarer fast, and a tutor who claims four HL subjects is usually stretching. The scheduling appeal of one tutor for two subjects is real in Mira Road, where travel is the constraint, but a weaker tutor in your child's harder subject is a bad trade for one fewer gate pass.

faqs.question: Nothing has changed after a month. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Raise it immediately rather than waiting for the term to end. First, check what you were given at four weeks: a specific diagnosis of missing topics and a plan, or a general report that things are progressing. If it is the second, the month was not used well. Tell us at the review and we will either reset the plan with the same tutor or shortlist a replacement from the same verified pool. There is no lock-in and no exit fee. We do not guarantee grades, but we do expect a tutor to produce a clear diagnosis within four sessions.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, and not in the room. For the first two or three sessions it helps if an adult is in the flat, partly for comfort and partly so you hear the tutor's five-minute summary at the end, which is the most useful part of the week. After that, many families in Mira Road leave the tutor and child to it and take the summary by message. What matters more than your presence is the space: a table, a chair, decent light, and no television in the room.

faqs.question: Do you cover Bhayandar and Vasai as well as Mira Road?
faqs.answer: Yes. Mira Road, Bhayandar, Dahisar and Vasai work as one matching area along the Western Line, and many tutors here teach across two or three of them. The practical difference is reliability by time of day. A Bhayandar-based tutor is the most dependable choice for a Mira Road weekday evening. A Vasai-based tutor is dependable for weekends and less so for a 6pm weekday slot. We tell you which category a tutor falls into rather than letting you find out in week four.

faqs.question: What happens if a session is missed because of traffic or illness?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule on the discovery call, before it happens. The arrangement most families and tutors settle on is that a session cancelled with reasonable notice on either side is rescheduled within the same week, and a session the tutor misses without notice is simply not charged. Monsoon evenings in this part of Mumbai will take out an occasional in-person slot, which is one practical argument for a hybrid pattern: the online slot still happens when the Western Express Highway does not cooperate.

faqs.question: How quickly can home classes start after I send my brief?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE Mathematics, the sciences at Core or Extended tier, and most MYP subjects, a shortlist usually reaches you within a few working days and a first session follows the discovery call. For IB Diploma Programme Higher Level sciences, Economics at Higher Level and less common languages, be prepared for longer, because the local pool around Mira Road and Bhayandar is genuinely thin for those. In that situation we will usually offer a strong online specialist alongside the in-person option rather than make you wait weeks for a nearby compromise.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment or an Extended Essay draft?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor can teach the skills the piece assesses, explain the criteria in plain language, mark a past exemplar, and read a draft your school has permitted and ask hard questions about the reasoning and the evidence. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or supply any part of the work, and we do not allow it. Schools authenticate this work and are good at spotting a voice that is not the student's. Any tutor who offers to produce the piece for you should be declined on the spot.

sections.heading: How IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mulund East is actually set up
paragraphs: A two-board household is a scheduling problem before it is a teaching problem, so we start there. The question is not who is the strongest tutor but how many separate visits your week can absorb. The answer for most families on this side of Mumbai is two, sometimes three, and that constraint decides everything else. Once we know it, we work out which subjects can share a tutor across consecutive slots, which need their own person, and which are better pushed online so the weekday evening is not carrying more traffic than it can. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mulund East is planned as a timetable for the household rather than as a booking for one child.

The sequence runs like this. 1. You tell us each child's programme and year: Primary Years Programme, Middle Years Programme, Diploma Programme, or Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE at Years 9 to 11. 2. You list the subjects in priority order, because almost nobody can staff all of them in one week and pretending otherwise wastes a month. 3. You give the two or three windows the household can genuinely hold. 4. We propose a staffing plan, not a tutor: who comes when, which subjects pair, and what goes online. 5. You take free discovery calls with the shortlisted tutors and approve or reject the plan before anything starts.

Step four is where this differs from a single-child match. A plan might be one tutor on Tuesday covering the Year 11 Cambridge Mathematics for ninety minutes and then the MYP Year 3 Mathematics for forty-five, because the same person can legitimately do both and the travel is paid once. The same plan might put Diploma Programme Chemistry on Saturday morning with a specialist from Thane West, and the younger child's English online on a Thursday. One home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families need does not exist, but a coherent three-person plan does.

A request for an all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Mulund East therefore gets answered with a timetable rather than a name. We will tell you plainly which subject is the weakest link in the plan and which one you should drop for this term if the week will not hold it. That conversation is uncomfortable and it saves families from the commonest two-board failure, which is four subjects half-covered rather than two covered properly.

sections.heading: Two boards in one household: what actually changes between them?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) and the International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) differ most in how they decide what a good answer is. IGCSE assessment, whether Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, is built on written papers with published mark schemes and tightly defined command words: state, describe, explain, compare, evaluate. The IB grades against criteria, which in the Middle Years Programme means criteria A to D within each subject group, and in the Diploma Programme means papers plus an Internal Assessment (IA) that the student produces themselves over months.

That difference changes what a tutor does week to week. An IGCSE tutor works towards a paper and is largely teaching technique against a scheme. An IB tutor in the Middle Years Programme is working on a criterion, which is a quality of thinking rather than a set of correct answers, and in the Diploma Programme is often working on a piece of long-form work the student owns. A parent running both children at once should expect the two sets of sessions to look genuinely different, and should be suspicious if they look identical.

The reporting also differs and it confuses households. An IGCSE report gives you percentages and predicted grades you can act on directly. A Middle Years Programme report gives criterion levels, so a child can be strong on knowledge and weak on communication within the same subject while the overall figure looks acceptable. Ask for the criterion breakdown, not the summary. The Diploma Programme sits between the two: subject grades plus comments on the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) that are easy to file and expensive to ignore.

Both systems revise their subject guides and assessment arrangements on their own cycles, so confirm the current structure with your school's coordinator or examinations officer rather than with any figure quoted online. What matters when you shortlist an IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai parents would recommend is whether that person has recently taught the specific programme and level in question. Experience in one does not transfer cleanly to the other, which is exactly why a two-board household usually needs two people.
