sections.heading: Which South Mumbai addresses share a two-board tutor pool?
paragraphs: Peddar Road, Kemps Corner, Cumballa Hill and Tardeo draw on the same set of tutors, and for a two-board household that matters more than it does for a single request. A tutor already holding three slots inside this catchment has the flexibility to take your two children in consecutive hours or on two different evenings without the journey destroying her week. Add Breach Candy, Gowalia Tank, Babulnath and lower Walkeshwar and you have the practical boundary within which IB and IGCSE tutors near me Peddar Road is a question with a real answer.

Grant Road is the nearest station on the Western Line, and it quietly widens the pool. A tutor travelling by train arrives on time regardless of the road and finishes the journey on foot or by auto, which is why some of the most reliable evening tutors here do not own a car. Tutors who drive are faster in the afternoon and slower from half past six. For a household needing two consecutive slots, the train-based tutor is often the better match, because she is not trying to leave before the traffic.

The travel reality is worth saying without decoration: South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow. A tutor crossing from Worli towards Colaba covers only a few kilometres and can still lose a long stretch of the evening to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals. That is why IB and IGCSE home tuition in Peddar Road is matched from within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs. For a two-child arrangement the stakes are doubled, because a tutor who starts rescheduling disrupts two timetables rather than one.

There is one more local point specific to two-board families. Because this catchment is small and its schools overlap, your DP1 student and your Year 10 student may well be taught by tutors who know each other and who have taught each other's students. That is ordinary in a square kilometre like this one. Treat it as useful continuity rather than as a conflict, but do ask each tutor to keep your children's coursework conversations separate, because the two should not be comparing work across boards or across years.

sections.heading: The two calendars a Peddar Road household runs on
paragraphs: Activity High School is on Peddar Road itself and follows an IGCSE pathway, which is why so much of the demand on this road is IGCSE demand and why IB families here are usually commuting out. Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo runs both IGCSE and the Diploma Programme, which is the other reason two-board households are common in this catchment: an older sibling has moved up or across while a younger one is still in Years 9 to 11. A single family can therefore be living inside two different assessment years at once.

Those two years do not line up. The IGCSE pressure runs November and December for mocks, then January and February for coursework and practical deadlines, then written papers in spring. The Diploma Programme pressure peaks earlier and harder in January and February, when Internal Assessment final deadlines, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay converge before study leave, with DP2 mocks in the preceding weeks. The overlap fortnight, usually late January, is the one to plan for: two children, two sets of deadlines, one dining table and one road that is not getting any faster.

The practical answer is to front-load. Move the lighter child's tutoring earlier in the year rather than keeping both at the same weekly intensity, and book the extra sessions for late January in October, because every other family in this catchment will be asking for them in the same fortnight. Families who treat tutoring as a constant monthly cost end up short exactly when it matters. Families who treat it as a resource to be concentrated get far more out of the same spend.

To be explicit: IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Activity High School, Aditya Birla World Academy or any other school named on this page. We name them because they are the landscape a Peddar Road parent already knows and because their calendars determine when tutoring is worth buying. sections.heading: Home tuition for two boards, or one tutor online in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Start with home tutoring in the flat. For a two-child household in Mumbai the in-person format has a specific advantage that has nothing to do with teaching quality: one visit can serve two children, which halves the travel cost embedded in your fee and makes the arrangement far more likely to survive until March. A tutor who walks in at five and leaves at half past seven having taught a Year 10 student and a DP1 student has had a productive evening. The same two lessons split across two trips on different days is a much weaker proposition for her.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Peddar Road earns its place where the subject is scarce or the task is a document. A Theory of Knowledge essay, an Extended Essay structure conversation, a mathematics exploration write-up, or marked-script review on either board all work better with a shared screen than with two people over one page. Online is also the honest answer when a Higher Level subject has no credible specialist on the island: a nearby generalist teaching Higher Level content from the guide is worse than an online teacher who has actually examined it.

Hybrid, for a two-board family, is less a compromise than a design. Keep one in-person visit a week covering both children in consecutive slots, and add one short online session for whichever child is in the harder month. That lets you move intensity between the two without renegotiating the whole arrangement, and it keeps the tutor's weekly journey count at one. It is the configuration our longest-running Peddar Road placements use, usually after discovering it by accident in a difficult January.

The honest limitations. In-person lessons cost more per hour, are the first thing an evening jam removes, and depend on one adult's week staying stable for months. Online is cheap to sustain and almost never cancelled, but a younger student with a laptop and no supervision is in another tab within ten minutes. And one tutor across two boards only works where her history genuinely covers both; where it does not, two tutors is the cheaper mistake to avoid making.

sections.heading: A tutor who claims both boards should be asked to prove it
paragraphs: Two-board claims are the easiest thing to overstate on a tutoring profile, because the subject names are the same. Any IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai who lists both boards should be asked which cohorts she actually taught. So before anybody is introduced, IB Gram confirms a government photo identity document, the qualification claimed, and a teaching history separated by board and by programme. We want to know how many Diploma Programme cohorts she has actually taken through an Internal Assessment in that subject, and which IGCSE syllabuses she has prepared students for, and we want references from families we can telephone about each.

Your own test is simple and takes one question. Ask the tutor to describe the difference between how an IGCSE paper and a Diploma Programme paper reward the same piece of knowledge in her subject. Someone who has taught both answers immediately and concretely: the mark scheme line versus the evaluative paragraph, the named example versus the sustained argument. Someone who has taught one and read about the other gives you a general answer about rigour. Then hand her a marked script from each child and ask where the marks went.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, a predicted-grade improvement, or a specific points total across two boards. No honest teacher can promise that, and the offer tells you the diagnosis has not happened yet. We do not guarantee grades either, on either board, and we would rather lose an enquiry than imply otherwise. The commitments we will make are about process: the person who arrives is the person described, and a wrong match is replaced without you restarting.

Settle logistics in the first week. Register the tutor's name with building security so that two consecutive lessons are not interrupted by an entry negotiation. Agree what happens when one child is ill and the other is not, since a two-child visit has a failure mode a single lesson does not. Agree that both children have marked work ready before she arrives. Most two-board arrangements that fall apart do so over scheduling rather than teaching.

sections.heading: The Year 11 to DP1 handover is the whole reason this page exists
paragraphs: Most families who search for two-board tutoring are standing at one specific point: a child finishing IGCSE in the spring and starting the Diploma Programme in July. The months around that line are the highest-value tutoring window in the entire twelve years, and they are the window almost everybody skips, because the examinations have just finished and nobody wants to think about school. Six to eight weeks of focused work in that gap routinely saves a whole first term of confusion in DP1.

What that work consists of is not content revision. It is three skills the Diploma Programme assumes and the IGCSE did not teach. Writing at length with evidence, which a student who has only ever produced structured short answers has never had to sustain. Designing an investigation without a specified method, which is what every science Internal Assessment demands and no practical paper asks for. And managing concurrent deadlines set by six different teachers who do not coordinate, which is the single most common reason a capable DP1 student looks like she has stopped trying by October.

There is a mathematics-specific piece too, and it decides more than parents realise. The route chosen at the start of DP1 depends heavily on how solid the IGCSE algebra and trigonometry actually are rather than on the grade awarded, because a grade can be earned with gaps that only surface under Higher Level pressure. A tutor who has taught both sides can diagnose that in one session using Year 11 papers, which is a far better use of an hour in June than starting DP content early.

What IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Peddar Road depend on reflects this split work. Board and level come first, because Diploma Programme Higher Level teaching draws on a smaller pool than IGCSE support does. Subject scarcity next. Then session length and frequency, which for handover work is usually short and intensive rather than weekly across a year. Then travel, which is why some families looking for an IB and IGCSE private tutor Peddar Road side find the same tutor costs differently at five o'clock and at seven. We publish no price list, because a figure with none of those variables attached misleads. Describe the handover you need and ask for a range.

sections.heading: What changes in four weeks when two children share one tutor
paragraphs: Four weeks in, you are checking two diagnoses rather than one, and the test is whether they differ. A tutor covering a Year 10 student and a DP1 student should be telling you two genuinely different stories: a tier and technique story for one, a sustained-writing and deadline story for the other. If the feedback on both children sounds the same, she is describing her method rather than your children, and that is the signal to intervene. Ask each child separately what she is bad at and compare the answers with the tutor's.

By one term, the sibling arrangement should have produced something a two-tutor arrangement would not: a household where the two assessment calendars are visible and the arguments about the dining table have reduced. Marks should be moving where predicted. For the IGCSE student the honest term win is a mock script whose errors are new rather than repeated; for the Diploma Programme student it is an Internal Assessment draft submitted on time and in a shape the teacher can actually respond to. Neither is dramatic and both precede any numbers.

Across a full cycle, expect each child to know the structure and timing of her own papers, coursework handed in without a crisis weekend, and a clear trajectory. Do not expect promised results on either board. We do not guarantee grades, and no tutor controls the marking, the paper that appears, or whether a seventeen-year-old slept. Preparation is the controllable part, and it is what home tuition in Mumbai is actually selling.

The case for not doing this is real and specific to two-board households. If one child is thriving and you are adding tutoring only for symmetry, stop; a tutor in the house for a child who does not need one teaches her that help is normal rather than that effort is. If both children are already committed four evenings a week, a fifth costs sleep and the marks follow sleep. And if an IGCSE student is six weeks from papers while a DP2 sibling is in study leave, choose which one gets the intensity, because trying to serve both evenly serves neither. We give that advice regularly and lose the second booking.

Thin subject knowledge, explanations one child cannot follow, timing that slips, or no rapport are four different problems. faqs.question: Can one tutor really teach both IGCSE and the IB Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: In some subjects yes, and you should ask an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Peddar Road for evidence rather than accepting the claim. Mathematics, the sciences and economics are the usual cases where a genuinely experienced teacher covers both, because the content overlaps even though the assessment style does not. The test is whether she can describe how an IGCSE paper and a Diploma Programme paper reward the same knowledge differently. Someone who has taught both answers that concretely and immediately. Someone who has taught one and read about the other gives a general answer about rigour, which tells you to hire two tutors.

faqs.question: Should we change tutors when our child moves from Year 11 into DP1?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and the decision should turn on the subject rather than the stage. A tutor with real Diploma Programme history in that subject is worth keeping, because she already knows how your child thinks and that knowledge is expensive to rebuild. A tutor whose experience stops at IGCSE should hand over, and the handover is more useful than a clean break: ask her to write a page on what your child's recurring weaknesses are and give it to the new tutor. The worst outcome is keeping an IGCSE specialist through DP1 out of loyalty.

faqs.question: Can one tutor do two children on two boards in the same evening at home?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the arrangement we recommend most for two-board households. Two consecutive lessons in one visit removes the travel cost from your fee and makes the slot far more durable, because the tutor has had a productive evening rather than a trip for one hour. Give the younger or more tired child the earlier slot. Agree in advance what happens when one child is ill and the other is not, because that is the failure mode a two-lesson visit has and a single lesson does not.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects must we keep to take Higher Level sciences later?
faqs.answer: The science itself, at Extended tier, plus mathematics at Extended. A student who wants Higher Level Chemistry in the Diploma Programme needs an IGCSE chemistry that was taken seriously rather than survived, and she needs algebra solid enough to carry quantitative work. Dropping a science at the end of Year 9 to lighten a timetable is the decision families most often regret two years later. Keeping it open costs very little in Year 10. Reopening it in DP1 costs a term of catching up at exactly the wrong moment.

faqs.question: Our two children are three years apart. Is one tutor cheaper than two?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, for travel reasons rather than teaching ones. A single visit covering two consecutive lessons spreads the tutor's journey across two hours, which is real money on a road where an evening trip can cost her forty minutes each way. But it only works where her history genuinely covers both boards or both stages in the subject you need. Where it does not, two tutors is the cheaper outcome, because a stretched generalist costs you a term of progress for a modest saving on fees.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Peddar Road depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things. Board and level, since Diploma Programme Higher Level teaching draws on a much smaller pool than IGCSE support. Subject scarcity, because an uncommon language or option has few experienced teachers on the island. Session length and weekly frequency. The hour of the slot, because an evening lesson on this road costs the tutor far more travel time than a five o'clock one. And whether you want one tutor across two children or a specialist each. We publish no price list; send the combination and ask for a range.

faqs.question: Does the gap between IGCSE and DP1 need summer tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is the highest-value window in the whole twelve years and the one most families in Mumbai skip, and short-burst home tuition is the right shape for it. Six to eight focused weeks after IGCSE papers can teach the three things the Diploma Programme assumes: writing at length with evidence, designing an investigation with no specified method, and managing deadlines set by six teachers who do not coordinate. None of that is content revision, which is why it feels unnecessary in June and obvious in October. If you do only one piece of tutoring across the transition, do this one.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our Peddar Road flat twice a week for two children?
faqs.answer: A tutor based in Tardeo, Cumballa Hill, Kemps Corner or Breach Candy will, particularly if both children are in one visit. South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow, so two separate trips in a week are a much weaker proposition than one visit with two consecutive lessons, and tutors price and plan accordingly. If you genuinely need two separate evenings, expect either a higher rate or a tutor who lives within walking distance, and be flexible about which evenings they are.

faqs.question: Is the jump from IGCSE to DP1 maths the hardest part?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes, and it is a foundations problem rather than a difficulty problem. An IGCSE grade can be earned with gaps in algebra and trigonometry that never surface until Higher Level work compresses them. The useful diagnostic is a tutor working through old Year 11 papers in June, looking at method rather than marks, and reporting what is actually secure. That one session determines whether the DP mathematics route chosen in July is realistic, and it is a far better use of an hour than starting Diploma Programme content early.

faqs.question: What if our child is doing IGCSE now but will move schools for the IB?
faqs.answer: Then the transition is academic and social at once, and the tutoring should acknowledge both. A new school means new teachers, new internal deadlines, and a cohort that already knows each other, on top of a new assessment style. A tutor who stays constant across the move is genuinely stabilising, which is one of the better arguments for choosing an island-based tutor who is not tied to one school's calendar. Ask her to rebuild the deadline map in the first fortnight of DP1, because the new school's internal dates will not match the old one's.

faqs.question: How does online home tuition work when two boards are involved?
faqs.answer: It works best as the second half of a hybrid rather than the whole arrangement. Keep one in-person visit covering both children, then use short online sessions for whichever child is in the harder month, which lets you move intensity without renegotiating anything. Online is particularly good for marked-script review on either board and for document work such as an Extended Essay plan or a Theory of Knowledge essay. It is weakest for younger students and for practical science handling, where somebody has to be in the room.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is good for one child and wrong for the other?
faqs.answer: Replace her for one child only, and do it quickly. This is common and not a failure: a tutor can be excellent with a DP1 student who wants to argue and poor with a Year 10 student who needs structure, or the reverse. Tell us which child and precisely what failed, and we shortlist again from the island pool for that child alone while the working arrangement continues untouched. Families who replace both tutors to keep things symmetrical lose a working placement for no reason.

sections.heading: How one request becomes an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Pokhran Road
paragraphs: The request that arrives from this road is rarely about a single child. It is a parent with a Year 10 student at one school and a younger child in the Middle Years Programme (MYP) at another, both on the same stretch, both home inside the same half hour, and one adult trying to supervise two completely different kinds of homework. So the first thing we map is the household rather than the student: who finishes school when, who gets home first, which evenings already have a commitment in them, and which child is the actual reason you are writing.

Then the boards, separately, because they are not variants of one another. Cambridge International Education runs its Years 9 to 11 courses towards terminal papers with a tier entry that caps the available grades. The International Baccalaureate (IB) assesses MYP against published criteria throughout and the Diploma Programme (DP) through a mix of examinations and internal assessment. A parent reading one child's criterion levels and the other child's percentage marks in the same week is being asked to hold two reporting languages at once, and most of the confusion we untangle on first calls is exactly that. Nearly every two-board household we arrange home tuition for in Mumbai starts the conversation there.

Third, we ask what is actually failing. For one child it may be a content gap, for the other a planning problem, and the answer determines whether you need one tutor twice a week or two tutors once each. We ask for marked work from both children rather than grades, because a criterion level with the teacher's comment attached tells us more than a report summary ever does. Sometimes the honest answer is that the younger child does not need a tutor yet and the money is better spent on more hours for the older one.

Then the routing, which on this corridor is unusually forgiving. Pokhran Road No. 1 and No. 2 connect Thane station to the Ghodbunder stretch, so a tutor working anywhere along the road can take a half past four slot and a six o'clock slot at the same address without crossing the district. That is why a single visit covering two children is realistic here. Anybody offering IB and IGCSE home tuition in Pokhran Road should be able to tell you where they are arriving from and what happens to their timing in July.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP, DP and IGCSE in one household: what does each actually demand?
paragraphs: The Primary Years Programme (PYP) asks almost nothing formal of a family and a great deal informally. There are few tests, the reporting is descriptive, and a parent who wants a tutor at this stage is usually right to be thinking about reading fluency, number sense or written expression rather than about examinations. Tuition here should look like twenty-five focused minutes and a book, not a syllabus. A PYP child sharing a table with a sibling revising for Cambridge papers needs the shorter slot first, while they are still fresh, which is a scheduling decision rather than an academic one.

MYP changes the vocabulary entirely. Marks arrive as criterion levels, each subject has its own criteria, command terms matter, and the personal project arrives in the final year. Parents consistently misread a criterion level of three as a failure or a five as a triumph, when what they describe is a profile: strong knowledge and weak communication, or good investigation and poor evaluation. That profile is the useful thing, and it predicts what will happen in the Diploma Programme far better than an overall grade does.

Cambridge IGCSE at Years 9 to 11 is linear and terminal, and carries the tier decision that families discover too late. Core or Extended in several subjects, decided in Year 9 or early Year 10 from classroom evidence, and difficult to change afterwards. A household running MYP and IGCSE together often finds the younger child's criterion feedback more informative than the older child's percentage, because the criterion names the weakness. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Pokhran Road who has taught both boards will translate between them without being asked, which is the single most useful thing in a two-board house. It is also the hardest quality to find in a home tutor anywhere in Mumbai, so it is worth asking about directly.

The Diploma Programme sits above all of it and the handover from IGCSE is the dangerous moment. Theory of Knowledge (TOK), an Extended Essay (EE), six subjects each with an Internal Assessment (IA), and Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices that are not simply harder and easier versions of the same course. Confirm structure with the programme coordinator and the current subject guide rather than with any website, because the boards revise guides on their own cycles and the arrangement that applied to an older sibling may not apply to a younger one.

sections.heading: Subject and level decisions that follow a child for two years
paragraphs: Every subject choice carries hidden workload, and in a household with two children on two boards the choices interact. Three separate sciences at Cambridge means three paper sets and three practical skillsets rather than one broader award. A second language begun in Year 10 is a two-year sprint with no coasting in it. At Diploma Programme level, mathematics at Higher Level brings a written exploration as well as the papers, and a science at Higher Level brings an investigation on top of additional content. Put two of those in one house in the same year and the evenings stop working arithmetically, however good the tutors are.

The internal assessments are where home tuition does its most useful work, because they happen at your table rather than in a hall. An MYP criterion task, a coursework component where a specification still carries one, and a DP internal assessment all reward the same three things: narrowing a question, redrafting, and reading the criteria as instructions rather than as decoration. Schools have limited time for that and one-to-one work has nothing but time for it. A tutor covering all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Pokhran Road could be asked for is not a real person; one who owns two or three subjects properly is.

Language pathways deserve a separate conversation in a two-board house, because the two systems treat them differently and a child can get stranded. A student who studied Hindi through MYP and wants it as a Diploma Programme Language A is moving into a different course rather than continuing the same one. A student picking up a language from scratch in Diploma Programme year one has two years to reach a standard that normally takes longer. In Thane, what a school actually offers at each level quietly determines a child's whole language route, and that is worth checking before the option form rather than after.

Where the boards genuinely help each other is technique. The command-word discipline that Cambridge papers demand, describe against explain against evaluate, is the same discipline that lifts MYP criterion marks and Diploma Programme examination answers. A tutor working with both children can teach it once and apply it twice, which is the strongest practical argument for a shared specialist in a two-board household. All IB and IGCSE subjects as home classes in Pokhran Road from one person is unrealistic, but one person teaching answer structure across two boards is not. That is the strongest reason to arrange home classes in Mumbai rather than two separate centre bookings.

The wider district sets the limits. sections.heading: Which weeks of the Mumbai school year collide for two children at once?
paragraphs: Pokhran Road No. 2 is Thane's school corridor, with Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School on it and the Hiranandani Estate schools along the same stretch, and that single fact is why a two-child timetable is feasible here. Children from different schools on one road come home inside the same half hour instead of trickling in across two. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to Singhania, to NES International School or to any other school named here; we name them because their gates and their calendars are what make the schedule work or fail.

The collisions are predictable once you know where to look. August and September look empty and are not: MYP criterion tasks are being set, Diploma Programme year one students are told an Extended Essay exists, and Year 9 departments are forming tier views that nobody announces. October is when both children's first real feedback arrives in the same fortnight, which is when most of our requests from this road are made and when the good early slots disappear. A household that books in August chooses its hours.

January is the month that genuinely hurts a two-board house. IGCSE mocks and Diploma Programme mocks often sit in the same weeks, the internal assessment and TOK deadlines land alongside them, and the MYP child's project work does not pause out of politeness. One adult cannot supervise all of that, and this is the argument for having the tutors in place before the collision rather than hiring during it. Home tuition demand across Mumbai, Maharashtra peaks in exactly these weeks, which is when the good hours have already gone. A tutor booked in January does triage on papers; a tutor booked in August can still fix the foundation that caused the problem.

March to May belongs to the examination boards and the only honest work is past papers, timing and keeping two teenagers functional in one flat. June is the quietest month and the most consequential, because next year's subject and level choices get made then, usually quickly. One advisory session in June, looking at both children's option forms together, prevents a year of the wrong course. For families searching IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Pokhran Road, that June session is the cheapest useful thing on the list.

sections.heading: Where do home classes in Pokhran Road beat a screen?
paragraphs: For younger children, almost everywhere. A PYP or early MYP child needs an adult in the room to start, to stay seated and to keep a notebook in order, and a screen makes all three harder to manage. For a two-child household the home session has a second advantage that nobody lists: the tutor sees the actual study environment, including the sibling who wanders in, the television in the next room and the table that is too small, and can tell you which of those is costing more marks than the syllabus is. That is worth the visit on its own, and it is why home tutoring remains the lead service we arrange in Mumbai rather than a fallback.

Online becomes the right answer in two cases and they are both about scarcity. The first is a Diploma Programme Higher Level subject taught well by few people, where an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Pokhran Road who genuinely knows the course beats a nearby generalist and it is not a close call. The second is the examination term for an older child, when three short marked sessions a week are more useful than one long teaching session and nobody has the travel budget for three visits. Online also keeps continuity when a child travels for sport.

Hybrid is where two-board households almost always end up, and the version that works is planned rather than stumbled into. The younger child at the table on a fixed weekday, the older child taught at home once and checked on a screen before each assessment. Agree both rates in the first week. A tutor who treats an online check as a favour will drop it in the week of the mock, which is the week it exists for. Write down which format applies to which child so the arrangement does not quietly drift towards whichever is easier for the adult.

The honest trade-off is supervision. In the room you hear the session from the next door and you know within three weeks whether it works. On a screen you are reading reported progress, so insist on the artefacts: the shared document, the marked draft, the photographed working. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai does not exist, and a remote arrangement that leaves no paper trail is impossible for a parent to evaluate until a report arrives, which is far too late.

sections.heading: Can one tutor be right for both of your children?
paragraphs: Sometimes, and the test is narrower than parents expect. Within one subject area, a strong mathematician can genuinely teach a Year 10 Cambridge candidate and an MYP sibling in one visit, because the content overlaps and only the marking language differs. Across subject areas it rarely works: a person claiming mathematics, chemistry, English and economics across two boards is spread too thin to be useful in any of them. Ask which two or three subjects they would defend under questioning, and ask whether they enjoy the younger years, because plenty of excellent Diploma Programme teachers honestly do not.

What we check before a profile reaches you is identity against government photo identification, the subject qualification rather than an adjacent degree used as a proxy, and board experience as a specific question: which boards, which levels, how many cohorts, and whether they have worked from published criteria and mark schemes. References from previous families are part of it, as is a direct conversation about which hours that person can hold for an academic year rather than for a comfortable October. For a two-child booking we also ask whether they have taught siblings consecutively before, because it is more tiring than it sounds.

Your own checks are the ones that decide, and with two children you get two chances to run them. Listen to the first session of each from the next room: are questions being asked and answered? Ask the tutor to mark one piece of each child's work in front of you and name three marks that were available and not taken. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, and be wary of one who has no preference between a nine-year-old and a seventeen-year-old. The best IB and IGCSE tutor in Pokhran Road for your house is the one who can say which of your two children they are better placed to help.

Then write the administration down, because a two-child arrangement has twice as many moving parts. Days, hours, durations for each child, cancellation notice on both sides, what happens in mock and examination weeks, and whether reading drafts between sessions is included. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Pokhran Road who states the boundary before the first session is the one still arriving in March, and a household that agreed the rules in week one is not renegotiating them during the January collision.

sections.heading: Building one household timetable on Pokhran Road
paragraphs: Start from the arrival times, not from the subjects. On this road children are often home by four, which gives a household two usable blocks before seven instead of the single late slot most Mumbai families work with. Put the youngest child first, at half past four, for the shortest session: attention is the scarce resource and it is at its highest then. Put the older child second, at six, when they have eaten and the younger one is finished. That ordering is unglamorous and it is the difference between an arrangement that survives the year and one that collapses in December.

Then protect the blocks against the things that will attack them. A sport or music commitment on one evening should move the whole arrangement to a different day rather than compressing a session. A tutor whose previous appointment is up Ghodbunder Road should not be given the half past four slot, because that is the one journey that cannot absorb a delay. And both children should not be assessed in the same subject week after week by the same adult at home, which is how parents end up supervising instead of parenting. Of all the home tuition timetables we build in Mumbai, the two-child ones fail most often on ordering rather than on teaching. Where there is a bookable society study room, using it for the older child while the younger one works at the table solves more problems than another tutor would.

Review the whole timetable twice a year rather than tinkering with it monthly. The right moments are June, when option forms appear, and the end of October, when the first real feedback for both children has arrived. At each review ask three questions: is each child working on the thing their marked work says is weakest, is each slot still actually happening at the agreed time, and is anybody in the house studying after nine because the schedule is wrong rather than because the work is hard. Most households can answer the third question honestly and do not like the answer.

Fees in a two-child arrangement follow a different arithmetic and are still a function rather than a figure. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Pokhran Road move on board and level, because Diploma Programme Higher Level work with internal assessment supervision is a bigger job than MYP reinforcement. They move on subject scarcity. They move on travel, which is low on this corridor and lower still for consecutive sessions at one address, which is the one genuine saving available to a two-child household. And they move on session length, frequency, and whether reading drafts between sessions is included. Ask about consecutive-slot terms explicitly; many tutors price them differently and almost none mention it unprompted.

sections.heading: What four weeks and one term of home tuition in Mumbai should show
paragraphs: At four weeks, for each child separately, look for three things and ignore the marks. The child can name a specific weakness in the language of the subject rather than saying it is hard. Written work gets longer, which looks like regression and is the opposite, because credit lives in the steps students used to skip. And work starts earlier in the evening, because a page they expected to fail is no longer being avoided. In a two-child arrangement it is common for one child to show all three and the other none, which is information about the match rather than about the child.

By the end of a term the marks answer, in a predictable order. Accuracy and presentation first, because they are mechanical. Structure and command-word responses second, as planning becomes automatic. Content-heavy topic scores last, because they rest on the first two. For an MYP child, the realistic target is a criterion profile that has evened out rather than a single level jumping. For a Year 10 or Year 11 Cambridge candidate, it is full attempts with no blanks and the right shape of answer for each command word. Those are the same term targets we set for home tuition students across Mumbai, because they are the ones that effort reliably reaches.

The limits need saying before March rather than during it. A child entered at a tier or a level that does not fit is not rescued by a third session a week; that conversation belongs with the school. Two years of missing foundations do not compress into one month. A child who does not want to be in the room will absorb the fee and learn nothing, and splitting a household budget across two children who both half-want it is worse than spending it properly on one. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a tutor who offers you one is selling rather than teaching.

Three failure modes recur in two-board households specifically. The first is the homework service, where both children's assignments get finished, marks stay flat and nothing transfers. The second is attention drift, where the older child's deadlines absorb every session and the younger child's slot quietly shortens each week. The third is translation failure, where the tutor is strong on one board and treats the other child's criterion feedback as a curiosity. Ask at six weeks which of those is happening, because one of them usually is.

paragraphs: Send the household rather than the subject. For each child: the board and programme year as the school writes it, the most recent marked work with teacher comments attached, and the time they actually get home. Then the evenings that are already committed. Parents who send that get a shortlist within days, including an honest view on whether one tutor can cover both children or whether you want two. Parents who send two subject names get a longer conversation before anything useful happens.

Prepare the space for two users. A table with room for one child to work while the other is taught, or a second surface in another room, because two siblings in one space on the same evening produces the least productive hour of the week. Good light. The calculator each school actually uses, charged. The school portal logins. And both children's previous year exercise books, which show the habits that caused this year's problem better than the current ones do.

Settle the building access once. In the larger developments along this stretch, register the tutor for a standing weekly entry rather than as a fresh visitor, keep the day and hours fixed so the security desk recognises the pattern, and tell us in advance if your society needs a day's notice or restricts visitor hours. If you plan to use a bookable study room for the older child, check its rules the same week rather than at six on a Tuesday with a tutor at the gate.

Then review in writing and briefly, per child. Two lines after every third session: what was covered, what the child can now do unaided. One piece of marked work read by you each month for each child, so you are reading evidence rather than a summary. If the notes stop for one child, that is almost always the one whose slot is being absorbed by the other's deadlines. Fixing that in week six costs a conversation; finding it in February costs a term.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both my children if they are on different boards?
faqs.answer: Within one subject area, often yes. A strong mathematician or scientist can teach a Year 10 Cambridge candidate and a Middle Years Programme sibling in a single visit, because the content overlaps and only the marking language differs. Across different subjects it rarely works well, and somebody claiming four subjects on two boards is spread too thin to be useful in any of them. Ask which two or three subjects they would defend and whether they enjoy teaching the younger years, because many excellent Diploma Programme teachers honestly prefer not to. Put the younger child first in the evening.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Pokhran Road for two back-to-back evening slots?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this corridor is one of the few places in Mumbai where it is genuinely practical. Because Pokhran Road No. 2 is the school corridor, children are often home by four, so a half past four start and a six o'clock second slot both sit inside the usable window. What makes it fail is a tutor whose previous appointment is up Ghodbunder Road, where the evening peak stretches journeys badly. Ask where the tutor is coming from before agreeing the earlier of the two slots, because that is the journey with no slack in it.

faqs.question: How does society gate access work for a tutor visiting twice a week?
faqs.answer: Register it once as a standing arrangement covering both slots rather than as separate visitor entries. In the larger developments on this road the resident initiates the entry, the tutor carries photo identification matching the profile, and fixed days and hours mean the security desk stops treating each visit as a new event. Tell us during matching if your society requires a day's notice, caps visitor hours, or restricts entry during events. If you want to use a bookable study room for the older child while the younger one works at the table, check its rules in the same week.

faqs.question: My children report in criterion levels and percentages. How do I compare them?
faqs.answer: You should not try to. Middle Years Programme criterion levels describe a profile rather than an overall standard: strong knowledge with weak communication reads very differently from the reverse, even at the same total. Cambridge percentages and tier predictions describe distance from a grade boundary. The useful move is to stop comparing the children and start reading each report for its weakest component, then check that the tutor is working on exactly that. A tutor who has taught both boards will translate between the two reporting languages without being asked, which is the practical reason to look for one.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tuition before the move from IGCSE to the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the final IGCSE term is better value than Diploma Programme year one. The handover is where capable students lose ground: a child who succeeded through organisation and past papers meets Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and six subjects each demanding an Internal Assessment written to unfamiliar criteria. A few sessions before the switch can settle subject and level choices, which is the decision with the longest consequences, and build the independent reading habit the programme assumes. Once year one starts, a tutor is working around deadlines rather than ahead of them.

faqs.question: What do fees depend on for two children?
faqs.answer: Board and level first, since Higher Level work with internal assessment supervision is a bigger job than reinforcement for a younger child. Then subject scarcity, then travel, then session length and frequency, then whether reading drafts between sessions is included. The one genuine saving available to a two-child household is consecutive slots at a single address, because the tutor makes one journey instead of two. Many tutors price that differently and almost none mention it unprompted, so ask about consecutive-slot terms explicitly before the first session rather than after the fourth.

faqs.question: What if one child improves and the other does not?
faqs.answer: That is information about the match rather than about the child, and it is common. Check three things for the child who has not moved: can they name a specific weakness, has their written work got longer, and is the work starting earlier in the evening. If all three are no after a month, the pairing is wrong and we will replace the tutor for that child while keeping the one that works. The other possibility, which is more common than parents expect, is that the older child's deadlines have been quietly absorbing both slots.

faqs.question: Do you cover Majiwada, Thane West and Vasant Vihar Thane too?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they draw on the same tutor pool as Pokhran Road. Thane West towards the station, Majiwada at the Ghodbunder junction and Vasant Vihar Thane just off the same stretch are close enough that the journeys between them hold up through the monsoon rather than only in September. Further up Ghodbunder Road the conversation becomes evening-only, because that stretch slows badly in the peak. We tell you which side of the junction a tutor is arriving from before you agree an hour, because that is what determines whether the hour survives.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home while two children are being taught?
faqs.answer: For the first session of each child, yes, and in the early weeks it helps. You are not supervising the teaching; you are listening for whether questions are being asked and answered, which is audible from the next room. With two children the practical minimum is harder: somebody must admit the tutor, the second child needs a surface away from the session, and the household has to treat both hours as fixed rather than flexible. Most families step back from the older child's slot after a few weeks and stay closer to the younger one's for longer.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does each child need?
faqs.answer: One for a younger child and two for a subject in difficulty is the usual shape. Two sessions let a tutor teach in the first and check retention in the second, which is where learning sticks; one is enough when the gap is narrow or the child is young enough that attention is the limit. Three or more in a single subject generally signals something structural: the level is wrong, the foundations are missing by years, or the household is buying reassurance. In the examination term, shorter and more frequent beats long and weekly for the older child.

faqs.question: What should the first session with each child actually cover?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis rather than teaching, and it should feel slightly unproductive. A good tutor spends most of the first hour on the child's own work: the questions they got wrong, the draft they abandoned, the topic they claim to understand. By the end they should be able to name two specific gaps and the order in which they intend to close them. If the first session was a general tour of the syllabus, no work has started yet. Ask for the findings in writing within a day, for each child separately, and keep them to compare against the next report.

sections.heading: How IB and IGCSE home tuition in Powai gets arranged, step by step
paragraphs: The request that arrives most often from Powai is not about one child. It is a parent with a Year 4 Primary Years Programme (PYP) child whose reading has stalled and a Year 9 Middle Years Programme (MYP) child whose criteria marks have dropped, asking whether one arrangement can cover both. It usually can, and the reason is logistical rather than academic: the hard part of tutoring in this corner of Mumbai is getting a qualified person through your gate on a fixed evening, so once that journey is being made, it is worth filling.

That shapes how we handle the brief. We ask for each child's programme stage, their school, the subjects in question, and the most recent report in whatever format the school issues. An MYP report with criteria letters and a Diploma Programme (DP) report with 1 to 7 subject grades tell a tutor completely different things, and a tutor who has only taught one of those formats will misread the other. We then ask where in Powai you are and which evenings exist, because that is what decides which of our verified tutors can actually hold the slot.

What comes back is a shortlist of two or three profiles with a free discovery call attached to each. Nobody is assigned to you. For a two-child household we usually propose one tutor covering both stages where the subjects allow it, and two tutors on the same evening where they do not, because a DP Chemistry specialist is not the right person for PYP literacy and pretending otherwise wastes a term. Arranging IB and IGCSE home tuition in Powai this way costs a little more coordination up front and considerably less rework later.

IB Gram is an independent platform. We have no affiliation with Hiranandani Foundation School, Oberoi International School, Podar International School or any other school named on this page, and we cannot guarantee grades. We are responsible for the shortlist, the verification behind it, and replacing a match that is not working.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: which part of the IB is your child actually in?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate is three distinct programmes that share a philosophy and almost nothing else operationally. The Primary Years Programme runs through the early years and is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than subjects. There is no external examination and no grade, which is precisely why parents struggle to tell whether anything is wrong. The signal to watch is not a mark but fluency: whether a child can read a question and start, whether they can explain their own thinking aloud, whether written output matches spoken ability.

The Middle Years Programme covers the next five years across eight subject groups, and it is assessed against criteria A to D in each subject rather than by percentage. This is the stage at which Mumbai parents most often decide they need help, usually because a criteria letter dropped and nobody explained what that means. The honest answer is that criteria marking rewards a specific kind of evidence: a student who understands the content but never addresses the criterion the task was set against will score low while knowing the material perfectly well. Year 5 of the MYP also carries the personal project, which is a genuine workload spike.

The Diploma Programme is the two-year final stage, with six subjects split between Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and creativity, activity, service. Every DP subject carries at least one Internal Assessment (IA), and the IAs are where most families lose ground, because they are deadlines rather than exams and so they slip. A good IB and IGCSE private tutor Powai families book at this stage spends as much effort on sequencing those deadlines as on teaching content.

One practical point that cuts across all three. Do not rely on any weighting, mark total or deadline figure you read online, including in older guides. The IB revises subject guides and assessment structures on its own cycle, and your school's programme coordinator holds the version that applies to your child's cohort. Ask them, and ask the current subject guide. A tutor who quotes a percentage from memory is a tutor working from an outdated document.

sections.heading: Internal assessments are where IB marks are quietly decided
paragraphs: Ask a Mumbai parent what worries them about the Diploma Programme and they will say the final exams. Ask a Diploma coordinator and they will say the Internal Assessments. Every DP subject carries at least one: a mathematical exploration, a scientific investigation, a written assignment in a language, a historical investigation. They are produced over months, marked inside the school and moderated by the IB, and they contribute to the final grade. Because there is no exam hall and no invigilator, they are the easiest thing in the whole programme to postpone.

The failure mode is always the same and it is not laziness. A DP1 student is given an IA brief in February with a draft deadline months away, has no idea how to choose a question, and so does nothing while feeling anxious about it. By the time they start, the good questions are taken and the available data is thin. The fix is early and small: a tutor spending two sessions in the first term purely on question selection prevents a term of drift. That is unglamorous work and it changes outcomes more than most content teaching does.

The same logic applies one stage down. MYP criteria tasks are internal, set by the subject teacher, and marked against published criteria the student can read. A tutor who sits with a student and the criteria sheet side by side, working out what evidence criterion C is actually asking for, often produces a letter-grade shift in one assessment cycle without teaching any new content. This is the clearest argument for a home tutor over a group class: criteria work is individual, because the gap between what a student knows and what they evidenced is different for every student.

Boundaries matter here more than anywhere. A tutor explains criteria, models technique on a different question, and reads a draft for structure. A tutor does not choose the research question, write the analysis, or edit the prose into their own voice. The IB's academic honesty requirements are strict and a flagged IA is a far worse outcome than a mediocre one. Any tutor who offers to produce the work is a tutor to pass on, and be wary of one who promises a guaranteed grade on an internally assessed piece, because the moderation is outside their control.

sections.heading: Which areas around Powai one home tutor can realistically cover
paragraphs: Powai is the strangest place in Mumbai, Maharashtra to arrange a weekly tutor, for one reason that is easy to miss on a map. It has no railway station of its own. Every tutor who sits at your table arrived by road, from Andheri East, from Kanjurmarg or from Ghatkopar. There is no train leg that ends anywhere useful. Everything else about scheduling here follows from that single fact, and a Mumbai platform that ignores it will happily match you with someone brilliant who cannot actually come.

The workable radius for a tutor based in or around Powai runs across Hiranandani Gardens, Chandivali, and the Powai–JVLR corridor itself, with Andheri East and Kanjurmarg at the edges. Within that radius an evening slot survives a full term. Beyond it, the approach is the problem rather than the distance: JVLR from Andheri East is unremarkable at four in the afternoon and a serious obstacle at seven, while the Kanjurmarg approach off the Eastern Express Highway is usually the quickest way into Powai during the evening peak. Ghatkopar tutors have Metro Line 1 for their own commute but still finish by road.

Few places in Mumbai have a radius this sharply defined. For a two-child household it matters twice over. Two consecutive sessions in one visit means the tutor is at your building for three hours, so they need to be close enough that the journey home is not punishing. We therefore match sibling pairs almost exclusively from inside Powai and Chandivali. For a single child one evening a week, the radius can stretch to Andheri East and Kanjurmarg comfortably. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Powai who is honest about their own travel will tell you which of those two situations they are suited to.

Within Powai the society matters as much as the area. At Hiranandani Gardens and at Lodha Bellissimo the visitor protocol is the thing that decides whether the lesson starts on time, and both allow a recurring entry to be registered rather than phoned through weekly. Where lessons happen matters too. Several Powai complexes have shared study rooms that work well for a DP student who needs quiet, and badly for a PYP child who needs a parent within reach. sections.heading: Why does the IB calendar in Powai run on a different clock?
paragraphs: Because the IB assessment year is not the school year most parents in Mumbai grew up with. Hiranandani Foundation School sits in Powai itself, Oberoi International School is across JVLR, and Podar International School is a short road hop; families here attend all of them and others besides. These are local context only, with no connection to IB Gram. What they share is an IB rhythm in which the pressure points are deadlines scattered through the year rather than one examination block at the end of it.

For a Diploma Programme family the year has a specific shape. The reopening after the summer break is when DP1 students are given their IA briefs and when DP2 students should be finishing drafts that were set the previous spring. October and November bring the first serious internal deadlines alongside TOK work. The Diwali break is structurally important in a way it is not for other boards: DP2 students who use it for exploration write-up arrive in January in control, and those who do not spend January choosing between an IA and mock preparation. February and March are mock season, and the May examination series is set by the IB rather than the school.

An MYP family's year looks different again, built around criteria assessment cycles in each of the eight subject groups, with the Year 5 personal project running underneath everything from the start of the year. A PYP family has almost no external dates at all, which sounds easier and is harder to read: there is no report that tells you something is wrong until a child reaches the MYP and the criteria start appearing.

The practical consequence for home tuition is that the right month to start differs by programme. Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Powai in June gives a DP1 student the whole of the IA cycle with support in place. Starting in November with the same student means triage, and we will say so rather than taking the booking quietly. For an MYP student almost any point in the year works, because the next criteria cycle is never far away. For a PYP child the trigger is behavioural, not calendrical: start when the child stops wanting to read aloud.

sections.heading: Is home tuition better than online for an IB student in Powai?
paragraphs: For most IB students in Powai and across Mumbai, yes, and the reason is specific to this curriculum rather than general. IB work is produced, not just answered. A tutor needs to see the student's own document, their own data table, their own draft, and the fastest way to do that badly is over a screen share where the student controls what is visible. A tutor sitting beside a DP student with the exploration open on the laptop and the criteria printed on the table works at a completely different speed. Home tuition also solves the sibling problem, which online does not: two children, one visit, one gate entry.

Online IB tuition is the right answer in two cases and it is worth naming them honestly. The first is scarcity. Specialists in some DP subjects at Higher Level are thin on the ground within road reach of Powai, and an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Powai with real Higher Level experience is a better purchase than a nearby generalist. The second is intensity near a deadline. A DP2 student in the fortnight before an IA submission benefits from three thirty-minute check-ins rather than one long visit, and nobody is driving across JVLR three times for that.

The pattern most Powai families reach by the second term is hybrid, and it is the strongest of the three rather than a halfway house. One substantial home session a week does the teaching and the diagnosis, placed late enough in the evening that the approach road has cleared. One short online session does the follow-up: checking a draft section, marking a past paper, confirming the week's plan. The travel cost is paid once, which keeps the total lower than two home visits.

The trade-off that goes the other way is worth stating. Online sessions with PYP and lower MYP children generally do not hold. A nine-year-old needs a person in the room, and what actually happens is that a parent sits in to maintain attention, which means you are paying for supervision you are providing. For those ages book IB and IGCSE home classes in Powai and keep them at home. From MYP Year 4 upwards the calculation changes and online becomes genuinely useful.

sections.heading: What an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Powai should be able to prove
paragraphs: We verify identity, qualifications and programme-specific teaching history before a profile is listed, and the programme-specific part is the one that matters. A tutor who has taught the Diploma Programme has marked against IB assessment criteria and has supervised Internal Assessments. A tutor who has taught a different board and read the IB subject guide has not, and the difference appears in week two. So the interview asks which programme, which subjects, which levels, and which years. Vague answers end the conversation.

Then there are the checks only you can make, and they are quick. Hand the tutor your child's actual report at the discovery call and ask them to read it back to you. A genuine MYP tutor will explain what a criterion C letter means in that subject; someone unfamiliar will talk about percentages. Ask a DP tutor which IA that subject carries and what a weak research question looks like. Ask what session one will consist of, and listen for diagnosis rather than a lesson plan. Ask them to describe a student they could not help, which separates honest practitioners from salespeople faster than any other question.

The household checks are separate and just as practical. Settle the gate protocol at Hiranandani Gardens, Lodha Bellissimo or wherever you are before the first session rather than during it, because a tutor stranded at the gate for ten minutes every week loses a meaningful part of the lesson over a term. Fix where the lesson happens, in a shared room with the door open rather than a bedroom. Decide who is at home. For two children in consecutive sessions, decide the order, and put the younger one first while they can still concentrate.

What verification does not buy is also worth saying. It does not promise that a particular tutor will suit a particular child, and it does not promise an outcome. We do not guarantee grades, and nobody offering IB and IGCSE home classes in Powai honestly can, because moderation, mock timetables and the student's own work between sessions are all outside a tutor's control. What we do commit to is replacing a match that is not working, with a fresh shortlist rather than a substitute.

sections.heading: Can one tutor really teach two children in the same flat?
paragraphs: Sometimes, and the answer turns entirely on how far apart the two children are. A Year 7 and a Year 9 MYP student in overlapping subject groups can genuinely share a tutor across consecutive sessions, because the criteria framework is the same and the subject content is adjacent. A PYP child and a DP2 Higher Level student cannot, whatever a tutor claims, because literacy inquiry work and Higher Level mathematics are different professions. The honest dividing line sits roughly at the MYP boundary: within one programme, often yes; across two non-adjacent programmes, book two people.

Where it does work, the mechanics need deciding in advance. Two sixty-minute sessions back to back are better than one long joint session, because the IB rewards individual evidence and a shared session produces shared work. Put the younger child first. Give each child their own physical space for their hour, even if that means one works at the dining table and the other in a bedroom with the door open while the first is taught. And accept that the second hour will occasionally run short when the first child needs more time, which is a reason to have the slot early in the evening rather than at the edge of bedtime.

The economics are the honest attraction and they deserve to be stated without exaggeration. Travel into Powai is a real cost because there is no station, so a tutor pricing a single sixty-minute visit is pricing the road time too. Two sessions in one visit spreads that overhead across both children, which is why IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Powai for a sibling pair usually work out lower per hour than two separate bookings. It is also why we match sibling arrangements from inside Powai and Chandivali: a three-hour stay followed by a long drive does not survive a term.

When it stops working, it usually stops for a reason you can see coming. The commonest, in Mumbai households at least, is that one child progresses and the other does not, and the arrangement persists because splitting it feels like a failure. It is not. Ending a shared arrangement and booking a specialist for the child who needs one is the correct move, and you can make it at any point because there is no lock-in. Families who arrange IB and IGCSE home tuition in Powai around a household rather than a student should also be willing to unbundle it when the household changes.

sections.heading: What four weeks should show you in a Mumbai IB household
paragraphs: Four weeks is four to six sessions and no grade will have moved, so judge something else. For a Diploma Programme student the signal is control of dates. At four weeks a DP1 student should be able to tell you which IA they are working on, what their research question is, and when the next internal deadline falls. If they cannot, the tutor has been teaching content and leaving the sequencing problem untouched, which is the thing that actually sinks Diploma students. For an MYP student the signal is vocabulary: they should be describing their work in criteria terms rather than saying they got a four.

For a PYP child four weeks looks different again, because there is nothing to measure. What you watch for is willingness. A child who picks up a book without being asked, or who explains their thinking at dinner without being prompted, has had a good month. A child who is quieter about school than they were has had a bad one, and that is worth raising immediately rather than at the twelve-week point.

At one term, ten to twelve weeks, something measurable should have moved for MYP and DP students. Criteria letters are the clearest evidence at MYP; at DP it is marks on timed questions and a completed IA section rather than an overall grade. One term is also when a competent tutor can tell you where the realistic ceiling sits for the next reporting cycle and what it would take to exceed it. If nothing has shifted at twelve weeks, treat that as information. The honest options are a different tutor, a different diagnosis, or the conclusion that the obstacle is not academic and tuition is the wrong instrument.

Over a full Diploma cycle the question becomes whether the student can work unaided, because that is what May measures. The limits, plainly: tuition cannot replace attendance, cannot substitute for work done between sessions, and cannot reliably convert a 4 into a 7 across two subjects in a term. We do not guarantee grades and we publish no success rates, because any figure we published would be unverifiable and a platform that quotes one is asking you to trust arithmetic you cannot check. What we do is review the match with you at four weeks and change it if it is wrong.

sections.heading: Booking your first IB and IGCSE home classes in Mumbai
paragraphs: Gather three things and the first call does real work. The most recent report for each child in whatever format the school issues, because an MYP criteria sheet and a DP grade summary are read differently and a tutor needs the real one. The programme stage and subject list, confirmed with the school's academic office if the report is ambiguous. And the two or three evenings that genuinely exist in your week once school transport, activities and homework are accounted for. In Powai that last item shapes the match more than anything else, because the tutor pool that can hold a 6pm start is smaller than the pool that can hold 7:30pm.

You will receive two or three verified profiles per child, each showing the IB programmes and subjects they have actually taught and an honest travel window into the Powai–JVLR corridor. Each comes with a free discovery call. Ask every candidate the same two questions: what will you do in session one, and how will we know at four weeks whether this is working. Compare the answers rather than the credentials, because the credentials are already verified and the answers are not.

Session one is a diagnostic. Expect the tutor to watch your child work more than they talk, and expect a short written summary afterwards of what they found and what they propose. For a DP student that summary should name the IA and the next deadline. For an MYP student it should name a criterion. If a tutor arrives with a prepared lecture, they decided what was wrong before meeting the child. A good home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents ask about will also tell you if the gap is smaller than you feared.

From there it runs weekly at the slot you chose, with a check-in at four weeks and no lock-in at any point. Parents hunting for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Powai are rarely after a superlative; they want someone programme-literate, close enough to be reliable on a Tuesday, and straight about what tuition cannot fix. That is the shortlist we try to put in front of you, and an IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai families keep for a full year is almost always one who was honest in the first twenty minutes.
