One tutor covering Cambridge Chemistry and Diploma Programme English is two different people being asked to be one. The honest test is whether you would hire each half separately. Format, in order of usefulness for a two-child household. Home tuition first, because consecutive sessions in your own flat remove two drop-offs from your week and let a tutor hand one child a task while starting the other. Most of the IB and IGCSE home classes in Santacruz West we arrange for dual-board families run as a long early-evening block twice weekly. The cost is rigidity: the block cannot move by forty minutes because one child has a school event, and when it does move, both children lose the session.

Online is the right answer for the scarce half of a dual brief. If your Cambridge child needs Mathematics, which has real local depth, and your Diploma Programme child needs a second language, which does not, the sensible structure is a local tutor at home for one and an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Santacruz West for the other. That mixed arrangement is far commoner than people expect and it works, provided you accept that the online half needs more parental attention to attendance, because a screen cannot see a teenager with a second tab open.

Hybrid is where most dual-board households land by the second term. One home block a week for both children, teaching and accountability, plus separate online sessions for problem sets and marked work at times that suit each child individually. It halves the tutor's travel, which materially widens who will keep a long evening slot through July, and it stops the younger child's session being squeezed every time the older child's deadline arrives. sections.heading: How do you check a tutor who claims both boards?
paragraphs: Ask about each board separately and listen for asymmetry. Which board's papers have you prepared students for, and across how many series each? Have you supervised a Diploma Programme internal assessment, and what was the hardest part? Have you taken a student through an Extended-tier Cambridge paper, and which component did they lose most on? A tutor strong in both will answer both pairs with specifics. A tutor strong in one will answer one pair with specifics and the other with generalities, and that pattern is easy to hear once you are listening for it.

Our checking covers identity, qualifications, and the specific claim to have taught each named subject at each named level or tier, for each board. Where a claim is not evidenced, the profile records it as unevidenced rather than presenting it as confirmed, because on a dual-board profile the unevidenced half is usually the one you are about to rely on. What verification cannot test is fit with two different children in one household, which is why the discovery call is free and why we would rather you took two calls than one.

Then the checking only you can do, and in a dual-board household it has an extra dimension. In the first three sessions, be in the flat and listen to the ratio of talk for each child, not just the one you were worried about. The quieter child in a consecutive block is the one who gets the tired half hour. Check that both children get a handover, not one combined message, because a combined message hides which half of the evening actually worked. Three weeks of one-line household updates is a signal.

Two warnings. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade for either child; nobody knows what a moderator will do with a script in June, and on a dual brief the promise is twice as unlikely. And be wary of a tutor who claims equal fluency across both systems and every subject your household needs. That claim is almost always a panel, and a panel will not notice that your younger child has stopped writing methods down.

sections.heading: The Year 11 to DP1 bridge that nobody timetables
paragraphs: The crossover summer is the most consequential and least supported period in a dual-board family's calendar, and it is almost entirely invisible. A student finishes Cambridge Year 11 in one system, has a long gap, and starts the Diploma Programme in another. School hands over at the start of DP1 and begins teaching content. Nobody teaches the skills the new system assumes: reading criteria rather than mark schemes, framing a researchable question, writing something that will be revised over months, and managing a workload where three subjects can have work due in the same week without anybody coordinating.

A worked example of what that costs. A student from a Santacruz Cambridge campus arrives in DP1 at a Juhu campus with excellent Mathematics content. Her first internal assessment style task asks her to choose her own exploration topic. She chooses something she can already do, executes it perfectly, and scores modestly, because the criteria reward the handling of an unfamiliar problem rather than the neat execution of a familiar one. Nobody told her, and the mark looks like a mathematics failure. It is not. It is a criteria-literacy failure, and it is the single most common crossover loss we see from this locality.

What a tutor should actually do in that bridge period, in sequence. Read the published criteria for one subject with the student, out loud, and translate each one into a question she can ask of her own work. Take one piece of her Cambridge work and re-mark it against those criteria so she can see the difference with her own eyes. Practise framing three research questions, two of which are deliberately too easy, and discuss why. Then set one long task with a two-week horizon so she experiences a deadline that is not a week away. None of that is content teaching, and all of it is the reason the first DP1 report comes back better than it otherwise would.

The reverse bridge, from the Middle Years Programme into Cambridge Year 10, needs a different four weeks: timed-paper discipline, command-term reading, minute allocation, and the willingness to abandon a question that is consuming time. Both bridges are short pieces of work with large effects, and both are far cheaper than the remedial term that follows skipping them. For a household running both systems, the bridge is also where one tutor genuinely serves both children, because the skill being taught is assessment literacy rather than subject content.

sections.heading: What does a term of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai change?
paragraphs: At four weeks you are measuring behaviour, per child. Each student should be able to name her weakness as a component rather than as a subject: not I am bad at Chemistry, but I lose marks when a question asks me to describe a method. Each should have a fixed slot she arrives at with questions written down. And you should have had at least one message about each child that you did not enjoy reading. In a two-child arrangement the absence of bad news about one child is the thing to chase, because the quieter brief is the one that drifts.

At one term, the schools' own marking in the components named in session one. For the Cambridge child, coursework or practical write-ups should exist in draft and have been through real mark-scheme feedback. For the Diploma Programme child, an internal assessment should exist in draft and have been read against the published criteria, not sympathetically. Prerequisite gaps from the previous year should have closed, which the students will not notice and a test will. A term with no movement in a named component means the match, the diagnosis or the work between lessons is wrong, and that is a week-twelve conversation.

At one examination cycle, the plain position: IB Gram does not guarantee grades, no tutor on this platform may promise one, and any provider quoting a success rate is selling. What home tuition reliably recovers are the marks lost to not understanding the assessment, which on a borderline is frequently the whole grade: command terms misread, method not shown, an internal assessment answered against the wrong criterion, a paper mismanaged in its first fifteen minutes. What it cannot do is replace two years of missing foundation, and in a dual-board household the temptation to believe otherwise is doubled because one child's improvement makes the other's flat term feel like a tutoring problem.

The limits deserve saying for a household in particular. Twice-weekly lessons will not fix a student who is not sleeping or not attending, and they will not rescue a subject combination chosen badly two years earlier. They also will not equalise two children. Siblings move at different speeds, in different systems, with different teachers, and comparing them across boards is not a measurement, it is a mood. A tutor who says that out loud is worth keeping.

faqs.question: Can one tutor really teach a Cambridge Year 10 and a DP1 student?
faqs.answer: In the same subject area, yes, and it is often the best arrangement. Mathematics across those two points, or the sciences, overlaps substantially in content, and what the tutor switches between is assessment logic rather than subject matter. Across different subject areas, no: a tutor covering Cambridge Chemistry for one child and Diploma Programme English for the other is two hires pretending to be one. The test is whether you would hire each half separately on its own merits. If one half fails that test, the convenience is costing you a grade rather than saving you money.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Santacruz West for a long early-evening block?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the journey has slack in it, which in practice means a tutor based along this stretch of the Western Line. faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home when two children are taught back to back?
faqs.answer: For the first three sessions, yes, and listen to both halves rather than the one you were worried about. The quieter child in a consecutive block tends to get the tired half hour, and that is invisible from a combined summary. After the first fortnight most families here are present only for the handovers, of which there should be two, one per child, each naming what was covered and what is owed. faqs.question: My child is crossing from Cambridge Year 11 to the IB Diploma. What should the summer cover?
faqs.answer: Criteria literacy, not content. The common and expensive failure is a student who executes a familiar task perfectly and scores modestly because the criteria reward handling something unfamiliar. Four useful weeks look like this: read one subject's published criteria out loud and translate each into a question she can ask of her own work; re-mark one piece of her Cambridge work against those criteria so the gap is visible; practise framing research questions, including deliberately weak ones, and discuss why they are weak; and set one task with a two-week horizon.

faqs.question: Which board is harder?
faqs.answer: Neither in general, and that framing causes real harm in a dual-board household because it turns a difference into a sibling comparison. They are hard in different places. Cambridge concentrates difficulty in timed papers and tier-appropriate content. The Diploma Programme spreads it across self-directed work, criteria-based marking and the volume of parallel deadlines in the second year. A student can find one comfortable and the other punishing for reasons that have nothing to do with ability. Compare each child to her own last term, not to her sibling in another system.

faqs.question: How do I handle two schools' deadlines colliding?
faqs.answer: Get both schools' internal assessment and mock dates in writing at the start of the year and put them on one calendar. Collisions then become visible months ahead and can be answered with scheduling rather than panic: shift the Cambridge child's extra sessions earlier, protect the Diploma Programme child's draft fortnight, and book the tutor's additional hours before the rest of the neighbourhood needs them. Because the Santacruz campuses share term dates closely, the Cambridge crunch is predictable, which makes it the easier of the two to plan around.

faqs.question: Is online tuition acceptable for one child and home tuition for the other?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the more sensible structures available to a dual-board household. Use a local tutor at home for the subject with real local depth, usually Mathematics or a science, and an online specialist for the scarce one, usually a Diploma Programme second language or a minority-board subject. The honest trade is that the online half needs more attendance supervision from you, because a screen cannot see a teenager with a second tab open. Expect to be more involved in the online child's first month than the other's.

faqs.question: Is society gate access an issue for a tutor visiting twice a week?
faqs.answer: Only if you treat each visit as a new one. Register the tutor at your building office once as a recurring weekly visitor rather than signing in a guest every Tuesday; five minutes of paperwork removes a doorstep argument on the one rainy evening the lessons actually matter. Parking around Linking Road in the evening peak is the genuine constraint, which is why several tutors here prefer to arrive by train at Santacruz and take an auto. Ask on the call how they intend to travel, then tell your gate the same.

faqs.question: One child is improving and the other is not. Is the tutor the problem?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and this is the most common misreading in a dual-board household. Two children in two systems with different teachers, different components and different term shapes will not move at the same rate, and the flat one is not automatically the badly taught one. Run the four-week test on the flat brief specifically: can she name her weakness as a component, is there a written plan from session one, and has the tutor sent you anything unwelcome about her. Three noes means the match is wrong for that child and we replace the tutor for that child alone.

faqs.question: What if we need to change one tutor but keep the other?
faqs.answer: That is the normal case and it is handled per child, not per household. Tell us which brief is not working and what specifically went wrong, and we replace that tutor with no notice period, no exit fee and no effect on the arrangement that is working. The reason matters because it changes the next shortlist: a tutor who is capable but too gentle for a student who needs pushing is a different failure from one whose Higher Level experience turned out thinner than the brief required, and the second is our shortlisting error.

sections.heading: How IB Gram arranges IB and IGCSE home tuition in Seawoods

sections.heading: How does IGCSE Year 11 actually connect to IB DP1?
paragraphs: Less smoothly than the brochures imply, and the gap is in habits rather than content. An IGCSE course rewards a student who can answer a well-posed question accurately under time pressure. The International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) rewards a student who can define their own question, sustain an argument across several thousand words and reflect on their own method. A Year 11 student who scored well by being quick and accurate can land in DP1 and struggle for a term, not because the content is harder but because nobody is posing the question for them any more.

Three structural differences matter most. The Diploma Programme splits subjects into Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), so the choice made at the end of Year 11 locks in two years of workload. Every DP subject carries an Internal Assessment (IA), an open task designed by the student, which has no real IGCSE equivalent even in subjects that carried coursework. And the core adds the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) on top of six subjects, which is where time management stops being advice and becomes the binding constraint.

Command terms are the practical bridge and the cheapest thing to fix early. Both boards use them, the DP uses a longer list, and the difference between state, explain, discuss and evaluate is worth real marks in both systems. A student who has learned at IGCSE that a long answer scores well discovers in DP1 that an answer which does not do what the command term asked scores poorly however long it is. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Seawoods that covers both boards usually starts here, because the work transfers in both directions.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) deserves a mention for families whose children were in the IB system before IGCSE or will return to it. MYP marks against four criteria per subject with descriptors that look nothing like percentages, and a student moving between criterion-referenced and mark-scheme marking needs that translated once, properly. Confirm current assessment components with your school's Diploma Programme coordinator rather than any website, since the IB and the examination boards revise their guides on their own cycles.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE subjects feed which Diploma Programme choices
paragraphs: The question most Year 11 parents in Seawoods ask in January is which Higher Levels their child can realistically take, and the honest answer depends on evidence rather than ambition. A student comfortable at the upper IGCSE tier in Mathematics has a route into Mathematics at Higher Level, and a student who found the lower tier demanding does not, whatever the university listing says. The sciences are similar: the laboratory skills a scientific investigation demands are built by handling apparatus, so a student who met practical work only through a written alternative paper starts DP1 with a real gap.

English is the quiet one. A student who wrote competent IGCSE essays can struggle with a Language A course built around set texts and close analysis, because the skill being tested shifts from organising a response to reading carefully and arguing about meaning. Conversely, a student who found IGCSE English dull sometimes flourishes in the DP version. This is the subject where a tutor's judgement at the end of Year 11 is worth more than any grade on a report, and where across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Seawoods will tell you the grade predicts least.

Subject combination is the decision parents underweight. Six subjects with three at Higher Level is a sustained two-year load, and a student taking three sciences at Higher Level while writing an Extended Essay is carrying something that shows up as broken sleep by October of DP1. Where a family is choosing between a Diploma Programme and another post-sixteen pathway, the deciding question is not which is more respected but whether this particular student works better with breadth and continuous assessment or with depth and terminal examinations.

The internal assessment pattern is where both boards finally resemble each other. IGCSE coursework, where a school offers it, and a DP internal assessment both reward a student who starts early, keeps a record of what they did, and writes about their method rather than only their result. A tutor supervising either is doing structure work before content work: a research question that is narrow enough, a timeline with the first draft well before the school's deadline, and somebody who reads the draft properly. That is why one tutor can often support both children in a two-board household.

sections.heading: One tutor, two boards, across Seawoods, Nerul and CBD Belapur
paragraphs: Seawoods sits on the Seawoods–Palm Beach Road corridor with Seawoods–Darave on the Harbour Line as its station, and the usable tutoring radius is Nerul immediately north, Sanpada towards Vashi and CBD Belapur a short run south. For a two-board household this radius matters twice over, because you are asking one tutor to hold two consecutive slots in your flat on the same evening. A tutor from Nerul can do that comfortably. A tutor from across the creek cannot, and the second child's slot is the one that gets cancelled.

Navi Mumbai being planned in nodes is what makes the double slot practical. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel each sit a short drive from the next along the Sion–Panvel Highway and Palm Beach Road, so a tutor can reach you, teach for two hours and be home at a reasonable time. The Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 between Belapur and Pendhar extends that to Kharghar for a tutor without a car, and the Trans-Harbour Line between Thane and Vashi supports weekend work. The exception is genuine scarcity: a Theory of Knowledge supervisor, a Higher Level Economics specialist or a less commonly taught second language may simply not exist in this node, and then a screen is the honest answer rather than a long drive.

A two-board household has one scheduling advantage worth using. If the two children's subjects overlap at all, which they often do in mathematics and the sciences, the tutor's preparation serves both and the standing slot becomes more valuable to them than two separate bookings would be. That makes the arrangement stickier, which in tutoring is the quality that matters most. The two boards put their pressure in different months, which is the single most useful thing a parent of two can know. Diploma Programme internal assessment drafts cluster in DP1 from roughly September onwards and again in the first months of DP2, with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay landing in between. sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid when two boards share a house?
paragraphs: Home tuition leads, and in a two-board household it leads for a reason that has nothing to do with teaching quality. One tutor arriving once covers two children, which no online arrangement replicates, because two screen sessions mean two separate hours with two separate set-ups and one parent policing both. The practical shape most families here settle into is a single visit with back-to-back slots, the younger child first while they are still fresh from the short school run, the older one second.

Online is right for the same two cases as always, and they occur more often in a two-board house because the subject list is longer. Where a subject has no local supply, a screen specialist is the only real option. And a Diploma Programme student in DP2 who already works independently gets more from two short past-paper sessions a week than from one long visit, so the older child sometimes moves online while the younger keeps the home slot. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Seawoods used that way is being used well.

Online is the wrong choice for the younger child in almost every two-board household we see. A Year 9 or Year 10 student who cannot yet work alone for half an hour needs somebody in the room, and the fact that the family has already set up a video call for the older sibling is a convenience argument, not an educational one. It is also wrong wherever the difficulty is attention rather than content, since a parent ends up sitting beside the child keeping them on the call.

Hybrid is the common end state by the second term: one home visit covering both children, plus a short screen session for whichever child has something due. Because the tutor is from Nerul or Sanpada, the screen session can convert to an in-person one in a hard week, which a purely remote arrangement cannot offer. If a tutor proposes hybrid, ask which half does the teaching and which does the checking, and make sure the answer is different for each child.

sections.heading: How do you check that a tutor really teaches both boards?
paragraphs: Ask for cohort counts per board and listen for the gap. IB Gram verifies government photo identity, the qualification claimed and the board experience stated before a tutor reaches a shortlist, and on two-board requests it asks the question separately for each pathway: which subjects, at which levels or tiers, across how many full cohorts. A profile that says IB and IGCSE experience is a label. Four Cambridge Year 11 cohorts and two Diploma Programme cohorts at Standard Level is information, and it tells you exactly where this tutor is strong.

The second question is about the internal work, because that is where a thin claim shows. Ask what they do differently when supervising a Diploma Programme internal assessment compared with IGCSE coursework. A tutor who genuinely works across both will talk about the research question, the reflection on method, and the school's internal deadline sitting well before the real one. A tutor who answers in generalities about helping students structure their work has supervised one of the two and is guessing about the other.

Parents reach the same service by several names and none of them changes what needs checking. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Seawoods families recommend to each other, an agency placement, and an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Seawoods matched by a platform all require the same answers. Searches for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Seawoods presume a ranking exists; it does not, and in a two-board household the right question is who can serve both children adequately rather than who is strongest with one. Sometimes the answer is two tutors, and an honest coordinator will say so.

Decline on the usual signals, and one extra. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because no honest tutor can promise one on either board. Be cautious of anyone claiming an official link with a named school, and of anyone unwilling to run a separate diagnostic session for each child, because a single joint session is a scheduling convenience that produces one diagnosis and two assumptions. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no tutor may suggest otherwise on our behalf.

sections.heading: The summer between Year 11 and DP1 in Seawoods
paragraphs: This is the most valuable tutoring window in the whole two-board sequence and almost nobody uses it. Between the last IGCSE paper and the first week of DP1 there is a stretch with no deadlines, no reports and no pressure, and it is the only time a student can build the habits the Diploma Programme assumes without also keeping up with a syllabus. Six to eight sessions in that window do more than twenty in the middle of DP1, and the work is specific rather than vague: command terms, reading at length, writing to a plan, and keeping a research log.

Seawoods makes this unusually practical. Because the area is planned sector housing next to the Nerul campus cluster, families are generally in town and the children are not commuting anywhere, so a morning session is possible in a way an evening one never is during term. A tutor who normally works from four o'clock onwards has mornings free in the holidays, which means the best local tutors are available at exactly the hours that suit a student with nothing else on. Across the home classes in Mumbai arranged in that window, the morning slot is the one families report as most productive.

What the sessions should actually contain is worth being concrete about. Take one Higher Level subject the student intends to study and work through an introductory topic properly, so they arrive in DP1 knowing the pace. Take one past Theory of Knowledge prompt and have them write four hundred words on it, badly, and then discuss why it is bad. Read one long non-fiction piece and have them summarise the argument rather than the content. Practise a research question for an internal assessment and narrow it three times. None of that is remedial and none of it needs a syllabus.

The honest limit is that this only works if the student is willing. A sixteen-year-old who has just finished eight examinations is entitled to a break, and a parent who books eight sessions into the first fortnight of the holidays will get resistance and little else. The arrangement that works is a gap of three or four weeks, then two sessions a week for a month, in the morning, with the understanding that nothing is being marked. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Seawoods in that shape is the single best value available in the whole two-board pathway.

sections.heading: Progress across two boards from four weeks to one cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: Judge each child separately and resist the urge to compare them. At four weeks the IGCSE student should be showing working unprompted and attempting homework before the tutor arrives, and the tutor should be able to name two precise weaknesses. The Diploma Programme student at four weeks should have a deadline map, a narrowed internal assessment question, and a first draft date that sits before the school's. Those are different results from the same tutor in the same month, and a parent expecting both children to look the same will misread one of them.

At one term the IGCSE picture moves through topic tests, which rise in the worked areas before the overall grade does. The Diploma Programme picture moves through drafts: submitted on time, responding to feedback rather than ignoring it, and a predicted grade conversation with school that is based on work rather than impression. A DP1 student whose marks have not moved but whose Extended Essay now has a title, a supervisor meeting and a reading list has made more progress than their marks show, and that is the normal shape of it.

At one examination cycle outcomes vary honestly on both boards. Some students gain two grades, some one, and some hold a grade they were visibly losing, which is a genuine success that never feels like one. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and publishes no success rate, because such a number describes whichever students were counted and says nothing about yours. What we see reliably is that the students who used the bridge window between Year 11 and DP1 have an easier first year than those who did not.

If one child's match is working and the other's is not, change only the one that is failing, and say what specifically is missing: no written feedback, the hour has become homework supervision, the student has gone quiet. A replacement is drawn from the same node and briefed on what was covered. Splitting a double slot across two tutors is also a legitimate outcome rather than a defeat, and it is better than keeping one tutor who is strong with the older child and merely adequate with the younger.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home classes in Seawoods, Mumbai
paragraphs: Write one short paragraph per child. Year group, board, subjects, examination series, and the single thing each child says is hardest. Then two evening windows that will survive to November, and your sector within Seawoods so the travel radius is calculated properly rather than assumed. A two-board enquiry written as one paragraph about the household produces a general shortlist, and a two-board enquiry written as two paragraphs produces two accurate ones.

Have each child's last marked work ready, with the marking visible, and clear two working surfaces if the slots are back to back, because the second child sitting in a room where the first child's session is still being packed up loses ten minutes every week. Expect each diagnostic session to feel slow. The tutor listens to the student work aloud, stops where fluency breaks, and asks what the student thinks the question is asking. Almost no new content is taught in session one, which is the point.

Ask for three sentences per child afterwards: what they can already do reliably, the first repair, and roughly how long it should take. Specific answers mean a good match. General answers mean ask again after session two and then change. Be in the flat for both first sessions, available for the next two, and then leave the room, because a student performs for an audience instead of working.

A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai will tell you the same thing about session one whatever the board, and across all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Seawoods open the same diagnostic way. What differs afterwards is the shape of the help. A Year 10 needs content and coursework scheduling. A Year 11 needs timed papers and a tier decision. A DP1 student needs a deadline map and somebody who reads drafts properly. A DP2 student needs triage. Say which combination is in your house and the first shortlist will usually be right.

One practical note on the bridge year. If your Year 11 is moving into the Diploma Programme, mention it even if the current problem is an IGCSE subject, because it changes which tutor is right. A tutor who will still be useful in September is worth more than one who is marginally better at the paper in February, and IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Seawoods are rarely the deciding factor once you count the cost of changing tutor twice in one year.

faqs.question: Can one tutor really handle both an IGCSE and a Diploma Programme child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and you should check rather than assume. Many tutors list both boards and teach one of them properly, which is fine as long as nobody pretends otherwise. Ask how many full cohorts they have taken through each pathway, and ask what they find hardest about the one they teach less often. Where the two children's subjects overlap, usually in mathematics or a science, one tutor works well and the preparation serves both. Where the older child needs a Higher Level specialist in something scarce, two tutors is the honest answer and we will say so.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Seawoods for two back-to-back slots?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this node suits it better than most of Mumbai. Because the school run from the Nerul campus cluster is short, both children are home and fed by half past four, so a tutor from Nerul or Sanpada can teach from four thirty to six thirty and be home at a sane hour. Ask where the tutor actually lives rather than how far they will travel. A double slot is more valuable to a tutor than a single one, so it is usually easier to fill, but it is also the arrangement that collapses fastest if the tutor is crossing the creek.

faqs.question: What do we arrange at the society gate for a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor with security in the first week and the problem stops existing. Most Seawoods complexes use a visitor app or a gate register, and a tutor processed as a new guest each week loses five to ten minutes at the entrance, which matters twice as much when two sessions are scheduled back to back. Give security the name, phone number and standing day and time, and ask whether a recurring pass is issued. If the resident has to approve each entry by app, keep your phone reachable at the start of the first slot rather than the second.

faqs.question: What changes between IGCSE Year 11 and IB DP1?
faqs.answer: The habits, more than the content. IGCSE rewards accurate answers to well-posed questions under time pressure. The Diploma Programme asks the student to pose the question, sustain an argument at length and reflect on their own method, which is why a fast, accurate Year 11 student can struggle for a term in DP1. The three concrete differences are the Higher Level and Standard Level split, the Internal Assessment in every subject, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge sitting on top of six subjects. Confirm the current components with your school's Diploma Programme coordinator.

faqs.question: Is the summer between Year 11 and DP1 worth tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is the best value window in the entire pathway and hardly anyone uses it. There are no deadlines, no reports and no syllabus to keep up with, so six to eight sessions can build the habits the Diploma Programme assumes: command terms, reading at length, writing to a plan, keeping a research log. In Seawoods it is also practical, because families are in town and mornings are free, which is when the best local tutors are available in the holidays. Leave three or four weeks clear after the last paper first, or you will get resistance and little work.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Seawoods depend on?
faqs.answer: Programme stage first, because Diploma Programme Higher Level work needs a narrower specialist than IGCSE support. Then subject scarcity, which is the biggest swing in this node: Theory of Knowledge, Higher Level Economics and rarer second languages are hard to find in Navi Mumbai. Then the tutor's cohort record on the relevant board, session length and weekly frequency, and travel, which is mild inside the node. A double slot usually costs less per child than two separate bookings because travel is paid once. Ask what the rate includes, since marked work and written feedback are not automatic.

faqs.question: Should our Year 11 take three Higher Levels?
faqs.answer: Only on evidence, not on ambition. Three Higher Levels plus an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge is a sustained two-year load, and the common failure is a student who takes three sciences at Higher Level because a future application might want them and spends two years at partial comprehension. The usable evidence is upper-tier IGCSE performance in that specific subject, how the student handled practical work, and whether they can already read and write at length. A tutor can give you a read in two sessions by setting a Higher Level introductory topic and watching where the student stops.

faqs.question: Do the two boards clash in the same household calendar?
faqs.answer: They overlap almost continuously from September to April, which is the real argument for planning in June. IGCSE coursework briefs land through September and October, with mocks in January and February. Diploma Programme internal assessment drafts cluster from September in DP1 and again early in DP2, with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay in between. The only calm stretch in Mumbai is late June and July, which is also when the best tutors in this node still have slots and when a double booking can be set up without rushing.

faqs.question: Which schools do your Seawoods families use?
faqs.answer: Mostly the Nerul campus cluster, with D.Y. Patil International School and Ryan Global School appearing most often in enquiries from this part of Navi Mumbai. Several Mumbai international campuses run IGCSE through Year 11 and a Diploma Programme afterwards, which is why two-board households are ordinary here. Tell us the school and the tutor arrives knowing the timetable rather than discovering it.

faqs.question: Does online work for the older child while the younger stays at home?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is a sensible split. A DP2 student who already works independently gains more from two short screen sessions a week than from one long visit, because past-paper practice works better spread out, and an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Seawoods marking a script live while the student watches is genuinely effective. The younger child should stay in the room with a tutor. The mistake to avoid is moving the younger child online because the video call is already set up, which is a convenience argument dressed as an educational one.

faqs.question: One child's tutor is working and the other's is not. What now?
faqs.answer: Change only the failing match and say precisely what is missing: no written feedback, the hour has become homework supervision, the student has stopped speaking in sessions, the drafts are still not started. A replacement is drawn from the same node and briefed on what was already covered, so you are not paying to repeat ground. Splitting a double slot across two tutors is a legitimate outcome rather than a failure, and it is better than keeping one tutor who is strong with the older child and merely adequate with the younger one.

faqs.question: Will you promise a grade on either board?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and publishes no success rate, on either board, and a tutor who promises a specific grade is telling you something useful about their judgement. What a good arrangement reliably produces is a student who knows what is due and when, who starts drafts before the school's deadline, and who loses fewer marks to technique than to knowledge. Those changes usually move grades, sometimes substantially and sometimes less than a parent hoped. We would rather say that plainly in June than manage a disappointed conversation in May.

sections.heading: How a weekly home tuition timetable gets built for a Seven Bungalows family
paragraphs: The useful question is not who is available, it is what the week can hold. So an enquiry for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Seven Bungalows gets turned into a timetable before it gets turned into a shortlist. We ask what time the school bus drops, which two evenings are already taken by sport or music, whether a weekend morning is genuinely free, and which single subject is doing the most damage. Only then do we look at who can teach it, because a tutor matched to a slot that does not exist is a cancellation waiting to happen.

1. You tell us the programme and year for each child, the subjects, and the two weekday windows plus one weekend option you can protect. 2. We build the week on paper first: which subject gets two contacts, which gets one, where the homework days fall. 3. We shortlist tutors who can hold that specific shape from within the Versova and Andheri West pool rather than from the whole Mumbai panel. 4. You speak to them and choose. 5. The slot is booked for the term, with a review conversation fixed at the four-week mark before anyone has to chase it.

Booking by the term rather than by the session is the part that changes outcomes, and it is also the part parents resist, usually for a sensible reason: they do not yet know if the tutor is any good. The answer is not to book week to week, it is to make the exit easy. A term-long commitment with an honest four-week review gives the tutor a reason to plan a sequence of topics instead of answering whatever homework is urgent, and it gives you a defined moment to stop without an argument. Week-to-week booking produces week-to-week teaching.

IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named on this page, and we do not take a position on which board your child should be sitting. What we do is hold the logistics together, because that is where these arrangements fail. The teaching is rarely the problem. The problem is a slot that moved three times in October, a tutor who went to Pune for a wedding and never rebooked, and a parent who found out in December that nothing had been covered since Diwali.

sections.heading: Can MYP, DP and IGCSE students share one weekly timetable?
paragraphs: They can share a timetable, and they cannot share a tutor past about Year 9. A household in Seven Bungalows with one child in the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and another in Year 10 Cambridge is running two different jobs. The MYP child needs criterion-referenced work: the tutor has to understand how the four criteria in a subject group are assessed and what a level 6 piece of written work looks like compared with a level 4. The Year 10 child needs syllabus coverage and examination technique against a paper structure that will not change much before they sit it.

In the Diploma Programme (DP) the work splits again. A DP1 student is choosing between Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) in one or two subjects and starting to think about Internal Assessment (IA) titles. A DP2 student is managing IA drafts, the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and content revision at the same time, which is why DP2 families usually want more hours and want them front-loaded into the first half of the year rather than spread evenly.

For scheduling purposes the useful distinction is which child is working to a deadline and which is working to a paper. Deadline-driven work, meaning MYP criterion tasks, IGCSE coursework, the IA and the EE, has to be timetabled when the school says, and the tutor has no freedom to move it. Paper-driven work, meaning content and examination technique, can be moved around. So you build the week around the deadlines and fill the gaps with the content. Families who do it the other way round find themselves adding emergency sessions in the week a draft is due.

Primary Years Programme (PYP) and early MYP families usually need one weekly session and a parent who is willing to be slightly involved; Year 11 and DP2 families need two or three and a parent who stays out of the room. Mixing both in one household is normal here, and IB and IGCSE home tuition in Seven Bungalows is usually sold to such a family as one arrangement with two tutors inside it. The practical arrangement is two different tutors, back to back on the same evening, which also halves the number of times you are clearing an evening for a visitor.

sections.heading: How many hours a week does each subject actually need?
paragraphs: One ninety-minute session a week per subject is the honest baseline, and it moves a grade only if the student works between visits. Two sessions a week is what actually shifts a subject that has gone wrong, because the second visit lands before the first one has faded and the tutor can hold the student to work set three days earlier. Three sessions a week in one subject is an exam-term measure, not a year-round one, and in practice it only works in the eight to ten weeks before a paper. Beyond that it produces a tired child and diminishing returns.

Subject by subject the dosage differs in ways most fee discussions ignore. Mathematics and the sciences respond to frequency: two shorter contacts beat one long one, because the skill is procedural and needs repetition. English and the humanities respond to cycles: one longer session, then a week for the student to write, then a session marking what they wrote. Languages need short and frequent, which is the one case where a thirty-minute online contact three times a week genuinely outperforms a single visit. Coursework subjects need the hours bunched around draft deadlines and almost nothing in between.

None of that means one tutor teaches everything. A parent looking for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai wide will be better served by two specialists on fixed evenings than by one generalist carrying five syllabuses badly.

The number parents should settle before choosing a tutor is the total weekly load across the house, not per subject. Four hours of tuition a week in a Year 11 household is sustainable. Eight is not, once you count school, travel on the Link Road and whatever the child does that is not academic. If the arithmetic comes out above about five hours, the right response is to cut a subject from the plan rather than to shorten every session, because a sixty-minute session that was designed as ninety covers the content and skips the practice.

sections.heading: What a term-long Seven Bungalows slot costs a tutor who drives in
paragraphs: Seven Bungalows sits at the end of the Seven Bungalows–Versova corridor, with Versova as its nearest station and Metro Line 1 running Versova to Andheri to Ghatkopar. A tutor committing to the same slot here every week for sixteen weeks is committing to a specific journey sixteen times, and whether they can sustain that is a question about the journey rather than about their goodwill. From Versova or Four Bungalows it is a ten-minute approach. From Andheri West it is fifteen to twenty-five depending on the hour. From Juhu or Santacruz West it is a weekend proposition in the evening peak.

The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, so the corridor moves and the cross-streets do not. A tutor travelling from Bandra to Andheri is quick off-peak and painful at six in the evening. Matching along the line, Khar to Santacruz or Malad to Kandivali, works far better than matching across it. For a term-long arrangement this is not advice, it is the whole constraint: the slot that holds in November is the slot that was geographically honest in July.

Here the local detail works in your favour, and it is worth understanding because it widens your choice. Seven Bungalows is low-rise and residential right up to the Versova beach end, so a tutor who drives parks on the lane and walks in. There is no visitor pass queue, no basement to circle, no ten-minute hunt that turns a 6.30 arrival into 6.45. Tutors who drive actively prefer this over Lokhandwala, where the tower parking eats the margin on every visit. The practical effect is that a Seven Bungalows family can hold a driving tutor from Andheri West for a full term where a Lokhandwala family often cannot.

What that gives you in planning terms is a two-ring pool. The inner ring, Versova, Four Bungalows and the nearer parts of Andheri West, is where you take two or three sessions a week. The outer ring, Oshiwara, Juhu, Santacruz West and Khar, is where you take the one weekly specialist session or a Saturday morning. sections.heading: The Mumbai school year in three terms, and where tuition hours should sit
paragraphs: Families on this corridor send children to international schools a bus ride away, and two recur in enquiries from here: JBCN International School, Oshiwara and Billabong High International School. Their weeks set the shape of yours. The bus goes early and comes back in the late afternoon, which leaves a usable window from roughly six to eight on a weekday, and that window is what every family in Seven Bungalows is competing for. Saturday mornings are the release valve, and the families who book them in June rather than in December get the better tutors.

A Mumbai international school year divides roughly into three working stretches, and the right tuition load differs in each. The first stretch, from the start of the year to the mid-year break, is where foundations get built and where a single weekly session per subject is usually right. The second stretch, running into mocks, is where the load should rise and where coursework drafts collide with internal tests. The third, the run-up to the final series, is short, intense and almost entirely past papers. Spending the same number of hours in all three is the commonest planning error. Demand for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Seven Bungalows rises twice a year, once when the first proper report lands and again around six weeks before mocks, and on both occasions the better tutors in the Versova pool are already committed.

Where the pressure points fall exactly depends on your school, and this is one place not to take a date from any tutoring page. Examination series, entry deadlines, Internal Assessment submission windows and coursework deadlines are set by the school as the examination centre and revised by the International Baccalaureate and Cambridge International Education on their own cycles. Get the current dates from your school's examinations officer or programme coordinator and plan the tuition backwards from them. A tutor who quotes a deadline from memory is guessing with your child's year.

Naming those schools is local context and nothing further. IB Gram is not affiliated with JBCN International School, Oshiwara, with Billabong High International School, or with any school in Mumbai, Maharashtra. We have no access to any school's internal marks, predicted grades or coursework records, and no tutor on the panel should imply that they do. What the school calendar genuinely gives us is a reality check on which evenings exist, which is worth more to a family planning a year than any claim about relationships.

sections.heading: Should term-long home classes run in person, online or both?
paragraphs: In person for the main subject, every week, same time. That is the default for a term-long arrangement because continuity depends on habit, and a physical visit creates a habit in a way a calendar invite does not. A tutor sitting beside a Year 10 student sees the hesitation before the wrong line gets written, can take the pen, and can tell in ninety seconds whether the homework was done properly or copied in the corridor. For the subject that is actually failing, home tuition is not a preference, it is the thing that works.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Seven Bungalows earns a permanent place in the timetable for three jobs, and they are specific. Scarce subjects: if the right Computer Science, Economics or second-language specialist is in Powai, Thane or Navi Mumbai, a weekly video session with them beats a nearby generalist learning the syllabus one week ahead of your child. Monsoon weeks, when a session that would have been cancelled simply happens. And short marking contacts: twenty minutes on a Sunday to go through one past paper question is useful and would never justify a visit.

Most Seven Bungalows families end up hybrid by the second term without having decided to. Two visits a week for the subject that matters, one online contact for the scarce subject, and a short call before a test. Tutors prefer this too, because it keeps their week sensible and it keeps the main relationship physical. If you want a rule: in person for frequency and accountability, online for expertise and flexibility, and never online for the subject your child is avoiding. A hybrid week is still IB and IGCSE home tuition in Seven Bungalows, because the visits carry the teaching and the calls only carry the marking.

The honest costs of each. In person, you are paying for travel inside the rate, a cancelled session is hard to replace, and you have to clear a space in the flat twice a week. Online, you lose the ability to see a half-written solution being erased, a nine in the evening video call teaches very little, and a student who will not engage simply switches off the camera. A term-long arrangement should be built mostly on visits, with online as the part you can flex when the week goes wrong.

sections.heading: What checks sit behind a tutor who will be in your flat every week
paragraphs: A term-long arrangement means letting the same person into your home thirty or forty times, so the checking is proportionate to that rather than to a trial session. Before a tutor reaches a shortlist, IB Gram verifies government photo identity against the name given, the qualification claimed, and the teaching record in detail: which board, which programme, which subjects, which years, and whether they have carried a cohort through a full examination series or only tutored around one. We take references from families they have worked with and ask the unglamorous questions about punctuality and cancellations, because those are what break a long arrangement.

For a long engagement there is a second thing worth verifying that nobody asks about: whether the tutor is actually available for the whole term. A tutor in their final university year, or one waiting on a school appointment, or one who spends two months of the year out of Mumbai, will be excellent for six weeks and gone by January. We ask directly, and so should you. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Seven Bungalows families keep for two years is usually someone whose working life is settled, which is a duller quality than brilliance and matters more over time.

Then the checks you run yourself, during the first fortnight rather than the first hour. Ask which syllabus version and series they are teaching to and have them name it. Ask what they will send you after each session and then see whether it arrives in week two. Ask what happens if they are away. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, quotes a success rate, or implies a relationship with your child's school. Those three claims are the clearest signal that you are talking to a salesperson.

What verification buys is narrower than it sounds, and worth stating. It confirms the person is real and has taught what they say they taught. It does not predict whether your child will work with them, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades. The genuine protection in a term-long arrangement is not the background check, it is the four-week review and the fact that a replacement can be arranged without you starting the whole search over.

sections.heading: What does the rate for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Seven Bungalows include?
paragraphs: What a family is actually buying when they commission IB and IGCSE home tuition in Seven Bungalows is a weekly block of teaching plus the preparation behind it, and the edge of that is worth drawing on day one. It includes the session, the preparation behind it and the short note to you afterwards. It does not automatically include marking a mock paper at home, building a revision plan for a subject the tutor does not teach, attending a parent meeting at school, or answering messages at eleven at night. None of that is unreasonable to ask for; the mistake is assuming it is bundled. Settle it in the first conversation, because the arrangements that sour at the three-month mark almost always sour over scope rather than over money.

IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Seven Bungalows move on five factors and no page should quote you a figure. The board and the level, since Higher Level and Year 11 work costs more than early MYP. How scarce the subject is in this part of Mumbai, which is the biggest single lever. How far the tutor travels and at what hour, because an evening crossing of the Western Express Highway is an hour of their life you never see itemised. The session length. And whether you are booking one subject or a whole weekly timetable, which usually changes the arithmetic in the family's favour.

Two factors behave differently in a term-long arrangement than in a short one. Travel matters more, because you are buying the same journey sixteen times rather than four, which is exactly why the two-ring pool above is worth taking seriously. And scarcity matters less in June than in December: a tutor giving up a Year 11 January slot is giving up something they could sell three times over, so the same person prices the same hour differently depending on when you ask. Booking the year early is the one genuine saving available to a family here.

What you should insist on in writing, loosely, is simple. The slot and its length. What happens to a session you cancel with a day's notice, and to one the tutor cancels. What arrives after each session. When the review conversation is. And what happens if you want to stop. Families who settle those five things in week one rarely have a billing conversation again, and families who skip them tend to have one in the week of the mocks, which is the worst possible time.
bullets: Included: the session, the preparation, the note to the parent
Not automatic: home marking, school meetings, late-night messaging
Fees move on board, level, scarcity, travel, length and timetable size
Scarcity prices higher in December than in June for the same tutor

sections.heading: How progress reaches a parent between sessions in Mumbai
paragraphs: A four-line note after each session is worth more than a monthly report, and it is the single clearest marker of a tutor who is actually planning. What was covered. What the student found hard. What has been set for the week. What is next. Four lines, sent the same evening, takes a tutor three minutes and tells you in week three whether a sequence exists or whether each visit is being improvised around whatever homework was urgent. Parents who are out of the house during sessions depend on this entirely, and most families here are out of the house.

At the four-week mark there should be a real conversation rather than a reassurance. The tutor should be able to name the gaps in order, say which are closed, and say what they expect the school's next internal test to show. Marks may not have moved yet, which is normal. What should have moved is the method: a solution laid out the way the board wants it, an essay planned before it is written, homework that stops being a negotiation. If none of those three has changed by session eight, the honest read is that the match is wrong.

By the end of a term the evidence should be on paper, and your yardstick is the school's own marking rather than the tutor's. Internal test scores generally start moving between weeks eight and fourteen, because that is how long a reworked method takes to survive timed conditions. A term is also long enough to find out whether this tutor can make a student draft, redraft and submit, which is a different skill from teaching content. Plenty of good content teachers cannot run a coursework deadline, and you will discover that in the first coursework cycle rather than from a reference.

The limits, stated plainly. Steady home tuition changes what a student can do under timed conditions, how they read a command word, and how many marks they lose to presentation. It does not change aptitude, it does not rescue a subject chosen against the grain, and it cannot compensate for a child who does nothing between visits. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, in any subject, at any level, and a tutor who offers one is telling you something useful about themselves.
bullets: Four lines after each session: covered, struggled, set, next
Four weeks: method changes, not necessarily marks
Weeks eight to fourteen: school internal scores usually start moving

sections.heading: Starting term-long home tuition in Seven Bungalows: the first fortnight
paragraphs: Bring four things to the enquiry and the setup takes days rather than a fortnight. The most recent report and one marked paper per subject, teacher comments included, because those say more than a parent's summary. The programme and year for each child, with Higher Level and Standard Level choices if they are settled. Two weekday windows you can genuinely protect plus one weekend option. And one sentence on the outcome you want: a grade lifted, a topic rescued, coursework submitted on time, or a child who stops dreading the subject.

The first session is a diagnosis. Expect the tutor to spend most of it on your child's own written work rather than teaching from the front: a past paper question attempted cold, a marked test gone through line by line, two or three topics probed to find where understanding actually stops. They should finish by saying out loud, in front of the student, the order in which they will fix things and roughly how long the first block takes. If instead they deliver a polished lesson and ask nothing, you have hired a performer rather than a teacher.

The second session is where you learn whether the arrangement will hold. Did the note arrive? Was the homework set and then actually checked? Did the tutor start where the diagnosis ended rather than from the top? Did they arrive at the agreed time without a message about traffic? Those four answers in week two predict the next six months better than any credential does. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Seven Bungalows who gets all four right in the first fortnight is usually still there in March.

If something is wrong, say it in week two or three. Name the specific thing rather than offering a general impression, and a replacement is arranged with the diagnosis notes handed across so your child is not interviewed twice about the same gaps. Parents who ask us for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Seven Bungalows almost always want this and cannot phrase it: not a prodigy, but someone who comes at the same time every week, teaches a planned sequence, writes four honest lines afterwards, and says clearly at four weeks whether this is working.
bullets: Have reports, one marked paper per subject, and protected slots ready
First session diagnoses from the student's own work
Week two tests the note, the homework check and the arrival time
Name the specific problem early; notes transfer to a replacement
Judge the fortnight, then judge the term, not the first ninety minutes

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Year 10 student in Seven Bungalows have?
faqs.answer: Two per subject for the subject that has gone wrong, one for subjects you are maintaining, and no more than about five hours across the household. Two sessions a week works because the second lands before the first has faded, so the tutor can hold the student to work set three days earlier rather than restarting each visit. One session a week holds ground and rarely moves a grade on its own. If the arithmetic pushes past five hours once you count school and travel, drop a subject from the plan instead of shortening every session.

faqs.question: Should we book for the whole term or only for the exam term?
faqs.answer: Book the term, with an honest review at four weeks. Term booking is what lets a tutor plan a sequence of topics instead of firefighting whatever homework is due, and it is the difference between teaching and supervision. Exam-term-only booking has a second problem specific to this corridor: by the time January arrives, the tutors in the Versova and Andheri West pool who can hold a 7pm slot are already committed to families who booked in June. If you want exam-term intensity, book the slot early at one session a week and increase it later. Most families who run IB and IGCSE home tuition in Seven Bungalows for a full year started with a single weekly slot taken before the school year opened.

faqs.question: What happens to our slot when the tutor has to travel out of Mumbai?
faqs.answer: The slot is held, and you should agree how before it happens. Three workable arrangements exist: the session runs as a video call from wherever the tutor is, a named cover tutor takes it with the diagnosis notes handed over, or the slot is formally skipped and made up on an agreed weekend morning. What should never happen is silence followed by a three-week gap. Ask in the first conversation how much notice you will get and which of those three is the default, because a tutor who has thought about it will answer immediately.

faqs.question: How will I know what was covered if I am not at home during the session?
faqs.answer: From a short written note the same evening, which you should treat as part of the arrangement rather than a favour. Four lines are enough: what was covered, what the student struggled with, what has been set, and what comes next. If that note stops arriving in week three, the teaching has usually stopped being planned at the same time. Most parents on this corridor are not in the flat at seven in the evening, so the note is the whole feedback loop, and it is also your evidence at the four-week review.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Seven Bungalows not include?
faqs.answer: Usually anything that happens outside the session: marking a full mock paper at home, building a revision timetable for subjects the tutor does not teach, attending a school meeting, or replying to messages late at night. None of it is an unreasonable request and some tutors include some of it. The error is assuming. Settle the scope in the first conversation along with the slot, the cancellation terms and what arrives after each session, because long arrangements that go wrong at three months almost always go wrong over scope rather than over the rate. Ask what the quoted hour for IB and IGCSE home classes in Seven Bungalows covers before the second session, not after the third month.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover a DP student and an IGCSE sibling in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Rarely the same tutor, but very often the same evening, and that is the arrangement worth asking for. Diploma Programme Higher Level work and Year 10 Cambridge work need different specialists past about Year 9, so expect two people. Scheduling them back to back on one evening means you clear the space once, the flat is set up once, and you are not hosting visitors four nights a week. Tutors in the Versova and Four Bungalows pool will often coordinate the handover themselves once they know the other slot exists.

faqs.question: Do we pay for a session we cancel on the day?
faqs.answer: That depends on what you agreed in week one, which is why it should be agreed in week one. The common and fair arrangement is that a session cancelled with a day's notice is rescheduled or dropped without charge, and one cancelled on the day is charged, because the tutor has already given up the slot and travelled or prepared. The mirror of that matters just as much: ask what happens when the tutor cancels on the day. A reasonable answer involves a makeup session rather than an apology.

faqs.question: Is one ninety-minute session better than two sixty-minute ones?
faqs.answer: For maths and the sciences, two sixty-minute sessions are better. The skill is procedural, so repetition across the week beats a single long stretch, and the second contact lets the tutor check work set three days earlier. For English, the humanities and coursework subjects, one longer session is better, because the useful unit is read, plan, write, then mark, and that does not fit into an hour. Languages are the clear case for short and frequent. Decide per subject rather than setting one house rule.

faqs.question: Can the tutor also mark work between sessions?
faqs.answer: Many will, and you should ask rather than assume it is included. Marking a timed past paper properly against a mark scheme takes a tutor the better part of an hour, so expect it to be treated as work rather than goodwill. A sensible middle arrangement is that short pieces and homework are marked in the session itself, while full mock papers are either marked as paid work or brought to the next visit and gone through together. The second option is often more useful anyway, since the student hears the reasoning.

faqs.question: Does a tutor parking on our lane in Seven Bungalows change the rate?
faqs.answer: Not directly, but it changes who will take the slot, which matters more over a term. Because Seven Bungalows is low-rise right up to the Versova beach end, a tutor who drives parks on the lane and walks in, with no visitor pass queue and no basement to circle. Tutors who drive prefer this corridor to the Lokhandwala towers for exactly that reason, so your shortlist is slightly deeper than the distance from the station suggests. What does affect the rate is the length and timing of their journey, not where the car ends up.

faqs.question: Our DP2 child has Internal Assessment deadlines and mocks in the same month. How do we split the hours?
faqs.answer: Deadlines first, content second, because a draft cannot be moved and revision can. Put the hours onto the Internal Assessment in the fortnight before the school's submission date, drop content sessions to one a week while that runs, then swap the ratio immediately afterwards for the mocks. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are the two that get squeezed out and then become emergencies in the last term. Confirm every date with your programme coordinator rather than working from last year's calendar, since the school sets those windows.

faqs.question: When should we stop home tuition altogether?
faqs.answer: When the student starts correcting their own work before the tutor arrives, and when the school's internal marks have held for two cycles rather than one. A good tutor will raise this before you do, and that is the clearest sign you hired a teacher. Stopping abruptly in the term before a final series is usually a mistake even when things look settled, because exam technique decays faster than content. A reasonable taper is from two sessions a week to one, then to a fortnightly check, rather than stopping in one step.

We will come back with a proposed weekly shape and two or three tutors from the Versova and Andheri West pool who can hold it for the term. You speak to them first. The slot, the cancellation terms and the review date are settled before the first session, so nothing important gets discussed for the first time in the week of the mocks.

sections.heading: How a home tuition request from Sewri becomes a shortlist
paragraphs: A request for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Sewri usually arrives with three facts and a dozen missing ones. A parent writes that their daughter is in Year 10, that maths and chemistry are the problem, and that anything earlier than seven in the evening is impossible because of the school bus run. What is still unknown is which board the school actually enters students for, whether the difficulty sits inside one topic or in the whole habit of working alone, and how many weeks the family expects this to run. The first phone call exists to get those three answers on the table, because every later decision follows from them.

Once they are known, matching becomes a scheduling problem as much as an academic one. South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow, so a tutor who lives towards Wadala and already teaches two students near Parel can hold a Tuesday and Friday slot in Sewri for thirty weeks without drama. A tutor living off the Western Express Highway cannot, however good the subject knowledge, because the fourth cancelled session in a row ends the arrangement anyway. We shortlist for the slot you genuinely need first and the subject second, since a weekly commitment that collapses in week six has taught nobody anything and cost a term of momentum.

You then speak to every shortlisted tutor yourself before anyone is booked. Ten minutes on a call tells a parent more than any written profile. Listen for whether the tutor asks to see the last school report before the first session, whether they ask which syllabus code the school is running, and whether they are willing to say plainly that a particular subject is not theirs. A home tutor who asks for the name of the coordinator and the date of the next unit test is reading the job correctly. One who promises a specific grade in the opening conversation is telling you they have not looked at the work yet.

The diagnostic session comes next, and it is deliberately not a lesson. The tutor sits at your dining table with the last two class tests and one past paper question, watches where the pen stops moving, and writes you a short note on what the real gap is. Sometimes that note says a standing weekly arrangement is the wrong purchase and four focused sessions before the next unit test would do more. We would rather lose a booking than set up IB and IGCSE home tuition in Sewri that nobody in the family actually needed.

sections.heading: IB or IGCSE in Mumbai: which structure is your child actually inside?
paragraphs: Your child sits inside one of three structures, and the answer changes what tuition is for. Cambridge IGCSE runs roughly Years 9 to 11 and is examined externally at the end, with a Core or Extended tier entry decided subject by subject. The International Baccalaureate Middle Years Programme (MYP) is criterion-assessed through school tasks. The IB Diploma Programme (DP) occupies Years 11 and 12 with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices. Ask the school which one, in writing, before you book a tutor.

This matters more in the Sewri and Parel pocket than it does in most of Mumbai, because the schools families here use run both pathways under one roof. A parent can have one child doing MYP coursework and an older one sitting Cambridge papers, and the two need different help entirely. MYP work is marked against published criteria by the child's own teacher, so the useful intervention is understanding what the criterion wording is asking for. IGCSE work is marked by an external examiner who has never met the student, so the useful intervention is paper technique against a published mark scheme.

There is a third possibility that catches families out at admission time. Some Mumbai schools enter students for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE rather than Cambridge International Education, and a few run both in different subjects. The syllabus names look similar and the papers are not. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Sewri who has taught the wrong board's specification will be teaching correct mathematics against the wrong assessment objectives, which is a subtle way to waste a term. Confirm the awarding body and the syllabus code with the school examinations officer, then put both in your tuition request.

For the Years 9 to 11 window this page is written for, the practical sequence is straightforward. Year 9 is where the tier and subject decisions get made, often faster than parents expect. Year 10 is where the coursework and the first serious internal examinations land. Year 11 is where paper technique either exists or does not. Tuition started in Year 9 is a cheaper and calmer thing than tuition started in Year 11, because the work is building a habit rather than reversing one. Both are worth doing. They are not the same purchase.
bullets: Get the awarding body and syllabus code in writing from the school

sections.heading: How do you choose subjects across both boards in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Choose on evidence from the last two years of marked work, not on which subject sounds impressive on a university application. At Cambridge IGCSE the live question is Core or Extended tier per subject. At IB Diploma level it is which three subjects go to Higher Level (HL) and which three stay at Standard Level (SL). Every subject in both systems also carries internal assessment that the student produces and the school marks or moderates, and that is where most of the quiet mark loss happens.

The tier decision is the one parents most often get wrong, in both directions. Entering a capable student at Core caps the grade available to them regardless of how well they perform. Entering a struggling student at Extended on principle produces a paper they cannot finish. The honest test is a full past paper under timed conditions in Year 10, marked against the published scheme, with the tutor and the subject teacher both looking at the script. Ask the school examinations officer what the current entry deadline for tier changes is, because it closes earlier in the year than families assume.

At Diploma level the Higher Level choice has a second-order effect families underestimate. Three Higher Level subjects each carry a deeper internal assessment and a heavier reading load, and they all land in the same calendar months as the Extended Essay (EE) and the Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay. A student who has chosen three Higher Level sciences has not chosen three harder subjects, they have chosen a January that does not fit in a week. A good tutor will tell you that in Year 11, before the choice is locked, rather than in Year 12 when it cannot be changed.

A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families might want does not exist, and anyone offering it should be treated carefully. Mathematics, physics, chemistry, economics, English and the second-language subjects each need someone who has taught that specification and marked that paper. What a platform can do is cover all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Sewri might be asked for by matching a different specialist per subject, usually with one of them acting as the main point of contact. Do not reproduce weightings or timings from any blog. Read the current subject guide the school uses.
