sections.heading: Two boards in one flat: how IB and IGCSE differ in practice
paragraphs: The difference parents feel first is not difficulty, it is how marks are earned. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE courses build towards written papers sat in one block at the end of a two-year run, with practical or coursework components set along the way. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs criterion-referenced assessment through MYP and then moves into the Diploma Programme (DP), where Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices, Internal Assessment (IA) coursework, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) all run in parallel across two years.

That produces genuinely different homework. An IGCSE Year 10 student should be building a bank of marked past-paper answers and learning what each command word demands. An MYP Year 8 student should be learning to read a task-specific rubric and to write the reflection and evaluation sections that criteria C and D reward. A parent who applies the same standard to both children will conclude that one is working harder than the other, when in fact they are being measured on different things entirely.

There is one more practical difference worth knowing. IGCSE results arrive as a set of subject grades that feed into a sixth-form decision; IB DP results arrive as a points total with core requirements attached. Families here often run an IGCSE child towards a DP entry two years later, which means the Extended tier choices made in Year 9 matter for what the Diploma will allow. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Wadala East parents hire for both children should be able to explain that link in one sentence. Programme structures are revised on the boards' own cycles, so confirm current requirements with your school's coordinator.

sections.heading: Which subjects overlap between the boards, and which do not?

The subjects that do not transfer are the ones built around their own assessment machinery. MYP Design, Visual Arts and the personal project have no IGCSE equivalent. DP Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are IB-only pieces of work with their own assessment criteria. On the Cambridge and Edexcel side, the alternative-to-practical paper, the coursework routes in History and Geography, and the language orals are specific skills that an IB-only tutor will not have taught. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Wadala East is asked to cover, this is where the honest limit sits.

Ask what they would do with your Year 10 student's last marked paper and with your MYP child's last marked task, and expect the mark scheme to come up in one answer and the rubric in the other. A tutor who gives one blended answer for both children has not understood the request. The best IB and IGCSE tutor in Wadala East for your household is the one who sees two distinct problems.

Two warnings are worth stating plainly. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or quotes a success rate, because nobody who has taught a full cohort on either board speaks that way. And be cautious of a tutor reluctant to be registered at the security desk under their real name, or who wants to shift the lesson somewhere else in the first fortnight. sections.heading: What does the IGCSE to Diploma Programme bridge actually need?
paragraphs: Three things, and none of them is more content. The first is independent reading and note-taking, because the Diploma Programme assumes a student can work from a source without being walked through it, and an IGCSE student who has been taught to a mark scheme for two years often cannot. The second is extended writing: DP essays and IA reports are longer and more structured than anything IGCSE asked for. The third is deadline management across parallel commitments, which is the thing that actually breaks students in DP1.

The subject choices made at IGCSE constrain the Diploma more than parents realise. A student entered for Core rather than Extended Mathematics, or who dropped a science, finds some HL combinations closed two years later. This is why we treat the Year 9 option conversation as part of the bridge rather than a separate event, and why IB and IGCSE home tuition in Wadala East is often booked for a Year 9 child whose grades are fine. The work there is strategic rather than remedial, and it is cheaper than the remedial version in DP1. Few families in Mumbai think about the bridge until the first Diploma report arrives.

Cost follows the same shape. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Wadala East depend on the level, the subject's local scarcity, the tutor's travel, the session length and frequency, and whether marking between lessons is included. Two children on two boards is not twice one child if the slots are back to back, because the travel leg is shared; it is close to twice if they need separate specialists on separate days. Ask every tutor whether draft marking between sessions is in the fee, because that assumption causes most mid-term disputes.

paragraphs: Measure each child separately, on the signs that fit their board. For the IGCSE child, four weeks should bring better question habits: writing down what the question gives before reaching for a method, attempting the long-mark questions, summarising the last lesson unprompted. For the MYP or DP child, four weeks should bring the ability to name the criterion or component being assessed and to explain what a higher band would require. Neither of those is a grade change, and a tutor promising one in a month is not watching your child.

Across a term, the gaps named in week one should be closed and retested for both children, and the school's feedback should shift from effort to accuracy. A term is also long enough to prove a mismatch, and with two children it is common for one match to work and the other not. A Year 11 student who began the year two years behind in algebra will close real ground and may still not reach the band the family hoped for, and a DP1 student who cannot yet plan parallel deadlines will not be fixed by a single term of weekly sessions. sections.heading: Choosing six Diploma subjects: the decisions made in the MYP year before
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate runs as three connected programmes. The Primary Years Programme covers the early school years with no external examinations. The Middle Years Programme spans the next five years and marks against published criteria rather than percentages. The Diploma Programme fills the final two years with six subjects, three usually at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and an Internal Assessment (IA) in every subject.

The decision that shapes everything is taken at the end of the Middle Years Programme, when a fifteen-year-old picks six subjects across the subject groups and nominates which three go to Higher Level. Families treat this as a preference exercise. It is closer to a structural commitment, because Higher Level is not a longer version of Standard Level; it adds material and asks a different kind of question. A student who enjoyed Biology at Middle Years and chooses it at Higher Level because she liked the teacher is making a two-year decision on one year of evidence.

Three mistakes recur in this pocket of Mumbai often enough to be worth naming. Choosing a Mathematics route by reputation rather than by what the student actually wants to study later, when Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation suit genuinely different destinations. Taking three sciences at Higher Level because a university listing somewhere mentioned it, which produces a timetable with three investigations due in the same term. And treating Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay as administrative, when both are graded and both can move the final outcome.

A tutor hired in the final Middle Years year or the first Diploma year is often doing subject-choice work rather than subject teaching, and that is time well spent. The honest conversation is about what the child wants to study after school, what she is genuinely good at as opposed to what she enjoys, and what the combination will feel like in the second Diploma year when the coursework stacks. Component structures and subject-group rules are revised by the IB on its own cycle, so confirm the current requirements with your school's Diploma coordinator rather than relying on any figure printed in a guide.

Middle Years marks published criteria rather than percentages

sections.heading: What a Higher Level choice commits your child to
paragraphs: Subject choice across the programme, the Higher Level and Standard Level decision, and the internal assessment each subject carries are the three things a tutor in this pocket is most often hired to untangle. Take the sciences first. At Higher Level the syllabus includes material that Standard Level does not meet at all, and the examination asks the student to apply it to unfamiliar contexts rather than recall it. A student who is comfortable with the Standard Level content and uncomfortable with being asked something she has not seen before will find the Higher Level paper genuinely different in kind.

Mathematics divides along a different axis. Analysis and Approaches is the route for students heading towards engineering, physics, economics at a quantitative university, or mathematics itself; Applications and Interpretation suits destinations where modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work matter more than proof. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level. The common error is choosing the route by perceived prestige and then discovering that the required habits of mind do not match the student's.

The languages carry an oral component assessed internally, which is where confident writers often lose ground, and Language A carries literary analysis that a student can be entirely unprepared for if the Middle Years work leaned towards comprehension. Individuals and Societies subjects reward precise use of terminology and a structured argument, and they punish the well-written essay that never engages with the specific command word in the question.

Each subject also carries its own internal assessment, and that is the common thread. An investigation, an exploration, an oral, a research essay: produced over months, marked against published criteria, and declared as the student's own work. A tutor may teach the skill, press on the research question until it is answerable, explain what each criterion rewards and give feedback on a draft. A tutor may not write any part of it. Anyone offering to rewrite your daughter's draft is proposing to put an academic honesty case on her record, and we decline that request every time it is made. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai schools teach is not a real professional; a specialist for the two subjects causing trouble is.

sections.heading: Does the school calendar in Mumbai decide when to start tutoring?
paragraphs: Largely, yes, and the best month to start is August rather than January. Families here mostly attend JBCN International School, Parel and Don Bosco International School, with some travelling to Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo or Bombay International School at Babulnath. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here; we name them because their internal calendars, not ours, set the months when a child stops coping.

The year opens in June in the monsoon, and the first weeks are quiet in a misleading way. A new Middle Years cohort meets criteria nobody has taught them to read. A first-year Diploma group meets six subjects at once and begins to discover that one or two choices were made for the wrong reasons. No work is due. Then the first criterion-marked tasks come back in late August, and that is the month when a parent has maximum information and maximum runway. Starting then is cheap in every sense.

October and November are the first genuine crunch: internal examinations, the earliest Internal Assessment checkpoints, and for second-year Diploma students the Extended Essay drafts that have been comfortably postponed since the summer. December loses half its weeks to the break and to travel. January and February are the mock examination months, and they are when most enquiries actually arrive, by which point a tutor is triaging rather than teaching.

For a Primary Years child there is no examination to anchor any of this, which makes the signal harder to read and the delay longer. A slide in reading fluency or number confidence shows up as reluctance rather than a mark, and it shows up in the same October window because that is when the work steps up. Parents wait for a report that never says anything alarming. If your eight-year-old has started avoiding a subject, that is the signal, and waiting for evidence that looks like a grade means waiting a year. Term dates shift annually, so check your own school's published calendar rather than any date in a listing.

sections.heading: Home classes, online or both for an IB student in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home classes are the default here and the reason is physical rather than sentimental. A tutor at the table sees the page, the crossing-out, the reach for the calculator, the moment a student stops following. They can take the pen and mark in front of her, which is the single most effective thing a tutor does and the thing that translates least well to a screen. For Primary Years and Middle Years children, home tuition across this part of Mumbai is usually the only format that holds attention for a full hour. That is the reason IB and IGCSE home tuition in Wadala is what we lead with rather than a screen.

Online has three legitimate uses and we recommend it for those and not for others. The first is scarcity: for Higher Level Economics, Visual Arts or a less common Language B, an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Wadala may be the only route to somebody who has actually taught the course. The second is coursework check-ins, where a shared screen and a draft open side by side beats a journey. The third is the examination run-in, when short, frequent sessions become more valuable than long ones and travel makes short sessions uneconomic.

Hybrid is where most Diploma families here settle by the second term. One home session a week for the teaching and the marking, one online for question practice or an Internal Assessment review. It halves the travel load, which keeps the rate sustainable and the slot stable across an eighteen-month programme, and stability matters more than any individual lesson. It asks the student to be able to work on a screen without a second tab open, which roughly half of sixteen-year-olds can do.

Be clear-eyed about the costs. Home hours carry travel time that somebody absorbs, so they cost more per hour. Online loses the sideways correction and is weak for a student who needs a person in the room. Group formats are cheaper again and a poor fit for Internal Assessment work, where the entire point is that your child's research question is her own. A tutor who says one format is right for every family is describing their own schedule. Families searching for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Wadala usually find the format question matters more than they expected.

sections.heading: What should I ask before letting a tutor into my flat?
paragraphs: Ask for government photo identity at the gate on the first visit, ask which board and programme they have actually taught and for how many cohorts, and ask them to react to a specific piece of your child's work. Those three take four minutes and they are worth more than any rating. On our side, identity and the degree supporting the subject claim are verified before an introduction happens, and we hold a conversation with every tutor about the programme they say they know, because criterion marking and Internal Assessment supervision are learned skills rather than automatic consequences of a good degree. No IB and IGCSE home tutor in Wadala reaches a family's door before those three checks are complete.

References from previous families get checked on the dull dimensions that actually predict whether a placement survives. Punctuality. Rescheduling frequency. Whether they told the parent, unprompted, that the child was not doing the work between sessions. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Wadala families keep for two years is almost always one who delivered unwelcome news early rather than one who sent reassuring messages until February.

Then there are the checks only you can make, and the first fortnight is when to make them. Keep early sessions in a part of the flat an adult walks through. After session two, ask what specifically is going wrong and what the plan is; an answer that names a topic, a criterion or a paper type means a diagnosis has happened, and an answer about confidence and effort means it has not. Ask directly how they handle coursework and listen for someone who draws a firm line at writing anything.

Finally, the claims that should end a conversation. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and will not quote an improvement for a child nobody has assessed. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, publishes a success rate, or implies any relationship with a named school. None of those can be honestly said, and a person who says them is telling you how they will behave in the difficult month. Ask instead what they will do if there is no movement at four weeks, and listen for a plan rather than reassurance.

paragraphs: Here is the thing that is specifically true of this address. Wadala is the Eastern Freeway and Monorail hub, which puts Chembur a short run away and makes it the cheapest address adjacent to South Mumbai to staff with a suburban tutor. A tutor living in Chembur or Ghatkopar can construct a week that includes Wadala and Wadala East without ever entering the congested core of the island. Where your slot sits in that route decides your hour. The tutor arriving from the east is travelling after their own working day, so the eastern stops get the later slots, and a family insisting on half past six is implicitly asking for an island-based tutor from Matunga, Dadar or Parel. The dependency created by the Freeway should be managed rather than ignored. The arrangement that survives is a later start, a written understanding of what counts as late and when the session shortens or moves online, and an online fallback tested once while everything is calm. sections.heading: Measuring progress in a programme with no exam until the end
paragraphs: The hardest thing about judging tutoring in the International Baccalaureate is that the external examination arrives at the very end, so for most of the time you are reading proxies. The useful proxies are criterion levels in the Middle Years Programme, internal assessment marks and predicted grades in the Diploma Programme, and the quality of a draft compared with the one before it. None of those is a grade, and all of them move before a grade does.

At four weeks, look for a diagnosis rather than an improvement. The tutor should be able to tell you something you did not know and would not have guessed: that the Chemistry problem is the evaluation strand and not the content, that the Mathematics gap sits two years back in algebraic manipulation, that your daughter's essays lose marks because she never addresses the command word. If after a month the feedback is still about attitude, nothing has been diagnosed and you should say so plainly.

By one term, which is roughly June to October or November to February here, criterion levels and internal marks begin to move, and the movement is lumpy. One subject jumps a band while another sits still, because method corrections land one at a time rather than all at once. Across the full two-year Diploma arc you are looking at a student with different working habits, better draft discipline and a mark that reflects both. We do not promise particular grades and we publish no success rates, because a figure like that describes a selected set of other children.

The limits matter as much as the gains and we would rather state them now. Home tuition cannot compress a year of missed content into six weeks. It cannot carry a student who does nothing between sessions, which is the commonest reason a placement fails and is not a problem a tutor can solve. It cannot write coursework. It cannot undo a Higher Level registration after the window has closed, although it can make the two years considerably more survivable. And if the match is wrong, tell us in week three rather than month three: we replace rather than argue for patience, and the second placement is usually better because you can now say precisely what was missing.

sections.heading: Your first month of IB home tuition in Wadala, Mumbai
paragraphs: Week zero is a message with five facts: programme stage, year group, subject and level, school, and the weekday hours your child is genuinely free including who is home. That last clause is the one families leave out and the one that determines whether the first introduction works. With it, two or three names reach you within a couple of days, each already working within reach of Wadala Road.

Week one is the diagnostic session. The tutor reads marked work with your child instead of teaching new material, asks for two or three questions attempted cold, and watches how the work is set out. If coursework is live, they read the task criteria and the current draft, and they do not suggest sentences. Afterwards, expect ten minutes with you containing specifics rather than philosophy: the topics to rebuild, the strand that is costing marks, and what the next three sessions will cover.

Weeks two and three are where the habit forms or does not. The things to watch are small: whether the set work between sessions is being done, whether your child can say what the last session was about, whether the tutor arrives when they said they would. Set up the room properly once and you stop thinking about it: a table rather than a bed, the right books out, the calculator present, the phone in another room, and the building entry registered for a repeating weekly visit.

Week four is the review you booked at the start. You tell us whether the gap you first described is closing, and the answer leads somewhere: carry on, change the approach, or change the tutor. We do the third quickly when it is needed rather than defending the first slowly. That is what IB and IGCSE home tuition in Wadala looks like when it is organised properly, and an IB and IGCSE home tutor Mumbai families keep for a full programme is almost always one who was reviewed honestly in the first month.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our building in Wadala East on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and Wadala East is one of the easier addresses in this zone to staff. Tutors reach it from Chembur and the near Eastern Suburbs over the Eastern Freeway, or by Monorail, and from Matunga, Dadar and Parel on the island side. The constraint is the start time rather than the address: a tutor travelling from the east after their own working day wants a later evening slot, while a half past six request narrows you to island-based tutors. Give us the real window and we match inside it.

faqs.question: My child is in the last MYP year. Should we start now or wait for DP?
faqs.answer: Now, because the most valuable work available in that year is subject selection rather than subject teaching. A tutor who knows the Diploma Programme can look honestly at what your child is good at, as distinct from what she enjoys, and at what she might study after school, and can say whether three Higher Level choices will produce a survivable second year. Waiting until the Diploma starts means the structural decision has already been made, and the tutoring then has to work inside it rather than help shape it.

faqs.question: Where in the flat should a home tuition session actually happen?
faqs.answer: At a table in a room an adult passes through, with the textbooks out, the calculator present if the subject needs one, and the phone somewhere else entirely. Avoid the bedroom, which changes how a sixteen-year-old works more than parents expect. If the flat is noisy at that hour and your building has a bookable study room, as managed complexes in this part of Mumbai often do, that is a reasonable alternative provided the booking is standing rather than weekly. Settle the room before the first visit instead of improvising at the door.

faqs.question: What determines the fees for a tutor coming to our home?
faqs.answer: Four things, and no honest range exists before they are known. Programme stage and level, because Diploma Higher Level work commands more than Middle Years. Subject scarcity, which is the largest single factor and the reason a Visual Arts or Higher Level Economics specialist costs differently from a Mathematics one. Travel, where Wadala benefits from the Freeway opening the suburban pool. And session length and frequency, since two shorter weekly sessions often total less than one long one and generally work better. Tell us the combination and we give a realistic range for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Wadala rather than a headline figure that is wrong for somebody.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear enough to state in a sentence: a tutor can teach research method, press on the question until it is narrow enough to answer in the available length, explain what the assessment criteria reward and give feedback on a draft, exactly as a school supervisor does. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or supply text. Essays fail far more often on scope than on effort, so the most valuable hour is usually the first one, spent making the question smaller rather than the writing better.

faqs.question: Is it a problem if the tutor travels from Chembur rather than the island?
faqs.answer: Not if you design the arrangement for it. Crossing the Eastern Freeway or taking the Monorail from Chembur is predictable most of the time and unreliable several evenings a monsoon, when the alternative route through Sewri and Wadala East is slow. The arrangements that survive share three features: a later weekday start so the tutor is not travelling in the worst of it, a written understanding of what happens when they are late, and an online fallback both sides have tested once in calm conditions rather than discovered in a crisis.

faqs.question: How do I know whether the tutor is any good after a month?
faqs.answer: Judge the diagnosis, not the marks. After four sessions a good tutor tells you something concrete you did not already know: which criterion strand is costing levels, which two-year-old gap is causing the current problem, which command words your child consistently ignores. They should also be able to say what the next three sessions will cover and why. Feedback that is still about confidence and effort at four weeks means no diagnosis has happened, and that is a reason to change rather than to wait.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for a Primary Years child?
faqs.answer: Rarely well, and we usually say so rather than take the booking. Young learners need a person in the room to hold attention for a full session, and much of the useful work at that stage is reading aloud, writing by hand and being watched while doing both. Online can suit a short, specific intervention with an older primary child who is already engaged. If the specialist you need genuinely does not exist nearby, a shorter and more frequent online pattern works better than trying to replicate an hour on a screen.

faqs.question: What happens if we need to change tutors mid-term?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we replace, without a conversation about giving it more time. Tell us in week three rather than month three, because an early change costs almost nothing and a late one costs a term. We will ask what specifically was missing, which is usually more precise the second time, and that makes the replacement better matched. Handover is practical rather than ceremonial: the new tutor gets the diagnosis, the recent work and the plan, and starts from where things actually are.

faqs.question: Which schools do IB families in this part of Mumbai attend?
faqs.answer: Locally, JBCN International School, Parel and Don Bosco International School, with some families travelling to Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo or Bombay International School at Babulnath. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to any of them. We ask because the internal calendar differs between schools, and a tutor who knows when a particular school runs its internal examinations and Internal Assessment checkpoints plans the autumn differently from one working off a generic timetable.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all the subjects my child is struggling with?
faqs.answer: No, and the arithmetic of trying does not work out in your favour. Knowledge of a Higher Level science paper, a Mathematics route and a Language A oral are three separate specialisms, and one person covering all three delivers supervised homework in all three. If budget is the constraint, better economies exist: fewer subjects done properly, shorter and more frequent sessions, or a hybrid pattern that cuts travel. Two well-chosen subjects taught properly move more than five supervised ones, reliably.

faqs.question: How quickly can home tuition start once we agree?
faqs.answer: Commonly within a few days for Mathematics, the sciences and English, and longer where the specialist pool is thin. The real variable is your availability rather than ours. A flexible later evening can often be filled almost immediately because the cross-Freeway pool is open; a fixed early weekday slot needs an island-based tutor and takes longer to find. We would rather take an extra week and introduce somebody who holds the slot through the monsoon than fill it on Monday with a tutor who disappears in August.

sections.heading: How does IB and IGCSE home tuition in Walkeshwar get set up?
paragraphs: In four steps, and the whole thing is usually done inside a week. What makes it slow is not our process but missing information: parents who cannot yet say which board each child is on, which year they are in, or which hour of the week is genuinely free. The hour is the one most people get wrong. They offer the hour they would like to use rather than the hour that will still be free in November when a music class, a cousin's wedding and a work dinner have all made claims on the evening.

Households here are often mixed, and that shapes the match. One child might be in the Middle Years Programme (MYP) at a school down the hill while an older sibling is sitting Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel papers in Year 10 or Year 11. A request for IB and IGCSE home tuition in Walkeshwar from that household is really two requests, and the question is whether one tutor can carry both or whether the sensible answer is one tutor and one shorter second slot. We work that out before shortlisting rather than after, because a tutor stretched across two boards and three years delivers two mediocre half-sessions.

The output of the process is not a tutor; it is an arrangement. A named hour, a named room, an agreed rate and cancellation rule, a make-up policy, and a format for the note that comes to you afterwards. Families who settle all five in the first week almost never have a difficult conversation in month four. Families who settle none of them have the same conversation every six weeks.

sections.heading: One household, two boards: what each programme actually demands of a weekly hour
paragraphs: A Primary Years Programme (PYP) child and a Year 11 candidate cannot use the same kind of home tutor hour, and a household running both needs to accept that early. For the younger child the hour should be split: twenty minutes of reading and explaining aloud, twenty minutes of the thing that is currently hard, and a short piece of writing. Long sessions at that age produce a tired child and a tutor filling time. Three short visits beat one long one, which is a reason to prefer a tutor who lives close enough to make three visits plausible.

In the Middle Years Programme the hour becomes about criteria. MYP work is marked against separate criteria with their own descriptors, and students lose marks by answering a different criterion from the one in front of them. That is a teachable skill and it transfers across subjects, so an MYP student is often the best case for a single generalist tutor: fix the reading of task briefs once and six subjects improve. All IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Walkeshwar parents arrange for this age group are usually one evening a week with a second slot added before a submission.

At IGCSE Years 9 to 11 the hour divides differently again, and so does the decision-making. The structural choice is whether a subject is entered at Core or at Extended where both exist, with the lower tier carrying a ceiling on the grade available; the parallel decision in the Diploma Programme is Higher Level or Standard Level. Every one of those routes carries assessed components of its own, from practical skills in the sciences to speaking tasks in the languages and a coursework portfolio in some subjects. Those structures and anything resembling a weighting are revised by the boards on their own cycles, so take them from the current syllabus or subject guide for your child's examination session, or from the school's examinations officer, rather than from this page.

sections.heading: Which subjects justify a standing weekly slot?
paragraphs: The ones that compound. Mathematics is the clearest case, because almost every topic rests on an earlier one, and a gap left in Year 9 is still costing marks in Year 11. The sciences compound almost as much, particularly where quantitative work and practical write-ups are assessed. A second language compounds in a different way, through vocabulary and speaking fluency that only grow with regular use. These are the subjects where a weekly hour across a year does something that a month of intensive work before an examination cannot.

Some subjects are better served by a short burst than by a standing slot. Essay-based humanities often need three or four sessions on structure and argument and then nothing until a draft exists. Business and economics frequently need command-term work rather than content, and that can be taught in a fortnight. Arts subjects need a different kind of help entirely and usually sit outside what a home tutor can give. An honest conversation about this at the start of a year saves a family a term of paying for a slot that is producing little, and we would rather have it than keep the booking.

Where a household has two children, the subject mix decides whether one booking of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Walkeshwar can cover both. Sharing works only under narrow conditions. Two students in the same year and the same tier studying the same subject can genuinely share an hour, and on this ridge that happens more than you would expect because so many of the local Years 9 and 10 cohort are on one school calendar and therefore at the same point in the syllabus. Two students three years apart cannot share, however much the arithmetic appeals. What does work across a gap is sequencing: an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Walkeshwar taking the younger child for forty minutes and the older for an hour in one visit, which removes a second evening of travel and keeps the arrangement economic.

sections.heading: A tutor's evening circuit from Walkeshwar to Girgaon
paragraphs: IB and IGCSE home tuition in Walkeshwar works as a standing arrangement because it fits into a tutor's circuit. The ones who serve this area build an evening out of two or three stops within a few minutes of each other: Walkeshwar on the Malabar Hill ridge, Malabar Hill above it, Napean Sea Road along the western side, and Girgaon just below to the east. If your slot sits neatly inside that circuit it is stable for a year. If it sits awkwardly at the far end of it, it is the slot that gets moved when something else comes up.

This is why the island matters more than the map. South Mumbai is dense and short on distance but slow on time: a tutor crossing from Worli towards Colaba covers very little ground and can still lose most of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. Tutors here are matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs, and the reason is specifically about durability rather than convenience. A long commute is survivable for a month of enthusiasm and not for thirty weeks of ordinary Tuesdays.

Charni Road on the Western Line is the station that defines the catchment, with Grant Road a short way further along, and tutors living within reach of either can hold an early evening slot on the ridge indefinitely. Off-peak the geography has loosened slightly: the Coastal Road has shortened some runs along the western edge, and Metro Line 3 gives tutors who work in the Bandra Kurla Complex corridor during the day a route back into South Mumbai that avoids the highway entirely. That helps a weekend morning or a 7.45pm start. It does not help a 6.15pm Wednesday, and a year-long arrangement should be designed around the Wednesday.

sections.heading: Building the tuition year around your school's calendar in Mumbai
paragraphs: A standing arrangement needs a shape, and the shape comes from the school. Ask for the term's assessed submission dates, the mock examination window and the reporting dates in the first week of term, in writing, and give them to the tutor. From those four pieces of information a tutor can plan backwards, which is the difference between a year of useful work and a year of reacting. Parents who hold the dates in their head rather than on paper end up reacting, because the dates always arrive sooner than remembered.

Walkeshwar has one local feature that nowhere else in Mumbai shares in quite this way. Gopi Birla Memorial School is inside the locality and runs an IGCSE pathway, so its Years 9 and 10 students work to its internal calendar and its coursework deadlines cluster tightly into a short stretch rather than spreading across the year. For a family here that produces two effects. If your child is at that school, your year has a visible spike and the plan should be built to arrive at the spike with the weakest subject already stable. If your child is elsewhere, the spike still takes the ridge's evening slots, so your arrangement needs to be locked in before it opens.

Bombay International School at Babulnath, a short way down from the ridge, runs its own internal rhythm, as do the South Mumbai schools further along the island that families here also attend. None of them synchronise, which is why advice passed between neighbours is so often a month out. Use your own school's paper and ignore the rest, and when a neighbour tells you something has been brought forward, check it rather than rescheduling the tutor.

IB Gram is an independent platform. We are not affiliated with Gopi Birla Memorial School, Bombay International School or any other school named here, and no tutor on the platform represents a school or has access to its systems. sections.heading: Why home tuition stays the spine of the arrangement in South Mumbai
paragraphs: Because the thing a standing arrangement is buying is compliance, and compliance needs a person in the room. Over a year, the sessions that matter most are the ordinary ones in the middle of a term when nothing is due and a student is quietly repairing something from last year. Those are exactly the sessions a teenager will talk themselves out of if the format makes it easy. A tutor at the table also keeps seeing the physical record: whether the past papers are being attempted under time, whether working is written or done in the head, whether the practical notebook has been maintained since the start of the year.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Walkeshwar is a sensible part of the arrangement rather than a replacement for it. Use a screen session when the subject is scarce enough that the right specialist is not on the island, when the student is in a revision phase and wants two or three short slots a week, and when a monsoon evening or an illness would otherwise mean losing a week. For speaking tasks, practical rehearsal and the uncomfortable conversation about effort, in person stays better by a wide margin.

The hybrid version that works over a year is deliberately unbalanced: keep the full weekly slot of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Walkeshwar all year, and add short online sessions in the specific weeks they are needed rather than as a standing second commitment. A second standing commitment is what families abandon in February. Agree the split explicitly and revisit it once a term. If a tutor proposes moving the whole arrangement online in the first month, ask what changed, because the answer is sometimes about the subject and sometimes about Peddar Road.

sections.heading: What should you agree before a tutor becomes a weekly fixture?
paragraphs: Five things, all boring, all worth ten minutes before home classes become a weekly fixture. The hour and the day, including what happens if the family needs to move it. The cancellation and make-up rule, specifically who absorbs a session the family cancels late and whether a tutor-cancelled session is made up or credited. The format of the note after each session. And the review point: a date, four or five weeks out, when both sides say honestly whether this is working.

Our side of the checking is already complete before you speak to anyone. Government photo identity is verified against the profile name. Board experience is probed by asking which programme, which level or tier, and which components the tutor has taught through to an examination session, and by asking them to describe a recent student's internal assessment in enough detail that invention would show. References are requested and followed up, and a tutor who cannot provide a contactable one is not listed.

Your own checks are about fit and about the household. Ask what the tutor will do in the first half hour. Ask which subjects and levels they decline, because an answer of none is a warning. sections.heading: What a full year of home tuition in Walkeshwar actually looks like
paragraphs: A year of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Walkeshwar has three distinct phases, and the first term is build. Weeks one to four are diagnosis and one repair: the single topic that most other topics depend on, plus one routine installed, usually a dated weekly plan or a checking pass at the end of every written answer. Weeks five to twelve widen out, working through the dependency topics in order while the tutor keeps an eye on the school's assessed components. This is the quietest and most productive part of the year, and it is also the part parents are most tempted to interrupt because nothing visible is happening.

The second term is pressure. Submissions cluster, mocks arrive, and the tutor's role shifts from teaching to triage: deciding what gets tonight, what can be adequate, what is abandoned. Families often want extra sessions here, and extra sessions are reasonable, but the gains made in this term were mostly earned in the first one. A student who arrives at the cluster with their weakest subject already stable sails through it; one who arrives with three unstable subjects does not, and no amount of additional hours in February fixes a decision made in August.

The third term splits depending on the year group. For a Year 11 or Diploma Programme 2 student it is paper technique, timed practice and recovery of the specific topics the mocks exposed. For everyone else it is the opposite: the term to go back and close the content skipped during the pressure weeks, which is the gap that otherwise surfaces a year later. The common mistake is to stop tuition the moment the pressure passes, and the better move is to keep the slot for four to six weeks and spend it on exactly that.

Then there is the long break, and families handle it badly in both directions. Stopping entirely for eight weeks costs a mathematics or language student real ground and makes the restart slow. Running the full weekly arrangement through a holiday that the child needed produces resentment and poor sessions. A reduced pattern works better: one session a week for half the break on the subject that compounds most, nothing on the rest. Families looking for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai often assume the break is when the sweep happens; in practice the break is for consolidation, not for new ground.

sections.heading: What should we expect by week four, and by the end of the year?
paragraphs: IB and IGCSE home tuition in Walkeshwar moves different things at different speeds. By week four, expect changed behaviour and nothing on paper. Timed practice happening without being asked for, working written out properly, and a child who can name the specific thing they do not understand rather than saying they are bad at the subject. By the end of a term, internal marks and classwork usually move, because those respond to method and to completed work. Across a full examination cycle a final grade can move, sometimes considerably, and how far depends on when you started and on what happens in the six days a week nobody is supervising.

We publish no success rates and we do not guarantee grades. An honest figure would have to account for students who stopped attending, students whose difficulty was never academic, and students who would have improved regardless. There are also situations where a standing arrangement is the wrong answer and we will say so: a child already over-scheduled and short of sleep, an unassessed reading or attention difficulty, a subject taken under pressure from an adult. Adding a weekly hour to any of those makes the week worse rather than better, and the useful advice is a conversation with the school about workload, tier or accommodation.

Parents also look for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Walkeshwar, and a year-long arrangement is exactly the context in which that question is least useful. Over thirty sessions, reliability beats brilliance by a distance. The tutor who arrives every week, sends a three-line note, and tells you in week four that something is not working is worth more than a more impressive tutor who delivers twenty sessions out of thirty. Judge IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Walkeshwar against sessions actually delivered and against what you can see in the notes, rather than against an hourly rate in isolation.

faqs.answer: It is driven by five inputs and we give you the realistic range for your request before any introduction. Board and year group, since Year 11 and Diploma Programme 2 work prices above Middle Years Programme support. Level or tier, because Higher Level and top-end Extended work needs a stronger specialist. Subject scarcity, which matters most of all. Travel, which is why a tutor walking over from Malabar Hill and one crossing the island do not quote the same number. And session length and frequency. Across a year the number that matters is cost per session actually delivered, which is why reliability is worth paying for.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both my children if they are on different boards?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on the gap rather than the boards. A tutor comfortable with both Cambridge and Diploma Programme mathematics can take a Year 10 student and a Diploma Programme 1 student in back-to-back slots on the same visit, which saves an evening of travel and keeps the arrangement affordable. What does not work is one hour split between two children at different stages, which produces two half-sessions and satisfies neither. If the children are three or more years apart, plan for two slots with one tutor rather than one shared slot, and expect the younger child's to be shorter.

faqs.question: Where in the home should a weekly session happen if we have no study room?
faqs.answer: A dining table is better than a dedicated room that happens to be a bedroom. What matters is a hard surface with space for two people and papers, a chair the tutor can use for an hour without displacing anyone, no television in the line of sight, and no phone on the table. Sessions behind a closed bedroom door are not a sensible arrangement for anybody involved. If the dining area is where the household gathers, agree the hour with everyone in the flat rather than assuming they will notice; in a compact South Mumbai home that single conversation prevents most interruptions.

faqs.question: Should I sit in on sessions, or leave them to it?
faqs.answer: Sit in on the first one and then stay out of the room but in the flat. The first session is a diagnostic and you will understand the tutor's reading of the problem far better by hearing it than by reading a summary. After that, a parent in the room changes how a teenager behaves and usually makes them less willing to admit what they do not understand, which is the most useful thing they can do. Being in the flat matters for a different reason: it keeps the session's boundaries real. Read the written note instead of listening at the door.

faqs.question: What happens to the slot during school holidays?
faqs.answer: Decide it in advance rather than week by week, because an undecided holiday is how a good arrangement quietly ends. A reduced pattern works best: keep one session a week for roughly half the break, focused on the subject that compounds most, usually mathematics or a language, and stop entirely for the rest. Running the full arrangement through a holiday a child genuinely needed produces resentment and poor sessions. Stopping for eight weeks costs real ground and makes the restart slow. Tell the tutor your plan early, since they are planning their own year too.

faqs.question: What happens when a tutor is delayed commuting across South Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens, because it will happen. A reasonable arrangement is that a delay of up to about fifteen minutes is absorbed and the session runs short, and anything longer is rescheduled rather than squeezed. The Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak are the usual culprits, which is exactly why we match within the island rather than bringing tutors down from the suburbs. If delays become a pattern rather than an occurrence, that is a sign the slot is wrong for that tutor's circuit, and the fix is to change the hour or change the tutor.

faqs.question: Does the building need to be told every week, or just once?
faqs.answer: Usually once, and it is worth getting right at the start. Give your society office or security desk the tutor's full name, mobile number, the day and the time, and ask whether they want a standing entry in the visitor register or a weekly intimation from your flat. Most buildings on the ridge are happy with a standing arrangement for a regular visitor. Where photo identity has to be recorded, the tutor will already have been identity-checked by us and will carry it. Doing this once removes the single most common cause of a late start across a year.

faqs.question: How many subjects can one weekly hour realistically carry?
faqs.answer: One, properly, or two if they are closely related and the student is reasonably organised. An hour spread across four subjects is a conversation rather than teaching, and it produces the familiar outcome where a parent feels helped and nothing changes. If a child needs help in four subjects, the honest answer is usually that the problem is not four subjects but one shared skill, most often how written answers are structured or how work is planned across a week. Fix the shared skill in one subject and watch whether the others follow; if they do not, add a second slot rather than subdividing the first.

faqs.question: What should the tutor send us after each session?
faqs.answer: Three or four lines is enough and more than most families get. What was covered, what the student could not do, what has been set for the week, and anything you should know. The value is cumulative: twelve such notes read together show you a trajectory that no single session reveals, and they make the four-week review a factual conversation rather than an exchange of impressions. Ask for this before the first session and treat reluctance as information. A tutor who is comfortable being observed writes the note without being chased.

faqs.question: When is the right time to stop?
faqs.answer: When the student is doing the work the tutor used to supervise without being supervised, which is a recognisable moment rather than a vague feeling. Signs include a child who starts the week with a plan, attempts past papers unprompted, and brings specific questions to the session instead of a general sense of being behind. At that point reduce to a fortnightly slot before stopping altogether, so there is a check in place if the habit slips. Stopping abruptly at the end of a term that went well is how families find themselves restarting from a worse position six months later.

faqs.question: The tutor is good, but the slot keeps moving. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Treat it as the serious problem it is, because over a year a moving slot costs more than a weaker tutor would. Raise it once, directly, and ask whether the hour is simply wrong for their circuit; often it is, and moving to a different fixed evening solves it permanently. If the pattern continues after that conversation, ask us for a replacement. The sessions a drifting tutor loses are the ordinary mid-term ones, which is where most of the progress is made, so the damage is larger and less visible than a cancelled session before an examination.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with Gopi Birla Memorial School, Bombay International School, or any other school named here. We name schools because their internal calendars are the actual structure of a family's year on the Malabar Hill ridge, and because a tutor who understands a school's rhythm plans better around it. sections.heading: How we build a home tuition arrangement that lasts more than a term
paragraphs: Most tutoring on this corridor fails for structural reasons rather than pedagogical ones, so the matching is built backwards from durability. Before subject or stage we establish three things: which evening is permanently free rather than currently free, who is in the flat at that hour, and where in the flat a person can sit and write for ninety minutes. Those answers eliminate more candidate arrangements than any question about teaching does, and getting them wrong is why a family finds itself re-hiring every six months.

The International Baccalaureate stage comes next and it filters hard. A tutor who is strong with a Diploma Programme (DP) student finishing an Internal Assessment (IA) is often the wrong person for a Grade 3 Primary Years Programme (PYP) child, because what is being taught differs in kind. Middle Years Programme (MYP) work needs someone who reads criterion descriptors rather than syllabi. We ask the stage first, then the subject, then what the school has actually said is wrong, in that order.

Only then does travel enter. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Worli Sea Face has to be reachable on the same evening every week for years rather than weeks, which in practice means a tutor already living or teaching within the island. We shortlist two or three people who fit the stage, tell you which of them is a stretch on the journey, and arrange calls. Nobody is sent to your tower before you have chosen, and the first paid session is a diagnostic that produces written notes the same week.

The last part of the build is the paperwork, which sounds trivial and is the reason these arrangements last. We pass the tutor's identity details to you on confirmation, you lodge them once with the building office, and from the second visit the tutor signs against a standing entry. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Worli Sea Face who has to be cleared as a visitor every week is an arrangement with a slow leak in it, and the home tuition we arrange across this part of Mumbai is set up specifically to avoid that. One with a standing pass can change its day, add a sibling, or pause for a term and resume without any administration at all.

sections.heading: How does tutoring change from PYP to MYP to DP?
paragraphs: It changes from habits to criteria to coursework, and recognising which of the three you are in saves a term of wrong help. In the Primary Years Programme the work is reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining thinking aloud. There is no syllabus to revise, so a tutor who arrives with worksheets has misread the stage. Progress here looks like a child who reads something longer than they did two months ago and can say what happened in it without being prompted question by question.

In the Middle Years Programme the organising unit becomes the assessment criterion. Work is reported against separate criteria across eight subject groups, and a child sitting at a middle level in two of them and a high level in the others produces a report that reads as fine while a specific skill is quietly failing. A tutor at this stage should be able to name the lowest criterion and describe what the next level up requires in writing. The detailed Middle Years material, including the Year 5 personal project, belongs to a dedicated page rather than this one.

In the Diploma Programme the difficulty moves into coursework and sequencing. Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices, an Internal Assessment in every subject, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) all carry their own deadlines, and a student who leaves them to the same fortnight produces four weak pieces instead of two strong ones. Most of the value a tutor adds in these two years is in the research question and the schedule rather than in content delivery.

The transitions between stages are where households get caught out. A child who was comfortable in the Primary Years Programme can struggle badly in the first Middle Years year because the demand shifts from knowing to justifying. A Middle Years student with good criterion levels can still find the Diploma Programme's coursework volume a shock. This is the strongest argument for keeping one tutor across a transition: they already know what the student does when the work gets unfamiliar, which is the only diagnosis that transfers between stages.

sections.heading: Subject depth, Higher Level choices and the coursework that follows
paragraphs: Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Worli Sea Face covers, the matching variable that matters is the component rather than the title. A student can know a subject well and lose marks because nobody explained that one assessment rewards sustained structured argument while another rewards short precise working. So we match on the component the school has flagged: a Diploma Programme Mathematics request gets someone who has supervised explorations, not just someone who can do the mathematics.

Higher Level choices deserve a blunt conversation early. Three Higher Level subjects carry the deepest content and three sets of coursework, and the regret we hear most often is not that a subject was too hard. It is that a Higher Level was chosen for a university application the student had already lost interest in. The honest test is whether the student would read around the subject unprompted. A tutor can carry a difficult choice; nobody can manufacture an interest that was never there.

The Internal Assessments are where a long arrangement earns its keep, because they are not a single event. In the sciences the work is an investigation with a defensible research question, properly controlled variables and honest uncertainty treatment. In Mathematics it is an exploration where the mathematics must be used rather than described. In the humanities and languages there are written tasks with their own command terms. A tutor who has read the actual criteria for your child's subject will spend the first session on the question alone, which parents sometimes think was a wasted session and which usually turns out to be the decisive one.

Programme guides are revised on the International Baccalaureate's own cycle, so component names and structures change between cohorts. Nothing on this page quotes a weighting, a duration or a mark total for that reason, and any tutor who does should be asked where the figure comes from. Get the current subject guide from the school's programme coordinator, hand it to the tutor, and have them plan the term from it. All IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Worli Sea Face families arrange should begin from that document rather than from a tutor's memory of an earlier syllabus.

sections.heading: Worli, Prabhadevi and Mahalaxmi: the home tuition catchment in South Mumbai
paragraphs: A tutor placed on this stretch covers Worli, Prabhadevi and Mahalaxmi, and for a multi-year arrangement that radius is tighter than it looks. South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow: crossing from Worli to Colaba is about eight kilometres and can still cost forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, so tutors here are matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs. A journey that is merely tolerable in July becomes the reason for a cancelled session in December, which is why home classes in this part of Mumbai are matched on the journey before anything else.

Prabhadevi is the nearest station and the reference point for anyone arriving by train. The Western Line through Churchgate, Grant Road and Mumbai Central brings tutors down the island quickly; the Harbour Line through CSMT, Dockyard and Sewri covers the eastern edge; and Metro Line 3 on the Aqua corridor between Cuffe Parade and BKC has made some cross-city matches realistic that were not before. The Coastal Road has shortened the northbound evening run without doing anything for the junctions that actually cost time.

Within the locality the useful unit stops being the area and becomes the tower. Buildings along Worli Sea Face each run their own lobby protocol, and getting from the gate to a high-floor flat in Omkar 1973 or Piramal Aranya can take longer than the drive from Mahalaxmi did. A tutor who has done the trip before knows which lift bank serves which floors and where the pass list sits. For a weekly arrangement running across years, that saved time compounds into several full sessions.

Families occasionally ask whether to look towards Lower Parel or Dadar for a scarce Higher Level subject. For one subject, yes. For three, no. One tutor making a slightly longer journey for a single standing slot is sustainable; three tutors converging on one tower from three different corridors in the same week is the arrangement that fails first, usually in the second term. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Worli Sea Face works best when the whole household timetable is built around one or two reliable journeys rather than four optimistic ones.

sections.heading: What does the Mumbai school calendar do to an IB household?
paragraphs: It concentrates everything into two stretches and leaves the rest of the year comparatively open, which is useful if you plan for it. Families on this corridor commonly send children to Ryan Global School and Aditya Birla World Academy. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with either school or any other named on this site; they appear because school-set deadlines, not the International Baccalaureate's own calendar, decide when the household is under pressure. Two schools on the same programme can set draft deadlines weeks apart.

The pattern runs roughly like this. June to September builds content while the load is light, and is the best window to establish a new arrangement because tutors have slot choice. October to early December is the collision: Diploma Programme coursework drafts, mock examinations and Middle Years summative tasks land together, and demand for evening home classes along the sea face peaks. January and February carry final Internal Assessment submissions and the Extended Essay deadline. From March a Diploma Programme student sitting the May session is in revision proper, and tutoring shifts to timed papers.

A household with two children in different programmes feels this differently from a household with one. A Grade 5 Primary Years exhibition and a Diploma Programme first-year coursework push can land in the same month, and both children want the same adult attention and the same quiet room. This is the single most common scheduling problem on this corridor and it has a dull fix: stagger the two tutoring slots onto different evenings rather than running them back to back, so the flat has one occupied room at a time.

The practical instruction from all of this is to call before the calendar decides for you. A family enquiring in late October is competing for the same two slots as every neighbour and asking a tutor to repair in six weeks a habit built over a year. The same enquiry in June gets a wider shortlist, a tutor who can take a convenient evening rather than a leftover one, and enough runway that the first diagnostic changes something before anything is formally assessed.

sections.heading: Where should the lesson actually happen in a sea-facing flat?
paragraphs: At a table with chairs on both sides, in a room without a television, and the number of arrangements that fail because this was not sorted out is larger than anyone would guess. A tutor needs to see the page as it is being written, which rules out a sofa, a bed and a high stool at a kitchen counter. A child's bedroom desk is usually too small for two people and faces a wall of distractions. The dining table, cleared, with the tutor sitting adjacent rather than opposite, is the arrangement that works in most flats along this stretch.

Several towers here have a common study room or a library space, and it is worth knowing when to use it. It suits two siblings working with the same tutor in sequence, since nobody has to be moved out of a bedroom. It suits a household where a younger child cannot be kept quiet for ninety minutes. It is poor for a student who looks up every time a neighbour walks past, and it is poor for anything involving spoken practice in a language. Decide before the first visit, because changing the venue in week three costs a session to re-establish.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Worli Sea Face is the right answer in three specific cases rather than as a default. A scarce Higher Level subject where the only genuinely experienced teacher is in another city. The weeks before an examination session, when three short contacts outperform one long one. And any stretch where travel, illness or monsoon disruption would otherwise collapse the arrangement. Document work in particular, such as an Extended Essay draft with margin comments appearing live, is often better online than over a printed copy.

The honest limits of online are consistent. Younger students leak attention within a quarter of an hour unless an adult is within earshot. Mathematics and the sciences slow badly when diagrams have to be drawn with a mouse or a tablet pen. And a tutor who has never been in the flat has no idea whether the study space is usable, which matters more than parents expect. The settlement most households here reach is one weekly home visit as the anchor plus a short online contact, with the balance tilting online as an examination session approaches.

Qualification, meaning the degree or teaching credential exists and is in the subject claimed. And programme experience, which is checked hardest because it is where profiles blur: a national-board teaching history is not International Baccalaureate experience, and a tutor claiming Diploma Programme Biology should be able to describe what separates a weak research question from a strong one without being prompted.

Verification cannot establish fit and never will. A tutor can clear every check and be entirely wrong for one particular thirteen-year-old. That is why you speak to candidates before confirmation and why the first paid session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson. For a multi-year arrangement this matters more, not less: the cost of a poor fit discovered in week two is an awkward call, and the cost of the same fit discovered in month five is a wasted term.

Your own checks are short. Ask the tutor to describe the assessment components for your child's exact subject and stage, and treat vagueness as disqualifying. Ask what the first session consists of, listening for whether it involves reading the student's own marked work. Ask what arrives after four weeks. Be wary of anyone who answers with a promised grade rather than a plan, because IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor offers one.

The check that is specific to this corridor is the building. Worli Sea Face is a line of sea-facing towers with strict visitor registration, so tutors here are given a standing gate pass rather than being cleared session by session. Practically: you lodge the tutor's identity details with the building office in the first week, and from the second visit the tutor signs against a standing entry. For a long arrangement the pass becomes an asset. It is what lets you shift the slot from Tuesday to Thursday, add a younger sibling on the same evening, or pause for the monsoon and resume in July without re-establishing anything at the gate.

sections.heading: Can one tutor work with two children at different stages?
paragraphs: Sometimes, and the deciding factor is the gap between the stages rather than the subjects. Two Middle Years children two years apart can genuinely share a tutor, often in consecutive forty-five-minute halves of one visit, because the skills being built are close enough that the tutor is not switching profession between them. A Primary Years child and a Diploma Programme sibling cannot sensibly share one, whatever the economics suggest, because the second half of the visit requires a different kind of teacher from the first.

Where sharing does work it works because of the travel, not the teaching. One journey, one gate entry, two students: that is what makes IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Worli Sea Face more manageable for a two-child household, since the travel cost that sits invisibly inside every quoted rate is paid once instead of twice. What it does not do is halve the teaching time, and a parent expecting ninety minutes each from a ninety-minute visit will be disappointed. Ask for the split explicitly and have it written into the arrangement.

The sequencing matters more than people expect. Put the younger child first, while they are still alert and before homework has eaten the evening, and the older one second, when they can work independently for the first ten minutes while the tutor finishes next door. Running it the other way produces a nine-year-old being taught at 8pm, which is a waste of everyone's money. If both children need full attention in the same hour, the honest answer is two tutors on two evenings.

There is also a version of this question about years rather than siblings. A tutor who worked with a child through two Middle Years years is usually the right person to continue into the Diploma Programme if they have genuine experience at that stage, and the wrong person if they do not. We say which, rather than letting a comfortable relationship carry into a stage the tutor has not taught. Where a change is needed we ask for handover notes, so the new tutor starts from two years of evidence rather than from a fresh diagnostic.

sections.heading: Four weeks, one term, one exam session: what each should show in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks you are looking for behaviour, not marks, and the markers are checkable without knowing the subject. The student starts work without asking whether they are allowed to. They attempt the parts they used to leave blank. They can restate a task before attempting it. They arrive at the session with their own list of confusions. Two of those four is normal at four weeks. None of them is a signal to have a direct conversation with the tutor that week, which is far cheaper than having it in February.

At one term the change should be visible in school work. A Diploma Programme student should have a research question their teacher has accepted, or a draft returned with comments about refinement rather than about starting again. A Middle Years student should have gained a level in at least one criterion and be able to say which and why. A Primary Years child should be choosing longer books. The tutor should be able to name secure and weak topics specifically. A report that things are going well is not a report.

Across a full examination cycle the claim worth making is narrow. A good arrangement closes the gap between what a student knows and what they produce under timed conditions, and that gap is often the largest single recoverable loss. It does not change school teaching quality, the student's willingness to work, or performance in subjects nobody is tutoring. IB Gram publishes no success rates and does not guarantee grades, and a platform offering either is describing its marketing.

The multi-year version of this is worth saying separately, because it is the honest case for a long arrangement. The gain from year three of the same tutor is not that they teach better than they did in year one. It is that nothing has to be rediagnosed, the student no longer performs for a stranger, and the tutor can tell in one session whether a bad report is a content gap or a motivation dip. Those are real advantages and they are the whole argument for durability. They are not a substitute for the student doing the work, and no arrangement however long makes a grade certain.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach two of our children on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes if their stages are close, no if they are far apart. Two Middle Years children two years apart share a tutor well, usually as consecutive halves of one visit. A Primary Years child and a Diploma Programme sibling need different kinds of teacher and should not share. Where sharing works, the saving is the travel rather than the teaching, so agree the time split explicitly instead of assuming ninety minutes each from one ninety-minute visit. Teach the younger child first, while they are still alert.

faqs.question: Should we keep the same tutor when our child moves from MYP into DP?
faqs.answer: Only if the tutor has genuine Diploma Programme experience in that subject. Continuity is valuable because nothing has to be rediagnosed and the student no longer performs for a stranger, but the Diploma Programme asks for coursework supervision and research-question work that a Middle Years specialist may never have done. We will say plainly which situation a tutor is in rather than letting a comfortable relationship carry into an untaught stage. A student who has been told a tutor is the consequence of a bad report arrives having decided to waste the hour, and no amount of teaching skill fixes that in a term. The arrangements that work start from a problem the student themselves recognises, even a small one. sections.heading: One house, two boards: what changes when a child moves from IGCSE into the DP?
paragraphs: Almost everything about how work is produced, and almost nothing about the content. An IGCSE student works in a world of defined syllabus content and terminal papers, where thorough coverage plus technique is a reliable route to a good grade. A Diploma Programme student works in a world of coursework, internal assessment and extended writing, where a well-covered syllabus is necessary and not sufficient. The marks that used to come from knowing come increasingly from structuring, evaluating and finishing things on time. Students who were comfortable at IGCSE and struggle in DP1 are usually meeting this change rather than a harder syllabus.

Concretely, the DP adds an Internal Assessment (IA) in each subject, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK), and these arrive in a cluster rather than spread out. A DP2 student can have an IA draft, a TOK deadline and a mock paper inside a single fortnight. No amount of subject knowledge helps with that; what helps is sequencing, and that is a tutoring job which looks nothing like the tutoring that worked in Year 11. Confirm the current shape of these components with your school's DP coordinator rather than trusting any web page, because the IB revises subject guides on its own cycle.

The transition in the other direction, from MYP into IGCSE, is less discussed and catches families out more. An MYP student is used to criteria A to D, where a task is marked against named skills and feedback says which skill was weak. An IGCSE student meets a mark scheme that rewards method and precision in ways nobody has previously explained. The six to eight weeks in which that penny drops are worth tutoring explicitly, and a tutor who has taught both systems can do it quickly. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Worli households keep across a transition is usually someone who has.

The practical point for a household with two children on different boards is that a single tutor who understands both systems is worth holding on to, because the younger child will eventually make the same journey. That continuity is the quiet argument for building a long arrangement rather than hiring per crisis. Families who arrange IB and IGCSE home tuition in Worli as a standing relationship rather than an emergency measure get the benefit twice.
